book.title: Bible
book.license: KJV: public domain. Hebrew: Miqra according to the Masorah via openscriptures/morphhb (CC BY 4.0). Greek: SBL Greek New Testament (CC BY-SA 4.0).
book.notes: Old Testament original is the Hebrew Masoretic text; New Testament original is the SBL Greek text. Transliteration is automatic and flagged. Hebrew verse numbering can differ from KJV numbering in a few psalms.

verses.original: Ἰησοῦς δὲ ⸂πλήρης πνεύματος ἁγίου⸃ ὑπέστρεψεν ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, καὶ ἤγετο ἐν τῷ πνεύματι ⸂ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ⸃
verses.translit: Iisous de pliris pneymatos agioy upestrepsen apo tou Iordanoy, kai egeto en to pneymati en te erimo
verses.translation: And Jesus being full of the Holy Ghost returned from Jordan, and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness,

verses.original: ἡμέρας τεσσεράκοντα πειραζόμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου. καὶ οὐκ ἔφαγεν οὐδὲν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις, καὶ συντελεσθεισῶν ⸀αὐτῶν ἐπείνασεν.
verses.translit: emeras tesserakonta peirazomenos upo tou diavoloy. kai ouk efagen ouden en tais emerais ekeinais, kai syntelestheison auton epeinasen.
verses.translation: Being forty days tempted of the devil. And in those days he did eat nothing: and when they were ended, he afterward hungered.

verses.original: ⸂εἶπεν δὲ⸃ αὐτῷ ὁ διάβολος· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰπὲ τῷ λίθῳ τούτῳ ἵνα γένηται ἄρτος.
verses.translit: eipen de auto o diavolos* Ei yios ei tou theou, eipe to litho toyto ina genitai artos.
verses.translation: And the devil said unto him, If thou be the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπεκρίθη ⸂πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃· Γέγραπται ὅτι Οὐκ ἐπʼ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ⸀ὁ ⸀ἄνθρωπος.
verses.translit: kai apekrithi pros auton o Iisous* Gegraptai oti Ouk ep' arto mono zisetai o anthropos.
verses.translation: And Jesus answered him, saying, It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀναγαγὼν ⸀αὐτὸν ἔδειξεν αὐτῷ πάσας τὰς βασιλείας τῆς οἰκουμένης ἐν στιγμῇ χρόνου·
verses.translit: Kai anagagon auton edeixen auto pasas tas vasileias tes oikoymenis en stigme hronoy*
verses.translation: And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ διάβολος· Σοὶ δώσω τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἅπασαν καὶ τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν, ὅτι ἐμοὶ παραδέδοται καὶ ᾧ ⸀ἂν θέλω δίδωμι αὐτήν·
verses.translit: kai eipen auto o diavolos* Soi doso ten exoysian taytin apasan kai ten doxan auton, oti emoi paradedotai kai o an thelo didomi autin*
verses.translation: And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.

verses.original: σὺ οὖν ἐὰν προσκυνήσῃς ἐνώπιον ἐμοῦ, ἔσται σοῦ πᾶσα.
verses.translit: su oun ean proskynises enopion emou, estai sou pasa.
verses.translation: If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ⸂ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ⸃· Γέγραπται· ⸂Κύριον τὸν θεόν σου προσκυνήσεις⸃ καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις.
verses.translit: kai apokritheis o Iisous eipen auto* Gegraptai* Kyrion ton theon soy proskyniseis kai auto mono latreyseis.
verses.translation: And Jesus answered and said unto him, Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.

verses.original: ⸂Ἤγαγεν δὲ⸃ αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ ⸀ἔστησεν ἐπὶ τὸ πτερύγιον τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, βάλε σεαυτὸν ἐντεῦθεν κάτω·
verses.translit: Egagen de auton eis Ieroysalem kai estisen epi to pterygion tou ierou, kai eipen auto* Ei yios ei tou theou, vale seayton enteuthen kato*
verses.translation: And he brought him to Jerusalem, and set him on a pinnacle of the temple, and said unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down from hence:

verses.original: γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ ἐντελεῖται περὶ σοῦ τοῦ διαφυλάξαι σε,
verses.translit: gegraptai gar oti Tois aggelois autou enteleitai peri sou tou diafylaxai se,
verses.translation: For it is written, He shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee:

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ὅτι Ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἀροῦσίν σε μήποτε προσκόψῃς πρὸς λίθον τὸν πόδα σου.
verses.translit: kai oti Epi heiron arousin se mipote proskopses pros lithon ton poda soy.
verses.translation: And in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Εἴρηται· Οὐκ ἐκπειράσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου.
verses.translit: kai apokritheis eipen auto o Iisous oti Eiritai* Ouk ekpeiraseis kyrion ton theon soy.
verses.translation: And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.

verses.original: καὶ συντελέσας πάντα πειρασμὸν ὁ διάβολος ἀπέστη ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ ἄχρι καιροῦ.
verses.translit: kai syntelesas panta peirasmon o diavolos apesti ap' autou ahri kairou.
verses.translation: And when the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season.

verses.original: Καὶ ὑπέστρεψεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ πνεύματος εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν. καὶ φήμη ἐξῆλθεν καθʼ ὅλης τῆς περιχώρου περὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Kai upestrepsen o Iisous en te dynamei tou pneymatos eis ten Galilaian. kai fimi exelthen kath' olis tes perihoroy peri autou.
verses.translation: And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee: and there went out a fame of him through all the region round about.

verses.original: καὶ αὐτὸς ἐδίδασκεν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν, δοξαζόμενος ὑπὸ πάντων.
verses.translit: kai autos edidasken en tais synagogais auton, doxazomenos upo panton.
verses.translation: And he taught in their synagogues, being glorified of all.

verses.original: Καὶ ἦλθεν ⸀εἰς Ναζαρά, οὗ ἦν τεθραμμένος, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν κατὰ τὸ εἰωθὸς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων εἰς τὴν συναγωγήν, καὶ ἀνέστη ἀναγνῶναι.
verses.translit: Kai elthen eis Nazara, ou en tethrammenos, kai eiselthen kata to eiothos auto en te emera ton savvaton eis ten synagogin, kai anesti anagnonai.
verses.translation: And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπεδόθη αὐτῷ βιβλίον ⸂τοῦ προφήτου Ἠσαΐου⸃ καὶ ⸀ἀναπτύξας τὸ βιβλίον εὗρεν τὸν τόπον οὗ ἦν γεγραμμένον·
verses.translit: kai epedothi auto vivlion tou profitoy EsaIoy kai anaptyxas to vivlion euren ton topon ou en gegrammenon*
verses.translation: And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias. And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written,

verses.original: Πνεῦμα κυρίου ἐπʼ ἐμέ, οὗ εἵνεκεν ἔχρισέν με εὐαγγελίσασθαι πτωχοῖς, ἀπέσταλκέν ⸀με κηρύξαι αἰχμαλώτοις ἄφεσιν καὶ τυφλοῖς ἀνάβλεψιν, ἀποστεῖλαι τεθραυσμένους ἐν ἀφέσει,
verses.translit: Pneuma kyrioy ep' eme, ou eineken ehrisen me euaggelisasthai ptohois, apestalken me kiryxai aihmalotois afesin kai tyflois anavlepsin, aposteilai tethraysmenoys en afesei,
verses.translation: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised,

verses.original: κηρύξαι ἐνιαυτὸν κυρίου δεκτόν.
verses.translit: kiryxai eniayton kyrioy dekton.
verses.translation: To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.

verses.original: καὶ πτύξας τὸ βιβλίον ἀποδοὺς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ ἐκάθισεν· καὶ πάντων ⸂οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ⸃ ἦσαν ἀτενίζοντες αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai ptyxas to vivlion apodous to upirete ekathisen* kai panton oi ofthalmoi en te synagoge esan atenizontes auto.
verses.translation: And he closed the book, and he gave it again to the minister, and sat down. And the eyes of all them that were in the synagogue were fastened on him.

verses.original: ἤρξατο δὲ λέγειν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Σήμερον πεπλήρωται ἡ γραφὴ αὕτη ἐν τοῖς ὠσὶν ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: erxato de legein pros autous oti Simeron peplirotai e grafe auti en tois osin umon.
verses.translation: And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.

verses.original: καὶ πάντες ἐμαρτύρουν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις τῆς χάριτος τοῖς ἐκπορευομένοις ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔλεγον· ⸂Οὐχὶ υἱός ἐστιν Ἰωσὴφ οὗτος⸃;
verses.translit: kai pantes emartyroyn auto kai ethaymazon epi tois logois tes haritos tois ekporeyomenois ek tou stomatos autou, kai elegon* Ouhi yios estin Iosef outos;
verses.translation: And all bare him witness, and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth. And they said, Is not this Joseph’s son?

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Πάντως ἐρεῖτέ μοι τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην· Ἰατρέ, θεράπευσον σεαυτόν· ὅσα ἠκούσαμεν γενόμενα ⸂εἰς τὴν Καφαρναοὺμ⸃ ποίησον καὶ ὧδε ἐν τῇ πατρίδι σου.
verses.translit: kai eipen pros autoys* Pantos ereite moi ten paravolen taytin* Iatre, therapeyson seayton* osa ekoysamen genomena eis ten Kafarnaoum poiison kai ode en te patridi soy.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Ye will surely say unto me this proverb, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country.

verses.original: εἶπεν δέ· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς προφήτης δεκτός ἐστιν ἐν τῇ πατρίδι αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: eipen de* Amen lego umin oti oudeis profitis dektos estin en te patridi autou.
verses.translation: And he said, Verily I say unto you, No prophet is accepted in his own country.

verses.original: ἐπʼ ἀληθείας δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, πολλαὶ χῆραι ἦσαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἠλίου ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ, ὅτε ἐκλείσθη ὁ οὐρανὸς ⸀ἐπὶ ἔτη τρία καὶ μῆνας ἕξ, ὡς ἐγένετο λιμὸς μέγας ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν,
verses.translit: ep' alitheias de lego umin, pollai herai esan en tais emerais Elioy en to Israil, ote ekleisthi o ouranos epi eti tria kai menas ex, os egeneto limos megas epi pasan ten gen,
verses.translation: But I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land;

verses.original: καὶ πρὸς οὐδεμίαν αὐτῶν ἐπέμφθη Ἠλίας εἰ μὴ εἰς Σάρεπτα τῆς ⸀Σιδωνίας πρὸς γυναῖκα χήραν.
verses.translit: kai pros oudemian auton epemfthi Elias ei me eis Sarepta tes Sidonias pros gynaika hiran.
verses.translation: But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.

verses.original: καὶ πολλοὶ λεπροὶ ἦσαν ⸂ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ ἐπὶ Ἐλισαίου τοῦ προφήτου⸃, καὶ οὐδεὶς αὐτῶν ἐκαθαρίσθη, εἰ μὴ Ναιμὰν ὁ Σύρος.
verses.translit: kai polloi leproi esan en to Israel epi Elisaioy tou profitoy, kai oudeis auton ekatharisthi, ei me Naiman o Syros.
verses.translation: And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν πάντες θυμοῦ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἀκούοντες ταῦτα,
verses.translit: kai eplisthisan pantes thymou en te synagoge akoyontes tauta,
verses.translation: And all they in the synagogue, when they heard these things, were filled with wrath,

verses.original: καὶ ἀναστάντες ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἕως ὀφρύος τοῦ ὄρους ἐφʼ οὗ ἡ πόλις ⸂ᾠκοδόμητο αὐτῶν, ὥστε⸃ κατακρημνίσαι αὐτόν·
verses.translit: kai anastantes exevalon auton exo tes poleos, kai egagon auton eos ofryos tou oroys ef' ou e polis okodomito auton, oste katakrimnisai auton*
verses.translation: And rose up, and thrust him out of the city, and led him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might cast him down headlong.

verses.original: αὐτὸς δὲ διελθὼν διὰ μέσου αὐτῶν ἐπορεύετο.
verses.translit: autos de dielthon dia mesoy auton eporeyeto.
verses.translation: But he passing through the midst of them went his way,

verses.original: Καὶ κατῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ πόλιν τῆς Γαλιλαίας. καὶ ἦν διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν·
verses.translit: Kai katelthen eis Kafarnaoum polin tes Galilaias. kai en didaskon autous en tois savvasin*
verses.translation: And came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and taught them on the sabbath days.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐν ἐξουσίᾳ ἦν ὁ λόγος αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai exeplissonto epi te didahe autou, oti en exoysia en o logos autou.
verses.translation: And they were astonished at his doctrine: for his word was with power.

verses.original: καὶ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἦν ἄνθρωπος ἔχων πνεῦμα δαιμονίου ἀκαθάρτου, καὶ ἀνέκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ·
verses.translit: kai en te synagoge en anthropos ehon pneuma daimonioy akathartoy, kai anekraxen fone megale*
verses.translation: And in the synagogue there was a man, which had a spirit of an unclean devil, and cried out with a loud voice,

verses.original: ⸀Ἔα, τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ Ναζαρηνέ; ἦλθες ἀπολέσαι ἡμᾶς; οἶδά σε τίς εἶ, ὁ ἅγιος τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: Ea, ti emin kai soi, Iisou Nazarine; elthes apolesai emas; oida se tis ei, o agios tou theou.
verses.translation: Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art; the Holy One of God.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Φιμώθητι καὶ ἔξελθε ⸀ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ. καὶ ῥίψαν αὐτὸν τὸ δαιμόνιον εἰς ⸀τὸ μέσον ἐξῆλθεν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ μηδὲν βλάψαν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai epetimisen auto o Iisous legon* Fimothiti kai exelthe ap' autou. kai Ripsan auton to daimonion eis to meson exelthen ap' autou miden vlapsan auton.
verses.translation: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him. And when the devil had thrown him in the midst, he came out of him, and hurt him not.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο θάμβος ἐπὶ πάντας, καὶ συνελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες· Τίς ὁ λόγος οὗτος ὅτι ἐν ἐξουσίᾳ καὶ δυνάμει ἐπιτάσσει τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις πνεύμασιν, καὶ ἐξέρχονται;
verses.translit: kai egeneto thamvos epi pantas, kai synelaloyn pros alliloys legontes* Tis o logos outos oti en exoysia kai dynamei epitassei tois akathartois pneymasin, kai exerhontai;
verses.translation: And they were all amazed, and spake among themselves, saying, What a word is this! for with authority and power he commandeth the unclean spirits, and they come out.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξεπορεύετο ἦχος περὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς πάντα τόπον τῆς περιχώρου.
verses.translit: kai exeporeyeto ehos peri autou eis panta topon tes perihoroy.
verses.translation: And the fame of him went out into every place of the country round about.

verses.original: Ἀναστὰς δὲ ⸀ἀπὸ τῆς συναγωγῆς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν Σίμωνος. πενθερὰ δὲ τοῦ Σίμωνος ἦν συνεχομένη πυρετῷ μεγάλῳ, καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν περὶ αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: Anastas de apo tes synagoges eiselthen eis ten oikian Simonos. penthera de tou Simonos en synehomeni pyreto megalo, kai erotisan auton peri autes.
verses.translation: And he arose out of the synagogue, and entered into Simon’s house. And Simon’s wife’s mother was taken with a great fever; and they besought him for her.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπιστὰς ἐπάνω αὐτῆς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ πυρετῷ, καὶ ἀφῆκεν αὐτήν· παραχρῆμα δὲ ἀναστᾶσα διηκόνει αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: kai epistas epano autes epetimisen to pyreto, kai afeken autin* parahrema de anastasa diikonei autois.
verses.translation: And he stood over her, and rebuked the fever; and it left her: and immediately she arose and ministered unto them.

verses.original: Δύνοντος δὲ τοῦ ἡλίου ⸀ἅπαντες ὅσοι εἶχον ἀσθενοῦντας νόσοις ποικίλαις ἤγαγον αὐτοὺς πρὸς αὐτόν· ὁ δὲ ἑνὶ ἑκάστῳ αὐτῶν τὰς χεῖρας ⸂ἐπιτιθεὶς ἐθεράπευεν⸃ αὐτούς.
verses.translit: Dynontos de tou elioy apantes osoi eihon asthenountas nosois poikilais egagon autous pros auton* o de eni ekasto auton tas heiras epititheis etherapeyen autoys.
verses.translation: Now when the sun was setting, all they that had any sick with divers diseases brought them unto him; and he laid his hands on every one of them, and healed them.

verses.original: ἐξήρχετο δὲ καὶ δαιμόνια ἀπὸ πολλῶν ⸀κραυγάζοντα καὶ λέγοντα ὅτι Σὺ ⸀εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ. καὶ ἐπιτιμῶν οὐκ εἴα αὐτὰ λαλεῖν, ὅτι ᾔδεισαν τὸν χριστὸν αὐτὸν εἶναι.
verses.translit: exirheto de kai daimonia apo pollon kraygazonta kai legonta oti Su ei o yios tou theou. kai epitimon ouk eia auta lalein, oti edeisan ton hriston auton einai.
verses.translation: And devils also came out of many, crying out, and saying, Thou art Christ the Son of God. And he rebuking them suffered them not to speak: for they knew that he was Christ.

verses.original: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη εἰς ἔρημον τόπον· καὶ οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπεζήτουν αὐτόν, καὶ ἦλθον ἕως αὐτοῦ, καὶ κατεῖχον αὐτὸν τοῦ μὴ πορεύεσθαι ἀπʼ αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Genomenis de emeras exelthon eporeythi eis erimon topon* kai oi ohloi epezitoyn auton, kai elthon eos autou, kai kateihon auton tou me poreyesthai ap' auton.
verses.translation: And when it was day, he departed and went into a desert place: and the people sought him, and came unto him, and stayed him, that he should not depart from them.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Καὶ ταῖς ἑτέραις πόλεσιν εὐαγγελίσασθαί με δεῖ τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, ὅτι ⸀ἐπὶ τοῦτο ⸀ἀπεστάλην.
verses.translit: o de eipen pros autous oti Kai tais eterais polesin euaggelisasthai me dei ten vasileian tou theou, oti epi touto apestalin.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent.

verses.original: καὶ ἦν κηρύσσων ⸂εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς⸃ τῆς ⸀Ἰουδαίας.
verses.translit: kai en kirysson eis tas synagogas tes Ioydaias.
verses.translation: And he preached in the synagogues of Galilee.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν ὄχλον ἐπικεῖσθαι αὐτῷ ⸀καὶ ἀκούειν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἑστὼς παρὰ τὴν λίμνην Γεννησαρέτ,
verses.translit: Egeneto de en to ton ohlon epikeisthai auto kai akoyein ton logon tou theou kai autos en estos para ten limnin Gennisaret,
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that, as the people pressed upon him to hear the word of God, he stood by the lake of Gennesaret,

verses.original: καὶ εἶδεν ⸂δύο πλοῖα⸃ ἑστῶτα παρὰ τὴν λίμνην, οἱ δὲ ἁλιεῖς ⸂ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ἀποβάντες⸃ ⸀ἔπλυνον τὰ δίκτυα.
verses.translit: kai eiden dyo ploia estota para ten limnin, oi de alieis ap' auton apovantes eplynon ta diktya.
verses.translation: And saw two ships standing by the lake: but the fishermen were gone out of them, and were washing their nets.

verses.original: ἐμβὰς δὲ εἰς ἓν τῶν πλοίων, ὃ ⸀ἦν Σίμωνος, ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἐπαναγαγεῖν ὀλίγον, ⸂καθίσας δὲ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου ἐδίδασκεν⸃ τοὺς ὄχλους.
verses.translit: emvas de eis en ton ploion, o en Simonos, erotisen auton apo tes ges epanagagein oligon, kathisas de ek tou ploioy edidasken tous ohloys.
verses.translation: And he entered into one of the ships, which was Simon’s, and prayed him that he would thrust out a little from the land. And he sat down, and taught the people out of the ship.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἐπαύσατο λαλῶν, εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα· Ἐπανάγαγε εἰς τὸ βάθος καὶ χαλάσατε τὰ δίκτυα ὑμῶν εἰς ἄγραν.
verses.translit: os de epaysato lalon, eipen pros ton Simona* Epanagage eis to vathos kai halasate ta diktya umon eis agran.
verses.translation: Now when he had left speaking, he said unto Simon, Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ⸀Σίμων ⸀εἶπεν· Ἐπιστάτα, διʼ ⸀ὅλης νυκτὸς κοπιάσαντες οὐδὲν ἐλάβομεν, ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ ῥήματί σου χαλάσω ⸂τὰ δίκτυα⸃.
verses.translit: kai apokritheis Simon eipen* Epistata, di' olis nyktos kopiasantes ouden elavomen, epi de to Rimati soy halaso ta diktya.
verses.translation: And Simon answering said unto him, Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net.

verses.original: καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσαντες συνέκλεισαν πλῆθος ἰχθύων πολύ, ⸀διερρήσσετο δὲ ⸂τὰ δίκτυα⸃ αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai touto poiisantes synekleisan plethos ihthyon poly, dierrisseto de ta diktya auton.
verses.translation: And when they had this done, they inclosed a great multitude of fishes: and their net brake.

verses.original: καὶ κατένευσαν τοῖς ⸀μετόχοις ἐν τῷ ἑτέρῳ πλοίῳ τοῦ ἐλθόντας συλλαβέσθαι αὐτοῖς· καὶ ἦλθον, καὶ ἔπλησαν ἀμφότερα τὰ πλοῖα ὥστε βυθίζεσθαι αὐτά.
verses.translit: kai kateneysan tois metohois en to etero ploio tou elthontas syllavesthai autois* kai elthon, kai eplisan amfotera ta ploia oste vythizesthai auta.
verses.translation: And they beckoned unto their partners, which were in the other ship, that they should come and help them. And they came, and filled both the ships, so that they began to sink.

verses.original: ἰδὼν δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος προσέπεσεν τοῖς γόνασιν Ἰησοῦ λέγων· Ἔξελθε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτωλός εἰμι, κύριε·
verses.translit: idon de Simon Petros prosepesen tois gonasin Iisou legon* Exelthe ap' emou, oti aner amartolos eimi, kyrie*
verses.translation: When Simon Peter saw it , he fell down at Jesus’ knees, saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.

verses.original: θάμβος γὰρ περιέσχεν αὐτὸν καὶ πάντας τοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τῇ ἄγρᾳ τῶν ἰχθύων ⸀ὧν συνέλαβον,
verses.translit: thamvos gar perieshen auton kai pantas tous sun auto epi te agra ton ihthyon on synelavon,
verses.translation: For he was astonished, and all that were with him, at the draught of the fishes which they had taken:

verses.original: ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου, οἳ ἦσαν κοινωνοὶ τῷ Σίμωνι. καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ φοβοῦ· ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ἀνθρώπους ἔσῃ ζωγρῶν.
verses.translit: omoios de kai Iakovon kai Ioannin yious Zevedaioy, oi esan koinonoi to Simoni. kai eipen pros ton Simona o Iisous* Me fovou* apo tou nun anthropoys ese zogron.
verses.translation: And so was also James, and John, the sons of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.

verses.original: καὶ καταγαγόντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἀφέντες ⸀πάντα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai katagagontes ta ploia epi ten gen afentes panta ekoloythisan auto.
verses.translation: And when they had brought their ships to land, they forsook all, and followed him.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν μιᾷ τῶν πόλεων καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ πλήρης λέπρας· ⸂καὶ ἰδὼν⸃ τὸν Ἰησοῦν πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ἐδεήθη αὐτοῦ λέγων· Κύριε, ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.
verses.translit: Kai egeneto en to einai auton en mia ton poleon kai idou aner pliris lepras* kai idon ton Iisoun peson epi prosopon edeithi autou legon* Kyrie, ean theles dynasai me katharisai.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, when he was in a certain city, behold a man full of leprosy: who seeing Jesus fell on his face, and besought him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.

verses.original: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἥψατο αὐτοῦ ⸀εἰπών· Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι· καὶ εὐθέως ἡ λέπρα ἀπῆλθεν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai ekteinas ten heira epsato autou eipon* Thelo, katharisthiti* kai eutheos e lepra apelthen ap' autou.
verses.translation: And he put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will: be thou clean. And immediately the leprosy departed from him.

verses.original: καὶ αὐτὸς παρήγγειλεν αὐτῷ μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν, ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν δεῖξον σεαυτὸν τῷ ἱερεῖ, καὶ προσένεγκε περὶ τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ σου καθὼς προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: kai autos pariggeilen auto mideni eipein, alla apelthon deixon seayton to ierei, kai prosenegke peri tou katharismou soy kathos prosetaxen Moyses eis martyrion autois.
verses.translation: And he charged him to tell no man: but go, and shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing, according as Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

verses.original: διήρχετο δὲ μᾶλλον ὁ λόγος περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ συνήρχοντο ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀκούειν καὶ ⸀θεραπεύεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἀσθενειῶν αὐτῶν·
verses.translit: diirheto de mallon o logos peri autou, kai synirhonto ohloi polloi akoyein kai therapeyesthai apo ton astheneion auton*
verses.translation: But so much the more went there a fame abroad of him: and great multitudes came together to hear, and to be healed by him of their infirmities.

verses.original: αὐτὸς δὲ ἦν ὑποχωρῶν ἐν ταῖς ἐρήμοις καὶ προσευχόμενος.
verses.translit: autos de en upohoron en tais erimois kai proseyhomenos.
verses.translation: And he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διδάσκων, καὶ ἦσαν καθήμενοι Φαρισαῖοι καὶ νομοδιδάσκαλοι οἳ ἦσαν ἐληλυθότες ἐκ πάσης κώμης τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ· καὶ δύναμις κυρίου ἦν εἰς τὸ ἰᾶσθαι ⸀αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Kai egeneto en mia ton emeron kai autos en didaskon, kai esan kathimenoi Farisaioi kai nomodidaskaloi oi esan elilythotes ek pasis komis tes Galilaias kai Ioydaias kai Ieroysalim* kai dynamis kyrioy en eis to iasthai auton.
verses.translation: And it came to pass on a certain day, as he was teaching, that there were Pharisees and doctors of the law sitting by, which were come out of every town of Galilee, and Judæa, and Jerusalem: and the power of the Lord was present to heal them.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες φέροντες ἐπὶ κλίνης ἄνθρωπον ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος, καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν εἰσενεγκεῖν καὶ ⸀θεῖναι ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai idou andres ferontes epi klinis anthropon os en paralelymenos, kai ezitoyn auton eisenegkein kai theinai enopion autou.
verses.translation: And, behold, men brought in a bed a man which was taken with a palsy: and they sought means to bring him in, and to lay him before him.

verses.original: καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ποίας εἰσενέγκωσιν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀναβάντες ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα διὰ τῶν κεράμων καθῆκαν αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ κλινιδίῳ εἰς τὸ μέσον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: kai me eurontes poias eisenegkosin auton dia ton ohlon anavantes epi to doma dia ton keramon kathekan auton sun to klinidio eis to meson emprosthen tou Iisou.
verses.translation: And when they could not find by what way they might bring him in because of the multitude, they went upon the housetop, and let him down through the tiling with his couch into the midst before Jesus.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν ⸀εἶπεν· Ἄνθρωπε, ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου.
verses.translit: kai idon ten pistin auton eipen* Anthrope, afeontai soi ai amartiai soy.
verses.translation: And when he saw their faith, he said unto him, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee.

verses.original: καὶ ἤρξαντο διαλογίζεσθαι οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι λέγοντες· Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὃς λαλεῖ βλασφημίας; τίς δύναται ⸂ἁμαρτίας ἀφεῖναι⸃ εἰ μὴ μόνος ὁ θεός;
verses.translit: kai erxanto dialogizesthai oi grammateis kai oi Farisaioi legontes* Tis estin outos os lalei vlasfimias; tis dynatai amartias afeinai ei me monos o theos;
verses.translation: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, Who is this which speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?

verses.original: ἐπιγνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;
verses.translit: epignous de o Iisous tous dialogismous auton apokritheis eipen pros autoys* Ti dialogizesthe en tais kardiais umon;
verses.translation: But when Jesus perceived their thoughts, he answering said unto them, What reason ye in your hearts?

verses.original: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν· Ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου, ἢ εἰπεῖν· ⸀Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει;
verses.translit: ti estin eukopoteron, eipein* Afeontai soi ai amartiai soy, e eipein* Egeire kai peripatei;
verses.translation: Whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Rise up and walk?

verses.original: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ⸂ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐξουσίαν ἔχει⸃ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας— εἶπεν τῷ παραλελυμένῳ· Σοὶ λέγω, ⸀ἔγειρε καὶ ἄρας τὸ κλινίδιόν σου πορεύου εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.
verses.translit: ina de eidete oti o yios tou anthropoy exoysian ehei epi tes ges afienai amartias-- eipen to paralelymeno* Soi lego, egeire kai aras to klinidion soy poreyoy eis ton oikon soy.
verses.translation: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power upon earth to forgive sins, (he said unto the sick of the palsy,) I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy couch, and go into thine house.

verses.original: καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀναστὰς ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν, ἄρας ἐφʼ ὃ κατέκειτο, ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ δοξάζων τὸν θεόν.
verses.translit: kai parahrema anastas enopion auton, aras ef' o katekeito, apelthen eis ton oikon autou doxazon ton theon.
verses.translation: And immediately he rose up before them, and took up that whereon he lay, and departed to his own house, glorifying God.

verses.original: καὶ ἔκστασις ἔλαβεν ἅπαντας καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεόν, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν φόβου λέγοντες ὅτι Εἴδομεν παράδοξα σήμερον.
verses.translit: kai ekstasis elaven apantas kai edoxazon ton theon, kai eplisthisan fovoy legontes oti Eidomen paradoxa simeron.
verses.translation: And they were all amazed, and they glorified God, and were filled with fear, saying, We have seen strange things to day.

verses.original: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξῆλθεν καὶ ἐθεάσατο τελώνην ὀνόματι Λευὶν καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι.
verses.translit: Kai meta tauta exelthen kai etheasato telonin onomati Leyin kathimenon epi to telonion, kai eipen auto* Akoloythei moi.
verses.translation: And after these things he went forth, and saw a publican, named Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom: and he said unto him, Follow me.

verses.original: καὶ καταλιπὼν ⸀πάντα ἀναστὰς ⸀ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai katalipon panta anastas ekoloythei auto.
verses.translation: And he left all, rose up, and followed him.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐποίησεν δοχὴν μεγάλην Λευὶς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἦν ὄχλος ⸂πολὺς τελωνῶν⸃ καὶ ἄλλων οἳ ἦσαν μετʼ αὐτῶν κατακείμενοι.
verses.translit: Kai epoiisen dohen megalin Leyis auto en te oikia autou* kai en ohlos polus telonon kai allon oi esan met' auton katakeimenoi.
verses.translation: And Levi made him a great feast in his own house: and there was a great company of publicans and of others that sat down with them.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγόγγυζον οἱ ⸂Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν⸃ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίετε καὶ πίνετε;
verses.translit: kai egoggyzon oi Farisaioi kai oi grammateis auton pros tous mathitas autou legontes* Dia ti meta ton telonon kai amartolon esthiete kai pinete;
verses.translation: But their scribes and Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, Why do ye eat and drink with publicans and sinners?

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ὑγιαίνοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες·
verses.translit: kai apokritheis o Iisous eipen pros autoys* Ou hreian ehoysin oi ugiainontes iatrou alla oi kakos ehontes*
verses.translation: And Jesus answering said unto them, They that are whole need not a physician; but they that are sick.

verses.original: οὐκ ἐλήλυθα καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν.
verses.translit: ouk elilytha kalesai dikaioys alla amartolous eis metanoian.
verses.translation: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν· ⸀Οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου νηστεύουσιν πυκνὰ καὶ δεήσεις ποιοῦνται, ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ τῶν Φαρισαίων, οἱ δὲ σοὶ ἐσθίουσιν καὶ πίνουσιν.
verses.translit: Oi de eipan pros auton* Oi mathitai Ioannoy nisteyoysin pykna kai deiseis poiountai, omoios kai oi ton Farisaion, oi de soi esthioysin kai pinoysin.
verses.translation: And they said unto him, Why do the disciples of John fast often, and make prayers, and likewise the disciples of the Pharisees; but thine eat and drink?

verses.original: ὁ ⸀δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μὴ δύνασθε τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετʼ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ποιῆσαι ⸀νηστεῦσαι;
verses.translit: o de eipen pros autoys* Me dynasthe tous yious tou nymfonos en o o nymfios met' auton estin poiesai nisteusai;
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Can ye make the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them?

verses.original: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι, καὶ ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις.
verses.translit: eleysontai de emerai, kai otan aparthe ap' auton o nymfios tote nisteysoysin en ekeinais tais emerais.
verses.translation: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.

verses.original: ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ⸀ἀπὸ ἱματίου καινοῦ ⸀σχίσας ἐπιβάλλει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν· εἰ δὲ μήγε, καὶ τὸ καινὸν ⸀σχίσει καὶ τῷ παλαιῷ οὐ ⸂συμφωνήσει τὸ ἐπίβλημα⸃ τὸ ἀπὸ τοῦ καινοῦ.
verses.translit: elegen de kai paravolen pros autous oti Oudeis epivlima apo imatioy kainou shisas epivallei epi imation palaion* ei de mige, kai to kainon shisei kai to palaio ou symfonisei to epivlima to apo tou kainou.
verses.translation: And he spake also a parable unto them; No man putteth a piece of a new garment upon an old; if otherwise, then both the new maketh a rent, and the piece that was taken out of the new agreeth not with the old.

verses.original: καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μήγε, ῥήξει ὁ ⸂οἶνος ὁ νέος⸃ τοὺς ἀσκούς, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐκχυθήσεται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπολοῦνται·
verses.translit: kai oudeis vallei oinon neon eis askous palaioys* ei de mige, Rixei o oinos o neos tous askoys, kai autos ekhythisetai kai oi askoi apolountai*
verses.translation: And no man putteth new wine into old bottles; else the new wine will burst the bottles, and be spilled, and the bottles shall perish.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινοὺς ⸀βλητέον.
verses.translit: alla oinon neon eis askous kainous vliteon.
verses.translation: But new wine must be put into new bottles; and both are preserved.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ οὐδεὶς πιὼν ⸀παλαιὸν θέλει νέον· λέγει γάρ· Ὁ παλαιὸς ⸀χρηστός ἐστιν.
verses.translit: kai oudeis pion palaion thelei neon* legei gar* O palaios hristos estin.
verses.translation: No man also having drunk old wine straightway desireth new: for he saith, The old is better.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ⸀σαββάτῳ διαπορεύεσθαι αὐτὸν ⸀διὰ σπορίμων, καὶ ἔτιλλον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ⸂καὶ ἤσθιον τοὺς στάχυας⸃ ψώχοντες ταῖς χερσίν.
verses.translit: Egeneto de en savvato diaporeyesthai auton dia sporimon, kai etillon oi mathitai autou kai esthion tous stahyas psohontes tais hersin.
verses.translation: And it came to pass on the second sabbath after the first, that he went through the corn fields; and his disciples plucked the ears of corn, and did eat, rubbing them in their hands.

verses.original: τινὲς δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων ⸀εἶπαν· Τί ποιεῖτε ὃ οὐκ ⸀ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν;
verses.translit: tines de ton Farisaion eipan* Ti poieite o ouk exestin tois savvasin;
verses.translation: And certain of the Pharisees said unto them, Why do ye that which is not lawful to do on the sabbath days?

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐδὲ τοῦτο ἀνέγνωτε ὃ ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ⸀ὁπότε ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ⸀ὄντες;
verses.translit: kai apokritheis pros autous eipen o Iisous* Oude touto anegnote o epoiisen Dayid opote epeinasen autos kai oi met' autou ontes?
verses.translation: And Jesus answering them said, Have ye not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was an hungred, and they which were with him;

verses.original: ⸀ὡς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ⸀λαβὼν ἔφαγεν καὶ ⸀ἔδωκεν τοῖς μετʼ αὐτοῦ, οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ μόνους τοὺς ἱερεῖς;
verses.translit: os eiselthen eis ton oikon tou theou kai tous artoys tes protheseos lavon efagen kai edoken tois met' autou, ous ouk exestin fagein ei me monoys tous iereis;
verses.translation: How he went into the house of God, and did take and eat the shewbread, and gave also to them that were with him; which it is not lawful to eat but for the priests alone?

verses.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν ⸀αὐτοῖς· Κύριός ἐστιν ⸂τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου⸃.
verses.translit: kai elegen autois* Kyrios estin tou savvatoy o yios tou anthropoy.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, That the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο ⸀δὲ ἐν ἑτέρῳ σαββάτῳ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν καὶ διδάσκειν· καὶ ἦν ⸂ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖ⸃ καὶ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ ἡ δεξιὰ ἦν ξηρά·
verses.translit: Egeneto de en etero savvato eiselthein auton eis ten synagogen kai didaskein* kai en anthropos ekei kai e heir autou e dexia en xira*
verses.translation: And it came to pass also on another sabbath, that he entered into the synagogue and taught: and there was a man whose right hand was withered.

verses.original: ⸀παρετηροῦντο ⸀δὲ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εἰ ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ ⸀θεραπεύει, ἵνα εὕρωσιν ⸀κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: paretirounto de oi grammateis kai oi Farisaioi ei en to savvato therapeyei, ina eurosin katigorein autou.
verses.translation: And the scribes and Pharisees watched him, whether he would heal on the sabbath day; that they might find an accusation against him.

verses.original: αὐτὸς δὲ ᾔδει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν, ⸂εἶπεν δὲ⸃ τῷ ⸀ἀνδρὶ τῷ ξηρὰν ἔχοντι τὴν χεῖρα· ⸀Ἔγειρε καὶ στῆθι εἰς τὸ μέσον· ⸀καὶ ἀναστὰς ἔστη.
verses.translit: autos de edei tous dialogismous auton, eipen de to andri to xiran ehonti ten heira* Egeire kai stethi eis to meson* kai anastas esti.
verses.translation: But he knew their thoughts, and said to the man which had the withered hand, Rise up, and stand forth in the midst. And he arose and stood forth.

verses.original: εἶπεν ⸀δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτούς· ⸀Ἐπερωτῶ ὑμᾶς, ⸀εἰ ἔξεστιν ⸂τῷ σαββάτῳ⸃ ἀγαθοποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι, ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ⸀ἀπολέσαι;
verses.translit: eipen de o Iisous pros autoys* Eperoto umas, ei exestin to savvato agathopoiesai e kakopoiesai, psyhen sosai e apolesai;
verses.translation: Then said Jesus unto them, I will ask you one thing; Is it lawful on the sabbath days to do good, or to do evil? to save life, or to destroy it ?

verses.original: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντας αὐτοὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρά σου· ὁ δὲ ἐποίησεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ ⸀αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai perivlepsamenos pantas autous eipen auto* Ekteinon ten heira soy* o de epoiisen, kai apekatestathi e heir autou.
verses.translation: And looking round about upon them all, he said unto the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he did so: and his hand was restored whole as the other.

verses.original: αὐτοὶ δὲ ἐπλήσθησαν ἀνοίας, καὶ διελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους τί ἂν ποιήσαιεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: autoi de eplisthisan anoias, kai dielaloyn pros alliloys ti an poiisaien to Iisou.
verses.translation: And they were filled with madness; and communed one with another what they might do to Jesus.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ⸂ἐξελθεῖν αὐτὸν⸃ εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι, καὶ ἦν διανυκτερεύων ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: Egeneto de en tais emerais taytais exelthein auton eis to oros proseyxasthai, kai en dianyktereyon en te proseyhe tou theou.
verses.translation: And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.

verses.original: καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡμέρα, προσεφώνησεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκλεξάμενος ἀπʼ αὐτῶν δώδεκα, οὓς καὶ ἀποστόλους ὠνόμασεν,
verses.translit: kai ote egeneto emera, prosefonisen tous mathitas autou, kai eklexamenos ap' auton dodeka, ous kai apostoloys onomasen,
verses.translation: And when it was day, he called unto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles;

verses.original: Σίμωνα ὃν καὶ ὠνόμασεν Πέτρον καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ⸀καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην ⸁καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον
verses.translit: Simona on kai onomasen Petron kai Andrean ton adelfon autou kai Iakovon kai Ioannin kai Filippon kai Vartholomaion
verses.translation: Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,

verses.original: ⸀καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν ⸁καὶ ⸀Ἰάκωβον Ἁλφαίου καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν καλούμενον Ζηλωτὴν
verses.translit: kai Maththaion kai Thoman kai Iakovon Alfaioy kai Simona ton kaloymenon Ziloten
verses.translation: Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphæus, and Simon called Zelotes,

verses.original: ⸀καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰούδαν ⸀Ἰσκαριὼθ ⸀ὃς ἐγένετο προδότης.
verses.translit: kai Ioydan Iakovoy kai Ioydan Iskarioth os egeneto prodotis.
verses.translation: And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.

verses.original: Καὶ καταβὰς μετʼ αὐτῶν ἔστη ἐπὶ τόπου πεδινοῦ, καὶ ὄχλος ⸀πολὺς μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, καὶ πλῆθος πολὺ τοῦ λαοῦ ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ τῆς παραλίου Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος,
verses.translit: Kai katavas met' auton esti epi topoy pedinou, kai ohlos polus mathiton autou, kai plethos polu tou laou apo pasis tes Ioydaias kai Ieroysalem kai tes paralioy Tyroy kai Sidonos,
verses.translation: And he came down with them, and stood in the plain, and the company of his disciples, and a great multitude of people out of all Judæa and Jerusalem, and from the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, which came to hear him, and to be healed of their diseases;

verses.original: οἳ ἦλθον ἀκοῦσαι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰαθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν νόσων αὐτῶν· καὶ οἱ ⸂ἐνοχλούμενοι ἀπὸ⸃ πνευμάτων ⸀ἀκαθάρτων ἐθεραπεύοντο·
verses.translit: oi elthon akousai autou kai iathenai apo ton noson auton* kai oi enohloymenoi apo pneymaton akatharton etherapeyonto*
verses.translation: And they that were vexed with unclean spirits: and they were healed.

verses.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ⸀ἐζήτουν ἅπτεσθαι αὐτοῦ, ὅτι δύναμις παρʼ αὐτοῦ ἐξήρχετο καὶ ἰᾶτο πάντας.
verses.translit: kai pas o ohlos ezitoyn aptesthai autou, oti dynamis par' autou exirheto kai iato pantas.
verses.translation: And the whole multitude sought to touch him: for there went virtue out of him, and healed them all.

verses.original: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν· Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοί, ὅτι ὑμετέρα ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: Kai autos eparas tous ofthalmous autou eis tous mathitas autou elegen* Makarioi oi ptohoi, oti umetera estin e vasileia tou theou.
verses.translation: And he lifted up his eyes on his disciples, and said, Blessed be ye poor: for yours is the kingdom of God.

verses.original: μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες νῦν, ὅτι χορτασθήσεσθε. μακάριοι οἱ κλαίοντες νῦν, ὅτι γελάσετε.
verses.translit: makarioi oi peinontes nun, oti hortasthisesthe. makarioi oi klaiontes nun, oti gelasete.
verses.translation: Blessed are ye that hunger now: for ye shall be filled. Blessed are ye that weep now: for ye shall laugh.

verses.original: Μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν μισήσωσιν ὑμᾶς οἱ ἄνθρωποι, καὶ ὅταν ἀφορίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ ὀνειδίσωσιν καὶ ἐκβάλωσιν τὸ ὄνομα ὑμῶν ὡς πονηρὸν ἕνεκα τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
verses.translit: Makarioi este otan misisosin umas oi anthropoi, kai otan aforisosin umas kai oneidisosin kai ekvalosin to onoma umon os poniron eneka tou yiou tou anthropoy*
verses.translation: Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company , and shall reproach you , and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man’s sake.

verses.original: χάρητε ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ σκιρτήσατε, ἰδοὺ γὰρ ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ· κατὰ ⸂τὰ αὐτὰ⸃ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς προφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: harite en ekeine te emera kai skirtisate, idou gar o misthos umon polus en to ourano* kata ta auta gar epoioyn tois profitais oi pateres auton.
verses.translation: Rejoice ye in that day, and leap for joy: for, behold, your reward is great in heaven: for in the like manner did their fathers unto the prophets.

verses.original: πλὴν οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς πλουσίοις, ὅτι ἀπέχετε τὴν παράκλησιν ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: plen ouai umin tois ploysiois, oti apehete ten paraklisin umon.
verses.translation: But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.

verses.original: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, οἱ ἐμπεπλησμένοι ⸀νῦν, ὅτι πεινάσετε. ⸀οὐαί, οἱ γελῶντες νῦν, ὅτι πενθήσετε καὶ κλαύσετε.
verses.translit: ouai umin, oi empeplismenoi nun, oti peinasete. ouai, oi gelontes nun, oti penthisete kai klaysete.
verses.translation: Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.

verses.original: Οὐαὶ ὅταν ⸂καλῶς ὑμᾶς⸃ εἴπωσιν ⸀πάντες οἱ ἄνθρωποι, κατὰ ⸂τὰ αὐτὰ⸃ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς ψευδοπροφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Ouai otan kalos umas eiposin pantes oi anthropoi, kata ta auta gar epoioyn tois pseydoprofitais oi pateres auton.
verses.translation: Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets.

verses.original: Ἀλλὰ ὑμῖν λέγω τοῖς ἀκούουσιν, ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν, καλῶς ποιεῖτε τοῖς μισοῦσιν ὑμᾶς,
verses.translit: Alla umin lego tois akoyoysin, agapate tous ehthrous umon, kalos poieite tois misousin umas,
verses.translation: But I say unto you which hear, Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you,

verses.original: εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς καταρωμένους ⸀ὑμᾶς, προσεύχεσθε ⸀περὶ τῶν ἐπηρεαζόντων ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: eulogeite tous kataromenoys umas, proseyhesthe peri ton epireazonton umas.
verses.translation: Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.

verses.original: τῷ τύπτοντί σε ἐπὶ τὴν σιαγόνα πάρεχε καὶ τὴν ἄλλην, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντός σου τὸ ἱμάτιον καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα μὴ κωλύσῃς.
verses.translit: to typtonti se epi ten siagona parehe kai ten allin, kai apo tou airontos soy to imation kai ton hitona me kolyses.
verses.translation: And unto him that smiteth thee on the one cheek offer also the other; and him that taketh away thy cloke forbid not to take thy coat also.

verses.original: ⸀παντὶ αἰτοῦντί σε δίδου, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντος τὰ σὰ μὴ ἀπαίτει.
verses.translit: panti aitounti se didoy, kai apo tou airontos ta sa me apaitei.
verses.translation: Give to every man that asketh of thee; and of him that taketh away thy goods ask them not again.

verses.original: καὶ καθὼς θέλετε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ⸀ἄνθρωποι, ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς ὁμοίως.
verses.translit: kai kathos thelete ina poiosin umin oi anthropoi, poieite autois omoios.
verses.translation: And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.

verses.original: Καὶ εἰ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν; καὶ γὰρ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας αὐτοὺς ἀγαπῶσιν.
verses.translit: Kai ei agapate tous agapontas umas, poia umin haris estin; kai gar oi amartoloi tous agapontas autous agaposin.
verses.translation: For if ye love them which love you, what thank have ye? for sinners also love those that love them.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ ἐὰν ἀγαθοποιῆτε τοὺς ἀγαθοποιοῦντας ὑμᾶς, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν; ⸁καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν.
verses.translit: kai ean agathopoiete tous agathopoiountas umas, poia umin haris estin; kai oi amartoloi to auto poiousin.
verses.translation: And if ye do good to them which do good to you, what thank have ye? for sinners also do even the same.

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν ⸀δανίσητε παρʼ ὧν ἐλπίζετε ⸀λαβεῖν, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν; ⸀καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἁμαρτωλοῖς δανίζουσιν ἵνα ἀπολάβωσιν τὰ ἴσα.
verses.translit: kai ean danisite par' on elpizete lavein, poia umin haris estin; kai amartoloi amartolois danizoysin ina apolavosin ta isa.
verses.translation: And if ye lend to them of whom ye hope to receive, what thank have ye? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again.

verses.original: πλὴν ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ ἀγαθοποιεῖτε καὶ δανίζετε μηδὲν ἀπελπίζοντες· καὶ ἔσται ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολύς, καὶ ἔσεσθε υἱοὶ Ὑψίστου, ὅτι αὐτὸς χρηστός ἐστιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀχαρίστους καὶ πονηρούς.
verses.translit: plen agapate tous ehthrous umon kai agathopoieite kai danizete miden apelpizontes* kai estai o misthos umon polys, kai esesthe yioi Upsistoy, oti autos hristos estin epi tous aharistoys kai poniroys.
verses.translation: But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil.

verses.original: ⸀γίνεσθε οἰκτίρμονες ⸀καθὼς ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν οἰκτίρμων ἐστίν·
verses.translit: ginesthe oiktirmones kathos o pater umon oiktirmon estin*
verses.translation: Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.

verses.original: Καὶ μὴ κρίνετε, καὶ οὐ μὴ κριθῆτε· ⸀καὶ μὴ καταδικάζετε, καὶ οὐ μὴ καταδικασθῆτε. ἀπολύετε, καὶ ἀπολυθήσεσθε·
verses.translit: Kai me krinete, kai ou me krithete* kai me katadikazete, kai ou me katadikasthete. apolyete, kai apolythisesthe*
verses.translation: Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive, and ye shall be forgiven:

verses.original: δίδοτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· μέτρον καλὸν πεπιεσμένον ⸀σεσαλευμένον ὑπερεκχυννόμενον δώσουσιν εἰς τὸν κόλπον ὑμῶν· ⸂ᾧ γὰρ μέτρῳ⸃ μετρεῖτε ἀντιμετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: didote, kai dothisetai umin* metron kalon pepiesmenon sesaleymenon uperekhynnomenon dosoysin eis ton kolpon umon* o gar metro metreite antimetrithisetai umin.
verses.translation: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ⸀καὶ παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς· Μήτι δύναται τυφλὸς τυφλὸν ὁδηγεῖν; οὐχὶ ἀμφότεροι εἰς βόθυνον ⸀ἐμπεσοῦνται;
verses.translit: Eipen de kai paravolen autois* Miti dynatai tyflos tyflon odigein; ouhi amfoteroi eis vothynon empesountai;
verses.translation: And he spake a parable unto them, Can the blind lead the blind? shall they not both fall into the ditch?

verses.original: οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν ⸀διδάσκαλον, κατηρτισμένος δὲ πᾶς ἔσται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: ouk estin mathites uper ton didaskalon, katirtismenos de pas estai os o didaskalos autou.
verses.translation: The disciple is not above his master: but every one that is perfect shall be as his master.

verses.original: τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου, τὴν δὲ δοκὸν τὴν ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ ὀφθαλμῷ οὐ κατανοεῖς;
verses.translit: ti de vlepeis to karfos to en to ofthalmo tou adelfou soy, ten de dokon ten en to idio ofthalmo ou katanoeis;
verses.translation: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but perceivest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

verses.original: ⸀πῶς δύνασαι λέγειν τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου· Ἀδελφέ, ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σου, αὐτὸς τὴν ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ δοκὸν οὐ βλέπων; ὑποκριτά, ἔκβαλε πρῶτον τὴν δοκὸν ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ, καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις ⸂τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου ἐκβαλεῖν⸃.
verses.translit: pos dynasai legein to adelfo soy* Adelfe, afes ekvalo to karfos to en to ofthalmo soy, autos ten en to ofthalmo sou dokon ou vlepon; upokrita, ekvale proton ten dokon ek tou ofthalmou sou, kai tote diavlepseis to karfos to en to ofthalmo tou adelfou soy ekvalein.
verses.translation: Either how canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let me pull out the mote that is in thine eye, when thou thyself beholdest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye, and then shalt thou see clearly to pull out the mote that is in thy brother’s eye.

verses.original: Οὐ γάρ ἐστιν δένδρον καλὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν σαπρόν, οὐδὲ ⸀πάλιν δένδρον σαπρὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλόν.
verses.translit: Ou gar estin dendron kalon poioun karpon sapron, oude palin dendron sapron poioun karpon kalon.
verses.translation: For a good tree bringeth not forth corrupt fruit; neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.

verses.original: ἕκαστον γὰρ δένδρον ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου καρποῦ γινώσκεται· οὐ γὰρ ἐξ ἀκανθῶν συλλέγουσιν σῦκα, οὐδὲ ἐκ βάτου ⸂σταφυλὴν τρυγῶσιν⸃.
verses.translit: ekaston gar dendron ek tou idioy karpou ginosketai* ou gar ex akanthon syllegoysin suka, oude ek vatoy stafylen trygosin.
verses.translation: For every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes.

verses.original: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ τῆς καρδίας ⸀αὐτοῦ προφέρει τὸ ἀγαθόν, καὶ ὁ ⸀πονηρὸς ἐκ τοῦ ⸀πονηροῦ προφέρει τὸ πονηρόν· ἐκ γὰρ ⸀περισσεύματος καρδίας λαλεῖ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: o agathos anthropos ek tou agathou thisayrou tes kardias autou proferei to agathon, kai o poniros ek tou ponirou proferei to poniron* ek gar perisseymatos kardias lalei to stoma autou.
verses.translation: A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.

verses.original: Τί δέ με καλεῖτε· Κύριε κύριε, καὶ οὐ ποιεῖτε ἃ λέγω;
verses.translit: Ti de me kaleite* Kyrie kyrie, kai ou poieite a lego;
verses.translation: And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?

verses.original: πᾶς ὁ ἐρχόμενος πρός με καὶ ἀκούων μου τῶν λόγων καὶ ποιῶν αὐτούς, ὑποδείξω ὑμῖν τίνι ἐστὶν ὅμοιος·
verses.translit: pas o erhomenos pros me kai akoyon moy ton logon kai poion autoys, upodeixo umin tini estin omoios*
verses.translation: Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like:

verses.original: ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομοῦντι οἰκίαν ὃς ἔσκαψεν καὶ ἐβάθυνεν καὶ ἔθηκεν θεμέλιον ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν· πλημμύρης δὲ γενομένης προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμὸς τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν σαλεῦσαι αὐτὴν ⸂διὰ τὸ καλῶς οἰκοδομῆσθαι αὐτήν⸃.
verses.translit: omoios estin anthropo oikodomounti oikian os eskapsen kai evathynen kai ethiken themelion epi ten petran* plimmyris de genomenis proserixen o potamos te oikia ekeine, kai ouk ishysen saleusai auten dia to kalos oikodomesthai autin.
verses.translation: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας καὶ μὴ ποιήσας ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομήσαντι οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν χωρὶς θεμελίου, ᾗ προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμός, καὶ ⸂εὐθὺς συνέπεσεν⸃, καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ ῥῆγμα τῆς οἰκίας ἐκείνης μέγα.
verses.translit: o de akoysas kai me poiisas omoios estin anthropo oikodomisanti oikian epi ten gen horis themelioy, e proserixen o potamos, kai euthus synepesen, kai egeneto to Regma tes oikias ekeinis mega.
verses.translation: But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.

verses.original: ⸀Ἐπειδὴ ἐπλήρωσεν πάντα τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς τοῦ λαοῦ, εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναούμ.
verses.translit: Epeide eplirosen panta ta Rimata autou eis tas akoas tou laou, eiselthen eis Kafarnaoym.
verses.translation: Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.

verses.original: Ἑκατοντάρχου δέ τινος δοῦλος κακῶς ἔχων ἤμελλεν τελευτᾶν, ὃς ἦν αὐτῷ ἔντιμος.
verses.translit: Ekatontarhoy de tinos doulos kakos ehon emellen teleytan, os en auto entimos.
verses.translation: And a certain centurion’s servant, who was dear unto him, was sick, and ready to die.

verses.original: ἀκούσας δὲ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν πρεσβυτέρους τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἐρωτῶν αὐτὸν ὅπως ἐλθὼν διασώσῃ τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: akoysas de peri tou Iisou apesteilen pros auton presvyteroys ton Ioydaion, eroton auton opos elthon diasose ton doulon autou.
verses.translation: And when he heard of Jesus, he sent unto him the elders of the Jews, beseeching him that he would come and heal his servant.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ παραγενόμενοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν σπουδαίως λέγοντες ὅτι Ἄξιός ἐστιν ᾧ ⸀παρέξῃ τοῦτο,
verses.translit: oi de paragenomenoi pros ton Iisoun parekaloyn auton spoydaios legontes oti Axios estin o parexe touto,
verses.translation: And when they came to Jesus, they besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this:

verses.original: ἀγαπᾷ γὰρ τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτὸς ᾠκοδόμησεν ἡμῖν.
verses.translit: agapa gar to ethnos emon kai ten synagogen autos okodomisen emin.
verses.translation: For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐπορεύετο σὺν αὐτοῖς. ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ οὐ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος ἀπὸ τῆς οἰκίας ἔπεμψεν ⸂φίλους ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης⸃ λέγων αὐτῷ· Κύριε, μὴ σκύλλου, οὐ γὰρ ⸂ἱκανός εἰμι⸃ ἵνα ὑπὸ τὴν στέγην μου εἰσέλθῃς·
verses.translit: o de Iisous eporeyeto sun autois. edi de autou ou makran apehontos apo tes oikias epempsen filoys o ekatontarhis legon auto* Kyrie, me skylloy, ou gar ikanos eimi ina upo ten stegin moy eiselthes*
verses.translation: Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof:

verses.original: διὸ οὐδὲ ἐμαυτὸν ἠξίωσα πρὸς σὲ ἐλθεῖν· ἀλλὰ εἰπὲ λόγῳ, καὶ ⸀ἰαθήτω ὁ παῖς μου·
verses.translit: dio oude emayton exiosa pros se elthein* alla eipe logo, kai iathito o pais moy*
verses.translation: Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed.

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπός εἰμι ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν τασσόμενος, ἔχων ὑπʼ ἐμαυτὸν στρατιώτας, καὶ λέγω τούτῳ· Πορεύθητι, καὶ πορεύεται, καὶ ἄλλῳ· Ἔρχου, καὶ ἔρχεται, καὶ τῷ δούλῳ μου· Ποίησον τοῦτο, καὶ ποιεῖ.
verses.translit: kai gar ego anthropos eimi upo exoysian tassomenos, ehon up' emayton stratiotas, kai lego toyto* Poreythiti, kai poreyetai, kai allo* Erhoy, kai erhetai, kai to doylo moy* Poiison touto, kai poiei.
verses.translation: For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say unto one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it .

verses.original: ἀκούσας δὲ ταῦτα ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐθαύμασεν αὐτόν, καὶ στραφεὶς τῷ ἀκολουθοῦντι αὐτῷ ὄχλῳ εἶπεν· Λέγω ὑμῖν, ⸀οὐδὲ ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ τοσαύτην πίστιν εὗρον.
verses.translit: akoysas de tauta o Iisous ethaymasen auton, kai strafeis to akoloythounti auto ohlo eipen* Lego umin, oude en to Israel tosaytin pistin euron.
verses.translation: When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned him about, and said unto the people that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.

verses.original: καὶ ὑποστρέψαντες ⸂εἰς τὸν οἶκον οἱ πεμφθέντες⸃ εὗρον ⸀τὸν δοῦλον ὑγιαίνοντα.
verses.translit: kai upostrepsantes eis ton oikon oi pemfthentes euron ton doulon ugiainonta.
verses.translation: And they that were sent, returning to the house, found the servant whole that had been sick.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἑξῆς ⸀ἐπορεύθη εἰς πόλιν καλουμένην Ναΐν, καὶ συνεπορεύοντο αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ ⸀αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλος πολύς.
verses.translit: Kai egeneto en to exes eporeythi eis polin kaloymenin NaIn, kai syneporeyonto auto oi mathitai autou kai ohlos polys.
verses.translation: And it came to pass the day after, that he went into a city called Nain; and many of his disciples went with him, and much people.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἤγγισεν τῇ πύλῃ τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐξεκομίζετο τεθνηκὼς ⸂μονογενὴς υἱὸς⸃ τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτὴ ⸀ἦν χήρα, καὶ ὄχλος τῆς πόλεως ἱκανὸς ⸁ἦν σὺν αὐτῇ.
verses.translit: os de eggisen te pyle tes poleos, kai idou exekomizeto tethnikos monogenes yios te mitri autou, kai aute en hira, kai ohlos tes poleos ikanos en sun aute.
verses.translation: Now when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν ὁ κύριος ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπʼ αὐτῇ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Μὴ κλαῖε.
verses.translit: kai idon auten o kyrios esplaghnisthi ep' aute kai eipen aute* Me klaie.
verses.translation: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not.

verses.original: καὶ προσελθὼν ἥψατο τῆς σοροῦ, οἱ δὲ βαστάζοντες ἔστησαν, καὶ εἶπεν· Νεανίσκε, σοὶ λέγω, ἐγέρθητι.
verses.translit: kai proselthon epsato tes sorou, oi de vastazontes estisan, kai eipen* Neaniske, soi lego, egerthiti.
verses.translation: And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.

verses.original: καὶ ἀνεκάθισεν ὁ νεκρὸς καὶ ἤρξατο λαλεῖν, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai anekathisen o nekros kai erxato lalein, kai edoken auton te mitri autou.
verses.translation: And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he delivered him to his mother.

verses.original: ἔλαβεν δὲ φόβος πάντας, καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεὸν λέγοντες ὅτι Προφήτης μέγας ⸀ἠγέρθη ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ ὅτι Ἐπεσκέψατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: elaven de fovos pantas, kai edoxazon ton theon legontes oti Profitis megas egerthi en emin, kai oti Epeskepsato o theos ton laon autou.
verses.translation: And there came a fear on all: and they glorified God, saying, That a great prophet is risen up among us; and, That God hath visited his people.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ λόγος οὗτος ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ περὶ αὐτοῦ ⸀καὶ πάσῃ τῇ περιχώρῳ.
verses.translit: kai exelthen o logos outos en ole te Ioydaia peri autou kai pase te perihoro.
verses.translation: And this rumour of him went forth throughout all Judæa, and throughout all the region round about.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν Ἰωάννῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ περὶ πάντων τούτων. καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος δύο τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰωάννης
verses.translit: Kai apiggeilan Ioanne oi mathitai autou peri panton toyton. kai proskalesamenos dyo tinas ton mathiton autou o Ioannis
verses.translation: And the disciples of John shewed him of all these things.

verses.original: ἔπεμψεν πρὸς τὸν ⸀κύριον λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ⸀ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν;
verses.translit: epempsen pros ton kyrion legon* Su ei o erhomenos e allon prosdokomen;
verses.translation: And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?

verses.original: παραγενόμενοι δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες εἶπαν· Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς ⸀ἀπέστειλεν ἡμᾶς πρὸς σὲ λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν;
verses.translit: paragenomenoi de pros auton oi andres eipan* Ioannis o vaptistes apesteilen emas pros se legon* Su ei o erhomenos e allon prosdokomen;
verses.translation: When the men were come unto him, they said, John Baptist hath sent us unto thee, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?

verses.original: ἐν ⸀ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐθεράπευσεν πολλοὺς ἀπὸ νόσων καὶ μαστίγων καὶ πνευμάτων πονηρῶν, καὶ τυφλοῖς πολλοῖς ⸀ἐχαρίσατο βλέπειν.
verses.translit: en ekeine te ora etherapeysen pollous apo noson kai mastigon kai pneymaton poniron, kai tyflois pollois eharisato vlepein.
verses.translation: And in that same hour he cured many of their infirmities and plagues, and of evil spirits; and unto many that were blind he gave sight.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάννῃ ἃ εἴδετε καὶ ἠκούσατε· ⸀τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσιν, χωλοὶ περιπατοῦσιν, λεπροὶ καθαρίζονται, ⸀κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν, νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται, πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται·
verses.translit: kai apokritheis eipen autois* Poreythentes apaggeilate Ioanne a eidete kai ekoysate* tyfloi anavlepoysin, holoi peripatousin, leproi katharizontai, kofoi akoyoysin, nekroi egeirontai, ptohoi euaggelizontai*
verses.translation: Then Jesus answering said unto them, Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached.

verses.original: καὶ μακάριός ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν μὴ σκανδαλισθῇ ἐν ἐμοί.
verses.translit: kai makarios estin os ean me skandalisthe en emoi.
verses.translation: And blessed is he , whosoever shall not be offended in me.

verses.original: Ἀπελθόντων δὲ τῶν ἀγγέλων Ἰωάννου ἤρξατο λέγειν ⸂πρὸς τοὺς ὄχλους⸃ περὶ Ἰωάννου· Τί ⸀ἐξήλθατε εἰς τὴν ἔρημον θεάσασθαι; κάλαμον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου σαλευόμενον;
verses.translit: Apelthonton de ton aggelon Ioannoy erxato legein pros tous ohloys peri Ioannoy* Ti exilthate eis ten erimon theasasthai; kalamon upo anemoy saleyomenon;
verses.translation: And when the messengers of John were departed, he began to speak unto the people concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness for to see? A reed shaken with the wind?

verses.original: ἀλλὰ τί ⸀ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν; ἄνθρωπον ἐν μαλακοῖς ἱματίοις ἠμφιεσμένον; ἰδοὺ οἱ ἐν ἱματισμῷ ἐνδόξῳ καὶ τρυφῇ ὑπάρχοντες ἐν τοῖς βασιλείοις εἰσίν.
verses.translit: alla ti exilthate idein; anthropon en malakois imatiois emfiesmenon; idou oi en imatismo endoxo kai tryfe uparhontes en tois vasileiois eisin.
verses.translation: But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? Behold, they which are gorgeously apparelled, and live delicately, are in kings’ courts.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ τί ⸀ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν; προφήτην; ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, καὶ περισσότερον προφήτου.
verses.translit: alla ti exilthate idein; profitin; nai, lego umin, kai perissoteron profitoy.
verses.translation: But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? Yea, I say unto you, and much more than a prophet.

verses.original: οὗτός ἐστιν περὶ οὗ γέγραπται· ⸀Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου.
verses.translit: outos estin peri ou gegraptai* Idou apostello ton aggelon moy pro prosopoy soy, os kataskeyasei ten odon soy emprosthen soy.
verses.translation: This is he , of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.

verses.original: ⸀λέγω ὑμῖν, μείζων ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν ⸀Ἰωάννου οὐδείς ἐστιν· ὁ δὲ μικρότερος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ μείζων αὐτοῦ ἐστιν.
verses.translit: lego umin, meizon en gennitois gynaikon Ioannoy oudeis estin* o de mikroteros en te vasileia tou theou meizon autou estin.
verses.translation: For I say unto you, Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist: but he that is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.

verses.original: (καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἀκούσας καὶ οἱ τελῶναι ἐδικαίωσαν τὸν θεόν, βαπτισθέντες τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου·
verses.translit: (kai pas o laos akoysas kai oi telonai edikaiosan ton theon, vaptisthentes to vaptisma Ioannoy*
verses.translation: And all the people that heard him , and the publicans, justified God, being baptized with the baptism of John.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ νομικοὶ τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ἠθέτησαν εἰς ἑαυτούς, μὴ βαπτισθέντες ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ.)
verses.translit: oi de Farisaioi kai oi nomikoi ten voylen tou theou ethetisan eis eaytoys, me vaptisthentes up' autou.)
verses.translation: But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected the counsel of God against themselves, being not baptized of him.

verses.original: Τίνι οὖν ὁμοιώσω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης, καὶ τίνι εἰσὶν ὅμοιοι;
verses.translit: Tini oun omoioso tous anthropoys tes geneas taytis, kai tini eisin omoioi;
verses.translation: And the Lord said, Whereunto then shall I liken the men of this generation? and to what are they like?

verses.original: ὅμοιοί εἰσιν παιδίοις τοῖς ἐν ἀγορᾷ καθημένοις καὶ προσφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις, ⸂ἃ λέγει⸃· Ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε· ⸀ἐθρηνήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐκλαύσατε·
verses.translit: omoioi eisin paidiois tois en agora kathimenois kai prosfonousin allilois, a legei* Iulisamen umin kai ouk orhisasthe* ethrinisamen kai ouk eklaysate*
verses.translation: They are like unto children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned to you, and ye have not wept.

verses.original: ἐλήλυθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς ⸀μὴ ⸂ἐσθίων ἄρτον μήτε πίνων οἶνον⸃, καὶ λέγετε· Δαιμόνιον ἔχει·
verses.translit: elilythen gar Ioannis o vaptistes me esthion arton mite pinon oinon, kai legete* Daimonion ehei*
verses.translation: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine; and ye say, He hath a devil.

verses.original: ἐλήλυθεν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων, καὶ λέγετε· Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης, φίλος τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν.
verses.translit: elilythen o yios tou anthropoy esthion kai pinon, kai legete* Idou anthropos fagos kai oinopotis, filos telonon kai amartolon.
verses.translation: The Son of man is come eating and drinking; and ye say, Behold a gluttonous man, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners!

verses.original: καὶ ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ ⸂πάντων τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς⸃.
verses.translit: kai edikaiothi e sofia apo panton ton teknon autes.
verses.translation: But wisdom is justified of all her children.

verses.original: Ἠρώτα δέ τις αὐτὸν τῶν Φαρισαίων ἵνα φάγῃ μετʼ αὐτοῦ· καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς ⸂τὸν οἶκον⸃ τοῦ Φαρισαίου ⸀κατεκλίθη.
verses.translit: Erota de tis auton ton Farisaion ina fage met' autou* kai eiselthon eis ton oikon tou Farisaioy kateklithi.
verses.translation: And one of the Pharisees desired him that he would eat with him. And he went into the Pharisee’s house, and sat down to meat.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ ⸂ἥτις ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει⸃ ἁμαρτωλός, ⸀καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα ὅτι ⸀κατάκειται ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τοῦ Φαρισαίου, κομίσασα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου
verses.translit: kai idou gyne etis en en te polei amartolos, kai epignousa oti katakeitai en te oikia tou Farisaioy, komisasa alavastron myroy
verses.translation: And, behold, a woman in the city, which was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at meat in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster box of ointment,

verses.original: καὶ στᾶσα ⸂ὀπίσω παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ⸃ κλαίουσα, ⸂τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἤρξατο βρέχειν τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ⸃ καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς ἐξέμασσεν, καὶ κατεφίλει τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤλειφεν τῷ μύρῳ.
verses.translit: kai stasa opiso para tous podas autou klaioysa, tois dakrysin erxato vrehein tous podas autou kai tais thrixin tes kefales autes exemassen, kai katefilei tous podas autou kai eleifen to myro.
verses.translation: And stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment.

verses.original: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Φαρισαῖος ὁ καλέσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Οὗτος εἰ ⸀ἦν προφήτης, ἐγίνωσκεν ἂν τίς καὶ ποταπὴ ἡ γυνὴ ἥτις ἅπτεται αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν.
verses.translit: idon de o Farisaios o kalesas auton eipen en eayto legon* Outos ei en profitis, eginosken an tis kai potape e gyne etis aptetai autou, oti amartolos estin.
verses.translation: Now when the Pharisee which had bidden him saw it , he spake within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him: for she is a sinner.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Σίμων, ἔχω σοί τι εἰπεῖν. ὁ δέ· ⸂Διδάσκαλε, εἰπέ, φησίν⸃.
verses.translit: kai apokritheis o Iisous eipen pros auton* Simon, eho soi ti eipein. o de* Didaskale, eipe, fisin.
verses.translation: And Jesus answering said unto him, Simon, I have somewhat to say unto thee. And he saith, Master, say on.

verses.original: δύο χρεοφειλέται ἦσαν δανιστῇ τινι· ὁ εἷς ὤφειλεν δηνάρια πεντακόσια, ὁ δὲ ἕτερος πεντήκοντα.
verses.translit: dyo hreofeiletai esan daniste tini* o eis ofeilen dinaria pentakosia, o de eteros pentikonta.
verses.translation: There was a certain creditor which had two debtors: the one owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty.

verses.original: μὴ ⸀ἐχόντων αὐτῶν ἀποδοῦναι ἀμφοτέροις ἐχαρίσατο. τίς οὖν ⸀αὐτῶν πλεῖον ⸂ἀγαπήσει αὐτόν⸃;
verses.translit: me ehonton auton apodounai amfoterois eharisato. tis oun auton pleion agapisei auton;
verses.translation: And when they had nothing to pay, he frankly forgave them both. Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most?

verses.original: ⸀ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν· Ὑπολαμβάνω ὅτι ᾧ τὸ πλεῖον ἐχαρίσατο. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὀρθῶς ἔκρινας.
verses.translit: apokritheis Simon eipen* Upolamvano oti o to pleion eharisato. o de eipen auto* Orthos ekrinas.
verses.translation: Simon answered and said, I suppose that he , to whom he forgave most. And he said unto him, Thou hast rightly judged.

verses.original: καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα τῷ Σίμωνι ἔφη· Βλέπεις ταύτην τὴν γυναῖκα; εἰσῆλθόν σου εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν, ὕδωρ ⸀μοι ἐπὶ ⸀πόδας οὐκ ἔδωκας· αὕτη δὲ τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἔβρεξέν μου τοὺς πόδας καὶ ταῖς ⸀θριξὶν αὐτῆς ἐξέμαξεν.
verses.translit: kai strafeis pros ten gynaika to Simoni efi* Vlepeis taytin ten gynaika; eiselthon soy eis ten oikian, udor moi epi podas ouk edokas* auti de tois dakrysin evrexen moy tous podas kai tais thrixin autes exemaxen.
verses.translation: And he turned to the woman, and said unto Simon, Seest thou this woman? I entered into thine house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head.

verses.original: φίλημά μοι οὐκ ἔδωκας· αὕτη δὲ ἀφʼ ἧς εἰσῆλθον οὐ διέλιπεν καταφιλοῦσά μου τοὺς πόδας.
verses.translit: filima moi ouk edokas* auti de af' es eiselthon ou dielipen katafilousa moy tous podas.
verses.translation: Thou gavest me no kiss: but this woman since the time I came in hath not ceased to kiss my feet.

verses.original: ἐλαίῳ τὴν κεφαλήν μου οὐκ ἤλειψας· αὕτη δὲ μύρῳ ἤλειψεν ⸂τοὺς πόδας μου⸃.
verses.translit: elaio ten kefalin moy ouk eleipsas* auti de myro eleipsen tous podas moy.
verses.translation: My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but this woman hath anointed my feet with ointment.

verses.original: οὗ χάριν, λέγω σοι, ἀφέωνται αἱ ἁμαρτίαι αὐτῆς αἱ πολλαί, ὅτι ἠγάπησεν πολύ· ᾧ δὲ ὀλίγον ἀφίεται, ὀλίγον ἀγαπᾷ.
verses.translit: ou harin, lego soi, afeontai ai amartiai autes ai pollai, oti egapisen poly* o de oligon afietai, oligon agapa.
verses.translation: Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῇ· Ἀφέωνταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.
verses.translit: eipen de aute* Afeontai soy ai amartiai.
verses.translation: And he said unto her, Thy sins are forgiven.

verses.original: καὶ ἤρξαντο οἱ συνανακείμενοι λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Τίς οὗτός ἐστιν ὃς καὶ ἁμαρτίας ἀφίησιν;
verses.translit: kai erxanto oi synanakeimenoi legein en eaytois* Tis outos estin os kai amartias afiisin;
verses.translation: And they that sat at meat with him began to say within themselves, Who is this that forgiveth sins also?

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα· Ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην.
verses.translit: eipen de pros ten gynaika* E pistis soy sesoken se* poreyoy eis eirinin.
verses.translation: And he said to the woman, Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ καθεξῆς καὶ αὐτὸς διώδευεν κατὰ πόλιν καὶ κώμην κηρύσσων καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ οἱ δώδεκα σὺν αὐτῷ,
verses.translit: Kai egeneto en to kathexes kai autos diodeyen kata polin kai komin kirysson kai euaggelizomenos ten vasileian tou theou, kai oi dodeka sun auto,
verses.translation: And it came to pass afterward, that he went throughout every city and village, preaching and shewing the glad tidings of the kingdom of God: and the twelve were with him,

verses.original: καὶ γυναῖκές τινες αἳ ἦσαν τεθεραπευμέναι ἀπὸ πνευμάτων πονηρῶν καὶ ἀσθενειῶν, Μαρία ἡ καλουμένη Μαγδαληνή, ἀφʼ ἧς δαιμόνια ἑπτὰ ἐξεληλύθει,
verses.translit: kai gynaikes tines ai esan tetherapeymenai apo pneymaton poniron kai astheneion, Maria e kaloymeni Magdalini, af' es daimonia epta exelilythei,
verses.translation: And certain women, which had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils,

verses.original: καὶ Ἰωάννα γυνὴ Χουζᾶ ἐπιτρόπου Ἡρῴδου καὶ Σουσάννα καὶ ἕτεραι πολλαί, αἵτινες διηκόνουν αὐτοῖς ⸀ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐταῖς.
verses.translit: kai Ioanna gyne Hoyza epitropoy Erodoy kai Soysanna kai eterai pollai, aitines diikonoyn autois ek ton uparhonton autais.
verses.translation: And Joanna the wife of Chuza Herod’s steward, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance.

verses.original: Συνιόντος δὲ ὄχλου πολλοῦ καὶ τῶν κατὰ πόλιν ἐπιπορευομένων πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν διὰ παραβολῆς·
verses.translit: Syniontos de ohloy pollou kai ton kata polin epiporeyomenon pros auton eipen dia paravoles*
verses.translation: And when much people were gathered together, and were come to him out of every city, he spake by a parable:

verses.original: Ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπεῖραι τὸν σπόρον αὐτοῦ. καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ὃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ κατεπατήθη καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατέφαγεν αὐτό.
verses.translit: Exelthen o speiron tou speirai ton sporon autou. kai en to speirein auton o men epesen para ten odon, kai katepatithi kai ta peteina tou ouranou katefagen auto.
verses.translation: A sower went out to sow his seed: and as he sowed, some fell by the way side; and it was trodden down, and the fowls of the air devoured it.

verses.original: καὶ ἕτερον ⸀κατέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν, καὶ φυὲν ἐξηράνθη διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ἰκμάδα.
verses.translit: kai eteron katepesen epi ten petran, kai fyen exiranthi dia to me ehein ikmada.
verses.translation: And some fell upon a rock; and as soon as it was sprung up, it withered away, because it lacked moisture.

verses.original: καὶ ἕτερον ἔπεσεν ἐν μέσῳ τῶν ἀκανθῶν, καὶ συμφυεῖσαι αἱ ἄκανθαι ἀπέπνιξαν αὐτό.
verses.translit: kai eteron epesen en meso ton akanthon, kai symfyeisai ai akanthai apepnixan auto.
verses.translation: And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up with it, and choked it.

verses.original: καὶ ἕτερον ἔπεσεν εἰς τὴν γῆν τὴν ἀγαθήν, καὶ φυὲν ἐποίησεν καρπὸν ἑκατονταπλασίονα. ταῦτα λέγων ἐφώνει· Ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.
verses.translit: kai eteron epesen eis ten gen ten agathin, kai fyen epoiisen karpon ekatontaplasiona. tauta legon efonei* O ehon ota akoyein akoyeto.
verses.translation: And other fell on good ground, and sprang up, and bare fruit an hundredfold. And when he had said these things, he cried, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

verses.original: Ἐπηρώτων δὲ αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ ⸀αὐτοῦ τίς ⸂αὕτη εἴη ἡ παραβολή⸃.
verses.translit: Epiroton de auton oi mathitai autou tis auti eii e paravoli.
verses.translation: And his disciples asked him, saying, What might this parable be?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ὑμῖν δέδοται γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ, τοῖς δὲ λοιποῖς ἐν παραβολαῖς, ἵνα βλέποντες μὴ βλέπωσιν καὶ ἀκούοντες μὴ συνιῶσιν.
verses.translit: o de eipen* Umin dedotai gnonai ta mystiria tes vasileias tou theou, tois de loipois en paravolais, ina vlepontes me vleposin kai akoyontes me syniosin.
verses.translation: And he said, Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God: but to others in parables; that seeing they might not see, and hearing they might not understand.

verses.original: Ἔστιν δὲ αὕτη ἡ παραβολή· Ὁ σπόρος ἐστὶν ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: Estin de auti e paravoli* O sporos estin o logos tou theou.
verses.translation: Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν εἰσιν οἱ ⸀ἀκούσαντες, εἶτα ἔρχεται ὁ διάβολος καὶ αἴρει τὸν λόγον ἀπὸ τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν, ἵνα μὴ πιστεύσαντες σωθῶσιν.
verses.translit: oi de para ten odon eisin oi akoysantes, eita erhetai o diavolos kai airei ton logon apo tes kardias auton, ina me pisteysantes sothosin.
verses.translation: Those by the way side are they that hear; then cometh the devil, and taketh away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐπὶ τῆς πέτρας οἳ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν μετὰ χαρᾶς δέχονται τὸν λόγον, καὶ οὗτοι ῥίζαν οὐκ ἔχουσιν, οἳ πρὸς καιρὸν πιστεύουσιν καὶ ἐν καιρῷ πειρασμοῦ ἀφίστανται.
verses.translit: oi de epi tes petras oi otan akoysosin meta haras dehontai ton logon, kai outoi Rizan ouk ehoysin, oi pros kairon pisteyoysin kai en kairo peirasmou afistantai.
