verses.translation: They on the rock are they , which, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root, which for a while believe, and in time of temptation fall away.

verses.original: τὸ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας πεσόν, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἀκούσαντες, καὶ ὑπὸ μεριμνῶν καὶ πλούτου καὶ ἡδονῶν τοῦ βίου πορευόμενοι συμπνίγονται καὶ οὐ τελεσφοροῦσιν.
verses.translit: to de eis tas akanthas peson, outoi eisin oi akoysantes, kai upo merimnon kai ploytoy kai edonon tou vioy poreyomenoi sympnigontai kai ou telesforousin.
verses.translation: And that which fell among thorns are they, which, when they have heard, go forth, and are choked with cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and bring no fruit to perfection.

verses.original: τὸ δὲ ἐν τῇ καλῇ γῇ, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἵτινες ἐν καρδίᾳ καλῇ καὶ ἀγαθῇ ἀκούσαντες τὸν λόγον κατέχουσιν καὶ καρποφοροῦσιν ἐν ὑπομονῇ.
verses.translit: to de en te kale ge, outoi eisin oitines en kardia kale kai agathe akoysantes ton logon katehoysin kai karpoforousin en upomone.
verses.translation: But that on the good ground are they, which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it , and bring forth fruit with patience.

verses.original: Οὐδεὶς δὲ λύχνον ἅψας καλύπτει αὐτὸν σκεύει ἢ ὑποκάτω κλίνης τίθησιν, ἀλλʼ ἐπὶ λυχνίας ⸀τίθησιν, ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι βλέπωσιν τὸ φῶς.
verses.translit: Oudeis de lyhnon apsas kalyptei auton skeyei e upokato klinis tithisin, all' epi lyhnias tithisin, ina oi eisporeyomenoi vleposin to fos.
verses.translation: No man, when he hath lighted a candle, covereth it with a vessel, or putteth it under a bed; but setteth it on a candlestick, that they which enter in may see the light.

verses.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ φανερὸν γενήσεται, οὐδὲ ἀπόκρυφον ὃ οὐ ⸂μὴ γνωσθῇ⸃ καὶ εἰς φανερὸν ἔλθῃ.
verses.translit: ou gar estin krypton o ou faneron genisetai, oude apokryfon o ou me gnosthe kai eis faneron elthe.
verses.translation: For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.

verses.original: βλέπετε οὖν πῶς ἀκούετε· ὃς ⸂ἂν γὰρ⸃ ἔχῃ, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ, καὶ ὃς ⸀ἂν μὴ ἔχῃ, καὶ ὃ δοκεῖ ἔχειν ἀρθήσεται ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: vlepete oun pos akoyete* os an gar ehe, dothisetai auto, kai os an me ehe, kai o dokei ehein arthisetai ap' autou.
verses.translation: Take heed therefore how ye hear: for whosoever hath, to him shall be given; and whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he seemeth to have.

verses.original: ⸀Παρεγένετο δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ μήτηρ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐκ ἠδύναντο συντυχεῖν αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον.
verses.translit: Paregeneto de pros auton e mitir kai oi adelfoi autou, kai ouk edynanto syntyhein auto dia ton ohlon.
verses.translation: Then came to him his mother and his brethren, and could not come at him for the press.

verses.original: ⸂ἀπηγγέλη δὲ⸃ ⸀αὐτῷ· Ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἑστήκασιν ἔξω ἰδεῖν ⸂σε θέλοντες⸃.
verses.translit: apiggeli de auto* E mitir soy kai oi adelfoi soy estikasin exo idein se thelontes.
verses.translation: And it was told him by certain which said, Thy mother and thy brethren stand without, desiring to see thee.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μήτηρ μου καὶ ἀδελφοί μου οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ ἀκούοντες καὶ ⸀ποιοῦντες.
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen pros autoys* Mitir moy kai adelfoi moy outoi eisin oi ton logon tou theou akoyontes kai poiountes.
verses.translation: And he answered and said unto them, My mother and my brethren are these which hear the word of God, and do it.

verses.original: ⸂Ἐγένετο δὲ⸃ ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἐνέβη εἰς πλοῖον καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς λίμνης, καὶ ἀνήχθησαν.
verses.translit: Egeneto de en mia ton emeron kai autos enevi eis ploion kai oi mathitai autou, kai eipen pros autoys* Dielthomen eis to peran tes limnis, kai anihthisan.
verses.translation: Now it came to pass on a certain day, that he went into a ship with his disciples: and he said unto them, Let us go over unto the other side of the lake. And they launched forth.

verses.original: πλεόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἀφύπνωσεν. καὶ κατέβη λαῖλαψ ἀνέμου εἰς τὴν λίμνην, καὶ συνεπληροῦντο καὶ ἐκινδύνευον.
verses.translit: pleonton de auton afypnosen. kai katevi lailaps anemoy eis ten limnin, kai syneplirounto kai ekindyneyon.
verses.translation: But as they sailed he fell asleep: and there came down a storm of wind on the lake; and they were filled with water , and were in jeopardy.

verses.original: προσελθόντες δὲ διήγειραν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Ἐπιστάτα ἐπιστάτα, ἀπολλύμεθα· ὁ δὲ ⸀διεγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ ἀνέμῳ καὶ τῷ κλύδωνι τοῦ ὕδατος, καὶ ἐπαύσαντο, καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη.
verses.translit: proselthontes de diigeiran auton legontes* Epistata epistata, apollymetha* o de diegertheis epetimisen to anemo kai to klydoni tou udatos, kai epaysanto, kai egeneto galini.
verses.translation: And they came to him, and awoke him, saying, Master, master, we perish. Then he arose, and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water: and they ceased, and there was a calm.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· ⸀Ποῦ ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν; φοβηθέντες δὲ ἐθαύμασαν, λέγοντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Τίς ἄρα οὗτός ἐστιν ὅτι καὶ τοῖς ἀνέμοις ἐπιτάσσει καὶ τῷ ὕδατι, καὶ ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ;
verses.translit: eipen de autois* Pou e pistis umon; fovithentes de ethaymasan, legontes pros alliloys* Tis ara outos estin oti kai tois anemois epitassei kai to udati, kai upakoyoysin auto;
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Where is your faith? And they being afraid wondered, saying one to another, What manner of man is this! for he commandeth even the winds and water, and they obey him.

verses.original: Καὶ κατέπλευσαν εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν ⸀Γερασηνῶν, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἀντιπέρα τῆς Γαλιλαίας.
verses.translit: Kai katepleysan eis ten horan ton Gerasinon, etis estin antipera tes Galilaias.
verses.translation: And they arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is over against Galilee.

verses.original: ἐξελθόντι δὲ αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ⸀ὑπήντησεν ἀνήρ τις ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ⸀ἔχων δαιμόνια· ⸂καὶ χρόνῳ ἱκανῷ οὐκ ἐνεδύσατο ἱμάτιον⸃, καὶ ἐν οἰκίᾳ οὐκ ἔμενεν ἀλλʼ ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν.
verses.translit: exelthonti de auto epi ten gen upintisen anir tis ek tes poleos ehon daimonia* kai hrono ikano ouk enedysato imation, kai en oikia ouk emenen all' en tois mnimasin.
verses.translation: And when he went forth to land, there met him out of the city a certain man, which had devils long time, and ware no clothes, neither abode in any house, but in the tombs.

verses.original: ἰδὼν δὲ τὸν ⸀Ἰησοῦν ἀνακράξας προσέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ φωνῇ μεγάλῃ εἶπεν· Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου; δέομαί σου, μή με βασανίσῃς·
verses.translit: idon de ton Iisoun anakraxas prosepesen auto kai fone megale eipen* Ti emoi kai soi, Iisou yie tou theou tou upsistoy; deomai soy, mi me vasanises*
verses.translation: When he saw Jesus, he cried out, and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God most high? I beseech thee, torment me not.

verses.original: ⸀παρήγγελλεν γὰρ τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ ἐξελθεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου. πολλοῖς γὰρ χρόνοις συνηρπάκει αὐτόν, καὶ ⸀ἐδεσμεύετο ἁλύσεσιν καὶ πέδαις φυλασσόμενος, καὶ διαρρήσσων τὰ δεσμὰ ἠλαύνετο ⸀ὑπὸ τοῦ ⸀δαιμονίου εἰς τὰς ἐρήμους.
verses.translit: pariggellen gar to pneymati to akatharto exelthein apo tou anthropoy. pollois gar hronois synirpakei auton, kai edesmeyeto alysesin kai pedais fylassomenos, kai diarrisson ta desma elayneto upo tou daimonioy eis tas erimoys.
verses.translation: (For he had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For oftentimes it had caught him: and he was kept bound with chains and in fetters; and he brake the bands, and was driven of the devil into the wilderness.)

verses.original: ἐπηρώτησεν δὲ αὐτὸν ὁ ⸀Ἰησοῦς· Τί σοι ⸂ὄνομά ἐστιν⸃; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Λεγιών, ὅτι ⸂εἰσῆλθεν δαιμόνια πολλὰ⸃ εἰς αὐτόν.
verses.translit: epirotisen de auton o Iisous* Ti soi onoma estin; o de eipen* Legion, oti eiselthen daimonia polla eis auton.
verses.translation: And Jesus asked him, saying, What is thy name? And he said, Legion: because many devils were entered into him.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα μὴ ἐπιτάξῃ αὐτοῖς εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον ἀπελθεῖν.
verses.translit: kai parekaloyn auton ina me epitaxe autois eis ten avysson apelthein.
verses.translation: And they besought him that he would not command them to go out into the deep.

verses.original: Ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ ἀγέλη χοίρων ἱκανῶν ⸀βοσκομένη ἐν τῷ ὄρει· καὶ ⸀παρεκάλεσαν αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιτρέψῃ αὐτοῖς εἰς ἐκείνους εἰσελθεῖν· καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: En de ekei ageli hoiron ikanon voskomeni en to orei* kai parekalesan auton ina epitrepse autois eis ekeinoys eiselthein* kai epetrepsen autois.
verses.translation: And there was there an herd of many swine feeding on the mountain: and they besought him that he would suffer them to enter into them. And he suffered them.

verses.original: ἐξελθόντα δὲ τὰ δαιμόνια ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰσῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, καὶ ὥρμησεν ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν λίμνην καὶ ἀπεπνίγη.
verses.translit: exelthonta de ta daimonia apo tou anthropoy eiselthon eis tous hoiroys, kai ormisen e ageli kata tou krimnou eis ten limnin kai apepnigi.
verses.translation: Then went the devils out of the man, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the lake, and were choked.

verses.original: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ βόσκοντες τὸ ⸀γεγονὸς ἔφυγον καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἀγρούς.
verses.translit: Idontes de oi voskontes to gegonos efygon kai apiggeilan eis ten polin kai eis tous agroys.
verses.translation: When they that fed them saw what was done, they fled, and went and told it in the city and in the country.

verses.original: ἐξῆλθον δὲ ἰδεῖν τὸ γεγονὸς καὶ ἦλθον πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ εὗρον καθήμενον τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἀφʼ οὗ τὰ δαιμόνια ⸀ἐξῆλθεν ἱματισμένον καὶ σωφρονοῦντα παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν.
verses.translit: exelthon de idein to gegonos kai elthon pros ton Iisoun, kai euron kathimenon ton anthropon af' ou ta daimonia exelthen imatismenon kai sofronounta para tous podas tou Iisou, kai efovithisan.
verses.translation: Then they went out to see what was done; and came to Jesus, and found the man, out of whom the devils were departed, sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.

verses.original: ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ ⸀αὐτοῖς οἱ ἰδόντες πῶς ἐσώθη ὁ δαιμονισθείς.
verses.translit: apiggeilan de autois oi idontes pos esothi o daimonistheis.
verses.translation: They also which saw it told them by what means he that was possessed of the devils was healed.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος τῆς περιχώρου τῶν ⸀Γερασηνῶν ἀπελθεῖν ἀπʼ αὐτῶν, ὅτι φόβῳ μεγάλῳ συνείχοντο· αὐτὸς δὲ ἐμβὰς ⸀εἰς πλοῖον ὑπέστρεψεν.
verses.translit: kai erotisen auton apan to plethos tes perihoroy ton Gerasinon apelthein ap' auton, oti fovo megalo syneihonto* autos de emvas eis ploion upestrepsen.
verses.translation: Then the whole multitude of the country of the Gadarenes round about besought him to depart from them; for they were taken with great fear: and he went up into the ship, and returned back again.

verses.original: ἐδεῖτο δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ ἀνὴρ ἀφʼ οὗ ἐξεληλύθει τὰ δαιμόνια εἶναι σὺν αὐτῷ· ἀπέλυσεν δὲ ⸀αὐτὸν λέγων·
verses.translit: edeito de autou o aner af' ou exelilythei ta daimonia einai sun auto* apelysen de auton legon*
verses.translation: Now the man out of whom the devils were departed besought him that he might be with him: but Jesus sent him away, saying,

verses.original: Ὑπόστρεφε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου, καὶ διηγοῦ ὅσα ⸂σοι ἐποίησεν⸃ ὁ θεός. καὶ ἀπῆλθεν καθʼ ὅλην τὴν πόλιν κηρύσσων ὅσα ἐποίησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
verses.translit: Upostrefe eis ton oikon soy, kai diigou osa soi epoiisen o theos. kai apelthen kath' olin ten polin kirysson osa epoiisen auto o Iisous.
verses.translation: Return to thine own house, and shew how great things God hath done unto thee. And he went his way, and published throughout the whole city how great things Jesus had done unto him.

verses.original: ⸂Ἐν δὲ⸃ τῷ ⸀ὑποστρέφειν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπεδέξατο αὐτὸν ὁ ὄχλος, ἦσαν γὰρ πάντες προσδοκῶντες αὐτόν.
verses.translit: En de to upostrefein ton Iisoun apedexato auton o ohlos, esan gar pantes prosdokontes auton.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that, when Jesus was returned, the people gladly received him: for they were all waiting for him.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἦλθεν ἀνὴρ ᾧ ὄνομα Ἰάϊρος, καὶ ⸀οὗτος ἄρχων τῆς συναγωγῆς ὑπῆρχεν, καὶ πεσὼν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας ⸀τοῦ Ἰησοῦ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: kai idou elthen aner o onoma Iairos, kai outos arhon tes synagoges uperhen, kai peson para tous podas tou Iisou parekalei auton eiselthein eis ton oikon autou,
verses.translation: And, behold, there came a man named Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue: and he fell down at Jesus’ feet, and besought him that he would come into his house:

verses.original: ὅτι θυγάτηρ μονογενὴς ἦν αὐτῷ ὡς ἐτῶν δώδεκα καὶ αὐτὴ ἀπέθνῃσκεν. Ἐν δὲ τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτὸν οἱ ὄχλοι συνέπνιγον αὐτόν.
verses.translit: oti thygatir monogenes en auto os eton dodeka kai aute apethnesken. En de to upagein auton oi ohloi synepnigon auton.
verses.translation: For he had one only daughter, about twelve years of age, and she lay a dying. But as he went the people thronged him.

verses.original: καὶ γυνὴ οὖσα ἐν ῥύσει αἵματος ἀπὸ ἐτῶν δώδεκα, ἥτις ⸂ἰατροῖς προσαναλώσασα ὅλον τὸν βίον⸃ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν ⸀ἀπʼ οὐδενὸς θεραπευθῆναι,
verses.translit: kai gyne ousa en Rysei aimatos apo eton dodeka, etis iatrois prosanalosasa olon ton vion ouk ishysen ap' oudenos therapeythenai,
verses.translation: And a woman having an issue of blood twelve years, which had spent all her living upon physicians, neither could be healed of any,

verses.original: προσελθοῦσα ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ, καὶ παραχρῆμα ἔστη ἡ ῥύσις τοῦ αἵματος αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: proselthousa opisthen epsato tou kraspedoy tou imatioy autou, kai parahrema esti e Rysis tou aimatos autes.
verses.translation: Came behind him , and touched the border of his garment: and immediately her issue of blood stanched.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τίς ὁ ἁψάμενός μου; ἀρνουμένων δὲ πάντων εἶπεν ὁ ⸀Πέτρος· Ἐπιστάτα, οἱ ὄχλοι συνέχουσίν σε καὶ ⸀ἀποθλίβουσιν.
verses.translit: kai eipen o Iisous* Tis o apsamenos moy; arnoymenon de panton eipen o Petros* Epistata, oi ohloi synehoysin se kai apothlivoysin.
verses.translation: And Jesus said, Who touched me? When all denied, Peter and they that were with him said, Master, the multitude throng thee and press thee , and sayest thou, Who touched me?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἥψατό μού τις, ἐγὼ γὰρ ἔγνων δύναμιν ⸀ἐξεληλυθυῖαν ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ.
verses.translit: o de Iisous eipen* Epsato moy tis, ego gar egnon dynamin exelilythyian ap' emou.
verses.translation: And Jesus said, Somebody hath touched me: for I perceive that virtue is gone out of me.

verses.original: ἰδοῦσα δὲ ἡ γυνὴ ὅτι οὐκ ἔλαθεν τρέμουσα ἦλθεν καὶ προσπεσοῦσα αὐτῷ διʼ ἣν αἰτίαν ἥψατο αὐτοῦ ⸀ἀπήγγειλεν ἐνώπιον παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ὡς ἰάθη παραχρῆμα.
verses.translit: idousa de e gyne oti ouk elathen tremoysa elthen kai prospesousa auto di' en aitian epsato autou apiggeilen enopion pantos tou laou kai os iathi parahrema.
verses.translation: And when the woman saw that she was not hid, she came trembling, and falling down before him, she declared unto him before all the people for what cause she had touched him, and how she was healed immediately.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· ⸀Θυγάτηρ, ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην.
verses.translit: o de eipen aute* Thygatir, e pistis soy sesoken se* poreyoy eis eirinin.
verses.translation: And he said unto her, Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.

verses.original: Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἔρχεταί τις παρὰ τοῦ ἀρχισυναγώγου ⸀λέγων ὅτι Τέθνηκεν ἡ θυγάτηρ σου, ⸀μηκέτι σκύλλε τὸν διδάσκαλον.
verses.translit: Eti autou lalountos erhetai tis para tou arhisynagogoy legon oti Tethniken e thygatir soy, miketi skylle ton didaskalon.
verses.translation: While he yet spake, there cometh one from the ruler of the synagogue’s house , saying to him, Thy daughter is dead; trouble not the Master.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀκούσας ἀπεκρίθη ⸀αὐτῷ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, μόνον ⸀πίστευσον, καὶ σωθήσεται.
verses.translit: o de Iisous akoysas apekrithi auto* Me fovou, monon pisteyson, kai sothisetai.
verses.translation: But when Jesus heard it , he answered him, saying, Fear not: believe only, and she shall be made whole.

verses.original: ἐλθὼν δὲ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν οὐκ ἀφῆκεν εἰσελθεῖν ⸂τινα σὺν αὐτῷ⸃ εἰ μὴ Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ τὸν πατέρα τῆς παιδὸς καὶ τὴν μητέρα.
verses.translit: elthon de eis ten oikian ouk afeken eiselthein tina sun auto ei me Petron kai Ioannin kai Iakovon kai ton patera tes paidos kai ten mitera.
verses.translation: And when he came into the house, he suffered no man to go in, save Peter, and James, and John, and the father and the mother of the maiden.

verses.original: ἔκλαιον δὲ πάντες καὶ ἐκόπτοντο αὐτήν. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Μὴ κλαίετε, ⸂οὐ γὰρ⸃ ἀπέθανεν ἀλλὰ καθεύδει.
verses.translit: eklaion de pantes kai ekoptonto autin. o de eipen* Me klaiete, ou gar apethanen alla katheydei.
verses.translation: And all wept, and bewailed her: but he said, Weep not; she is not dead, but sleepeth.

verses.original: καὶ κατεγέλων αὐτοῦ, εἰδότες ὅτι ἀπέθανεν.
verses.translit: kai kategelon autou, eidotes oti apethanen.
verses.translation: And they laughed him to scorn, knowing that she was dead.

verses.original: αὐτὸς ⸀δὲ κρατήσας τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς ἐφώνησεν λέγων· Ἡ παῖς, ⸀ἔγειρε.
verses.translit: autos de kratisas tes heiros autes efonisen legon* E pais, egeire.
verses.translation: And he put them all out, and took her by the hand, and called, saying, Maid, arise.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπέστρεψεν τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτῆς, καὶ ἀνέστη παραχρῆμα, καὶ διέταξεν αὐτῇ δοθῆναι φαγεῖν.
verses.translit: kai epestrepsen to pneuma autes, kai anesti parahrema, kai dietaxen aute dothenai fagein.
verses.translation: And her spirit came again, and she arose straightway: and he commanded to give her meat.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξέστησαν οἱ γονεῖς αὐτῆς· ὁ δὲ παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν τὸ γεγονός.
verses.translit: kai exestisan oi goneis autes* o de pariggeilen autois mideni eipein to gegonos.
verses.translation: And her parents were astonished: but he charged them that they should tell no man what was done.

verses.original: Συγκαλεσάμενος δὲ τοὺς δώδεκα ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς δύναμιν καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ δαιμόνια καὶ νόσους θεραπεύειν,
verses.translit: Sygkalesamenos de tous dodeka edoken autois dynamin kai exoysian epi panta ta daimonia kai nosoys therapeyein,
verses.translation: Then he called his twelve disciples together, and gave them power and authority over all devils, and to cure diseases.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς κηρύσσειν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἰᾶσθαι ⸂τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς⸃,
verses.translit: kai apesteilen autous kiryssein ten vasileian tou theou kai iasthai tous astheneis,
verses.translation: And he sent them to preach the kingdom of God, and to heal the sick.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μηδὲν αἴρετε εἰς τὴν ὁδόν, μήτε ⸀ῥάβδον μήτε πήραν μήτε ἄρτον μήτε ἀργύριον, μήτε ⸀ἀνὰ δύο χιτῶνας ἔχειν.
verses.translit: kai eipen pros autoys* Miden airete eis ten odon, mite Ravdon mite piran mite arton mite argyrion, mite ana dyo hitonas ehein.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Take nothing for your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece.

verses.original: καὶ εἰς ἣν ἂν οἰκίαν εἰσέλθητε, ἐκεῖ μένετε καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἐξέρχεσθε.
verses.translit: kai eis en an oikian eiselthite, ekei menete kai ekeithen exerhesthe.
verses.translation: And whatsoever house ye enter into, there abide, and thence depart.

verses.original: καὶ ὅσοι ⸀ἂν μὴ ⸀δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐξερχόμενοι ἀπὸ τῆς πόλεως ⸀ἐκείνης τὸν κονιορτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν ⸀ἀποτινάσσετε εἰς μαρτύριον ἐπʼ αὐτούς.
verses.translit: kai osoi an me dehontai umas, exerhomenoi apo tes poleos ekeinis ton koniorton apo ton podon umon apotinassete eis martyrion ep' autoys.
verses.translation: And whosoever will not receive you, when ye go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.

verses.original: ἐξερχόμενοι δὲ διήρχοντο κατὰ τὰς κώμας εὐαγγελιζόμενοι καὶ θεραπεύοντες πανταχοῦ.
verses.translit: exerhomenoi de diirhonto kata tas komas euaggelizomenoi kai therapeyontes pantahou.
verses.translation: And they departed, and went through the towns, preaching the gospel, and healing every where.

verses.original: Ἤκουσεν δὲ Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης τὰ ⸀γινόμενα πάντα, καὶ διηπόρει διὰ τὸ λέγεσθαι ὑπό τινων ὅτι Ἰωάννης ⸀ἠγέρθη ἐκ νεκρῶν,
verses.translit: Ekoysen de Erodis o tetraarhis ta ginomena panta, kai diiporei dia to legesthai upo tinon oti Ioannis egerthi ek nekron,
verses.translation: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was done by him: and he was perplexed, because that it was said of some, that John was risen from the dead;

verses.original: ὑπό τινων δὲ ὅτι Ἠλίας ἐφάνη, ἄλλων δὲ ὅτι προφήτης ⸀τις τῶν ἀρχαίων ἀνέστη.
verses.translit: upo tinon de oti Elias efani, allon de oti profitis tis ton arhaion anesti.
verses.translation: And of some, that Elias had appeared; and of others, that one of the old prophets was risen again.

verses.original: ⸂εἶπεν δὲ⸃ ⸀ὁ Ἡρῴδης· Ἰωάννην ἐγὼ ἀπεκεφάλισα· τίς δέ ἐστιν οὗτος περὶ ⸀οὗ ἀκούω τοιαῦτα; καὶ ἐζήτει ἰδεῖν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: eipen de o Erodis* Ioannin ego apekefalisa* tis de estin outos peri ou akoyo toiauta; kai ezitei idein auton.
verses.translation: And Herod said, John have I beheaded: but who is this, of whom I hear such things? And he desired to see him.

verses.original: Καὶ ὑποστρέψαντες οἱ ἀπόστολοι διηγήσαντο αὐτῷ ὅσα ἐποίησαν. καὶ παραλαβὼν αὐτοὺς ὑπεχώρησεν κατʼ ἰδίαν εἰς ⸂πόλιν καλουμένην Βηθσαϊδά⸃.
verses.translit: Kai upostrepsantes oi apostoloi diigisanto auto osa epoiisan. kai paralavon autous upehorisen kat' idian eis polin kaloymenin Vithsaida.
verses.translation: And the apostles, when they were returned, told him all that they had done. And he took them, and went aside privately into a desert place belonging to the city called Bethsaida.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι γνόντες ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ. καὶ ⸀ἀποδεξάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ τοὺς χρείαν ἔχοντας θεραπείας ἰᾶτο.
verses.translit: oi de ohloi gnontes ekoloythisan auto. kai apodexamenos autous elalei autois peri tes vasileias tou theou, kai tous hreian ehontas therapeias iato.
verses.translation: And the people, when they knew it , followed him: and he received them, and spake unto them of the kingdom of God, and healed them that had need of healing.

verses.original: Ἡ δὲ ἡμέρα ἤρξατο κλίνειν· προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δώδεκα εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἀπόλυσον τὸν ὄχλον, ἵνα ⸀πορευθέντες εἰς τὰς κύκλῳ κώμας ⸀καὶ ἀγροὺς καταλύσωσιν καὶ εὕρωσιν ἐπισιτισμόν, ὅτι ὧδε ἐν ἐρήμῳ τόπῳ ἐσμέν.
verses.translit: E de emera erxato klinein* proselthontes de oi dodeka eipan auto* Apolyson ton ohlon, ina poreythentes eis tas kyklo komas kai agrous katalysosin kai eurosin episitismon, oti ode en erimo topo esmen.
verses.translation: And when the day began to wear away, then came the twelve, and said unto him, Send the multitude away, that they may go into the towns and country round about, and lodge, and get victuals: for we are here in a desert place.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Δότε αὐτοῖς ⸂ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν⸃. οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Οὐκ εἰσὶν ἡμῖν πλεῖον ἢ ⸂ἄρτοι πέντε⸃ καὶ ἰχθύες δύο, εἰ μήτι πορευθέντες ἡμεῖς ἀγοράσωμεν εἰς πάντα τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον βρώματα.
verses.translit: eipen de pros autoys* Dote autois umeis fagein. oi de eipan* Ouk eisin emin pleion e artoi pente kai ihthyes dyo, ei miti poreythentes emeis agorasomen eis panta ton laon touton vromata.
verses.translation: But he said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they said, We have no more but five loaves and two fishes; except we should go and buy meat for all this people.

verses.original: ἦσαν γὰρ ὡσεὶ ἄνδρες πεντακισχίλιοι. εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Κατακλίνατε αὐτοὺς κλισίας ⸀ὡσεὶ ἀνὰ πεντήκοντα.
verses.translit: esan gar osei andres pentakishilioi. eipen de pros tous mathitas autou* Kataklinate autous klisias osei ana pentikonta.
verses.translation: For they were about five thousand men. And he said to his disciples, Make them sit down by fifties in a company.

verses.original: καὶ ἐποίησαν οὕτως καὶ ⸀κατέκλιναν ἅπαντας.
verses.translit: kai epoiisan outos kai kateklinan apantas.
verses.translation: And they did so, and made them all sit down.

verses.original: λαβὼν δὲ τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ κατέκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς ⸀παραθεῖναι τῷ ὄχλῳ.
verses.translit: lavon de tous pente artoys kai tous dyo ihthyas anavlepsas eis ton ouranon eulogisen autous kai kateklasen kai edidoy tois mathitais paratheinai to ohlo.
verses.translation: Then he took the five loaves and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed them, and brake, and gave to the disciples to set before the multitude.

verses.original: καὶ ἔφαγον καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν πάντες, καὶ ἤρθη τὸ περισσεῦσαν αὐτοῖς κλασμάτων κόφινοι δώδεκα.
verses.translit: kai efagon kai ehortasthisan pantes, kai erthi to perisseusan autois klasmaton kofinoi dodeka.
verses.translation: And they did eat, and were all filled: and there was taken up of fragments that remained to them twelve baskets.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν προσευχόμενον κατὰ μόνας συνῆσαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί, καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς λέγων· Τίνα με ⸂οἱ ὄχλοι λέγουσιν⸃ εἶναι;
verses.translit: Kai egeneto en to einai auton proseyhomenon kata monas synesan auto oi mathitai, kai epirotisen autous legon* Tina me oi ohloi legoysin einai;
verses.translation: And it came to pass, as he was alone praying, his disciples were with him: and he asked them, saying, Whom say the people that I am?

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἀποκριθέντες εἶπαν· Ἰωάννην τὸν βαπτιστήν, ἄλλοι δὲ Ἠλίαν, ἄλλοι δὲ ὅτι προφήτης τις τῶν ἀρχαίων ἀνέστη.
verses.translit: oi de apokrithentes eipan* Ioannin ton vaptistin, alloi de Elian, alloi de oti profitis tis ton arhaion anesti.
verses.translation: They answering said, John the Baptist; but some say , Elias; and others say , that one of the old prophets is risen again.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι; ⸂Πέτρος δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς⸃ εἶπεν· Τὸν χριστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: eipen de autois* Umeis de tina me legete einai; Petros de apokritheis eipen* Ton hriston tou theou.
verses.translation: He said unto them, But whom say ye that I am? Peter answering said, The Christ of God.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ ἐπιτιμήσας αὐτοῖς παρήγγειλεν μηδενὶ ⸀λέγειν τοῦτο,
verses.translit: O de epitimisas autois pariggeilen mideni legein touto,
verses.translation: And he straitly charged them, and commanded them to tell no man that thing;

verses.original: εἰπὼν ὅτι Δεῖ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ ἀρχιερέων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ⸀ἐγερθῆναι.
verses.translit: eipon oti Dei ton yion tou anthropoy polla pathein kai apodokimasthenai apo ton presvyteron kai arhiereon kai grammateon kai apoktanthenai kai te trite emera egerthenai.
verses.translation: Saying, The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be slain, and be raised the third day.

verses.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς πάντας· Εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ⸂ἔρχεσθαι, ἀρνησάσθω⸃ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ ⸂καθʼ ἡμέραν⸃, καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι.
verses.translit: Elegen de pros pantas* Ei tis thelei opiso moy erhesthai, arnisastho eayton kai arato ton stayron autou kath' emeran, kai akoloytheito moi.
verses.translation: And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.

verses.original: ὃς γὰρ ⸀ἂν θέλῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ σῶσαι, ἀπολέσει αὐτήν· ὃς δʼ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ, οὗτος σώσει αὐτήν.
verses.translit: os gar an thele ten psyhen autou sosai, apolesei autin* os d' an apolese ten psyhen autou eneken emou, outos sosei autin.
verses.translation: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it.

verses.original: τί γὰρ ὠφελεῖται ἄνθρωπος κερδήσας τὸν κόσμον ὅλον ἑαυτὸν δὲ ἀπολέσας ἢ ζημιωθείς;
verses.translit: ti gar ofeleitai anthropos kerdisas ton kosmon olon eayton de apolesas e zimiotheis;
verses.translation: For what is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away?

verses.original: ὃς γὰρ ἂν ἐπαισχυνθῇ με καὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους, τοῦτον ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπαισχυνθήσεται, ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐν τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων.
verses.translit: os gar an epaishynthe me kai tous emous logoys, touton o yios tou anthropoy epaishynthisetai, otan elthe en te doxe autou kai tou patros kai ton agion aggelon.
verses.translation: For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he shall come in his own glory, and in his Father’s, and of the holy angels.

verses.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ἀληθῶς, εἰσίν τινες τῶν ⸀αὐτοῦ ⸀ἑστηκότων οἳ οὐ μὴ γεύσωνται θανάτου ἕως ἂν ἴδωσιν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: lego de umin alithos, eisin tines ton autou estikoton oi ou me geysontai thanatoy eos an idosin ten vasileian tou theou.
verses.translation: But I tell you of a truth, there be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ μετὰ τοὺς λόγους τούτους ὡσεὶ ἡμέραι ὀκτὼ ⸀καὶ παραλαβὼν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Ἰάκωβον ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι.
verses.translit: Egeneto de meta tous logoys toytoys osei emerai okto kai paralavon Petron kai Ioannin kai Iakovon anevi eis to oros proseyxasthai.
verses.translation: And it came to pass about an eight days after these sayings, he took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ προσεύχεσθαι αὐτὸν τὸ εἶδος τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἕτερον καὶ ὁ ἱματισμὸς αὐτοῦ λευκὸς ἐξαστράπτων.
verses.translit: kai egeneto en to proseyhesthai auton to eidos tou prosopoy autou eteron kai o imatismos autou leykos exastrapton.
verses.translation: And as he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and his raiment was white and glistering.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο συνελάλουν αὐτῷ, οἵτινες ἦσαν Μωϋσῆς καὶ Ἠλίας,
verses.translit: kai idou andres dyo synelaloyn auto, oitines esan Moyses kai Elias,
verses.translation: And, behold, there talked with him two men, which were Moses and Elias:

verses.original: οἳ ὀφθέντες ἐν δόξῃ ἔλεγον τὴν ἔξοδον αὐτοῦ ἣν ἤμελλεν πληροῦν ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ.
verses.translit: oi ofthentes en doxe elegon ten exodon autou en emellen pliroun en Ieroysalim.
verses.translation: Who appeared in glory, and spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ ἦσαν βεβαρημένοι ὕπνῳ· διαγρηγορήσαντες δὲ εἶδον τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς δύο ἄνδρας τοὺς συνεστῶτας αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: o de Petros kai oi sun auto esan vevarimenoi upno* diagrigorisantes de eidon ten doxan autou kai tous dyo andras tous synestotas auto.
verses.translation: But Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep: and when they were awake, they saw his glory, and the two men that stood with him.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ διαχωρίζεσθαι αὐτοὺς ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ εἶπεν ⸀ὁ Πέτρος πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν· Ἐπιστάτα, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι, καὶ ποιήσωμεν σκηνὰς τρεῖς, μίαν σοὶ καὶ μίαν Μωϋσεῖ καὶ μίαν Ἠλίᾳ, μὴ εἰδὼς ὃ λέγει.
verses.translit: kai egeneto en to diahorizesthai autous ap' autou eipen o Petros pros ton Iisoun* Epistata, kalon estin emas ode einai, kai poiisomen skinas treis, mian soi kai mian Moysei kai mian Elia, me eidos o legei.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, as they departed from him, Peter said unto Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias: not knowing what he said.

verses.original: ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ἐγένετο νεφέλη καὶ ⸀ἐπεσκίαζεν αὐτούς· ἐφοβήθησαν δὲ ἐν τῷ ⸂εἰσελθεῖν αὐτοὺς⸃ εἰς τὴν νεφέλην.
verses.translit: tauta de autou legontos egeneto nefeli kai epeskiazen autoys* efovithisan de en to eiselthein autous eis ten nefelin.
verses.translation: While he thus spake, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud.

verses.original: καὶ φωνὴ ἐγένετο ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ⸀ἐκλελεγμένος, αὐτοῦ ἀκούετε.
verses.translit: kai fone egeneto ek tes nefelis legoysa* Outos estin o yios moy o eklelegmenos, autou akoyete.
verses.translation: And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.

verses.original: καὶ ἐν τῷ γενέσθαι τὴν φωνὴν ⸀εὑρέθη Ἰησοῦς μόνος. καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐσίγησαν καὶ οὐδενὶ ἀπήγγειλαν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις οὐδὲν ὧν ἑώρακαν.
verses.translit: kai en to genesthai ten fonen eurethi Iisous monos. kai autoi esigisan kai oudeni apiggeilan en ekeinais tais emerais ouden on eorakan.
verses.translation: And when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone. And they kept it close, and told no man in those days any of those things which they had seen.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο ⸀δὲ τῇ ἑξῆς ἡμέρᾳ κατελθόντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄρους συνήντησεν αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς.
verses.translit: Egeneto de te exes emera katelthonton auton apo tou oroys synintisen auto ohlos polys.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that on the next day, when they were come down from the hill, much people met him.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου ⸀ἐβόησεν λέγων· Διδάσκαλε, δέομαί σου ἐπιβλέψαι ἐπὶ τὸν υἱόν μου, ὅτι μονογενής ⸂μοί ἐστιν⸃,
verses.translit: kai idou aner apo tou ohloy evoisen legon* Didaskale, deomai soy epivlepsai epi ton yion moy, oti monogenis moi estin,
verses.translation: And, behold, a man of the company cried out, saying, Master, I beseech thee, look upon my son: for he is mine only child.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ πνεῦμα λαμβάνει αὐτόν, καὶ ἐξαίφνης κράζει, καὶ σπαράσσει αὐτὸν μετὰ ἀφροῦ καὶ ⸀μόγις ἀποχωρεῖ ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ συντρῖβον αὐτόν·
verses.translit: kai idou pneuma lamvanei auton, kai exaifnis krazei, kai sparassei auton meta afrou kai mogis apohorei ap' autou syntrivon auton*
verses.translation: And, lo, a spirit taketh him, and he suddenly crieth out; and it teareth him that he foameth again, and bruising him hardly departeth from him.

verses.original: καὶ ἐδεήθην τῶν μαθητῶν σου ἵνα ἐκβάλωσιν αὐτό, καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν.
verses.translit: kai edeithin ton mathiton soy ina ekvalosin auto, kai ouk edynithisan.
verses.translation: And I besought thy disciples to cast him out; and they could not.

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος καὶ διεστραμμένη, ἕως πότε ἔσομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν; προσάγαγε ⸂ὧδε τὸν υἱόν σου⸃.
verses.translit: apokritheis de o Iisous eipen* O genea apistos kai diestrammeni, eos pote esomai pros umas kai anexomai umon; prosagage ode ton yion soy.
verses.translation: And Jesus answering said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you, and suffer you? Bring thy son hither.

verses.original: ἔτι δὲ προσερχομένου αὐτοῦ ἔρρηξεν αὐτὸν τὸ δαιμόνιον καὶ συνεσπάραξεν· ἐπετίμησεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ, καὶ ἰάσατο τὸν παῖδα καὶ ἀπέδωκεν αὐτὸν τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: eti de proserhomenoy autou errixen auton to daimonion kai synesparaxen* epetimisen de o Iisous to pneymati to akatharto, kai iasato ton paida kai apedoken auton to patri autou.
verses.translation: And as he was yet a coming, the devil threw him down, and tare him . And Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the child, and delivered him again to his father.

verses.original: ἐξεπλήσσοντο δὲ πάντες ἐπὶ τῇ μεγαλειότητι τοῦ θεοῦ. Πάντων δὲ θαυμαζόντων ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ⸀ἐποίει εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: exeplissonto de pantes epi te megaleiotiti tou theou. Panton de thaymazonton epi pasin ois epoiei eipen pros tous mathitas autou*
verses.translation: And they were all amazed at the mighty power of God. But while they wondered every one at all things which Jesus did, he said unto his disciples,

verses.original: Θέσθε ὑμεῖς εἰς τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν τοὺς λόγους τούτους, ὁ γὰρ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μέλλει παραδίδοσθαι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων.
verses.translit: Thesthe umeis eis ta ota umon tous logoys toytoys, o gar yios tou anthropoy mellei paradidosthai eis heiras anthropon.
verses.translation: Let these sayings sink down into your ears: for the Son of man shall be delivered into the hands of men.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἠγνόουν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο, καὶ ἦν παρακεκαλυμμένον ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ἵνα μὴ αἴσθωνται αὐτό, καὶ ἐφοβοῦντο ἐρωτῆσαι αὐτὸν περὶ τοῦ ῥήματος τούτου.
verses.translit: oi de egnooyn to Rema touto, kai en parakekalymmenon ap' auton ina me aisthontai auto, kai efovounto erotesai auton peri tou Rimatos toytoy.
verses.translation: But they understood not this saying, and it was hid from them, that they perceived it not: and they feared to ask him of that saying.

verses.original: Εἰσῆλθεν δὲ διαλογισμὸς ἐν αὐτοῖς, τὸ τίς ἂν εἴη μείζων αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Eiselthen de dialogismos en autois, to tis an eii meizon auton.
verses.translation: Then there arose a reasoning among them, which of them should be greatest.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ⸀εἰδὼς τὸν διαλογισμὸν τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν ἐπιλαβόμενος ⸀παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ παρʼ ἑαυτῷ,
verses.translit: o de Iisous eidos ton dialogismon tes kardias auton epilavomenos paidion estisen auto par' eayto,
verses.translation: And Jesus, perceiving the thought of their heart, took a child, and set him by him,

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὃς ⸀ἂν δέξηται τοῦτο τὸ παιδίον ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου ἐμὲ δέχεται, καὶ ὃς ⸁ἂν ἐμὲ δέξηται δέχεται τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με· ὁ γὰρ μικρότερος ἐν πᾶσιν ὑμῖν ὑπάρχων οὗτός ⸀ἐστιν μέγας.
verses.translit: kai eipen autois* Os an dexitai touto to paidion epi to onomati moy eme dehetai, kai os an eme dexitai dehetai ton aposteilanta me* o gar mikroteros en pasin umin uparhon outos estin megas.
verses.translation: And said unto them, Whosoever shall receive this child in my name receiveth me: and whosoever shall receive me receiveth him that sent me: for he that is least among you all, the same shall be great.

verses.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς ⸀δὲ Ἰωάννης εἶπεν· Ἐπιστάτα, εἴδομέν τινα ⸀ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἐκβάλλοντα δαιμόνια, καὶ ⸀ἐκωλύομεν αὐτὸν ὅτι οὐκ ἀκολουθεῖ μεθʼ ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: Apokritheis de Ioannis eipen* Epistata, eidomen tina en to onomati soy ekvallonta daimonia, kai ekolyomen auton oti ouk akoloythei meth' emon.
verses.translation: And John answered and said, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name; and we forbad him, because he followeth not with us.

verses.original: ⸂εἶπεν δὲ⸃ πρὸς αὐτὸν ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ κωλύετε, ὃς γὰρ οὐκ ἔστιν καθʼ ⸂ὑμῶν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν⸃ ἐστιν.
verses.translit: eipen de pros auton o Iisous* Me kolyete, os gar ouk estin kath' umon uper umon estin.
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto him, Forbid him not: for he that is not against us is for us.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι τὰς ἡμέρας τῆς ἀναλήμψεως αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς τὸ ⸀πρόσωπον ⸀ἐστήρισεν τοῦ πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ,
verses.translit: Egeneto de en to symplirousthai tas emeras tes analimpseos autou kai autos to prosopon estirisen tou poreyesthai eis Ieroysalim,
verses.translation: And it came to pass, when the time was come that he should be received up, he stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem,

verses.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν ἀγγέλους πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ. καὶ πορευθέντες εἰσῆλθον εἰς κώμην Σαμαριτῶν, ⸀ὡς ἑτοιμάσαι αὐτῷ·
verses.translit: kai apesteilen aggeloys pro prosopoy autou. kai poreythentes eiselthon eis komin Samariton, os etoimasai auto*
verses.translation: And sent messengers before his face: and they went, and entered into a village of the Samaritans, to make ready for him.

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἐδέξαντο αὐτόν, ὅτι τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ἦν πορευόμενον εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ.
verses.translit: kai ouk edexanto auton, oti to prosopon autou en poreyomenon eis Ieroysalim.
verses.translation: And they did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem.

verses.original: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ⸀μαθηταὶ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωάννης εἶπαν· Κύριε, θέλεις εἴπωμεν πῦρ καταβῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἀναλῶσαι ⸀αὐτούς;
verses.translit: idontes de oi mathitai Iakovos kai Ioannis eipan* Kyrie, theleis eipomen pur katavenai apo tou ouranou kai analosai autoys;
verses.translation: And when his disciples James and John saw this , they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?

verses.original: στραφεὶς δὲ ἐπετίμησεν ⸀αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: strafeis de epetimisen autois.
verses.translation: But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ ἐπορεύθησαν εἰς ἑτέραν κώμην.
verses.translit: kai eporeythisan eis eteran komin.
verses.translation: For the Son of man is not come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them . And they went to another village.

verses.original: ⸀Καὶ πορευομένων αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶπέν τις πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἀκολουθήσω σοι ὅπου ⸀ἐὰν ⸀ἀπέρχῃ.
verses.translit: Kai poreyomenon auton en te odo eipen tis pros auton* Akoloythiso soi opoy ean aperhe.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that, as they went in the way, a certain man said unto him, Lord, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Αἱ ἀλώπεκες φωλεοὺς ἔχουσιν καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνώσεις, ὁ δὲ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἔχει ποῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν κλίνῃ.
verses.translit: kai eipen auto o Iisous* Ai alopekes foleous ehoysin kai ta peteina tou ouranou kataskinoseis, o de yios tou anthropoy ouk ehei pou ten kefalen kline.
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto him, Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς ἕτερον· Ἀκολούθει μοι. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· ⸀Κύριε, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι ⸂ἀπελθόντι πρῶτον⸃ θάψαι τὸν πατέρα μου.
verses.translit: eipen de pros eteron* Akoloythei moi. o de eipen* Kyrie, epitrepson moi apelthonti proton thapsai ton patera moy.
verses.translation: And he said unto another, Follow me. But he said, Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ⸀αὐτῷ· Ἄφες τοὺς νεκροὺς θάψαι τοὺς ἑαυτῶν νεκρούς, σὺ δὲ ἀπελθὼν διάγγελλε τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: eipen de auto* Afes tous nekrous thapsai tous eayton nekroys, su de apelthon diaggelle ten vasileian tou theou.
verses.translation: Jesus said unto him, Let the dead bury their dead: but go thou and preach the kingdom of God.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ καὶ ἕτερος· Ἀκολουθήσω σοι, κύριε· πρῶτον δὲ ἐπίτρεψόν μοι ἀποτάξασθαι τοῖς εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου.
verses.translit: eipen de kai eteros* Akoloythiso soi, kyrie* proton de epitrepson moi apotaxasthai tois eis ton oikon moy.
verses.translation: And another also said, Lord, I will follow thee; but let me first go bid them farewell, which are at home at my house.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ⸂ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃· Οὐδεὶς ἐπιβαλὼν τὴν ⸀χεῖρα ἐπʼ ἄροτρον καὶ βλέπων εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω εὔθετός ἐστιν ⸂τῇ βασιλείᾳ⸃ τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: eipen de o Iisous* Oudeis epivalon ten heira ep' arotron kai vlepon eis ta opiso euthetos estin te vasileia tou theou.
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.

verses.original: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ἀνέδειξεν ὁ κύριος ⸀καὶ ἑτέρους ἑβδομήκοντα ⸀δύο καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς ἀνὰ δύο ⸁δύο πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ εἰς πᾶσαν πόλιν καὶ τόπον οὗ ἤμελλεν αὐτὸς ἔρχεσθαι.
verses.translit: Meta de tauta anedeixen o kyrios kai eteroys evdomikonta dyo kai apesteilen autous ana dyo dyo pro prosopoy autou eis pasan polin kai topon ou emellen autos erhesthai.
verses.translation: After these things the Lord appointed other seventy also, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place, whither he himself would come.

verses.original: ἔλεγεν ⸀δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὁ μὲν θερισμὸς πολύς, οἱ δὲ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι· δεήθητε οὖν τοῦ κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὅπως ⸂ἐργάτας ἐκβάλῃ⸃ εἰς τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: elegen de pros autoys* O men therismos polys, oi de ergatai oligoi* deithite oun tou kyrioy tou therismou opos ergatas ekvale eis ton therismon autou.
verses.translation: Therefore said he unto them, The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he would send forth labourers into his harvest.

verses.original: ὑπάγετε· ⸀ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς ἄρνας ἐν μέσῳ λύκων.
verses.translit: upagete* idou apostello umas os arnas en meso lykon.
verses.translation: Go your ways: behold, I send you forth as lambs among wolves.

verses.original: μὴ βαστάζετε βαλλάντιον, μὴ πήραν, ⸀μὴ ὑποδήματα, καὶ μηδένα κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἀσπάσησθε.
verses.translit: me vastazete vallantion, me piran, me upodimata, kai midena kata ten odon aspasisthe.
verses.translation: Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes: and salute no man by the way.

verses.original: εἰς ἣν δʼ ἂν ⸂εἰσέλθητε οἰκίαν⸃ πρῶτον λέγετε· Εἰρήνη τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ.
verses.translit: eis en d' an eiselthite oikian proton legete* Eirini to oiko toyto.
verses.translation: And into whatsoever house ye enter, first say, Peace be to this house.

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν ⸂ᾖ ἐκεῖ⸃ υἱὸς εἰρήνης, ἐπαναπαήσεται ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν· εἰ δὲ μήγε, ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς ἀνακάμψει.
verses.translit: kai ean e ekei yios eirinis, epanapaisetai ep' auton e eirini umon* ei de mige, ef' umas anakampsei.
verses.translation: And if the son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon it: if not, it shall turn to you again.

verses.original: ἐν αὐτῇ δὲ τῇ οἰκίᾳ μένετε, ἐσθίοντες καὶ πίνοντες τὰ παρʼ αὐτῶν, ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τοῦ μισθοῦ ⸀αὐτοῦ. μὴ μεταβαίνετε ἐξ οἰκίας εἰς οἰκίαν.
verses.translit: en aute de te oikia menete, esthiontes kai pinontes ta par' auton, axios gar o ergatis tou misthou autou. me metavainete ex oikias eis oikian.
verses.translation: And in the same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give: for the labourer is worthy of his hire. Go not from house to house.

verses.original: καὶ εἰς ἣν ἂν πόλιν εἰσέρχησθε καὶ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐσθίετε τὰ παρατιθέμενα ὑμῖν,
verses.translit: kai eis en an polin eiserhisthe kai dehontai umas, esthiete ta paratithemena umin,
verses.translation: And into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you, eat such things as are set before you:

verses.original: καὶ θεραπεύετε τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ ἀσθενεῖς, καὶ λέγετε αὐτοῖς· Ἤγγικεν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: kai therapeyete tous en aute astheneis, kai legete autois* Eggiken ef' umas e vasileia tou theou.
verses.translation: And heal the sick that are therein, and say unto them, The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.

verses.original: εἰς ἣν δʼ ἂν πόλιν ⸀εἰσέλθητε καὶ μὴ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς, ἐξελθόντες εἰς τὰς πλατείας αὐτῆς εἴπατε·
verses.translit: eis en d' an polin eiselthite kai me dehontai umas, exelthontes eis tas plateias autes eipate*
verses.translation: But into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you not, go your ways out into the streets of the same, and say,

verses.original: Καὶ τὸν κονιορτὸν τὸν κολληθέντα ἡμῖν ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ὑμῶν ⸂εἰς τοὺς πόδας⸃ ἀπομασσόμεθα ὑμῖν· πλὴν τοῦτο γινώσκετε ὅτι ⸀ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: Kai ton koniorton ton kollithenta emin ek tes poleos umon eis tous podas apomassometha umin* plen touto ginoskete oti eggiken e vasileia tou theou.
verses.translation: Even the very dust of your city, which cleaveth on us, we do wipe off against you: notwithstanding be ye sure of this, that the kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.

verses.original: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι Σοδόμοις ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἢ τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.
verses.translit: lego umin oti Sodomois en te emera ekeine anektoteron estai e te polei ekeine.
verses.translation: But I say unto you, that it shall be more tolerable in that day for Sodom, than for that city.

verses.original: Οὐαί σοι, Χοραζίν· οὐαί σοι, Βηθσαϊδά· ὅτι εἰ ἐν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ⸀ἐγενήθησαν αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν ὑμῖν, πάλαι ἂν ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σποδῷ ⸀καθήμενοι μετενόησαν.
verses.translit: Ouai soi, Horazin* ouai soi, Vithsaida* oti ei en Tyro kai Sidoni egenithisan ai dynameis ai genomenai en umin, palai an en sakko kai spodo kathimenoi metenoisan.
verses.translation: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon, which have been done in you, they had a great while ago repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

verses.original: πλὴν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν τῇ κρίσει ἢ ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: plen Tyro kai Sidoni anektoteron estai en te krisei e umin.
verses.translation: But it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment, than for you.

verses.original: καὶ σύ, Καφαρναούμ, ⸂μὴ ἕως οὐρανοῦ ὑψωθήσῃ⸃; ἕως ⸀τοῦ ᾅδου ⸀καταβιβασθήσῃ.
verses.translit: kai sy, Kafarnaoym, me eos ouranou upsothise; eos tou adoy katavivasthise.
verses.translation: And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shalt be thrust down to hell.

verses.original: Ὁ ἀκούων ὑμῶν ἐμοῦ ἀκούει, καὶ ὁ ἀθετῶν ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ ἀθετεῖ· ὁ δὲ ἐμὲ ἀθετῶν ἀθετεῖ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με.
verses.translit: O akoyon umon emou akoyei, kai o atheton umas eme athetei* o de eme atheton athetei ton aposteilanta me.
verses.translation: He that heareth you heareth me; and he that despiseth you despiseth me; and he that despiseth me despiseth him that sent me.

verses.original: Ὑπέστρεψαν δὲ οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα ⸀δύο μετὰ χαρᾶς λέγοντες· Κύριε, καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια ὑποτάσσεται ἡμῖν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου.
verses.translit: Upestrepsan de oi evdomikonta dyo meta haras legontes* Kyrie, kai ta daimonia upotassetai emin en to onomati soy.
verses.translation: And the seventy returned again with joy, saying, Lord, even the devils are subject unto us through thy name.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἐθεώρουν τὸν Σατανᾶν ὡς ἀστραπὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πεσόντα.
verses.translit: eipen de autois* Etheoroyn ton Satanan os astrapen ek tou ouranou pesonta.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.

verses.original: ἰδοὺ ⸀δέδωκα ὑμῖν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πατεῖν ἐπάνω ὄφεων καὶ σκορπίων, καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ ἐχθροῦ, καὶ οὐδὲν ὑμᾶς οὐ μὴ ⸀ἀδικήσῃ.
verses.translit: idou dedoka umin ten exoysian tou patein epano ofeon kai skorpion, kai epi pasan ten dynamin tou ehthrou, kai ouden umas ou me adikise.
verses.translation: Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you.

verses.original: πλὴν ἐν τούτῳ μὴ χαίρετε ὅτι τὰ πνεύματα ὑμῖν ὑποτάσσεται, χαίρετε δὲ ὅτι τὰ ὀνόματα ὑμῶν ⸀ἐγγέγραπται ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.
verses.translit: plen en toyto me hairete oti ta pneymata umin upotassetai, hairete de oti ta onomata umon eggegraptai en tois ouranois.
verses.translation: Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.

verses.original: Ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἠγαλλιάσατο ⸀τῷ πνεύματι ⸂τῷ ἁγίῳ⸃ καὶ εἶπεν· Ἐξομολογοῦμαί σοι, πάτερ κύριε τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ἀπέκρυψας ταῦτα ἀπὸ σοφῶν καὶ συνετῶν, καὶ ἀπεκάλυψας αὐτὰ νηπίοις· ναί, ὁ πατήρ, ὅτι οὕτως ⸂εὐδοκία ἐγένετο⸃ ἔμπροσθέν σου.
verses.translit: En aute te ora egalliasato to pneymati to agio kai eipen* Exomologoumai soi, pater kyrie tou ouranou kai tes ges, oti apekrypsas tauta apo sofon kai syneton, kai apekalypsas auta nipiois* nai, o patir, oti outos eudokia egeneto emprosthen soy.
verses.translation: In that hour Jesus rejoiced in spirit, and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes: even so, Father; for so it seemed good in thy sight.

verses.original: ⸀πάντα μοι παρεδόθη ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός μου, καὶ οὐδεὶς γινώσκει τίς ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς εἰ μὴ ὁ πατήρ, καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ πατὴρ εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱὸς καὶ ᾧ ⸀ἐὰν βούληται ὁ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι.
verses.translit: panta moi paredothi upo tou patros moy, kai oudeis ginoskei tis estin o yios ei me o patir, kai tis estin o pater ei me o yios kai o ean voylitai o yios apokalypsai.
verses.translation: All things are delivered to me of my Father: and no man knoweth who the Son is, but the Father; and who the Father is, but the Son, and he to whom the Son will reveal him.

verses.original: Καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς κατʼ ἰδίαν εἶπεν· Μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ οἱ βλέποντες ἃ βλέπετε.
verses.translit: Kai strafeis pros tous mathitas kat' idian eipen* Makarioi oi ofthalmoi oi vlepontes a vlepete.
verses.translation: And he turned him unto his disciples, and said privately, Blessed are the eyes which see the things that ye see:

verses.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ βασιλεῖς ἠθέλησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ ὑμεῖς βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν.
verses.translit: lego gar umin oti polloi profetai kai vasileis ethelisan idein a umeis vlepete kai ouk eidan, kai akousai a akoyete kai ouk ekoysan.
verses.translation: For I tell you, that many prophets and kings have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them ; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them.

verses.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ νομικός τις ἀνέστη ἐκπειράζων ⸀αὐτὸν λέγων· Διδάσκαλε, τί ποιήσας ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;
verses.translit: Kai idou nomikos tis anesti ekpeirazon auton legon* Didaskale, ti poiisas zoen aionion klironomiso;
verses.translation: And, behold, a certain lawyer stood up, and tempted him, saying, Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἐν τῷ νόμῳ τί γέγραπται; πῶς ἀναγινώσκεις;
verses.translit: o de eipen pros auton* En to nomo ti gegraptai; pos anaginoskeis;
verses.translation: He said unto him, What is written in the law? how readest thou?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐξ ὅλης ⸀τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ⸂ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ⸃ σου καὶ ⸂ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ἰσχύϊ⸃ σου καὶ ⸂ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ⸃ σου, καὶ τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen* Agapiseis kyrion ton theon soy ex olis tes kardias soy kai en ole te psyhe soy kai en ole te ishyi soy kai en ole te dianoia soy, kai ton plision soy os seayton.
verses.translation: And he answering said, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and thy neighbour as thyself.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Ὀρθῶς ἀπεκρίθης· τοῦτο ποίει καὶ ζήσῃ.
verses.translit: eipen de auto* Orthos apekrithis* touto poiei kai zise.
verses.translation: And he said unto him, Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ θέλων ⸀δικαιῶσαι ἑαυτὸν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν· Καὶ τίς ἐστίν μου πλησίον;
verses.translit: O de thelon dikaiosai eayton eipen pros ton Iisoun* Kai tis estin moy plision;
verses.translation: But he, willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour?

verses.original: ὑπολαβὼν ⸀δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἄνθρωπός τις κατέβαινεν ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλὴμ εἰς Ἰεριχὼ καὶ λῃσταῖς περιέπεσεν, οἳ καὶ ἐκδύσαντες αὐτὸν καὶ πληγὰς ἐπιθέντες ἀπῆλθον ἀφέντες ⸀ἡμιθανῆ.
verses.translit: upolavon de o Iisous eipen* Anthropos tis katevainen apo Ieroysalem eis Ieriho kai lestais periepesen, oi kai ekdysantes auton kai pligas epithentes apelthon afentes emithane.
verses.translation: And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him , and departed, leaving him half dead.

verses.original: κατὰ συγκυρίαν δὲ ἱερεύς τις κατέβαινεν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ἀντιπαρῆλθεν·
verses.translit: kata sygkyrian de iereys tis katevainen en te odo ekeine, kai idon auton antiparelthen*
verses.translation: And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.

verses.original: ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ ⸀Λευίτης κατὰ τὸν τόπον ἐλθὼν καὶ ἰδὼν ἀντιπαρῆλθεν.
verses.translit: omoios de kai Leyitis kata ton topon elthon kai idon antiparelthen.
verses.translation: And likewise a Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked on him , and passed by on the other side.

verses.original: Σαμαρίτης δέ τις ὁδεύων ἦλθεν κατʼ αὐτὸν καὶ ⸀ἰδὼν ἐσπλαγχνίσθη,
verses.translit: Samaritis de tis odeyon elthen kat' auton kai idon esplaghnisthi,
verses.translation: But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him ,

verses.original: καὶ προσελθὼν κατέδησεν τὰ τραύματα αὐτοῦ ἐπιχέων ἔλαιον καὶ οἶνον, ἐπιβιβάσας δὲ αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ ἴδιον κτῆνος ἤγαγεν αὐτὸν εἰς πανδοχεῖον καὶ ἐπεμελήθη αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai proselthon katedisen ta traymata autou epiheon elaion kai oinon, epivivasas de auton epi to idion ktenos egagen auton eis pandoheion kai epemelithi autou.
verses.translation: And went to him , and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν ⸀αὔριον ἐκβαλὼν ⸂δύο δηνάρια ἔδωκεν⸃ τῷ πανδοχεῖ καὶ ⸀εἶπεν· Ἐπιμελήθητι αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὅ τι ἂν προσδαπανήσῃς ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ ἐπανέρχεσθαί με ἀποδώσω σοι.
verses.translit: kai epi ten aurion ekvalon dyo dinaria edoken to pandohei kai eipen* Epimelithiti autou, kai o ti an prosdapanises ego en to epanerhesthai me apodoso soi.
verses.translation: And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.

verses.original: ⸀τίς τούτων τῶν τριῶν πλησίον δοκεῖ σοι γεγονέναι τοῦ ἐμπεσόντος εἰς τοὺς λῃστάς;
verses.translit: tis toyton ton trion plision dokei soi gegonenai tou empesontos eis tous lestas;
verses.translation: Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ὁ ποιήσας τὸ ἔλεος μετʼ αὐτοῦ. εἶπεν ⸀δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πορεύου καὶ σὺ ποίει ὁμοίως.
verses.translit: o de eipen* O poiisas to eleos met' autou. eipen de auto o Iisous* Poreyoy kai su poiei omoios.
verses.translation: And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.

verses.original: ⸂Ἐν δὲ⸃ τῷ πορεύεσθαι ⸀αὐτοὺς αὐτὸς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς κώμην τινά· γυνὴ δέ τις ὀνόματι Μάρθα ὑπεδέξατο ⸀αὐτὸν.
verses.translit: En de to poreyesthai autous autos eiselthen eis komin tina* gyne de tis onomati Martha upedexato auton.
verses.translation: Now it came to pass, as they went, that he entered into a certain village: and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.

verses.original: καὶ τῇδε ἦν ἀδελφὴ καλουμένη ⸀Μαριάμ, ἣ καὶ ⸂παρακαθεσθεῖσα πρὸς⸃ τοὺς πόδας τοῦ ⸀Ἰησοῦ ἤκουεν τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai tede en adelfe kaloymeni Mariam, e kai parakathestheisa pros tous podas tou Iisou ekoyen ton logon autou.
verses.translation: And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word.

verses.original: ἡ δὲ Μάρθα περιεσπᾶτο περὶ πολλὴν διακονίαν· ἐπιστᾶσα δὲ εἶπεν· Κύριε, οὐ μέλει σοι ὅτι ἡ ἀδελφή μου μόνην με ⸀κατέλειπεν διακονεῖν; ⸀εἰπὲ οὖν αὐτῇ ἵνα μοι συναντιλάβηται.
verses.translit: e de Martha periespato peri pollen diakonian* epistasa de eipen* Kyrie, ou melei soi oti e adelfi moy monin me kateleipen diakonein; eipe oun aute ina moi synantilavitai.
verses.translation: But Martha was cumbered about much serving, and came to him, and said, Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ ⸀κύριος· Μάρθα Μάρθα, μεριμνᾷς καὶ ⸀θορυβάζῃ περὶ πολλά,
verses.translit: apokritheis de eipen aute o kyrios* Martha Martha, merimnas kai thoryvaze peri polla,
verses.translation: And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things:

verses.original: ⸂ὀλίγων δέ ἐστιν χρεία ἢ ἑνός⸃· ⸂Μαριὰμ γὰρ⸃ τὴν ἀγαθὴν μερίδα ἐξελέξατο ἥτις οὐκ ἀφαιρεθήσεται ⸀αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: oligon de estin hreia e enos* Mariam gar ten agathen merida exelexato etis ouk afairethisetai autes.
verses.translation: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν τόπῳ τινὶ προσευχόμενον, ὡς ἐπαύσατο, εἶπέν τις τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν· Κύριε, δίδαξον ἡμᾶς προσεύχεσθαι, καθὼς καὶ Ἰωάννης ἐδίδαξεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Kai egeneto en to einai auton en topo tini proseyhomenon, os epaysato, eipen tis ton mathiton autou pros auton* Kyrie, didaxon emas proseyhesthai, kathos kai Ioannis edidaxen tous mathitas autou.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that, as he was praying in a certain place, when he ceased, one of his disciples said unto him, Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ὅταν προσεύχησθε, λέγετε· ⸀Πάτερ, ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου· ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία ⸀σου·
verses.translit: eipen de autois* Otan proseyhisthe, legete* Pater, agiasthito to onoma soy* eltheto e vasileia soy*
verses.translation: And he said unto them, When ye pray, say, Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth.

verses.original: τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δίδου ἡμῖν τὸ καθʼ ἡμέραν·
verses.translit: ton arton emon ton epioysion didoy emin to kath' emeran*
verses.translation: Give us day by day our daily bread.

verses.original: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, καὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ ἀφίομεν παντὶ ὀφείλοντι ἡμῖν· καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς ⸀πειρασμόν.
verses.translit: kai afes emin tas amartias emon, kai gar autoi afiomen panti ofeilonti emin* kai me eisenegkes emas eis peirasmon.
verses.translation: And forgive us our sins; for we also forgive every one that is indebted to us. And lead us not into temptation; but deliver us from evil.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τίς ἐξ ὑμῶν ἕξει φίλον καὶ πορεύσεται πρὸς αὐτὸν μεσονυκτίου καὶ εἴπῃ αὐτῷ· Φίλε, χρῆσόν μοι τρεῖς ἄρτους,
verses.translit: Kai eipen pros autoys* Tis ex umon exei filon kai poreysetai pros auton mesonyktioy kai eipe auto* File, hreson moi treis artoys,
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Which of you shall have a friend, and shall go unto him at midnight, and say unto him, Friend, lend me three loaves;

verses.original: ἐπειδὴ φίλος ⸀μου παρεγένετο ἐξ ὁδοῦ πρός με καὶ οὐκ ἔχω ὃ παραθήσω αὐτῷ·
verses.translit: epeide filos moy paregeneto ex odou pros me kai ouk eho o parathiso auto*
verses.translation: For a friend of mine in his journey is come to me, and I have nothing to set before him?

verses.original: κἀκεῖνος ἔσωθεν ἀποκριθεὶς εἴπῃ· Μή μοι κόπους πάρεχε· ἤδη ἡ θύρα κέκλεισται, καὶ τὰ παιδία μου μετʼ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὴν κοίτην εἰσίν· οὐ δύναμαι ἀναστὰς δοῦναί σοι.
verses.translit: kakeinos esothen apokritheis eipe* Mi moi kopoys parehe* edi e thyra kekleistai, kai ta paidia moy met' emou eis ten koitin eisin* ou dynamai anastas dounai soi.
verses.translation: And he from within shall answer and say, Trouble me not: the door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot rise and give thee.

verses.original: λέγω ὑμῖν, εἰ καὶ οὐ δώσει αὐτῷ ἀναστὰς διὰ τὸ εἶναι ⸂φίλον αὐτοῦ⸃, διά γε τὴν ἀναίδειαν αὐτοῦ ἐγερθεὶς δώσει αὐτῷ ⸀ὅσων χρῄζει.
verses.translit: lego umin, ei kai ou dosei auto anastas dia to einai filon autou, dia ge ten anaideian autou egertheis dosei auto oson hrezei.
verses.translation: I say unto you, Though he will not rise and give him, because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needeth.

verses.original: Κἀγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω, αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν·
verses.translit: Kago umin lego, aiteite, kai dothisetai umin* ziteite, kai eurisete* kroyete, kai anoigisetai umin*
verses.translation: And I say unto you, Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.

verses.original: πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει, καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει, καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.
verses.translit: pas gar o aiton lamvanei, kai o ziton euriskei, kai to kroyonti anoigisetai.
verses.translation: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.

verses.original: τίνα δὲ ⸀ἐξ ὑμῶν τὸν πατέρα αἰτήσει ὁ ⸀υἱὸς ἰχθύν, ⸀καὶ ἀντὶ ἰχθύος ὄφιν ⸂αὐτῷ ἐπιδώσει⸃;
verses.translit: tina de ex umon ton patera aitisei o yios ihthyn, kai anti ihthyos ofin auto epidosei;
verses.translation: If a son shall ask bread of any of you that is a father, will he give him a stone? or if he ask a fish, will he for a fish give him a serpent?

verses.original: ἢ καὶ ⸀αἰτήσει ᾠόν, ⸀ἐπιδώσει αὐτῷ σκορπίον;
verses.translit: e kai aitisei oon, epidosei auto skorpion;
verses.translation: Or if he shall ask an egg, will he offer him a scorpion?

verses.original: εἰ οὖν ὑμεῖς πονηροὶ ὑπάρχοντες οἴδατε δόματα ἀγαθὰ διδόναι τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὁ πατὴρ ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ δώσει πνεῦμα ἅγιον τοῖς αἰτοῦσιν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: ei oun umeis poniroi uparhontes oidate domata agatha didonai tois teknois umon, poso mallon o pater o ex ouranou dosei pneuma agion tois aitousin auton.
verses.translation: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?

verses.original: Καὶ ἦν ἐκβάλλων ⸀δαιμόνιον κωφόν· ἐγένετο δὲ τοῦ δαιμονίου ἐξελθόντος ἐλάλησεν ὁ κωφός. καὶ ἐθαύμασαν οἱ ὄχλοι·
verses.translit: Kai en ekvallon daimonion kofon* egeneto de tou daimonioy exelthontos elalisen o kofos. kai ethaymasan oi ohloi*
verses.translation: And he was casting out a devil, and it was dumb. And it came to pass, when the devil was gone out, the dumb spake; and the people wondered.

verses.original: τινὲς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶπον· Ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ⸀τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια·
verses.translit: tines de ex auton eipon* En Veelzevoul to arhonti ton daimonion ekvallei ta daimonia*
verses.translation: But some of them said, He casteth out devils through Beelzebub the chief of the devils.

verses.original: ἕτεροι δὲ πειράζοντες σημεῖον ⸂ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐζήτουν παρʼ αὐτοῦ⸃.
verses.translit: eteroi de peirazontes simeion ex ouranou ezitoyn par' autou.
verses.translation: And others, tempting him , sought of him a sign from heaven.

verses.original: αὐτὸς δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὰ διανοήματα εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πᾶσα βασιλεία ἐφʼ ἑαυτὴν διαμερισθεῖσα ἐρημοῦται, καὶ οἶκος ἐπὶ οἶκον πίπτει.
verses.translit: autos de eidos auton ta dianoimata eipen autois* Pasa vasileia ef' eayten diameristheisa erimoutai, kai oikos epi oikon piptei.
verses.translation: But he, knowing their thoughts, said unto them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and a house divided against a house falleth.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐφʼ ἑαυτὸν διεμερίσθη, πῶς σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ; ὅτι λέγετε ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλειν με τὰ δαιμόνια.
verses.translit: ei de kai o Satanas ef' eayton diemeristhi, pos stathisetai e vasileia autou; oti legete en Veelzevoul ekvallein me ta daimonia.
verses.translation: If Satan also be divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? because ye say that I cast out devils through Beelzebub.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν; διὰ τοῦτο ⸂αὐτοὶ ὑμῶν κριταὶ⸃ ἔσονται.
verses.translit: ei de ego en Veelzevoul ekvallo ta daimonia, oi yioi umon en tini ekvalloysin; dia touto autoi umon kritai esontai.
verses.translation: And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your sons cast them out? therefore shall they be your judges.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ἐν δακτύλῳ ⸀θεοῦ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: ei de en daktylo theou ekvallo ta daimonia, ara efthasen ef' umas e vasileia tou theou.
verses.translation: But if I with the finger of God cast out devils, no doubt the kingdom of God is come upon you.

verses.original: ὅταν ὁ ἰσχυρὸς καθωπλισμένος φυλάσσῃ τὴν ἑαυτοῦ αὐλήν, ἐν εἰρήνῃ ἐστὶν τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: otan o ishyros kathoplismenos fylasse ten eaytou aulin, en eirine estin ta uparhonta autou*
verses.translation: When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, his goods are in peace:

verses.original: ἐπὰν ⸀δὲ ἰσχυρότερος ⸀αὐτοῦ ἐπελθὼν νικήσῃ αὐτόν, τὴν πανοπλίαν αὐτοῦ αἴρει ἐφʼ ᾗ ἐπεποίθει, καὶ τὰ σκῦλα αὐτοῦ διαδίδωσιν.
verses.translit: epan de ishyroteros autou epelthon nikise auton, ten panoplian autou airei ef' e epepoithei, kai ta skula autou diadidosin.
verses.translation: But when a stronger than he shall come upon him, and overcome him, he taketh from him all his armour wherein he trusted, and divideth his spoils.

verses.original: ὁ μὴ ὢν μετʼ ἐμοῦ κατʼ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετʼ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει.
verses.translit: o me on met' emou kat' emou estin, kai o me synagon met' emou skorpizei.
verses.translation: He that is not with me is against me: and he that gathereth not with me scattereth.

verses.original: Ὅταν τὸ ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα ἐξέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, διέρχεται διʼ ἀνύδρων τόπων ζητοῦν ἀνάπαυσιν, καὶ μὴ ⸀εὑρίσκον λέγει· Ὑποστρέψω εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου ὅθεν ἐξῆλθον·
verses.translit: Otan to akatharton pneuma exelthe apo tou anthropoy, dierhetai di' anydron topon zitoun anapaysin, kai me euriskon legei* Upostrepso eis ton oikon moy othen exelthon*
verses.translation: When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest; and finding none, he saith, I will return unto my house whence I came out.

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθὸν ⸀εὑρίσκει σεσαρωμένον καὶ κεκοσμημένον.
verses.translit: kai elthon euriskei sesaromenon kai kekosmimenon.
verses.translation: And when he cometh, he findeth it swept and garnished.

verses.original: τότε πορεύεται καὶ παραλαμβάνει ⸂ἕτερα πνεύματα πονηρότερα ἑαυτοῦ ἑπτά⸃, καὶ ⸀εἰσελθόντα κατοικεῖ ἐκεῖ, καὶ γίνεται τὰ ἔσχατα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκείνου χείρονα τῶν πρώτων.
verses.translit: tote poreyetai kai paralamvanei etera pneymata ponirotera eaytou epta, kai eiselthonta katoikei ekei, kai ginetai ta eshata tou anthropoy ekeinoy heirona ton proton.
verses.translation: Then goeth he, and taketh to him seven other spirits more wicked than himself; and they enter in, and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ λέγειν αὐτὸν ταῦτα ἐπάρασά τις ⸂φωνὴν γυνὴ⸃ ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακαρία ἡ κοιλία ἡ βαστάσασά σε καὶ μαστοὶ οὓς ἐθήλασας·
verses.translit: Egeneto de en to legein auton tauta eparasa tis fonen gyne ek tou ohloy eipen auto* Makaria e koilia e vastasasa se kai mastoi ous ethilasas*
verses.translation: And it came to pass, as he spake these things, a certain woman of the company lifted up her voice, and said unto him, Blessed is the womb that bare thee, and the paps which thou hast sucked.

verses.original: αὐτὸς δὲ εἶπεν· ⸀Μενοῦν μακάριοι οἱ ἀκούοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ⸀φυλάσσοντες.
verses.translit: autos de eipen* Menoun makarioi oi akoyontes ton logon tou theou kai fylassontes.
verses.translation: But he said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.

verses.original: Τῶν δὲ ὄχλων ἐπαθροιζομένων ἤρξατο λέγειν· Ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ⸀γενεὰ πονηρά ἐστιν· σημεῖον ⸀ζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον ⸀Ἰωνᾶ.
verses.translit: Ton de ohlon epathroizomenon erxato legein* E genea auti genea ponira estin* simeion zitei, kai simeion ou dothisetai aute ei me to simeion Iona.
verses.translation: And when the people were gathered thick together, he began to say, This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet.

verses.original: καθὼς γὰρ ἐγένετο ⸀Ἰωνᾶς ⸂τοῖς Νινευίταις σημεῖον⸃, οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ.
verses.translit: kathos gar egeneto Ionas tois Nineyitais simeion, outos estai kai o yios tou anthropoy te genea tayte.
verses.translation: For as Jonas was a sign unto the Ninevites, so shall also the Son of man be to this generation.

verses.original: βασίλισσα νότου ἐγερθήσεται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῶν ἀνδρῶν τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινεῖ αὐτούς· ὅτι ἦλθεν ἐκ τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς ἀκοῦσαι τὴν σοφίαν Σολομῶνος, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Σολομῶνος ὧδε.
verses.translit: vasilissa notoy egerthisetai en te krisei meta ton andron tes geneas taytis kai katakrinei autoys* oti elthen ek ton peraton tes ges akousai ten sofian Solomonos, kai idou pleion Solomonos ode.
verses.translation: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and condemn them: for she came from the utmost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

verses.original: ἄνδρες ⸀Νινευῖται ἀναστήσονται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτήν· ὅτι μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε.
verses.translit: andres Nineyitai anastisontai en te krisei meta tes geneas taytis kai katakrinousin autin* oti metenoisan eis to kirygma Iona, kai idou pleion Iona ode.
verses.translation: The men of Nineve shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here.

verses.original: ⸀Οὐδεὶς λύχνον ἅψας εἰς κρύπτην τίθησιν οὐδὲ ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον ἀλλʼ ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν, ἵνα οἱ εἰσπορευόμενοι τὸ ⸀φέγγος βλέπωσιν.
verses.translit: Oudeis lyhnon apsas eis kryptin tithisin oude upo ton modion all' epi ten lyhnian, ina oi eisporeyomenoi to feggos vleposin.
verses.translation: No man, when he hath lighted a candle, putteth it in a secret place, neither under a bushel, but on a candlestick, that they which come in may see the light.

verses.original: ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός ⸀σου. ⸀ὅταν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς ᾖ, καὶ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινόν ἐστιν· ἐπὰν δὲ πονηρὸς ᾖ, καὶ τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινόν.
verses.translit: o lyhnos tou somatos estin o ofthalmos soy. otan o ofthalmos soy aplous e, kai olon to soma soy foteinon estin* epan de poniros e, kai to soma soy skoteinon.
verses.translation: The light of the body is the eye: therefore when thine eye is single, thy whole body also is full of light; but when thine eye is evil, thy body also is full of darkness.

verses.original: σκόπει οὖν μὴ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν.
verses.translit: skopei oun me to fos to en soi skotos estin.
verses.translation: Take heed therefore that the light which is in thee be not darkness.

verses.original: εἰ οὖν τὸ σῶμά σου ὅλον φωτεινόν, μὴ ἔχον ⸂μέρος τι⸃ σκοτεινόν, ἔσται φωτεινὸν ὅλον ὡς ὅταν ὁ λύχνος τῇ ἀστραπῇ φωτίζῃ σε.
verses.translit: ei oun to soma soy olon foteinon, me ehon meros ti skoteinon, estai foteinon olon os otan o lyhnos te astrape fotize se.
verses.translation: If thy whole body therefore be full of light, having no part dark, the whole shall be full of light, as when the bright shining of a candle doth give thee light.

verses.original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ λαλῆσαι ⸀ἐρωτᾷ αὐτὸν ⸀Φαρισαῖος ὅπως ἀριστήσῃ παρʼ αὐτῷ· εἰσελθὼν δὲ ἀνέπεσεν.
verses.translit: En de to lalesai erota auton Farisaios opos aristise par' auto* eiselthon de anepesen.
verses.translation: And as he spake, a certain Pharisee besought him to dine with him: and he went in, and sat down to meat.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Φαρισαῖος ἰδὼν ἐθαύμασεν ὅτι οὐ πρῶτον ἐβαπτίσθη πρὸ τοῦ ἀρίστου.
verses.translit: o de Farisaios idon ethaymasen oti ou proton evaptisthi pro tou aristoy.
verses.translation: And when the Pharisee saw it , he marvelled that he had not first washed before dinner.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν· Νῦν ὑμεῖς οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τοῦ πίνακος καθαρίζετε, τὸ δὲ ἔσωθεν ὑμῶν γέμει ἁρπαγῆς καὶ πονηρίας.
verses.translit: eipen de o kyrios pros auton* Nun umeis oi Farisaioi to exothen tou potirioy kai tou pinakos katharizete, to de esothen umon gemei arpages kai ponirias.
verses.translation: And the Lord said unto him, Now do ye Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and the platter; but your inward part is full of ravening and wickedness.

verses.original: ἄφρονες, οὐχ ὁ ποιήσας τὸ ἔξωθεν καὶ τὸ ἔσωθεν ἐποίησεν;
verses.translit: afrones, ouh o poiisas to exothen kai to esothen epoiisen;
verses.translation: Ye fools, did not he that made that which is without make that which is within also?

verses.original: πλὴν τὰ ἐνόντα δότε ἐλεημοσύνην, καὶ ἰδοὺ πάντα καθαρὰ ὑμῖν ἐστιν.
verses.translit: plen ta enonta dote eleimosynin, kai idou panta kathara umin estin.
verses.translation: But rather give alms of such things as ye have; and, behold, all things are clean unto you.

verses.original: Ἀλλὰ οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ πήγανον καὶ πᾶν λάχανον, καὶ παρέρχεσθε τὴν κρίσιν καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ θεοῦ· ταῦτα ⸀δὲ ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ ⸀παρεῖναι.
verses.translit: Alla ouai umin tois Farisaiois, oti apodekatoute to edyosmon kai to piganon kai pan lahanon, kai parerhesthe ten krisin kai ten agapin tou theou* tauta de edei poiesai kakeina me pareinai.
verses.translation: But woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.

verses.original: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς Φαρισαίοις, ὅτι ἀγαπᾶτε τὴν πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς.
verses.translit: ouai umin tois Farisaiois, oti agapate ten protokathedrian en tais synagogais kai tous aspasmous en tais agorais.
verses.translation: Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets.

verses.original: οὐαὶ ⸀ὑμῖν, ὅτι ἐστὲ ὡς τὰ μνημεῖα τὰ ἄδηλα, καὶ οἱ ἄνθρωποι ⸀οἱ περιπατοῦντες ἐπάνω οὐκ οἴδασιν.
verses.translit: ouai umin, oti este os ta mnimeia ta adila, kai oi anthropoi oi peripatountes epano ouk oidasin.
verses.translation: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are as graves which appear not, and the men that walk over them are not aware of them.

verses.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δέ τις τῶν νομικῶν λέγει αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, ταῦτα λέγων καὶ ἡμᾶς ὑβρίζεις.
verses.translit: Apokritheis de tis ton nomikon legei auto* Didaskale, tauta legon kai emas uvrizeis.
verses.translation: Then answered one of the lawyers, and said unto him, Master, thus saying thou reproachest us also.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς οὐαί, ὅτι φορτίζετε τοὺς ἀνθρώπους φορτία δυσβάστακτα, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἑνὶ τῶν δακτύλων ὑμῶν οὐ προσψαύετε τοῖς φορτίοις.
verses.translit: o de eipen* Kai umin tois nomikois ouai, oti fortizete tous anthropoys fortia dysvastakta, kai autoi eni ton daktylon umon ou prospsayete tois fortiois.
verses.translation: And he said, Woe unto you also, ye lawyers! for ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers.

verses.original: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν προφητῶν οἱ δὲ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτούς.
verses.translit: ouai umin, oti oikodomeite ta mnimeia ton profiton oi de pateres umon apekteinan autoys.
verses.translation: Woe unto you! for ye build the sepulchres of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.

verses.original: ἄρα ⸂μάρτυρές ἐστε⸃ καὶ συνευδοκεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν, ὅτι αὐτοὶ μὲν ἀπέκτειναν αὐτοὺς ὑμεῖς δὲ ⸀οἰκοδομεῖτε.
