verses.translit: ara martyres este kai syneydokeite tois ergois ton pateron umon, oti autoi men apekteinan autous umeis de oikodomeite.
verses.translation: Truly ye bear witness that ye allow the deeds of your fathers: for they indeed killed them, and ye build their sepulchres.

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἡ σοφία τοῦ θεοῦ εἶπεν· Ἀποστελῶ εἰς αὐτοὺς προφήτας καὶ ἀποστόλους, καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀποκτενοῦσιν καὶ ⸀διώξουσιν,
verses.translit: dia touto kai e sofia tou theou eipen* Apostelo eis autous profitas kai apostoloys, kai ex auton apoktenousin kai dioxoysin,
verses.translation: Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they shall slay and persecute:

verses.original: ἵνα ἐκζητηθῇ τὸ αἷμα πάντων τῶν προφητῶν τὸ ἐκκεχυμένον ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης,
verses.translit: ina ekzitithe to aima panton ton profiton to ekkehymenon apo katavoles kosmoy apo tes geneas taytis,
verses.translation: That the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;

verses.original: ⸀ἀπὸ αἵματος Ἅβελ ⸀ἕως αἵματος Ζαχαρίου τοῦ ἀπολομένου μεταξὺ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καὶ τοῦ οἴκου· ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐκζητηθήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης.
verses.translit: apo aimatos Avel eos aimatos Zaharioy tou apolomenoy metaxu tou thysiastirioy kai tou oikoy* nai, lego umin, ekzitithisetai apo tes geneas taytis.
verses.translation: From the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, which perished between the altar and the temple: verily I say unto you, It shall be required of this generation.

verses.original: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς νομικοῖς, ὅτι ἤρατε τὴν κλεῖδα τῆς γνώσεως· αὐτοὶ οὐκ εἰσήλθατε καὶ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἐκωλύσατε.
verses.translit: ouai umin tois nomikois, oti erate ten kleida tes gnoseos* autoi ouk eisilthate kai tous eiserhomenoys ekolysate.
verses.translation: Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.

verses.original: ⸂Κἀκεῖθεν ἐξελθόντος αὐτοῦ⸃ ἤρξαντο οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι δεινῶς ἐνέχειν καὶ ἀποστοματίζειν αὐτὸν περὶ πλειόνων,
verses.translit: Kakeithen exelthontos autou erxanto oi grammateis kai oi Farisaioi deinos enehein kai apostomatizein auton peri pleionon,
verses.translation: And as he said these things unto them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to urge him vehemently, and to provoke him to speak of many things:

verses.original: ἐνεδρεύοντες ⸀αὐτὸν θηρεῦσαί τι ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ⸀αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: enedreyontes auton thireusai ti ek tou stomatos autou.
verses.translation: Laying wait for him, and seeking to catch something out of his mouth, that they might accuse him.

verses.original: Ἐν οἷς ἐπισυναχθεισῶν τῶν μυριάδων τοῦ ὄχλου, ὥστε καταπατεῖν ἀλλήλους, ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ πρῶτον· Προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης, ⸂ἥτις ἐστὶν ὑπόκρισις, τῶν Φαρισαίων⸃.
verses.translit: En ois episynahtheison ton myriadon tou ohloy, oste katapatein alliloys, erxato legein pros tous mathitas autou proton* Prosehete eaytois apo tes zymis, etis estin upokrisis, ton Farisaion.
verses.translation: In the mean time, when there were gathered together an innumerable multitude of people, insomuch that they trode one upon another, he began to say unto his disciples first of all, Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

verses.original: οὐδὲν δὲ συγκεκαλυμμένον ἐστὶν ὃ οὐκ ἀποκαλυφθήσεται, καὶ κρυπτὸν ὃ οὐ γνωσθήσεται.
verses.translit: ouden de sygkekalymmenon estin o ouk apokalyfthisetai, kai krypton o ou gnosthisetai.
verses.translation: For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known.

verses.original: ἀνθʼ ὧν ὅσα ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ εἴπατε ἐν τῷ φωτὶ ἀκουσθήσεται, καὶ ὃ πρὸς τὸ οὖς ἐλαλήσατε ἐν τοῖς ταμείοις κηρυχθήσεται ἐπὶ τῶν δωμάτων.
verses.translit: anth' on osa en te skotia eipate en to foti akoysthisetai, kai o pros to ous elalisate en tois tameiois kiryhthisetai epi ton domaton.
verses.translation: Therefore whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness shall be heard in the light; and that which ye have spoken in the ear in closets shall be proclaimed upon the housetops.

verses.original: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν τοῖς φίλοις μου, μὴ φοβηθῆτε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποκτεινόντων τὸ σῶμα καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα μὴ ἐχόντων περισσότερόν τι ποιῆσαι.
verses.translit: Lego de umin tois filois moy, me fovithete apo ton apokteinonton to soma kai meta tauta me ehonton perissoteron ti poiesai.
verses.translation: And I say unto you my friends, Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.

verses.original: ὑποδείξω δὲ ὑμῖν τίνα φοβηθῆτε· φοβήθητε τὸν μετὰ τὸ ἀποκτεῖναι ⸂ἔχοντα ἐξουσίαν⸃ ἐμβαλεῖν εἰς τὴν γέενναν· ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, τοῦτον φοβήθητε.
verses.translit: upodeixo de umin tina fovithete* fovithite ton meta to apokteinai ehonta exoysian emvalein eis ten geennan* nai, lego umin, touton fovithite.
verses.translation: But I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.

verses.original: οὐχὶ πέντε στρουθία ⸀πωλοῦνται ἀσσαρίων δύο; καὶ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔστιν ἐπιλελησμένον ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: ouhi pente stroythia polountai assarion dyo; kai en ex auton ouk estin epilelismenon enopion tou theou.
verses.translation: Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God?

verses.original: ἀλλὰ καὶ αἱ τρίχες τῆς κεφαλῆς ὑμῶν πᾶσαι ἠρίθμηνται· ⸀μὴ φοβεῖσθε· πολλῶν στρουθίων διαφέρετε.
verses.translit: alla kai ai trihes tes kefales umon pasai erithmintai* me foveisthe* pollon stroythion diaferete.
verses.translation: But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows.

verses.original: Λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, πᾶς ὃς ἂν ⸀ὁμολογήσῃ ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὁμολογήσει ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ·
verses.translit: Lego de umin, pas os an omologise en emoi emprosthen ton anthropon, kai o yios tou anthropoy omologisei en auto emprosthen ton aggelon tou theou*
verses.translation: Also I say unto you, Whosoever shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of man also confess before the angels of God:

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀρνησάμενός με ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπαρνηθήσεται ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: o de arnisamenos me enopion ton anthropon aparnithisetai enopion ton aggelon tou theou.
verses.translation: But he that denieth me before men shall be denied before the angels of God.

verses.original: καὶ πᾶς ὃς ἐρεῖ λόγον εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ τῷ δὲ εἰς τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα βλασφημήσαντι οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται.
verses.translit: kai pas os erei logon eis ton yion tou anthropoy, afethisetai auto to de eis to agion pneuma vlasfimisanti ouk afethisetai.
verses.translation: And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Ghost it shall not be forgiven.

verses.original: ὅταν δὲ ⸀εἰσφέρωσιν ὑμᾶς ἐπὶ τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας, μὴ ⸀μεριμνήσητε πῶς ⸂ἢ τί⸃ ἀπολογήσησθε ἢ τί εἴπητε·
verses.translit: otan de eisferosin umas epi tas synagogas kai tas arhas kai tas exoysias, me merimnisite pos e ti apologisisthe e ti eipite*
verses.translation: And when they bring you unto the synagogues, and unto magistrates, and powers, take ye no thought how or what thing ye shall answer, or what ye shall say:

verses.original: τὸ γὰρ ἅγιον πνεῦμα διδάξει ὑμᾶς ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἃ δεῖ εἰπεῖν.
verses.translit: to gar agion pneuma didaxei umas en aute te ora a dei eipein.
verses.translation: For the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δέ τις ⸂ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου αὐτῷ⸃· Διδάσκαλε, εἰπὲ τῷ ἀδελφῷ μου μερίσασθαι μετʼ ἐμοῦ τὴν κληρονομίαν.
verses.translit: Eipen de tis ek tou ohloy auto* Didaskale, eipe to adelfo moy merisasthai met' emou ten klironomian.
verses.translation: And one of the company said unto him, Master, speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἄνθρωπε, τίς με κατέστησεν ⸀κριτὴν ἢ μεριστὴν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς;
verses.translit: o de eipen auto* Anthrope, tis me katestisen kriten e meristen ef' umas;
verses.translation: And he said unto him, Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὁρᾶτε καὶ φυλάσσεσθε ἀπὸ ⸀πάσης πλεονεξίας, ὅτι οὐκ ἐν τῷ περισσεύειν τινὶ ἡ ζωὴ ⸀αὐτοῦ ἐστιν ἐκ τῶν ὑπαρχόντων ⸀αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: eipen de pros autoys* Orate kai fylassesthe apo pasis pleonexias, oti ouk en to perisseyein tini e zoe autou estin ek ton uparhonton auto.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγων· Ἀνθρώπου τινὸς πλουσίου εὐφόρησεν ἡ χώρα.
verses.translit: eipen de paravolen pros autous legon* Anthropoy tinos ploysioy euforisen e hora.
verses.translation: And he spake a parable unto them, saying, The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully:

verses.original: καὶ διελογίζετο ἐν ⸀ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Τί ποιήσω, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχω ποῦ συνάξω τοὺς καρπούς μου;
verses.translit: kai dielogizeto en eayto legon* Ti poiiso, oti ouk eho pou synaxo tous karpoys moy;
verses.translation: And he thought within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits?

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν· Τοῦτο ποιήσω· καθελῶ μου τὰς ἀποθήκας καὶ μείζονας οἰκοδομήσω, καὶ συνάξω ἐκεῖ πάντα ⸂τὸν σῖτον⸃ καὶ τὰ ἀγαθά μου,
verses.translit: kai eipen* Touto poiiso* kathelo moy tas apothikas kai meizonas oikodomiso, kai synaxo ekei panta ton siton kai ta agatha moy,
verses.translation: And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods.

verses.original: καὶ ἐρῶ τῇ ψυχῇ μου· Ψυχή, ἔχεις πολλὰ ἀγαθὰ κείμενα εἰς ἔτη πολλά· ἀναπαύου, φάγε, πίε, εὐφραίνου.
verses.translit: kai ero te psyhe moy* Psyhi, eheis polla agatha keimena eis eti polla* anapayoy, fage, pie, eufrainoy.
verses.translation: And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ θεός· ⸀Ἄφρων, ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ τὴν ψυχήν σου ⸀ἀπαιτοῦσιν ἀπὸ σοῦ· ἃ δὲ ἡτοίμασας, τίνι ἔσται;
verses.translit: eipen de auto o theos* Afron, tayte te nykti ten psyhin soy apaitousin apo sou* a de etoimasas, tini estai;
verses.translation: But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?

verses.original: οὕτως ὁ θησαυρίζων ⸀ἑαυτῷ καὶ μὴ εἰς θεὸν πλουτῶν.
verses.translit: outos o thisayrizon eayto kai me eis theon ployton.
verses.translation: So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Διὰ τοῦτο ⸂λέγω ὑμῖν⸃, μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ⸀ψυχῇ τί φάγητε, μηδὲ τῷ ⸀σώματι τί ἐνδύσησθε.
verses.translit: Eipen de pros tous mathitas autou* Dia touto lego umin, me merimnate te psyhe ti fagite, mide to somati ti endysisthe.
verses.translation: And he said unto his disciples, Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat; neither for the body, what ye shall put on.

verses.original: ἡ ⸀γὰρ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος.
verses.translit: e gar psyhe pleion estin tes trofes kai to soma tou endymatos.
verses.translation: The life is more than meat, and the body is more than raiment.

verses.original: κατανοήσατε τοὺς κόρακας ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν, οἷς οὐκ ἔστιν ταμεῖον οὐδὲ ἀποθήκη, καὶ ὁ θεὸς τρέφει αὐτούς· πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμεῖς διαφέρετε τῶν πετεινῶν.
verses.translit: katanoisate tous korakas oti ou speiroysin oude therizoysin, ois ouk estin tameion oude apothiki, kai o theos trefei autoys* poso mallon umeis diaferete ton peteinon.
verses.translation: Consider the ravens: for they neither sow nor reap; which neither have storehouse nor barn; and God feedeth them: how much more are ye better than the fowls?

verses.original: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται ⸂ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ προσθεῖναι⸃ ⸀πῆχυν;
verses.translit: tis de ex umon merimnon dynatai epi ten elikian autou prostheinai pehyn;
verses.translation: And which of you with taking thought can add to his stature one cubit?

verses.original: εἰ οὖν ⸀οὐδὲ ἐλάχιστον δύνασθε, τί περὶ τῶν λοιπῶν μεριμνᾶτε;
verses.translit: ei oun oude elahiston dynasthe, ti peri ton loipon merimnate;
verses.translation: If ye then be not able to do that thing which is least, why take ye thought for the rest?

verses.original: κατανοήσατε τὰ κρίνα πῶς αὐξάνει· οὐ κοπιᾷ οὐδὲ νήθει· λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.
verses.translit: katanoisate ta krina pos auxanei* ou kopia oude nithei* lego de umin, oude Solomon en pase te doxe autou perievaleto os en toyton.
verses.translation: Consider the lilies how they grow: they toil not, they spin not; and yet I say unto you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ⸂ἐν ἀγρῷ τὸν χόρτον ὄντα σήμερον⸃ καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ θεὸς οὕτως ⸀ἀμφιέζει, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι.
verses.translit: ei de en agro ton horton onta simeron kai aurion eis klivanon vallomenon o theos outos amfiezei, poso mallon umas, oligopistoi.
verses.translation: If then God so clothe the grass, which is to day in the field, and to morrow is cast into the oven; how much more will he clothe you, O ye of little faith?

verses.original: καὶ ὑμεῖς μὴ ζητεῖτε τί φάγητε ⸀καὶ τί πίητε, καὶ μὴ μετεωρίζεσθε,
verses.translit: kai umeis me ziteite ti fagite kai ti piite, kai me meteorizesthe,
verses.translation: And seek not ye what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink, neither be ye of doubtful mind.

verses.original: ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη τοῦ κόσμου ⸀ἐπιζητοῦσιν, ὑμῶν δὲ ὁ πατὴρ οἶδεν ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων.
verses.translit: tauta gar panta ta ethni tou kosmoy epizitousin, umon de o pater oiden oti hrezete toyton.
verses.translation: For all these things do the nations of the world seek after: and your Father knoweth that ye have need of these things.

verses.original: πλὴν ζητεῖτε τὴν βασιλείαν ⸀αὐτοῦ, καὶ ⸀ταῦτα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: plen ziteite ten vasileian autou, kai tauta prostethisetai umin.
verses.translation: But rather seek ye the kingdom of God; and all these things shall be added unto you.

verses.original: Μὴ φοβοῦ, τὸ μικρὸν ποίμνιον, ὅτι εὐδόκησεν ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν δοῦναι ὑμῖν τὴν βασιλείαν.
verses.translit: Me fovou, to mikron poimnion, oti eudokisen o pater umon dounai umin ten vasileian.
verses.translation: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.

verses.original: πωλήσατε τὰ ὑπάρχοντα ὑμῶν καὶ δότε ἐλεημοσύνην· ποιήσατε ἑαυτοῖς βαλλάντια μὴ παλαιούμενα, θησαυρὸν ἀνέκλειπτον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, ὅπου κλέπτης οὐκ ἐγγίζει οὐδὲ σὴς διαφθείρει·
verses.translit: polisate ta uparhonta umon kai dote eleimosynin* poiisate eaytois vallantia me palaioymena, thisayron anekleipton en tois ouranois, opoy kleptis ouk eggizei oude ses diaftheirei*
verses.translation: Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.

verses.original: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρὸς ὑμῶν, ἐκεῖ καὶ ἡ καρδία ὑμῶν ἔσται.
verses.translit: opoy gar estin o thisayros umon, ekei kai e kardia umon estai.
verses.translation: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

verses.original: Ἔστωσαν ὑμῶν αἱ ὀσφύες περιεζωσμέναι καὶ οἱ λύχνοι καιόμενοι,
verses.translit: Estosan umon ai osfyes periezosmenai kai oi lyhnoi kaiomenoi,
verses.translation: Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning;

verses.original: καὶ ὑμεῖς ὅμοιοι ἀνθρώποις προσδεχομένοις τὸν κύριον ἑαυτῶν πότε ἀναλύσῃ ἐκ τῶν γάμων, ἵνα ἐλθόντος καὶ κρούσαντος εὐθέως ἀνοίξωσιν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai umeis omoioi anthropois prosdehomenois ton kyrion eayton pote analyse ek ton gamon, ina elthontos kai kroysantos eutheos anoixosin auto.
verses.translation: And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding; that when he cometh and knocketh, they may open unto him immediately.

verses.original: μακάριοι οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι, οὓς ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος εὑρήσει γρηγοροῦντας· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι περιζώσεται καὶ ἀνακλινεῖ αὐτοὺς καὶ παρελθὼν διακονήσει αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: makarioi oi douloi ekeinoi, ous elthon o kyrios eurisei grigorountas* amen lego umin oti perizosetai kai anaklinei autous kai parelthon diakonisei autois.
verses.translation: Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching: verily I say unto you, that he shall gird himself, and make them to sit down to meat, and will come forth and serve them.

verses.original: ⸂κἂν ἐν τῇ δευτέρᾳ κἂν⸃ ἐν τῇ τρίτῃ φυλακῇ ἔλθῃ καὶ εὕρῃ οὕτως, μακάριοί ⸀εἰσιν ἐκεῖνοι.
verses.translit: kan en te deytera kan en te trite fylake elthe kai eure outos, makarioi eisin ekeinoi.
verses.translation: And if he shall come in the second watch, or come in the third watch, and find them so, blessed are those servants.

verses.original: Τοῦτο δὲ γινώσκετε ὅτι εἰ ᾔδει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ποίᾳ ὥρᾳ ὁ κλέπτης ἔρχεται, ⸂οὐκ ἂν⸃ ἀφῆκεν ⸀διορυχθῆναι τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Touto de ginoskete oti ei edei o oikodespotis poia ora o kleptis erhetai, ouk an afeken dioryhthenai ton oikon autou.
verses.translation: And this know, that if the goodman of the house had known what hour the thief would come, he would have watched, and not have suffered his house to be broken through.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ὑμεῖς γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι, ὅτι ᾗ ὥρᾳ οὐ δοκεῖτε ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται.
verses.translit: kai umeis ginesthe etoimoi, oti e ora ou dokeite o yios tou anthropoy erhetai.
verses.translation: Be ye therefore ready also: for the Son of man cometh at an hour when ye think not.

verses.original: Εἶπεν ⸀δὲ ὁ Πέτρος· Κύριε, πρὸς ἡμᾶς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγεις ἢ καὶ πρὸς πάντας;
verses.translit: Eipen de o Petros* Kyrie, pros emas ten paravolen taytin legeis e kai pros pantas;
verses.translation: Then Peter said unto him, Lord, speakest thou this parable unto us, or even to all?

verses.original: ⸂καὶ εἶπεν⸃ ὁ κύριος· Τίς ἄρα ἐστὶν ὁ πιστὸς οἰκονόμος, ⸀ὁ φρόνιμος, ὃν καταστήσει ὁ κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς θεραπείας αὐτοῦ τοῦ διδόναι ἐν καιρῷ ⸀τὸ σιτομέτριον;
verses.translit: kai eipen o kyrios* Tis ara estin o pistos oikonomos, o fronimos, on katastisei o kyrios epi tes therapeias autou tou didonai en kairo to sitometrion;
verses.translation: And the Lord said, Who then is that faithful and wise steward, whom his lord shall make ruler over his household, to give them their portion of meat in due season?

verses.original: μακάριος ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος, ὃν ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εὑρήσει ποιοῦντα οὕτως·
verses.translit: makarios o doulos ekeinos, on elthon o kyrios autou eurisei poiounta outos*
verses.translation: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.

verses.original: ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ὑπάρχουσιν αὐτοῦ καταστήσει αὐτόν.
verses.translit: alithos lego umin oti epi pasin tois uparhoysin autou katastisei auton.
verses.translation: Of a truth I say unto you, that he will make him ruler over all that he hath.

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπῃ ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· Χρονίζει ὁ κύριός μου ἔρχεσθαι, καὶ ἄρξηται τύπτειν τοὺς παῖδας καὶ τὰς παιδίσκας, ἐσθίειν τε καὶ πίνειν καὶ μεθύσκεσθαι,
verses.translit: ean de eipe o doulos ekeinos en te kardia autou* Hronizei o kyrios moy erhesthai, kai arxitai typtein tous paidas kai tas paidiskas, esthiein te kai pinein kai methyskesthai,
verses.translation: But and if that servant say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; and shall begin to beat the menservants and maidens, and to eat and drink, and to be drunken;

verses.original: ἥξει ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἐν ἡμέρᾳ ᾗ οὐ προσδοκᾷ καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ᾗ οὐ γινώσκει, καὶ διχοτομήσει αὐτὸν καὶ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀπίστων θήσει.
verses.translit: exei o kyrios tou doyloy ekeinoy en emera e ou prosdoka kai en ora e ou ginoskei, kai dihotomisei auton kai to meros autou meta ton apiston thisei.
verses.translation: The lord of that servant will come in a day when he looketh not for him , and at an hour when he is not aware, and will cut him in sunder, and will appoint him his portion with the unbelievers.

verses.original: ἐκεῖνος δὲ ὁ δοῦλος ὁ γνοὺς τὸ θέλημα τοῦ κυρίου ⸀αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ ἑτοιμάσας ⸀ἢ ποιήσας πρὸς τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ δαρήσεται πολλάς·
verses.translit: ekeinos de o doulos o gnous to thelima tou kyrioy autou kai me etoimasas e poiisas pros to thelima autou darisetai pollas*
verses.translation: And that servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself , neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes .

verses.original: ὁ δὲ μὴ γνοὺς ποιήσας δὲ ἄξια πληγῶν δαρήσεται ὀλίγας. παντὶ δὲ ᾧ ἐδόθη πολύ, πολὺ ζητηθήσεται παρʼ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ᾧ παρέθεντο πολύ, περισσότερον αἰτήσουσιν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: o de me gnous poiisas de axia pligon darisetai oligas. panti de o edothi poly, polu zitithisetai par' autou, kai o parethento poly, perissoteron aitisoysin auton.
verses.translation: But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes . For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more.

verses.original: Πῦρ ἦλθον βαλεῖν ⸀ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ τί θέλω εἰ ἤδη ἀνήφθη;
verses.translit: Pur elthon valein epi ten gen, kai ti thelo ei edi anifthi?
verses.translation: I am come to send fire on the earth; and what will I, if it be already kindled?

verses.original: βάπτισμα δὲ ἔχω βαπτισθῆναι, καὶ πῶς συνέχομαι ἕως ⸀ὅτου τελεσθῇ.
verses.translit: vaptisma de eho vaptisthenai, kai pos synehomai eos otoy telesthe.
verses.translation: But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished!

verses.original: δοκεῖτε ὅτι εἰρήνην παρεγενόμην δοῦναι ἐν τῇ γῇ; οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλʼ ἢ διαμερισμόν.
verses.translit: dokeite oti eirinin paregenomin dounai en te ge; ouhi, lego umin, all' e diamerismon.
verses.translation: Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:

verses.original: ἔσονται γὰρ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν πέντε ἐν ⸂ἑνὶ οἴκῳ⸃ διαμεμερισμένοι, τρεῖς ἐπὶ δυσὶν καὶ δύο ἐπὶ τρισίν,
verses.translit: esontai gar apo tou nun pente en eni oiko diamemerismenoi, treis epi dysin kai dyo epi trisin,
verses.translation: For from henceforth there shall be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.

verses.original: ⸀διαμερισθήσονται πατὴρ ἐπὶ υἱῷ καὶ υἱὸς ἐπὶ πατρί, μήτηρ ⸀ἐπὶ ⸀θυγατέρα καὶ θυγάτηρ ἐπὶ ⸂τὴν μητέρα⸃, πενθερὰ ἐπὶ τὴν νύμφην αὐτῆς καὶ νύμφη ἐπὶ τὴν ⸀πενθεράν.
verses.translit: diameristhisontai pater epi yio kai yios epi patri, mitir epi thygatera kai thygatir epi ten mitera, penthera epi ten nymfin autes kai nymfi epi ten pentheran.
verses.translation: The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.

verses.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις· Ὅταν ⸀ἴδητε νεφέλην ἀνατέλλουσαν ⸀ἐπὶ δυσμῶν, εὐθέως λέγετε ⸀ὅτι Ὄμβρος ἔρχεται, καὶ γίνεται οὕτως·
verses.translit: Elegen de kai tois ohlois* Otan idite nefelin anatelloysan epi dysmon, eutheos legete oti Omvros erhetai, kai ginetai outos*
verses.translation: And he said also to the people, When ye see a cloud rise out of the west, straightway ye say, There cometh a shower; and so it is.

verses.original: καὶ ὅταν νότον πνέοντα, λέγετε ὅτι Καύσων ἔσται, καὶ γίνεται.
verses.translit: kai otan noton pneonta, legete oti Kayson estai, kai ginetai.
verses.translation: And when ye see the south wind blow, ye say, There will be heat; and it cometh to pass.

verses.original: ὑποκριταί, τὸ πρόσωπον τῆς γῆς καὶ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν, τὸν ⸂δὲ καιρὸν⸃ τοῦτον πῶς ⸂οὐκ οἴδατε δοκιμάζειν⸃;
verses.translit: upokritai, to prosopon tes ges kai tou ouranou oidate dokimazein, ton de kairon touton pos ouk oidate dokimazein;
verses.translation: Ye hypocrites, ye can discern the face of the sky and of the earth; but how is it that ye do not discern this time?

verses.original: Τί δὲ καὶ ἀφʼ ἑαυτῶν οὐ κρίνετε τὸ δίκαιον;
verses.translit: Ti de kai af' eayton ou krinete to dikaion;
verses.translation: Yea, and why even of yourselves judge ye not what is right?

verses.original: ὡς γὰρ ὑπάγεις μετὰ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου σου ἐπʼ ἄρχοντα, ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ δὸς ἐργασίαν ἀπηλλάχθαι ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ, μήποτε κατασύρῃ σε πρὸς τὸν κριτήν, καὶ ὁ κριτής σε ⸀παραδώσει τῷ πράκτορι, καὶ ὁ πράκτωρ σε ⸀βαλεῖ εἰς φυλακήν.
verses.translit: os gar upageis meta tou antidikoy soy ep' arhonta, en te odo dos ergasian apillahthai ap' autou, mipote katasyre se pros ton kritin, kai o kritis se paradosei to praktori, kai o praktor se valei eis fylakin.
verses.translation: When thou goest with thine adversary to the magistrate, as thou art in the way, give diligence that thou mayest be delivered from him; lest he hale thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and the officer cast thee into prison.

verses.original: λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως ⸂καὶ τὸ⸃ ἔσχατον λεπτὸν ἀποδῷς.
verses.translit: lego soi, ou me exelthes ekeithen eos kai to eshaton lepton apodos.
verses.translation: I tell thee, thou shalt not depart thence, till thou hast paid the very last mite.

verses.original: Παρῆσαν δέ τινες ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ καιρῷ ἀπαγγέλλοντες αὐτῷ περὶ τῶν Γαλιλαίων ὧν τὸ αἷμα Πιλᾶτος ἔμιξεν μετὰ τῶν θυσιῶν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Paresan de tines en auto to kairo apaggellontes auto peri ton Galilaion on to aima Pilatos emixen meta ton thysion auton.
verses.translation: There were present at that season some that told him of the Galilæans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Δοκεῖτε ὅτι οἱ Γαλιλαῖοι οὗτοι ἁμαρτωλοὶ παρὰ πάντας τοὺς Γαλιλαίους ἐγένοντο, ὅτι ⸀ταῦτα πεπόνθασιν;
verses.translit: kai apokritheis eipen autois* Dokeite oti oi Galilaioi outoi amartoloi para pantas tous Galilaioys egenonto, oti tauta peponthasin;
verses.translation: And Jesus answering said unto them, Suppose ye that these Galilæans were sinners above all the Galilæans, because they suffered such things?

verses.original: οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλʼ ἐὰν μὴ μετανοῆτε πάντες ⸀ὁμοίως ἀπολεῖσθε.
verses.translit: ouhi, lego umin, all' ean me metanoete pantes omoios apoleisthe.
verses.translation: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

verses.original: ἢ ἐκεῖνοι οἱ ⸀δεκαοκτὼ ἐφʼ οὓς ἔπεσεν ὁ πύργος ἐν τῷ Σιλωὰμ καὶ ἀπέκτεινεν αὐτούς, δοκεῖτε ὅτι ⸀αὐτοὶ ὀφειλέται ἐγένοντο παρὰ πάντας ⸀τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς ⸀κατοικοῦντας Ἰερουσαλήμ;
verses.translit: e ekeinoi oi dekaokto ef' ous epesen o pyrgos en to Siloam kai apekteinen autoys, dokeite oti autoi ofeiletai egenonto para pantas tous anthropoys tous katoikountas Ieroysalim;
verses.translation: Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem?

verses.original: οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλʼ ἐὰν μὴ ⸀μετανοῆτε πάντες ⸀ὡσαύτως ἀπολεῖσθε.
verses.translit: ouhi, lego umin, all' ean me metanoete pantes osaytos apoleisthe.
verses.translation: I tell you, Nay: but, except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish.

verses.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ ταύτην τὴν παραβολήν. Συκῆν εἶχέν τις ⸂πεφυτευμένην ἐν τῷ ἀμπελῶνι αὐτοῦ⸃, καὶ ἦλθεν ζητῶν καρπὸν ἐν αὐτῇ καὶ οὐχ εὗρεν.
verses.translit: Elegen de taytin ten paravolin. Syken eihen tis pefyteymenin en to ampeloni autou, kai elthen ziton karpon en aute kai ouh euren.
verses.translation: He spake also this parable; A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τὸν ἀμπελουργόν· Ἰδοὺ τρία ἔτη ⸂ἀφʼ οὗ⸃ ἔρχομαι ζητῶν καρπὸν ἐν τῇ συκῇ ταύτῃ καὶ οὐχ εὑρίσκω· ⸀ἔκκοψον αὐτήν· ἱνατί καὶ τὴν γῆν καταργεῖ;
verses.translit: eipen de pros ton ampeloyrgon* Idou tria eti af' ou erhomai ziton karpon en te syke tayte kai ouh eurisko* ekkopson autin* inati kai ten gen katargei;
verses.translation: Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς λέγει αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἄφες αὐτὴν καὶ τοῦτο τὸ ἔτος, ἕως ὅτου σκάψω περὶ αὐτὴν καὶ βάλω κόπρια·
verses.translit: o de apokritheis legei auto* Kyrie, afes auten kai touto to etos, eos otoy skapso peri auten kai valo kopria*
verses.translation: And he answering said unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it :

verses.original: κἂν μὲν ποιήσῃ καρπὸν ⸂εἰς τὸ μέλλον— εἰ δὲ μήγε,⸃ ἐκκόψεις αὐτήν.
verses.translit: kan men poiise karpon eis to mellon-- ei de mige, ekkopseis autin.
verses.translation: And if it bear fruit, well : and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.

verses.original: Ἦν δὲ διδάσκων ἐν μιᾷ τῶν συναγωγῶν ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν.
verses.translit: En de didaskon en mia ton synagogon en tois savvasin.
verses.translation: And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ⸀γυνὴ πνεῦμα ἔχουσα ἀσθενείας ἔτη ⸀δεκαοκτώ, καὶ ἦν συγκύπτουσα καὶ μὴ δυναμένη ἀνακύψαι εἰς τὸ παντελές.
verses.translit: kai idou gyne pneuma ehoysa astheneias eti dekaokto, kai en sygkyptoysa kai me dynameni anakypsai eis to panteles.
verses.translation: And, behold, there was a woman which had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years, and was bowed together, and could in no wise lift up herself .

verses.original: ἰδὼν δὲ αὐτὴν ὁ Ἰησοῦς προσεφώνησεν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Γύναι, ἀπολέλυσαι τῆς ἀσθενείας σου,
verses.translit: idon de auten o Iisous prosefonisen kai eipen aute* Gynai, apolelysai tes astheneias soy,
verses.translation: And when Jesus saw her, he called her to him , and said unto her, Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτῇ τὰς χεῖρας· καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀνωρθώθη, καὶ ἐδόξαζεν τὸν θεόν.
verses.translit: kai epethiken aute tas heiras* kai parahrema anorthothi, kai edoxazen ton theon.
verses.translation: And he laid his hands on her: and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος, ἀγανακτῶν ὅτι τῷ σαββάτῳ ἐθεράπευσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ἔλεγεν τῷ ὄχλῳ ⸀ὅτι Ἓξ ἡμέραι εἰσὶν ἐν αἷς δεῖ ἐργάζεσθαι· ἐν ⸀αὐταῖς οὖν ἐρχόμενοι θεραπεύεσθε καὶ μὴ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου.
verses.translit: apokritheis de o arhisynagogos, aganakton oti to savvato etherapeysen o Iisous, elegen to ohlo oti Ex emerai eisin en ais dei ergazesthai* en autais oun erhomenoi therapeyesthe kai me te emera tou savvatoy.
verses.translation: And the ruler of the synagogue answered with indignation, because that Jesus had healed on the sabbath day, and said unto the people, There are six days in which men ought to work: in them therefore come and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη ⸀δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος καὶ εἶπεν· Ὑποκριταί, ἕκαστος ὑμῶν τῷ σαββάτῳ οὐ λύει τὸν βοῦν αὐτοῦ ἢ τὸν ὄνον ἀπὸ τῆς φάτνης καὶ ⸀ἀπαγαγὼν ποτίζει;
verses.translit: apekrithi de auto o kyrios kai eipen* Upokritai, ekastos umon to savvato ou lyei ton voun autou e ton onon apo tes fatnis kai apagagon potizei;
verses.translation: The Lord then answered him, and said, Thou hypocrite, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering?

verses.original: ταύτην δὲ θυγατέρα Ἀβραὰμ οὖσαν, ἣν ἔδησεν ὁ Σατανᾶς ἰδοὺ δέκα καὶ ὀκτὼ ἔτη, οὐκ ἔδει λυθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ δεσμοῦ τούτου τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου;
verses.translit: taytin de thygatera Avraam ousan, en edisen o Satanas idou deka kai okto eti, ouk edei lythenai apo tou desmou toytoy te emera tou savvatoy;
verses.translation: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?

verses.original: καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντος αὐτοῦ κατῃσχύνοντο πάντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι αὐτῷ, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἔχαιρεν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐνδόξοις τοῖς γινομένοις ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai tauta legontos autou kateshynonto pantes oi antikeimenoi auto, kai pas o ohlos ehairen epi pasin tois endoxois tois ginomenois up' autou.
verses.translation: And when he had said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed: and all the people rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.

verses.original: Ἔλεγεν ⸀οὖν· Τίνι ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ τίνι ὁμοιώσω αὐτήν;
verses.translit: Elegen oun* Tini omoia estin e vasileia tou theou, kai tini omoioso autin;
verses.translation: Then said he, Unto what is the kingdom of God like? and whereunto shall I resemble it?

verses.original: ὁμοία ἐστὶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔβαλεν εἰς κῆπον ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ ηὔξησεν καὶ ἐγένετο εἰς ⸀δένδρον, καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατεσκήνωσεν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: omoia estin kokko sinapeos, on lavon anthropos evalen eis kepon eaytou, kai iuxisen kai egeneto eis dendron, kai ta peteina tou ouranou kateskinosen en tois kladois autou.
verses.translation: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and cast into his garden; and it grew, and waxed a great tree; and the fowls of the air lodged in the branches of it.

verses.original: ⸀Καὶ πάλιν εἶπεν· Τίνι ὁμοιώσω τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ;
verses.translit: Kai palin eipen* Tini omoioso ten vasileian tou theou;
verses.translation: And again he said, Whereunto shall I liken the kingdom of God?

verses.original: ὁμοία ἐστὶν ζύμῃ, ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ⸀ἔκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον.
verses.translit: omoia estin zyme, en lavousa gyne ekrypsen eis aleyroy sata tria eos ou ezymothi olon.
verses.translation: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.

verses.original: Καὶ διεπορεύετο κατὰ πόλεις καὶ κώμας διδάσκων καὶ πορείαν ποιούμενος εἰς ⸀Ἱεροσόλυμα.
verses.translit: Kai dieporeyeto kata poleis kai komas didaskon kai poreian poioymenos eis Ierosolyma.
verses.translation: And he went through the cities and villages, teaching, and journeying toward Jerusalem.

verses.original: εἶπεν δέ τις αὐτῷ· Κύριε, εἰ ὀλίγοι οἱ σῳζόμενοι; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς·
verses.translit: eipen de tis auto* Kyrie, ei oligoi oi sozomenoi; o de eipen pros autoys*
verses.translation: Then said one unto him, Lord, are there few that be saved? And he said unto them,

verses.original: Ἀγωνίζεσθε εἰσελθεῖν διὰ τῆς στενῆς ⸀θύρας, ὅτι πολλοί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ζητήσουσιν εἰσελθεῖν καὶ οὐκ ἰσχύσουσιν,
verses.translit: Agonizesthe eiselthein dia tes stenes thyras, oti polloi, lego umin, zitisoysin eiselthein kai ouk ishysoysin,
verses.translation: Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able.

verses.original: ἀφʼ οὗ ἂν ἐγερθῇ ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης καὶ ἀποκλείσῃ τὴν θύραν, καὶ ἄρξησθε ἔξω ἑστάναι καὶ κρούειν τὴν θύραν λέγοντες· ⸀Κύριε, ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν· καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ἐρεῖ ὑμῖν· Οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς πόθεν ἐστέ.
verses.translit: af' ou an egerthe o oikodespotis kai apokleise ten thyran, kai arxisthe exo estanai kai kroyein ten thyran legontes* Kyrie, anoixon emin* kai apokritheis erei umin* Ouk oida umas pothen este.
verses.translation: When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are:

verses.original: τότε ἄρξεσθε λέγειν· Ἐφάγομεν ἐνώπιόν σου καὶ ἐπίομεν, καὶ ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις ἡμῶν ἐδίδαξας·
verses.translit: tote arxesthe legein* Efagomen enopion soy kai epiomen, kai en tais plateiais emon edidaxas*
verses.translation: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets.

verses.original: καὶ ἐρεῖ ⸀λέγων ὑμῖν· Οὐκ ⸀οἶδα πόθεν ἐστέ· ἀπόστητε ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ, πάντες ⸀ἐργάται ἀδικίας.
verses.translit: kai erei legon umin* Ouk oida pothen este* apostite ap' emou, pantes ergatai adikias.
verses.translation: But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.

verses.original: ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων, ὅταν ⸀ὄψησθε Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ Ἰακὼβ καὶ πάντας τοὺς προφήτας ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὑμᾶς δὲ ἐκβαλλομένους ἔξω.
verses.translit: ekei estai o klaythmos kai o vrygmos ton odonton, otan opsisthe Avraam kai Isaak kai Iakov kai pantas tous profitas en te vasileia tou theou, umas de ekvallomenoys exo.
verses.translation: There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.

verses.original: καὶ ἥξουσιν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν καὶ δυσμῶν καὶ ⸀ἀπὸ βορρᾶ καὶ νότου καὶ ἀνακλιθήσονται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: kai exoysin apo anatolon kai dysmon kai apo vorra kai notoy kai anaklithisontai en te vasileia tou theou.
verses.translation: And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ εἰσὶν ἔσχατοι οἳ ἔσονται πρῶτοι, καὶ εἰσὶν πρῶτοι οἳ ἔσονται ἔσχατοι.
verses.translit: kai idou eisin eshatoi oi esontai protoi, kai eisin protoi oi esontai eshatoi.
verses.translation: And, behold, there are last which shall be first, and there are first which shall be last.

verses.original: Ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ⸀ὥρᾳ προσῆλθάν τινες Φαρισαῖοι λέγοντες αὐτῷ· Ἔξελθε καὶ πορεύου ἐντεῦθεν, ὅτι Ἡρῴδης θέλει σε ἀποκτεῖναι.
verses.translit: En aute te ora proselthan tines Farisaioi legontes auto* Exelthe kai poreyoy enteuthen, oti Erodis thelei se apokteinai.
verses.translation: The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying unto him, Get thee out, and depart hence: for Herod will kill thee.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες εἴπατε τῇ ἀλώπεκι ταύτῃ· Ἰδοὺ ἐκβάλλω δαιμόνια καὶ ἰάσεις ⸀ἀποτελῶ σήμερον καὶ αὔριον, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ τελειοῦμαι.
verses.translit: kai eipen autois* Poreythentes eipate te alopeki tayte* Idou ekvallo daimonia kai iaseis apotelo simeron kai aurion, kai te trite teleioumai.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected.

verses.original: πλὴν δεῖ με σήμερον καὶ αὔριον καὶ τῇ ἐχομένῃ πορεύεσθαι, ὅτι οὐκ ἐνδέχεται προφήτην ἀπολέσθαι ἔξω Ἰερουσαλήμ.
verses.translit: plen dei me simeron kai aurion kai te ehomene poreyesthai, oti ouk endehetai profitin apolesthai exo Ieroysalim.
verses.translation: Nevertheless I must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem.

verses.original: Ἰερουσαλὴμ Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἡ ἀποκτείνουσα τοὺς προφήτας καὶ λιθοβολοῦσα τοὺς ἀπεσταλμένους πρὸς αὐτήν— ποσάκις ἠθέλησα ἐπισυνάξαι τὰ τέκνα σου ὃν τρόπον ὄρνις τὴν ἑαυτῆς νοσσιὰν ὑπὸ τὰς πτέρυγας, καὶ οὐκ ἠθελήσατε.
verses.translit: Ieroysalem Ieroysalim, e apokteinoysa tous profitas kai lithovolousa tous apestalmenoys pros autin-- posakis ethelisa episynaxai ta tekna soy on tropon ornis ten eaytes nossian upo tas pterygas, kai ouk ethelisate.
verses.translation: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not!

verses.original: ἰδοὺ ἀφίεται ὑμῖν ὁ οἶκος ⸀ὑμῶν. λέγω ⸀δὲ ⸀ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ ⸂ἴδητέ με⸃ ἕως ⸂ἥξει ὅτε⸃ εἴπητε· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου.
verses.translit: idou afietai umin o oikos umon. lego de umin, ou me idite me eos exei ote eipite* Eulogimenos o erhomenos en onomati kyrioy.
verses.translation: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until the time come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἐλθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς οἶκόν τινος τῶν ἀρχόντων τῶν Φαρισαίων σαββάτῳ φαγεῖν ἄρτον καὶ αὐτοὶ ἦσαν παρατηρούμενοι αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Kai egeneto en to elthein auton eis oikon tinos ton arhonton ton Farisaion savvato fagein arton kai autoi esan paratiroymenoi auton.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, as he went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees to eat bread on the sabbath day, that they watched him.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν ὑδρωπικὸς ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai idou anthropos tis en udropikos emprosthen autou.
verses.translation: And, behold, there was a certain man before him which had the dropsy.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς νομικοὺς καὶ Φαρισαίους λέγων· ⸀Ἔξεστιν τῷ σαββάτῳ ⸂θεραπεῦσαι ἢ οὔ⸃;
verses.translit: kai apokritheis o Iisous eipen pros tous nomikous kai Farisaioys legon* Exestin to savvato therapeusai e ou;
verses.translation: And Jesus answering spake unto the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἡσύχασαν. καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενος ἰάσατο αὐτὸν καὶ ἀπέλυσεν.
verses.translit: oi de esyhasan. kai epilavomenos iasato auton kai apelysen.
verses.translation: And they held their peace. And he took him , and healed him, and let him go;

verses.original: ⸀καὶ πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν· Τίνος ὑμῶν υἱὸς ἢ βοῦς εἰς φρέαρ ⸀πεσεῖται, καὶ οὐκ εὐθέως ἀνασπάσει αὐτὸν ⸀ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου;
verses.translit: kai pros autous eipen* Tinos umon yios e vous eis frear peseitai, kai ouk eutheos anaspasei auton en emera tou savvatoy;
verses.translation: And answered them, saying, Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day?

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν ⸀ἀνταποκριθῆναι πρὸς ταῦτα.
verses.translit: kai ouk ishysan antapokrithenai pros tauta.
verses.translation: And they could not answer him again to these things.

verses.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς κεκλημένους παραβολήν, ἐπέχων πῶς τὰς πρωτοκλισίας ἐξελέγοντο, λέγων πρὸς αὐτούς·
verses.translit: Elegen de pros tous keklimenoys paravolin, epehon pos tas protoklisias exelegonto, legon pros autoys*
verses.translation: And he put forth a parable to those which were bidden, when he marked how they chose out the chief rooms; saying unto them,

verses.original: Ὅταν κληθῇς ὑπό τινος εἰς γάμους, μὴ κατακλιθῇς εἰς τὴν πρωτοκλισίαν, μήποτε ἐντιμότερός σου ᾖ κεκλημένος ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ
verses.translit: Otan klithes upo tinos eis gamoys, me kataklithes eis ten protoklisian, mipote entimoteros soy e keklimenos up' autou
verses.translation: When thou art bidden of any man to a wedding, sit not down in the highest room; lest a more honourable man than thou be bidden of him;

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν ὁ σὲ καὶ αὐτὸν καλέσας ἐρεῖ σοι· Δὸς τούτῳ τόπον, καὶ τότε ἄρξῃ μετὰ αἰσχύνης τὸν ἔσχατον τόπον κατέχειν.
verses.translit: kai elthon o se kai auton kalesas erei soi* Dos toyto topon, kai tote arxe meta aishynis ton eshaton topon katehein.
verses.translation: And he that bade thee and him come and say to thee, Give this man place; and thou begin with shame to take the lowest room.

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ὅταν κληθῇς πορευθεὶς ἀνάπεσε εἰς τὸν ἔσχατον τόπον, ἵνα ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὁ κεκληκώς σε ⸀ἐρεῖ σοι· Φίλε, προσανάβηθι ἀνώτερον· τότε ἔσται σοι δόξα ἐνώπιον ⸀πάντων τῶν συνανακειμένων σοι.
verses.translit: all' otan klithes poreytheis anapese eis ton eshaton topon, ina otan elthe o keklikos se erei soi* File, prosanavithi anoteron* tote estai soi doxa enopion panton ton synanakeimenon soi.
verses.translation: But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that bade thee cometh, he may say unto thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee.

verses.original: ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὑψῶν ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται καὶ ὁ ταπεινῶν ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται.
verses.translit: oti pas o upson eayton tapeinothisetai kai o tapeinon eayton upsothisetai.
verses.translation: For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

verses.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τῷ κεκληκότι αὐτόν· Ὅταν ποιῇς ἄριστον ἢ δεῖπνον, μὴ φώνει τοὺς φίλους σου μηδὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου μηδὲ τοὺς συγγενεῖς σου μηδὲ γείτονας πλουσίους, μήποτε καὶ αὐτοὶ ⸂ἀντικαλέσωσίν σε⸃ καὶ γένηται ⸂ἀνταπόδομά σοι⸃.
verses.translit: Elegen de kai to keklikoti auton* Otan poies ariston e deipnon, me fonei tous filoys soy mide tous adelfoys soy mide tous syggeneis soy mide geitonas ploysioys, mipote kai autoi antikalesosin se kai genitai antapodoma soi.
verses.translation: Then said he also to him that bade him, When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends, nor thy brethren, neither thy kinsmen, nor thy rich neighbours; lest they also bid thee again, and a recompence be made thee.

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ὅταν ⸂δοχὴν ποιῇς⸃, κάλει πτωχούς, ἀναπείρους, χωλούς, τυφλούς·
verses.translit: all' otan dohen poies, kalei ptohoys, anapeiroys, holoys, tyfloys*
verses.translation: But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind:

verses.original: καὶ μακάριος ἔσῃ, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἀνταποδοῦναί σοι, ἀνταποδοθήσεται γάρ σοι ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τῶν δικαίων.
verses.translit: kai makarios ese, oti ouk ehoysin antapodounai soi, antapodothisetai gar soi en te anastasei ton dikaion.
verses.translation: And thou shalt be blessed; for they cannot recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just.

verses.original: Ἀκούσας δέ τις τῶν συνανακειμένων ταῦτα εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακάριος ⸀ὅστις φάγεται ⸀ἄρτον ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: Akoysas de tis ton synanakeimenon tauta eipen auto* Makarios ostis fagetai arton en te vasileia tou theou.
verses.translation: And when one of them that sat at meat with him heard these things, he said unto him, Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἄνθρωπός τις ⸀ἐποίει δεῖπνον μέγα, καὶ ἐκάλεσεν πολλούς,
verses.translit: o de eipen auto* Anthropos tis epoiei deipnon mega, kai ekalesen polloys,
verses.translation: Then said he unto him, A certain man made a great supper, and bade many:

verses.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦ δείπνου εἰπεῖν τοῖς κεκλημένοις· Ἔρχεσθε, ὅτι ἤδη ἕτοιμά ⸀ἐστιν.
verses.translit: kai apesteilen ton doulon autou te ora tou deipnoy eipein tois keklimenois* Erhesthe, oti edi etoima estin.
verses.translation: And sent his servant at supper time to say to them that were bidden, Come; for all things are now ready.

verses.original: καὶ ἤρξαντο ἀπὸ μιᾶς ⸂πάντες παραιτεῖσθαι⸃. ὁ πρῶτος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀγρὸν ἠγόρασα καὶ ἔχω ἀνάγκην ⸀ἐξελθὼν ἰδεῖν αὐτόν· ἐρωτῶ σε, ἔχε με παρῃτημένον.
verses.translit: kai erxanto apo mias pantes paraiteisthai. o protos eipen auto* Agron egorasa kai eho anagkin exelthon idein auton* eroto se, ehe me paretimenon.
verses.translation: And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said unto him, I have bought a piece of ground, and I must needs go and see it: I pray thee have me excused.

verses.original: καὶ ἕτερος εἶπεν· Ζεύγη βοῶν ἠγόρασα πέντε καὶ πορεύομαι δοκιμάσαι αὐτά· ἐρωτῶ σε, ἔχε με παρῃτημένον.
verses.translit: kai eteros eipen* Zeygi voon egorasa pente kai poreyomai dokimasai auta* eroto se, ehe me paretimenon.
verses.translation: And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused.

verses.original: καὶ ἕτερος εἶπεν· Γυναῖκα ἔγημα καὶ διὰ τοῦτο οὐ δύναμαι ἐλθεῖν.
verses.translit: kai eteros eipen* Gynaika egima kai dia touto ou dynamai elthein.
verses.translation: And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.

verses.original: καὶ παραγενόμενος ὁ ⸀δοῦλος ἀπήγγειλεν τῷ κυρίῳ αὐτοῦ ταῦτα. τότε ὀργισθεὶς ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης εἶπεν τῷ δούλῳ αὐτοῦ· Ἔξελθε ταχέως εἰς τὰς πλατείας καὶ ῥύμας τῆς πόλεως, καὶ τοὺς πτωχοὺς καὶ ἀναπείρους καὶ ⸂τυφλοὺς καὶ χωλοὺς⸃ εἰσάγαγε ὧδε.
verses.translit: kai paragenomenos o doulos apiggeilen to kyrio autou tauta. tote orgistheis o oikodespotis eipen to doylo autou* Exelthe taheos eis tas plateias kai Rymas tes poleos, kai tous ptohous kai anapeiroys kai tyflous kai holous eisagage ode.
verses.translation: So that servant came, and shewed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ δοῦλος· Κύριε, γέγονεν ⸀ὃ ἐπέταξας, καὶ ἔτι τόπος ἐστίν.
verses.translit: kai eipen o doulos* Kyrie, gegonen o epetaxas, kai eti topos estin.
verses.translation: And the servant said, Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος πρὸς τὸν δοῦλον· Ἔξελθε εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς καὶ φραγμοὺς καὶ ἀνάγκασον εἰσελθεῖν, ἵνα γεμισθῇ ⸂μου ὁ οἶκος⸃·
verses.translit: kai eipen o kyrios pros ton doulon* Exelthe eis tas odous kai fragmous kai anagkason eiselthein, ina gemisthe moy o oikos*
verses.translation: And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.

verses.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων τῶν κεκλημένων γεύσεταί μου τοῦ ⸀δείπνου.
verses.translit: lego gar umin oti oudeis ton andron ekeinon ton keklimenon geysetai moy tou deipnoy.
verses.translation: For I say unto you, That none of those men which were bidden shall taste of my supper.

verses.original: Συνεπορεύοντο δὲ αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοί, καὶ στραφεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς·
verses.translit: Syneporeyonto de auto ohloi polloi, kai strafeis eipen pros autoys*
verses.translation: And there went great multitudes with him: and he turned, and said unto them,

verses.original: Εἴ τις ἔρχεται πρός με καὶ οὐ μισεῖ τὸν πατέρα ⸀ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ τὰ τέκνα καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τὰς ἀδελφάς, ἔτι ⸀τε καὶ τὴν ⸂ψυχὴν ἑαυτοῦ⸃, οὐ δύναται ⸂εἶναί μου μαθητής⸃.
verses.translit: Ei tis erhetai pros me kai ou misei ton patera eaytou kai ten mitera kai ten gynaika kai ta tekna kai tous adelfous kai tas adelfas, eti te kai ten psyhen eaytou, ou dynatai einai moy mathitis.
verses.translation: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.

verses.original: ⸀ὅστις οὐ βαστάζει τὸν σταυρὸν ⸀ἑαυτοῦ καὶ ἔρχεται ὀπίσω μου, οὐ δύναται εἶναί μου μαθητής.
verses.translit: ostis ou vastazei ton stayron eaytou kai erhetai opiso moy, ou dynatai einai moy mathitis.
verses.translation: And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.

verses.original: τίς γὰρ ἐξ ⸀ὑμῶν θέλων πύργον οἰκοδομῆσαι οὐχὶ πρῶτον καθίσας ψηφίζει τὴν δαπάνην, εἰ ⸀ἔχει εἰς ἀπαρτισμόν;
verses.translit: tis gar ex umon thelon pyrgon oikodomesai ouhi proton kathisas psifizei ten dapanin, ei ehei eis apartismon;
verses.translation: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it ?

verses.original: ἵνα μήποτε θέντος αὐτοῦ θεμέλιον καὶ μὴ ἰσχύοντος ἐκτελέσαι πάντες οἱ θεωροῦντες ἄρξωνται ⸂αὐτῷ ἐμπαίζειν⸃
verses.translit: ina mipote thentos autou themelion kai me ishyontos ektelesai pantes oi theorountes arxontai auto empaizein
verses.translation: Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it , all that behold it begin to mock him,

verses.original: λέγοντες ὅτι Οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἤρξατο οἰκοδομεῖν καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν ἐκτελέσαι.
verses.translit: legontes oti Outos o anthropos erxato oikodomein kai ouk ishysen ektelesai.
verses.translation: Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.

verses.original: ἢ τίς βασιλεὺς πορευόμενος ⸂ἑτέρῳ βασιλεῖ συμβαλεῖν⸃ εἰς πόλεμον οὐχὶ καθίσας πρῶτον ⸀βουλεύσεται εἰ δυνατός ἐστιν ἐν δέκα χιλιάσιν ⸀ὑπαντῆσαι τῷ μετὰ εἴκοσι χιλιάδων ἐρχομένῳ ἐπʼ αὐτόν;
verses.translit: e tis vasileus poreyomenos etero vasilei symvalein eis polemon ouhi kathisas proton voyleysetai ei dynatos estin en deka hiliasin upantesai to meta eikosi hiliadon erhomeno ep' auton;
verses.translation: Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?

verses.original: εἰ δὲ μήγε, ἔτι ⸂αὐτοῦ πόρρω⸃ ὄντος πρεσβείαν ἀποστείλας ἐρωτᾷ ⸀τὰ πρὸς εἰρήνην.
verses.translit: ei de mige, eti autou porro ontos presveian aposteilas erota ta pros eirinin.
verses.translation: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace.

verses.original: οὕτως οὖν πᾶς ἐξ ὑμῶν ὃς οὐκ ἀποτάσσεται πᾶσιν τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ ὑπάρχουσιν οὐ δύναται ⸂εἶναί μου⸃ μαθητής.
verses.translit: outos oun pas ex umon os ouk apotassetai pasin tois eaytou uparhoysin ou dynatai einai moy mathitis.
verses.translation: So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.

verses.original: Καλὸν ⸀οὖν τὸ ἅλας· ἐὰν δὲ ⸀καὶ τὸ ἅλας μωρανθῇ, ἐν τίνι ἀρτυθήσεται;
verses.translit: Kalon oun to alas* ean de kai to alas moranthe, en tini artythisetai;
verses.translation: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be seasoned?

verses.original: οὔτε εἰς γῆν οὔτε εἰς κοπρίαν εὔθετόν ἐστιν· ἔξω βάλλουσιν αὐτό. ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.
verses.translit: oute eis gen oute eis koprian eutheton estin* exo valloysin auto. o ehon ota akoyein akoyeto.
verses.translation: It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill; but men cast it out. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

verses.original: Ἦσαν δὲ ⸂αὐτῷ ἐγγίζοντες⸃ πάντες οἱ τελῶναι καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Esan de auto eggizontes pantes oi telonai kai oi amartoloi akoyein autou.
verses.translation: Then drew near unto him all the publicans and sinners for to hear him.

verses.original: καὶ διεγόγγυζον οἵ ⸀τε Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγοντες ὅτι Οὗτος ἁμαρτωλοὺς προσδέχεται καὶ συνεσθίει αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: kai diegoggyzon oi te Farisaioi kai oi grammateis legontes oti Outos amartolous prosdehetai kai synesthiei autois.
verses.translation: And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην λέγων·
verses.translit: eipen de pros autous ten paravolen taytin legon*
verses.translation: And he spake this parable unto them, saying,

verses.original: Τίς ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ὑμῶν ἔχων ἑκατὸν πρόβατα καὶ ⸀ἀπολέσας ⸂ἐξ αὐτῶν ἓν⸃ οὐ καταλείπει τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ καὶ πορεύεται ἐπὶ τὸ ἀπολωλὸς ἕως εὕρῃ αὐτό;
verses.translit: Tis anthropos ex umon ehon ekaton provata kai apolesas ex auton en ou kataleipei ta enenikonta ennea en te erimo kai poreyetai epi to apololos eos eure auto;
verses.translation: What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?

verses.original: καὶ εὑρὼν ἐπιτίθησιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους ⸀αὐτοῦ χαίρων,
verses.translit: kai euron epitithisin epi tous omoys autou hairon,
verses.translation: And when he hath found it , he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον συγκαλεῖ τοὺς φίλους καὶ τοὺς γείτονας, λέγων αὐτοῖς· Συγχάρητέ μοι ὅτι εὗρον τὸ πρόβατόν μου τὸ ἀπολωλός.
verses.translit: kai elthon eis ton oikon sygkalei tous filoys kai tous geitonas, legon autois* Sygharite moi oti euron to provaton moy to apololos.
verses.translation: And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.

verses.original: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὕτως χαρὰ ⸂ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἔσται⸃ ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι ἢ ἐπὶ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα δικαίοις οἵτινες οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν μετανοίας.
verses.translit: lego umin oti outos hara en to ourano estai epi eni amartolo metanoounti e epi enenikonta ennea dikaiois oitines ou hreian ehoysin metanoias.
verses.translation: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.

verses.original: Ἢ τίς γυνὴ δραχμὰς ἔχουσα δέκα, ἐὰν ἀπολέσῃ δραχμὴν μίαν, οὐχὶ ἅπτει λύχνον καὶ σαροῖ τὴν οἰκίαν καὶ ζητεῖ ἐπιμελῶς ἕως ⸀οὗ εὕρῃ;
verses.translit: E tis gyne drahmas ehoysa deka, ean apolese drahmen mian, ouhi aptei lyhnon kai saroi ten oikian kai zitei epimelos eos ou eure;
verses.translation: Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it ?

verses.original: καὶ εὑροῦσα ⸀συγκαλεῖ τὰς φίλας ⸀καὶ γείτονας λέγουσα· Συγχάρητέ μοι ὅτι εὗρον τὴν δραχμὴν ἣν ἀπώλεσα.
verses.translit: kai eurousa sygkalei tas filas kai geitonas legoysa* Sygharite moi oti euron ten drahmen en apolesa.
verses.translation: And when she hath found it , she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.

verses.original: οὕτως, λέγω ὑμῖν, ⸂γίνεται χαρὰ⸃ ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ ἑνὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ μετανοοῦντι.
verses.translit: outos, lego umin, ginetai hara enopion ton aggelon tou theou epi eni amartolo metanoounti.
verses.translation: Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δέ· Ἄνθρωπός τις εἶχεν δύο υἱούς.
verses.translit: Eipen de* Anthropos tis eihen dyo yioys.
verses.translation: And he said, A certain man had two sons:

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ νεώτερος αὐτῶν τῷ πατρί· Πάτερ, δός μοι τὸ ἐπιβάλλον μέρος τῆς οὐσίας· ⸂ὁ δὲ⸃ διεῖλεν αὐτοῖς τὸν βίον.
verses.translit: kai eipen o neoteros auton to patri* Pater, dos moi to epivallon meros tes ousias* o de dieilen autois ton vion.
verses.translation: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me . And he divided unto them his living.

verses.original: καὶ μετʼ οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας συναγαγὼν ⸀πάντα ὁ νεώτερος υἱὸς ἀπεδήμησεν εἰς χώραν μακράν, καὶ ἐκεῖ διεσκόρπισεν τὴν οὐσίαν αὐτοῦ ζῶν ἀσώτως.
verses.translit: kai met' ou pollas emeras synagagon panta o neoteros yios apedimisen eis horan makran, kai ekei dieskorpisen ten ousian autou zon asotos.
verses.translation: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.

verses.original: δαπανήσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ πάντα ἐγένετο λιμὸς ⸀ἰσχυρὰ κατὰ τὴν χώραν ἐκείνην, καὶ αὐτὸς ἤρξατο ὑστερεῖσθαι.
verses.translit: dapanisantos de autou panta egeneto limos ishyra kata ten horan ekeinin, kai autos erxato ustereisthai.
verses.translation: And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.

verses.original: καὶ πορευθεὶς ἐκολλήθη ἑνὶ τῶν πολιτῶν τῆς χώρας ἐκείνης, καὶ ἔπεμψεν αὐτὸν εἰς τοὺς ἀγροὺς αὐτοῦ βόσκειν χοίρους·
verses.translit: kai poreytheis ekollithi eni ton politon tes horas ekeinis, kai epempsen auton eis tous agrous autou voskein hoiroys*
verses.translation: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπεθύμει ⸂γεμίσαι τὴν κοιλίαν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ⸃ τῶν κερατίων ὧν ἤσθιον οἱ χοῖροι, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδίδου αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai epethymei gemisai ten koilian autou apo ton keration on esthion oi hoiroi, kai oudeis edidoy auto.
verses.translation: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.

verses.original: εἰς ἑαυτὸν δὲ ἐλθὼν ⸀ἔφη· Πόσοι μίσθιοι τοῦ πατρός μου ⸀περισσεύονται ἄρτων, ἐγὼ δὲ ⸂λιμῷ ὧδε⸃ ἀπόλλυμαι·
verses.translit: eis eayton de elthon efi* Posoi misthioi tou patros moy perisseyontai arton, ego de limo ode apollymai*
verses.translation: And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!

verses.original: ἀναστὰς πορεύσομαι πρὸς τὸν πατέρα μου καὶ ἐρῶ αὐτῷ· Πάτερ, ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου,
verses.translit: anastas poreysomai pros ton patera moy kai ero auto* Pater, emarton eis ton ouranon kai enopion soy,
verses.translation: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,

verses.original: ⸀οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἄξιος κληθῆναι υἱός σου· ποίησόν με ὡς ἕνα τῶν μισθίων σου.
verses.translit: ouketi eimi axios klithenai yios soy* poiison me os ena ton misthion soy.
verses.translation: And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.

verses.original: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα ⸀ἑαυτοῦ. ἔτι δὲ αὐτοῦ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος εἶδεν αὐτὸν ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη καὶ δραμὼν ἐπέπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai anastas elthen pros ton patera eaytou. eti de autou makran apehontos eiden auton o pater autou kai esplaghnisthi kai dramon epepesen epi ton trahilon autou kai katefilisen auton.
verses.translation: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ⸂ὁ υἱὸς αὐτῷ⸃· Πάτερ, ἥμαρτον εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐνώπιόν σου, ⸀οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἄξιος κληθῆναι υἱός ⸀σου.
verses.translit: eipen de o yios auto* Pater, emarton eis ton ouranon kai enopion soy, ouketi eimi axios klithenai yios soy.
verses.translation: And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ πατὴρ πρὸς τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ· ⸀Ταχὺ ⸀ἐξενέγκατε στολὴν τὴν πρώτην καὶ ἐνδύσατε αὐτόν, καὶ δότε δακτύλιον εἰς τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ καὶ ὑποδήματα εἰς τοὺς πόδας,
verses.translit: eipen de o pater pros tous doyloys autou* Tahu exenegkate stolen ten protin kai endysate auton, kai dote daktylion eis ten heira autou kai upodimata eis tous podas,
verses.translation: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:

verses.original: καὶ ⸀φέρετε τὸν μόσχον τὸν σιτευτόν, θύσατε, καὶ φαγόντες εὐφρανθῶμεν,
verses.translit: kai ferete ton moshon ton siteyton, thysate, kai fagontes eufranthomen,
verses.translation: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it ; and let us eat, and be merry:

verses.original: ὅτι οὗτος ὁ υἱός μου νεκρὸς ἦν καὶ ἀνέζησεν, ⸂ἦν ἀπολωλὼς⸃ καὶ εὑρέθη. καὶ ἤρξαντο εὐφραίνεσθαι.
verses.translit: oti outos o yios moy nekros en kai anezisen, en apololos kai eurethi. kai erxanto eufrainesthai.
verses.translation: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.

verses.original: Ἦν δὲ ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ὁ πρεσβύτερος ἐν ἀγρῷ· καὶ ὡς ἐρχόμενος ἤγγισεν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, ἤκουσεν συμφωνίας καὶ χορῶν,
verses.translit: En de o yios autou o presvyteros en agro* kai os erhomenos eggisen te oikia, ekoysen symfonias kai horon,
verses.translation: Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard musick and dancing.

verses.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ἕνα τῶν παίδων ἐπυνθάνετο τί ⸀ἂν εἴη ταῦτα·
verses.translit: kai proskalesamenos ena ton paidon epynthaneto ti an eii tauta*
verses.translation: And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὅτι Ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἥκει, καὶ ἔθυσεν ὁ πατήρ σου τὸν μόσχον τὸν σιτευτόν, ὅτι ὑγιαίνοντα αὐτὸν ἀπέλαβεν.
verses.translit: o de eipen auto oti O adelfos soy ekei, kai ethysen o patir soy ton moshon ton siteyton, oti ugiainonta auton apelaven.
verses.translation: And he said unto him, Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.

verses.original: ὠργίσθη δὲ καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν εἰσελθεῖν. ὁ ⸀δὲ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ἐξελθὼν παρεκάλει αὐτόν.
verses.translit: orgisthi de kai ouk ethelen eiselthein. o de pater autou exelthon parekalei auton.
verses.translation: And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν τῷ πατρὶ ⸀αὐτοῦ· Ἰδοὺ τοσαῦτα ἔτη δουλεύω σοι καὶ οὐδέποτε ἐντολήν σου παρῆλθον, καὶ ἐμοὶ οὐδέποτε ἔδωκας ἔριφον ἵνα μετὰ τῶν φίλων μου εὐφρανθῶ·
verses.translit: o de apokritheis eipen to patri autou* Idou tosauta eti doyleyo soi kai oudepote entolin soy parelthon, kai emoi oudepote edokas erifon ina meta ton filon moy eufrantho*
verses.translation: And he answering said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:

verses.original: ὅτε δὲ ὁ υἱός σου οὗτος ὁ καταφαγών σου τὸν βίον ⸀μετὰ πορνῶν ἦλθεν, ἔθυσας αὐτῷ τὸν ⸂σιτευτὸν μόσχον⸃.
verses.translit: ote de o yios soy outos o katafagon soy ton vion meta pornon elthen, ethysas auto ton siteyton moshon.
verses.translation: But as soon as this thy son was come, which hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τέκνον, σὺ πάντοτε μετʼ ἐμοῦ εἶ, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐμὰ σά ἐστιν·
verses.translit: o de eipen auto* Teknon, su pantote met' emou ei, kai panta ta ema sa estin*
verses.translation: And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.

verses.original: εὐφρανθῆναι δὲ καὶ χαρῆναι ἔδει, ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου οὗτος νεκρὸς ἦν καὶ ⸀ἔζησεν, καὶ ⸀ἀπολωλὼς καὶ εὑρέθη.
verses.translit: eufranthenai de kai harenai edei, oti o adelfos soy outos nekros en kai ezisen, kai apololos kai eurethi.
verses.translation: It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.

verses.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ⸀μαθητάς· Ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν πλούσιος ὃς εἶχεν οἰκονόμον, καὶ οὗτος διεβλήθη αὐτῷ ὡς διασκορπίζων τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Elegen de kai pros tous mathitas* Anthropos tis en ploysios os eihen oikonomon, kai outos dievlithi auto os diaskorpizon ta uparhonta autou.
verses.translation: And he said also unto his disciples, There was a certain rich man, which had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he had wasted his goods.

verses.original: καὶ φωνήσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Τί τοῦτο ἀκούω περὶ σοῦ; ἀπόδος τὸν λόγον τῆς οἰκονομίας σου, οὐ γὰρ ⸀δύνῃ ἔτι οἰκονομεῖν.
verses.translit: kai fonisas auton eipen auto* Ti touto akoyo peri sou; apodos ton logon tes oikonomias soy, ou gar dyne eti oikonomein.
verses.translation: And he called him, and said unto him, How is it that I hear this of thee? give an account of thy stewardship; for thou mayest be no longer steward.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ ὁ οἰκονόμος· Τί ποιήσω ὅτι ὁ κύριός μου ἀφαιρεῖται τὴν οἰκονομίαν ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ; σκάπτειν οὐκ ἰσχύω, ἐπαιτεῖν αἰσχύνομαι·
verses.translit: eipen de en eayto o oikonomos* Ti poiiso oti o kyrios moy afaireitai ten oikonomian ap' emou; skaptein ouk ishyo, epaitein aishynomai*
verses.translation: Then the steward said within himself, What shall I do? for my lord taketh away from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; to beg I am ashamed.

verses.original: ἔγνων τί ποιήσω, ἵνα ὅταν μετασταθῶ ⸀ἐκ τῆς οἰκονομίας δέξωνταί με εἰς τοὺς οἴκους ⸀ἑαυτῶν.
verses.translit: egnon ti poiiso, ina otan metastatho ek tes oikonomias dexontai me eis tous oikoys eayton.
verses.translation: I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.

verses.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ἕνα ἕκαστον τῶν χρεοφειλετῶν τοῦ κυρίου ἑαυτοῦ ἔλεγεν τῷ πρώτῳ· Πόσον ὀφείλεις τῷ κυρίῳ μου;
verses.translit: kai proskalesamenos ena ekaston ton hreofeileton tou kyrioy eaytou elegen to proto* Poson ofeileis to kyrio moy;
verses.translation: So he called every one of his lord’s debtors unto him , and said unto the first, How much owest thou unto my lord?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἑκατὸν βάτους ἐλαίου· ⸂ὁ δὲ⸃ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Δέξαι σου ⸂τὰ γράμματα⸃ καὶ καθίσας ταχέως γράψον πεντήκοντα.
verses.translit: o de eipen* Ekaton vatoys elaioy* o de eipen auto* Dexai soy ta grammata kai kathisas taheos grapson pentikonta.
verses.translation: And he said, An hundred measures of oil. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and sit down quickly, and write fifty.

verses.original: ἔπειτα ἑτέρῳ εἶπεν· Σὺ δὲ πόσον ὀφείλεις; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἑκατὸν κόρους σίτου· ⸀λέγει αὐτῷ· Δέξαι σου ⸂τὰ γράμματα⸃ καὶ γράψον ὀγδοήκοντα.
verses.translit: epeita etero eipen* Su de poson ofeileis; o de eipen* Ekaton koroys sitoy* legei auto* Dexai soy ta grammata kai grapson ogdoikonta.
verses.translation: Then said he to another, And how much owest thou? And he said, An hundred measures of wheat. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and write fourscore.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπῄνεσεν ὁ κύριος τὸν οἰκονόμον τῆς ἀδικίας ὅτι φρονίμως ἐποίησεν· ὅτι οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου φρονιμώτεροι ὑπὲρ τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ φωτὸς εἰς τὴν γενεὰν τὴν ἑαυτῶν εἰσιν.
verses.translit: kai epenesen o kyrios ton oikonomon tes adikias oti fronimos epoiisen* oti oi yioi tou aionos toytoy fronimoteroi uper tous yious tou fotos eis ten genean ten eayton eisin.
verses.translation: And the lord commended the unjust steward, because he had done wisely: for the children of this world are in their generation wiser than the children of light.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω, ⸂ἑαυτοῖς ποιήσατε⸃ φίλους ἐκ τοῦ μαμωνᾶ τῆς ἀδικίας, ἵνα ὅταν ⸀ἐκλίπῃ δέξωνται ὑμᾶς εἰς τὰς αἰωνίους σκηνάς.
verses.translit: kai ego umin lego, eaytois poiisate filoys ek tou mamona tes adikias, ina otan eklipe dexontai umas eis tas aionioys skinas.
verses.translation: And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.

verses.original: Ὁ πιστὸς ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ καὶ ἐν πολλῷ πιστός ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ ἄδικος καὶ ἐν πολλῷ ἄδικός ἐστιν.
verses.translit: O pistos en elahisto kai en pollo pistos estin, kai o en elahisto adikos kai en pollo adikos estin.
verses.translation: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.

verses.original: εἰ οὖν ἐν τῷ ἀδίκῳ μαμωνᾷ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε, τὸ ἀληθινὸν τίς ὑμῖν πιστεύσει;
verses.translit: ei oun en to adiko mamona pistoi ouk egenesthe, to alithinon tis umin pisteysei;
verses.translation: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches ?

verses.original: καὶ εἰ ἐν τῷ ἀλλοτρίῳ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε, τὸ ⸀ὑμέτερον τίς ⸂δώσει ὑμῖν⸃;
verses.translit: kai ei en to allotrio pistoi ouk egenesthe, to umeteron tis dosei umin;
verses.translation: And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another man’s, who shall give you that which is your own?

verses.original: οὐδεὶς οἰκέτης δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν· ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει. οὐ δύνασθε θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ.
verses.translit: oudeis oiketis dynatai dysi kyriois doyleyein* e gar ton ena misisei kai ton eteron agapisei, e enos anthexetai kai tou eteroy katafronisei. ou dynasthe theo doyleyein kai mamona.
verses.translation: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

verses.original: Ἤκουον δὲ ταῦτα ⸀πάντα οἱ Φαρισαῖοι φιλάργυροι ὑπάρχοντες, καὶ ἐξεμυκτήριζον αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Ekoyon de tauta panta oi Farisaioi filargyroi uparhontes, kai exemyktirizon auton.
verses.translation: And the Pharisees also, who were covetous, heard all these things: and they derided him.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ δικαιοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁ δὲ θεὸς γινώσκει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν· ὅτι τὸ ἐν ἀνθρώποις ὑψηλὸν βδέλυγμα ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: kai eipen autois* Umeis este oi dikaiountes eaytous enopion ton anthropon, o de theos ginoskei tas kardias umon* oti to en anthropois upsilon vdelygma enopion tou theou.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.

verses.original: Ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται ⸀μέχρι Ἰωάννου· ἀπὸ τότε ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ εὐαγγελίζεται καὶ πᾶς εἰς αὐτὴν βιάζεται.
verses.translit: O nomos kai oi profetai mehri Ioannoy* apo tote e vasileia tou theou euaggelizetai kai pas eis auten viazetai.
verses.translation: The law and the prophets were until John: since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and every man presseth into it.

verses.original: Εὐκοπώτερον δέ ἐστιν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν παρελθεῖν ἢ τοῦ νόμου μίαν κεραίαν πεσεῖν.
verses.translit: Eukopoteron de estin ton ouranon kai ten gen parelthein e tou nomoy mian keraian pesein.
verses.translation: And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail.

verses.original: Πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμῶν ἑτέραν μοιχεύει, ⸀καὶ ὁ ἀπολελυμένην ἀπὸ ἀνδρὸς γαμῶν μοιχεύει.
verses.translit: Pas o apolyon ten gynaika autou kai gamon eteran moiheyei, kai o apolelymenin apo andros gamon moiheyei.
verses.translation: Whosoever putteth away his wife, and marrieth another, committeth adultery: and whosoever marrieth her that is put away from her husband committeth adultery.

verses.original: Ἄνθρωπος δέ τις ἦν πλούσιος, καὶ ἐνεδιδύσκετο πορφύραν καὶ βύσσον εὐφραινόμενος καθʼ ἡμέραν λαμπρῶς.
verses.translit: Anthropos de tis en ploysios, kai enedidysketo porfyran kai vysson eufrainomenos kath' emeran lampros.
verses.translation: There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day:

verses.original: πτωχὸς δέ ⸀τις ὀνόματι ⸀Λάζαρος ἐβέβλητο πρὸς τὸν πυλῶνα αὐτοῦ εἱλκωμένος
verses.translit: ptohos de tis onomati Lazaros evevlito pros ton pylona autou eilkomenos
verses.translation: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores,

verses.original: καὶ ἐπιθυμῶν χορτασθῆναι ⸀ἀπὸ τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης τοῦ πλουσίου· ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ κύνες ἐρχόμενοι ⸀ἐπέλειχον τὰ ἕλκη αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai epithymon hortasthenai apo ton piptonton apo tes trapezis tou ploysioy* alla kai oi kynes erhomenoi epeleihon ta elki autou.
verses.translation: And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.

verses.original: ἐγένετο δὲ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πτωχὸν καὶ ἀπενεχθῆναι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀγγέλων εἰς τὸν κόλπον Ἀβραάμ· ἀπέθανεν δὲ καὶ ὁ πλούσιος καὶ ἐτάφη.
verses.translit: egeneto de apothanein ton ptohon kai apenehthenai auton upo ton aggelon eis ton kolpon Avraam* apethanen de kai o ploysios kai etafi.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;

verses.original: καὶ ἐν τῷ ᾅδῃ ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ, ὑπάρχων ἐν βασάνοις, ⸀ὁρᾷ Ἀβραὰμ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν καὶ Λάζαρον ἐν τοῖς κόλποις αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai en to ade eparas tous ofthalmous autou, uparhon en vasanois, ora Avraam apo makrothen kai Lazaron en tois kolpois autou.
verses.translation: And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.

verses.original: καὶ αὐτὸς φωνήσας εἶπεν· Πάτερ Ἀβραάμ, ἐλέησόν με καὶ πέμψον Λάζαρον ἵνα βάψῃ τὸ ἄκρον τοῦ δακτύλου αὐτοῦ ὕδατος καὶ καταψύξῃ τὴν γλῶσσάν μου, ὅτι ὀδυνῶμαι ἐν τῇ φλογὶ ταύτῃ.
verses.translit: kai autos fonisas eipen* Pater Avraam, eleison me kai pempson Lazaron ina vapse to akron tou daktyloy autou udatos kai katapsyxe ten glossan moy, oti odynomai en te flogi tayte.
verses.translation: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ Ἀβραάμ· Τέκνον, μνήσθητι ὅτι ⸀ἀπέλαβες τὰ ἀγαθά σου ἐν τῇ ζωῇ σου, καὶ Λάζαρος ὁμοίως τὰ κακά· νῦν δὲ ὧδε παρακαλεῖται σὺ δὲ ὀδυνᾶσαι.
verses.translit: eipen de Avraam* Teknon, mnisthiti oti apelaves ta agatha soy en te zoe soy, kai Lazaros omoios ta kaka* nun de ode parakaleitai su de odynasai.
verses.translation: But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἐν πᾶσι τούτοις μεταξὺ ἡμῶν καὶ ὑμῶν χάσμα μέγα ἐστήρικται, ὅπως οἱ θέλοντες διαβῆναι ἔνθεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς μὴ δύνωνται, ⸀μηδὲ ἐκεῖθεν πρὸς ἡμᾶς διαπερῶσιν.
verses.translit: kai en pasi toytois metaxu emon kai umon hasma mega estiriktai, opos oi thelontes diavenai enthen pros umas me dynontai, mide ekeithen pros emas diaperosin.
verses.translation: And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.

verses.original: εἶπεν δέ· Ἐρωτῶ ⸂σε οὖν⸃, πάτερ, ἵνα πέμψῃς αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρός μου,
verses.translit: eipen de* Eroto se oun, pater, ina pempses auton eis ton oikon tou patros moy,
verses.translation: Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house:

verses.original: ἔχω γὰρ πέντε ἀδελφούς, ὅπως διαμαρτύρηται αὐτοῖς, ἵνα μὴ καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔλθωσιν εἰς τὸν τόπον τοῦτον τῆς βασάνου.
verses.translit: eho gar pente adelfoys, opos diamartyritai autois, ina me kai autoi elthosin eis ton topon touton tes vasanoy.
verses.translation: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.

verses.original: λέγει ⸀δὲ Ἀβραάμ· Ἔχουσι Μωϋσέα καὶ τοὺς προφήτας· ἀκουσάτωσαν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: legei de Avraam* Ehoysi Moysea kai tous profitas* akoysatosan auton.
verses.translation: Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Οὐχί, πάτερ Ἀβραάμ, ἀλλʼ ἐάν τις ἀπὸ νεκρῶν πορευθῇ πρὸς αὐτοὺς μετανοήσουσιν.
verses.translit: o de eipen* Ouhi, pater Avraam, all' ean tis apo nekron poreythe pros autous metanoisoysin.
verses.translation: And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Εἰ Μωϋσέως καὶ τῶν προφητῶν οὐκ ἀκούουσιν, οὐδʼ ἐάν τις ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ πεισθήσονται.
verses.translit: eipen de auto* Ei Moyseos kai ton profiton ouk akoyoysin, oud' ean tis ek nekron anaste peisthisontai.
verses.translation: And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς ⸀αὐτοῦ· Ἀνένδεκτόν ἐστιν τοῦ ⸂τὰ σκάνδαλα μὴ ἐλθεῖν⸃, ⸂πλὴν οὐαὶ⸃ διʼ οὗ ἔρχεται·
verses.translit: Eipen de pros tous mathitas autou* Anendekton estin tou ta skandala me elthein, plen ouai di' ou erhetai*
verses.translation: Then said he unto the disciples, It is impossible but that offences will come: but woe unto him , through whom they come!

verses.original: λυσιτελεῖ αὐτῷ εἰ ⸂λίθος μυλικὸς⸃ περίκειται περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔρριπται εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν ἢ ἵνα σκανδαλίσῃ ⸂τῶν μικρῶν τούτων ἕνα⸃.
