verses.translit: lysitelei auto ei lithos mylikos perikeitai peri ton trahilon autou kai erriptai eis ten thalassan e ina skandalise ton mikron toyton ena.
verses.translation: It were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea, than that he should offend one of these little ones.

verses.original: προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς. ἐὰν ⸀ἁμάρτῃ ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἐπιτίμησον αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐὰν μετανοήσῃ ἄφες αὐτῷ·
verses.translit: prosehete eaytois. ean amarte o adelfos soy epitimison auto, kai ean metanoise afes auto*
verses.translation: Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν ἑπτάκις τῆς ἡμέρας ⸀ἁμαρτήσῃ εἰς σὲ καὶ ⸀ἑπτάκις ἐπιστρέψῃ ⸂πρὸς σὲ⸃ λέγων· Μετανοῶ, ἀφήσεις αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai ean eptakis tes emeras amartise eis se kai eptakis epistrepse pros se legon* Metanoo, afiseis auto.
verses.translation: And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπαν οἱ ἀπόστολοι τῷ κυρίῳ· Πρόσθες ἡμῖν πίστιν.
verses.translit: Kai eipan oi apostoloi to kyrio* Prosthes emin pistin.
verses.translation: And the apostles said unto the Lord, Increase our faith.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος· Εἰ ἔχετε πίστιν ὡς κόκκον σινάπεως, ἐλέγετε ἂν τῇ συκαμίνῳ ταύτῃ· Ἐκριζώθητι καὶ φυτεύθητι ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ· καὶ ὑπήκουσεν ἂν ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: eipen de o kyrios* Ei ehete pistin os kokkon sinapeos, elegete an te sykamino tayte* Ekrizothiti kai fyteythiti en te thalasse* kai upikoysen an umin.
verses.translation: And the Lord said, If ye had faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye might say unto this sycamine tree, Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou planted in the sea; and it should obey you.

verses.original: Τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν δοῦλον ἔχων ἀροτριῶντα ἢ ποιμαίνοντα, ὃς εἰσελθόντι ἐκ τοῦ ἀγροῦ ἐρεῖ ⸀αὐτῷ· Εὐθέως παρελθὼν ἀνάπεσε,
verses.translit: Tis de ex umon doulon ehon arotrionta e poimainonta, os eiselthonti ek tou agrou erei auto* Eutheos parelthon anapese,
verses.translation: But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding cattle, will say unto him by and by, when he is come from the field, Go and sit down to meat?

verses.original: ἀλλʼ οὐχὶ ἐρεῖ αὐτῷ· Ἑτοίμασον τί δειπνήσω καὶ περιζωσάμενος διακόνει μοι ἕως φάγω καὶ πίω, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα φάγεσαι καὶ πίεσαι σύ;
verses.translit: all' ouhi erei auto* Etoimason ti deipniso kai perizosamenos diakonei moi eos fago kai pio, kai meta tauta fagesai kai piesai sy;
verses.translation: And will not rather say unto him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink?

verses.original: μὴ ⸂ἔχει χάριν⸃ τῷ ⸀δούλῳ ὅτι ἐποίησεν τὰ ⸀διαταχθέντα;
verses.translit: me ehei harin to doylo oti epoiisen ta diatahthenta;
verses.translation: Doth he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I trow not.

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ποιήσητε πάντα τὰ διαταχθέντα ὑμῖν, λέγετε ὅτι Δοῦλοι ἀχρεῖοί ἐσμεν, ⸂ὃ ὠφείλομεν⸃ ποιῆσαι πεποιήκαμεν.
verses.translit: outos kai umeis, otan poiisite panta ta diatahthenta umin, legete oti Douloi ahreioi esmen, o ofeilomen poiesai pepoiikamen.
verses.translation: So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ⸀πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ αὐτὸς διήρχετο διὰ ⸀μέσον Σαμαρείας καὶ Γαλιλαίας.
verses.translit: Kai egeneto en to poreyesthai eis Ieroysalem kai autos diirheto dia meson Samareias kai Galilaias.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.

verses.original: καὶ εἰσερχομένου αὐτοῦ εἴς τινα κώμην ⸀ἀπήντησαν δέκα λεπροὶ ἄνδρες, οἳ ⸀ἔστησαν πόρρωθεν,
verses.translit: kai eiserhomenoy autou eis tina komin apintisan deka leproi andres, oi estisan porrothen,
verses.translation: And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, which stood afar off:

verses.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἦραν φωνὴν λέγοντες· Ἰησοῦ ἐπιστάτα, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς.
verses.translit: kai autoi eran fonen legontes* Iisou epistata, eleison emas.
verses.translation: And they lifted up their voices, and said, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδὼν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες ἐπιδείξατε ἑαυτοὺς τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν. καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτοὺς ἐκαθαρίσθησαν.
verses.translit: kai idon eipen autois* Poreythentes epideixate eaytous tois iereusin. kai egeneto en to upagein autous ekatharisthisan.
verses.translation: And when he saw them , he said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed.

verses.original: εἷς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν, ἰδὼν ὅτι ἰάθη, ὑπέστρεψεν μετὰ φωνῆς μεγάλης δοξάζων τὸν θεόν,
verses.translit: eis de ex auton, idon oti iathi, upestrepsen meta fones megalis doxazon ton theon,
verses.translation: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God,

verses.original: καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ εὐχαριστῶν αὐτῷ· καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Σαμαρίτης.
verses.translit: kai epesen epi prosopon para tous podas autou euhariston auto* kai autos en Samaritis.
verses.translation: And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· ⸀Οὐχὶ οἱ δέκα ἐκαθαρίσθησαν; οἱ δὲ ἐννέα ποῦ;
verses.translit: apokritheis de o Iisous eipen* Ouhi oi deka ekatharisthisan; oi de ennea pou;
verses.translation: And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?

verses.original: οὐχ εὑρέθησαν ὑποστρέψαντες δοῦναι δόξαν τῷ θεῷ εἰ μὴ ὁ ἀλλογενὴς οὗτος;
verses.translit: ouh eurethisan upostrepsantes dounai doxan to theo ei me o allogenes outos;
verses.translation: There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀναστὰς πορεύου· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.
verses.translit: kai eipen auto* Anastas poreyoy* e pistis soy sesoken se.
verses.translation: And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.

verses.original: Ἐπερωτηθεὶς δὲ ὑπὸ τῶν Φαρισαίων πότε ἔρχεται ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς καὶ εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἔρχεται ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ μετὰ παρατηρήσεως,
verses.translit: Eperotitheis de upo ton Farisaion pote erhetai e vasileia tou theou apekrithi autois kai eipen* Ouk erhetai e vasileia tou theou meta paratiriseos,
verses.translation: And when he was demanded of the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God should come, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God cometh not with observation:

verses.original: οὐδὲ ἐροῦσιν· Ἰδοὺ ὧδε ἤ· ⸀Ἐκεῖ· ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἐντὸς ὑμῶν ἐστιν.
verses.translit: oude erousin* Idou ode e* Ekei* idou gar e vasileia tou theou entos umon estin.
verses.translation: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητάς· Ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι ὅτε ἐπιθυμήσετε μίαν τῶν ἡμερῶν τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἰδεῖν καὶ οὐκ ὄψεσθε.
verses.translit: Eipen de pros tous mathitas* Eleysontai emerai ote epithymisete mian ton emeron tou yiou tou anthropoy idein kai ouk opsesthe.
verses.translation: And he said unto the disciples, The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it .

verses.original: καὶ ἐροῦσιν ὑμῖν· Ἰδοὺ ⸂ἐκεῖ· Ἰδοὺ ὧδε⸃· μὴ ἀπέλθητε μηδὲ διώξητε.
verses.translit: kai erousin umin* Idou ekei* Idou ode* me apelthite mide dioxite.
verses.translation: And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them , nor follow them .

verses.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ ⸀ἀστραπὴ ἀστράπτουσα ἐκ τῆς ⸂ὑπὸ τὸν⸃ οὐρανὸν εἰς τὴν ὑπʼ οὐρανὸν λάμπει, οὕτως ἔσται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ⸂ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ αὐτοῦ⸃.
verses.translit: osper gar e astrape astraptoysa ek tes upo ton ouranon eis ten up' ouranon lampei, outos estai o yios tou anthropoy en te emera autou.
verses.translation: For as the lightning, that lighteneth out of the one part under heaven, shineth unto the other part under heaven; so shall also the Son of man be in his day.

verses.original: πρῶτον δὲ δεῖ αὐτὸν πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης.
verses.translit: proton de dei auton polla pathein kai apodokimasthenai apo tes geneas taytis.
verses.translation: But first must he suffer many things, and be rejected of this generation.

verses.original: καὶ καθὼς ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Νῶε, οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
verses.translit: kai kathos egeneto en tais emerais Noe, outos estai kai en tais emerais tou yiou tou anthropoy*
verses.translation: And as it was in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man.

verses.original: ἤσθιον, ἔπινον, ἐγάμουν, ⸀ἐγαμίζοντο, ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας εἰσῆλθεν Νῶε εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν, καὶ ἦλθεν ὁ κατακλυσμὸς καὶ ἀπώλεσεν ⸀πάντας.
verses.translit: esthion, epinon, egamoyn, egamizonto, ahri es emeras eiselthen Noe eis ten kivoton, kai elthen o kataklysmos kai apolesen pantas.
verses.translation: They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.

verses.original: ὁμοίως ⸀καθὼς ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Λώτ· ἤσθιον, ἔπινον, ἠγόραζον, ἐπώλουν, ἐφύτευον, ᾠκοδόμουν·
verses.translit: omoios kathos egeneto en tais emerais Lot* esthion, epinon, egorazon, epoloyn, efyteyon, okodomoyn*
verses.translation: Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot; they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded;

verses.original: ᾗ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ ἐξῆλθεν Λὼτ ἀπὸ Σοδόμων, ἔβρεξεν πῦρ καὶ θεῖον ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἀπώλεσεν ⸀πάντας.
verses.translit: e de emera exelthen Lot apo Sodomon, evrexen pur kai theion ap' ouranou kai apolesen pantas.
verses.translation: But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all.

verses.original: κατὰ ⸂τὰ αὐτὰ⸃ ἔσται ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀποκαλύπτεται.
verses.translit: kata ta auta estai e emera o yios tou anthropoy apokalyptetai.
verses.translation: Even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed.

verses.original: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ὃς ἔσται ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος καὶ τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, μὴ καταβάτω ἆραι αὐτά, καὶ ὁ ⸀ἐν ἀγρῷ ὁμοίως μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω.
verses.translit: en ekeine te emera os estai epi tou domatos kai ta skeyi autou en te oikia, me katavato arai auta, kai o en agro omoios me epistrepsato eis ta opiso.
verses.translation: In that day, he which shall be upon the housetop, and his stuff in the house, let him not come down to take it away: and he that is in the field, let him likewise not return back.

verses.original: μνημονεύετε τῆς γυναικὸς Λώτ.
verses.translit: mnimoneyete tes gynaikos Lot.
verses.translation: Remember Lot’s wife.

verses.original: ὃς ἐὰν ζητήσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ⸀περιποιήσασθαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν, ⸂ὃς δʼ ἂν⸃ ⸀ἀπολέσῃ ζῳογονήσει αὐτήν.
verses.translit: os ean zitise ten psyhen autou peripoiisasthai apolesei autin, os d' an apolese zoogonisei autin.
verses.translation: Whosoever shall seek to save his life shall lose it; and whosoever shall lose his life shall preserve it.

verses.original: λέγω ὑμῖν, ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ ἔσονται δύο ἐπὶ κλίνης μιᾶς, ⸀ὁ εἷς παραλημφθήσεται καὶ ὁ ἕτερος ἀφεθήσεται·
verses.translit: lego umin, tayte te nykti esontai dyo epi klinis mias, o eis paralimfthisetai kai o eteros afethisetai*
verses.translation: I tell you, in that night there shall be two men in one bed; the one shall be taken, and the other shall be left.

verses.original: ⸂ἔσονται δύο⸃ ἀλήθουσαι ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, ⸀ἡ μία παραλημφθήσεται ⸂ἡ δὲ⸃ ἑτέρα ⸀ἀφεθήσεται.
verses.translit: esontai dyo alithoysai epi to auto, e mia paralimfthisetai e de etera afethisetai.
verses.translation: Two women shall be grinding together; the one shall be taken, and the other left.
Two men shall be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ποῦ, κύριε; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅπου τὸ σῶμα, ἐκεῖ ⸂καὶ οἱ ἀετοὶ ἐπισυναχθήσονται⸃.
verses.translit: kai apokrithentes legoysin auto* Pou, kyrie; o de eipen autois* Opoy to soma, ekei kai oi aetoi episynahthisontai.
verses.translation: And they answered and said unto him, Where, Lord? And he said unto them, Wheresoever the body is , thither will the eagles be gathered together.

verses.original: Ἔλεγεν ⸀δὲ παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς πρὸς τὸ δεῖν πάντοτε προσεύχεσθαι ⸀αὐτοὺς καὶ μὴ ἐγκακεῖν,
verses.translit: Elegen de paravolen autois pros to dein pantote proseyhesthai autous kai me egkakein,
verses.translation: And he spake a parable unto them to this end , that men ought always to pray, and not to faint;

verses.original: λέγων· Κριτής τις ἦν ἔν τινι πόλει τὸν θεὸν μὴ φοβούμενος καὶ ἄνθρωπον μὴ ἐντρεπόμενος.
verses.translit: legon* Kritis tis en en tini polei ton theon me fovoymenos kai anthropon me entrepomenos.
verses.translation: Saying, There was in a city a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man:

verses.original: χήρα δὲ ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ καὶ ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγουσα· Ἐκδίκησόν με ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου μου.
verses.translit: hira de en en te polei ekeine kai erheto pros auton legoysa* Ekdikison me apo tou antidikoy moy.
verses.translation: And there was a widow in that city; and she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary.

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ⸀ἤθελεν ἐπὶ χρόνον, μετὰ ⸂ταῦτα δὲ⸃ εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ· Εἰ καὶ τὸν θεὸν οὐ φοβοῦμαι ⸂οὐδὲ ἄνθρωπον⸃ ἐντρέπομαι,
verses.translit: kai ouk ethelen epi hronon, meta tauta de eipen en eayto* Ei kai ton theon ou fovoumai oude anthropon entrepomai,
verses.translation: And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man;

verses.original: διά γε τὸ παρέχειν μοι κόπον τὴν χήραν ταύτην ἐκδικήσω αὐτήν, ἵνα μὴ εἰς τέλος ἐρχομένη ὑπωπιάζῃ με.
verses.translit: dia ge to parehein moi kopon ten hiran taytin ekdikiso autin, ina me eis telos erhomeni upopiaze me.
verses.translation: Yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος· Ἀκούσατε τί ὁ κριτὴς τῆς ἀδικίας λέγει·
verses.translit: eipen de o kyrios* Akoysate ti o krites tes adikias legei*
verses.translation: And the Lord said, Hear what the unjust judge saith.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ θεὸς οὐ μὴ ποιήσῃ τὴν ἐκδίκησιν τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ τῶν βοώντων ⸀αὐτῷ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός, καὶ ⸀μακροθυμεῖ ἐπʼ αὐτοῖς;
verses.translit: o de theos ou me poiise ten ekdikisin ton eklekton autou ton voonton auto emeras kai nyktos, kai makrothymei ep' autois;
verses.translation: And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them?

verses.original: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ποιήσει τὴν ἐκδίκησιν αὐτῶν ἐν τάχει. πλὴν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐλθὼν ἆρα εὑρήσει τὴν πίστιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς;
verses.translit: lego umin oti poiisei ten ekdikisin auton en tahei. plen o yios tou anthropoy elthon ara eurisei ten pistin epi tes ges;
verses.translation: I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ⸀καὶ πρός τινας τοὺς πεποιθότας ἐφʼ ἑαυτοῖς ὅτι εἰσὶν δίκαιοι καὶ ἐξουθενοῦντας τοὺς λοιποὺς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην·
verses.translit: Eipen de kai pros tinas tous pepoithotas ef' eaytois oti eisin dikaioi kai exoythenountas tous loipous ten paravolen taytin*
verses.translation: And he spake this parable unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others:

verses.original: Ἄνθρωποι δύο ἀνέβησαν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν προσεύξασθαι, ⸀ὁ εἷς Φαρισαῖος καὶ ὁ ἕτερος τελώνης.
verses.translit: Anthropoi dyo anevisan eis to ieron proseyxasthai, o eis Farisaios kai o eteros telonis.
verses.translation: Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.

verses.original: ὁ Φαρισαῖος σταθεὶς ⸂πρὸς ἑαυτὸν ταῦτα⸃ προσηύχετο· Ὁ θεός, εὐχαριστῶ σοι ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ⸀ὥσπερ οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ἅρπαγες, ἄδικοι, μοιχοί, ἢ καὶ ὡς οὗτος ὁ τελώνης·
verses.translit: o Farisaios statheis pros eayton tauta prosiyheto* O theos, euharisto soi oti ouk eimi osper oi loipoi ton anthropon, arpages, adikoi, moihoi, e kai os outos o telonis*
verses.translation: The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are , extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican.

verses.original: νηστεύω δὶς τοῦ σαββάτου, ⸀ἀποδεκατῶ πάντα ὅσα κτῶμαι.
verses.translit: nisteyo dis tou savvatoy, apodekato panta osa ktomai.
verses.translation: I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess.

verses.original: ⸂ὁ δὲ⸃ τελώνης μακρόθεν ἑστὼς οὐκ ἤθελεν οὐδὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ⸂ἐπᾶραι εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν⸃, ἀλλʼ ⸀ἔτυπτε τὸ στῆθος ⸀αὐτοῦ λέγων· Ὁ θεός, ἱλάσθητί μοι τῷ ἁμαρτωλῷ.
verses.translit: o de telonis makrothen estos ouk ethelen oude tous ofthalmous eparai eis ton ouranon, all' etypte to stethos autou legon* O theos, ilasthiti moi to amartolo.
verses.translation: And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner.

verses.original: λέγω ὑμῖν, κατέβη οὗτος δεδικαιωμένος εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ ⸂παρʼ ἐκεῖνον⸃· ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὑψῶν ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται, ὁ δὲ ταπεινῶν ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται.
verses.translit: lego umin, katevi outos dedikaiomenos eis ton oikon autou par' ekeinon* oti pas o upson eayton tapeinothisetai, o de tapeinon eayton upsothisetai.
verses.translation: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

verses.original: Προσέφερον δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ τὰ βρέφη ἵνα αὐτῶν ἅπτηται· ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ⸀ἐπετίμων αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: Proseferon de auto kai ta vrefi ina auton aptitai* idontes de oi mathitai epetimon autois.
verses.translation: And they brought unto him also infants, that he would touch them: but when his disciples saw it , they rebuked them.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ⸂προσεκαλέσατο αὐτὰ λέγων⸃· Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με καὶ μὴ κωλύετε αὐτά, τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: o de Iisous prosekalesato auta legon* Afete ta paidia erhesthai pros me kai me kolyete auta, ton gar toioyton estin e vasileia tou theou.
verses.translation: But Jesus called them unto him , and said, Suffer little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.

verses.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὃς ⸀ἂν μὴ δέξηται τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ὡς παιδίον, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτήν.
verses.translit: amen lego umin, os an me dexitai ten vasileian tou theou os paidion, ou me eiselthe eis autin.
verses.translation: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child shall in no wise enter therein.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐπηρώτησέν τις αὐτὸν ἄρχων λέγων· Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ, τί ποιήσας ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω;
verses.translit: Kai epirotisen tis auton arhon legon* Didaskale agathe, ti poiisas zoen aionion klironomiso;
verses.translation: And a certain ruler asked him, saying, Good Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν; οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός.
verses.translit: eipen de auto o Iisous* Ti me legeis agathon; oudeis agathos ei me eis o theos.
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? none is good, save one, that is , God.

verses.original: τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας· Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς, Μὴ φονεύσῃς, Μὴ κλέψῃς, Μὴ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς, Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν ⸀μητέρα.
verses.translit: tas entolas oidas* Me moiheyses, Me foneyses, Me klepses, Me pseydomartyrises, Tima ton patera soy kai ten mitera.
verses.translation: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honour thy father and thy mother.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ταῦτα πάντα ⸀ἐφύλαξα ἐκ νεότητος ⸀μου.
verses.translit: o de eipen* Tauta panta efylaxa ek neotitos moy.
verses.translation: And he said, All these have I kept from my youth up.

verses.original: ἀκούσας ⸀δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἔτι ἕν σοι λείπει· πάντα ὅσα ἔχεις πώλησον καὶ διάδος πτωχοῖς, καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν ⸀οὐρανοῖς, καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι.
verses.translit: akoysas de o Iisous eipen auto* Eti en soi leipei* panta osa eheis polison kai diados ptohois, kai exeis thisayron en ouranois, kai deuro akoloythei moi.
verses.translation: Now when Jesus heard these things, he said unto him, Yet lackest thou one thing: sell all that thou hast, and distribute unto the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας ταῦτα περίλυπος ⸀ἐγενήθη, ἦν γὰρ πλούσιος σφόδρα.
verses.translit: o de akoysas tauta perilypos egenithi, en gar ploysios sfodra.
verses.translation: And when he heard this, he was very sorrowful: for he was very rich.

verses.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ αὐτὸν ὁ ⸀Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Πῶς δυσκόλως οἱ τὰ χρήματα ἔχοντες ⸂εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσπορεύονται⸃·
verses.translit: Idon de auton o Iisous eipen* Pos dyskolos oi ta hrimata ehontes eis ten vasileian tou theou eisporeyontai*
verses.translation: And when Jesus saw that he was very sorrowful, he said, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!

verses.original: εὐκοπώτερον γάρ ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ ⸂τρήματος βελόνης⸃ εἰσελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν.
verses.translit: eukopoteron gar estin kamilon dia trimatos velonis eiselthein e ploysion eis ten vasileian tou theou eiselthein.
verses.translation: For it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

verses.original: Εἶπαν δὲ οἱ ἀκούσαντες· Καὶ τίς δύναται σωθῆναι;
verses.translit: Eipan de oi akoysantes* Kai tis dynatai sothenai;
verses.translation: And they that heard it said, Who then can be saved?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Τὰ ἀδύνατα παρὰ ἀνθρώποις δυνατὰ ⸂παρὰ τῷ θεῷ ἐστιν⸃.
verses.translit: o de eipen* Ta adynata para anthropois dynata para to theo estin.
verses.translation: And he said, The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ⸀ὁ Πέτρος· Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ⸂ἀφέντες τὰ ἴδια⸃ ἠκολουθήσαμέν σοι.
verses.translit: Eipen de o Petros* Idou emeis afentes ta idia ekoloythisamen soi.
verses.translation: Then Peter said, Lo, we have left all, and followed thee.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδείς ἐστιν ὃς ἀφῆκεν οἰκίαν ἢ ⸂γυναῖκα ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ γονεῖς⸃ ἢ τέκνα ἕνεκεν τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ,
verses.translit: o de eipen autois* Amen lego umin oti oudeis estin os afeken oikian e gynaika e adelfous e goneis e tekna eneken tes vasileias tou theou,
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or parents, or brethren, or wife, or children, for the kingdom of God’s sake,

verses.original: ὃς ⸀οὐχὶ μὴ ⸀ἀπολάβῃ πολλαπλασίονα ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ καὶ ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
verses.translit: os ouhi me apolave pollaplasiona en to kairo toyto kai en to aioni to erhomeno zoen aionion.
verses.translation: Who shall not receive manifold more in this present time, and in the world to come life everlasting.

verses.original: Παραλαβὼν δὲ τοὺς δώδεκα εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς ⸀Ἰερουσαλήμ, καὶ τελεσθήσεται πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα διὰ τῶν προφητῶν τῷ υἱῷ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
verses.translit: Paralavon de tous dodeka eipen pros autoys* Idou anavainomen eis Ieroysalim, kai telesthisetai panta ta gegrammena dia ton profiton to yio tou anthropoy*
verses.translation: Then he took unto him the twelve, and said unto them, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished.

verses.original: παραδοθήσεται γὰρ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν καὶ ἐμπαιχθήσεται καὶ ὑβρισθήσεται καὶ ἐμπτυσθήσεται,
verses.translit: paradothisetai gar tois ethnesin kai empaihthisetai kai uvristhisetai kai emptysthisetai,
verses.translation: For he shall be delivered unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and spitefully entreated, and spitted on:

verses.original: καὶ μαστιγώσαντες ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ ἀναστήσεται.
verses.translit: kai mastigosantes apoktenousin auton, kai te emera te trite anastisetai.
verses.translation: And they shall scourge him , and put him to death: and the third day he shall rise again.

verses.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ οὐδὲν τούτων συνῆκαν, καὶ ἦν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο κεκρυμμένον ἀπʼ αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐκ ἐγίνωσκον τὰ λεγόμενα.
verses.translit: kai autoi ouden toyton synekan, kai en to Rema touto kekrymmenon ap' auton, kai ouk eginoskon ta legomena.
verses.translation: And they understood none of these things: and this saying was hid from them, neither knew they the things which were spoken.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ἐγγίζειν αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰεριχὼ τυφλός τις ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ⸀ἐπαιτῶν.
verses.translit: Egeneto de en to eggizein auton eis Ieriho tyflos tis ekathito para ten odon epaiton.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that as he was come nigh unto Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the way side begging:

verses.original: ἀκούσας δὲ ὄχλου διαπορευομένου ἐπυνθάνετο ⸀τί εἴη τοῦτο·
verses.translit: akoysas de ohloy diaporeyomenoy epynthaneto ti eii touto*
verses.translation: And hearing the multitude pass by, he asked what it meant.

verses.original: ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ αὐτῷ ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος παρέρχεται.
verses.translit: apiggeilan de auto oti Iisous o Nazoraios parerhetai.
verses.translation: And they told him, that Jesus of Nazareth passeth by.

verses.original: καὶ ἐβόησεν λέγων· Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ Δαυίδ, ἐλέησόν με.
verses.translit: kai evoisen legon* Iisou yie Dayid, eleison me.
verses.translation: And he cried, saying, Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me.

verses.original: καὶ οἱ προάγοντες ἐπετίμων αὐτῷ ἵνα ⸀σιγήσῃ· αὐτὸς δὲ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἔκραζεν· Υἱὲ Δαυίδ, ἐλέησόν με.
verses.translit: kai oi proagontes epetimon auto ina sigise* autos de pollo mallon ekrazen* Yie Dayid, eleison me.
verses.translation: And they which went before rebuked him, that he should hold his peace: but he cried so much the more, Thou Son of David, have mercy on me.

verses.original: σταθεὶς δὲ ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν ἀχθῆναι πρὸς αὐτόν. ἐγγίσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτόν·
verses.translit: statheis de o Iisous ekeleysen auton ahthenai pros auton. eggisantos de autou epirotisen auton*
verses.translation: And Jesus stood, and commanded him to be brought unto him: and when he was come near, he asked him,

verses.original: ⸀Τί σοι θέλεις ποιήσω; ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Κύριε, ἵνα ἀναβλέψω.
verses.translit: Ti soi theleis poiiso; o de eipen* Kyrie, ina anavlepso.
verses.translation: Saying, What wilt thou that I shall do unto thee? And he said, Lord, that I may receive my sight.

verses.original: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀνάβλεψον· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.
verses.translit: kai o Iisous eipen auto* Anavlepson* e pistis soy sesoken se.
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto him, Receive thy sight: thy faith hath saved thee.

verses.original: καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀνέβλεψεν, καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ δοξάζων τὸν θεόν. καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἰδὼν ἔδωκεν αἶνον τῷ θεῷ.
verses.translit: kai parahrema anevlepsen, kai ekoloythei auto doxazon ton theon. kai pas o laos idon edoken ainon to theo.
verses.translation: And immediately he received his sight, and followed him, glorifying God: and all the people, when they saw it , gave praise unto God.

verses.original: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν διήρχετο τὴν Ἰεριχώ.
verses.translit: Kai eiselthon diirheto ten Ieriho.
verses.translation: And Jesus entered and passed through Jericho.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι ⸀καλούμενος Ζακχαῖος, καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἀρχιτελώνης καὶ ⸀αὐτὸς πλούσιος·
verses.translit: kai idou aner onomati kaloymenos Zakhaios, kai autos en arhitelonis kai autos ploysios*
verses.translation: And, behold, there was a man named Zacchæus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.

verses.original: καὶ ἐζήτει ἰδεῖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν τίς ἐστιν, καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου ὅτι τῇ ἡλικίᾳ μικρὸς ἦν.
verses.translit: kai ezitei idein ton Iisoun tis estin, kai ouk edynato apo tou ohloy oti te elikia mikros en.
verses.translation: And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature.

verses.original: καὶ προδραμὼν ⸂εἰς τὸ⸃ ἔμπροσθεν ἀνέβη ἐπὶ συκομορέαν ἵνα ἴδῃ αὐτόν, ὅτι ἐκείνης ἤμελλεν διέρχεσθαι.
verses.translit: kai prodramon eis to emprosthen anevi epi sykomorean ina ide auton, oti ekeinis emellen dierhesthai.
verses.translation: And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way .

verses.original: καὶ ὡς ἦλθεν ἐπὶ τὸν τόπον, ἀναβλέψας ὁ ⸀Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ζακχαῖε, σπεύσας κατάβηθι, σήμερον γὰρ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ σου δεῖ με μεῖναι.
verses.translit: kai os elthen epi ton topon, anavlepsas o Iisous eipen pros auton* Zakhaie, speysas katavithi, simeron gar en to oiko soy dei me meinai.
verses.translation: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zacchæus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.

verses.original: καὶ σπεύσας κατέβη, καὶ ὑπεδέξατο αὐτὸν χαίρων.
verses.translit: kai speysas katevi, kai upedexato auton hairon.
verses.translation: And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδόντες πάντες διεγόγγυζον λέγοντες ὅτι Παρὰ ἁμαρτωλῷ ἀνδρὶ εἰσῆλθεν καταλῦσαι.
verses.translit: kai idontes pantes diegoggyzon legontes oti Para amartolo andri eiselthen katalusai.
verses.translation: And when they saw it , they all murmured, saying, That he was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner.

verses.original: σταθεὶς δὲ Ζακχαῖος εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν κύριον· Ἰδοὺ τὰ ⸀ἡμίσιά ⸂μου τῶν ὑπαρχόντων⸃, κύριε, ⸂τοῖς πτωχοῖς δίδωμι⸃, καὶ εἴ τινός τι ἐσυκοφάντησα ἀποδίδωμι τετραπλοῦν.
verses.translit: statheis de Zakhaios eipen pros ton kyrion* Idou ta emisia moy ton uparhonton, kyrie, tois ptohois didomi, kai ei tinos ti esykofantisa apodidomi tetraploun.
verses.translation: And Zacchæus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Σήμερον σωτηρία τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ ἐγένετο, καθότι καὶ αὐτὸς υἱὸς Ἀβραάμ ἐστιν·
verses.translit: eipen de pros auton o Iisous oti Simeron sotiria to oiko toyto egeneto, kathoti kai autos yios Avraam estin*
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.

verses.original: ἦλθεν γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ζητῆσαι καὶ σῶσαι τὸ ἀπολωλός.
verses.translit: elthen gar o yios tou anthropoy zitesai kai sosai to apololos.
verses.translation: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

verses.original: Ἀκουόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ταῦτα προσθεὶς εἶπεν παραβολὴν διὰ τὸ ἐγγὺς ⸂εἶναι Ἰερουσαλὴμ αὐτὸν⸃ καὶ δοκεῖν αὐτοὺς ὅτι παραχρῆμα μέλλει ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἀναφαίνεσθαι·
verses.translit: Akoyonton de auton tauta prostheis eipen paravolen dia to eggus einai Ieroysalem auton kai dokein autous oti parahrema mellei e vasileia tou theou anafainesthai*
verses.translation: And as they heard these things, he added and spake a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God should immediately appear.

verses.original: εἶπεν οὖν· Ἄνθρωπός τις εὐγενὴς ἐπορεύθη εἰς χώραν μακρὰν λαβεῖν ἑαυτῷ βασιλείαν καὶ ὑποστρέψαι.
verses.translit: eipen oun* Anthropos tis eugenes eporeythi eis horan makran lavein eayto vasileian kai upostrepsai.
verses.translation: He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.

verses.original: καλέσας δὲ δέκα δούλους ἑαυτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς δέκα μνᾶς καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· ⸀Πραγματεύσασθε ⸂ἐν ᾧ⸃ ἔρχομαι.
verses.translit: kalesas de deka doyloys eaytou edoken autois deka mnas kai eipen pros autoys* Pragmateysasthe en o erhomai.
verses.translation: And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ πολῖται αὐτοῦ ἐμίσουν αὐτόν, καὶ ἀπέστειλαν πρεσβείαν ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Οὐ θέλομεν τοῦτον βασιλεῦσαι ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς.
verses.translit: oi de politai autou emisoyn auton, kai apesteilan presveian opiso autou legontes* Ou thelomen touton vasileusai ef' emas.
verses.translation: But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἐπανελθεῖν αὐτὸν λαβόντα τὴν βασιλείαν καὶ εἶπεν φωνηθῆναι αὐτῷ τοὺς δούλους τούτους οἷς ⸀δεδώκει τὸ ἀργύριον, ἵνα ⸀γνοῖ τί ⸀διεπραγματεύσαντο.
verses.translit: kai egeneto en to epanelthein auton lavonta ten vasileian kai eipen fonithenai auto tous doyloys toytoys ois dedokei to argyrion, ina gnoi ti diepragmateysanto.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that when he was returned, having received the kingdom, then he commanded these servants to be called unto him, to whom he had given the money, that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.

verses.original: παρεγένετο δὲ ὁ πρῶτος λέγων· Κύριε, ἡ μνᾶ σου ⸂δέκα προσηργάσατο⸃ μνᾶς.
verses.translit: paregeneto de o protos legon* Kyrie, e mna soy deka prosirgasato mnas.
verses.translation: Then came the first, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· ⸀Εὖγε, ἀγαθὲ δοῦλε, ὅτι ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ πιστὸς ἐγένου, ἴσθι ἐξουσίαν ἔχων ἐπάνω δέκα πόλεων.
verses.translit: kai eipen auto* Euge, agathe doule, oti en elahisto pistos egenoy, isthi exoysian ehon epano deka poleon.
verses.translation: And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.

verses.original: καὶ ἦλθεν ὁ δεύτερος λέγων· ⸂Ἡ μνᾶ σου, κύριε⸃, ἐποίησεν πέντε μνᾶς.
verses.translit: kai elthen o deyteros legon* E mna soy, kyrie, epoiisen pente mnas.
verses.translation: And the second came, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ καὶ τούτῳ· Καὶ σὺ ⸂ἐπάνω γίνου⸃ πέντε πόλεων.
verses.translit: eipen de kai toyto* Kai su epano ginoy pente poleon.
verses.translation: And he said likewise to him, Be thou also over five cities.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ὁ ἕτερος ἦλθεν λέγων· Κύριε, ἰδοὺ ἡ μνᾶ σου ἣν εἶχον ἀποκειμένην ἐν σουδαρίῳ·
verses.translit: kai o eteros elthen legon* Kyrie, idou e mna soy en eihon apokeimenin en soydario*
verses.translation: And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin:

verses.original: ἐφοβούμην γάρ σε ὅτι ἄνθρωπος αὐστηρὸς εἶ, αἴρεις ὃ οὐκ ἔθηκας καὶ θερίζεις ὃ οὐκ ἔσπειρας.
verses.translit: efovoymin gar se oti anthropos austiros ei, aireis o ouk ethikas kai therizeis o ouk espeiras.
verses.translation: For I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up that thou layedst not down, and reapest that thou didst not sow.

verses.original: ⸀λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἐκ τοῦ στόματός σου κρίνω σε, πονηρὲ δοῦλε· ᾔδεις ὅτι ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος αὐστηρός εἰμι, αἴρων ὃ οὐκ ἔθηκα καὶ θερίζων ὃ οὐκ ἔσπειρα;
verses.translit: legei auto* Ek tou stomatos soy krino se, ponire doule* edeis oti ego anthropos austiros eimi, airon o ouk ethika kai therizon o ouk espeira;
verses.translation: And he saith unto him, Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant. Thou knewest that I was an austere man, taking up that I laid not down, and reaping that I did not sow:

verses.original: καὶ διὰ τί οὐκ ἔδωκάς ⸂μου τὸ ἀργύριον⸃ ἐπὶ τράπεζαν; κἀγὼ ἐλθὼν σὺν τόκῳ ἂν ⸂αὐτὸ ἔπραξα⸃.
verses.translit: kai dia ti ouk edokas moy to argyrion epi trapezan; kago elthon sun toko an auto epraxa.
verses.translation: Wherefore then gavest not thou my money into the bank, that at my coming I might have required mine own with usury?

verses.original: καὶ τοῖς παρεστῶσιν εἶπεν· Ἄρατε ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ τὴν μνᾶν καὶ δότε τῷ τὰς δέκα μνᾶς ἔχοντι—
verses.translit: kai tois parestosin eipen* Arate ap' autou ten mnan kai dote to tas deka mnas ehonti--
verses.translation: And he said unto them that stood by, Take from him the pound, and give it to him that hath ten pounds.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἔχει δέκα μνᾶς—
verses.translit: kai eipan auto* Kyrie, ehei deka mnas--
verses.translation: (And they said unto him, Lord, he hath ten pounds.)

verses.original: ⸀λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι παντὶ τῷ ἔχοντι δοθήσεται, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ μὴ ἔχοντος καὶ ὃ ἔχει ⸀ἀρθήσεται.
verses.translit: lego umin oti panti to ehonti dothisetai, apo de tou me ehontos kai o ehei arthisetai.
verses.translation: For I say unto you, That unto every one which hath shall be given; and from him that hath not, even that he hath shall be taken away from him.

verses.original: πλὴν τοὺς ἐχθρούς μου ⸀τούτους τοὺς μὴ θελήσαντάς με βασιλεῦσαι ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς ἀγάγετε ὧδε καὶ κατασφάξατε ⸀αὐτοὺς ἔμπροσθέν μου.
verses.translit: plen tous ehthroys moy toytoys tous me thelisantas me vasileusai ep' autous agagete ode kai katasfaxate autous emprosthen moy.
verses.translation: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.

verses.original: Καὶ εἰπὼν ταῦτα ἐπορεύετο ἔμπροσθεν ἀναβαίνων εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
verses.translit: Kai eipon tauta eporeyeto emprosthen anavainon eis Ierosolyma.
verses.translation: And when he had thus spoken, he went before, ascending up to Jerusalem.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἤγγισεν εἰς Βηθφαγὴ καὶ Βηθανίαν πρὸς τὸ ὄρος τὸ καλούμενον Ἐλαιῶν, ἀπέστειλεν δύο τῶν ⸀μαθητῶν
verses.translit: Kai egeneto os eggisen eis Vithfage kai Vithanian pros to oros to kaloymenon Elaion, apesteilen dyo ton mathiton
verses.translation: And it came to pass, when he was come nigh to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called the mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples,

verses.original: ⸀λέγων· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν κατέναντι κώμην, ἐν ᾗ εἰσπορευόμενοι εὑρήσετε πῶλον δεδεμένον, ἐφʼ ὃν οὐδεὶς πώποτε ἀνθρώπων ἐκάθισεν, ⸀καὶ λύσαντες αὐτὸν ἀγάγετε.
verses.translit: legon* Upagete eis ten katenanti komin, en e eisporeyomenoi eurisete polon dedemenon, ef' on oudeis popote anthropon ekathisen, kai lysantes auton agagete.
verses.translation: Saying, Go ye into the village over against you ; in the which at your entering ye shall find a colt tied, whereon yet never man sat: loose him, and bring him hither .

verses.original: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμᾶς ἐρωτᾷ· Διὰ τί λύετε; οὕτως ⸀ἐρεῖτε ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχει.
verses.translit: kai ean tis umas erota* Dia ti lyete; outos ereite oti O kyrios autou hreian ehei.
verses.translation: And if any man ask you, Why do ye loose him ? thus shall ye say unto him, Because the Lord hath need of him.

verses.original: ἀπελθόντες δὲ οἱ ἀπεσταλμένοι εὗρον καθὼς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: apelthontes de oi apestalmenoi euron kathos eipen autois.
verses.translation: And they that were sent went their way, and found even as he had said unto them.

verses.original: λυόντων δὲ αὐτῶν τὸν πῶλον εἶπαν οἱ κύριοι αὐτοῦ πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί λύετε τὸν πῶλον;
verses.translit: lyonton de auton ton polon eipan oi kyrioi autou pros autoys* Ti lyete ton polon;
verses.translation: And as they were loosing the colt, the owners thereof said unto them, Why loose ye the colt?

verses.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν ⸀ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχει.
verses.translit: oi de eipan oti O kyrios autou hreian ehei.
verses.translation: And they said, The Lord hath need of him.

verses.original: καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ἐπιρίψαντες ⸀αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐπὶ τὸν πῶλον ἐπεβίβασαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν·
verses.translit: kai egagon auton pros ton Iisoun, kai epiripsantes auton ta imatia epi ton polon epevivasan ton Iisoun*
verses.translation: And they brought him to Jesus: and they cast their garments upon the colt, and they set Jesus thereon.

verses.original: πορευομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ὑπεστρώννυον τὰ ἱμάτια ⸀ἑαυτῶν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.
verses.translit: poreyomenoy de autou upestronnyon ta imatia eayton en te odo.
verses.translation: And as he went, they spread their clothes in the way.

verses.original: ἐγγίζοντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἤδη πρὸς τῇ καταβάσει τοῦ Ὄρους τῶν Ἐλαιῶν ἤρξαντο ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος τῶν μαθητῶν χαίροντες αἰνεῖν τὸν θεὸν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ περὶ ⸀πασῶν ὧν εἶδον δυνάμεων,
verses.translit: eggizontos de autou edi pros te katavasei tou Oroys ton Elaion erxanto apan to plethos ton mathiton hairontes ainein ton theon fone megale peri pason on eidon dynameon,
verses.translation: And when he was come nigh, even now at the descent of the mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works that they had seen;

verses.original: λέγοντες· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ⸀βασιλεὺς ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου· ⸂ἐν οὐρανῷ εἰρήνη⸃ καὶ δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις.
verses.translit: legontes* Eulogimenos o erhomenos vasileus en onomati kyrioy* en ourano eirini kai doxa en upsistois.
verses.translation: Saying, Blessed be the King that cometh in the name of the Lord: peace in heaven, and glory in the highest.

verses.original: καί τινες τῶν Φαρισαίων ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν· Διδάσκαλε, ἐπιτίμησον τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου.
verses.translit: kai tines ton Farisaion apo tou ohloy eipan pros auton* Didaskale, epitimison tois mathitais soy.
verses.translation: And some of the Pharisees from among the multitude said unto him, Master, rebuke thy disciples.

verses.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ⸀εἶπεν· Λέγω ὑμῖν, ⸀ὅτι ἐὰν οὗτοι ⸀σιωπήσουσιν, οἱ λίθοι ⸀κράξουσιν.
verses.translit: kai apokritheis eipen* Lego umin, oti ean outoi siopisoysin, oi lithoi kraxoysin.
verses.translation: And he answered and said unto them, I tell you that, if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out.

verses.original: Καὶ ὡς ἤγγισεν, ἰδὼν τὴν πόλιν ἔκλαυσεν ἐπʼ ⸀αὐτήν,
verses.translit: Kai os eggisen, idon ten polin eklaysen ep' autin,
verses.translation: And when he was come near, he beheld the city, and wept over it,

verses.original: λέγων ὅτι Εἰ ἔγνως ⸂ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ταύτῃ καὶ σὺ⸃ τὰ πρὸς ⸀εἰρήνην— νῦν δὲ ἐκρύβη ἀπὸ ὀφθαλμῶν σου.
verses.translit: legon oti Ei egnos en te emera tayte kai su ta pros eirinin-- nun de ekryvi apo ofthalmon soy.
verses.translation: Saying, If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.

verses.original: ὅτι ἥξουσιν ἡμέραι ἐπὶ σὲ καὶ ⸀παρεμβαλοῦσιν οἱ ἐχθροί σου χάρακά σοι καὶ περικυκλώσουσίν σε καὶ συνέξουσίν σε πάντοθεν,
verses.translit: oti exoysin emerai epi se kai paremvalousin oi ehthroi soy haraka soi kai perikyklosoysin se kai synexoysin se pantothen,
verses.translation: For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side,

verses.original: καὶ ἐδαφιοῦσίν σε καὶ τὰ τέκνα σου ἐν σοί, καὶ οὐκ ἀφήσουσιν ⸂λίθον ἐπὶ λίθον ἐν σοί⸃, ἀνθʼ ὧν οὐκ ἔγνως τὸν καιρὸν τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς σου.
verses.translit: kai edafiousin se kai ta tekna soy en soi, kai ouk afisoysin lithon epi lithon en soi, anth' on ouk egnos ton kairon tes episkopes soy.
verses.translation: And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.

verses.original: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἤρξατο ἐκβάλλειν τοὺς ⸀πωλοῦντας,
verses.translit: Kai eiselthon eis to ieron erxato ekvallein tous polountas,
verses.translation: And he went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold therein, and them that bought;

verses.original: λέγων αὐτοῖς· Γέγραπται· ⸂Καὶ ἔσται⸃ ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος ⸀προσευχῆς, ὑμεῖς δὲ αὐτὸν ἐποιήσατε σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.
verses.translit: legon autois* Gegraptai* Kai estai o oikos moy oikos proseyhes, umeis de auton epoiisate spilaion leston.
verses.translation: Saying unto them, It is written, My house is the house of prayer: but ye have made it a den of thieves.

verses.original: Καὶ ἦν διδάσκων τὸ καθʼ ἡμέραν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ· οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν ἀπολέσαι καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι τοῦ λαοῦ,
verses.translit: Kai en didaskon to kath' emeran en to iero* oi de arhiereis kai oi grammateis ezitoyn auton apolesai kai oi protoi tou laou,
verses.translation: And he taught daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the chief of the people sought to destroy him,

verses.original: καὶ οὐχ ⸀εὕρισκον τὸ τί ποιήσωσιν, ὁ λαὸς γὰρ ἅπας ἐξεκρέματο αὐτοῦ ἀκούων.
verses.translit: kai ouh euriskon to ti poiisosin, o laos gar apas exekremato autou akoyon.
verses.translation: And could not find what they might do: for all the people were very attentive to hear him.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ⸀ἡμερῶν διδάσκοντος αὐτοῦ τὸν λαὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ εὐαγγελιζομένου ἐπέστησαν οἱ ⸀ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς σὺν τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις,
verses.translit: Kai egeneto en mia ton emeron didaskontos autou ton laon en to iero kai euaggelizomenoy epestisan oi arhiereis kai oi grammateis sun tois presvyterois,
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that on one of those days, as he taught the people in the temple, and preached the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes came upon him with the elders,

verses.original: καὶ εἶπαν ⸂λέγοντες πρὸς αὐτόν⸃· Εἰπὸν ἡμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς, ἢ τίς ἐστιν ὁ δούς σοι τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην;
verses.translit: kai eipan legontes pros auton* Eipon emin en poia exoysia tauta poieis, e tis estin o doys soi ten exoysian taytin;
verses.translation: And spake unto him, saying, Tell us, by what authority doest thou these things? or who is he that gave thee this authority?

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐρωτήσω ὑμᾶς ⸀κἀγὼ λόγον, καὶ εἴπατέ μοι·
verses.translit: apokritheis de eipen pros autoys* Erotiso umas kago logon, kai eipate moi*
verses.translation: And he answered and said unto them, I will also ask you one thing; and answer me:

verses.original: Τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἦν ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων;
verses.translit: To vaptisma Ioannoy ex ouranou en e ex anthropon;
verses.translation: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men?

verses.original: οἱ δὲ συνελογίσαντο πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες ὅτι Ἐὰν εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ἐρεῖ· Διὰ τί οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ;
verses.translit: oi de synelogisanto pros eaytous legontes oti Ean eipomen* Ex ouranou, erei* Dia ti ouk episteysate auto;
verses.translation: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then believed ye him not?

verses.original: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων, ⸂ὁ λαὸς ἅπας⸃ καταλιθάσει ἡμᾶς, πεπεισμένος γάρ ἐστιν Ἰωάννην προφήτην εἶναι·
verses.translit: ean de eipomen* Ex anthropon, o laos apas katalithasei emas, pepeismenos gar estin Ioannin profitin einai*
verses.translation: But and if we say, Of men; all the people will stone us: for they be persuaded that John was a prophet.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπεκρίθησαν μὴ εἰδέναι πόθεν.
verses.translit: kai apekrithisan me eidenai pothen.
verses.translation: And they answered, that they could not tell whence it was .

verses.original: καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ.
verses.translit: kai o Iisous eipen autois* Oude ego lego umin en poia exoysia tauta poio.
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.

verses.original: Ἤρξατο δὲ πρὸς τὸν λαὸν λέγειν τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην· ⸀Ἄνθρωπος ἐφύτευσεν ἀμπελῶνα, καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν χρόνους ἱκανούς.
verses.translit: Erxato de pros ton laon legein ten paravolen taytin* Anthropos efyteysen ampelona, kai exedeto auton georgois, kai apedimisen hronoys ikanoys.
verses.translation: Then began he to speak to the people this parable; A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it forth to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ καιρῷ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς δοῦλον, ἵνα ἀπὸ τοῦ καρποῦ τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος ⸀δώσουσιν αὐτῷ· οἱ δὲ γεωργοὶ ⸂ἐξαπέστειλαν αὐτὸν δείραντες⸃ κενόν.
verses.translit: kai kairo apesteilen pros tous georgous doulon, ina apo tou karpou tou ampelonos dosoysin auto* oi de georgoi exapesteilan auton deirantes kenon.
verses.translation: And at the season he sent a servant to the husbandmen, that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard: but the husbandmen beat him, and sent him away empty.

verses.original: καὶ προσέθετο ⸂ἕτερον πέμψαι⸃ δοῦλον· οἱ δὲ κἀκεῖνον δείραντες καὶ ἀτιμάσαντες ἐξαπέστειλαν κενόν.
verses.translit: kai prosetheto eteron pempsai doulon* oi de kakeinon deirantes kai atimasantes exapesteilan kenon.
verses.translation: And again he sent another servant: and they beat him also, and entreated him shamefully, and sent him away empty.

verses.original: καὶ προσέθετο ⸂τρίτον πέμψαι⸃· οἱ δὲ καὶ τοῦτον τραυματίσαντες ἐξέβαλον.
verses.translit: kai prosetheto triton pempsai* oi de kai touton traymatisantes exevalon.
verses.translation: And again he sent a third: and they wounded him also, and cast him out.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος· Τί ποιήσω; πέμψω τὸν υἱόν μου τὸν ἀγαπητόν· ἴσως ⸀τοῦτον ἐντραπήσονται.
verses.translit: eipen de o kyrios tou ampelonos* Ti poiiso; pempso ton yion moy ton agapiton* isos touton entrapisontai.
verses.translation: Then said the lord of the vineyard, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son: it may be they will reverence him when they see him.

verses.original: ἰδόντες δὲ αὐτὸν οἱ γεωργοὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ⸀ἀλλήλους λέγοντες· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος· ⸀ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτόν, ἵνα ἡμῶν γένηται ἡ κληρονομία·
verses.translit: idontes de auton oi georgoi dielogizonto pros alliloys legontes* Outos estin o klironomos* apokteinomen auton, ina emon genitai e klironomia*
verses.translation: But when the husbandmen saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, This is the heir: come, let us kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.

verses.original: καὶ ἐκβαλόντες αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος ἀπέκτειναν. τί οὖν ποιήσει αὐτοῖς ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος;
verses.translit: kai ekvalontes auton exo tou ampelonos apekteinan. ti oun poiisei autois o kyrios tou ampelonos;
verses.translation: So they cast him out of the vineyard, and killed him . What therefore shall the lord of the vineyard do unto them?

verses.original: ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀπολέσει τοὺς γεωργοὺς τούτους, καὶ δώσει τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἄλλοις. ἀκούσαντες δὲ εἶπαν· Μὴ γένοιτο.
verses.translit: eleysetai kai apolesei tous georgous toytoys, kai dosei ton ampelona allois. akoysantes de eipan* Me genoito.
verses.translation: He shall come and destroy these husbandmen, and shall give the vineyard to others. And when they heard it , they said, God forbid.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἐμβλέψας αὐτοῖς εἶπεν· Τί οὖν ἐστιν τὸ γεγραμμένον τοῦτο· Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες, οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας;
verses.translit: o de emvlepsas autois eipen* Ti oun estin to gegrammenon touto* Lithon on apedokimasan oi oikodomountes, outos egenithi eis kefalen gonias;
verses.translation: And he beheld them, and said, What is this then that is written, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner?

verses.original: πᾶς ὁ πεσὼν ἐπʼ ἐκεῖνον τὸν λίθον συνθλασθήσεται· ἐφʼ ὃν δʼ ἂν πέσῃ, λικμήσει αὐτόν.
verses.translit: pas o peson ep' ekeinon ton lithon synthlasthisetai* ef' on d' an pese, likmisei auton.
verses.translation: Whosoever shall fall upon that stone shall be broken; but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.

verses.original: καὶ ἐζήτησαν οἱ ⸂γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς⸃ ἐπιβαλεῖν ἐπʼ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν ⸂τὸν λαόν⸃, ἔγνωσαν γὰρ ὅτι πρὸς αὐτοὺς ⸂εἶπεν τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην⸃.
verses.translit: kai ezitisan oi grammateis kai oi arhiereis epivalein ep' auton tas heiras en aute te ora, kai efovithisan ton laon, egnosan gar oti pros autous eipen ten paravolen taytin.
verses.translation: And the chief priests and the scribes the same hour sought to lay hands on him; and they feared the people: for they perceived that he had spoken this parable against them.

verses.original: Καὶ παρατηρήσαντες ἀπέστειλαν ἐγκαθέτους ὑποκρινομένους ἑαυτοὺς δικαίους εἶναι, ἵνα ἐπιλάβωνται αὐτοῦ λόγου, ⸀ὥστε παραδοῦναι αὐτὸν τῇ ἀρχῇ καὶ τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος.
verses.translit: Kai paratirisantes apesteilan egkathetoys upokrinomenoys eaytous dikaioys einai, ina epilavontai autou logoy, oste paradounai auton te arhe kai te exoysia tou egemonos.
verses.translation: And they watched him , and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words, that so they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ὀρθῶς λέγεις καὶ διδάσκεις καὶ οὐ λαμβάνεις πρόσωπον, ἀλλʼ ἐπʼ ἀληθείας τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ διδάσκεις·
verses.translit: kai epirotisan auton legontes* Didaskale, oidamen oti orthos legeis kai didaskeis kai ou lamvaneis prosopon, all' ep' alitheias ten odon tou theou didaskeis*
verses.translation: And they asked him, saying, Master, we know that thou sayest and teachest rightly, neither acceptest thou the person of any , but teachest the way of God truly:

verses.original: ἔξεστιν ⸀ἡμᾶς Καίσαρι φόρον δοῦναι ἢ οὔ;
verses.translit: exestin emas Kaisari foron dounai e ou;
verses.translation: Is it lawful for us to give tribute unto Cæsar, or no?

verses.original: κατανοήσας δὲ αὐτῶν τὴν πανουργίαν εἶπεν πρὸς ⸀αὐτούς·
verses.translit: katanoisas de auton ten panoyrgian eipen pros autoys*
verses.translation: But he perceived their craftiness, and said unto them, Why tempt ye me?

verses.original: ⸀Δείξατέ μοι δηνάριον· τίνος ἔχει εἰκόνα καὶ ἐπιγραφήν; ⸀ἀποκριθέντες δὲ εἶπαν· Καίσαρος.
verses.translit: Deixate moi dinarion* tinos ehei eikona kai epigrafin; apokrithentes de eipan* Kaisaros.
verses.translation: Shew me a penny. Whose image and superscription hath it? They answered and said, Cæsar’s.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν ⸂πρὸς αὐτούς· Τοίνυν ἀπόδοτε⸃ τὰ Καίσαρος Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ θεῷ.
verses.translit: o de eipen pros autoys* Toinyn apodote ta Kaisaros Kaisari kai ta tou theou to theo.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Render therefore unto Cæsar the things which be Cæsar’s, and unto God the things which be God’s.

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν ἐπιλαβέσθαι ⸀τοῦ ῥήματος ἐναντίον τοῦ λαοῦ, καὶ θαυμάσαντες ἐπὶ τῇ ἀποκρίσει αὐτοῦ ἐσίγησαν.
verses.translit: kai ouk ishysan epilavesthai tou Rimatos enantion tou laou, kai thaymasantes epi te apokrisei autou esigisan.
verses.translation: And they could not take hold of his words before the people: and they marvelled at his answer, and held their peace.

verses.original: Προσελθόντες δέ τινες τῶν Σαδδουκαίων, οἱ ⸀ἀντιλέγοντες ἀνάστασιν μὴ εἶναι, ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν
verses.translit: Proselthontes de tines ton Saddoykaion, oi antilegontes anastasin me einai, epirotisan auton
verses.translation: Then came to him certain of the Sadducees, which deny that there is any resurrection; and they asked him,

verses.original: λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς ἔγραψεν ἡμῖν, ἐάν τινος ἀδελφὸς ἀποθάνῃ ἔχων γυναῖκα, καὶ οὗτος ἄτεκνος ⸀ᾖ, ἵνα λάβῃ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ ἐξαναστήσῃ σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: legontes* Didaskale, Moyses egrapsen emin, ean tinos adelfos apothane ehon gynaika, kai outos ateknos e, ina lave o adelfos autou ten gynaika kai exanastise sperma to adelfo autou.
verses.translation: Saying, Master, Moses wrote unto us, If any man’s brother die, having a wife, and he die without children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.

verses.original: ἑπτὰ οὖν ἀδελφοὶ ἦσαν· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος λαβὼν γυναῖκα ἀπέθανεν ἄτεκνος·
verses.translit: epta oun adelfoi esan* kai o protos lavon gynaika apethanen ateknos*
verses.translation: There were therefore seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and died without children.

verses.original: καὶ ⸂ὁ δεύτερος⸃
verses.translit: kai o deyteros
verses.translation: And the second took her to wife, and he died childless.

verses.original: καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἔλαβεν ⸀αὐτήν, ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ οὐ κατέλιπον τέκνα καὶ ἀπέθανον·
verses.translit: kai o tritos elaven autin, osaytos de kai oi epta ou katelipon tekna kai apethanon*
verses.translation: And the third took her; and in like manner the seven also: and they left no children, and died.

verses.original: ὕστερον ⸂καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἀπέθανεν⸃.
verses.translit: usteron kai e gyne apethanen.
verses.translation: Last of all the woman died also.

verses.original: ⸂ἡ γυνὴ οὖν ἐν τῇ⸃ ἀναστάσει τίνος αὐτῶν γίνεται γυνή; οἱ γὰρ ἑπτὰ ἔσχον αὐτὴν γυναῖκα.
verses.translit: e gyne oun en te anastasei tinos auton ginetai gyni; oi gar epta eshon auten gynaika.
verses.translation: Therefore in the resurrection whose wife of them is she? for seven had her to wife.

verses.original: ⸀Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου γαμοῦσιν καὶ ⸀γαμίσκονται,
verses.translit: Kai eipen autois o Iisous* Oi yioi tou aionos toytoy gamousin kai gamiskontai,
verses.translation: And Jesus answering said unto them, The children of this world marry, and are given in marriage:

verses.original: οἱ δὲ καταξιωθέντες τοῦ αἰῶνος ἐκείνου τυχεῖν καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τῆς ἐκ νεκρῶν οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε ⸀γαμίζονται·
verses.translit: oi de kataxiothentes tou aionos ekeinoy tyhein kai tes anastaseos tes ek nekron oute gamousin oute gamizontai*
verses.translation: But they which shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage:

verses.original: ⸀οὐδὲ γὰρ ἀποθανεῖν ἔτι δύνανται, ἰσάγγελοι γάρ εἰσιν καὶ υἱοί ⸀εἰσιν θεοῦ τῆς ἀναστάσεως υἱοὶ ὄντες.
verses.translit: oude gar apothanein eti dynantai, isaggeloi gar eisin kai yioi eisin theou tes anastaseos yioi ontes.
verses.translation: Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection.

verses.original: ὅτι δὲ ἐγείρονται οἱ νεκροὶ καὶ Μωϋσῆς ἐμήνυσεν ἐπὶ τῆς βάτου, ὡς λέγει κύριον τὸν θεὸν Ἀβραὰμ ⸀καὶ θεὸν Ἰσαὰκ ⸁καὶ θεὸν Ἰακώβ·
verses.translit: oti de egeirontai oi nekroi kai Moyses eminysen epi tes vatoy, os legei kyrion ton theon Avraam kai theon Isaak kai theon Iakov*
verses.translation: Now that the dead are raised, even Moses shewed at the bush, when he calleth the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.

verses.original: θεὸς δὲ οὐκ ἔστιν νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων, πάντες γὰρ αὐτῷ ζῶσιν.
verses.translit: theos de ouk estin nekron alla zonton, pantes gar auto zosin.
verses.translation: For he is not a God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him.

verses.original: ἀποκριθέντες δέ τινες τῶν γραμματέων εἶπαν· Διδάσκαλε, καλῶς εἶπας·
verses.translit: apokrithentes de tines ton grammateon eipan* Didaskale, kalos eipas*
verses.translation: Then certain of the scribes answering said, Master, thou hast well said.

verses.original: οὐκέτι ⸀γὰρ ἐτόλμων ἐπερωτᾶν αὐτὸν οὐδέν.
verses.translit: ouketi gar etolmon eperotan auton ouden.
verses.translation: And after that they durst not ask him any question at all .

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Πῶς λέγουσιν τὸν χριστὸν ⸂εἶναι Δαυὶδ υἱόν⸃;
verses.translit: Eipen de pros autoys* Pos legoysin ton hriston einai Dayid yion;
verses.translation: And he said unto them, How say they that Christ is David’s son?

verses.original: ⸂αὐτὸς γὰρ⸃ Δαυὶδ λέγει ἐν βίβλῳ ψαλμῶν· ⸀Εἶπεν κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου
verses.translit: autos gar Dayid legei en vivlo psalmon* Eipen kyrios to kyrio moy* Kathoy ek dexion moy
verses.translation: And David himself saith in the book of Psalms, The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand,

verses.original: ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου.
verses.translit: eos an tho tous ehthroys soy upopodion ton podon soy.
verses.translation: Till I make thine enemies thy footstool.

verses.original: Δαυὶδ οὖν ⸂αὐτὸν κύριον⸃ καλεῖ, καὶ πῶς ⸂αὐτοῦ υἱός⸃ ἐστιν;
verses.translit: Dayid oun auton kyrion kalei, kai pos autou yios estin;
verses.translation: David therefore calleth him Lord, how is he then his son?

verses.original: Ἀκούοντος δὲ παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ εἶπεν τοῖς ⸀μαθηταῖς·
verses.translit: Akoyontos de pantos tou laou eipen tois mathitais*
verses.translation: Then in the audience of all the people he said unto his disciples,

verses.original: Προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν γραμματέων τῶν θελόντων περιπατεῖν ἐν στολαῖς καὶ φιλούντων ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ πρωτοκλισίας ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις,
verses.translit: Prosehete apo ton grammateon ton thelonton peripatein en stolais kai filoynton aspasmous en tais agorais kai protokathedrias en tais synagogais kai protoklisias en tois deipnois,
verses.translation: Beware of the scribes, which desire to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the markets, and the highest seats in the synagogues, and the chief rooms at feasts;

verses.original: οἳ κατεσθίουσιν τὰς οἰκίας τῶν χηρῶν καὶ προφάσει μακρὰ προσεύχονται· οὗτοι λήμψονται περισσότερον κρίμα.
verses.translit: oi katesthioysin tas oikias ton hiron kai profasei makra proseyhontai* outoi limpsontai perissoteron krima.
verses.translation: Which devour widows’ houses, and for a shew make long prayers: the same shall receive greater damnation.

verses.original: Ἀναβλέψας δὲ εἶδεν τοὺς βάλλοντας ⸂εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον τὰ δῶρα αὐτῶν⸃ πλουσίους.
verses.translit: Anavlepsas de eiden tous vallontas eis to gazofylakion ta dora auton ploysioys.
verses.translation: And he looked up, and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury.

verses.original: εἶδεν δέ ⸀τινα χήραν πενιχρὰν βάλλουσαν ἐκεῖ ⸂λεπτὰ δύο⸃,
verses.translit: eiden de tina hiran penihran valloysan ekei lepta dyo,
verses.translation: And he saw also a certain poor widow casting in thither two mites.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν· Ἀληθῶς λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ χήρα ⸂ἡ πτωχὴ αὕτη⸃ πλεῖον πάντων ἔβαλεν·
verses.translit: kai eipen* Alithos lego umin oti e hira e ptohe auti pleion panton evalen*
verses.translation: And he said, Of a truth I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast in more than they all:

verses.original: ⸀πάντες γὰρ οὗτοι ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύοντος αὐτοῖς ἔβαλον εἰς τὰ ⸀δῶρα, αὕτη δὲ ἐκ τοῦ ὑστερήματος αὐτῆς ⸀πάντα τὸν βίον ὃν εἶχεν ἔβαλεν.
verses.translit: pantes gar outoi ek tou perisseyontos autois evalon eis ta dora, auti de ek tou usterimatos autes panta ton vion on eihen evalen.
verses.translation: For all these have of their abundance cast in unto the offerings of God: but she of her penury hath cast in all the living that she had.

verses.original: Καί τινων λεγόντων περὶ τοῦ ἱεροῦ, ὅτι λίθοις καλοῖς καὶ ἀναθήμασιν κεκόσμηται εἶπεν·
verses.translit: Kai tinon legonton peri tou ierou, oti lithois kalois kai anathimasin kekosmitai eipen*
verses.translation: And as some spake of the temple, how it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said,

verses.original: Ταῦτα ἃ θεωρεῖτε, ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι ἐν αἷς οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται λίθος ἐπὶ ⸀λίθῳ ὃς οὐ καταλυθήσεται.
verses.translit: Tauta a theoreite, eleysontai emerai en ais ouk afethisetai lithos epi litho os ou katalythisetai.
verses.translation: As for these things which ye behold, the days will come, in the which there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.

verses.original: Ἐπηρώτησαν δὲ αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, πότε οὖν ταῦτα ἔσται, καὶ τί τὸ σημεῖον ὅταν μέλλῃ ταῦτα γίνεσθαι;
verses.translit: Epirotisan de auton legontes* Didaskale, pote oun tauta estai, kai ti to simeion otan melle tauta ginesthai;
verses.translation: And they asked him, saying, Master, but when shall these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Βλέπετε μὴ πλανηθῆτε· πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐλεύσονται ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου ⸀λέγοντες· Ἐγώ εἰμι καί· Ὁ καιρὸς ἤγγικεν· ⸀μὴ πορευθῆτε ὀπίσω αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: o de eipen* Vlepete me planithete* polloi gar eleysontai epi to onomati moy legontes* Ego eimi kai* O kairos eggiken* me poreythete opiso auton.
verses.translation: And he said, Take heed that ye be not deceived: for many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ ; and the time draweth near: go ye not therefore after them.

verses.original: ὅταν δὲ ἀκούσητε πολέμους καὶ ἀκαταστασίας, μὴ πτοηθῆτε· δεῖ γὰρ ταῦτα γενέσθαι πρῶτον, ἀλλʼ οὐκ εὐθέως τὸ τέλος.
verses.translit: otan de akoysite polemoys kai akatastasias, me ptoithete* dei gar tauta genesthai proton, all' ouk eutheos to telos.
verses.translation: But when ye shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by.

verses.original: τότε ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐγερθήσεται ἔθνος ἐπʼ ἔθνος καὶ βασιλεία ἐπὶ βασιλείαν,
verses.translit: tote elegen autois* Egerthisetai ethnos ep' ethnos kai vasileia epi vasileian,
verses.translation: Then said he unto them, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom:

verses.original: σεισμοί τε μεγάλοι ⸂καὶ κατὰ τόπους⸃ ⸂λιμοὶ καὶ λοιμοὶ⸃ ἔσονται, φόβητρά τε καὶ ⸂σημεῖα ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ μεγάλα⸃ ἔσται.
verses.translit: seismoi te megaloi kai kata topoys limoi kai loimoi esontai, fovitra te kai simeia ap' ouranou megala estai.
verses.translation: And great earthquakes shall be in divers places, and famines, and pestilences; and fearful sights and great signs shall there be from heaven.

verses.original: Πρὸ δὲ τούτων πάντων ἐπιβαλοῦσιν ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν καὶ διώξουσιν, παραδιδόντες εἰς ⸀τὰς συναγωγὰς καὶ φυλακάς, ⸀ἀπαγομένους ἐπὶ βασιλεῖς καὶ ἡγεμόνας ἕνεκεν τοῦ ὀνόματός μου·
verses.translit: Pro de toyton panton epivalousin ef' umas tas heiras auton kai dioxoysin, paradidontes eis tas synagogas kai fylakas, apagomenoys epi vasileis kai egemonas eneken tou onomatos moy*
verses.translation: But before all these, they shall lay their hands on you, and persecute you , delivering you up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for my name’s sake.

verses.original: ⸀ἀποβήσεται ὑμῖν εἰς μαρτύριον.
verses.translit: apovisetai umin eis martyrion.
verses.translation: And it shall turn to you for a testimony.

verses.original: ⸀θέτε οὖν ⸂ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις⸃ ὑμῶν μὴ προμελετᾶν ἀπολογηθῆναι,
verses.translit: thete oun en tais kardiais umon me promeletan apologithenai,
verses.translation: Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before what ye shall answer:

verses.original: ἐγὼ γὰρ δώσω ὑμῖν στόμα καὶ σοφίαν ᾗ οὐ δυνήσονται ⸂ἀντιστῆναι ἢ ἀντειπεῖν⸃ ⸀ἅπαντες οἱ ἀντικείμενοι ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: ego gar doso umin stoma kai sofian e ou dynisontai antistenai e anteipein apantes oi antikeimenoi umin.
verses.translation: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.

verses.original: παραδοθήσεσθε δὲ καὶ ὑπὸ γονέων καὶ ⸂ἀδελφῶν καὶ συγγενῶν καὶ φίλων⸃, καὶ θανατώσουσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν,
verses.translit: paradothisesthe de kai upo goneon kai adelfon kai syggenon kai filon, kai thanatosoysin ex umon,
verses.translation: And ye shall be betrayed both by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolks, and friends; and some of you shall they cause to be put to death.

verses.original: καὶ ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου.
verses.translit: kai esesthe misoymenoi upo panton dia to onoma moy.
verses.translation: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake.

verses.original: καὶ θρὶξ ἐκ τῆς κεφαλῆς ὑμῶν οὐ μὴ ἀπόληται.
verses.translit: kai thrix ek tes kefales umon ou me apolitai.
verses.translation: But there shall not an hair of your head perish.

verses.original: ἐν τῇ ὑπομονῇ ὑμῶν ⸀κτήσασθε τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: en te upomone umon ktisasthe tas psyhas umon.
verses.translation: In your patience possess ye your souls.

verses.original: Ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε κυκλουμένην ὑπὸ ⸀στρατοπέδων Ἰερουσαλήμ, τότε γνῶτε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ ἐρήμωσις αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: Otan de idite kykloymenin upo stratopedon Ieroysalim, tote gnote oti eggiken e erimosis autes.
verses.translation: And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.

verses.original: τότε οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ φευγέτωσαν εἰς τὰ ὄρη, καὶ οἱ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῆς ἐκχωρείτωσαν, καὶ οἱ ἐν ταῖς χώραις μὴ εἰσερχέσθωσαν εἰς αὐτήν,
verses.translit: tote oi en te Ioydaia feygetosan eis ta ori, kai oi en meso autes ekhoreitosan, kai oi en tais horais me eiserhesthosan eis autin,
verses.translation: Then let them which are in Judæa flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto.

verses.original: ὅτι ἡμέραι ἐκδικήσεως αὗταί εἰσιν τοῦ πλησθῆναι πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα.
verses.translit: oti emerai ekdikiseos autai eisin tou plisthenai panta ta gegrammena.
verses.translation: For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.

verses.original: ⸀οὐαὶ ταῖς ἐν γαστρὶ ἐχούσαις καὶ ταῖς θηλαζούσαις ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις· ἔσται γὰρ ἀνάγκη μεγάλη ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ⸀ὀργὴ τῷ λαῷ τούτῳ,
verses.translit: ouai tais en gastri ehoysais kai tais thilazoysais en ekeinais tais emerais* estai gar anagki megali epi tes ges kai orge to lao toyto,
verses.translation: But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people.

verses.original: καὶ πεσοῦνται στόματι μαχαίρης καὶ αἰχμαλωτισθήσονται εἰς ⸂τὰ ἔθνη πάντα⸃, καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἔσται πατουμένη ὑπὸ ἐθνῶν, ἄχρι ⸀οὗ ⸀πληρωθῶσιν καιροὶ ἐθνῶν.
verses.translit: kai pesountai stomati mahairis kai aihmalotisthisontai eis ta ethni panta, kai Ieroysalem estai patoymeni upo ethnon, ahri ou plirothosin kairoi ethnon.
verses.translation: And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.

verses.original: Καὶ ⸀ἔσονται σημεῖα ἐν ἡλίῳ καὶ σελήνῃ καὶ ἄστροις, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς συνοχὴ ἐθνῶν ἐν ἀπορίᾳ ⸀ἤχους θαλάσσης καὶ σάλου,
verses.translit: Kai esontai simeia en elio kai seline kai astrois, kai epi tes ges synohe ethnon en aporia ehoys thalassis kai saloy,
verses.translation: And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring;

verses.original: ἀποψυχόντων ἀνθρώπων ἀπὸ φόβου καὶ προσδοκίας τῶν ἐπερχομένων τῇ οἰκουμένῃ, αἱ γὰρ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν σαλευθήσονται.
verses.translit: apopsyhonton anthropon apo fovoy kai prosdokias ton eperhomenon te oikoymene, ai gar dynameis ton ouranon saleythisontai.
verses.translation: Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.

verses.original: καὶ τότε ὄψονται τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐρχόμενον ἐν νεφέλῃ μετὰ δυνάμεως καὶ δόξης πολλῆς.
verses.translit: kai tote opsontai ton yion tou anthropoy erhomenon en nefele meta dynameos kai doxis polles.
verses.translation: And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

verses.original: ἀρχομένων δὲ τούτων γίνεσθαι ἀνακύψατε καὶ ἐπάρατε τὰς κεφαλὰς ὑμῶν, διότι ἐγγίζει ἡ ἀπολύτρωσις ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: arhomenon de toyton ginesthai anakypsate kai eparate tas kefalas umon, dioti eggizei e apolytrosis umon.
verses.translation: And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς· Ἴδετε τὴν συκῆν καὶ πάντα τὰ δένδρα·
verses.translit: Kai eipen paravolen autois* Idete ten syken kai panta ta dendra*
verses.translation: And he spake to them a parable; Behold the fig tree, and all the trees;

verses.original: ὅταν προβάλωσιν ἤδη, βλέποντες ἀφʼ ἑαυτῶν γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤδη ἐγγὺς τὸ θέρος ἐστίν·
verses.translit: otan provalosin edi, vlepontes af' eayton ginoskete oti edi eggus to theros estin*
verses.translation: When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand.

verses.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ἴδητε ταῦτα γινόμενα, γινώσκετε ὅτι ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: outos kai umeis, otan idite tauta ginomena, ginoskete oti eggys estin e vasileia tou theou.
verses.translation: So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand.

verses.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.
verses.translit: amen lego umin oti ou me parelthe e genea auti eos an panta genitai.
verses.translation: Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled.

verses.original: ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ ⸀παρελεύσονται, οἱ δὲ λόγοι μου οὐ μὴ παρελεύσονται.
verses.translit: o ouranos kai e ge pareleysontai, oi de logoi moy ou me pareleysontai.
verses.translation: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.

verses.original: Προσέχετε δὲ ἑαυτοῖς μήποτε βαρηθῶσιν ⸂ὑμῶν αἱ καρδίαι⸃ ἐν κραιπάλῃ καὶ μέθῃ καὶ μερίμναις βιωτικαῖς, καὶ ⸂ἐπιστῇ ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς αἰφνίδιος⸃ ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνη
verses.translit: Prosehete de eaytois mipote varithosin umon ai kardiai en kraipale kai methe kai merimnais viotikais, kai episte ef' umas aifnidios e emera ekeini
verses.translation: And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares.

verses.original: ὡς παγίς· ⸂ἐπεισελεύσεται γὰρ⸃ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς καθημένους ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: os pagis* epeiseleysetai gar epi pantas tous kathimenoys epi prosopon pasis tes ges.
verses.translation: For as a snare shall it come on all them that dwell on the face of the whole earth.

verses.original: ἀγρυπνεῖτε ⸀δὲ ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ δεόμενοι ἵνα ⸀κατισχύσητε ἐκφυγεῖν ⸀ταῦτα πάντα τὰ μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι, καὶ σταθῆναι ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
verses.translit: agrypneite de en panti kairo deomenoi ina katishysite ekfygein tauta panta ta mellonta ginesthai, kai stathenai emprosthen tou yiou tou anthropoy.
verses.translation: Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.

verses.original: Ἦν δὲ τὰς ἡμέρας ⸂ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων⸃, τὰς δὲ νύκτας ἐξερχόμενος ηὐλίζετο εἰς τὸ ὄρος τὸ καλούμενον Ἐλαιῶν·
verses.translit: En de tas emeras en to iero didaskon, tas de nyktas exerhomenos iulizeto eis to oros to kaloymenon Elaion*
verses.translation: And in the day time he was teaching in the temple; and at night he went out, and abode in the mount that is called the mount of Olives.

verses.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ὤρθριζεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai pas o laos orthrizen pros auton en to iero akoyein autou.
verses.translation: And all the people came early in the morning to him in the temple, for to hear him.

verses.original: Ἤγγιζεν δὲ ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν ἀζύμων ἡ λεγομένη Πάσχα.
verses.translit: Eggizen de e eorte ton azymon e legomeni Pasha.
verses.translation: Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.

verses.original: καὶ ἐζήτουν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τὸ πῶς ἀνέλωσιν αὐτόν, ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ τὸν λαόν.
verses.translit: kai ezitoyn oi arhiereis kai oi grammateis to pos anelosin auton, efovounto gar ton laon.
verses.translation: And the chief priests and scribes sought how they might kill him; for they feared the people.

verses.original: Εἰσῆλθεν δὲ Σατανᾶς εἰς Ἰούδαν τὸν ⸀καλούμενον Ἰσκαριώτην, ὄντα ἐκ τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ τῶν δώδεκα·
verses.translit: Eiselthen de Satanas eis Ioydan ton kaloymenon Iskariotin, onta ek tou arithmou ton dodeka*
verses.translation: Then entered Satan into Judas surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπελθὼν συνελάλησεν τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ στρατηγοῖς τὸ πῶς ⸂αὐτοῖς παραδῷ αὐτόν⸃.
verses.translit: kai apelthon synelalisen tois arhiereusin kai stratigois to pos autois parado auton.
verses.translation: And he went his way, and communed with the chief priests and captains, how he might betray him unto them.

verses.original: καὶ ἐχάρησαν καὶ συνέθεντο αὐτῷ ἀργύριον δοῦναι.
verses.translit: kai eharisan kai synethento auto argyrion dounai.
verses.translation: And they were glad, and covenanted to give him money.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξωμολόγησεν, καὶ ἐζήτει εὐκαιρίαν τοῦ παραδοῦναι αὐτὸν ⸂ἄτερ ὄχλου αὐτοῖς⸃.
verses.translit: kai exomologisen, kai ezitei eukairian tou paradounai auton ater ohloy autois.
verses.translation: And he promised, and sought opportunity to betray him unto them in the absence of the multitude.

verses.original: Ἦλθεν δὲ ἡ ἡμέρα τῶν ἀζύμων, ⸀ᾗ ἔδει θύεσθαι τὸ πάσχα·
verses.translit: Elthen de e emera ton azymon, e edei thyesthai to pasha*
verses.translation: Then came the day of unleavened bread, when the passover must be killed.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην εἰπών· Πορευθέντες ἑτοιμάσατε ἡμῖν τὸ πάσχα ἵνα φάγωμεν.
verses.translit: kai apesteilen Petron kai Ioannin eipon* Poreythentes etoimasate emin to pasha ina fagomen.
verses.translation: And he sent Peter and John, saying, Go and prepare us the passover, that we may eat.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ποῦ θέλεις ⸀ἑτοιμάσωμεν;
verses.translit: oi de eipan auto* Pou theleis etoimasomen;
verses.translation: And they said unto him, Where wilt thou that we prepare?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἰδοὺ εἰσελθόντων ὑμῶν εἰς τὴν πόλιν συναντήσει ὑμῖν ἄνθρωπος κεράμιον ὕδατος βαστάζων· ἀκολουθήσατε αὐτῷ εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ⸂εἰς ἣν⸃ εἰσπορεύεται.
verses.translit: o de eipen autois* Idou eiselthonton umon eis ten polin synantisei umin anthropos keramion udatos vastazon* akoloythisate auto eis ten oikian eis en eisporeyetai.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Behold, when ye are entered into the city, there shall a man meet you, bearing a pitcher of water; follow him into the house where he entereth in.

verses.original: καὶ ἐρεῖτε τῷ οἰκοδεσπότῃ τῆς οἰκίας· Λέγει σοι ὁ διδάσκαλος· Ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ κατάλυμα ὅπου τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου φάγω;
verses.translit: kai ereite to oikodespote tes oikias* Legei soi o didaskalos* Pou estin to katalyma opoy to pasha meta ton mathiton moy fago;
verses.translation: And ye shall say unto the goodman of the house, The Master saith unto thee, Where is the guestchamber, where I shall eat the passover with my disciples?

verses.original: κἀκεῖνος ὑμῖν δείξει ἀνάγαιον μέγα ἐστρωμένον· ἐκεῖ ἑτοιμάσατε.
verses.translit: kakeinos umin deixei anagaion mega estromenon* ekei etoimasate.
verses.translation: And he shall shew you a large upper room furnished: there make ready.

verses.original: ἀπελθόντες δὲ εὗρον καθὼς ⸀εἰρήκει αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα.
verses.translit: apelthontes de euron kathos eirikei autois, kai etoimasan to pasha.
verses.translation: And they went, and found as he had said unto them: and they made ready the passover.

verses.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡ ὥρα, ἀνέπεσεν καὶ ⸀οἱ ἀπόστολοι σὺν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: Kai ote egeneto e ora, anepesen kai oi apostoloi sun auto.
verses.translation: And when the hour was come, he sat down, and the twelve apostles with him.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἐπεθύμησα τοῦτο τὸ πάσχα φαγεῖν μεθʼ ὑμῶν πρὸ τοῦ με παθεῖν·
verses.translit: kai eipen pros autoys* Epithymia epethymisa touto to pasha fagein meth' umon pro tou me pathein*
verses.translation: And he said unto them, With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer:
