verses.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ⸀ὅτι οὐ μὴ φάγω ⸀αὐτὸ ἕως ὅτου πληρωθῇ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: lego gar umin oti ou me fago auto eos otoy plirothe en te vasileia tou theou.
verses.translation: For I say unto you, I will not any more eat thereof, until it be fulfilled in the kingdom of God.

verses.original: καὶ δεξάμενος ποτήριον εὐχαριστήσας εἶπεν· Λάβετε τοῦτο καὶ διαμερίσατε ⸂εἰς ἑαυτούς⸃·
verses.translit: kai dexamenos potirion euharistisas eipen* Lavete touto kai diamerisate eis eaytoys*
verses.translation: And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and said, Take this, and divide it among yourselves:

verses.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν, ⸀οὐ μὴ πίω ἀπὸ τοῦ ⸂νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ⸃ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως ⸀οὗ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἔλθῃ.
verses.translit: lego gar umin, ou me pio apo tou nun apo tou genimatos tes ampeloy eos ou e vasileia tou theou elthe.
verses.translation: For I say unto you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine, until the kingdom of God shall come.

verses.original: καὶ λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου ⸂[τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν διδόμενον· τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν.
verses.translit: kai lavon arton euharistisas eklasen kai edoken autois legon* Touto estin to soma moy [to uper umon didomenon* touto poieite eis ten emen anamnisin.
verses.translation: And he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it , and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.

verses.original: ⸄καὶ τὸ ποτήριον ὡσαύτως⸅ μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι, λέγων· Τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη ἐν τῷ αἵματί μου, τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐκχυννόμενον]⸃.
verses.translit: kai to potirion osaytos meta to deipnesai, legon* Touto to potirion e kaine diathiki en to aimati moy, to uper umon ekhynnomenon].
verses.translation: Likewise also the cup after supper, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.

verses.original: πλὴν ἰδοὺ ἡ χεὶρ τοῦ παραδιδόντος με μετʼ ἐμοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς τραπέζης·
verses.translit: plen idou e heir tou paradidontos me met' emou epi tes trapezis*
verses.translation: But, behold, the hand of him that betrayeth me is with me on the table.

verses.original: ⸂ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς μὲν⸃ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ⸂κατὰ τὸ ὡρισμένον πορεύεται⸃, πλὴν οὐαὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ διʼ οὗ παραδίδοται.
verses.translit: oti o yios men tou anthropoy kata to orismenon poreyetai, plen ouai to anthropo ekeino di' ou paradidotai.
verses.translation: And truly the Son of man goeth, as it was determined: but woe unto that man by whom he is betrayed!

verses.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἤρξαντο συζητεῖν πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς τὸ τίς ἄρα εἴη ἐξ αὐτῶν ὁ τοῦτο μέλλων πράσσειν.
verses.translit: kai autoi erxanto syzitein pros eaytous to tis ara eii ex auton o touto mellon prassein.
verses.translation: And they began to enquire among themselves, which of them it was that should do this thing.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ καὶ φιλονεικία ἐν αὐτοῖς, τὸ τίς αὐτῶν δοκεῖ εἶναι μείζων.
verses.translit: Egeneto de kai filoneikia en autois, to tis auton dokei einai meizon.
verses.translation: And there was also a strife among them, which of them should be accounted the greatest.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οἱ βασιλεῖς τῶν ἐθνῶν κυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ ἐξουσιάζοντες αὐτῶν εὐεργέται καλοῦνται.
verses.translit: o de eipen autois* Oi vasileis ton ethnon kyrieyoysin auton kai oi exoysiazontes auton euergetai kalountai.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors.

verses.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐχ οὕτως, ἀλλʼ ὁ μείζων ἐν ὑμῖν ⸀γινέσθω ὡς ὁ νεώτερος, καὶ ὁ ἡγούμενος ὡς ὁ διακονῶν·
verses.translit: umeis de ouh outos, all' o meizon en umin ginestho os o neoteros, kai o egoymenos os o diakonon*
verses.translation: But ye shall not be so: but he that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve.

verses.original: τίς γὰρ μείζων, ὁ ἀνακείμενος ἢ ὁ διακονῶν; οὐχὶ ὁ ἀνακείμενος; ἐγὼ δὲ ⸂ἐν μέσῳ ὑμῶν εἰμι⸃ ὡς ὁ διακονῶν.
verses.translit: tis gar meizon, o anakeimenos e o diakonon; ouhi o anakeimenos; ego de en meso umon eimi os o diakonon.
verses.translation: For whether is greater, he that sitteth at meat, or he that serveth? is not he that sitteth at meat? but I am among you as he that serveth.

verses.original: Ὑμεῖς δέ ἐστε οἱ διαμεμενηκότες μετʼ ἐμοῦ ἐν τοῖς πειρασμοῖς μου·
verses.translit: Umeis de este oi diamemenikotes met' emou en tois peirasmois moy*
verses.translation: Ye are they which have continued with me in my temptations.

verses.original: κἀγὼ διατίθεμαι ὑμῖν, καθὼς διέθετό μοι ὁ πατήρ μου βασιλείαν,
verses.translit: kago diatithemai umin, kathos dietheto moi o patir moy vasileian,
verses.translation: And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me;

verses.original: ἵνα ⸀ἔσθητε καὶ πίνητε ἐπὶ τῆς τραπέζης μου ⸂ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ μου⸃, καὶ ⸀καθήσεσθε ἐπὶ θρόνων ⸂τὰς δώδεκα φυλὰς κρίνοντες⸃ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.
verses.translit: ina esthite kai pinite epi tes trapezis moy en te vasileia moy, kai kathisesthe epi thronon tas dodeka fylas krinontes tou Israil.
verses.translation: That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

verses.original: ⸀Σίμων Σίμων, ἰδοὺ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἐξῃτήσατο ὑμᾶς τοῦ σινιάσαι ὡς τὸν σῖτον·
verses.translit: Simon Simon, idou o Satanas exetisato umas tou siniasai os ton siton*
verses.translation: And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat:

verses.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ἐδεήθην περὶ σοῦ ἵνα μὴ ἐκλίπῃ ἡ πίστις σου· καὶ σύ ποτε ἐπιστρέψας ⸀στήρισον τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου.
verses.translit: ego de edeithin peri sou ina me eklipe e pistis soy* kai sy pote epistrepsas stirison tous adelfoys soy.
verses.translation: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, μετὰ σοῦ ἕτοιμός εἰμι καὶ εἰς φυλακὴν καὶ εἰς θάνατον πορεύεσθαι.
verses.translit: o de eipen auto* Kyrie, meta sou etoimos eimi kai eis fylaken kai eis thanaton poreyesthai.
verses.translation: And he said unto him, Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Λέγω σοι, Πέτρε, οὐ ⸀φωνήσει σήμερον ἀλέκτωρ ⸀ἕως τρίς ⸂με ἀπαρνήσῃ εἰδέναι⸃.
verses.translit: o de eipen* Lego soi, Petre, ou fonisei simeron alektor eos tris me aparnise eidenai.
verses.translation: And he said, I tell thee, Peter, the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅτε ἀπέστειλα ὑμᾶς ἄτερ βαλλαντίου καὶ πήρας καὶ ὑποδημάτων, μή τινος ὑστερήσατε; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Οὐθενός.
verses.translit: Kai eipen autois* Ote apesteila umas ater vallantioy kai piras kai upodimaton, mi tinos usterisate; oi de eipan* Outhenos.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, When I sent you without purse, and scrip, and shoes, lacked ye any thing? And they said, Nothing.

verses.original: εἶπεν ⸀δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἀλλὰ νῦν ὁ ἔχων βαλλάντιον ἀράτω, ὁμοίως καὶ πήραν, καὶ ὁ μὴ ἔχων ⸀πωλησάτω τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ καὶ ⸀ἀγορασάτω μάχαιραν.
verses.translit: eipen de autois* Alla nun o ehon vallantion arato, omoios kai piran, kai o me ehon polisato to imation autou kai agorasato mahairan.
verses.translation: Then said he unto them, But now, he that hath a purse, let him take it , and likewise his scrip: and he that hath no sword, let him sell his garment, and buy one.

verses.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ⸀ὅτι τοῦτο τὸ γεγραμμένον δεῖ τελεσθῆναι ἐν ἐμοί, τό· Καὶ μετὰ ἀνόμων ἐλογίσθη· καὶ γὰρ ⸀τὸ περὶ ἐμοῦ τέλος ἔχει.
verses.translit: lego gar umin oti touto to gegrammenon dei telesthenai en emoi, to* Kai meta anomon elogisthi* kai gar to peri emou telos ehei.
verses.translation: For I say unto you, that this that is written must yet be accomplished in me, And he was reckoned among the transgressors: for the things concerning me have an end.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Κύριε, ἰδοὺ μάχαιραι ὧδε δύο. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἱκανόν ἐστιν.
verses.translit: oi de eipan* Kyrie, idou mahairai ode dyo. o de eipen autois* Ikanon estin.
verses.translation: And they said, Lord, behold, here are two swords. And he said unto them, It is enough.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη κατὰ τὸ ἔθος εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν· ἠκολούθησαν δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ ⸀μαθηταί.
verses.translit: Kai exelthon eporeythi kata to ethos eis to Oros ton Elaion* ekoloythisan de auto kai oi mathitai.
verses.translation: And he came out, and went, as he was wont, to the mount of Olives; and his disciples also followed him.

verses.original: γενόμενος δὲ ἐπὶ τοῦ τόπου εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Προσεύχεσθε μὴ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς πειρασμόν.
verses.translit: genomenos de epi tou topoy eipen autois* Proseyhesthe me eiselthein eis peirasmon.
verses.translation: And when he was at the place, he said unto them, Pray that ye enter not into temptation.

verses.original: καὶ αὐτὸς ἀπεσπάσθη ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λίθου βολήν, καὶ θεὶς τὰ γόνατα προσηύχετο
verses.translit: kai autos apespasthi ap' auton osei lithoy volin, kai theis ta gonata prosiyheto
verses.translation: And he was withdrawn from them about a stone’s cast, and kneeled down, and prayed,

verses.original: λέγων· Πάτερ, εἰ βούλει ⸀παρένεγκε ⸂τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον⸃ ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ· πλὴν μὴ τὸ θέλημά μου ἀλλὰ τὸ σὸν ⸀γινέσθω.
verses.translit: legon* Pater, ei voylei parenegke touto to potirion ap' emou* plen me to thelima moy alla to son ginestho.
verses.translation: Saying, Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.

verses.original: ⸂ὤφθη δὲ αὐτῷ ἄγγελος ⸀ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ ἐνισχύων αὐτόν.
verses.translit: ofthi de auto aggelos ap' ouranou enishyon auton.
verses.translation: And there appeared an angel unto him from heaven, strengthening him.

verses.original: καὶ γενόμενος ἐν ἀγωνίᾳ ἐκτενέστερον προσηύχετο· ⸄καὶ ἐγένετο⸅ ὁ ἱδρὼς αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ θρόμβοι αἵματος καταβαίνοντες ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν.⸃
verses.translit: kai genomenos en agonia ektenesteron prosiyheto* kai egeneto o idros autou osei thromvoi aimatos katavainontes epi ten gen.
verses.translation: And being in an agony he prayed more earnestly: and his sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground.

verses.original: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἀπὸ τῆς προσευχῆς ἐλθὼν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς εὗρεν ⸂κοιμωμένους αὐτοὺς⸃ ἀπὸ τῆς λύπης,
verses.translit: kai anastas apo tes proseyhes elthon pros tous mathitas euren koimomenoys autous apo tes lypis,
verses.translation: And when he rose up from prayer, and was come to his disciples, he found them sleeping for sorrow,

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί καθεύδετε; ἀναστάντες προσεύχεσθε, ἵνα μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν.
verses.translit: kai eipen autois* Ti katheydete; anastantes proseyhesthe, ina me eiselthite eis peirasmon.
verses.translation: And said unto them, Why sleep ye? rise and pray, lest ye enter into temptation.

verses.original: ⸀Ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ ὄχλος, καὶ ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα προήρχετο αὐτούς, καὶ ἤγγισεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ φιλῆσαι αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Eti autou lalountos idou ohlos, kai o legomenos Ioydas eis ton dodeka proirheto autoys, kai eggisen to Iisou filesai auton.
verses.translation: And while he yet spake, behold a multitude, and he that was called Judas, one of the twelve, went before them, and drew near unto Jesus to kiss him.

verses.original: ⸂Ἰησοῦς δὲ⸃ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἰούδα, φιλήματι τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδως;
verses.translit: Iisous de eipen auto* Ioyda, filimati ton yion tou anthropoy paradidos;
verses.translation: But Jesus said unto him, Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?

verses.original: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ περὶ αὐτὸν τὸ ἐσόμενον ⸀εἶπαν· Κύριε, εἰ πατάξομεν ἐν μαχαίρῃ;
verses.translit: idontes de oi peri auton to esomenon eipan* Kyrie, ei pataxomen en mahaire;
verses.translation: When they which were about him saw what would follow, they said unto him, Lord, shall we smite with the sword?

verses.original: καὶ ἐπάταξεν εἷς τις ἐξ αὐτῶν ⸂τοῦ ἀρχιερέως τὸν δοῦλον⸃ καὶ ἀφεῖλεν ⸂τὸ οὖς αὐτοῦ⸃ τὸ δεξιόν.
verses.translit: kai epataxen eis tis ex auton tou arhiereos ton doulon kai afeilen to ous autou to dexion.
verses.translation: And one of them smote the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear.

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἐᾶτε ἕως τούτου· καὶ ἁψάμενος τοῦ ⸀ὠτίου ἰάσατο αὐτόν.
verses.translit: apokritheis de o Iisous eipen* Eate eos toytoy* kai apsamenos tou otioy iasato auton.
verses.translation: And Jesus answered and said, Suffer ye thus far. And he touched his ear, and healed him.

verses.original: εἶπεν ⸀δὲ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς τοὺς παραγενομένους ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ στρατηγοὺς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ πρεσβυτέρους· Ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν ⸀ἐξήλθατε μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων;
verses.translit: eipen de Iisous pros tous paragenomenoys ep' auton arhiereis kai stratigous tou ierou kai presvyteroys* Os epi lesten exilthate meta mahairon kai xylon;
verses.translation: Then Jesus said unto the chief priests, and captains of the temple, and the elders, which were come to him, Be ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and staves?

verses.original: καθʼ ἡμέραν ὄντος μου μεθʼ ὑμῶν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ οὐκ ἐξετείνατε τὰς χεῖρας ἐπʼ ἐμέ· ἀλλʼ αὕτη ⸂ἐστὶν ὑμῶν⸃ ἡ ὥρα καὶ ἡ ἐξουσία τοῦ σκότους.
verses.translit: kath' emeran ontos moy meth' umon en to iero ouk exeteinate tas heiras ep' eme* all' auti estin umon e ora kai e exoysia tou skotoys.
verses.translation: When I was daily with you in the temple, ye stretched forth no hands against me: but this is your hour, and the power of darkness.

verses.original: Συλλαβόντες δὲ αὐτὸν ἤγαγον καὶ ⸀εἰσήγαγον εἰς ⸂τὴν οἰκίαν⸃ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως· ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἠκολούθει μακρόθεν.
verses.translit: Syllavontes de auton egagon kai eisigagon eis ten oikian tou arhiereos* o de Petros ekoloythei makrothen.
verses.translation: Then took they him, and led him , and brought him into the high priest’s house. And Peter followed afar off.

verses.original: ⸀περιαψάντων δὲ πῦρ ἐν μέσῳ τῆς αὐλῆς καὶ ⸀συγκαθισάντων ἐκάθητο ὁ Πέτρος ⸀μέσος αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: periapsanton de pur en meso tes aules kai sygkathisanton ekathito o Petros mesos auton.
verses.translation: And when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the hall, and were set down together, Peter sat down among them.

verses.original: ἰδοῦσα δὲ αὐτὸν παιδίσκη τις καθήμενον πρὸς τὸ φῶς καὶ ἀτενίσασα αὐτῷ εἶπεν· Καὶ οὗτος σὺν αὐτῷ ἦν·
verses.translit: idousa de auton paidiski tis kathimenon pros to fos kai atenisasa auto eipen* Kai outos sun auto en*
verses.translation: But a certain maid beheld him as he sat by the fire, and earnestly looked upon him, and said, This man was also with him.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ⸀ἠρνήσατο λέγων· ⸂Οὐκ οἶδα αὐτόν, γύναι⸃.
verses.translit: o de ernisato legon* Ouk oida auton, gynai.
verses.translation: And he denied him, saying, Woman, I know him not.

verses.original: καὶ μετὰ βραχὺ ἕτερος ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ἔφη· Καὶ σὺ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ· ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ⸀ἔφη· Ἄνθρωπε, οὐκ εἰμί.
verses.translit: kai meta vrahu eteros idon auton efi* Kai su ex auton ei* o de Petros efi* Anthrope, ouk eimi.
verses.translation: And after a little while another saw him, and said, Thou art also of them. And Peter said, Man, I am not.

verses.original: καὶ διαστάσης ὡσεὶ ὥρας μιᾶς ἄλλος τις διϊσχυρίζετο λέγων· Ἐπʼ ἀληθείας καὶ οὗτος μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἦν, καὶ γὰρ Γαλιλαῖός ἐστιν·
verses.translit: kai diastasis osei oras mias allos tis diishyrizeto legon* Ep' alitheias kai outos met' autou en, kai gar Galilaios estin*
verses.translation: And about the space of one hour after another confidently affirmed, saying, Of a truth this fellow also was with him: for he is a Galilæan.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος· Ἄνθρωπε, οὐκ οἶδα ὃ λέγεις. καὶ παραχρῆμα ἔτι λαλοῦντος αὐτοῦ ἐφώνησεν ἀλέκτωρ.
verses.translit: eipen de o Petros* Anthrope, ouk oida o legeis. kai parahrema eti lalountos autou efonisen alektor.
verses.translation: And Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he yet spake, the cock crew.

verses.original: καὶ στραφεὶς ὁ κύριος ἐνέβλεψεν τῷ Πέτρῳ, καὶ ὑπεμνήσθη ὁ Πέτρος τοῦ ⸀λόγου τοῦ κυρίου ὡς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὅτι Πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι ⸀σήμερον ἀπαρνήσῃ με τρίς.
verses.translit: kai strafeis o kyrios enevlepsen to Petro, kai upemnisthi o Petros tou logoy tou kyrioy os eipen auto oti Prin alektora fonesai simeron aparnise me tris.
verses.translation: And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξελθὼν ⸀ἔξω ἔκλαυσεν πικρῶς.
verses.translit: kai exelthon exo eklaysen pikros.
verses.translation: And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.

verses.original: Καὶ οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ συνέχοντες ⸀αὐτὸν ἐνέπαιζον αὐτῷ δέροντες,
verses.translit: Kai oi andres oi synehontes auton enepaizon auto derontes,
verses.translation: And the men that held Jesus mocked him, and smote him .

verses.original: καὶ περικαλύψαντες ⸂αὐτὸν ἐπηρώτων⸃ λέγοντες· Προφήτευσον, τίς ἐστιν ὁ παίσας σε;
verses.translit: kai perikalypsantes auton epiroton legontes* Profiteyson, tis estin o paisas se;
verses.translation: And when they had blindfolded him, they struck him on the face, and asked him, saying, Prophesy, who is it that smote thee?

verses.original: καὶ ἕτερα πολλὰ βλασφημοῦντες ἔλεγον εἰς αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai etera polla vlasfimountes elegon eis auton.
verses.translation: And many other things blasphemously spake they against him.

verses.original: Καὶ ὡς ἐγένετο ἡμέρα, συνήχθη τὸ πρεσβυτέριον τοῦ λαοῦ, ἀρχιερεῖς ⸀τε καὶ γραμματεῖς, καὶ ⸀ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ συνέδριον αὐτῶν,
verses.translit: Kai os egeneto emera, synihthi to presvyterion tou laou, arhiereis te kai grammateis, kai apigagon auton eis to synedrion auton,
verses.translation: And as soon as it was day, the elders of the people and the chief priests and the scribes came together, and led him into their council, saying,

verses.original: λέγοντες· Εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστός, εἰπὸν ἡμῖν. εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἐὰν ὑμῖν εἴπω οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε·
verses.translit: legontes* Ei su ei o hristos, eipon emin. eipen de autois* Ean umin eipo ou me pisteysite*
verses.translation: Art thou the Christ? tell us. And he said unto them, If I tell you, ye will not believe:

verses.original: ἐὰν ⸀δὲ ἐρωτήσω, οὐ μὴ ⸀ἀποκριθῆτε.
verses.translit: ean de erotiso, ou me apokrithete.
verses.translation: And if I also ask you , ye will not answer me, nor let me go.

verses.original: ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ⸀δὲ ἔσται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καθήμενος ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: apo tou nun de estai o yios tou anthropoy kathimenos ek dexion tes dynameos tou theou.
verses.translation: Hereafter shall the Son of man sit on the right hand of the power of God.

verses.original: εἶπαν δὲ πάντες· Σὺ οὖν εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ; ὁ δὲ πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἔφη· Ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι.
verses.translit: eipan de pantes* Su oun ei o yios tou theou; o de pros autous efi* Umeis legete oti ego eimi.
verses.translation: Then said they all, Art thou then the Son of God? And he said unto them, Ye say that I am.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Τί ἔτι ⸂ἔχομεν μαρτυρίας χρείαν⸃; αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἠκούσαμεν ἀπὸ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: oi de eipan* Ti eti ehomen martyrias hreian; autoi gar ekoysamen apo tou stomatos autou.
verses.translation: And they said, What need we any further witness? for we ourselves have heard of his own mouth.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀναστὰν ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος αὐτῶν ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Πιλᾶτον.
verses.translit: Kai anastan apan to plethos auton egagon auton epi ton Pilaton.
verses.translation: And the whole multitude of them arose, and led him unto Pilate.

verses.original: ἤρξαντο δὲ κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Τοῦτον εὕραμεν διαστρέφοντα τὸ ἔθνος ⸀ἡμῶν καὶ κωλύοντα ⸂φόρους Καίσαρι⸃ διδόναι ⸀καὶ λέγοντα ⸀αὑτὸν χριστὸν βασιλέα εἶναι.
verses.translit: erxanto de katigorein autou legontes* Touton euramen diastrefonta to ethnos emon kai kolyonta foroys Kaisari didonai kai legonta auton hriston vasilea einai.
verses.translation: And they began to accuse him, saying, We found this fellow perverting the nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Cæsar, saying that he himself is Christ a King.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ⸀ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ἔφη· Σὺ λέγεις.
verses.translit: o de Pilatos erotisen auton legon* Su ei o vasileus ton Ioydaion; o de apokritheis auto efi* Su legeis.
verses.translation: And Pilate asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews? And he answered him and said, Thou sayest it .

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τοὺς ὄχλους· Οὐδὲν εὑρίσκω αἴτιον ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ.
verses.translit: o de Pilatos eipen pros tous arhiereis kai tous ohloys* Ouden eurisko aition en to anthropo toyto.
verses.translation: Then said Pilate to the chief priests and to the people, I find no fault in this man.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐπίσχυον λέγοντες ὅτι Ἀνασείει τὸν λαὸν διδάσκων καθʼ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας, ⸀καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἕως ὧδε.
verses.translit: oi de epishyon legontes oti Anaseiei ton laon didaskon kath' olis tes Ioydaias, kai arxamenos apo tes Galilaias eos ode.
verses.translation: And they were the more fierce, saying, He stirreth up the people, teaching throughout all Jewry, beginning from Galilee to this place.

verses.original: Πιλᾶτος δὲ ⸀ἀκούσας ἐπηρώτησεν εἰ ὁ ἄνθρωπος Γαλιλαῖός ἐστιν,
verses.translit: Pilatos de akoysas epirotisen ei o anthropos Galilaios estin,
verses.translation: When Pilate heard of Galilee, he asked whether the man were a Galilæan.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι ἐκ τῆς ἐξουσίας Ἡρῴδου ἐστὶν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν πρὸς Ἡρῴδην, ὄντα καὶ αὐτὸν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν ταύταις ταῖς ἡμέραις.
verses.translit: kai epignous oti ek tes exoysias Erodoy estin anepempsen auton pros Erodin, onta kai auton en Ierosolymois en taytais tais emerais.
verses.translation: And as soon as he knew that he belonged unto Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who himself also was at Jerusalem at that time.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἡρῴδης ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐχάρη λίαν, ἦν γὰρ ⸂ἐξ ἱκανῶν χρόνων θέλων⸃ ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸ ⸀ἀκούειν περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἤλπιζέν τι σημεῖον ἰδεῖν ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ γινόμενον.
verses.translit: o de Erodis idon ton Iisoun ehari lian, en gar ex ikanon hronon thelon idein auton dia to akoyein peri autou, kai elpizen ti simeion idein up' autou ginomenon.
verses.translation: And when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceeding glad: for he was desirous to see him of a long season , because he had heard many things of him; and he hoped to have seen some miracle done by him.

verses.original: ἐπηρώτα δὲ αὐτὸν ἐν λόγοις ἱκανοῖς· αὐτὸς δὲ οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: epirota de auton en logois ikanois* autos de ouden apekrinato auto.
verses.translation: Then he questioned with him in many words; but he answered him nothing.

verses.original: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς εὐτόνως κατηγοροῦντες αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: eistikeisan de oi arhiereis kai oi grammateis eutonos katigorountes autou.
verses.translation: And the chief priests and scribes stood and vehemently accused him.

verses.original: ἐξουθενήσας δὲ αὐτὸν ⸀καὶ ὁ Ἡρῴδης σὺν τοῖς στρατεύμασιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμπαίξας ⸀περιβαλὼν ἐσθῆτα λαμπρὰν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν τῷ Πιλάτῳ.
verses.translit: exoythenisas de auton kai o Erodis sun tois strateymasin autou kai empaixas perivalon estheta lampran anepempsen auton to Pilato.
verses.translation: And Herod with his men of war set him at nought, and mocked him , and arrayed him in a gorgeous robe, and sent him again to Pilate.

verses.original: ἐγένοντο δὲ φίλοι ὅ τε ⸂Ἡρῴδης καὶ ὁ Πιλᾶτος⸃ ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ μετʼ ἀλλήλων· προϋπῆρχον γὰρ ἐν ἔχθρᾳ ὄντες πρὸς ⸀αὑτούς.
verses.translit: egenonto de filoi o te Erodis kai o Pilatos en aute te emera met' allilon* proyperhon gar en ehthra ontes pros autoys.
verses.translation: And the same day Pilate and Herod were made friends together: for before they were at enmity between themselves.

verses.original: Πιλᾶτος δὲ συγκαλεσάμενος τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας καὶ τὸν λαὸν
verses.translit: Pilatos de sygkalesamenos tous arhiereis kai tous arhontas kai ton laon
verses.translation: And Pilate, when he had called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,

verses.original: εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Προσηνέγκατέ μοι τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦτον ὡς ἀποστρέφοντα τὸν λαόν, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐνώπιον ὑμῶν ἀνακρίνας ⸀οὐθὲν εὗρον ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ αἴτιον ὧν κατηγορεῖτε κατʼ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: eipen pros autoys* Prosinegkate moi ton anthropon touton os apostrefonta ton laon, kai idou ego enopion umon anakrinas outhen euron en to anthropo toyto aition on katigoreite kat' autou.
verses.translation: Said unto them, Ye have brought this man unto me, as one that perverteth the people: and, behold, I, having examined him before you, have found no fault in this man touching those things whereof ye accuse him:

verses.original: ἀλλʼ οὐδὲ Ἡρῴδης, ⸂ἀνέπεμψεν γὰρ αὐτὸν πρὸς ἡμᾶς⸃· καὶ ἰδοὺ οὐδὲν ἄξιον θανάτου ἐστὶν πεπραγμένον αὐτῷ·
verses.translit: all' oude Erodis, anepempsen gar auton pros emas* kai idou ouden axion thanatoy estin pepragmenon auto*
verses.translation: No, nor yet Herod: for I sent you to him; and, lo, nothing worthy of death is done unto him.

verses.original: παιδεύσας οὖν αὐτὸν ⸀ἀπολύσω.
verses.translit: paideysas oun auton apolyso.
verses.translation: I will therefore chastise him, and release him .
(For of necessity he must release one unto them at the feast.)

verses.original: ⸀Ἀνέκραγον δὲ παμπληθεὶ λέγοντες· Αἶρε τοῦτον, ἀπόλυσον δὲ ἡμῖν ⸀τὸν Βαραββᾶν·
verses.translit: Anekragon de pamplithei legontes* Aire touton, apolyson de emin ton Varavvan*
verses.translation: And they cried out all at once, saying, Away with this man , and release unto us Barabbas:

verses.original: ὅστις ἦν διὰ στάσιν τινὰ γενομένην ἐν τῇ πόλει καὶ φόνον ⸂βληθεὶς ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ⸃.
verses.translit: ostis en dia stasin tina genomenin en te polei kai fonon vlitheis en te fylake.
verses.translation: (Who for a certain sedition made in the city, and for murder, was cast into prison.)

verses.original: πάλιν ⸀δὲ ὁ Πιλᾶτος ⸀προσεφώνησεν, θέλων ἀπολῦσαι τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: palin de o Pilatos prosefonisen, thelon apolusai ton Iisoun.
verses.translation: Pilate therefore, willing to release Jesus, spake again to them.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐπεφώνουν λέγοντες· ⸂Σταύρου σταύρου⸃ αὐτόν.
verses.translit: oi de epefonoyn legontes* Stayroy stayroy auton.
verses.translation: But they cried, saying, Crucify him , crucify him.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ τρίτον εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί γὰρ κακὸν ἐποίησεν οὗτος; οὐδὲν αἴτιον θανάτου εὗρον ἐν αὐτῷ· παιδεύσας οὖν αὐτὸν ἀπολύσω.
verses.translit: o de triton eipen pros autoys* Ti gar kakon epoiisen outos; ouden aition thanatoy euron en auto* paideysas oun auton apolyso.
verses.translation: And he said unto them the third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him: I will therefore chastise him, and let him go.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐπέκειντο φωναῖς μεγάλαις αἰτούμενοι αὐτὸν σταυρωθῆναι, καὶ κατίσχυον αἱ φωναὶ ⸀αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: oi de epekeinto fonais megalais aitoymenoi auton stayrothenai, kai katishyon ai fonai auton.
verses.translation: And they were instant with loud voices, requiring that he might be crucified. And the voices of them and of the chief priests prevailed.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ Πιλᾶτος ἐπέκρινεν γενέσθαι τὸ αἴτημα αὐτῶν·
verses.translit: kai Pilatos epekrinen genesthai to aitima auton*
verses.translation: And Pilate gave sentence that it should be as they required.

verses.original: ἀπέλυσεν δὲ τὸν διὰ στάσιν καὶ φόνον βεβλημένον ⸀εἰς φυλακὴν ὃν ᾐτοῦντο, τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν παρέδωκεν τῷ θελήματι αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: apelysen de ton dia stasin kai fonon vevlimenon eis fylaken on etounto, ton de Iisoun paredoken to thelimati auton.
verses.translation: And he released unto them him that for sedition and murder was cast into prison, whom they had desired; but he delivered Jesus to their will.

verses.original: Καὶ ὡς ἀπήγαγον αὐτόν, ἐπιλαβόμενοι ⸂Σίμωνά τινα Κυρηναῖον ἐρχόμενον⸃ ἀπʼ ἀγροῦ ἐπέθηκαν αὐτῷ τὸν σταυρὸν φέρειν ὄπισθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: Kai os apigagon auton, epilavomenoi Simona tina Kyrinaion erhomenon ap' agrou epethikan auto ton stayron ferein opisthen tou Iisou.
verses.translation: And as they led him away, they laid hold upon one Simon, a Cyrenian, coming out of the country, and on him they laid the cross, that he might bear it after Jesus.

verses.original: Ἠκολούθει δὲ αὐτῷ πολὺ πλῆθος τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ γυναικῶν ⸀αἳ ἐκόπτοντο καὶ ἐθρήνουν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Ekoloythei de auto polu plethos tou laou kai gynaikon ai ekoptonto kai ethrinoyn auton.
verses.translation: And there followed him a great company of people, and of women, which also bewailed and lamented him.

verses.original: στραφεὶς δὲ πρὸς αὐτὰς ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Θυγατέρες Ἰερουσαλήμ, μὴ κλαίετε ἐπʼ ἐμέ· πλὴν ἐφʼ ἑαυτὰς κλαίετε καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν,
verses.translit: strafeis de pros autas o Iisous eipen* Thygateres Ieroysalim, me klaiete ep' eme* plen ef' eaytas klaiete kai epi ta tekna umon,
verses.translation: But Jesus turning unto them said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children.

verses.original: ὅτι ἰδοὺ ἔρχονται ἡμέραι ἐν αἷς ἐροῦσιν Μακάριαι αἱ στεῖραι καὶ ⸀αἱ κοιλίαι αἳ οὐκ ἐγέννησαν καὶ μαστοὶ οἳ οὐκ ⸀ἔθρεψαν.
verses.translit: oti idou erhontai emerai en ais erousin Makariai ai steirai kai ai koiliai ai ouk egennisan kai mastoi oi ouk ethrepsan.
verses.translation: For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck.

verses.original: τότε ἄρξονται λέγειν τοῖς ὄρεσιν· Πέσετε ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς, καὶ τοῖς βουνοῖς· Καλύψατε ἡμᾶς·
verses.translit: tote arxontai legein tois oresin* Pesete ef' emas, kai tois voynois* Kalypsate emas*
verses.translation: Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us.

verses.original: ὅτι εἰ ἐν ⸀τῷ ὑγρῷ ξύλῳ ταῦτα ποιοῦσιν, ἐν τῷ ξηρῷ τί γένηται;
verses.translit: oti ei en to ugro xylo tauta poiousin, en to xiro ti genitai;
verses.translation: For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?

verses.original: Ἤγοντο δὲ καὶ ἕτεροι ⸂κακοῦργοι δύο⸃ σὺν αὐτῷ ἀναιρεθῆναι.
verses.translit: Egonto de kai eteroi kakourgoi dyo sun auto anairethenai.
verses.translation: And there were also two other, malefactors, led with him to be put to death.

verses.original: καὶ ὅτε ⸀ἦλθον ἐπὶ τὸν τόπον τὸν καλούμενον Κρανίον, ἐκεῖ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτὸν καὶ τοὺς κακούργους, ὃν μὲν ἐκ δεξιῶν ὃν δὲ ἐξ ἀριστερῶν.
verses.translit: kai ote elthon epi ton topon ton kaloymenon Kranion, ekei estayrosan auton kai tous kakoyrgoys, on men ek dexion on de ex aristeron.
verses.translation: And when they were come to the place, which is called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, and the other on the left.

verses.original: ⸂ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἔλεγεν· Πάτερ, ἄφες αὐτοῖς, οὐ γὰρ οἴδασιν τί ποιοῦσιν.⸃ διαμεριζόμενοι δὲ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἔβαλον ⸀κλήρους.
verses.translit: o de Iisous elegen* Pater, afes autois, ou gar oidasin ti poiousin. diamerizomenoi de ta imatia autou evalon kliroys.
verses.translation: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots.

verses.original: καὶ εἱστήκει ὁ λαὸς θεωρῶν. ἐξεμυκτήριζον δὲ καὶ οἱ ⸀ἄρχοντες λέγοντες· Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν, σωσάτω ἑαυτόν, εἰ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστὸς ⸂τοῦ θεοῦ, ὁ⸃ ἐκλεκτός.
verses.translit: kai eistikei o laos theoron. exemyktirizon de kai oi arhontes legontes* Alloys esosen, sosato eayton, ei outos estin o hristos tou theou, o eklektos.
verses.translation: And the people stood beholding. And the rulers also with them derided him , saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if he be Christ, the chosen of God.

verses.original: ⸀ἐνέπαιξαν δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ στρατιῶται προσερχόμενοι, ⸀ὄξος προσφέροντες αὐτῷ
verses.translit: enepaixan de auto kai oi stratiotai proserhomenoi, oxos prosferontes auto
verses.translation: And the soldiers also mocked him, coming to him, and offering him vinegar,

verses.original: καὶ λέγοντες· Εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων, σῶσον σεαυτόν.
verses.translit: kai legontes* Ei su ei o vasileus ton Ioydaion, soson seayton.
verses.translation: And saying, If thou be the king of the Jews, save thyself.

verses.original: ἦν δὲ καὶ ⸀ἐπιγραφὴ ἐπʼ ⸀αὐτῷ· Ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων ⸀οὗτος.
verses.translit: en de kai epigrafe ep' auto* O vasileus ton Ioydaion outos.
verses.translation: And a superscription also was written over him in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew, THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

verses.original: Εἷς δὲ τῶν κρεμασθέντων κακούργων ἐβλασφήμει αὐτόν ⸀λέγων· ⸀Οὐχὶ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστός; σῶσον σεαυτὸν καὶ ἡμᾶς.
verses.translit: Eis de ton kremasthenton kakoyrgon evlasfimei auton legon* Ouhi su ei o hristos; soson seayton kai emas.
verses.translation: And one of the malefactors which were hanged railed on him, saying, If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἕτερος ⸂ἐπιτιμῶν αὐτῷ ἔφη⸃· Οὐδὲ φοβῇ σὺ τὸν θεόν, ὅτι ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ κρίματι εἶ;
verses.translit: apokritheis de o eteros epitimon auto efi* Oude fove su ton theon, oti en to auto krimati ei;
verses.translation: But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?

verses.original: καὶ ἡμεῖς μὲν δικαίως, ἄξια γὰρ ὧν ἐπράξαμεν ἀπολαμβάνομεν· οὗτος δὲ οὐδὲν ἄτοπον ἔπραξεν.
verses.translit: kai emeis men dikaios, axia gar on epraxamen apolamvanomen* outos de ouden atopon epraxen.
verses.translation: And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἔλεγεν· Ἰησοῦ, μνήσθητί ⸀μου ὅταν ἔλθῃς ⸂ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ⸃ σου.
verses.translit: kai elegen* Iisou, mnisthiti moy otan elthes en te vasileia soy.
verses.translation: And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν ⸀αὐτῷ· Ἀμήν ⸂σοι λέγω⸃ σήμερον μετʼ ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ.
verses.translit: kai eipen auto* Amin soi lego simeron met' emou ese en to paradeiso.
verses.translation: And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

verses.original: ⸂Καὶ ἦν⸃ ⸀ἤδη ὡσεὶ ὥρα ἕκτη καὶ σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφʼ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης
verses.translit: Kai en edi osei ora ekti kai skotos egeneto ef' olin ten gen eos oras enatis
verses.translation: And it was about the sixth hour, and there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour.

verses.original: ⸂τοῦ ἡλίου ἐκλιπόντος⸃, ἐσχίσθη ⸀δὲ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ μέσον.
verses.translit: tou elioy eklipontos, eshisthi de to katapetasma tou naou meson.
verses.translation: And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst.

verses.original: καὶ φωνήσας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Πάτερ, εἰς χεῖράς σου ⸀παρατίθεμαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου. ⸂τοῦτο δὲ⸃ εἰπὼν ἐξέπνευσεν.
verses.translit: kai fonisas fone megale o Iisous eipen* Pater, eis heiras soy paratithemai to pneuma moy. touto de eipon exepneysen.
verses.translation: And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.

verses.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης τὸ γενόμενον ⸀ἐδόξαζεν τὸν θεὸν λέγων· Ὄντως ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος δίκαιος ἦν.
verses.translit: Idon de o ekatontarhis to genomenon edoxazen ton theon legon* Ontos o anthropos outos dikaios en.
verses.translation: Now when the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man.

verses.original: καὶ πάντες οἱ συμπαραγενόμενοι ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τὴν θεωρίαν ταύτην, ⸀θεωρήσαντες τὰ γενόμενα, ⸀τύπτοντες τὰ στήθη ὑπέστρεφον.
verses.translit: kai pantes oi symparagenomenoi ohloi epi ten theorian taytin, theorisantes ta genomena, typtontes ta stithi upestrefon.
verses.translation: And all the people that came together to that sight, beholding the things which were done, smote their breasts, and returned.

verses.original: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ πάντες οἱ γνωστοὶ ⸀αὐτῷ ⸀μακρόθεν, καὶ γυναῖκες αἱ ⸀συνακολουθοῦσαι αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, ὁρῶσαι ταῦτα.
verses.translit: eistikeisan de pantes oi gnostoi auto makrothen, kai gynaikes ai synakoloythousai auto apo tes Galilaias, orosai tauta.
verses.translation: And all his acquaintance, and the women that followed him from Galilee, stood afar off, beholding these things.

verses.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι Ἰωσὴφ βουλευτὴς ὑπάρχων, ⸀ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς καὶ δίκαιος—
verses.translit: Kai idou aner onomati Iosef voyleytes uparhon, aner agathos kai dikaios--
verses.translation: And, behold, there was a man named Joseph, a counsellor; and he was a good man, and a just:

verses.original: οὗτος οὐκ ἦν συγκατατεθειμένος τῇ βουλῇ καὶ τῇ πράξει αὐτῶν— ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας πόλεως τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὃς ⸀προσεδέχετο τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ,
verses.translit: outos ouk en sygkatatetheimenos te voyle kai te praxei auton-- apo Arimathaias poleos ton Ioydaion, os prosedeheto ten vasileian tou theou,
verses.translation: (The same had not consented to the counsel and deed of them;) he was of Arimathæa, a city of the Jews: who also himself waited for the kingdom of God.

verses.original: οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πιλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ,
verses.translit: outos proselthon to Pilato etisato to soma tou Iisou,
verses.translation: This man went unto Pilate, and begged the body of Jesus.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀καθελὼν ἐνετύλιξεν αὐτὸ σινδόνι, καὶ ἔθηκεν ⸀αὐτὸν ἐν μνήματι λαξευτῷ οὗ οὐκ ἦν ⸂οὐδεὶς οὔπω⸃ κείμενος.
verses.translit: kai kathelon enetylixen auto sindoni, kai ethiken auton en mnimati laxeyto ou ouk en oudeis oupo keimenos.
verses.translation: And he took it down, and wrapped it in linen, and laid it in a sepulchre that was hewn in stone, wherein never man before was laid.

verses.original: καὶ ἡμέρα ἦν ⸂παρασκευῆς, καὶ⸃ σάββατον ἐπέφωσκεν.
verses.translit: kai emera en paraskeyes, kai savvaton epefosken.
verses.translation: And that day was the preparation, and the sabbath drew on.

verses.original: κατακολουθήσασαι δὲ ⸀αἱ γυναῖκες, αἵτινες ἦσαν συνεληλυθυῖαι ⸂ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας αὐτῷ⸃, ἐθεάσαντο τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ ὡς ἐτέθη τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: katakoloythisasai de ai gynaikes, aitines esan synelilythyiai ek tes Galilaias auto, etheasanto to mnimeion kai os etethi to soma autou,
verses.translation: And the women also, which came with him from Galilee, followed after, and beheld the sepulchre, and how his body was laid.

verses.original: ὑποστρέψασαι δὲ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα καὶ μύρα. Καὶ τὸ μὲν σάββατον ἡσύχασαν κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν,
verses.translit: upostrepsasai de etoimasan aromata kai myra. Kai to men savvaton esyhasan kata ten entolin,
verses.translation: And they returned, and prepared spices and ointments; and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment.

verses.original: τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ὄρθρου βαθέως ⸂ἐπὶ τὸ μνῆμα ἦλθον⸃ φέρουσαι ἃ ἡτοίμασαν ⸀ἀρώματα.
verses.translit: te de mia ton savvaton orthroy vatheos epi to mnema elthon feroysai a etoimasan aromata.
verses.translation: Now upon the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came unto the sepulchre, bringing the spices which they had prepared, and certain others with them.

verses.original: εὗρον δὲ τὸν λίθον ἀποκεκυλισμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου,
verses.translit: euron de ton lithon apokekylismenon apo tou mnimeioy,
verses.translation: And they found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre.

verses.original: ⸂εἰσελθοῦσαι δὲ⸃ οὐχ εὗρον τὸ ⸀σῶμα.
verses.translit: eiselthousai de ouh euron to soma.
verses.translation: And they entered in, and found not the body of the Lord Jesus.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ⸀ἀπορεῖσθαι αὐτὰς περὶ τούτου καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο ἐπέστησαν αὐταῖς ἐν ⸂ἐσθῆτι ἀστραπτούσῃ⸃.
verses.translit: kai egeneto en to aporeisthai autas peri toytoy kai idou andres dyo epestisan autais en estheti astraptoyse.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, as they were much perplexed thereabout, behold, two men stood by them in shining garments:

verses.original: ἐμφόβων δὲ γενομένων αὐτῶν καὶ κλινουσῶν ⸂τὰ πρόσωπα⸃ εἰς τὴν γῆν εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτάς· Τί ζητεῖτε τὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τῶν νεκρῶν;
verses.translit: emfovon de genomenon auton kai klinoyson ta prosopa eis ten gen eipan pros autas* Ti ziteite ton zonta meta ton nekron;
verses.translation: And as they were afraid, and bowed down their faces to the earth, they said unto them, Why seek ye the living among the dead?

verses.original: ⸂οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε, ἀλλὰ ἠγέρθη.⸃ μνήσθητε ὡς ἐλάλησεν ὑμῖν ἔτι ὢν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ,
verses.translit: ouk estin ode, alla egerthi. mnisthite os elalisen umin eti on en te Galilaia,
verses.translation: He is not here, but is risen: remember how he spake unto you when he was yet in Galilee,

verses.original: λέγων ⸂τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὅτι δεῖ⸃ παραδοθῆναι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ σταυρωθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἀναστῆναι.
verses.translit: legon ton yion tou anthropoy oti dei paradothenai eis heiras anthropon amartolon kai stayrothenai kai te trite emera anastenai.
verses.translation: Saying, The Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again.

verses.original: καὶ ἐμνήσθησαν τῶν ῥημάτων αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: kai emnisthisan ton Rimaton autou,
verses.translation: And they remembered his words,

verses.original: καὶ ὑποστρέψασαι ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπήγγειλαν ταῦτα πάντα τοῖς ἕνδεκα καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς λοιποῖς.
verses.translit: kai upostrepsasai apo tou mnimeioy apiggeilan tauta panta tois endeka kai pasin tois loipois.
verses.translation: And returned from the sepulchre, and told all these things unto the eleven, and to all the rest.

verses.original: ἦσαν δὲ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ Μαρία καὶ Ἰωάννα καὶ Μαρία ⸀ἡ Ἰακώβου καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ σὺν αὐταῖς· ⸀ἔλεγον πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ταῦτα.
verses.translit: esan de e Magdaline Maria kai Ioanna kai Maria e Iakovoy kai ai loipai sun autais* elegon pros tous apostoloys tauta.
verses.translation: It was Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and other women that were with them, which told these things unto the apostles.

verses.original: καὶ ἐφάνησαν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λῆρος τὰ ῥήματα ⸀ταῦτα, καὶ ἠπίστουν αὐταῖς.
verses.translit: kai efanisan enopion auton osei leros ta Rimata tauta, kai epistoyn autais.
verses.translation: And their words seemed to them as idle tales, and they believed them not.

verses.original: ⸂Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἀναστὰς ἔδραμεν ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον· καὶ παρακύψας βλέπει τὰ ⸀ὀθόνια μόνα· καὶ ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς ⸀αὑτὸν θαυμάζων τὸ γεγονός.⸃
verses.translit: O de Petros anastas edramen epi to mnimeion* kai parakypsas vlepei ta othonia mona* kai apelthen pros auton thaymazon to gegonos.
verses.translation: Then arose Peter, and ran unto the sepulchre; and stooping down, he beheld the linen clothes laid by themselves, and departed, wondering in himself at that which was come to pass.

verses.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο ἐξ αὐτῶν ⸂ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἦσαν πορευόμενοι⸃ εἰς κώμην ἀπέχουσαν σταδίους ἑξήκοντα ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλήμ, ᾗ ὄνομα Ἐμμαοῦς,
verses.translit: Kai idou dyo ex auton en aute te emera esan poreyomenoi eis komin apehoysan stadioys exikonta apo Ieroysalim, e onoma Emmaous,
verses.translation: And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs.

verses.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡμίλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους περὶ πάντων τῶν συμβεβηκότων τούτων.
verses.translit: kai autoi omiloyn pros alliloys peri panton ton symvevikoton toyton.
verses.translation: And they talked together of all these things which had happened.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὁμιλεῖν αὐτοὺς καὶ συζητεῖν καὶ ⸀αὐτὸς Ἰησοῦς ἐγγίσας συνεπορεύετο αὐτοῖς,
verses.translit: kai egeneto en to omilein autous kai syzitein kai autos Iisous eggisas syneporeyeto autois,
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that, while they communed together and reasoned, Jesus himself drew near, and went with them.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν ἐκρατοῦντο τοῦ μὴ ἐπιγνῶναι αὐτόν.
verses.translit: oi de ofthalmoi auton ekratounto tou me epignonai auton.
verses.translation: But their eyes were holden that they should not know him.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Τίνες οἱ λόγοι οὗτοι οὓς ἀντιβάλλετε πρὸς ἀλλήλους περιπατοῦντες; καὶ ⸀ἐστάθησαν σκυθρωποί.
verses.translit: eipen de pros autoys* Tines oi logoi outoi ous antivallete pros alliloys peripatountes; kai estathisan skythropoi.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, What manner of communications are these that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad?

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ⸂εἷς ὀνόματι⸃ Κλεοπᾶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Σὺ μόνος παροικεῖς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ οὐκ ἔγνως τὰ γενόμενα ἐν αὐτῇ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις;
verses.translit: apokritheis de eis onomati Kleopas eipen pros auton* Su monos paroikeis Ieroysalem kai ouk egnos ta genomena en aute en tais emerais taytais;
verses.translation: And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto him, Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days?

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ποῖα; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Τὰ περὶ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ ⸀Ναζαρηνοῦ, ὃς ἐγένετο ἀνὴρ προφήτης δυνατὸς ἐν ἔργῳ καὶ λόγῳ ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ,
verses.translit: kai eipen autois* Poia; oi de eipan auto* Ta peri Iisou tou Nazarinou, os egeneto aner profitis dynatos en ergo kai logo enantion tou theou kai pantos tou laou,
verses.translation: And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people:

verses.original: ὅπως τε παρέδωκαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες ἡμῶν εἰς κρίμα θανάτου καὶ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: opos te paredokan auton oi arhiereis kai oi arhontes emon eis krima thanatoy kai estayrosan auton.
verses.translation: And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him.

verses.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἠλπίζομεν ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ μέλλων λυτροῦσθαι τὸν Ἰσραήλ· ἀλλά γε ⸀καὶ σὺν πᾶσιν τούτοις τρίτην ταύτην ἡμέραν ⸀ἄγει ἀφʼ οὗ ταῦτα ἐγένετο.
verses.translit: emeis de elpizomen oti autos estin o mellon lytrousthai ton Israil* alla ge kai sun pasin toytois tritin taytin emeran agei af' ou tauta egeneto.
verses.translation: But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel: and beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ καὶ γυναῖκές τινες ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξέστησαν ἡμᾶς, γενόμεναι ⸀ὀρθριναὶ ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον
verses.translit: alla kai gynaikes tines ex emon exestisan emas, genomenai orthrinai epi to mnimeion
verses.translation: Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre;

verses.original: καὶ μὴ εὑροῦσαι τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ἦλθον λέγουσαι καὶ ὀπτασίαν ἀγγέλων ἑωρακέναι, οἳ λέγουσιν αὐτὸν ζῆν.
verses.translit: kai me eurousai to soma autou elthon legoysai kai optasian aggelon eorakenai, oi legoysin auton zen.
verses.translation: And when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, which said that he was alive.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπῆλθόν τινες τῶν σὺν ἡμῖν ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ εὗρον οὕτως καθὼς ⸀καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες εἶπον, αὐτὸν δὲ οὐκ εἶδον.
verses.translit: kai apelthon tines ton sun emin epi to mnimeion, kai euron outos kathos kai ai gynaikes eipon, auton de ouk eidon.
verses.translation: And certain of them which were with us went to the sepulchre, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not.

verses.original: καὶ αὐτὸς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὦ ἀνόητοι καὶ βραδεῖς τῇ καρδίᾳ τοῦ πιστεύειν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἐλάλησαν οἱ προφῆται·
verses.translit: kai autos eipen pros autoys* O anoitoi kai vradeis te kardia tou pisteyein epi pasin ois elalisan oi profetai*
verses.translation: Then he said unto them, O fools, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken:

verses.original: οὐχὶ ταῦτα ἔδει παθεῖν τὸν χριστὸν καὶ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ;
verses.translit: ouhi tauta edei pathein ton hriston kai eiselthein eis ten doxan autou;
verses.translation: Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?

verses.original: καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ Μωϋσέως καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν προφητῶν ⸀διερμήνευσεν αὐτοῖς ἐν πάσαις ταῖς γραφαῖς τὰ περὶ ⸀ἑαυτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai arxamenos apo Moyseos kai apo panton ton profiton diermineysen autois en pasais tais grafais ta peri eaytou.
verses.translation: And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.

verses.original: Καὶ ἤγγισαν εἰς τὴν κώμην οὗ ἐπορεύοντο, καὶ αὐτὸς ⸀προσεποιήσατο ⸀πορρώτερον πορεύεσθαι.
verses.translit: Kai eggisan eis ten komin ou eporeyonto, kai autos prosepoiisato porroteron poreyesthai.
verses.translation: And they drew nigh unto the village, whither they went: and he made as though he would have gone further.

verses.original: καὶ παρεβιάσαντο αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Μεῖνον μεθʼ ἡμῶν, ὅτι πρὸς ἑσπέραν ἐστὶν καὶ κέκλικεν ⸀ἤδη ἡ ἡμέρα. καὶ εἰσῆλθεν τοῦ μεῖναι σὺν αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: kai pareviasanto auton legontes* Meinon meth' emon, oti pros esperan estin kai kekliken edi e emera. kai eiselthen tou meinai sun autois.
verses.translation: But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ κατακλιθῆναι αὐτὸν μετʼ αὐτῶν λαβὼν τὸν ἄρτον εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἐπεδίδου αὐτοῖς·
verses.translit: kai egeneto en to kataklithenai auton met' auton lavon ton arton eulogisen kai klasas epedidoy autois*
verses.translation: And it came to pass, as he sat at meat with them, he took bread, and blessed it , and brake, and gave to them.

verses.original: αὐτῶν δὲ διηνοίχθησαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτόν· καὶ αὐτὸς ἄφαντος ἐγένετο ἀπʼ αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: auton de diinoihthisan oi ofthalmoi kai epegnosan auton* kai autos afantos egeneto ap' auton.
verses.translation: And their eyes were opened, and they knew him; and he vanished out of their sight.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Οὐχὶ ἡ καρδία ἡμῶν καιομένη ἦν ⸂ἐν ἡμῖν⸃ ὡς ἐλάλει ἡμῖν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ⸀ὡς διήνοιγεν ἡμῖν τὰς γραφάς;
verses.translit: kai eipan pros alliloys* Ouhi e kardia emon kaiomeni en en emin os elalei emin en te odo, os diinoigen emin tas grafas;
verses.translation: And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?

verses.original: καὶ ἀναστάντες αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, καὶ εὗρον ⸀ἠθροισμένους τοὺς ἕνδεκα καὶ τοὺς σὺν αὐτοῖς,
verses.translit: kai anastantes aute te ora upestrepsan eis Ieroysalim, kai euron ethroismenoys tous endeka kai tous sun autois,
verses.translation: And they rose up the same hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and them that were with them,

verses.original: λέγοντας ὅτι ⸂ὄντως ἠγέρθη ὁ κύριος⸃ καὶ ὤφθη Σίμωνι.
verses.translit: legontas oti ontos egerthi o kyrios kai ofthi Simoni.
verses.translation: Saying, The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon.

verses.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐξηγοῦντο τὰ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ καὶ ὡς ἐγνώσθη αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ κλάσει τοῦ ἄρτου.
verses.translit: kai autoi exigounto ta en te odo kai os egnosthi autois en te klasei tou artoy.
verses.translation: And they told what things were done in the way, and how he was known of them in breaking of bread.

verses.original: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτῶν λαλούντων ⸀αὐτὸς ἔστη ἐν μέσῳ ⸀αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Tauta de auton laloynton autos esti en meso auton.
verses.translation: And as they thus spake, Jesus himself stood in the midst of them, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you.

verses.original: πτοηθέντες δὲ καὶ ἔμφοβοι γενόμενοι ἐδόκουν πνεῦμα θεωρεῖν.
verses.translit: ptoithentes de kai emfovoi genomenoi edokoyn pneuma theorein.
verses.translation: But they were terrified and affrighted, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί τεταραγμένοι ἐστέ, καὶ διὰ τί διαλογισμοὶ ἀναβαίνουσιν ἐν ⸂τῇ καρδίᾳ⸃ ὑμῶν;
verses.translit: kai eipen autois* Ti tetaragmenoi este, kai dia ti dialogismoi anavainoysin en te kardia umon;
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Why are ye troubled? and why do thoughts arise in your hearts?

verses.original: ἴδετε τὰς χεῖράς μου καὶ τοὺς πόδας μου ὅτι ⸂ἐγώ εἰμι αὐτός⸃· ψηλαφήσατέ με καὶ ἴδετε, ὅτι πνεῦμα σάρκα καὶ ὀστέα οὐκ ἔχει καθὼς ἐμὲ θεωρεῖτε ἔχοντα.
verses.translit: idete tas heiras moy kai tous podas moy oti ego eimi autos* psilafisate me kai idete, oti pneuma sarka kai ostea ouk ehei kathos eme theoreite ehonta.
verses.translation: Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself: handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have.

verses.original: ⸂[καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ⸀ἔδειξεν αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τοὺς πόδας.]⸃
verses.translit: [kai touto eipon edeixen autois tas heiras kai tous podas.]
verses.translation: And when he had thus spoken, he shewed them his hands and his feet.

verses.original: ἔτι δὲ ἀπιστούντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς καὶ θαυμαζόντων εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἔχετέ τι βρώσιμον ἐνθάδε;
verses.translit: eti de apistoynton auton apo tes haras kai thaymazonton eipen autois* Ehete ti vrosimon enthade;
verses.translation: And while they yet believed not for joy, and wondered, he said unto them, Have ye here any meat?

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐπέδωκαν αὐτῷ ἰχθύος ὀπτοῦ ⸀μέρος·
verses.translit: oi de epedokan auto ihthyos optou meros*
verses.translation: And they gave him a piece of a broiled fish, and of an honeycomb.

verses.original: καὶ λαβὼν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ἔφαγεν.
verses.translit: kai lavon enopion auton efagen.
verses.translation: And he took it , and did eat before them.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ⸂πρὸς αὐτούς⸃· Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι ⸀μου οὓς ἐλάλησα πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἔτι ὢν σὺν ὑμῖν, ὅτι δεῖ πληρωθῆναι πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα ἐν τῷ νόμῳ Μωϋσέως ⸀καὶ προφήταις καὶ ψαλμοῖς περὶ ἐμοῦ.
verses.translit: Eipen de pros autoys* Outoi oi logoi moy ous elalisa pros umas eti on sun umin, oti dei plirothenai panta ta gegrammena en to nomo Moyseos kai profitais kai psalmois peri emou.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.

verses.original: τότε διήνοιξεν αὐτῶν τὸν νοῦν τοῦ συνιέναι τὰς γραφάς,
verses.translit: tote diinoixen auton ton noun tou synienai tas grafas,
verses.translation: Then opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures,

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι οὕτως ⸀γέγραπται παθεῖν τὸν χριστὸν καὶ ἀναστῆναι ἐκ νεκρῶν τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ,
verses.translit: kai eipen autois oti outos gegraptai pathein ton hriston kai anastenai ek nekron te trite emera,
verses.translation: And said unto them, Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day:

verses.original: καὶ κηρυχθῆναι ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ μετάνοιαν ⸀καὶ ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη— ⸀ἀρξάμενοι ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλήμ·
verses.translit: kai kiryhthenai epi to onomati autou metanoian kai afesin amartion eis panta ta ethni-- arxamenoi apo Ieroysalim*
verses.translation: And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.

verses.original: ὑμεῖς ⸀ἐστε μάρτυρες τούτων.
verses.translit: umeis este martyres toyton.
verses.translation: And ye are witnesses of these things.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ⸀ἐξαποστέλλω τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πατρός μου ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς· ὑμεῖς δὲ καθίσατε ἐν τῇ ⸀πόλει ἕως οὗ ἐνδύσησθε ⸂ἐξ ὕψους δύναμιν⸃.
verses.translit: kai idou ego exapostello ten epaggelian tou patros moy ef' umas* umeis de kathisate en te polei eos ou endysisthe ex upsoys dynamin.
verses.translation: And, behold, I send the promise of my Father upon you: but tarry ye in the city of Jerusalem, until ye be endued with power from on high.

verses.original: Ἐξήγαγεν δὲ αὐτοὺς ⸀ἕως ⸀πρὸς Βηθανίαν, καὶ ἐπάρας τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ εὐλόγησεν αὐτούς.
verses.translit: Exigagen de autous eos pros Vithanian, kai eparas tas heiras autou eulogisen autoys.
verses.translation: And he led them out as far as to Bethany, and he lifted up his hands, and blessed them.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εὐλογεῖν αὐτὸν αὐτοὺς διέστη ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ⸂[καὶ ἀνεφέρετο εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν]⸃.
verses.translit: kai egeneto en to eulogein auton autous diesti ap' auton [kai anefereto eis ton ouranon].
verses.translation: And it came to pass, while he blessed them, he was parted from them, and carried up into heaven.

verses.original: καὶ αὐτοὶ ⸂[προσκυνήσαντες αὐτὸν]⸃ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ μετὰ χαρᾶς μεγάλης,
verses.translit: kai autoi [proskynisantes auton] upestrepsan eis Ieroysalem meta haras megalis,
verses.translation: And they worshipped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy:

verses.original: καὶ ἦσαν διὰ παντὸς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ⸀εὐλογοῦντες τὸν ⸀θεόν.
verses.translit: kai esan dia pantos en to iero eulogountes ton theon.
verses.translation: And were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

verses.original: Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ λόγος, καὶ ὁ λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν θεόν, καὶ θεὸς ἦν ὁ λόγος.
verses.translit: En arhe en o logos, kai o logos en pros ton theon, kai theos en o logos.
verses.translation: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

verses.original: οὗτος ἦν ἐν ἀρχῇ πρὸς τὸν θεόν.
verses.translit: outos en en arhe pros ton theon.
verses.translation: The same was in the beginning with God.

verses.original: πάντα διʼ αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο, καὶ χωρὶς αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο οὐδὲ ἕν. ὃ γέγονεν
verses.translit: panta di' autou egeneto, kai horis autou egeneto oude en. o gegonen
verses.translation: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.

verses.original: ἐν αὐτῷ ζωὴ ἦν, καὶ ἡ ζωὴ ἦν τὸ φῶς τῶν ἀνθρώπων·
verses.translit: en auto zoe en, kai e zoe en to fos ton anthropon*
verses.translation: In him was life; and the life was the light of men.

verses.original: καὶ τὸ φῶς ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ φαίνει, καὶ ἡ σκοτία αὐτὸ οὐ κατέλαβεν.
verses.translit: kai to fos en te skotia fainei, kai e skotia auto ou katelaven.
verses.translation: And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο ἄνθρωπος ἀπεσταλμένος παρὰ θεοῦ, ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἰωάννης·
verses.translit: Egeneto anthropos apestalmenos para theou, onoma auto Ioannis*
verses.translation: There was a man sent from God, whose name was John.

verses.original: οὗτος ἦλθεν εἰς μαρτυρίαν, ἵνα μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ φωτός, ἵνα πάντες πιστεύσωσιν διʼ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: outos elthen eis martyrian, ina martyrise peri tou fotos, ina pantes pisteysosin di' autou.
verses.translation: The same came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light, that all men through him might believe.

verses.original: οὐκ ἦν ἐκεῖνος τὸ φῶς, ἀλλʼ ἵνα μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ φωτός.
verses.translit: ouk en ekeinos to fos, all' ina martyrise peri tou fotos.
verses.translation: He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light.

verses.original: ἦν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ὃ φωτίζει πάντα ἄνθρωπον ἐρχόμενον εἰς τὸν κόσμον.
verses.translit: en to fos to alithinon o fotizei panta anthropon erhomenon eis ton kosmon.
verses.translation: That was the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world.

verses.original: Ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἦν, καὶ ὁ κόσμος διʼ αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο, καὶ ὁ κόσμος αὐτὸν οὐκ ἔγνω.
verses.translit: En to kosmo en, kai o kosmos di' autou egeneto, kai o kosmos auton ouk egno.
verses.translation: He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not.

verses.original: εἰς τὰ ἴδια ἦλθεν, καὶ οἱ ἴδιοι αὐτὸν οὐ παρέλαβον.
verses.translit: eis ta idia elthen, kai oi idioi auton ou parelavon.
verses.translation: He came unto his own, and his own received him not.

verses.original: ὅσοι δὲ ἔλαβον αὐτόν, ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τέκνα θεοῦ γενέσθαι, τοῖς πιστεύουσιν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: osoi de elavon auton, edoken autois exoysian tekna theou genesthai, tois pisteyoysin eis to onoma autou,
verses.translation: But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name:

verses.original: οἳ οὐκ ἐξ αἱμάτων οὐδὲ ἐκ θελήματος σαρκὸς οὐδὲ ἐκ θελήματος ἀνδρὸς ἀλλʼ ἐκ θεοῦ ἐγεννήθησαν.
verses.translit: oi ouk ex aimaton oude ek thelimatos sarkos oude ek thelimatos andros all' ek theou egennithisan.
verses.translation: Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ ἐθεασάμεθα τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, δόξαν ὡς μονογενοῦς παρὰ πατρός, πλήρης χάριτος καὶ ἀληθείας·
verses.translit: Kai o logos sarx egeneto kai eskinosen en emin, kai etheasametha ten doxan autou, doxan os monogenous para patros, pliris haritos kai alitheias*
verses.translation: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

verses.original: (Ἰωάννης μαρτυρεῖ περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ κέκραγεν λέγων· Οὗτος ἦν ⸂ὃν εἶπον⸃· Ὁ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος ἔμπροσθέν μου γέγονεν, ὅτι πρῶτός μου ἦν·)
verses.translit: (Ioannis martyrei peri autou kai kekragen legon* Outos en on eipon* O opiso moy erhomenos emprosthen moy gegonen, oti protos moy en*)
verses.translation: John bare witness of him, and cried, saying, This was he of whom I spake, He that cometh after me is preferred before me: for he was before me.

verses.original: ⸀ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ πληρώματος αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς πάντες ἐλάβομεν, καὶ χάριν ἀντὶ χάριτος·
verses.translit: oti ek tou pliromatos autou emeis pantes elavomen, kai harin anti haritos*
verses.translation: And of his fulness have all we received, and grace for grace.

verses.original: ὅτι ὁ νόμος διὰ Μωϋσέως ἐδόθη, ἡ χάρις καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐγένετο.
verses.translit: oti o nomos dia Moyseos edothi, e haris kai e alitheia dia Iisou Hristou egeneto.
verses.translation: For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ.

verses.original: θεὸν οὐδεὶς ἑώρακεν πώποτε· ⸂μονογενὴς θεὸς⸃ ὁ ὢν εἰς τὸν κόλπον τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκεῖνος ἐξηγήσατο.
verses.translit: theon oudeis eoraken popote* monogenes theos o on eis ton kolpon tou patros ekeinos exigisato.
verses.translation: No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.

verses.original: Καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία τοῦ Ἰωάννου ὅτε ⸀ἀπέστειλαν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐξ Ἱεροσολύμων ἱερεῖς καὶ Λευίτας ἵνα ἐρωτήσωσιν αὐτόν· Σὺ τίς εἶ;
verses.translit: Kai auti estin e martyria tou Ioannoy ote apesteilan oi Ioydaioi ex Ierosolymon iereis kai Leyitas ina erotisosin auton* Su tis ei;
verses.translation: And this is the record of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, Who art thou?

verses.original: καὶ ὡμολόγησεν καὶ οὐκ ἠρνήσατο, καὶ ὡμολόγησεν ὅτι ⸂Ἐγὼ οὐκ εἰμὶ⸃ ὁ χριστός.
verses.translit: kai omologisen kai ouk ernisato, kai omologisen oti Ego ouk eimi o hristos.
verses.translation: And he confessed, and denied not; but confessed, I am not the Christ.

verses.original: καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτόν· Τί οὖν; ⸂σὺ Ἠλίας εἶ⸃; καὶ λέγει· Οὐκ εἰμί. Ὁ προφήτης εἶ σύ; καὶ ἀπεκρίθη· Οὔ.
verses.translit: kai erotisan auton* Ti oun; su Elias ei; kai legei* Ouk eimi. O profitis ei sy; kai apekrithi* Ou.
verses.translation: And they asked him, What then? Art thou Elias? And he saith, I am not. Art thou that prophet? And he answered, No.

verses.original: εἶπαν οὖν αὐτῷ· Τίς εἶ; ἵνα ἀπόκρισιν δῶμεν τοῖς πέμψασιν ἡμᾶς· τί λέγεις περὶ σεαυτοῦ;
verses.translit: eipan oun auto* Tis ei; ina apokrisin domen tois pempsasin emas* ti legeis peri seaytou;
verses.translation: Then said they unto him, Who art thou? that we may give an answer to them that sent us. What sayest thou of thyself?

verses.original: ἔφη· Ἐγὼ φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Εὐθύνατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, καθὼς εἶπεν Ἠσαΐας ὁ προφήτης.
verses.translit: efi* Ego fone voontos en te erimo* Euthynate ten odon kyrioy, kathos eipen EsaIas o profitis.
verses.translation: He said, I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, as said the prophet Esaias.

verses.original: ⸀Καὶ ἀπεσταλμένοι ἦσαν ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων.
verses.translit: Kai apestalmenoi esan ek ton Farisaion.
verses.translation: And they which were sent were of the Pharisees.

verses.original: καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Τί οὖν βαπτίζεις εἰ σὺ οὐκ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ⸂οὐδὲ Ἠλίας οὐδὲ⸃ ὁ προφήτης;
verses.translit: kai erotisan auton kai eipan auto* Ti oun vaptizeis ei su ouk ei o hristos oude Elias oude o profitis;
verses.translation: And they asked him, and said unto him, Why baptizest thou then, if thou be not that Christ, nor Elias, neither that prophet?

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰωάννης λέγων· Ἐγὼ βαπτίζω ἐν ὕδατι· ⸀μέσος ὑμῶν ⸀ἕστηκεν ὃν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε,
verses.translit: apekrithi autois o Ioannis legon* Ego vaptizo en udati* mesos umon estiken on umeis ouk oidate,
verses.translation: John answered them, saying, I baptize with water: but there standeth one among you, whom ye know not;

verses.original: ⸀ὁ ὀπίσω μου ⸀ἐρχόμενος, οὗ ⸂οὐκ εἰμὶ⸃ ἄξιος ἵνα λύσω αὐτοῦ τὸν ἱμάντα τοῦ ὑποδήματος.
verses.translit: o opiso moy erhomenos, ou ouk eimi axios ina lyso autou ton imanta tou upodimatos.
verses.translation: He it is, who coming after me is preferred before me, whose shoe’s latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

verses.original: ταῦτα ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐγένετο πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, ὅπου ἦν ⸀ὁ Ἰωάννης βαπτίζων.
verses.translit: tauta en Vithania egeneto peran tou Iordanoy, opoy en o Ioannis vaptizon.
verses.translation: These things were done in Bethabara beyond Jordan, where John was baptizing.

verses.original: Τῇ ἐπαύριον βλέπει τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐρχόμενον πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ λέγει· Ἴδε ὁ ἀμνὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ αἴρων τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου.
verses.translit: Te epayrion vlepei ton Iisoun erhomenon pros auton, kai legei* Ide o amnos tou theou o airon ten amartian tou kosmoy.
verses.translation: The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.

verses.original: οὗτός ἐστιν ⸀ὑπὲρ οὗ ἐγὼ εἶπον· Ὀπίσω μου ἔρχεται ἀνὴρ ὃς ἔμπροσθέν μου γέγονεν, ὅτι πρῶτός μου ἦν·
verses.translit: outos estin uper ou ego eipon* Opiso moy erhetai aner os emprosthen moy gegonen, oti protos moy en*
verses.translation: This is he of whom I said, After me cometh a man which is preferred before me: for he was before me.

verses.original: κἀγὼ οὐκ ᾔδειν αὐτόν, ἀλλʼ ἵνα φανερωθῇ τῷ Ἰσραὴλ διὰ τοῦτο ἦλθον ἐγὼ ⸀ἐν ὕδατι βαπτίζων.
verses.translit: kago ouk edein auton, all' ina fanerothe to Israel dia touto elthon ego en udati vaptizon.
verses.translation: And I knew him not: but that he should be made manifest to Israel, therefore am I come baptizing with water.

verses.original: καὶ ἐμαρτύρησεν Ἰωάννης λέγων ὅτι Τεθέαμαι τὸ πνεῦμα καταβαῖνον ⸀ὡς περιστερὰν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐπʼ αὐτόν·
verses.translit: kai emartyrisen Ioannis legon oti Tetheamai to pneuma katavainon os peristeran ex ouranou, kai emeinen ep' auton*
verses.translation: And John bare record, saying, I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it abode upon him.

verses.original: κἀγὼ οὐκ ᾔδειν αὐτόν, ἀλλʼ ὁ πέμψας με βαπτίζειν ἐν ὕδατι ἐκεῖνός μοι εἶπεν· Ἐφʼ ὃν ἂν ἴδῃς τὸ πνεῦμα καταβαῖνον καὶ μένον ἐπʼ αὐτόν, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ·
verses.translit: kago ouk edein auton, all' o pempsas me vaptizein en udati ekeinos moi eipen* Ef' on an ides to pneuma katavainon kai menon ep' auton, outos estin o vaptizon en pneymati agio*
verses.translation: And I knew him not: but he that sent me to baptize with water, the same said unto me, Upon whom thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and remaining on him, the same is he which baptizeth with the Holy Ghost.

verses.original: κἀγὼ ἑώρακα, καὶ μεμαρτύρηκα ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ⸀ἐκλεκτὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: kago eoraka, kai memartyrika oti outos estin o eklektos tou theou.
verses.translation: And I saw, and bare record that this is the Son of God.

verses.original: Τῇ ἐπαύριον πάλιν εἱστήκει ⸀ὁ Ἰωάννης καὶ ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ δύο,
verses.translit: Te epayrion palin eistikei o Ioannis kai ek ton mathiton autou dyo,
verses.translation: Again the next day after John stood, and two of his disciples;

verses.original: καὶ ἐμβλέψας τῷ Ἰησοῦ περιπατοῦντι λέγει· Ἴδε ὁ ἀμνὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: kai emvlepsas to Iisou peripatounti legei* Ide o amnos tou theou.
verses.translation: And looking upon Jesus as he walked, he saith, Behold the Lamb of God!

verses.original: καὶ ἤκουσαν ⸂οἱ δύο μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ⸃ λαλοῦντος καὶ ἠκολούθησαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: kai ekoysan oi dyo mathitai autou lalountos kai ekoloythisan to Iisou.
verses.translation: And the two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.

verses.original: στραφεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ θεασάμενος αὐτοὺς ἀκολουθοῦντας λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί ζητεῖτε; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί (ὃ λέγεται ⸀μεθερμηνευόμενον Διδάσκαλε), ποῦ μένεις;
verses.translit: strafeis de o Iisous kai theasamenos autous akoloythountas legei autois* Ti ziteite; oi de eipan auto* Ravvi (o legetai methermineyomenon Didaskale), pou meneis;
verses.translation: Then Jesus turned, and saw them following, and saith unto them, What seek ye? They said unto him, Rabbi, (which is to say, being interpreted, Master,) where dwellest thou?

verses.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἔρχεσθε καὶ ⸂ὄψεσθε. ἦλθαν οὖν⸃ καὶ εἶδαν ποῦ μένει, καὶ παρʼ αὐτῷ ἔμειναν τὴν ἡμέραν ἐκείνην· ὥρα ἦν ὡς δεκάτη.
verses.translit: legei autois* Erhesthe kai opsesthe. elthan oun kai eidan pou menei, kai par' auto emeinan ten emeran ekeinin* ora en os dekati.
verses.translation: He saith unto them, Come and see. They came and saw where he dwelt, and abode with him that day: for it was about the tenth hour.

verses.original: ἦν Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς Σίμωνος Πέτρου εἷς ἐκ τῶν δύο τῶν ἀκουσάντων παρὰ Ἰωάννου καὶ ἀκολουθησάντων αὐτῷ·
verses.translit: en Andreas o adelfos Simonos Petroy eis ek ton dyo ton akoysanton para Ioannoy kai akoloythisanton auto*
verses.translation: One of the two which heard John speak , and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.

verses.original: εὑρίσκει οὗτος ⸀πρῶτον τὸν ἀδελφὸν τὸν ἴδιον Σίμωνα καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Εὑρήκαμεν τὸν Μεσσίαν (ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον χριστός).
verses.translit: euriskei outos proton ton adelfon ton idion Simona kai legei auto* Eurikamen ton Messian (o estin methermineyomenon hristos).
verses.translation: He first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias, which is, being interpreted, the Christ.

verses.original: ⸀ἤγαγεν αὐτὸν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν. ἐμβλέψας αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Σὺ εἶ Σίμων ὁ υἱὸς ⸀Ἰωάννου, σὺ κληθήσῃ Κηφᾶς (ὃ ἑρμηνεύεται Πέτρος).
verses.translit: egagen auton pros ton Iisoun. emvlepsas auto o Iisous eipen* Su ei Simon o yios Ioannoy, su klithise Kifas (o ermineyetai Petros).
verses.translation: And he brought him to Jesus. And when Jesus beheld him, he said, Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone.

verses.original: Τῇ ἐπαύριον ἠθέλησεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν. καὶ εὑρίσκει Φίλιππον καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀκολούθει μοι.
verses.translit: Te epayrion ethelisen exelthein eis ten Galilaian. kai euriskei Filippon kai legei auto o Iisous* Akoloythei moi.
verses.translation: The day following Jesus would go forth into Galilee, and findeth Philip, and saith unto him, Follow me.

verses.original: ἦν δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος ἀπὸ Βηθσαϊδά, ἐκ τῆς πόλεως Ἀνδρέου καὶ Πέτρου.
verses.translit: en de o Filippos apo Vithsaida, ek tes poleos Andreoy kai Petroy.
verses.translation: Now Philip was of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.

verses.original: εὑρίσκει Φίλιππος τὸν Ναθαναὴλ καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ὃν ἔγραψεν Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ νόμῳ καὶ οἱ προφῆται εὑρήκαμεν, ⸀Ἰησοῦν υἱὸν τοῦ Ἰωσὴφ τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρέτ.
verses.translit: euriskei Filippos ton Nathanael kai legei auto* On egrapsen Moyses en to nomo kai oi profetai eurikamen, Iisoun yion tou Iosef ton apo Nazaret.
verses.translation: Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ναθαναήλ· Ἐκ Ναζαρὲτ δύναταί τι ἀγαθὸν εἶναι; λέγει αὐτῷ ⸀ὁ Φίλιππος· Ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε.
verses.translit: kai eipen auto Nathanail* Ek Nazaret dynatai ti agathon einai; legei auto o Filippos* Erhoy kai ide.
verses.translation: And Nathanael said unto him, Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth? Philip saith unto him, Come and see.

verses.original: εἶδεν ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Ναθαναὴλ ἐρχόμενον πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ λέγει περὶ αὐτοῦ· Ἴδε ἀληθῶς Ἰσραηλίτης ἐν ᾧ δόλος οὐκ ἔστιν.
verses.translit: eiden o Iisous ton Nathanael erhomenon pros auton kai legei peri autou* Ide alithos Israilitis en o dolos ouk estin.
verses.translation: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and saith of him, Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!

verses.original: λέγει αὐτῷ Ναθαναήλ· Πόθεν με γινώσκεις; ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Πρὸ τοῦ σε Φίλιππον φωνῆσαι ὄντα ὑπὸ τὴν συκῆν εἶδόν σε.
verses.translit: legei auto Nathanail* Pothen me ginoskeis; apekrithi Iisous kai eipen auto* Pro tou se Filippon fonesai onta upo ten syken eidon se.
verses.translation: Nathanael saith unto him, Whence knowest thou me? Jesus answered and said unto him, Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη ⸂αὐτῷ Ναθαναήλ⸃· Ῥαββί, σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, σὺ ⸂βασιλεὺς εἶ⸃ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ.
verses.translit: apekrithi auto Nathanail* Ravvi, su ei o yios tou theou, su vasileus ei tou Israil.
verses.translation: Nathanael answered and saith unto him, Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel.

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὅτι εἶπόν σοι ⸀ὅτι εἶδόν σε ὑποκάτω τῆς συκῆς πιστεύεις; μείζω τούτων ⸀ὄψῃ.
verses.translit: apekrithi Iisous kai eipen auto* Oti eipon soi oti eidon se upokato tes sykes pisteyeis; meizo toyton opse.
verses.translation: Jesus answered and said unto him, Because I said unto thee, I saw thee under the fig tree, believest thou? thou shalt see greater things than these.

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ⸀ὑμῖν, ὄψεσθε τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεῳγότα καὶ τοὺς ἀγγέλους τοῦ θεοῦ ἀναβαίνοντας καὶ καταβαίνοντας ἐπὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
verses.translit: kai legei auto* Amen amen lego umin, opsesthe ton ouranon aneogota kai tous aggeloys tou theou anavainontas kai katavainontas epi ton yion tou anthropoy.
verses.translation: And he saith unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man.

verses.original: Καὶ τῇ ⸂ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ⸃ γάμος ἐγένετο ἐν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἦν ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐκεῖ·
verses.translit: Kai te emera te trite gamos egeneto en Kana tes Galilaias, kai en e mitir tou Iisou ekei*
verses.translation: And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:

verses.original: ἐκλήθη δὲ καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν γάμον.
verses.translit: eklithi de kai o Iisous kai oi mathitai autou eis ton gamon.
verses.translation: And both Jesus was called, and his disciples, to the marriage.

verses.original: καὶ ὑστερήσαντος οἴνου λέγει ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν· Οἶνον οὐκ ἔχουσιν.
verses.translit: kai usterisantos oinoy legei e mitir tou Iisou pros auton* Oinon ouk ehoysin.
verses.translation: And when they wanted wine, the mother of Jesus saith unto him, They have no wine.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, γύναι; οὔπω ἥκει ἡ ὥρα μου.
verses.translit: kai legei aute o Iisous* Ti emoi kai soi, gynai; oupo ekei e ora moy.
verses.translation: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, what have I to do with thee? mine hour is not yet come.

verses.original: λέγει ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ τοῖς διακόνοις· ⸂Ὅ τι⸃ ἂν λέγῃ ὑμῖν ποιήσατε.
verses.translit: legei e mitir autou tois diakonois* O ti an lege umin poiisate.
verses.translation: His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it .

verses.original: ἦσαν δὲ ἐκεῖ ⸂λίθιναι ὑδρίαι⸃ ἓξ ⸂κατὰ τὸν καθαρισμὸν τῶν Ἰουδαίων κείμεναι⸃, χωροῦσαι ἀνὰ μετρητὰς δύο ἢ τρεῖς.
verses.translit: esan de ekei lithinai udriai ex kata ton katharismon ton Ioydaion keimenai, horousai ana metritas dyo e treis.
verses.translation: And there were set there six waterpots of stone, after the manner of the purifying of the Jews, containing two or three firkins apiece.

verses.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Γεμίσατε τὰς ὑδρίας ὕδατος· καὶ ἐγέμισαν αὐτὰς ἕως ἄνω.
verses.translit: legei autois o Iisous* Gemisate tas udrias udatos* kai egemisan autas eos ano.
verses.translation: Jesus saith unto them, Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim.

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἀντλήσατε νῦν καὶ φέρετε τῷ ἀρχιτρικλίνῳ· ⸂οἱ δὲ⸃ ἤνεγκαν.
verses.translit: kai legei autois* Antlisate nun kai ferete to arhitriklino* oi de enegkan.
verses.translation: And he saith unto them, Draw out now, and bear unto the governor of the feast. And they bare it .

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἐγεύσατο ὁ ἀρχιτρίκλινος τὸ ὕδωρ οἶνον γεγενημένον, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει πόθεν ἐστίν, οἱ δὲ διάκονοι ᾔδεισαν οἱ ἠντληκότες τὸ ὕδωρ, φωνεῖ τὸν νυμφίον ὁ ἀρχιτρίκλινος
verses.translit: os de egeysato o arhitriklinos to udor oinon gegenimenon, kai ouk edei pothen estin, oi de diakonoi edeisan oi entlikotes to udor, fonei ton nymfion o arhitriklinos
verses.translation: When the ruler of the feast had tasted the water that was made wine, and knew not whence it was: (but the servants which drew the water knew;) the governor of the feast called the bridegroom,

verses.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Πᾶς ἄνθρωπος πρῶτον τὸν καλὸν οἶνον τίθησιν, καὶ ὅταν ⸀μεθυσθῶσιν τὸν ἐλάσσω· σὺ τετήρηκας τὸν καλὸν οἶνον ἕως ἄρτι.
verses.translit: kai legei auto* Pas anthropos proton ton kalon oinon tithisin, kai otan methysthosin ton elasso* su tetirikas ton kalon oinon eos arti.
verses.translation: And saith unto him, Every man at the beginning doth set forth good wine; and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse: but thou hast kept the good wine until now.

verses.original: ταύτην ⸀ἐποίησεν ἀρχὴν τῶν σημείων ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἐφανέρωσεν τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: taytin epoiisen arhen ton simeion o Iisous en Kana tes Galilaias kai efanerosen ten doxan autou, kai episteysan eis auton oi mathitai autou.
verses.translation: This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him.

verses.original: Μετὰ τοῦτο κατέβη εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ αὐτὸς καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ ⸀ἀδελφοὶ καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκεῖ ἔμειναν οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας.
verses.translit: Meta touto katevi eis Kafarnaoum autos kai e mitir autou kai oi adelfoi kai oi mathitai autou, kai ekei emeinan ou pollas emeras.
verses.translation: After this he went down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, and his brethren, and his disciples: and they continued there not many days.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγγὺς ἦν τὸ πάσχα τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ ἀνέβη εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
verses.translit: Kai eggus en to pasha ton Ioydaion, kai anevi eis Ierosolyma o Iisous.
verses.translation: And the Jews’ passover was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem,

verses.original: καὶ εὗρεν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τοὺς πωλοῦντας βόας καὶ πρόβατα καὶ περιστερὰς καὶ τοὺς κερματιστὰς καθημένους,
