verses.original: ἐγὼ περὶ αὐτῶν ἐρωτῶ· οὐ περὶ τοῦ κόσμου ἐρωτῶ ἀλλὰ περὶ ὧν δέδωκάς μοι, ὅτι σοί εἰσιν,
verses.translit: ego peri auton eroto* ou peri tou kosmoy eroto alla peri on dedokas moi, oti soi eisin,
verses.translation: I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine.

verses.original: καὶ τὰ ἐμὰ πάντα σά ἐστιν καὶ τὰ σὰ ἐμά, καὶ δεδόξασμαι ἐν αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: kai ta ema panta sa estin kai ta sa ema, kai dedoxasmai en autois.
verses.translation: And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them.

verses.original: καὶ οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, καὶ ⸀αὐτοὶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ εἰσίν, κἀγὼ πρὸς σὲ ἔρχομαι. πάτερ ἅγιε, τήρησον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ᾧ δέδωκάς μοι, ἵνα ὦσιν ἓν ⸀καθὼς ἡμεῖς.
verses.translit: kai ouketi eimi en to kosmo, kai autoi en to kosmo eisin, kago pros se erhomai. pater agie, tirison autous en to onomati soy o dedokas moi, ina osin en kathos emeis.
verses.translation: And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are .

verses.original: ὅτε ἤμην μετʼ ⸀αὐτῶν ἐγὼ ἐτήρουν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ⸀ᾧ δέδωκάς μοι, ⸀καὶ ἐφύλαξα, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀπώλετο εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας, ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ.
verses.translit: ote emin met' auton ego etiroyn autous en to onomati soy o dedokas moi, kai efylaxa, kai oudeis ex auton apoleto ei me o yios tes apoleias, ina e grafe plirothe.
verses.translation: While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled.

verses.original: νῦν δὲ πρὸς σὲ ἔρχομαι, καὶ ταῦτα λαλῶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἵνα ἔχωσιν τὴν χαρὰν τὴν ἐμὴν πεπληρωμένην ἐν ⸀ἑαυτοῖς.
verses.translit: nun de pros se erhomai, kai tauta lalo en to kosmo ina ehosin ten haran ten emen pepliromenin en eaytois.
verses.translation: And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves.

verses.original: ἐγὼ δέδωκα αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον σου, καὶ ὁ κόσμος ἐμίσησεν αὐτούς, ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶν ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου καθὼς ἐγὼ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου.
verses.translit: ego dedoka autois ton logon soy, kai o kosmos emisisen autoys, oti ouk eisin ek tou kosmoy kathos ego ouk eimi ek tou kosmoy.
verses.translation: I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.

verses.original: οὐκ ἐρωτῶ ἵνα ἄρῃς αὐτοὺς ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου ἀλλʼ ἵνα τηρήσῃς αὐτοὺς ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ.
verses.translit: ouk eroto ina ares autous ek tou kosmoy all' ina tirises autous ek tou ponirou.
verses.translation: I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.

verses.original: ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου οὐκ εἰσὶν καθὼς ἐγὼ ⸂οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου⸃.
verses.translit: ek tou kosmoy ouk eisin kathos ego ouk eimi ek tou kosmoy.
verses.translation: They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.

verses.original: ἁγίασον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ ⸀ἀληθείᾳ· ὁ λόγος ὁ σὸς ἀλήθειά ἐστιν.
verses.translit: agiason autous en te alitheia* o logos o sos alitheia estin.
verses.translation: Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.

verses.original: καθὼς ἐμὲ ἀπέστειλας εἰς τὸν κόσμον, κἀγὼ ἀπέστειλα αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν κόσμον·
verses.translit: kathos eme apesteilas eis ton kosmon, kago apesteila autous eis ton kosmon*
verses.translation: As thou hast sent me into the world, even so have I also sent them into the world.

verses.original: καὶ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἐγὼ ἁγιάζω ἐμαυτόν, ἵνα ⸂ὦσιν καὶ αὐτοὶ⸃ ἡγιασμένοι ἐν ἀληθείᾳ.
verses.translit: kai uper auton ego agiazo emayton, ina osin kai autoi egiasmenoi en alitheia.
verses.translation: And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they also might be sanctified through the truth.

verses.original: Οὐ περὶ τούτων δὲ ἐρωτῶ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ τῶν πιστευόντων διὰ τοῦ λόγου αὐτῶν εἰς ἐμέ,
verses.translit: Ou peri toyton de eroto monon, alla kai peri ton pisteyonton dia tou logoy auton eis eme,
verses.translation: Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word;

verses.original: ἵνα πάντες ἓν ὦσιν, καθὼς σύ, ⸀πάτερ, ἐν ἐμοὶ κἀγὼ ἐν σοί, ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐν ⸀ἡμῖν ὦσιν, ἵνα ὁ κόσμος ⸀πιστεύῃ ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας.
verses.translit: ina pantes en osin, kathos sy, pater, en emoi kago en soi, ina kai autoi en emin osin, ina o kosmos pisteye oti sy me apesteilas.
verses.translation: That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.

verses.original: κἀγὼ τὴν δόξαν ἣν δέδωκάς μοι δέδωκα αὐτοῖς, ἵνα ὦσιν ἓν καθὼς ἡμεῖς ⸀ἕν,
verses.translit: kago ten doxan en dedokas moi dedoka autois, ina osin en kathos emeis en,
verses.translation: And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one:

verses.original: ἐγὼ ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ σὺ ἐν ἐμοί, ἵνα ὦσιν τετελειωμένοι εἰς ἕν, ⸀ἵνα γινώσκῃ ὁ κόσμος ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας καὶ ἠγάπησας αὐτοὺς καθὼς ἐμὲ ἠγάπησας.
verses.translit: ego en autois kai su en emoi, ina osin teteleiomenoi eis en, ina ginoske o kosmos oti sy me apesteilas kai egapisas autous kathos eme egapisas.
verses.translation: I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one; and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them, as thou hast loved me.

verses.original: ⸀πάτερ, ⸀ὃ δέδωκάς μοι, θέλω ἵνα ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ κἀκεῖνοι ὦσιν μετʼ ἐμοῦ, ἵνα θεωρῶσιν τὴν δόξαν τὴν ἐμὴν ἣν ⸀δέδωκάς μοι, ὅτι ἠγάπησάς με πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.
verses.translit: pater, o dedokas moi, thelo ina opoy eimi ego kakeinoi osin met' emou, ina theorosin ten doxan ten emen en dedokas moi, oti egapisas me pro katavoles kosmoy.
verses.translation: Father, I will that they also, whom thou hast given me, be with me where I am; that they may behold my glory, which thou hast given me: for thou lovedst me before the foundation of the world.

verses.original: ⸀Πάτερ δίκαιε, καὶ ὁ κόσμος σε οὐκ ἔγνω, ἐγὼ δέ σε ἔγνων, καὶ οὗτοι ἔγνωσαν ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας,
verses.translit: Pater dikaie, kai o kosmos se ouk egno, ego de se egnon, kai outoi egnosan oti sy me apesteilas,
verses.translation: O righteous Father, the world hath not known thee: but I have known thee, and these have known that thou hast sent me.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγνώρισα αὐτοῖς τὸ ὄνομά σου καὶ γνωρίσω, ἵνα ἡ ἀγάπη ἣν ἠγάπησάς με ἐν αὐτοῖς ᾖ κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: kai egnorisa autois to onoma soy kai gnoriso, ina e agapi en egapisas me en autois e kago en autois.
verses.translation: And I have declared unto them thy name, and will declare it : that the love wherewith thou hast loved me may be in them, and I in them.

verses.original: Ταῦτα ⸀εἰπὼν Ἰησοῦς ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ πέραν τοῦ χειμάρρου ⸀τοῦ Κεδρὼν ὅπου ἦν κῆπος, εἰς ὃν εἰσῆλθεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Tauta eipon Iisous exelthen sun tois mathitais autou peran tou heimarroy tou Kedron opoy en kepos, eis on eiselthen autos kai oi mathitai autou.
verses.translation: When Jesus had spoken these words, he went forth with his disciples over the brook Cedron, where was a garden, into the which he entered, and his disciples.

verses.original: ᾔδει δὲ καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν τὸν τόπον, ὅτι πολλάκις ⸀συνήχθη Ἰησοῦς ἐκεῖ μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: edei de kai Ioydas o paradidous auton ton topon, oti pollakis synihthi Iisous ekei meta ton mathiton autou.
verses.translation: And Judas also, which betrayed him, knew the place: for Jesus ofttimes resorted thither with his disciples.

verses.original: ὁ οὖν Ἰούδας λαβὼν τὴν σπεῖραν καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ ⸂ἐκ τῶν⸃ Φαρισαίων ὑπηρέτας ἔρχεται ἐκεῖ μετὰ φανῶν καὶ λαμπάδων καὶ ὅπλων.
verses.translit: o oun Ioydas lavon ten speiran kai ek ton arhiereon kai ek ton Farisaion upiretas erhetai ekei meta fanon kai lampadon kai oplon.
verses.translation: Judas then, having received a band of men and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, cometh thither with lanterns and torches and weapons.

verses.original: Ἰησοῦς ⸀οὖν εἰδὼς πάντα τὰ ἐρχόμενα ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ⸂ἐξῆλθεν, καὶ λέγει⸃ αὐτοῖς· Τίνα ζητεῖτε;
verses.translit: Iisous oun eidos panta ta erhomena ep' auton exelthen, kai legei autois* Tina ziteite;
verses.translation: Jesus therefore, knowing all things that should come upon him, went forth, and said unto them, Whom seek ye?

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ· Ἰησοῦν τὸν Ναζωραῖον. λέγει ⸀αὐτοῖς· Ἐγώ εἰμι. εἱστήκει δὲ καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν μετʼ αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: apekrithisan auto* Iisoun ton Nazoraion. legei autois* Ego eimi. eistikei de kai Ioydas o paradidous auton met' auton.
verses.translation: They answered him, Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus saith unto them, I am he . And Judas also, which betrayed him, stood with them.

verses.original: ὡς οὖν εἶπεν ⸀αὐτοῖς· Ἐγώ εἰμι, ἀπῆλθον εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω καὶ ἔπεσαν χαμαί.
verses.translit: os oun eipen autois* Ego eimi, apelthon eis ta opiso kai epesan hamai.
verses.translation: As soon then as he had said unto them, I am he , they went backward, and fell to the ground.

verses.original: πάλιν οὖν ⸂ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτούς⸃· Τίνα ζητεῖτε; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἰησοῦν τὸν Ναζωραῖον.
verses.translit: palin oun epirotisen autoys* Tina ziteite; oi de eipan* Iisoun ton Nazoraion.
verses.translation: Then asked he them again, Whom seek ye? And they said, Jesus of Nazareth.

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· Εἶπον ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι· εἰ οὖν ἐμὲ ζητεῖτε, ἄφετε τούτους ὑπάγειν·
verses.translit: apekrithi Iisous* Eipon umin oti ego eimi* ei oun eme ziteite, afete toytoys upagein*
verses.translation: Jesus answered, I have told you that I am he : if therefore ye seek me, let these go their way:

verses.original: ἵνα πληρωθῇ ὁ λόγος ὃν εἶπεν ὅτι Οὓς δέδωκάς μοι οὐκ ἀπώλεσα ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐδένα.
verses.translit: ina plirothe o logos on eipen oti Ous dedokas moi ouk apolesa ex auton oudena.
verses.translation: That the saying might be fulfilled, which he spake, Of them which thou gavest me have I lost none.

verses.original: Σίμων οὖν Πέτρος ἔχων μάχαιραν εἵλκυσεν αὐτὴν καὶ ἔπαισεν τὸν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως δοῦλον καὶ ἀπέκοψεν αὐτοῦ τὸ ⸀ὠτάριον τὸ δεξιόν. ἦν δὲ ὄνομα τῷ δούλῳ Μάλχος.
verses.translit: Simon oun Petros ehon mahairan eilkysen auten kai epaisen ton tou arhiereos doulon kai apekopsen autou to otarion to dexion. en de onoma to doylo Malhos.
verses.translation: Then Simon Peter having a sword drew it, and smote the high priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.

verses.original: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ Πέτρῳ· Βάλε τὴν ⸀μάχαιραν εἰς τὴν θήκην· τὸ ποτήριον ὃ δέδωκέν μοι ὁ πατὴρ οὐ μὴ πίω αὐτό;
verses.translit: eipen oun o Iisous to Petro* Vale ten mahairan eis ten thikin* to potirion o dedoken moi o pater ou me pio auto;
verses.translation: Then said Jesus unto Peter, Put up thy sword into the sheath: the cup which my Father hath given me, shall I not drink it?

verses.original: Ἡ οὖν σπεῖρα καὶ ὁ χιλίαρχος καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται τῶν Ἰουδαίων συνέλαβον τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἔδησαν αὐτὸν
verses.translit: E oun speira kai o hiliarhos kai oi upiretai ton Ioydaion synelavon ton Iisoun kai edisan auton
verses.translation: Then the band and the captain and officers of the Jews took Jesus, and bound him,

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἤγαγον πρὸς Ἅνναν πρῶτον· ἦν γὰρ πενθερὸς τοῦ Καϊάφα, ὃς ἦν ἀρχιερεὺς τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου·
verses.translit: kai egagon pros Annan proton* en gar pentheros tou Kaiafa, os en arhiereus tou eniaytou ekeinoy*
verses.translation: And led him away to Annas first; for he was father in law to Caiaphas, which was the high priest that same year.

verses.original: ἦν δὲ Καϊάφας ὁ συμβουλεύσας τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὅτι συμφέρει ἕνα ἄνθρωπον ⸀ἀποθανεῖν ὑπὲρ τοῦ λαοῦ.
verses.translit: en de Kaiafas o symvoyleysas tois Ioydaiois oti symferei ena anthropon apothanein uper tou laou.
verses.translation: Now Caiaphas was he, which gave counsel to the Jews, that it was expedient that one man should die for the people.

verses.original: Ἠκολούθει δὲ τῷ Ἰησοῦ Σίμων Πέτρος ⸀καὶ ἄλλος μαθητής. ὁ δὲ μαθητὴς ἐκεῖνος ἦν γνωστὸς τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ καὶ συνεισῆλθεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως,
verses.translit: Ekoloythei de to Iisou Simon Petros kai allos mathitis. o de mathites ekeinos en gnostos to arhierei kai syneiselthen to Iisou eis ten aulen tou arhiereos,
verses.translation: And Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did another disciple: that disciple was known unto the high priest, and went in with Jesus into the palace of the high priest.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος εἱστήκει πρὸς τῇ θύρᾳ ἔξω. ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ μαθητὴς ὁ ἄλλος ⸀ὁ γνωστὸς ⸂τοῦ ἀρχιερέως⸃ καὶ εἶπεν τῇ θυρωρῷ καὶ εἰσήγαγεν τὸν Πέτρον.
verses.translit: o de Petros eistikei pros te thyra exo. exelthen oun o mathites o allos o gnostos tou arhiereos kai eipen te thyroro kai eisigagen ton Petron.
verses.translation: But Peter stood at the door without. Then went out that other disciple, which was known unto the high priest, and spake unto her that kept the door, and brought in Peter.

verses.original: λέγει οὖν ⸂τῷ Πέτρῳ ἡ παιδίσκη ἡ θυρωρός⸃· Μὴ καὶ σὺ ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν εἶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τούτου; λέγει ἐκεῖνος· Οὐκ εἰμί.
verses.translit: legei oun to Petro e paidiski e thyroros* Me kai su ek ton mathiton ei tou anthropoy toytoy; legei ekeinos* Ouk eimi.
verses.translation: Then saith the damsel that kept the door unto Peter, Art not thou also one of this man’s disciples? He saith, I am not.

verses.original: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ οἱ δοῦλοι καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται ἀνθρακιὰν πεποιηκότες, ὅτι ψῦχος ἦν, καὶ ἐθερμαίνοντο· ἦν δὲ ⸂καὶ ὁ Πέτρος μετʼ αὐτῶν⸃ ἑστὼς καὶ θερμαινόμενος.
verses.translit: eistikeisan de oi douloi kai oi upiretai anthrakian pepoiikotes, oti psuhos en, kai ethermainonto* en de kai o Petros met' auton estos kai thermainomenos.
verses.translation: And the servants and officers stood there, who had made a fire of coals; for it was cold: and they warmed themselves: and Peter stood with them, and warmed himself.

verses.original: Ὁ οὖν ἀρχιερεὺς ἠρώτησεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν περὶ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ περὶ τῆς διδαχῆς αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: O oun arhiereus erotisen ton Iisoun peri ton mathiton autou kai peri tes didahes autou.
verses.translation: The high priest then asked Jesus of his disciples, and of his doctrine.

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη ⸀αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐγὼ παρρησίᾳ ⸀λελάληκα τῷ κόσμῳ· ἐγὼ πάντοτε ἐδίδαξα ἐν συναγωγῇ καὶ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, ὅπου ⸀πάντες οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι συνέρχονται, καὶ ἐν κρυπτῷ ἐλάλησα οὐδέν·
verses.translit: apekrithi auto Iisous* Ego parrisia lelalika to kosmo* ego pantote edidaxa en synagoge kai en to iero, opoy pantes oi Ioydaioi synerhontai, kai en krypto elalisa ouden*
verses.translation: Jesus answered him, I spake openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort; and in secret have I said nothing.

verses.original: τί με ⸂ἐρωτᾷς; ἐρώτησον⸃ τοὺς ἀκηκοότας τί ἐλάλησα αὐτοῖς· ἴδε οὗτοι οἴδασιν ἃ εἶπον ἐγώ.
verses.translit: ti me erotas; erotison tous akikootas ti elalisa autois* ide outoi oidasin a eipon ego.
verses.translation: Why askest thou me? ask them which heard me, what I have said unto them: behold, they know what I said.

verses.original: ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ εἰπόντος εἷς ⸂παρεστηκὼς τῶν ὑπηρετῶν⸃ ἔδωκεν ῥάπισμα τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἰπών· Οὕτως ἀποκρίνῃ τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ;
verses.translit: tauta de autou eipontos eis parestikos ton upireton edoken Rapisma to Iisou eipon* Outos apokrine to arhierei;
verses.translation: And when he had thus spoken, one of the officers which stood by struck Jesus with the palm of his hand, saying, Answerest thou the high priest so?

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη ⸀αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς· Εἰ κακῶς ἐλάλησα, μαρτύρησον περὶ τοῦ κακοῦ· εἰ δὲ καλῶς, τί με δέρεις;
verses.translit: apekrithi auto Iisous* Ei kakos elalisa, martyrison peri tou kakou* ei de kalos, ti me dereis;
verses.translation: Jesus answered him, If I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil: but if well, why smitest thou me?

verses.original: ἀπέστειλεν ⸀οὖν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἅννας δεδεμένον πρὸς Καϊάφαν τὸν ἀρχιερέα.
verses.translit: apesteilen oun auton o Annas dedemenon pros Kaiafan ton arhierea.
verses.translation: Now Annas had sent him bound unto Caiaphas the high priest.

verses.original: Ἦν δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος ἑστὼς καὶ θερμαινόμενος. εἶπον οὖν αὐτῷ· Μὴ καὶ σὺ ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ εἶ; ⸀ἠρνήσατο ἐκεῖνος καὶ εἶπεν· Οὐκ εἰμί.
verses.translit: En de Simon Petros estos kai thermainomenos. eipon oun auto* Me kai su ek ton mathiton autou ei; ernisato ekeinos kai eipen* Ouk eimi.
verses.translation: And Simon Peter stood and warmed himself. They said therefore unto him, Art not thou also one of his disciples? He denied it , and said, I am not.

verses.original: λέγει εἷς ἐκ τῶν δούλων τοῦ ἀρχιερέως, συγγενὴς ὢν οὗ ἀπέκοψεν Πέτρος τὸ ὠτίον· Οὐκ ἐγώ σε εἶδον ἐν τῷ κήπῳ μετʼ αὐτοῦ;
verses.translit: legei eis ek ton doylon tou arhiereos, syggenes on ou apekopsen Petros to otion* Ouk ego se eidon en to kipo met' autou;
verses.translation: One of the servants of the high priest, being his kinsman whose ear Peter cut off, saith, Did not I see thee in the garden with him?

verses.original: πάλιν οὖν ⸀ἠρνήσατο Πέτρος· καὶ εὐθέως ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν.
verses.translit: palin oun ernisato Petros* kai eutheos alektor efonisen.
verses.translation: Peter then denied again: and immediately the cock crew.

verses.original: Ἄγουσιν οὖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ Καϊάφα εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον· ἦν δὲ πρωΐ· καὶ αὐτοὶ οὐκ εἰσῆλθον εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον, ἵνα μὴ μιανθῶσιν ⸀ἀλλὰ φάγωσιν τὸ πάσχα.
verses.translit: Agoysin oun ton Iisoun apo tou Kaiafa eis to praitorion* en de proI* kai autoi ouk eiselthon eis to praitorion, ina me mianthosin alla fagosin to pasha.
verses.translation: Then led they Jesus from Caiaphas unto the hall of judgment: and it was early; and they themselves went not into the judgment hall, lest they should be defiled; but that they might eat the passover.

verses.original: ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ Πιλᾶτος ⸀ἔξω πρὸς αὐτοὺς καὶ ⸀φησίν· Τίνα κατηγορίαν φέρετε ⸀κατὰ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τούτου;
verses.translit: exelthen oun o Pilatos exo pros autous kai fisin* Tina katigorian ferete kata tou anthropoy toytoy;
verses.translation: Pilate then went out unto them, and said, What accusation bring ye against this man?

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθησαν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Εἰ μὴ ἦν οὗτος ⸂κακὸν ποιῶν⸃, οὐκ ἄν σοι παρεδώκαμεν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: apekrithisan kai eipan auto* Ei me en outos kakon poion, ouk an soi paredokamen auton.
verses.translation: They answered and said unto him, If he were not a malefactor, we would not have delivered him up unto thee.

verses.original: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ⸀ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Λάβετε αὐτὸν ὑμεῖς, καὶ κατὰ τὸν νόμον ὑμῶν κρίνατε αὐτόν. ⸀εἶπον αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Ἡμῖν οὐκ ἔξεστιν ἀποκτεῖναι οὐδένα·
verses.translit: eipen oun autois o Pilatos* Lavete auton umeis, kai kata ton nomon umon krinate auton. eipon auto oi Ioydaioi* Emin ouk exestin apokteinai oudena*
verses.translation: Then said Pilate unto them, Take ye him, and judge him according to your law. The Jews therefore said unto him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death:

verses.original: ἵνα ὁ λόγος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ πληρωθῇ ὃν εἶπεν σημαίνων ποίῳ θανάτῳ ἤμελλεν ἀποθνῄσκειν.
verses.translit: ina o logos tou Iisou plirothe on eipen simainon poio thanato emellen apothneskein.
verses.translation: That the saying of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spake, signifying what death he should die.

verses.original: Εἰσῆλθεν οὖν ⸂πάλιν εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον⸃ ὁ Πιλᾶτος καὶ ἐφώνησεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων;
verses.translit: Eiselthen oun palin eis to praitorion o Pilatos kai efonisen ton Iisoun kai eipen auto* Su ei o vasileus ton Ioydaion;
verses.translation: Then Pilate entered into the judgment hall again, and called Jesus, and said unto him, Art thou the King of the Jews?

verses.original: ⸀ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· ⸂Ἀπὸ σεαυτοῦ⸃ σὺ τοῦτο λέγεις ἢ ἄλλοι ⸂εἶπόν σοι⸃ περὶ ἐμοῦ;
verses.translit: apekrithi Iisous* Apo seaytou su touto legeis e alloi eipon soi peri emou;
verses.translation: Jesus answered him, Sayest thou this thing of thyself, or did others tell it thee of me?

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Μήτι ἐγὼ Ἰουδαῖός εἰμι; τὸ ἔθνος τὸ σὸν καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς παρέδωκάν σε ἐμοί· τί ἐποίησας;
verses.translit: apekrithi o Pilatos* Miti ego Ioydaios eimi; to ethnos to son kai oi arhiereis paredokan se emoi* ti epoiisas;
verses.translation: Pilate answered, Am I a Jew? Thine own nation and the chief priests have delivered thee unto me: what hast thou done?

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς· Ἡ βασιλεία ἡ ἐμὴ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου τούτου· εἰ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου τούτου ἦν ἡ βασιλεία ἡ ἐμή, οἱ ὑπηρέται ⸂οἱ ἐμοὶ ἠγωνίζοντο ἄν⸃, ἵνα μὴ παραδοθῶ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις· νῦν δὲ ἡ βασιλεία ἡ ἐμὴ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐντεῦθεν.
verses.translit: apekrithi Iisous* E vasileia e eme ouk estin ek tou kosmoy toytoy* ei ek tou kosmoy toytoy en e vasileia e emi, oi upiretai oi emoi egonizonto an, ina me paradotho tois Ioydaiois* nun de e vasileia e eme ouk estin enteuthen.
verses.translation: Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from hence.

verses.original: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Οὐκοῦν βασιλεὺς εἶ σύ; ἀπεκρίθη ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Σὺ λέγεις ὅτι βασιλεύς ⸀εἰμι. ἐγὼ εἰς τοῦτο γεγέννημαι καὶ εἰς τοῦτο ἐλήλυθα εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἵνα μαρτυρήσω τῇ ἀληθείᾳ· πᾶς ὁ ὢν ἐκ τῆς ἀληθείας ἀκούει μου τῆς φωνῆς.
verses.translit: eipen oun auto o Pilatos* Oukoun vasileus ei sy; apekrithi o Iisous* Su legeis oti vasileys eimi. ego eis touto gegennimai kai eis touto elilytha eis ton kosmon ina martyriso te alitheia* pas o on ek tes alitheias akoyei moy tes fones.
verses.translation: Pilate therefore said unto him, Art thou a king then? Jesus answered, Thou sayest that I am a king. To this end was I born, and for this cause came I into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth. Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice.

verses.original: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Τί ἐστιν ἀλήθεια; Καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν πάλιν ἐξῆλθεν πρὸς τοὺς Ἰουδαίους, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἐγὼ οὐδεμίαν ⸂εὑρίσκω ἐν αὐτῷ αἰτίαν⸃·
verses.translit: legei auto o Pilatos* Ti estin alitheia; Kai touto eipon palin exelthen pros tous Ioydaioys, kai legei autois* Ego oudemian eurisko en auto aitian*
verses.translation: Pilate saith unto him, What is truth? And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Jews, and saith unto them, I find in him no fault at all .

verses.original: ἔστιν δὲ συνήθεια ὑμῖν ἵνα ἕνα ⸂ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν⸃ ἐν τῷ πάσχα· βούλεσθε οὖν ⸄ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν⸅ τὸν βασιλέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων;
verses.translit: estin de synitheia umin ina ena apolyso umin en to pasha* voylesthe oun apolyso umin ton vasilea ton Ioydaion;
verses.translation: But ye have a custom, that I should release unto you one at the passover: will ye therefore that I release unto you the King of the Jews?

verses.original: ἐκραύγασαν οὖν ⸀πάλιν λέγοντες· Μὴ τοῦτον ἀλλὰ τὸν Βαραββᾶν. ἦν δὲ ὁ Βαραββᾶς λῃστής.
verses.translit: ekraygasan oun palin legontes* Me touton alla ton Varavvan. en de o Varavvas lestis.
verses.translation: Then cried they all again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. Now Barabbas was a robber.

verses.original: Τότε οὖν ἔλαβεν ὁ Πιλᾶτος τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἐμαστίγωσεν.
verses.translit: Tote oun elaven o Pilatos ton Iisoun kai emastigosen.
verses.translation: Then Pilate therefore took Jesus, and scourged him .

verses.original: καὶ οἱ στρατιῶται πλέξαντες στέφανον ἐξ ἀκανθῶν ἐπέθηκαν αὐτοῦ τῇ κεφαλῇ, καὶ ἱμάτιον πορφυροῦν περιέβαλον αὐτόν,
verses.translit: kai oi stratiotai plexantes stefanon ex akanthon epethikan autou te kefale, kai imation porfyroun perievalon auton,
verses.translation: And the soldiers platted a crown of thorns, and put it on his head, and they put on him a purple robe,

verses.original: καὶ ⸂ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ⸃ ἔλεγον· Χαῖρε, ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων· καὶ ἐδίδοσαν αὐτῷ ῥαπίσματα.
verses.translit: kai erhonto pros auton kai elegon* Haire, o vasileus ton Ioydaion* kai edidosan auto Rapismata.
verses.translation: And said, Hail, King of the Jews! and they smote him with their hands.

verses.original: ⸂καὶ ἐξῆλθεν⸃ πάλιν ἔξω ὁ Πιλᾶτος καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἴδε ἄγω ὑμῖν αὐτὸν ἔξω, ἵνα γνῶτε ὅτι ⸂οὐδεμίαν αἰτίαν εὑρίσκω ἐν αὐτῷ⸃.
verses.translit: kai exelthen palin exo o Pilatos kai legei autois* Ide ago umin auton exo, ina gnote oti oudemian aitian eurisko en auto.
verses.translation: Pilate therefore went forth again, and saith unto them, Behold, I bring him forth to you, that ye may know that I find no fault in him.

verses.original: ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἔξω, φορῶν τὸν ἀκάνθινον στέφανον καὶ τὸ πορφυροῦν ἱμάτιον. καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· ⸀Ἰδοὺ ὁ ἄνθρωπος.
verses.translit: exelthen oun o Iisous exo, foron ton akanthinon stefanon kai to porfyroun imation. kai legei autois* Idou o anthropos.
verses.translation: Then came Jesus forth, wearing the crown of thorns, and the purple robe. And Pilate saith unto them, Behold the man!

verses.original: ὅτε οὖν εἶδον αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται ἐκραύγασαν λέγοντες· Σταύρωσον ⸀σταύρωσον. λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Λάβετε αὐτὸν ὑμεῖς καὶ σταυρώσατε, ἐγὼ γὰρ οὐχ εὑρίσκω ἐν αὐτῷ αἰτίαν.
verses.translit: ote oun eidon auton oi arhiereis kai oi upiretai ekraygasan legontes* Stayroson stayroson. legei autois o Pilatos* Lavete auton umeis kai stayrosate, ego gar ouh eurisko en auto aitian.
verses.translation: When the chief priests therefore and officers saw him, they cried out, saying, Crucify him , crucify him . Pilate saith unto them, Take ye him, and crucify him : for I find no fault in him.

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Ἡμεῖς νόμον ἔχομεν, καὶ κατὰ τὸν ⸀νόμον ὀφείλει ἀποθανεῖν, ὅτι ⸂υἱὸν θεοῦ ἑαυτὸν⸃ ἐποίησεν.
verses.translit: apekrithisan auto oi Ioydaioi* Emeis nomon ehomen, kai kata ton nomon ofeilei apothanein, oti yion theou eayton epoiisen.
verses.translation: The Jews answered him, We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.

verses.original: Ὅτε οὖν ἤκουσεν ὁ Πιλᾶτος τοῦτον τὸν λόγον, μᾶλλον ἐφοβήθη,
verses.translit: Ote oun ekoysen o Pilatos touton ton logon, mallon efovithi,
verses.translation: When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he was the more afraid;

verses.original: καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον πάλιν καὶ λέγει τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Πόθεν εἶ σύ; ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀπόκρισιν οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai eiselthen eis to praitorion palin kai legei to Iisou* Pothen ei sy; o de Iisous apokrisin ouk edoken auto.
verses.translation: And went again into the judgment hall, and saith unto Jesus, Whence art thou? But Jesus gave him no answer.

verses.original: λέγει οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Ἐμοὶ οὐ λαλεῖς; οὐκ οἶδας ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχω ⸂ἀπολῦσαί σε καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχω σταυρῶσαί⸃ σε;
verses.translit: legei oun auto o Pilatos* Emoi ou laleis; ouk oidas oti exoysian eho apolusai se kai exoysian eho stayrosai se;
verses.translation: Then saith Pilate unto him, Speakest thou not unto me? knowest thou not that I have power to crucify thee, and have power to release thee?

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη ⸀αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐκ εἶχες ἐξουσίαν ⸂κατʼ ἐμοῦ οὐδεμίαν⸃ εἰ μὴ ἦν ⸂δεδομένον σοι⸃ ἄνωθεν· διὰ τοῦτο ὁ ⸀παραδούς μέ σοι μείζονα ἁμαρτίαν ἔχει.
verses.translit: apekrithi auto Iisous* Ouk eihes exoysian kat' emou oudemian ei me en dedomenon soi anothen* dia touto o paradoys me soi meizona amartian ehei.
verses.translation: Jesus answered, Thou couldest have no power at all against me, except it were given thee from above: therefore he that delivered me unto thee hath the greater sin.

verses.original: ἐκ τούτου ⸂ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐζήτει⸃ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτόν· οἱ δὲ Ἰουδαῖοι ⸀ἐκραύγασαν λέγοντες· Ἐὰν τοῦτον ἀπολύσῃς, οὐκ εἶ φίλος τοῦ Καίσαρος· πᾶς ὁ βασιλέα ἑαυτὸν ποιῶν ἀντιλέγει τῷ Καίσαρι.
verses.translit: ek toytoy o Pilatos ezitei apolusai auton* oi de Ioydaioi ekraygasan legontes* Ean touton apolyses, ouk ei filos tou Kaisaros* pas o vasilea eayton poion antilegei to Kaisari.
verses.translation: And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Cæsar’s friend: whosoever maketh himself a king speaketh against Cæsar.

verses.original: Ὁ οὖν Πιλᾶτος ἀκούσας ⸂τῶν λόγων τούτων⸃ ἤγαγεν ἔξω τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ⸀ἐπὶ βήματος εἰς τόπον λεγόμενον Λιθόστρωτον, Ἑβραϊστὶ δὲ Γαββαθα.
verses.translit: O oun Pilatos akoysas ton logon toyton egagen exo ton Iisoun, kai ekathisen epi vimatos eis topon legomenon Lithostroton, Evraisti de Gavvatha.
verses.translation: When Pilate therefore heard that saying, he brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha.

verses.original: ἦν δὲ παρασκευὴ τοῦ πάσχα, ὥρα ⸂ἦν ὡς⸃ ἕκτη. καὶ λέγει τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις· Ἴδε ὁ βασιλεὺς ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: en de paraskeye tou pasha, ora en os ekti. kai legei tois Ioydaiois* Ide o vasileus umon.
verses.translation: And it was the preparation of the passover, and about the sixth hour: and he saith unto the Jews, Behold your King!

verses.original: ⸂ἐκραύγασαν οὖν ἐκεῖνοι⸃· Ἆρον ἆρον, σταύρωσον αὐτόν. λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Τὸν βασιλέα ὑμῶν σταυρώσω; ἀπεκρίθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς· Οὐκ ἔχομεν βασιλέα εἰ μὴ Καίσαρα.
verses.translit: ekraygasan oun ekeinoi* Aron aron, stayroson auton. legei autois o Pilatos* Ton vasilea umon stayroso; apekrithisan oi arhiereis* Ouk ehomen vasilea ei me Kaisara.
verses.translation: But they cried out, Away with him , away with him , crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cæsar.

verses.original: τότε οὖν παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν αὐτοῖς ἵνα σταυρωθῇ. Παρέλαβον ⸀οὖν τὸν ⸀Ἰησοῦν·
verses.translit: tote oun paredoken auton autois ina stayrothe. Parelavon oun ton Iisoun*
verses.translation: Then delivered he him therefore unto them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away.

verses.original: καὶ βαστάζων ⸂αὑτῷ τὸν σταυρὸν⸃ ἐξῆλθεν εἰς ⸀τὸν λεγόμενον Κρανίου Τόπον, ⸀ὃ λέγεται Ἑβραϊστὶ Γολγοθα,
verses.translit: kai vastazon auto ton stayron exelthen eis ton legomenon Kranioy Topon, o legetai Evraisti Golgotha,
verses.translation: And he bearing his cross went forth into a place called the place of a skull, which is called in the Hebrew Golgotha:

verses.original: ὅπου αὐτὸν ἐσταύρωσαν, καὶ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἄλλους δύο ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ἐντεῦθεν, μέσον δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: opoy auton estayrosan, kai met' autou alloys dyo enteuthen kai enteuthen, meson de ton Iisoun.
verses.translation: Where they crucified him, and two other with him, on either side one, and Jesus in the midst.

verses.original: ἔγραψεν δὲ καὶ τίτλον ὁ Πιλᾶτος καὶ ἔθηκεν ἐπὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ· ἦν δὲ γεγραμμένον· Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
verses.translit: egrapsen de kai titlon o Pilatos kai ethiken epi tou stayrou* en de gegrammenon* Iisous o Nazoraios o vasileus ton Ioydaion.
verses.translation: And Pilate wrote a title, and put it on the cross. And the writing was, JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS.

verses.original: τοῦτον οὖν τὸν τίτλον πολλοὶ ἀνέγνωσαν τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὅτι ἐγγὺς ἦν ὁ τόπος τῆς πόλεως ὅπου ἐσταυρώθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς· καὶ ἦν γεγραμμένον Ἑβραϊστί, ⸂Ῥωμαϊστί, Ἑλληνιστί⸃.
verses.translit: touton oun ton titlon polloi anegnosan ton Ioydaion, oti eggus en o topos tes poleos opoy estayrothi o Iisous* kai en gegrammenon Evraisti, Romaisti, Ellinisti.
verses.translation: This title then read many of the Jews: for the place where Jesus was crucified was nigh to the city: and it was written in Hebrew, and Greek, and Latin.

verses.original: ἔλεγον οὖν τῷ Πιλάτῳ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων· Μὴ γράφε· Ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἀλλʼ ὅτι ἐκεῖνος εἶπεν Βασιλεὺς ⸂τῶν Ἰουδαίων εἰμί⸃.
verses.translit: elegon oun to Pilato oi arhiereis ton Ioydaion* Me grafe* O vasileus ton Ioydaion, all' oti ekeinos eipen Vasileus ton Ioydaion eimi.
verses.translation: Then said the chief priests of the Jews to Pilate, Write not, The King of the Jews; but that he said, I am King of the Jews.

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Ὃ γέγραφα γέγραφα.
verses.translit: apekrithi o Pilatos* O gegrafa gegrafa.
verses.translation: Pilate answered, What I have written I have written.

verses.original: οἱ οὖν στρατιῶται ὅτε ἐσταύρωσαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἔλαβον τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐποίησαν τέσσαρα μέρη, ἑκάστῳ στρατιώτῃ μέρος, καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα. ἦν δὲ ὁ χιτὼν ἄραφος, ἐκ τῶν ἄνωθεν ὑφαντὸς διʼ ὅλου·
verses.translit: oi oun stratiotai ote estayrosan ton Iisoun elavon ta imatia autou kai epoiisan tessara meri, ekasto stratiote meros, kai ton hitona. en de o hiton arafos, ek ton anothen ufantos di' oloy*
verses.translation: Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments, and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also his coat: now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

verses.original: εἶπαν οὖν πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Μὴ σχίσωμεν αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ λάχωμεν περὶ αὐτοῦ τίνος ἔσται· ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ ⸂ἡ λέγουσα⸃· Διεμερίσαντο τὰ ἱμάτιά μου ἑαυτοῖς καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν ἱματισμόν μου ἔβαλον κλῆρον. Οἱ μὲν οὖν στρατιῶται ταῦτα ἐποίησαν.
verses.translit: eipan oun pros alliloys* Me shisomen auton, alla lahomen peri autou tinos estai* ina e grafe plirothe e legoysa* Diemerisanto ta imatia moy eaytois kai epi ton imatismon moy evalon kleron. Oi men oun stratiotai tauta epoiisan.
verses.translation: They said therefore among themselves, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be: that the scripture might be fulfilled, which saith, They parted my raiment among them, and for my vesture they did cast lots. These things therefore the soldiers did.

verses.original: Εἱστήκεισαν δὲ παρὰ τῷ σταυρῷ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ ἀδελφὴ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ, Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Κλωπᾶ καὶ Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνή.
verses.translit: Eistikeisan de para to stayro tou Iisou e mitir autou kai e adelfe tes mitros autou, Maria e tou Klopa kai Maria e Magdalini.
verses.translation: Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.

verses.original: Ἰησοῦς οὖν ἰδὼν τὴν μητέρα καὶ τὸν μαθητὴν παρεστῶτα ὃν ἠγάπα λέγει τῇ ⸀μητρί· Γύναι, ⸀ἴδε ὁ υἱός σου·
verses.translit: Iisous oun idon ten mitera kai ton mathiten parestota on egapa legei te mitri* Gynai, ide o yios soy*
verses.translation: When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son!

verses.original: εἶτα λέγει τῷ μαθητῇ· ⸀Ἴδε ἡ μήτηρ σου. καὶ ἀπʼ ἐκείνης τῆς ὥρας ἔλαβεν ὁ μαθητὴς αὐτὴν εἰς τὰ ἴδια.
verses.translit: eita legei to mathite* Ide e mitir soy. kai ap' ekeinis tes oras elaven o mathites auten eis ta idia.
verses.translation: Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.

verses.original: Μετὰ τοῦτο ⸀εἰδὼς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ⸂ἤδη πάντα⸃ τετέλεσται ἵνα τελειωθῇ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει· Διψῶ.
verses.translit: Meta touto eidos o Iisous oti edi panta tetelestai ina teleiothe e grafe legei* Dipso.
verses.translation: After this, Jesus knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the scripture might be fulfilled, saith, I thirst.

verses.original: ⸀σκεῦος ἔκειτο ὄξους μεστόν· ⸂σπόγγον οὖν μεστὸν τοῦ⸃ ὄξους ⸀ὑσσώπῳ περιθέντες προσήνεγκαν αὐτοῦ τῷ στόματι.
verses.translit: skeuos ekeito oxoys meston* spoggon oun meston tou oxoys ussopo perithentes prosinegkan autou to stomati.
verses.translation: Now there was set a vessel full of vinegar: and they filled a spunge with vinegar, and put it upon hyssop, and put it to his mouth.

verses.original: ὅτε οὖν ἔλαβεν τὸ ὄξος ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Τετέλεσται, καὶ κλίνας τὴν κεφαλὴν παρέδωκεν τὸ πνεῦμα.
verses.translit: ote oun elaven to oxos o Iisous eipen* Tetelestai, kai klinas ten kefalen paredoken to pneuma.
verses.translation: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.

verses.original: Οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι, ⸂ἐπεὶ παρασκευὴ ἦν, ἵνα μὴ μείνῃ ἐπὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ τὰ σώματα ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ⸃, ἦν γὰρ μεγάλη ἡ ἡμέρα ἐκείνου τοῦ σαββάτου, ἠρώτησαν τὸν Πιλᾶτον ἵνα κατεαγῶσιν αὐτῶν τὰ σκέλη καὶ ἀρθῶσιν.
verses.translit: Oi oun Ioydaioi, epei paraskeye en, ina me meine epi tou stayrou ta somata en to savvato, en gar megali e emera ekeinoy tou savvatoy, erotisan ton Pilaton ina kateagosin auton ta skeli kai arthosin.
verses.translation: The Jews therefore, because it was the preparation, that the bodies should not remain upon the cross on the sabbath day, (for that sabbath day was an high day,) besought Pilate that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away.

verses.original: ἦλθον οὖν οἱ στρατιῶται, καὶ τοῦ μὲν πρώτου κατέαξαν τὰ σκέλη καὶ τοῦ ἄλλου τοῦ συσταυρωθέντος αὐτῷ·
verses.translit: elthon oun oi stratiotai, kai tou men protoy kateaxan ta skeli kai tou alloy tou systayrothentos auto*
verses.translation: Then came the soldiers, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other which was crucified with him.

verses.original: ἐπὶ δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐλθόντες, ὡς εἶδον ⸂ἤδη αὐτὸν⸃ τεθνηκότα, οὐ κατέαξαν αὐτοῦ τὰ σκέλη,
verses.translit: epi de ton Iisoun elthontes, os eidon edi auton tethnikota, ou kateaxan autou ta skeli,
verses.translation: But when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs:

verses.original: ἀλλʼ εἷς τῶν στρατιωτῶν λόγχῃ αὐτοῦ τὴν πλευρὰν ἔνυξεν, καὶ ⸂ἐξῆλθεν εὐθὺς⸃ αἷμα καὶ ὕδωρ.
verses.translit: all' eis ton stratioton loghe autou ten pleyran enyxen, kai exelthen euthus aima kai udor.
verses.translation: But one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out blood and water.

verses.original: καὶ ὁ ἑωρακὼς μεμαρτύρηκεν, καὶ ἀληθινὴ ⸂αὐτοῦ ἐστιν⸃ ἡ μαρτυρία, καὶ ἐκεῖνος οἶδεν ὅτι ἀληθῆ λέγει, ἵνα ⸀καὶ ὑμεῖς ⸀πιστεύητε.
verses.translit: kai o eorakos memartyriken, kai alithine autou estin e martyria, kai ekeinos oiden oti alithe legei, ina kai umeis pisteyite.
verses.translation: And he that saw it bare record, and his record is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye might believe.

verses.original: ἐγένετο γὰρ ταῦτα ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ· Ὀστοῦν οὐ συντριβήσεται ⸀αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: egeneto gar tauta ina e grafe plirothe* Ostoun ou syntrivisetai autou.
verses.translation: For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.

verses.original: καὶ πάλιν ἑτέρα γραφὴ λέγει· Ὄψονται εἰς ὃν ἐξεκέντησαν.
verses.translit: kai palin etera grafe legei* Opsontai eis on exekentisan.
verses.translation: And again another scripture saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced.

verses.original: Μετὰ ⸀δὲ ταῦτα ἠρώτησεν τὸν Πιλᾶτον Ἰωσὴφ ⸀ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας, ὢν μαθητὴς τοῦ Ἰησοῦ κεκρυμμένος δὲ διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ· καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν ὁ Πιλᾶτος. ἦλθεν οὖν καὶ ἦρεν τὸ σῶμα ⸀αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Meta de tauta erotisen ton Pilaton Iosef apo Arimathaias, on mathites tou Iisou kekrymmenos de dia ton fovon ton Ioydaion, ina are to soma tou Iisou* kai epetrepsen o Pilatos. elthen oun kai eren to soma autou.
verses.translation: And after this Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, besought Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave him leave. He came therefore, and took the body of Jesus.

verses.original: ἦλθεν δὲ καὶ Νικόδημος, ὁ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ⸀αὐτὸν νυκτὸς τὸ πρῶτον, φέρων ⸀μίγμα σμύρνης καὶ ἀλόης ὡς λίτρας ἑκατόν.
verses.translit: elthen de kai Nikodimos, o elthon pros auton nyktos to proton, feron migma smyrnis kai alois os litras ekaton.
verses.translation: And there came also Nicodemus, which at the first came to Jesus by night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound weight .

verses.original: ἔλαβον οὖν τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ἔδησαν ⸀αὐτὸ ὀθονίοις μετὰ τῶν ἀρωμάτων, καθὼς ἔθος ἐστὶν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ἐνταφιάζειν.
verses.translit: elavon oun to soma tou Iisou kai edisan auto othoniois meta ton aromaton, kathos ethos estin tois Ioydaiois entafiazein.
verses.translation: Then took they the body of Jesus, and wound it in linen clothes with the spices, as the manner of the Jews is to bury.

verses.original: ἦν δὲ ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ὅπου ἐσταυρώθη κῆπος, καὶ ἐν τῷ κήπῳ μνημεῖον καινόν, ἐν ᾧ οὐδέπω οὐδεὶς ⸂ἦν τεθειμένος⸃·
verses.translit: en de en to topo opoy estayrothi kepos, kai en to kipo mnimeion kainon, en o oudepo oudeis en tetheimenos*
verses.translation: Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden; and in the garden a new sepulchre, wherein was never man yet laid.

verses.original: ἐκεῖ οὖν διὰ τὴν παρασκευὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὅτι ἐγγὺς ἦν τὸ μνημεῖον, ἔθηκαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: ekei oun dia ten paraskeyen ton Ioydaion, oti eggus en to mnimeion, ethikan ton Iisoun.
verses.translation: There laid they Jesus therefore because of the Jews’ preparation day ; for the sepulchre was nigh at hand.

verses.original: Τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ ἔρχεται πρωῒ σκοτίας ἔτι οὔσης εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ βλέπει τὸν λίθον ἠρμένον ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου.
verses.translit: Te de mia ton savvaton Maria e Magdaline erhetai proi skotias eti ousis eis to mnimeion, kai vlepei ton lithon ermenon ek tou mnimeioy.
verses.translation: The first day of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre, and seeth the stone taken away from the sepulchre.

verses.original: τρέχει οὖν καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς Σίμωνα Πέτρον καὶ πρὸς τὸν ἄλλον μαθητὴν ὃν ἐφίλει ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἦραν τὸν κύριον ἐκ τοῦ μνημείου, καὶ οὐκ οἴδαμεν ποῦ ἔθηκαν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: trehei oun kai erhetai pros Simona Petron kai pros ton allon mathiten on efilei o Iisous, kai legei autois* Eran ton kyrion ek tou mnimeioy, kai ouk oidamen pou ethikan auton.
verses.translation: Then she runneth, and cometh to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and saith unto them, They have taken away the Lord out of the sepulchre, and we know not where they have laid him.

verses.original: ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ Πέτρος καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητής, καὶ ἤρχοντο εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον.
verses.translit: exelthen oun o Petros kai o allos mathitis, kai erhonto eis to mnimeion.
verses.translation: Peter therefore went forth, and that other disciple, and came to the sepulchre.

verses.original: ἔτρεχον δὲ οἱ δύο ὁμοῦ· καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητὴς προέδραμεν τάχιον τοῦ Πέτρου καὶ ἦλθεν πρῶτος εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον,
verses.translit: etrehon de oi dyo omou* kai o allos mathites proedramen tahion tou Petroy kai elthen protos eis to mnimeion,
verses.translation: So they ran both together: and the other disciple did outrun Peter, and came first to the sepulchre.

verses.original: καὶ παρακύψας βλέπει κείμενα τὰ ὀθόνια, οὐ μέντοι εἰσῆλθεν.
verses.translit: kai parakypsas vlepei keimena ta othonia, ou mentoi eiselthen.
verses.translation: And he stooping down, and looking in , saw the linen clothes lying; yet went he not in.

verses.original: ἔρχεται οὖν ⸀καὶ Σίμων Πέτρος ἀκολουθῶν αὐτῷ, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον· καὶ θεωρεῖ τὰ ὀθόνια κείμενα,
verses.translit: erhetai oun kai Simon Petros akoloython auto, kai eiselthen eis to mnimeion* kai theorei ta othonia keimena,
verses.translation: Then cometh Simon Peter following him, and went into the sepulchre, and seeth the linen clothes lie,

verses.original: καὶ τὸ σουδάριον, ὃ ἦν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ, οὐ μετὰ τῶν ὀθονίων κείμενον ἀλλὰ χωρὶς ἐντετυλιγμένον εἰς ἕνα τόπον·
verses.translit: kai to soydarion, o en epi tes kefales autou, ou meta ton othonion keimenon alla horis entetyligmenon eis ena topon*
verses.translation: And the napkin, that was about his head, not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself.

verses.original: τότε οὖν εἰσῆλθεν καὶ ὁ ἄλλος μαθητὴς ὁ ἐλθὼν πρῶτος εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ εἶδεν καὶ ἐπίστευσεν·
verses.translit: tote oun eiselthen kai o allos mathites o elthon protos eis to mnimeion, kai eiden kai episteysen*
verses.translation: Then went in also that other disciple, which came first to the sepulchre, and he saw, and believed.

verses.original: οὐδέπω γὰρ ᾔδεισαν τὴν γραφὴν ὅτι δεῖ αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῆναι.
verses.translit: oudepo gar edeisan ten grafen oti dei auton ek nekron anastenai.
verses.translation: For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.

verses.original: ἀπῆλθον οὖν πάλιν πρὸς ⸀αὑτοὺς οἱ μαθηταί.
verses.translit: apelthon oun palin pros autous oi mathitai.
verses.translation: Then the disciples went away again unto their own home.

verses.original: Μαρία δὲ εἱστήκει πρὸς ⸂τῷ μνημείῳ ἔξω κλαίουσα⸃. ὡς οὖν ἔκλαιεν παρέκυψεν εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον,
verses.translit: Maria de eistikei pros to mnimeio exo klaioysa. os oun eklaien parekypsen eis to mnimeion,
verses.translation: But Mary stood without at the sepulchre weeping: and as she wept, she stooped down, and looked into the sepulchre,

verses.original: καὶ θεωρεῖ δύο ἀγγέλους ἐν λευκοῖς καθεζομένους, ἕνα πρὸς τῇ κεφαλῇ καὶ ἕνα πρὸς τοῖς ποσίν, ὅπου ἔκειτο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: kai theorei dyo aggeloys en leykois kathezomenoys, ena pros te kefale kai ena pros tois posin, opoy ekeito to soma tou Iisou.
verses.translation: And seeth two angels in white sitting, the one at the head, and the other at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.

verses.original: καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῇ ἐκεῖνοι· Γύναι, τί κλαίεις; λέγει αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ἦραν τὸν κύριόν μου, καὶ οὐκ οἶδα ποῦ ἔθηκαν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai legoysin aute ekeinoi* Gynai, ti klaieis; legei autois oti Eran ton kyrion moy, kai ouk oida pou ethikan auton.
verses.translation: And they say unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? She saith unto them, Because they have taken away my Lord, and I know not where they have laid him.

verses.original: ⸀ταῦτα εἰποῦσα ἐστράφη εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω, καὶ θεωρεῖ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἑστῶτα, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν.
verses.translit: tauta eipousa estrafi eis ta opiso, kai theorei ton Iisoun estota, kai ouk edei oti Iisous estin.
verses.translation: And when she had thus said, she turned herself back, and saw Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus.

verses.original: λέγει ⸀αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς· Γύναι, τί κλαίεις; τίνα ζητεῖς; ἐκείνη δοκοῦσα ὅτι ὁ κηπουρός ἐστιν λέγει αὐτῷ· Κύριε, εἰ σὺ ἐβάστασας αὐτόν, εἰπέ μοι ποῦ ἔθηκας αὐτόν, κἀγὼ αὐτὸν ἀρῶ.
verses.translit: legei aute Iisous* Gynai, ti klaieis; tina ziteis; ekeini dokousa oti o kipoyros estin legei auto* Kyrie, ei su evastasas auton, eipe moi pou ethikas auton, kago auton aro.
verses.translation: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.

verses.original: λέγει ⸀αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς· ⸀Μαριάμ. στραφεῖσα ἐκείνη λέγει αὐτῷ ⸀Ἑβραϊστί· Ραββουνι (ὃ λέγεται Διδάσκαλε).
verses.translit: legei aute Iisous* Mariam. strafeisa ekeini legei auto Evraisti* Ravvoyni (o legetai Didaskale).
verses.translation: Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master.

verses.original: λέγει ⸀αὐτῇ Ἰησοῦς· Μή μου ἅπτου, οὔπω γὰρ ἀναβέβηκα πρὸς τὸν ⸀πατέρα· πορεύου δὲ πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφούς μου καὶ εἰπὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἀναβαίνω πρὸς τὸν πατέρα μου καὶ πατέρα ὑμῶν καὶ θεόν μου καὶ θεὸν ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: legei aute Iisous* Mi moy aptoy, oupo gar anavevika pros ton patera* poreyoy de pros tous adelfoys moy kai eipe autois* Anavaino pros ton patera moy kai patera umon kai theon moy kai theon umon.
verses.translation: Jesus saith unto her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.

verses.original: ἔρχεται ⸀Μαριὰμ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ ⸀ἀγγέλλουσα τοῖς μαθηταῖς ὅτι ⸀Ἑώρακα τὸν κύριον καὶ ταῦτα εἶπεν αὐτῇ.
verses.translit: erhetai Mariam e Magdaline aggelloysa tois mathitais oti Eoraka ton kyrion kai tauta eipen aute.
verses.translation: Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and that he had spoken these things unto her.

verses.original: Οὔσης οὖν ὀψίας τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ τῇ ⸀μιᾷ σαββάτων, καὶ τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων ὅπου ἦσαν οἱ ⸀μαθηταὶ διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἔστη εἰς τὸ μέσον, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: Ousis oun opsias te emera ekeine te mia savvaton, kai ton thyron kekleismenon opoy esan oi mathitai dia ton fovon ton Ioydaion, elthen o Iisous kai esti eis to meson, kai legei autois* Eirini umin.
verses.translation: Then the same day at evening, being the first day of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, came Jesus and stood in the midst, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you.

verses.original: καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ⸀ἔδειξεν τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τὴν πλευρὰν ⸀αὐτοῖς. ἐχάρησαν οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ ἰδόντες τὸν κύριον.
verses.translit: kai touto eipon edeixen tas heiras kai ten pleyran autois. eharisan oun oi mathitai idontes ton kyrion.
verses.translation: And when he had so said, he shewed unto them his hands and his side. Then were the disciples glad, when they saw the Lord.

verses.original: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ⸂ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃ πάλιν· Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν· καθὼς ἀπέσταλκέν με ὁ πατήρ, κἀγὼ πέμπω ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: eipen oun autois o Iisous palin* Eirini umin* kathos apestalken me o patir, kago pempo umas.
verses.translation: Then said Jesus to them again, Peace be unto you: as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you.

verses.original: καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἐνεφύσησεν καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Λάβετε πνεῦμα ἅγιον·
verses.translit: kai touto eipon enefysisen kai legei autois* Lavete pneuma agion*
verses.translation: And when he had said this, he breathed on them , and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost:

verses.original: ἄν τινων ἀφῆτε τὰς ἁμαρτίας ⸀ἀφέωνται αὐτοῖς· ἄν τινων κρατῆτε κεκράτηνται.
verses.translit: an tinon afete tas amartias afeontai autois* an tinon kratete kekratintai.
verses.translation: Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them; and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained.

verses.original: Θωμᾶς δὲ εἷς ἐκ τῶν δώδεκα, ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος, οὐκ ἦν μετʼ αὐτῶν ὅτε ⸀ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς.
verses.translit: Thomas de eis ek ton dodeka, o legomenos Didymos, ouk en met' auton ote elthen Iisous.
verses.translation: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.

verses.original: ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτῷ οἱ ἄλλοι μαθηταί· Ἑωράκαμεν τὸν κύριον. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐὰν μὴ ἴδω ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτοῦ τὸν τύπον τῶν ἥλων καὶ βάλω τὸν δάκτυλόν μου εἰς τὸν τύπον τῶν ἥλων καὶ βάλω ⸂μου τὴν χεῖρα⸃ εἰς τὴν πλευρὰν αὐτοῦ, οὐ μὴ πιστεύσω.
verses.translit: elegon oun auto oi alloi mathitai* Eorakamen ton kyrion. o de eipen autois* Ean me ido en tais hersin autou ton typon ton elon kai valo ton daktylon moy eis ton typon ton elon kai valo moy ten heira eis ten pleyran autou, ou me pisteyso.
verses.translation: The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.

verses.original: Καὶ μεθʼ ἡμέρας ὀκτὼ πάλιν ἦσαν ἔσω οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ Θωμᾶς μετʼ αὐτῶν. ἔρχεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων, καὶ ἔστη εἰς τὸ μέσον καὶ εἶπεν· Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: Kai meth' emeras okto palin esan eso oi mathitai autou kai Thomas met' auton. erhetai o Iisous ton thyron kekleismenon, kai esti eis to meson kai eipen* Eirini umin.
verses.translation: And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.

verses.original: εἶτα λέγει τῷ Θωμᾷ· Φέρε τὸν δάκτυλόν σου ὧδε καὶ ἴδε τὰς χεῖράς μου, καὶ φέρε τὴν χεῖρά σου καὶ βάλε εἰς τὴν πλευράν μου, καὶ μὴ γίνου ἄπιστος ἀλλὰ πιστός.
verses.translit: eita legei to Thoma* Fere ton daktylon soy ode kai ide tas heiras moy, kai fere ten heira soy kai vale eis ten pleyran moy, kai me ginoy apistos alla pistos.
verses.translation: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.

verses.original: ⸀ἀπεκρίθη Θωμᾶς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὁ κύριός μου καὶ ὁ θεός μου.
verses.translit: apekrithi Thomas kai eipen auto* O kyrios moy kai o theos moy.
verses.translation: And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.

verses.original: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ὅτι ἑώρακάς με πεπίστευκας; μακάριοι οἱ μὴ ἰδόντες καὶ πιστεύσαντες.
verses.translit: legei auto o Iisous* Oti eorakas me pepisteykas; makarioi oi me idontes kai pisteysantes.
verses.translation: Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.

verses.original: Πολλὰ μὲν οὖν καὶ ἄλλα σημεῖα ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐνώπιον τῶν ⸀μαθητῶν, ἃ οὐκ ἔστιν γεγραμμένα ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τούτῳ·
verses.translit: Polla men oun kai alla simeia epoiisen o Iisous enopion ton mathiton, a ouk estin gegrammena en to vivlio toyto*
verses.translation: And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book:

verses.original: ταῦτα δὲ γέγραπται ἵνα ⸀πιστεύητε ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ἵνα πιστεύοντες ζωὴν ἔχητε ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: tauta de gegraptai ina pisteyite oti Iisous estin o hristos o yios tou theou, kai ina pisteyontes zoen ehite en to onomati autou.
verses.translation: But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.

verses.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἐφανέρωσεν ἑαυτὸν πάλιν ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης τῆς Τιβεριάδος· ἐφανέρωσεν δὲ οὕτως.
verses.translit: Meta tauta efanerosen eayton palin o Iisous tois mathitais epi tes thalassis tes Tiveriados* efanerosen de outos.
verses.translation: After these things Jesus shewed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and on this wise shewed he himself .

verses.original: ἦσαν ὁμοῦ Σίμων Πέτρος καὶ Θωμᾶς ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος καὶ Ναθαναὴλ ὁ ἀπὸ Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ οἱ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ ἄλλοι ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ δύο.
verses.translit: esan omou Simon Petros kai Thomas o legomenos Didymos kai Nathanael o apo Kana tes Galilaias kai oi tou Zevedaioy kai alloi ek ton mathiton autou dyo.
verses.translation: There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples.

verses.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς Σίμων Πέτρος· Ὑπάγω ἁλιεύειν· λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ἐρχόμεθα καὶ ἡμεῖς σὺν σοί. ἐξῆλθον καὶ ἐνέβησαν εἰς τὸ ⸀πλοῖον, καὶ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ νυκτὶ ἐπίασαν οὐδέν.
verses.translit: legei autois Simon Petros* Upago alieyein* legoysin auto* Erhometha kai emeis sun soi. exelthon kai enevisan eis to ploion, kai en ekeine te nykti epiasan ouden.
verses.translation: Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing.

verses.original: Πρωΐας δὲ ἤδη ⸀γενομένης ⸀ἔστη Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸν αἰγιαλόν· οὐ μέντοι ᾔδεισαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν.
verses.translit: ProIas de edi genomenis esti Iisous eis ton aigialon* ou mentoi edeisan oi mathitai oti Iisous estin.
verses.translation: But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.

verses.original: λέγει οὖν αὐτοῖς ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Παιδία, μή τι προσφάγιον ἔχετε; ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ· Οὔ.
verses.translit: legei oun autois o Iisous* Paidia, mi ti prosfagion ehete; apekrithisan auto* Ou.
verses.translation: Then Jesus saith unto them, Children, have ye any meat? They answered him, No.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Βάλετε εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη τοῦ πλοίου τὸ δίκτυον, καὶ εὑρήσετε. ἔβαλον οὖν, καὶ οὐκέτι αὐτὸ ἑλκύσαι ⸀ἴσχυον ἀπὸ τοῦ πλήθους τῶν ἰχθύων.
verses.translit: o de eipen autois* Valete eis ta dexia meri tou ploioy to diktyon, kai eurisete. evalon oun, kai ouketi auto elkysai ishyon apo tou plithoys ton ihthyon.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes.

verses.original: λέγει οὖν ὁ μαθητὴς ἐκεῖνος ὃν ἠγάπα ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ὁ κύριός ἐστιν. Σίμων οὖν Πέτρος, ἀκούσας ὅτι ὁ κύριός ἐστιν, τὸν ἐπενδύτην διεζώσατο, ἦν γὰρ γυμνός, καὶ ἔβαλεν ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν·
verses.translit: legei oun o mathites ekeinos on egapa o Iisous to Petro* O kyrios estin. Simon oun Petros, akoysas oti o kyrios estin, ton ependytin diezosato, en gar gymnos, kai evalen eayton eis ten thalassan*
verses.translation: Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved saith unto Peter, It is the Lord. Now when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girt his fisher’s coat unto him , (for he was naked,) and did cast himself into the sea.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἄλλοι μαθηταὶ τῷ πλοιαρίῳ ἦλθον, οὐ γὰρ ἦσαν μακρὰν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἀλλὰ ὡς ἀπὸ πηχῶν διακοσίων, σύροντες τὸ δίκτυον τῶν ἰχθύων.
verses.translit: oi de alloi mathitai to ploiario elthon, ou gar esan makran apo tes ges alla os apo pihon diakosion, syrontes to diktyon ton ihthyon.
verses.translation: And the other disciples came in a little ship; (for they were not far from land, but as it were two hundred cubits,) dragging the net with fishes.

verses.original: Ὡς οὖν ἀπέβησαν εἰς τὴν γῆν βλέπουσιν ἀνθρακιὰν κειμένην καὶ ὀψάριον ἐπικείμενον καὶ ἄρτον.
verses.translit: Os oun apevisan eis ten gen vlepoysin anthrakian keimenin kai opsarion epikeimenon kai arton.
verses.translation: As soon then as they were come to land, they saw a fire of coals there, and fish laid thereon, and bread.

verses.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐνέγκατε ἀπὸ τῶν ὀψαρίων ὧν ἐπιάσατε νῦν.
verses.translit: legei autois o Iisous* Enegkate apo ton opsarion on epiasate nun.
verses.translation: Jesus saith unto them, Bring of the fish which ye have now caught.

verses.original: ἀνέβη ⸀οὖν Σίμων Πέτρος καὶ εἵλκυσεν τὸ δίκτυον ⸂εἰς τὴν γῆν⸃ μεστὸν ἰχθύων μεγάλων ἑκατὸν πεντήκοντα τριῶν· καὶ τοσούτων ὄντων οὐκ ἐσχίσθη τὸ δίκτυον.
verses.translit: anevi oun Simon Petros kai eilkysen to diktyon eis ten gen meston ihthyon megalon ekaton pentikonta trion* kai tosoyton onton ouk eshisthi to diktyon.
verses.translation: Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land full of great fishes, an hundred and fifty and three: and for all there were so many, yet was not the net broken.

verses.original: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Δεῦτε ἀριστήσατε. οὐδεὶς ⸀δὲ ἐτόλμα τῶν μαθητῶν ἐξετάσαι αὐτόν· Σὺ τίς εἶ; εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ κύριός ἐστιν.
verses.translit: legei autois o Iisous* Deute aristisate. oudeis de etolma ton mathiton exetasai auton* Su tis ei; eidotes oti o kyrios estin.
verses.translation: Jesus saith unto them, Come and dine. And none of the disciples durst ask him, Who art thou? knowing that it was the Lord.

verses.original: ⸀ἔρχεται ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ λαμβάνει τὸν ἄρτον καὶ δίδωσιν αὐτοῖς, καὶ τὸ ὀψάριον ὁμοίως.
verses.translit: erhetai o Iisous kai lamvanei ton arton kai didosin autois, kai to opsarion omoios.
verses.translation: Jesus then cometh, and taketh bread, and giveth them, and fish likewise.

verses.original: τοῦτο ἤδη τρίτον ἐφανερώθη ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς ⸀μαθηταῖς ἐγερθεὶς ἐκ νεκρῶν.
verses.translit: touto edi triton efanerothi o Iisous tois mathitais egertheis ek nekron.
verses.translation: This is now the third time that Jesus shewed himself to his disciples, after that he was risen from the dead.

verses.original: Ὅτε οὖν ἠρίστησαν λέγει τῷ Σίμωνι Πέτρῳ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Σίμων ⸀Ἰωάννου, ἀγαπᾷς με πλέον τούτων; λέγει αὐτῷ· Ναί, κύριε, σὺ οἶδας ὅτι φιλῶ σε. λέγει αὐτῷ· Βόσκε τὰ ἀρνία μου.
verses.translit: Ote oun eristisan legei to Simoni Petro o Iisous* Simon Ioannoy, agapas me pleon toyton; legei auto* Nai, kyrie, su oidas oti filo se. legei auto* Voske ta arnia moy.
verses.translation: So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.

verses.original: λέγει αὐτῷ πάλιν δεύτερον· Σίμων ⸀Ἰωάννου, ἀγαπᾷς με; λέγει αὐτῷ· Ναί, κύριε, σὺ οἶδας ὅτι φιλῶ σε. λέγει αὐτῷ· Ποίμαινε τὰ πρόβατά μου.
verses.translit: legei auto palin deyteron* Simon Ioannoy, agapas me; legei auto* Nai, kyrie, su oidas oti filo se. legei auto* Poimaine ta provata moy.
verses.translation: He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep.

verses.original: λέγει αὐτῷ τὸ τρίτον· Σίμων ⸀Ἰωάννου, φιλεῖς με; ἐλυπήθη ὁ Πέτρος ὅτι εἶπεν αὐτῷ τὸ τρίτον· Φιλεῖς με; καὶ ⸀εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ⸂πάντα σὺ⸃ οἶδας, σὺ γινώσκεις ὅτι φιλῶ σε. λέγει αὐτῷ ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Βόσκε τὰ ⸀πρόβατά μου.
verses.translit: legei auto to triton* Simon Ioannoy, fileis me; elypithi o Petros oti eipen auto to triton* Fileis me; kai eipen auto* Kyrie, panta su oidas, su ginoskeis oti filo se. legei auto o Iisous* Voske ta provata moy.
verses.translation: He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.

verses.original: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, ὅτε ἦς νεώτερος, ἐζώννυες σεαυτὸν καὶ περιεπάτεις ὅπου ἤθελες· ὅταν δὲ γηράσῃς, ἐκτενεῖς τὰς χεῖράς σου, καὶ ἄλλος ⸂σε ζώσει⸃ καὶ οἴσει ὅπου οὐ θέλεις.
verses.translit: amen amen lego soi, ote es neoteros, ezonnyes seayton kai periepateis opoy etheles* otan de girases, ekteneis tas heiras soy, kai allos se zosei kai oisei opoy ou theleis.
verses.translation: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not.

verses.original: τοῦτο δὲ εἶπεν σημαίνων ποίῳ θανάτῳ δοξάσει τὸν θεόν. καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι.
verses.translit: touto de eipen simainon poio thanato doxasei ton theon. kai touto eipon legei auto* Akoloythei moi.
verses.translation: This spake he, signifying by what death he should glorify God. And when he had spoken this, he saith unto him, Follow me.

verses.original: ⸀Ἐπιστραφεὶς ὁ Πέτρος βλέπει τὸν μαθητὴν ὃν ἠγάπα ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀκολουθοῦντα, ὃς καὶ ἀνέπεσεν ἐν τῷ δείπνῳ ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπεν· Κύριε, τίς ἐστιν ὁ παραδιδούς σε;
verses.translit: Epistrafeis o Petros vlepei ton mathiten on egapa o Iisous akoloythounta, os kai anepesen en to deipno epi to stethos autou kai eipen* Kyrie, tis estin o paradidoys se;
verses.translation: Then Peter, turning about, seeth the disciple whom Jesus loved following; which also leaned on his breast at supper, and said, Lord, which is he that betrayeth thee?

verses.original: τοῦτον ⸀οὖν ἰδὼν ὁ Πέτρος λέγει τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Κύριε, οὗτος δὲ τί;
verses.translit: touton oun idon o Petros legei to Iisou* Kyrie, outos de ti;
verses.translation: Peter seeing him saith to Jesus, Lord, and what shall this man do ?

verses.original: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐὰν αὐτὸν θέλω μένειν ἕως ἔρχομαι, τί πρὸς σέ; σύ ⸂μοι ἀκολούθει⸃.
verses.translit: legei auto o Iisous* Ean auton thelo menein eos erhomai, ti pros se; sy moi akoloythei.
verses.translation: Jesus saith unto him, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me.

verses.original: ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ⸂οὗτος ὁ λόγος⸃ εἰς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὅτι ὁ μαθητὴς ἐκεῖνος οὐκ ἀποθνῄσκει. ⸂οὐκ εἶπεν δὲ⸃ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι οὐκ ἀποθνῄσκει ἀλλʼ· Ἐὰν αὐτὸν θέλω μένειν ἕως ἔρχομαι, τί πρὸς σέ;
verses.translit: exelthen oun outos o logos eis tous adelfous oti o mathites ekeinos ouk apothneskei. ouk eipen de auto o Iisous oti ouk apothneskei all'* Ean auton thelo menein eos erhomai, ti pros se;
verses.translation: Then went this saying abroad among the brethren, that that disciple should not die: yet Jesus said not unto him, He shall not die; but, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee?

verses.original: Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ μαθητὴς ὁ μαρτυρῶν περὶ τούτων καὶ ⸀ὁ γράψας ταῦτα, καὶ οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς ⸂αὐτοῦ ἡ μαρτυρία ἐστίν⸃.
verses.translit: Outos estin o mathites o martyron peri toyton kai o grapsas tauta, kai oidamen oti alithes autou e martyria estin.
verses.translation: This is the disciple which testifieth of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his testimony is true.

verses.original: ἔστιν δὲ καὶ ἄλλα πολλὰ ⸀ἃ ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ἅτινα ἐὰν γράφηται καθʼ ἕν, οὐδʼ αὐτὸν οἶμαι τὸν κόσμον ⸀χωρήσειν τὰ γραφόμενα ⸀βιβλία.
verses.translit: estin de kai alla polla a epoiisen o Iisous, atina ean grafitai kath' en, oud' auton oimai ton kosmon horisein ta grafomena vivlia.
verses.translation: And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written. Amen.

verses.original: Τὸν μὲν πρῶτον λόγον ἐποιησάμην περὶ πάντων, ὦ Θεόφιλε, ὧν ἤρξατο ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς ποιεῖν τε καὶ διδάσκειν
verses.translit: Ton men proton logon epoiisamin peri panton, o Theofile, on erxato o Iisous poiein te kai didaskein
verses.translation: The former treatise have I made, O Theophilus, of all that Jesus began both to do and teach,

verses.original: ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας ἐντειλάμενος τοῖς ἀποστόλοις διὰ πνεύματος ἁγίου οὓς ἐξελέξατο ἀνελήμφθη·
verses.translit: ahri es emeras enteilamenos tois apostolois dia pneymatos agioy ous exelexato anelimfthi*
verses.translation: Until the day in which he was taken up, after that he through the Holy Ghost had given commandments unto the apostles whom he had chosen:

verses.original: οἷς καὶ παρέστησεν ἑαυτὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τὸ παθεῖν αὐτὸν ἐν πολλοῖς τεκμηρίοις, διʼ ἡμερῶν τεσσεράκοντα ὀπτανόμενος αὐτοῖς καὶ λέγων τὰ περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ·
verses.translit: ois kai parestisen eayton zonta meta to pathein auton en pollois tekmiriois, di' emeron tesserakonta optanomenos autois kai legon ta peri tes vasileias tou theou*
verses.translation: To whom also he shewed himself alive after his passion by many infallible proofs, being seen of them forty days, and speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God:

verses.original: καὶ συναλιζόμενος παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων μὴ χωρίζεσθαι, ἀλλὰ περιμένειν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πατρὸς ἣν ἠκούσατέ μου·
verses.translit: kai synalizomenos pariggeilen autois apo Ierosolymon me horizesthai, alla perimenein ten epaggelian tou patros en ekoysate moy*
verses.translation: And, being assembled together with them , commanded them that they should not depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father, which, saith he , ye have heard of me.

verses.original: ὅτι Ἰωάννης μὲν ἐβάπτισεν ὕδατι, ὑμεῖς δὲ ⸂ἐν πνεύματι βαπτισθήσεσθε⸃ ἁγίῳ οὐ μετὰ πολλὰς ταύτας ἡμέρας.
verses.translit: oti Ioannis men evaptisen udati, umeis de en pneymati vaptisthisesthe agio ou meta pollas taytas emeras.
verses.translation: For John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence.

verses.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν συνελθόντες ⸀ἠρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Κύριε, εἰ ἐν τῷ χρόνῳ τούτῳ ἀποκαθιστάνεις τὴν βασιλείαν τῷ Ἰσραήλ;
verses.translit: Oi men oun synelthontes eroton auton legontes* Kyrie, ei en to hrono toyto apokathistaneis ten vasileian to Israil;
verses.translation: When they therefore were come together, they asked of him, saying, Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?

verses.original: εἶπεν ⸀δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Οὐχ ὑμῶν ἐστιν γνῶναι χρόνους ἢ καιροὺς οὓς ὁ πατὴρ ἔθετο ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ,
verses.translit: eipen de pros autoys* Ouh umon estin gnonai hronoys e kairous ous o pater etheto en te idia exoysia,
verses.translation: And he said unto them, It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ λήμψεσθε δύναμιν ἐπελθόντος τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἔσεσθέ ⸀μου μάρτυρες ἔν τε Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ ἐν πάσῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ καὶ Σαμαρείᾳ καὶ ἕως ἐσχάτου τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: alla limpsesthe dynamin epelthontos tou agioy pneymatos ef' umas, kai esesthe moy martyres en te Ieroysalem kai en pase te Ioydaia kai Samareia kai eos eshatoy tes ges.
verses.translation: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judæa, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.

verses.original: καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν βλεπόντων αὐτῶν ἐπήρθη καὶ νεφέλη ὑπέλαβεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai tauta eipon vleponton auton epirthi kai nefeli upelaven auton apo ton ofthalmon auton.
verses.translation: And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.

verses.original: καὶ ὡς ἀτενίζοντες ἦσαν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν πορευομένου αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο παρειστήκεισαν αὐτοῖς ἐν ⸂ἐσθήσεσι λευκαῖς⸃,
verses.translit: kai os atenizontes esan eis ton ouranon poreyomenoy autou, kai idou andres dyo pareistikeisan autois en esthisesi leykais,
verses.translation: And while they looked stedfastly toward heaven as he went up, behold, two men stood by them in white apparel;

verses.original: οἳ καὶ εἶπαν· Ἄνδρες Γαλιλαῖοι, τί ἑστήκατε ⸀βλέποντες εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν; οὗτος ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἀναλημφθεὶς ἀφʼ ὑμῶν εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν οὕτως ἐλεύσεται ὃν τρόπον ἐθεάσασθε αὐτὸν πορευόμενον εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.
verses.translit: oi kai eipan* Andres Galilaioi, ti estikate vlepontes eis ton ouranon; outos o Iisous o analimftheis af' umon eis ton ouranon outos eleysetai on tropon etheasasthe auton poreyomenon eis ton ouranon.
verses.translation: Which also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.

verses.original: Τότε ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἀπὸ ὄρους τοῦ καλουμένου Ἐλαιῶνος, ὅ ἐστιν ἐγγὺς Ἰερουσαλὴμ σαββάτου ἔχον ὁδόν.
verses.translit: Tote upestrepsan eis Ieroysalem apo oroys tou kaloymenoy Elaionos, o estin eggus Ieroysalem savvatoy ehon odon.
verses.translation: Then returned they unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is from Jerusalem a sabbath day’s journey.

verses.original: καὶ ὅτε εἰσῆλθον, ⸂εἰς τὸ ὑπερῷον ἀνέβησαν⸃ οὗ ἦσαν καταμένοντες, ὅ τε Πέτρος καὶ ⸂Ἰωάννης καὶ Ἰάκωβος⸃ καὶ Ἀνδρέας, Φίλιππος καὶ Θωμᾶς, Βαρθολομαῖος καὶ Μαθθαῖος, Ἰάκωβος Ἁλφαίου καὶ Σίμων ὁ ζηλωτὴς καὶ Ἰούδας Ἰακώβου.
verses.translit: kai ote eiselthon, eis to uperoon anevisan ou esan katamenontes, o te Petros kai Ioannis kai Iakovos kai Andreas, Filippos kai Thomas, Vartholomaios kai Maththaios, Iakovos Alfaioy kai Simon o zilotes kai Ioydas Iakovoy.
verses.translation: And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.

verses.original: οὗτοι πάντες ἦσαν προσκαρτεροῦντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν τῇ ⸀προσευχῇ σὺν γυναιξὶν καὶ ⸀Μαριὰμ τῇ μητρὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ⸀σὺν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: outoi pantes esan proskarterountes omothymadon te proseyhe sun gynaixin kai Mariam te mitri tou Iisou kai sun tois adelfois autou.
verses.translation: These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἀναστὰς Πέτρος ἐν μέσῳ τῶν ⸀ἀδελφῶν εἶπεν (ἦν τε ὄχλος ὀνομάτων ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ⸀ὡς ἑκατὸν εἴκοσι)·
verses.translit: Kai en tais emerais taytais anastas Petros en meso ton adelfon eipen (en te ohlos onomaton epi to auto os ekaton eikosi)*
verses.translation: And in those days Peter stood up in the midst of the disciples, and said, (the number of names together were about an hundred and twenty,)

verses.original: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἔδει πληρωθῆναι τὴν ⸀γραφὴν ἣν προεῖπε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον διὰ στόματος Δαυὶδ περὶ Ἰούδα τοῦ γενομένου ὁδηγοῦ τοῖς συλλαβοῦσιν ⸀Ἰησοῦν,
verses.translit: Andres adelfoi, edei plirothenai ten grafen en proeipe to pneuma to agion dia stomatos Dayid peri Ioyda tou genomenoy odigou tois syllavousin Iisoun,
verses.translation: Men and brethren, this scripture must needs have been fulfilled, which the Holy Ghost by the mouth of David spake before concerning Judas, which was guide to them that took Jesus.

verses.original: ὅτι κατηριθμημένος ἦν ⸀ἐν ἡμῖν καὶ ἔλαχεν τὸν κλῆρον τῆς διακονίας ταύτης.—
verses.translit: oti katirithmimenos en en emin kai elahen ton kleron tes diakonias taytis.--
verses.translation: For he was numbered with us, and had obtained part of this ministry.

verses.original: Οὗτος μὲν οὖν ἐκτήσατο χωρίον ἐκ μισθοῦ τῆς ἀδικίας, καὶ πρηνὴς γενόμενος ἐλάκησεν μέσος, καὶ ἐξεχύθη πάντα τὰ σπλάγχνα αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Outos men oun ektisato horion ek misthou tes adikias, kai prines genomenos elakisen mesos, kai exehythi panta ta splaghna autou.
verses.translation: Now this man purchased a field with the reward of iniquity; and falling headlong, he burst asunder in the midst, and all his bowels gushed out.

verses.original: καὶ γνωστὸν ἐγένετο πᾶσι τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν Ἰερουσαλήμ, ὥστε κληθῆναι τὸ χωρίον ἐκεῖνο τῇ ⸀ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ αὐτῶν Ἁκελδαμάχ, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν Χωρίον Αἵματος.—
verses.translit: kai gnoston egeneto pasi tois katoikousin Ieroysalim, oste klithenai to horion ekeino te idia dialekto auton Akeldamah, tout' estin Horion Aimatos.--
verses.translation: And it was known unto all the dwellers at Jerusalem; insomuch as that field is called in their proper tongue, Aceldama, that is to say, The field of blood.

verses.original: γέγραπται γὰρ ἐν βίβλῳ ψαλμῶν· Γενηθήτω ἡ ἔπαυλις αὐτοῦ ἔρημος καὶ μὴ ἔστω ὁ κατοικῶν ἐν αὐτῇ, καί· Τὴν ἐπισκοπὴν αὐτοῦ ⸀λαβέτω ἕτερος.
verses.translit: gegraptai gar en vivlo psalmon* Genithito e epaylis autou erimos kai me esto o katoikon en aute, kai* Ten episkopen autou laveto eteros.
verses.translation: For it is written in the book of Psalms, Let his habitation be desolate, and let no man dwell therein: and his bishoprick let another take.

verses.original: δεῖ οὖν τῶν συνελθόντων ἡμῖν ἀνδρῶν ἐν παντὶ χρόνῳ ⸀ᾧ εἰσῆλθεν καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς,
verses.translit: dei oun ton synelthonton emin andron en panti hrono o eiselthen kai exelthen ef' emas o kyrios Iisous,
verses.translation: Wherefore of these men which have companied with us all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,

verses.original: ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τοῦ βαπτίσματος Ἰωάννου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἧς ἀνελήμφθη ἀφʼ ἡμῶν, μάρτυρα τῆς ἀναστάσεως αὐτοῦ ⸂σὺν ἡμῖν γενέσθαι⸃ ἕνα τούτων.
verses.translit: arxamenos apo tou vaptismatos Ioannoy eos tes emeras es anelimfthi af' emon, martyra tes anastaseos autou sun emin genesthai ena toyton.
verses.translation: Beginning from the baptism of John, unto that same day that he was taken up from us, must one be ordained to be a witness with us of his resurrection.

verses.original: καὶ ἔστησαν δύο, Ἰωσὴφ τὸν καλούμενον Βαρσαββᾶν, ὃς ἐπεκλήθη Ἰοῦστος, καὶ Μαθθίαν.
verses.translit: kai estisan dyo, Iosef ton kaloymenon Varsavvan, os epeklithi Ioustos, kai Maththian.
verses.translation: And they appointed two, Joseph called Barsabas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.

verses.original: καὶ προσευξάμενοι εἶπαν Σὺ κύριε καρδιογνῶστα πάντων, ἀνάδειξον ὃν ἐξελέξω, ἐκ τούτων τῶν δύο ἕνα,
verses.translit: kai proseyxamenoi eipan Su kyrie kardiognosta panton, anadeixon on exelexo, ek toyton ton dyo ena,
verses.translation: And they prayed, and said, Thou, Lord, which knowest the hearts of all men , shew whether of these two thou hast chosen,

verses.original: λαβεῖν τὸν ⸀τόπον τῆς διακονίας ταύτης καὶ ἀποστολῆς, ⸀ἀφʼ ἧς παρέβη Ἰούδας πορευθῆναι εἰς τὸν τόπον τὸν ἴδιον.
verses.translit: lavein ton topon tes diakonias taytis kai apostoles, af' es parevi Ioydas poreythenai eis ton topon ton idion.
verses.translation: That he may take part of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas by transgression fell, that he might go to his own place.

verses.original: καὶ ἔδωκαν κλήρους ⸀αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἔπεσεν ὁ κλῆρος ἐπὶ Μαθθίαν, καὶ συγκατεψηφίσθη μετὰ τῶν ἕνδεκα ἀποστόλων.
verses.translit: kai edokan kliroys autois, kai epesen o kleros epi Maththian, kai sygkatepsifisthi meta ton endeka apostolon.
verses.translation: And they gave forth their lots; and the lot fell upon Matthias; and he was numbered with the eleven apostles.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς πεντηκοστῆς ἦσαν ⸂πάντες ὁμοῦ⸃ ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό,
verses.translit: Kai en to symplirousthai ten emeran tes pentikostes esan pantes omou epi to auto,
verses.translation: And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἄφνω ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἦχος ὥσπερ φερομένης πνοῆς βιαίας καὶ ἐπλήρωσεν ὅλον τὸν οἶκον οὗ ἦσαν καθήμενοι,
verses.translit: kai egeneto afno ek tou ouranou ehos osper feromenis pnoes viaias kai eplirosen olon ton oikon ou esan kathimenoi,
verses.translation: And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.

verses.original: καὶ ὤφθησαν αὐτοῖς διαμεριζόμεναι γλῶσσαι ὡσεὶ πυρός, ⸂καὶ ἐκάθισεν⸃ ἐφʼ ἕνα ἕκαστον αὐτῶν,
verses.translit: kai ofthisan autois diamerizomenai glossai osei pyros, kai ekathisen ef' ena ekaston auton,
verses.translation: And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν ⸀πάντες πνεύματος ἁγίου, καὶ ἤρξαντο λαλεῖν ἑτέραις γλώσσαις καθὼς τὸ πνεῦμα ἐδίδου ⸂ἀποφθέγγεσθαι αὐτοῖς⸃.
verses.translit: kai eplisthisan pantes pneymatos agioy, kai erxanto lalein eterais glossais kathos to pneuma edidoy apoftheggesthai autois.
verses.translation: And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.

verses.original: Ἦσαν δὲ ⸀ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ κατοικοῦντες Ἰουδαῖοι, ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔθνους τῶν ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανόν·
verses.translit: Esan de en Ieroysalem katoikountes Ioydaioi, andres eulaveis apo pantos ethnoys ton upo ton ouranon*
verses.translation: And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.

verses.original: γενομένης δὲ τῆς φωνῆς ταύτης συνῆλθε τὸ πλῆθος καὶ συνεχύθη, ὅτι ⸀ἤκουον εἷς ἕκαστος τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ λαλούντων αὐτῶν·
verses.translit: genomenis de tes fones taytis synelthe to plethos kai synehythi, oti ekoyon eis ekastos te idia dialekto laloynton auton*
verses.translation: Now when this was noised abroad, the multitude came together, and were confounded, because that every man heard them speak in his own language.

verses.original: ἐξίσταντο ⸀δὲ καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ⸀λέγοντες· ⸀Οὐχ ἰδοὺ ⸀πάντες οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ λαλοῦντες Γαλιλαῖοι;
verses.translit: existanto de kai ethaymazon legontes* Ouh idou pantes outoi eisin oi lalountes Galilaioi;
verses.translation: And they were all amazed and marvelled, saying one to another, Behold, are not all these which speak Galilæans?

verses.original: καὶ πῶς ἡμεῖς ἀκούομεν ἕκαστος τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ ἡμῶν ἐν ᾗ ἐγεννήθημεν;
verses.translit: kai pos emeis akoyomen ekastos te idia dialekto emon en e egennithimen;
verses.translation: And how hear we every man in our own tongue, wherein we were born?

verses.original: Πάρθοι καὶ Μῆδοι καὶ Ἐλαμῖται, καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες τὴν Μεσοποταμίαν, Ἰουδαίαν τε καὶ Καππαδοκίαν, Πόντον καὶ τὴν Ἀσίαν,
verses.translit: Parthoi kai Medoi kai Elamitai, kai oi katoikountes ten Mesopotamian, Ioydaian te kai Kappadokian, Ponton kai ten Asian,
