verses.translation: Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and the dwellers in Mesopotamia, and in Judæa, and Cappadocia, in Pontus, and Asia,

verses.original: Φρυγίαν τε καὶ Παμφυλίαν, Αἴγυπτον καὶ τὰ μέρη τῆς Λιβύης τῆς κατὰ Κυρήνην, καὶ οἱ ἐπιδημοῦντες Ῥωμαῖοι,
verses.translit: Frygian te kai Pamfylian, Aigypton kai ta meri tes Livyis tes kata Kyrinin, kai oi epidimountes Romaioi,
verses.translation: Phrygia, and Pamphylia, in Egypt, and in the parts of Libya about Cyrene, and strangers of Rome, Jews and proselytes,

verses.original: Ἰουδαῖοί τε καὶ προσήλυτοι, Κρῆτες καὶ Ἄραβες, ἀκούομεν λαλούντων αὐτῶν ταῖς ἡμετέραις γλώσσαις τὰ μεγαλεῖα τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: Ioydaioi te kai prosilytoi, Kretes kai Araves, akoyomen laloynton auton tais emeterais glossais ta megaleia tou theou.
verses.translation: Cretes and Arabians, we do hear them speak in our tongues the wonderful works of God.

verses.original: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες καὶ ⸀διηπόρουν, ἄλλος πρὸς ἄλλον λέγοντες· Τί ⸀θέλει τοῦτο εἶναι;
verses.translit: existanto de pantes kai diiporoyn, allos pros allon legontes* Ti thelei touto einai;
verses.translation: And they were all amazed, and were in doubt, saying one to another, What meaneth this?

verses.original: ἕτεροι δὲ ⸀διαχλευάζοντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Γλεύκους μεμεστωμένοι εἰσίν.
verses.translit: eteroi de diahleyazontes elegon oti Gleykoys memestomenoi eisin.
verses.translation: Others mocking said, These men are full of new wine.

verses.original: Σταθεὶς δὲ ⸀ὁ Πέτρος σὺν τοῖς ἕνδεκα ἐπῆρεν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπεφθέγξατο αὐτοῖς· Ἄνδρες Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες Ἰερουσαλὴμ ⸀πάντες, τοῦτο ὑμῖν γνωστὸν ἔστω καὶ ἐνωτίσασθε τὰ ῥήματά μου.
verses.translit: Statheis de o Petros sun tois endeka eperen ten fonen autou kai apefthegxato autois* Andres Ioydaioi kai oi katoikountes Ieroysalem pantes, touto umin gnoston esto kai enotisasthe ta Rimata moy.
verses.translation: But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and said unto them, Ye men of Judæa, and all ye that dwell at Jerusalem, be this known unto you, and hearken to my words:

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ὡς ὑμεῖς ὑπολαμβάνετε οὗτοι μεθύουσιν, ἔστιν γὰρ ὥρα τρίτη τῆς ἡμέρας,
verses.translit: ou gar os umeis upolamvanete outoi methyoysin, estin gar ora triti tes emeras,
verses.translation: For these are not drunken, as ye suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ εἰρημένον διὰ τοῦ προφήτου Ἰωήλ·
verses.translit: alla touto estin to eirimenon dia tou profitoy Ioil*
verses.translation: But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel;

verses.original: Καὶ ἔσται ἐν ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις, λέγει ὁ θεός, ἐκχεῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματός μου ἐπὶ πᾶσαν σάρκα, καὶ προφητεύσουσιν οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν καὶ αἱ θυγατέρες ὑμῶν, καὶ οἱ νεανίσκοι ὑμῶν ὁράσεις ὄψονται, καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ὑμῶν ⸀ἐνυπνίοις ἐνυπνιασθήσονται·
verses.translit: Kai estai en tais eshatais emerais, legei o theos, ekheo apo tou pneymatos moy epi pasan sarka, kai profiteysoysin oi yioi umon kai ai thygateres umon, kai oi neaniskoi umon oraseis opsontai, kai oi presvyteroi umon enypniois enypniasthisontai*
verses.translation: And it shall come to pass in the last days, saith God, I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams:

verses.original: καί γε ἐπὶ τοὺς δούλους μου καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς δούλας μου ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἐκχεῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματός μου, καὶ προφητεύσουσιν.
verses.translit: kai ge epi tous doyloys moy kai epi tas doylas moy en tais emerais ekeinais ekheo apo tou pneymatos moy, kai profiteysoysin.
verses.translation: And on my servants and on my handmaidens I will pour out in those days of my Spirit; and they shall prophesy:

verses.original: καὶ δώσω τέρατα ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἄνω καὶ σημεῖα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς κάτω, αἷμα καὶ πῦρ καὶ ἀτμίδα καπνοῦ·
verses.translit: kai doso terata en to ourano ano kai simeia epi tes ges kato, aima kai pur kai atmida kapnou*
verses.translation: And I will shew wonders in heaven above, and signs in the earth beneath; blood, and fire, and vapour of smoke:

verses.original: ὁ ἥλιος μεταστραφήσεται εἰς σκότος καὶ ἡ σελήνη εἰς αἷμα πρὶν ⸀ἢ ⸀ἐλθεῖν ἡμέραν κυρίου τὴν μεγάλην καὶ ἐπιφανῆ.
verses.translit: o elios metastrafisetai eis skotos kai e selini eis aima prin e elthein emeran kyrioy ten megalin kai epifane.
verses.translation: The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before that great and notable day of the Lord come:

verses.original: καὶ ἔσται πᾶς ὃς ⸀ἐὰν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου σωθήσεται.
verses.translit: kai estai pas os ean epikalesitai to onoma kyrioy sothisetai.
verses.translation: And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved.

verses.original: Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται, ἀκούσατε τοὺς λόγους τούτους. Ἰησοῦν τὸν Ναζωραῖον, ἄνδρα ⸂ἀποδεδειγμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ⸃ εἰς ὑμᾶς δυνάμεσι καὶ τέρασι καὶ σημείοις οἷς ἐποίησεν διʼ αὐτοῦ ὁ θεὸς ἐν μέσῳ ὑμῶν, ⸀καθὼς αὐτοὶ οἴδατε,
verses.translit: Andres Israilitai, akoysate tous logoys toytoys. Iisoun ton Nazoraion, andra apodedeigmenon apo tou theou eis umas dynamesi kai terasi kai simeiois ois epoiisen di' autou o theos en meso umon, kathos autoi oidate,
verses.translation: Ye men of Israel, hear these words; Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved of God among you by miracles and wonders and signs, which God did by him in the midst of you, as ye yourselves also know:

verses.original: τοῦτον τῇ ὡρισμένῃ βουλῇ καὶ προγνώσει τοῦ θεοῦ ⸀ἔκδοτον διὰ ⸀χειρὸς ἀνόμων προσπήξαντες ἀνείλατε,
verses.translit: touton te orismene voyle kai prognosei tou theou ekdoton dia heiros anomon prospixantes aneilate,
verses.translation: Him, being delivered by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God, ye have taken, and by wicked hands have crucified and slain:

verses.original: ὃν ὁ θεὸς ἀνέστησεν λύσας τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ θανάτου, καθότι οὐκ ἦν δυνατὸν κρατεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: on o theos anestisen lysas tas odinas tou thanatoy, kathoti ouk en dynaton krateisthai auton up' autou*
verses.translation: Whom God hath raised up, having loosed the pains of death: because it was not possible that he should be holden of it.

verses.original: Δαυὶδ γὰρ λέγει εἰς αὐτόν· Προορώμην τὸν κύριον ἐνώπιόν μου διὰ παντός, ὅτι ἐκ δεξιῶν μού ἐστιν ἵνα μὴ σαλευθῶ.
verses.translit: Dayid gar legei eis auton* Prooromin ton kyrion enopion moy dia pantos, oti ek dexion moy estin ina me saleytho.
verses.translation: For David speaketh concerning him, I foresaw the Lord always before my face, for he is on my right hand, that I should not be moved:

verses.original: διὰ τοῦτο ηὐφράνθη ⸂ἡ καρδία μου⸃ καὶ ἠγαλλιάσατο ἡ γλῶσσά μου, ἔτι δὲ καὶ ἡ σάρξ μου κατασκηνώσει ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι·
verses.translit: dia touto iufranthi e kardia moy kai egalliasato e glossa moy, eti de kai e sarx moy kataskinosei ep' elpidi*
verses.translation: Therefore did my heart rejoice, and my tongue was glad; moreover also my flesh shall rest in hope:

verses.original: ὅτι οὐκ ἐγκαταλείψεις τὴν ψυχήν μου εἰς ⸀ᾅδην, οὐδὲ δώσεις τὸν ὅσιόν σου ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν.
verses.translit: oti ouk egkataleipseis ten psyhin moy eis adin, oude doseis ton osion soy idein diafthoran.
verses.translation: Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell, neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.

verses.original: ἐγνώρισάς μοι ὁδοὺς ζωῆς, πληρώσεις με εὐφροσύνης μετὰ τοῦ προσώπου σου.
verses.translit: egnorisas moi odous zoes, pliroseis me eufrosynis meta tou prosopoy soy.
verses.translation: Thou hast made known to me the ways of life; thou shalt make me full of joy with thy countenance.

verses.original: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἐξὸν εἰπεῖν μετὰ παρρησίας πρὸς ὑμᾶς περὶ τοῦ πατριάρχου Δαυίδ, ὅτι καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν καὶ ἐτάφη, καὶ τὸ μνῆμα αὐτοῦ ἔστιν ἐν ἡμῖν ἄχρι τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης·
verses.translit: Andres adelfoi, exon eipein meta parrisias pros umas peri tou patriarhoy Dayid, oti kai eteleytisen kai etafi, kai to mnema autou estin en emin ahri tes emeras taytis*
verses.translation: Men and brethren, let me freely speak unto you of the patriarch David, that he is both dead and buried, and his sepulchre is with us unto this day.

verses.original: προφήτης οὖν ὑπάρχων, καὶ εἰδὼς ὅτι ὅρκῳ ὤμοσεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεὸς ἐκ καρποῦ τῆς ὀσφύος ⸀αὐτοῦ καθίσαι ἐπὶ ⸂τὸν θρόνον⸃ αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: profitis oun uparhon, kai eidos oti orko omosen auto o theos ek karpou tes osfyos autou kathisai epi ton thronon autou,
verses.translation: Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;

verses.original: προϊδὼν ἐλάλησεν περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τοῦ χριστοῦ ὅτι ⸂οὔτε ἐγκατελείφθη⸃ εἰς ⸀ᾅδην ⸀οὔτε ἡ σὰρξ αὐτοῦ εἶδεν διαφθοράν.
verses.translit: proidon elalisen peri tes anastaseos tou hristou oti oute egkateleifthi eis adin oute e sarx autou eiden diafthoran.
verses.translation: He seeing this before spake of the resurrection of Christ, that his soul was not left in hell, neither his flesh did see corruption.

verses.original: τοῦτον τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀνέστησεν ὁ θεός, οὗ πάντες ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν μάρτυρες.
verses.translit: touton ton Iisoun anestisen o theos, ou pantes emeis esmen martyres.
verses.translation: This Jesus hath God raised up, whereof we all are witnesses.

verses.original: τῇ δεξιᾷ οὖν τοῦ θεοῦ ὑψωθεὶς τήν τε ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ ⸂πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου⸃ λαβὼν παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐξέχεεν τοῦτο ⸀ὃ ⸀ὑμεῖς βλέπετε καὶ ἀκούετε.
verses.translit: te dexia oun tou theou upsotheis tin te epaggelian tou pneymatos tou agioy lavon para tou patros exeheen touto o umeis vlepete kai akoyete.
verses.translation: Therefore being by the right hand of God exalted, and having received of the Father the promise of the Holy Ghost, he hath shed forth this, which ye now see and hear.

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ Δαυὶδ ἀνέβη εἰς τοὺς οὐρανούς, λέγει δὲ αὐτός· Εἶπεν ⸀ὁ κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου,
verses.translit: ou gar Dayid anevi eis tous ouranoys, legei de autos* Eipen o kyrios to kyrio moy* Kathoy ek dexion moy,
verses.translation: For David is not ascended into the heavens: but he saith himself, The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand,

verses.original: ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου.
verses.translit: eos an tho tous ehthroys soy upopodion ton podon soy.
verses.translation: Until I make thy foes thy footstool.

verses.original: ἀσφαλῶς οὖν γινωσκέτω πᾶς οἶκος Ἰσραὴλ ὅτι καὶ κύριον ⸂αὐτὸν καὶ χριστὸν⸃ ⸂ἐποίησεν ὁ θεός⸃, τοῦτον τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὃν ὑμεῖς ἐσταυρώσατε.
verses.translit: asfalos oun ginosketo pas oikos Israel oti kai kyrion auton kai hriston epoiisen o theos, touton ton Iisoun on umeis estayrosate.
verses.translation: Therefore let all the house of Israel know assuredly, that God hath made that same Jesus, whom ye have crucified, both Lord and Christ.

verses.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ κατενύγησαν ⸂τὴν καρδίαν⸃, εἶπόν τε πρὸς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τοὺς λοιποὺς ἀποστόλους· Τί ⸀ποιήσωμεν, ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί;
verses.translit: Akoysantes de katenygisan ten kardian, eipon te pros ton Petron kai tous loipous apostoloys* Ti poiisomen, andres adelfoi;
verses.translation: Now when they heard this , they were pricked in their heart, and said unto Peter and to the rest of the apostles, Men and brethren, what shall we do?

verses.original: Πέτρος δὲ ⸂πρὸς αὐτούς· Μετανοήσατε⸃, καὶ βαπτισθήτω ἕκαστος ὑμῶν ⸀ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς ἄφεσιν ⸀τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ⸀ὑμῶν, καὶ λήμψεσθε τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος·
verses.translit: Petros de pros autoys* Metanoisate, kai vaptisthito ekastos umon epi to onomati Iisou Hristou eis afesin ton amartion umon, kai limpsesthe ten dorean tou agioy pneymatos*
verses.translation: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.

verses.original: ὑμῖν γάρ ἐστιν ἡ ἐπαγγελία καὶ τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς εἰς μακρὰν ὅσους ἂν προσκαλέσηται κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: umin gar estin e epaggelia kai tois teknois umon kai pasi tois eis makran osoys an proskalesitai kyrios o theos emon.
verses.translation: For the promise is unto you, and to your children, and to all that are afar off, even as many as the Lord our God shall call.

verses.original: ἑτέροις τε λόγοις πλείοσιν διεμαρτύρατο, καὶ παρεκάλει ⸀αὐτοὺς λέγων· Σώθητε ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς τῆς σκολιᾶς ταύτης.
verses.translit: eterois te logois pleiosin diemartyrato, kai parekalei autous legon* Sothite apo tes geneas tes skolias taytis.
verses.translation: And with many other words did he testify and exhort, saying, Save yourselves from this untoward generation.

verses.original: οἱ μὲν ⸀οὖν ἀποδεξάμενοι τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθησαν, καὶ προσετέθησαν ⸀ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ψυχαὶ ὡσεὶ τρισχίλιαι.
verses.translit: oi men oun apodexamenoi ton logon autou evaptisthisan, kai prosetethisan en te emera ekeine psyhai osei trishiliai.
verses.translation: Then they that gladly received his word were baptized: and the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls.

verses.original: ἦσαν δὲ προσκαρτεροῦντες τῇ διδαχῇ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ τῇ ⸀κοινωνίᾳ, τῇ κλάσει τοῦ ἄρτου καὶ ταῖς προσευχαῖς.
verses.translit: esan de proskarterountes te didahe ton apostolon kai te koinonia, te klasei tou artoy kai tais proseyhais.
verses.translation: And they continued stedfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.

verses.original: ⸀Ἐγίνετο δὲ πάσῃ ψυχῇ φόβος, πολλά ⸀τε τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα διὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐγίνετο.
verses.translit: Egineto de pase psyhe fovos, polla te terata kai simeia dia ton apostolon egineto.
verses.translation: And fear came upon every soul: and many wonders and signs were done by the apostles.

verses.original: πάντες δὲ οἱ ⸀πιστεύοντες ⸂ἦσαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ⸃ εἶχον ἅπαντα κοινά,
verses.translit: pantes de oi pisteyontes esan epi to auto kai eihon apanta koina,
verses.translation: And all that believed were together, and had all things common;

verses.original: καὶ τὰ κτήματα καὶ τὰς ὑπάρξεις ἐπίπρασκον καὶ διεμέριζον αὐτὰ πᾶσιν καθότι ἄν τις χρείαν εἶχεν·
verses.translit: kai ta ktimata kai tas uparxeis epipraskon kai diemerizon auta pasin kathoti an tis hreian eihen*
verses.translation: And sold their possessions and goods, and parted them to all men , as every man had need.

verses.original: καθʼ ἡμέραν τε προσκαρτεροῦντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, κλῶντές τε κατʼ οἶκον ἄρτον, μετελάμβανον τροφῆς ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει καὶ ἀφελότητι καρδίας,
verses.translit: kath' emeran te proskarterountes omothymadon en to iero, klontes te kat' oikon arton, metelamvanon trofes en agalliasei kai afelotiti kardias,
verses.translation: And they, continuing daily with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, did eat their meat with gladness and singleness of heart,

verses.original: αἰνοῦντες τὸν θεὸν καὶ ἔχοντες χάριν πρὸς ὅλον τὸν λαόν. ὁ δὲ κύριος προσετίθει τοὺς σῳζομένους καθʼ ἡμέραν ⸂ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό⸃.
verses.translit: ainountes ton theon kai ehontes harin pros olon ton laon. o de kyrios prosetithei tous sozomenoys kath' emeran epi to auto.
verses.translation: Praising God, and having favour with all the people. And the Lord added to the church daily such as should be saved.

verses.original: ⸂Πέτρος δὲ⸃ καὶ Ἰωάννης ἀνέβαινον εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἐπὶ τὴν ὥραν τῆς προσευχῆς τὴν ἐνάτην,
verses.translit: Petros de kai Ioannis anevainon eis to ieron epi ten oran tes proseyhes ten enatin,
verses.translation: Now Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour .

verses.original: καί τις ἀνὴρ χωλὸς ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς αὐτοῦ ὑπάρχων ἐβαστάζετο, ὃν ἐτίθουν καθʼ ἡμέραν πρὸς τὴν θύραν τοῦ ἱεροῦ τὴν λεγομένην Ὡραίαν τοῦ αἰτεῖν ἐλεημοσύνην παρὰ τῶν εἰσπορευομένων εἰς τὸ ἱερόν,
verses.translit: kai tis aner holos ek koilias mitros autou uparhon evastazeto, on etithoyn kath' emeran pros ten thyran tou ierou ten legomenin Oraian tou aitein eleimosynin para ton eisporeyomenon eis to ieron,
verses.translation: And a certain man lame from his mother’s womb was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask alms of them that entered into the temple;

verses.original: ὃς ἰδὼν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην μέλλοντας εἰσιέναι εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἠρώτα ἐλεημοσύνην ⸀λαβεῖν.
verses.translit: os idon Petron kai Ioannin mellontas eisienai eis to ieron erota eleimosynin lavein.
verses.translation: Who seeing Peter and John about to go into the temple asked an alms.

verses.original: ἀτενίσας δὲ Πέτρος εἰς αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ Ἰωάννῃ εἶπεν· Βλέψον εἰς ἡμᾶς.
verses.translit: atenisas de Petros eis auton sun to Ioanne eipen* Vlepson eis emas.
verses.translation: And Peter, fastening his eyes upon him with John, said, Look on us.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἐπεῖχεν αὐτοῖς προσδοκῶν τι παρʼ αὐτῶν λαβεῖν.
verses.translit: o de epeihen autois prosdokon ti par' auton lavein.
verses.translation: And he gave heed unto them, expecting to receive something of them.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ Πέτρος· Ἀργύριον καὶ χρυσίον οὐχ ὑπάρχει μοι, ὃ δὲ ἔχω τοῦτό σοι δίδωμι· ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου ⸀περιπάτει.
verses.translit: eipen de Petros* Argyrion kai hrysion ouh uparhei moi, o de eho touto soi didomi* en to onomati Iisou Hristou tou Nazoraioy peripatei.
verses.translation: Then Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk.

verses.original: καὶ πιάσας αὐτὸν τῆς δεξιᾶς χειρὸς ἤγειρεν ⸀αὐτόν· παραχρῆμα δὲ ἐστερεώθησαν ⸂αἱ βάσεις αὐτοῦ⸃ καὶ τὰ ⸀σφυδρά,
verses.translit: kai piasas auton tes dexias heiros egeiren auton* parahrema de estereothisan ai vaseis autou kai ta sfydra,
verses.translation: And he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up: and immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξαλλόμενος ἔστη καὶ περιεπάτει, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν σὺν αὐτοῖς εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν περιπατῶν καὶ ἁλλόμενος καὶ αἰνῶν τὸν θεόν.
verses.translit: kai exallomenos esti kai periepatei, kai eiselthen sun autois eis to ieron peripaton kai allomenos kai ainon ton theon.
verses.translation: And he leaping up stood, and walked, and entered with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God.

verses.original: καὶ εἶδεν ⸂πᾶς ὁ λαὸς αὐτὸν⸃ περιπατοῦντα καὶ αἰνοῦντα τὸν θεόν,
verses.translit: kai eiden pas o laos auton peripatounta kai ainounta ton theon,
verses.translation: And all the people saw him walking and praising God:

verses.original: ἐπεγίνωσκον ⸀δὲ αὐτὸν ὅτι ⸀οὗτος ἦν ὁ πρὸς τὴν ἐλεημοσύνην καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῇ Ὡραίᾳ Πύλῃ τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν θάμβους καὶ ἐκστάσεως ἐπὶ τῷ συμβεβηκότι αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: epeginoskon de auton oti outos en o pros ten eleimosynin kathimenos epi te Oraia Pyle tou ierou, kai eplisthisan thamvoys kai ekstaseos epi to symvevikoti auto.
verses.translation: And they knew that it was he which sat for alms at the Beautiful gate of the temple: and they were filled with wonder and amazement at that which had happened unto him.

verses.original: Κρατοῦντος δὲ ⸀αὐτοῦ τὸν Πέτρον καὶ ⸀τὸν Ἰωάννην συνέδραμεν ⸂πᾶς ὁ λαὸς πρὸς αὐτοὺς⸃ ἐπὶ τῇ στοᾷ τῇ καλουμένῃ Σολομῶντος ἔκθαμβοι.
verses.translit: Kratountos de autou ton Petron kai ton Ioannin synedramen pas o laos pros autous epi te stoa te kaloymene Solomontos ekthamvoi.
verses.translation: And as the lame man which was healed held Peter and John, all the people ran together unto them in the porch that is called Solomon’s, greatly wondering.

verses.original: ἰδὼν δὲ ⸀ὁ Πέτρος ἀπεκρίνατο πρὸς τὸν λαόν· Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται, τί θαυμάζετε ἐπὶ τούτῳ, ἢ ἡμῖν τί ἀτενίζετε ὡς ἰδίᾳ δυνάμει ἢ εὐσεβείᾳ πεποιηκόσιν τοῦ περιπατεῖν αὐτόν;
verses.translit: idon de o Petros apekrinato pros ton laon* Andres Israilitai, ti thaymazete epi toyto, e emin ti atenizete os idia dynamei e euseveia pepoiikosin tou peripatein auton;
verses.translation: And when Peter saw it , he answered unto the people, Ye men of Israel, why marvel ye at this? or why look ye so earnestly on us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made this man to walk?

verses.original: ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ⸂Ἰσαὰκ καὶ⸃ Ἰακώβ, ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, ἐδόξασεν τὸν παῖδα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν, ὃν ὑμεῖς ⸀μὲν παρεδώκατε καὶ ⸀ἠρνήσασθε κατὰ πρόσωπον Πιλάτου, κρίναντος ἐκείνου ἀπολύειν·
verses.translit: o theos Avraam kai Isaak kai Iakov, o theos ton pateron emon, edoxasen ton paida autou Iisoun, on umeis men paredokate kai ernisasthe kata prosopon Pilatoy, krinantos ekeinoy apolyein*
verses.translation: The God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God of our fathers, hath glorified his Son Jesus; whom ye delivered up, and denied him in the presence of Pilate, when he was determined to let him go.

verses.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ τὸν ἅγιον καὶ δίκαιον ἠρνήσασθε καὶ ᾐτήσασθε ἄνδρα φονέα χαρισθῆναι ὑμῖν,
verses.translit: umeis de ton agion kai dikaion ernisasthe kai etisasthe andra fonea haristhenai umin,
verses.translation: But ye denied the Holy One and the Just, and desired a murderer to be granted unto you;

verses.original: τὸν δὲ ἀρχηγὸν τῆς ζωῆς ἀπεκτείνατε, ὃν ὁ θεὸς ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν, οὗ ἡμεῖς μάρτυρές ἐσμεν.
verses.translit: ton de arhigon tes zoes apekteinate, on o theos egeiren ek nekron, ou emeis martyres esmen.
verses.translation: And killed the Prince of life, whom God hath raised from the dead; whereof we are witnesses.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἐπὶ τῇ πίστει τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ τοῦτον ὃν θεωρεῖτε καὶ οἴδατε ἐστερέωσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἡ πίστις ἡ διʼ αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ τὴν ὁλοκληρίαν ταύτην ἀπέναντι πάντων ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: kai epi te pistei tou onomatos autou touton on theoreite kai oidate estereosen to onoma autou, kai e pistis e di' autou edoken auto ten oloklirian taytin apenanti panton umon.
verses.translation: And his name through faith in his name hath made this man strong, whom ye see and know: yea, the faith which is by him hath given him this perfect soundness in the presence of you all.

verses.original: Καὶ νῦν, ἀδελφοί, οἶδα ὅτι κατὰ ἄγνοιαν ἐπράξατε, ὥσπερ καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες ὑμῶν·
verses.translit: Kai nun, adelfoi, oida oti kata agnoian epraxate, osper kai oi arhontes umon*
verses.translation: And now, brethren, I wot that through ignorance ye did it , as did also your rulers.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ θεὸς ἃ προκατήγγειλεν διὰ στόματος πάντων τῶν ⸀προφητῶν παθεῖν τὸν χριστὸν ⸀αὐτοῦ ἐπλήρωσεν οὕτως.
verses.translit: o de theos a prokatiggeilen dia stomatos panton ton profiton pathein ton hriston autou eplirosen outos.
verses.translation: But those things, which God before had shewed by the mouth of all his prophets, that Christ should suffer, he hath so fulfilled.

verses.original: μετανοήσατε οὖν καὶ ἐπιστρέψατε ⸀πρὸς τὸ ἐξαλειφθῆναι ὑμῶν τὰς ἁμαρτίας,
verses.translit: metanoisate oun kai epistrepsate pros to exaleifthenai umon tas amartias,
verses.translation: Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord;

verses.original: ὅπως ἂν ἔλθωσιν καιροὶ ἀναψύξεως ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ κυρίου καὶ ἀποστείλῃ τὸν προκεχειρισμένον ὑμῖν χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν,
verses.translit: opos an elthosin kairoi anapsyxeos apo prosopoy tou kyrioy kai aposteile ton prokeheirismenon umin hriston Iisoun,
verses.translation: And he shall send Jesus Christ, which before was preached unto you:

verses.original: ὃν δεῖ οὐρανὸν μὲν δέξασθαι ἄχρι χρόνων ἀποκαταστάσεως πάντων ὧν ἐλάλησεν ὁ θεὸς διὰ ⸀στόματος τῶν ἁγίων ⸂ἀπʼ αἰῶνος αὐτοῦ προφητῶν⸃.
verses.translit: on dei ouranon men dexasthai ahri hronon apokatastaseos panton on elalisen o theos dia stomatos ton agion ap' aionos autou profiton.
verses.translation: Whom the heaven must receive until the times of restitution of all things, which God hath spoken by the mouth of all his holy prophets since the world began.

verses.original: Μωϋσῆς ⸀μὲν εἶπεν ὅτι Προφήτην ὑμῖν ἀναστήσει κύριος ὁ ⸀θεὸς ἐκ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ὑμῶν ὡς ἐμέ· αὐτοῦ ἀκούσεσθε κατὰ πάντα ὅσα ἂν λαλήσῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: Moyses men eipen oti Profitin umin anastisei kyrios o theos ek ton adelfon umon os eme* autou akoysesthe kata panta osa an lalise pros umas.
verses.translation: For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear in all things whatsoever he shall say unto you.

verses.original: ἔσται δὲ πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἥτις ⸀ἂν μὴ ἀκούσῃ τοῦ προφήτου ἐκείνου ἐξολεθρευθήσεται ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ.
verses.translit: estai de pasa psyhe etis an me akoyse tou profitoy ekeinoy exolethreythisetai ek tou laou.
verses.translation: And it shall come to pass, that every soul, which will not hear that prophet, shall be destroyed from among the people.

verses.original: καὶ πάντες δὲ οἱ προφῆται ἀπὸ Σαμουὴλ καὶ τῶν καθεξῆς ὅσοι ἐλάλησαν καὶ κατήγγειλαν τὰς ἡμέρας ταύτας.
verses.translit: kai pantes de oi profetai apo Samoyel kai ton kathexes osoi elalisan kai katiggeilan tas emeras taytas.
verses.translation: Yea, and all the prophets from Samuel and those that follow after, as many as have spoken, have likewise foretold of these days.

verses.original: ὑμεῖς ἐστε ⸀οἱ υἱοὶ τῶν προφητῶν καὶ τῆς διαθήκης ἧς ⸂διέθετο ὁ θεὸς⸃ πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ⸀ὑμῶν, λέγων πρὸς Ἀβραάμ· Καὶ ἐν τῷ σπέρματί σου ⸀ἐνευλογηθήσονται πᾶσαι αἱ πατριαὶ τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: umeis este oi yioi ton profiton kai tes diathikis es dietheto o theos pros tous pateras umon, legon pros Avraam; Kai en to spermati soy eneylogithisontai pasai ai patriai tes ges.
verses.translation: Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed.

verses.original: ὑμῖν πρῶτον ⸂ἀναστήσας ὁ θεὸς⸃ τὸν παῖδα ⸀αὐτοῦ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτὸν εὐλογοῦντα ὑμᾶς ἐν τῷ ἀποστρέφειν ἕκαστον ἀπὸ τῶν πονηριῶν ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: umin proton anastisas o theos ton paida autou apesteilen auton eulogounta umas en to apostrefein ekaston apo ton ponirion umon.
verses.translation: Unto you first God, having raised up his Son Jesus, sent him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from his iniquities.

verses.original: Λαλούντων δὲ αὐτῶν πρὸς τὸν λαὸν ἐπέστησαν αὐτοῖς οἱ ⸀ἱερεῖς καὶ ὁ στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ οἱ Σαδδουκαῖοι,
verses.translit: Laloynton de auton pros ton laon epestisan autois oi iereis kai o stratigos tou ierou kai oi Saddoykaioi,
verses.translation: And as they spake unto the people, the priests, and the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees, came upon them,

verses.original: διαπονούμενοι διὰ τὸ διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς τὸν λαὸν καὶ καταγγέλλειν ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ τὴν ἀνάστασιν ⸂τὴν ἐκ⸃ νεκρῶν,
verses.translit: diaponoymenoi dia to didaskein autous ton laon kai kataggellein en to Iisou ten anastasin ten ek nekron,
verses.translation: Being grieved that they taught the people, and preached through Jesus the resurrection from the dead.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπέβαλον αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ ἔθεντο εἰς τήρησιν εἰς τὴν αὔριον, ἦν γὰρ ἑσπέρα ἤδη.
verses.translit: kai epevalon autois tas heiras kai ethento eis tirisin eis ten aurion, en gar espera edi.
verses.translation: And they laid hands on them, and put them in hold unto the next day: for it was now eventide.

verses.original: πολλοὶ δὲ τῶν ἀκουσάντων τὸν λόγον ἐπίστευσαν, καὶ ἐγενήθη ⸀ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ⸀ὡς χιλιάδες πέντε.
verses.translit: polloi de ton akoysanton ton logon episteysan, kai egenithi o arithmos ton andron os hiliades pente.
verses.translation: Howbeit many of them which heard the word believed; and the number of the men was about five thousand.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν αὔριον συναχθῆναι αὐτῶν τοὺς ἄρχοντας καὶ ⸀τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους καὶ ⸁τοὺς γραμματεῖς ⸀ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ
verses.translit: Egeneto de epi ten aurion synahthenai auton tous arhontas kai tous presvyteroys kai tous grammateis en Ieroysalim
verses.translation: And it came to pass on the morrow, that their rulers, and elders, and scribes,

verses.original: (καὶ ⸂Ἅννας ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ Καϊάφας καὶ Ἰωάννης καὶ Ἀλέξανδρος⸃ καὶ ὅσοι ἦσαν ἐκ γένους ἀρχιερατικοῦ),
verses.translit: (kai Annas o arhiereus kai Kaiafas kai Ioannis kai Alexandros kai osoi esan ek genoys arhieratikou),
verses.translation: And Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the kindred of the high priest, were gathered together at Jerusalem.

verses.original: καὶ στήσαντες αὐτοὺς ἐν ⸀τῷ μέσῳ ἐπυνθάνοντο· Ἐν ποίᾳ δυνάμει ἢ ἐν ποίῳ ὀνόματι ἐποιήσατε τοῦτο ὑμεῖς;
verses.translit: kai stisantes autous en to meso epynthanonto* En poia dynamei e en poio onomati epoiisate touto umeis;
verses.translation: And when they had set them in the midst, they asked, By what power, or by what name, have ye done this?

verses.original: τότε Πέτρος πλησθεὶς πνεύματος ἁγίου εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἄρχοντες τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ⸀πρεσβύτεροι,
verses.translit: tote Petros plistheis pneymatos agioy eipen pros autoys* Arhontes tou laou kai presvyteroi,
verses.translation: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, said unto them, Ye rulers of the people, and elders of Israel,

verses.original: εἰ ἡμεῖς σήμερον ἀνακρινόμεθα ἐπὶ εὐεργεσίᾳ ἀνθρώπου ἀσθενοῦς, ἐν τίνι οὗτος σέσωσται,
verses.translit: ei emeis simeron anakrinometha epi euergesia anthropoy asthenous, en tini outos sesostai,
verses.translation: If we this day be examined of the good deed done to the impotent man, by what means he is made whole;

verses.original: γνωστὸν ἔστω πᾶσιν ὑμῖν καὶ παντὶ τῷ λαῷ Ἰσραὴλ ὅτι ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου, ὃν ὑμεῖς ἐσταυρώσατε, ὃν ὁ θεὸς ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἐν τούτῳ οὗτος παρέστηκεν ἐνώπιον ὑμῶν ὑγιής.
verses.translit: gnoston esto pasin umin kai panti to lao Israel oti en to onomati Iisou Hristou tou Nazoraioy, on umeis estayrosate, on o theos egeiren ek nekron, en toyto outos parestiken enopion umon ugiis.
verses.translation: Be it known unto you all, and to all the people of Israel, that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom ye crucified, whom God raised from the dead, even by him doth this man stand here before you whole.

verses.original: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ λίθος ὁ ἐξουθενηθεὶς ὑφʼ ὑμῶν τῶν ⸀οἰκοδόμων, ὁ γενόμενος εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας.
verses.translit: outos estin o lithos o exoythenitheis uf' umon ton oikodomon, o genomenos eis kefalen gonias.
verses.translation: This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner.

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ἄλλῳ οὐδενὶ ἡ σωτηρία, ⸀οὐδὲ γὰρ ὄνομά ἐστιν ἕτερον ⸂ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν⸃ τὸ δεδομένον ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἐν ᾧ δεῖ σωθῆναι ἡμᾶς.
verses.translit: kai ouk estin en allo oudeni e sotiria, oude gar onoma estin eteron upo ton ouranon to dedomenon en anthropois en o dei sothenai emas.
verses.translation: Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.

verses.original: Θεωροῦντες δὲ τὴν τοῦ Πέτρου παρρησίαν καὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ καταλαβόμενοι ὅτι ἄνθρωποι ἀγράμματοί εἰσιν καὶ ἰδιῶται, ἐθαύμαζον, ἐπεγίνωσκόν τε αὐτοὺς ὅτι σὺν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἦσαν,
verses.translit: Theorountes de ten tou Petroy parrisian kai Ioannoy kai katalavomenoi oti anthropoi agrammatoi eisin kai idiotai, ethaymazon, epeginoskon te autous oti sun to Iisou esan,
verses.translation: Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.

verses.original: τόν ⸀τε ἄνθρωπον βλέποντες σὺν αὐτοῖς ἑστῶτα τὸν τεθεραπευμένον οὐδὲν εἶχον ἀντειπεῖν.
verses.translit: ton te anthropon vlepontes sun autois estota ton tetherapeymenon ouden eihon anteipein.
verses.translation: And beholding the man which was healed standing with them, they could say nothing against it.

verses.original: κελεύσαντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔξω τοῦ συνεδρίου ἀπελθεῖν συνέβαλλον πρὸς ἀλλήλους
verses.translit: keleysantes de autous exo tou synedrioy apelthein synevallon pros alliloys
verses.translation: But when they had commanded them to go aside out of the council, they conferred among themselves,

verses.original: λέγοντες· Τί ⸀ποιήσωμεν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τούτοις; ὅτι μὲν γὰρ γνωστὸν σημεῖον γέγονεν διʼ αὐτῶν πᾶσιν τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν Ἰερουσαλὴμ φανερόν, καὶ οὐ δυνάμεθα ⸀ἀρνεῖσθαι·
verses.translit: legontes* Ti poiisomen tois anthropois toytois; oti men gar gnoston simeion gegonen di' auton pasin tois katoikousin Ieroysalem faneron, kai ou dynametha arneisthai*
verses.translation: Saying, What shall we do to these men? for that indeed a notable miracle hath been done by them is manifest to all them that dwell in Jerusalem; and we cannot deny it .

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ἵνα μὴ ἐπὶ πλεῖον διανεμηθῇ εἰς τὸν λαόν, ⸀ἀπειλησώμεθα αὐτοῖς μηκέτι λαλεῖν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ μηδενὶ ἀνθρώπων.
verses.translit: all' ina me epi pleion dianemithe eis ton laon, apeilisometha autois miketi lalein epi to onomati toyto mideni anthropon.
verses.translation: But that it spread no further among the people, let us straitly threaten them, that they speak henceforth to no man in this name.

verses.original: καὶ καλέσαντες αὐτοὺς παρήγγειλαν ⸀τὸ καθόλου μὴ φθέγγεσθαι μηδὲ διδάσκειν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: kai kalesantes autous pariggeilan to katholoy me ftheggesthai mide didaskein epi to onomati tou Iisou.
verses.translation: And they called them, and commanded them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος καὶ Ἰωάννης ἀποκριθέντες ⸂εἶπον πρὸς αὐτούς⸃· Εἰ δίκαιόν ἐστιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ὑμῶν ἀκούειν μᾶλλον ἢ τοῦ θεοῦ, κρίνατε,
verses.translit: o de Petros kai Ioannis apokrithentes eipon pros autoys* Ei dikaion estin enopion tou theou umon akoyein mallon e tou theou, krinate,
verses.translation: But Peter and John answered and said unto them, Whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye.

verses.original: οὐ δυνάμεθα γὰρ ἡμεῖς ἃ εἴδαμεν καὶ ἠκούσαμεν μὴ λαλεῖν.
verses.translit: ou dynametha gar emeis a eidamen kai ekoysamen me lalein.
verses.translation: For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ προσαπειλησάμενοι ἀπέλυσαν αὐτούς, μηδὲν εὑρίσκοντες τὸ πῶς ⸀κολάσωνται αὐτούς, διὰ τὸν λαόν, ὅτι πάντες ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεὸν ἐπὶ τῷ γεγονότι·
verses.translit: oi de prosapeilisamenoi apelysan autoys, miden euriskontes to pos kolasontai autoys, dia ton laon, oti pantes edoxazon ton theon epi to gegonoti*
verses.translation: So when they had further threatened them, they let them go, finding nothing how they might punish them, because of the people: for all men glorified God for that which was done.

verses.original: ἐτῶν γὰρ ἦν πλειόνων τεσσεράκοντα ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐφʼ ὃν ⸀γεγόνει τὸ σημεῖον τοῦτο τῆς ἰάσεως.
verses.translit: eton gar en pleionon tesserakonta o anthropos ef' on gegonei to simeion touto tes iaseos.
verses.translation: For the man was above forty years old, on whom this miracle of healing was shewed.

verses.original: Ἀπολυθέντες δὲ ἦλθον πρὸς τοὺς ἰδίους καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν ὅσα πρὸς αὐτοὺς οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι εἶπαν.
verses.translit: Apolythentes de elthon pros tous idioys kai apiggeilan osa pros autous oi arhiereis kai oi presvyteroi eipan.
verses.translation: And being let go, they went to their own company, and reported all that the chief priests and elders had said unto them.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἦραν φωνὴν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ εἶπαν· Δέσποτα, ⸀σὺ ὁ ποιήσας τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς,
verses.translit: oi de akoysantes omothymadon eran fonen pros ton theon kai eipan* Despota, su o poiisas ton ouranon kai ten gen kai ten thalassan kai panta ta en autois,
verses.translation: And when they heard that, they lifted up their voice to God with one accord, and said, Lord, thou art God, which hast made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all that in them is:

verses.original: ὁ ⸂τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν⸃ διὰ ⸂πνεύματος ἁγίου⸃ στόματος Δαυὶδ παιδός σου εἰπών· Ἱνατί ἐφρύαξαν ἔθνη καὶ λαοὶ ἐμελέτησαν κενά;
verses.translit: o tou patros emon dia pneymatos agioy stomatos Dayid paidos soy eipon* Inati efryaxan ethni kai laoi emeletisan kena;
verses.translation: Who by the mouth of thy servant David hast said, Why did the heathen rage, and the people imagine vain things?

verses.original: παρέστησαν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ κατὰ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ κατὰ τοῦ χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: parestisan oi vasileis tes ges kai oi arhontes synihthisan epi to auto kata tou kyrioy kai kata tou hristou autou.
verses.translation: The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord, and against his Christ.

verses.original: συνήχθησαν γὰρ ἐπʼ ἀληθείας ⸂ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ⸃ ἐπὶ τὸν ἅγιον παῖδά σου Ἰησοῦν, ὃν ἔχρισας, Ἡρῴδης τε καὶ Πόντιος Πιλᾶτος σὺν ἔθνεσιν καὶ λαοῖς Ἰσραήλ,
verses.translit: synihthisan gar ep' alitheias en te polei tayte epi ton agion paida soy Iisoun, on ehrisas, Erodis te kai Pontios Pilatos sun ethnesin kai laois Israil,
verses.translation: For of a truth against thy holy child Jesus, whom thou hast anointed, both Herod, and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles, and the people of Israel, were gathered together,

verses.original: ποιῆσαι ὅσα ἡ χείρ σου καὶ ἡ ⸀βουλὴ προώρισεν γενέσθαι.
verses.translit: poiesai osa e heir soy kai e voyle proorisen genesthai.
verses.translation: For to do whatsoever thy hand and thy counsel determined before to be done.

verses.original: καὶ τὰ νῦν, κύριε, ἔπιδε ἐπὶ τὰς ἀπειλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ δὸς τοῖς δούλοις σου μετὰ παρρησίας πάσης λαλεῖν τὸν λόγον σου,
verses.translit: kai ta nun, kyrie, epide epi tas apeilas auton kai dos tois doylois soy meta parrisias pasis lalein ton logon soy,
verses.translation: And now, Lord, behold their threatenings: and grant unto thy servants, that with all boldness they may speak thy word,

verses.original: ἐν τῷ τὴν χεῖρά ⸀σου ἐκτείνειν σε εἰς ἴασιν καὶ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα γίνεσθαι διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ ἁγίου παιδός σου Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: en to ten heira soy ekteinein se eis iasin kai simeia kai terata ginesthai dia tou onomatos tou agioy paidos soy Iisou.
verses.translation: By stretching forth thine hand to heal; and that signs and wonders may be done by the name of thy holy child Jesus.

verses.original: καὶ δεηθέντων αὐτῶν ἐσαλεύθη ὁ τόπος ἐν ᾧ ἦσαν συνηγμένοι, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν ἅπαντες ⸂τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος⸃, καὶ ἐλάλουν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ μετὰ παρρησίας.
verses.translit: kai deithenton auton esaleythi o topos en o esan synigmenoi, kai eplisthisan apantes tou agioy pneymatos, kai elaloyn ton logon tou theou meta parrisias.
verses.translation: And when they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were assembled together; and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness.

verses.original: Τοῦ δὲ πλήθους τῶν πιστευσάντων ἦν ⸀καρδία καὶ ⸀ψυχὴ μία, καὶ οὐδὲ εἷς τι τῶν ὑπαρχόντων ⸀αὐτῷ ἔλεγεν ἴδιον εἶναι, ἀλλʼ ἦν αὐτοῖς ⸀πάντα κοινά.
verses.translit: Tou de plithoys ton pisteysanton en kardia kai psyhe mia, kai oude eis ti ton uparhonton auto elegen idion einai, all' en autois panta koina.
verses.translation: And the multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul: neither said any of them that ought of the things which he possessed was his own; but they had all things common.

verses.original: καὶ ⸂δυνάμει μεγάλῃ⸃ ἀπεδίδουν τὸ μαρτύριον οἱ ἀπόστολοι ⸂τῆς ἀναστάσεως τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ⸃, χάρις τε μεγάλη ἦν ἐπὶ πάντας αὐτούς.
verses.translit: kai dynamei megale apedidoyn to martyrion oi apostoloi tes anastaseos tou kyrioy Iisou, haris te megali en epi pantas autoys.
verses.translation: And with great power gave the apostles witness of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus: and great grace was upon them all.

verses.original: οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐνδεής τις ⸀ἦν ἐν αὐτοῖς· ὅσοι γὰρ κτήτορες χωρίων ἢ οἰκιῶν ὑπῆρχον, πωλοῦντες ἔφερον τὰς τιμὰς τῶν πιπρασκομένων
verses.translit: oude gar endeis tis en en autois* osoi gar ktitores horion e oikion uperhon, polountes eferon tas timas ton pipraskomenon
verses.translation: Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold,

verses.original: καὶ ἐτίθουν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων· διεδίδετο δὲ ἑκάστῳ καθότι ἄν τις χρείαν εἶχεν.
verses.translit: kai etithoyn para tous podas ton apostolon* diedideto de ekasto kathoti an tis hreian eihen.
verses.translation: And laid them down at the apostles’ feet: and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need.

verses.original: ⸀Ἰωσὴφ δὲ ὁ ἐπικληθεὶς Βαρναβᾶς ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων, ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον υἱὸς παρακλήσεως, Λευίτης, Κύπριος τῷ γένει,
verses.translit: Iosef de o epiklitheis Varnavas apo ton apostolon, o estin methermineyomenon yios parakliseos, Leyitis, Kyprios to genei,
verses.translation: And Joses, who by the apostles was surnamed Barnabas, (which is, being interpreted, The son of consolation,) a Levite, and of the country of Cyprus,

verses.original: ὑπάρχοντος αὐτῷ ἀγροῦ πωλήσας ἤνεγκεν τὸ χρῆμα καὶ ἔθηκεν ⸀παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων.
verses.translit: uparhontos auto agrou polisas enegken to hrema kai ethiken para tous podas ton apostolon.
verses.translation: Having land, sold it , and brought the money, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.

verses.original: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις Ἁνανίας ὀνόματι σὺν Σαπφίρῃ τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπώλησεν κτῆμα
verses.translit: Aner de tis Ananias onomati sun Sapfire te gynaiki autou epolisen ktema
verses.translation: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession,

verses.original: καὶ ἐνοσφίσατο ἀπὸ τῆς τιμῆς, συνειδυίης καὶ τῆς ⸀γυναικός, καὶ ἐνέγκας μέρος τι παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων ἔθηκεν.
verses.translit: kai enosfisato apo tes times, syneidyiis kai tes gynaikos, kai enegkas meros ti para tous podas ton apostolon ethiken.
verses.translation: And kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it , and brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ⸀ὁ Πέτρος· Ἁνανία, διὰ τί ἐπλήρωσεν ὁ Σατανᾶς τὴν καρδίαν σου, ψεύσασθαί σε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καὶ ⸀νοσφίσασθαι ἀπὸ τῆς τιμῆς τοῦ χωρίου;
verses.translit: eipen de o Petros* Anania, dia ti eplirosen o Satanas ten kardian soy, pseysasthai se to pneuma to agion kai nosfisasthai apo tes times tou horioy;
verses.translation: But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land?

verses.original: οὐχὶ μένον σοὶ ἔμενεν καὶ πραθὲν ἐν τῇ σῇ ἐξουσίᾳ ὑπῆρχεν; τί ὅτι ἔθου ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου τὸ πρᾶγμα τοῦτο; οὐκ ἐψεύσω ἀνθρώποις ἀλλὰ τῷ θεῷ.
verses.translit: ouhi menon soi emenen kai prathen en te se exoysia uperhen; ti oti ethoy en te kardia soy to pragma touto; ouk epseyso anthropois alla to theo.
verses.translation: Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power? why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.

verses.original: ἀκούων δὲ ὁ Ἁνανίας τοὺς λόγους τούτους πεσὼν ἐξέψυξεν· καὶ ἐγένετο φόβος μέγας ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ⸀ἀκούοντας.
verses.translit: akoyon de o Ananias tous logoys toytoys peson exepsyxen* kai egeneto fovos megas epi pantas tous akoyontas.
verses.translation: And Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost: and great fear came on all them that heard these things.

verses.original: ἀναστάντες δὲ οἱ νεώτεροι συνέστειλαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐξενέγκαντες ἔθαψαν.
verses.translit: anastantes de oi neoteroi synesteilan auton kai exenegkantes ethapsan.
verses.translation: And the young men arose, wound him up, and carried him out, and buried him .

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ὡς ὡρῶν τριῶν διάστημα καὶ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ μὴ εἰδυῖα τὸ γεγονὸς εἰσῆλθεν.
verses.translit: Egeneto de os oron trion diastima kai e gyne autou me eidyia to gegonos eiselthen.
verses.translation: And it was about the space of three hours after, when his wife, not knowing what was done, came in.

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ ⸂πρὸς αὐτὴν⸃ ⸀Πέτρος· Εἰπέ μοι, εἰ τοσούτου τὸ χωρίον ἀπέδοσθε; ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· Ναί, τοσούτου.
verses.translit: apekrithi de pros auten Petros* Eipe moi, ei tosoytoy to horion apedosthe; e de eipen* Nai, tosoytoy.
verses.translation: And Peter answered unto her, Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much? And she said, Yea, for so much.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ⸀Πέτρος πρὸς αὐτήν· Τί ὅτι συνεφωνήθη ὑμῖν πειράσαι τὸ πνεῦμα κυρίου; ἰδοὺ οἱ πόδες τῶν θαψάντων τὸν ἄνδρα σου ἐπὶ τῇ θύρᾳ καὶ ἐξοίσουσίν σε.
verses.translit: o de Petros pros autin* Ti oti synefonithi umin peirasai to pneuma kyrioy; idou oi podes ton thapsanton ton andra soy epi te thyra kai exoisoysin se.
verses.translation: Then Peter said unto her, How is it that ye have agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? behold, the feet of them which have buried thy husband are at the door, and shall carry thee out.

verses.original: ἔπεσεν δὲ παραχρῆμα ⸀πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξέψυξεν· εἰσελθόντες δὲ οἱ νεανίσκοι εὗρον αὐτὴν νεκράν, καὶ ἐξενέγκαντες ἔθαψαν πρὸς τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς.
verses.translit: epesen de parahrema pros tous podas autou kai exepsyxen* eiselthontes de oi neaniskoi euron auten nekran, kai exenegkantes ethapsan pros ton andra autes.
verses.translation: Then fell she down straightway at his feet, and yielded up the ghost: and the young men came in, and found her dead, and, carrying her forth, buried her by her husband.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο φόβος μέγας ἐφʼ ὅλην τὴν ἐκκλησίαν καὶ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας ταῦτα.
verses.translit: kai egeneto fovos megas ef' olin ten ekklisian kai epi pantas tous akoyontas tauta.
verses.translation: And great fear came upon all the church, and upon as many as heard these things.

verses.original: Διὰ δὲ τῶν χειρῶν τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐγίνετο σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ⸂πολλὰ ἐν τῷ λαῷ⸃· καὶ ἦσαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν ⸀ἅπαντες ἐν τῇ Στοᾷ Σολομῶντος·
verses.translit: Dia de ton heiron ton apostolon egineto simeia kai terata polla en to lao* kai esan omothymadon apantes en te Stoa Solomontos*
verses.translation: And by the hands of the apostles were many signs and wonders wrought among the people; (and they were all with one accord in Solomon’s porch.

verses.original: τῶν δὲ λοιπῶν οὐδεὶς ἐτόλμα κολλᾶσθαι αὐτοῖς, ἀλλʼ ἐμεγάλυνεν αὐτοὺς ὁ λαός,
verses.translit: ton de loipon oudeis etolma kollasthai autois, all' emegalynen autous o laos,
verses.translation: And of the rest durst no man join himself to them: but the people magnified them.

verses.original: μᾶλλον δὲ προσετίθεντο πιστεύοντες τῷ κυρίῳ πλήθη ἀνδρῶν τε καὶ γυναικῶν·
verses.translit: mallon de prosetithento pisteyontes to kyrio plithi andron te kai gynaikon*
verses.translation: And believers were the more added to the Lord, multitudes both of men and women.)

verses.original: ὥστε ⸂καὶ εἰς⸃ τὰς πλατείας ἐκφέρειν τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς καὶ τιθέναι ἐπὶ ⸀κλιναρίων καὶ κραβάττων, ἵνα ἐρχομένου Πέτρου κἂν ἡ σκιὰ ⸀ἐπισκιάσῃ τινὶ αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: oste kai eis tas plateias ekferein tous astheneis kai tithenai epi klinarion kai kravatton, ina erhomenoy Petroy kan e skia episkiase tini auton.
verses.translation: Insomuch that they brought forth the sick into the streets, and laid them on beds and couches, that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them.

verses.original: συνήρχετο δὲ καὶ τὸ πλῆθος τῶν πέριξ ⸀πόλεων Ἰερουσαλήμ, φέροντες ἀσθενεῖς καὶ ὀχλουμένους ὑπὸ πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων, οἵτινες ἐθεραπεύοντο ἅπαντες.
verses.translit: synirheto de kai to plethos ton perix poleon Ieroysalim, ferontes astheneis kai ohloymenoys upo pneymaton akatharton, oitines etherapeyonto apantes.
verses.translation: There came also a multitude out of the cities round about unto Jerusalem, bringing sick folks, and them which were vexed with unclean spirits: and they were healed every one.

verses.original: Ἀναστὰς δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ πάντες οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ, ἡ οὖσα αἵρεσις τῶν Σαδδουκαίων, ἐπλήσθησαν ζήλου
verses.translit: Anastas de o arhiereus kai pantes oi sun auto, e ousa airesis ton Saddoykaion, eplisthisan ziloy
verses.translation: Then the high priest rose up, and all they that were with him, (which is the sect of the Sadducees,) and were filled with indignation,

verses.original: καὶ ἐπέβαλον τὰς ⸀χεῖρας ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀποστόλους καὶ ἔθεντο αὐτοὺς ἐν τηρήσει δημοσίᾳ.
verses.translit: kai epevalon tas heiras epi tous apostoloys kai ethento autous en tirisei dimosia.
verses.translation: And laid their hands on the apostles, and put them in the common prison.

verses.original: ἄγγελος δὲ κυρίου ⸀διὰ νυκτὸς ⸀ἤνοιξε τὰς θύρας τῆς φυλακῆς ἐξαγαγών τε αὐτοὺς εἶπεν·
verses.translit: aggelos de kyrioy dia nyktos enoixe tas thyras tes fylakes exagagon te autous eipen*
verses.translation: But the angel of the Lord by night opened the prison doors, and brought them forth, and said,

verses.original: Πορεύεσθε καὶ σταθέντες λαλεῖτε ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τῷ λαῷ πάντα τὰ ῥήματα τῆς ζωῆς ταύτης.
verses.translit: Poreyesthe kai stathentes laleite en to iero to lao panta ta Rimata tes zoes taytis.
verses.translation: Go, stand and speak in the temple to the people all the words of this life.

verses.original: ἀκούσαντες δὲ εἰσῆλθον ὑπὸ τὸν ὄρθρον εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ ἐδίδασκον. Παραγενόμενος δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ συνεκάλεσαν τὸ συνέδριον καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γερουσίαν τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ, καὶ ἀπέστειλαν εἰς τὸ δεσμωτήριον ἀχθῆναι αὐτούς.
verses.translit: akoysantes de eiselthon upo ton orthron eis to ieron kai edidaskon. Paragenomenos de o arhiereus kai oi sun auto synekalesan to synedrion kai pasan ten geroysian ton yion Israil, kai apesteilan eis to desmotirion ahthenai autoys.
verses.translation: And when they heard that , they entered into the temple early in the morning, and taught. But the high priest came, and they that were with him, and called the council together, and all the senate of the children of Israel, and sent to the prison to have them brought.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ⸂παραγενόμενοι ὑπηρέται⸃ οὐχ εὗρον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ, ἀναστρέψαντες δὲ ἀπήγγειλαν
verses.translit: oi de paragenomenoi upiretai ouh euron autous en te fylake, anastrepsantes de apiggeilan
verses.translation: But when the officers came, and found them not in the prison, they returned, and told,

verses.original: λέγοντες ὅτι ⸀Τὸ δεσμωτήριον εὕρομεν κεκλεισμένον ἐν πάσῃ ἀσφαλείᾳ καὶ τοὺς φύλακας ἑστῶτας ⸀ἐπὶ τῶν θυρῶν, ἀνοίξαντες δὲ ἔσω οὐδένα εὕρομεν.
verses.translit: legontes oti To desmotirion euromen kekleismenon en pase asfaleia kai tous fylakas estotas epi ton thyron, anoixantes de eso oudena euromen.
verses.translation: Saying, The prison truly found we shut with all safety, and the keepers standing without before the doors: but when we had opened, we found no man within.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἤκουσαν τοὺς λόγους τούτους ὅ ⸀τε στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς, διηπόρουν περὶ αὐτῶν τί ἂν γένοιτο τοῦτο.
verses.translit: os de ekoysan tous logoys toytoys o te stratigos tou ierou kai oi arhiereis, diiporoyn peri auton ti an genoito touto.
verses.translation: Now when the high priest and the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these things, they doubted of them whereunto this would grow.

verses.original: παραγενόμενος δέ τις ἀπήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ἰδοὺ οἱ ἄνδρες οὓς ἔθεσθε ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ εἰσὶν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἑστῶτες καὶ διδάσκοντες τὸν λαόν.
verses.translit: paragenomenos de tis apiggeilen autois oti Idou oi andres ous ethesthe en te fylake eisin en to iero estotes kai didaskontes ton laon.
verses.translation: Then came one and told them, saying, Behold, the men whom ye put in prison are standing in the temple, and teaching the people.

verses.original: τότε ἀπελθὼν ὁ στρατηγὸς σὺν τοῖς ὑπηρέταις ⸀ἤγαγεν αὐτούς, οὐ μετὰ βίας, ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ τὸν λαόν, ⸀μὴ λιθασθῶσιν.
verses.translit: tote apelthon o stratigos sun tois upiretais egagen autoys, ou meta vias, efovounto gar ton laon, me lithasthosin.
verses.translation: Then went the captain with the officers, and brought them without violence: for they feared the people, lest they should have been stoned.

verses.original: Ἀγαγόντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔστησαν ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ. καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς
verses.translit: Agagontes de autous estisan en to synedrio. kai epirotisen autous o arhiereus
verses.translation: And when they had brought them, they set them before the council: and the high priest asked them,

verses.original: ⸀λέγων· Παραγγελίᾳ παρηγγείλαμεν ὑμῖν μὴ διδάσκειν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πεπληρώκατε τὴν Ἰερουσαλὴμ τῆς διδαχῆς ὑμῶν, καὶ βούλεσθε ἐπαγαγεῖν ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς τὸ αἷμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τούτου.
verses.translit: legon* Paraggelia pariggeilamen umin me didaskein epi to onomati toyto, kai idou peplirokate ten Ieroysalem tes didahes umon, kai voylesthe epagagein ef' emas to aima tou anthropoy toytoy.
verses.translation: Saying, Did not we straitly command you that ye should not teach in this name? and, behold, ye have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine, and intend to bring this man’s blood upon us.

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Πέτρος καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι εἶπαν· Πειθαρχεῖν δεῖ θεῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ἀνθρώποις.
verses.translit: apokritheis de Petros kai oi apostoloi eipan* Peitharhein dei theo mallon e anthropois.
verses.translation: Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.

verses.original: ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν ἤγειρεν Ἰησοῦν, ὃν ὑμεῖς διεχειρίσασθε κρεμάσαντες ἐπὶ ξύλου·
verses.translit: o theos ton pateron emon egeiren Iisoun, on umeis dieheirisasthe kremasantes epi xyloy*
verses.translation: The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.

verses.original: τοῦτον ὁ θεὸς ἀρχηγὸν καὶ σωτῆρα ὕψωσεν τῇ δεξιᾷ αὐτοῦ, ⸀τοῦ δοῦναι μετάνοιαν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν·
verses.translit: touton o theos arhigon kai sotera upsosen te dexia autou, tou dounai metanoian to Israel kai afesin amartion*
verses.translation: Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.

verses.original: καὶ ἡμεῖς ⸀ἐσμεν μάρτυρες τῶν ῥημάτων τούτων, καὶ τὸ ⸀πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ὃ ἔδωκεν ὁ θεὸς τοῖς πειθαρχοῦσιν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: kai emeis esmen martyres ton Rimaton toyton, kai to pneuma to agion o edoken o theos tois peitharhousin auto.
verses.translation: And we are his witnesses of these things; and so is also the Holy Ghost, whom God hath given to them that obey him.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ ⸀ἀκούσαντες διεπρίοντο καὶ ἐβούλοντο ἀνελεῖν αὐτούς.
verses.translit: Oi de akoysantes dieprionto kai evoylonto anelein autoys.
verses.translation: When they heard that , they were cut to the heart , and took counsel to slay them.

verses.original: ἀναστὰς δέ τις ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ Φαρισαῖος ὀνόματι Γαμαλιήλ, νομοδιδάσκαλος τίμιος παντὶ τῷ λαῷ, ἐκέλευσεν ἔξω ⸀βραχὺ τοὺς ⸀ἀνθρώπους ποιῆσαι,
verses.translit: anastas de tis en to synedrio Farisaios onomati Gamaliil, nomodidaskalos timios panti to lao, ekeleysen exo vrahu tous anthropoys poiesai,
verses.translation: Then stood there up one in the council, a Pharisee, named Gamaliel, a doctor of the law, had in reputation among all the people, and commanded to put the apostles forth a little space;

verses.original: εἶπέν τε πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται, προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τούτοις τί μέλλετε πράσσειν.
verses.translit: eipen te pros autoys* Andres Israilitai, prosehete eaytois epi tois anthropois toytois ti mellete prassein.
verses.translation: And said unto them, Ye men of Israel, take heed to yourselves what ye intend to do as touching these men.

verses.original: πρὸ γὰρ τούτων τῶν ἡμερῶν ἀνέστη Θευδᾶς, λέγων εἶναί τινα ἑαυτόν, ᾧ ⸀προσεκλίθη ⸂ἀνδρῶν ἀριθμὸς ὡς⸃ τετρακοσίων· ὃς ἀνῃρέθη, καὶ πάντες ὅσοι ἐπείθοντο αὐτῷ διελύθησαν καὶ ἐγένοντο εἰς οὐδέν.
verses.translit: pro gar toyton ton emeron anesti Theydas, legon einai tina eayton, o proseklithi andron arithmos os tetrakosion* os anerethi, kai pantes osoi epeithonto auto dielythisan kai egenonto eis ouden.
verses.translation: For before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves: who was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought.

verses.original: μετὰ τοῦτον ἀνέστη Ἰούδας ὁ Γαλιλαῖος ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς ἀπογραφῆς καὶ ἀπέστησε ⸀λαὸν ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ· κἀκεῖνος ἀπώλετο καὶ πάντες ὅσοι ἐπείθοντο αὐτῷ διεσκορπίσθησαν.
verses.translit: meta touton anesti Ioydas o Galilaios en tais emerais tes apografes kai apestise laon opiso autou* kakeinos apoleto kai pantes osoi epeithonto auto dieskorpisthisan.
verses.translation: After this man rose up Judas of Galilee in the days of the taxing, and drew away much people after him: he also perished; and all, even as many as obeyed him, were dispersed.

verses.original: καὶ τὰ νῦν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπόστητε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων τούτων καὶ ⸀ἄφετε αὐτούς· (ὅτι ἐὰν ᾖ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἡ βουλὴ ⸀αὕτη ἢ τὸ ἔργον τοῦτο, καταλυθήσεται,
verses.translit: kai ta nun lego umin, apostite apo ton anthropon toyton kai afete autoys* (oti ean e ex anthropon e voyle auti e to ergon touto, katalythisetai,
verses.translation: And now I say unto you, Refrain from these men, and let them alone: for if this counsel or this work be of men, it will come to nought:

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ἐκ θεοῦ ἐστιν, οὐ ⸀δυνήσεσθε καταλῦσαι ⸀αὐτούς·) μήποτε καὶ θεομάχοι εὑρεθῆτε. ἐπείσθησαν δὲ αὐτῷ,
verses.translit: ei de ek theou estin, ou dynisesthe katalusai autoys*) mipote kai theomahoi eurethete. epeisthisan de auto,
verses.translation: But if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it; lest haply ye be found even to fight against God.

verses.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενοι τοὺς ἀποστόλους δείραντες παρήγγειλαν μὴ λαλεῖν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ⸀ἀπέλυσαν.
verses.translit: kai proskalesamenoi tous apostoloys deirantes pariggeilan me lalein epi to onomati tou Iisou kai apelysan.
verses.translation: And to him they agreed: and when they had called the apostles, and beaten them , they commanded that they should not speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.

verses.original: οἱ μὲν οὖν ἐπορεύοντο χαίροντες ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ συνεδρίου ὅτι ⸂κατηξιώθησαν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος⸃ ἀτιμασθῆναι·
verses.translit: oi men oun eporeyonto hairontes apo prosopoy tou synedrioy oti katixiothisan uper tou onomatos atimasthenai*
verses.translation: And they departed from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for his name.

verses.original: πᾶσάν τε ἡμέραν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ κατʼ οἶκον οὐκ ἐπαύοντο διδάσκοντες καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ⸂τὸν χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν⸃.
verses.translit: pasan te emeran en to iero kai kat' oikon ouk epayonto didaskontes kai euaggelizomenoi ton hriston Iisoun.
verses.translation: And daily in the temple, and in every house, they ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ.

verses.original: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις πληθυνόντων τῶν μαθητῶν ἐγένετο γογγυσμὸς τῶν Ἑλληνιστῶν πρὸς τοὺς Ἑβραίους ὅτι παρεθεωροῦντο ἐν τῇ διακονίᾳ τῇ καθημερινῇ αἱ χῆραι αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: En de tais emerais taytais plithynonton ton mathiton egeneto goggysmos ton Elliniston pros tous Evraioys oti paretheorounto en te diakonia te kathimerine ai herai auton.
verses.translation: And in those days, when the number of the disciples was multiplied, there arose a murmuring of the Grecians against the Hebrews, because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration.

verses.original: προσκαλεσάμενοι δὲ οἱ δώδεκα τὸ πλῆθος τῶν μαθητῶν εἶπαν· Οὐκ ἀρεστόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς καταλείψαντας τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ διακονεῖν τραπέζαις·
verses.translit: proskalesamenoi de oi dodeka to plethos ton mathiton eipan* Ouk areston estin emas kataleipsantas ton logon tou theou diakonein trapezais*
verses.translation: Then the twelve called the multitude of the disciples unto them , and said, It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables.

verses.original: ἐπισκέψασθε ⸀δέ, ἀδελφοί, ἄνδρας ἐξ ὑμῶν μαρτυρουμένους ἑπτὰ πλήρεις ⸀πνεύματος καὶ σοφίας, οὓς ⸀καταστήσομεν ἐπὶ τῆς χρείας ταύτης·
verses.translit: episkepsasthe de, adelfoi, andras ex umon martyroymenoys epta plireis pneymatos kai sofias, ous katastisomen epi tes hreias taytis*
verses.translation: Wherefore, brethren, look ye out among you seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.

verses.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ τῇ διακονίᾳ τοῦ λόγου προσκαρτερήσομεν.
verses.translit: emeis de te proseyhe kai te diakonia tou logoy proskarterisomen.
verses.translation: But we will give ourselves continually to prayer, and to the ministry of the word.

verses.original: καὶ ἤρεσεν ὁ λόγος ἐνώπιον παντὸς τοῦ πλήθους, καὶ ἐξελέξαντο Στέφανον, ἄνδρα ⸀πλήρης πίστεως καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου, καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Πρόχορον καὶ Νικάνορα καὶ Τίμωνα καὶ Παρμενᾶν καὶ Νικόλαον προσήλυτον Ἀντιοχέα,
verses.translit: kai eresen o logos enopion pantos tou plithoys, kai exelexanto Stefanon, andra pliris pisteos kai pneymatos agioy, kai Filippon kai Prohoron kai Nikanora kai Timona kai Parmenan kai Nikolaon prosilyton Antiohea,
verses.translation: And the saying pleased the whole multitude: and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolas a proselyte of Antioch:

verses.original: οὓς ἔστησαν ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀποστόλων, καὶ προσευξάμενοι ἐπέθηκαν αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας.
verses.translit: ous estisan enopion ton apostolon, kai proseyxamenoi epethikan autois tas heiras.
verses.translation: Whom they set before the apostles: and when they had prayed, they laid their hands on them.

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ηὔξανεν, καὶ ἐπληθύνετο ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν μαθητῶν ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ σφόδρα, πολύς τε ὄχλος τῶν ἱερέων ὑπήκουον τῇ πίστει.
verses.translit: Kai o logos tou theou iuxanen, kai eplithyneto o arithmos ton mathiton en Ieroysalem sfodra, polys te ohlos ton iereon upikoyon te pistei.
verses.translation: And the word of God increased; and the number of the disciples multiplied in Jerusalem greatly; and a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.

verses.original: Στέφανος δὲ πλήρης ⸀χάριτος καὶ δυνάμεως ἐποίει τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα μεγάλα ἐν τῷ λαῷ.
verses.translit: Stefanos de pliris haritos kai dynameos epoiei terata kai simeia megala en to lao.
verses.translation: And Stephen, full of faith and power, did great wonders and miracles among the people.

verses.original: ἀνέστησαν δέ τινες τῶν ἐκ τῆς συναγωγῆς τῆς λεγομένης Λιβερτίνων καὶ Κυρηναίων καὶ Ἀλεξανδρέων καὶ τῶν ἀπὸ Κιλικίας καὶ Ἀσίας συζητοῦντες τῷ Στεφάνῳ,
verses.translit: anestisan de tines ton ek tes synagoges tes legomenis Livertinon kai Kyrinaion kai Alexandreon kai ton apo Kilikias kai Asias syzitountes to Stefano,
verses.translation: Then there arose certain of the synagogue, which is called the synagogue of the Libertines, and Cyrenians, and Alexandrians, and of them of Cilicia and of Asia, disputing with Stephen.

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυον ἀντιστῆναι τῇ σοφίᾳ καὶ τῷ πνεύματι ᾧ ἐλάλει.
verses.translit: kai ouk ishyon antistenai te sofia kai to pneymati o elalei.
verses.translation: And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the spirit by which he spake.

verses.original: τότε ὑπέβαλον ἄνδρας λέγοντας ὅτι Ἀκηκόαμεν αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ῥήματα βλάσφημα εἰς Μωϋσῆν καὶ τὸν θεόν·
verses.translit: tote upevalon andras legontas oti Akikoamen autou lalountos Rimata vlasfima eis Moysen kai ton theon*
verses.translation: Then they suborned men, which said, We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses, and against God.

verses.original: συνεκίνησάν τε τὸν λαὸν καὶ τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους καὶ τοὺς γραμματεῖς, καὶ ἐπιστάντες συνήρπασαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἤγαγον εἰς τὸ συνέδριον,
verses.translit: synekinisan te ton laon kai tous presvyteroys kai tous grammateis, kai epistantes synirpasan auton kai egagon eis to synedrion,
verses.translation: And they stirred up the people, and the elders, and the scribes, and came upon him , and caught him, and brought him to the council,

verses.original: ἔστησάν τε μάρτυρας ψευδεῖς λέγοντας· Ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος οὐ παύεται ⸂λαλῶν ῥήματα⸃ κατὰ τοῦ τόπου τοῦ ⸀ἁγίου καὶ τοῦ νόμου,
verses.translit: estisan te martyras pseydeis legontas* O anthropos outos ou payetai lalon Rimata kata tou topoy tou agioy kai tou nomoy,
verses.translation: And set up false witnesses, which said, This man ceaseth not to speak blasphemous words against this holy place, and the law:

verses.original: ἀκηκόαμεν γὰρ αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος οὗτος καταλύσει τὸν τόπον τοῦτον καὶ ἀλλάξει τὰ ἔθη ἃ παρέδωκεν ἡμῖν Μωϋσῆς.
verses.translit: akikoamen gar autou legontos oti Iisous o Nazoraios outos katalysei ton topon touton kai allaxei ta ethi a paredoken emin Moyses.
verses.translation: For we have heard him say, that this Jesus of Nazareth shall destroy this place, and shall change the customs which Moses delivered us.

verses.original: καὶ ἀτενίσαντες εἰς αὐτὸν ⸀πάντες οἱ καθεζόμενοι ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ εἶδον τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ πρόσωπον ἀγγέλου.
verses.translit: kai atenisantes eis auton pantes oi kathezomenoi en to synedrio eidon to prosopon autou osei prosopon aggeloy.
verses.translation: And all that sat in the council, looking stedfastly on him, saw his face as it had been the face of an angel.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεύς· ⸀Εἰ ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχει;
verses.translit: Eipen de o arhiereys* Ei tauta outos ehei;
verses.translation: Then said the high priest, Are these things so?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες, ἀκούσατε· Ὁ θεὸς τῆς δόξης ὤφθη τῷ πατρὶ ἡμῶν Ἀβραὰμ ὄντι ἐν τῇ Μεσοποταμίᾳ πρὶν ἢ κατοικῆσαι αὐτὸν ἐν Χαρράν,
verses.translit: o de efi* Andres adelfoi kai pateres, akoysate* O theos tes doxis ofthi to patri emon Avraam onti en te Mesopotamia prin e katoikesai auton en Harran,
verses.translation: And he said, Men, brethren, and fathers, hearken; The God of glory appeared unto our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran,

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἔξελθε ἐκ τῆς γῆς σου καὶ ⸀ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας σου, καὶ δεῦρο εἰς ⸀τὴν γῆν ἣν ἄν σοι δείξω.
verses.translit: kai eipen pros auton* Exelthe ek tes ges soy kai ek tes syggeneias soy, kai deuro eis ten gen en an soi deixo.
verses.translation: And said unto him, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and come into the land which I shall shew thee.

verses.original: τότε ἐξελθὼν ἐκ γῆς Χαλδαίων κατῴκησεν ἐν Χαρράν. κἀκεῖθεν μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ μετῴκισεν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν γῆν ταύτην εἰς ἣν ὑμεῖς νῦν κατοικεῖτε,
verses.translit: tote exelthon ek ges Haldaion katokisen en Harran. kakeithen meta to apothanein ton patera autou metokisen auton eis ten gen taytin eis en umeis nun katoikeite,
verses.translation: Then came he out of the land of the Chaldæans, and dwelt in Charran: and from thence, when his father was dead, he removed him into this land, wherein ye now dwell.

verses.original: καὶ οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ κληρονομίαν ἐν αὐτῇ οὐδὲ βῆμα ποδός, καὶ ἐπηγγείλατο δοῦναι αὐτῷ εἰς κατάσχεσιν αὐτὴν καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ μετʼ αὐτόν, οὐκ ὄντος αὐτῷ τέκνου.
verses.translit: kai ouk edoken auto klironomian en aute oude vema podos, kai epiggeilato dounai auto eis katashesin auten kai to spermati autou met' auton, ouk ontos auto teknoy.
verses.translation: And he gave him none inheritance in it, no, not so much as to set his foot on: yet he promised that he would give it to him for a possession, and to his seed after him, when as yet he had no child.

verses.original: ἐλάλησεν ⸀δὲ οὕτως ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ πάροικον ἐν γῇ ἀλλοτρίᾳ, καὶ δουλώσουσιν αὐτὸ καὶ κακώσουσιν ἔτη τετρακόσια·
verses.translit: elalisen de outos o theos oti estai to sperma autou paroikon en ge allotria, kai doylosoysin auto kai kakosoysin eti tetrakosia*
verses.translation: And God spake on this wise, That his seed should sojourn in a strange land; and that they should bring them into bondage, and entreat them evil four hundred years.

verses.original: καὶ τὸ ἔθνος ᾧ ⸀ἐὰν ⸀δουλεύσουσιν κρινῶ ἐγώ, ⸂ὁ θεὸς εἶπεν⸃, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξελεύσονται καὶ λατρεύσουσίν μοι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ τούτῳ.
verses.translit: kai to ethnos o ean doyleysoysin krino ego, o theos eipen, kai meta tauta exeleysontai kai latreysoysin moi en to topo toyto.
verses.translation: And the nation to whom they shall be in bondage will I judge, said God: and after that shall they come forth, and serve me in this place.

verses.original: καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ διαθήκην περιτομῆς· καὶ οὕτως ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ, ⸀καὶ Ἰσαὰκ τὸν Ἰακώβ, ⸁καὶ Ἰακὼβ τοὺς δώδεκα πατριάρχας.
verses.translit: kai edoken auto diathikin peritomes* kai outos egennisen ton Isaak kai perietemen auton te emera te ogdoe, kai Isaak ton Iakov, kai Iakov tous dodeka patriarhas.
verses.translation: And he gave him the covenant of circumcision: and so Abraham begat Isaac, and circumcised him the eighth day; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat the twelve patriarchs.

verses.original: Καὶ οἱ πατριάρχαι ζηλώσαντες τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἀπέδοντο εἰς Αἴγυπτον· καὶ ἦν ὁ θεὸς μετʼ αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: Kai oi patriarhai zilosantes ton Iosef apedonto eis Aigypton* kai en o theos met' autou,
verses.translation: And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but God was with him,

verses.original: καὶ ἐξείλατο αὐτὸν ἐκ πασῶν τῶν θλίψεων αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ χάριν καὶ σοφίαν ἐναντίον Φαραὼ βασιλέως Αἰγύπτου, καὶ κατέστησεν αὐτὸν ἡγούμενον ἐπʼ Αἴγυπτον ⸀καὶ ὅλον τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai exeilato auton ek pason ton thlipseon autou, kai edoken auto harin kai sofian enantion Farao vasileos Aigyptoy, kai katestisen auton egoymenon ep' Aigypton kai olon ton oikon autou.
verses.translation: And delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favour and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he made him governor over Egypt and all his house.

verses.original: ἦλθεν δὲ λιμὸς ἐφʼ ὅλην τὴν ⸀Αἴγυπτον καὶ Χανάαν καὶ θλῖψις μεγάλη, καὶ οὐχ ηὕρισκον χορτάσματα οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν·
verses.translit: elthen de limos ef' olin ten Aigypton kai Hanaan kai thlipsis megali, kai ouh iuriskon hortasmata oi pateres emon*
verses.translation: Now there came a dearth over all the land of Egypt and Chanaan, and great affliction: and our fathers found no sustenance.

verses.original: ἀκούσας δὲ Ἰακὼβ ὄντα ⸂σιτία εἰς Αἴγυπτον⸃ ἐξαπέστειλεν τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν πρῶτον·
verses.translit: akoysas de Iakov onta sitia eis Aigypton exapesteilen tous pateras emon proton*
verses.translation: But when Jacob heard that there was corn in Egypt, he sent out our fathers first.

verses.original: καὶ ἐν τῷ δευτέρῳ ⸀ἀνεγνωρίσθη Ἰωσὴφ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ, καὶ φανερὸν ἐγένετο τῷ Φαραὼ τὸ ⸀γένος Ἰωσήφ.
verses.translit: kai en to deytero anegnoristhi Iosef tois adelfois autou, kai faneron egeneto to Farao to genos Iosif.
verses.translation: And at the second time Joseph was made known to his brethren; and Joseph’s kindred was made known unto Pharaoh.

verses.original: ἀποστείλας δὲ Ἰωσὴφ μετεκαλέσατο ⸂Ἰακὼβ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ⸃ καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν συγγένειαν ἐν ψυχαῖς ἑβδομήκοντα πέντε,
verses.translit: aposteilas de Iosef metekalesato Iakov ton patera autou kai pasan ten syggeneian en psyhais evdomikonta pente,
verses.translation: Then sent Joseph, and called his father Jacob to him , and all his kindred, threescore and fifteen souls.

verses.original: ⸂καὶ κατέβη⸃ Ἰακὼβ εἰς Αἴγυπτον. καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν,
verses.translit: kai katevi Iakov eis Aigypton. kai eteleytisen autos kai oi pateres emon,
verses.translation: So Jacob went down into Egypt, and died, he, and our fathers,

verses.original: καὶ μετετέθησαν εἰς Συχὲμ καὶ ἐτέθησαν ἐν τῷ μνήματι ⸀ᾧ ὠνήσατο Ἀβραὰμ τιμῆς ἀργυρίου παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἑμμὼρ ⸀ἐν Συχέμ.
verses.translit: kai metetethisan eis Syhem kai etethisan en to mnimati o onisato Avraam times argyrioy para ton yion Emmor en Syhem.
verses.translation: And were carried over into Sychem, and laid in the sepulchre that Abraham bought for a sum of money of the sons of Emmor the father of Sychem.

verses.original: Καθὼς δὲ ἤγγιζεν ὁ χρόνος τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ἧς ⸀ὡμολόγησεν ὁ θεὸς τῷ Ἀβραάμ, ηὔξησεν ὁ λαὸς καὶ ἐπληθύνθη ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ,
verses.translit: Kathos de eggizen o hronos tes epaggelias es omologisen o theos to Avraam, iuxisen o laos kai eplithynthi en Aigypto,
verses.translation: But when the time of the promise drew nigh, which God had sworn to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,

verses.original: ἄχρι οὗ ἀνέστη βασιλεὺς ἕτερος ⸂ἐπʼ Αἴγυπτον⸃, ὃς οὐκ ᾔδει τὸν Ἰωσήφ.
verses.translit: ahri ou anesti vasileus eteros ep' Aigypton, os ouk edei ton Iosif.
verses.translation: Till another king arose, which knew not Joseph.

verses.original: οὗτος κατασοφισάμενος τὸ γένος ἡμῶν ἐκάκωσεν τοὺς ⸀πατέρας τοῦ ποιεῖν ⸂τὰ βρέφη ἔκθετα⸃ αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ μὴ ζῳογονεῖσθαι.
verses.translit: outos katasofisamenos to genos emon ekakosen tous pateras tou poiein ta vrefi ektheta auton eis to me zoogoneisthai.
verses.translation: The same dealt subtilly with our kindred, and evil entreated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children, to the end they might not live.

verses.original: ἐν ᾧ καιρῷ ἐγεννήθη Μωϋσῆς, καὶ ἦν ἀστεῖος τῷ θεῷ· ὃς ἀνετράφη μῆνας τρεῖς ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ τοῦ πατρός·
verses.translit: en o kairo egennithi Moyses, kai en asteios to theo* os anetrafi menas treis en to oiko tou patros*
verses.translation: In which time Moses was born, and was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months:

verses.original: ⸂ἐκτεθέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀνείλατο αὐτὸν⸃ ἡ θυγάτηρ Φαραὼ καὶ ἀνεθρέψατο αὐτὸν ἑαυτῇ εἰς υἱόν.
verses.translit: ektethentos de autou aneilato auton e thygatir Farao kai anethrepsato auton eayte eis yion.
verses.translation: And when he was cast out, Pharaoh’s daughter took him up, and nourished him for her own son.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπαιδεύθη ⸀Μωϋσῆς πάσῃ σοφίᾳ Αἰγυπτίων, ἦν δὲ δυνατὸς ἐν λόγοις καὶ ἔργοις ⸀αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai epaideythi Moyses pase sofia Aigyption, en de dynatos en logois kai ergois autou.
verses.translation: And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦτο αὐτῷ τεσσερακονταετὴς χρόνος, ἀνέβη ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ ἐπισκέψασθαι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραήλ.
verses.translit: Os de eplirouto auto tesserakontaetes hronos, anevi epi ten kardian autou episkepsasthai tous adelfous autou tous yious Israil.
verses.translation: And when he was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδών τινα ἀδικούμενον ἠμύνατο καὶ ἐποίησεν ἐκδίκησιν τῷ καταπονουμένῳ πατάξας τὸν Αἰγύπτιον.
verses.translit: kai idon tina adikoymenon emynato kai epoiisen ekdikisin to kataponoymeno pataxas ton Aigyption.
verses.translation: And seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him , and avenged him that was oppressed, and smote the Egyptian:

verses.original: ἐνόμιζεν δὲ συνιέναι τοὺς ⸀ἀδελφοὺς ὅτι ὁ θεὸς διὰ χειρὸς αὐτοῦ δίδωσιν ⸂σωτηρίαν αὐτοῖς⸃, οἱ δὲ οὐ συνῆκαν.
verses.translit: enomizen de synienai tous adelfous oti o theos dia heiros autou didosin sotirian autois, oi de ou synekan.
verses.translation: For he supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not.

verses.original: τῇ τε ἐπιούσῃ ἡμέρᾳ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς μαχομένοις καὶ ⸀συνήλλασσεν αὐτοὺς εἰς εἰρήνην εἰπών· Ἄνδρες, ἀδελφοί ⸀ἐστε· ἱνατί ἀδικεῖτε ἀλλήλους;
verses.translit: te te epioyse emera ofthi autois mahomenois kai synillassen autous eis eirinin eipon* Andres, adelfoi este* inati adikeite alliloys;
verses.translation: And the next day he shewed himself unto them as they strove, and would have set them at one again, saying, Sirs, ye are brethren; why do ye wrong one to another?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀδικῶν τὸν πλησίον ἀπώσατο αὐτὸν εἰπών· Τίς σε κατέστησεν ἄρχοντα καὶ δικαστὴν ἐφʼ ⸀ἡμῶν;
verses.translit: o de adikon ton plision aposato auton eipon* Tis se katestisen arhonta kai dikasten ef' emon;
verses.translation: But he that did his neighbour wrong thrust him away, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us?

verses.original: μὴ ἀνελεῖν με σὺ θέλεις ὃν τρόπον ἀνεῖλες ⸀ἐχθὲς τὸν Αἰγύπτιον;
verses.translit: me anelein me su theleis on tropon aneiles ehthes ton Aigyption;
verses.translation: Wilt thou kill me, as thou diddest the Egyptian yesterday?

verses.original: ἔφυγεν δὲ Μωϋσῆς ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ, καὶ ἐγένετο πάροικος ἐν γῇ Μαδιάμ, οὗ ἐγέννησεν υἱοὺς δύο.
verses.translit: efygen de Moyses en to logo toyto, kai egeneto paroikos en ge Madiam, ou egennisen yious dyo.
verses.translation: Then fled Moses at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Madian, where he begat two sons.

verses.original: Καὶ πληρωθέντων ἐτῶν τεσσεράκοντα ὤφθη αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τοῦ ὄρους Σινᾶ ⸀ἄγγελος ἐν φλογὶ πυρὸς βάτου·
verses.translit: Kai plirothenton eton tesserakonta ofthi auto en te erimo tou oroys Sina aggelos en flogi pyros vatoy*
verses.translation: And when forty years were expired, there appeared to him in the wilderness of mount Sina an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire in a bush.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Μωϋσῆς ἰδὼν ⸀ἐθαύμασεν τὸ ὅραμα. προσερχομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ κατανοῆσαι ἐγένετο φωνὴ ⸀κυρίου·
verses.translit: o de Moyses idon ethaymasen to orama. proserhomenoy de autou katanoesai egeneto fone kyrioy*
verses.translation: When Moses saw it , he wondered at the sight: and as he drew near to behold it , the voice of the Lord came unto him,

verses.original: Ἐγὼ ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου, ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ ⸀καὶ Ἰσαὰκ ⸁καὶ Ἰακώβ. ἔντρομος δὲ γενόμενος Μωϋσῆς οὐκ ἐτόλμα κατανοῆσαι.
verses.translit: Ego o theos ton pateron soy, o theos Avraam kai Isaak kai Iakov. entromos de genomenos Moyses ouk etolma katanoesai.
verses.translation: Saying , I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. Then Moses trembled, and durst not behold.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος· Λῦσον τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν σου, ὁ γὰρ τόπος ⸀ἐφʼ ᾧ ἕστηκας γῆ ἁγία ἐστίν.
verses.translit: eipen de auto o kyrios* Luson to upodima ton podon soy, o gar topos ef' o estikas ge agia estin.
verses.translation: Then said the Lord to him, Put off thy shoes from thy feet: for the place where thou standest is holy ground.

verses.original: ἰδὼν εἶδον τὴν κάκωσιν τοῦ λαοῦ μου τοῦ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ, καὶ τοῦ στεναγμοῦ ⸀αὐτοῦ ἤκουσα, καὶ κατέβην ἐξελέσθαι αὐτούς· καὶ νῦν δεῦρο ⸀ἀποστείλω σε εἰς Αἴγυπτον.
verses.translit: idon eidon ten kakosin tou laou moy tou en Aigypto, kai tou stenagmou autou ekoysa, kai katevin exelesthai autoys* kai nun deuro aposteilo se eis Aigypton.
verses.translation: I have seen, I have seen the affliction of my people which is in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and am come down to deliver them. And now come, I will send thee into Egypt.

verses.original: Τοῦτον τὸν Μωϋσῆν, ὃν ἠρνήσαντο εἰπόντες· Τίς σε κατέστησεν ἄρχοντα καὶ δικαστήν, τοῦτον ὁ θεὸς ⸀καὶ ἄρχοντα καὶ λυτρωτὴν ⸂ἀπέσταλκεν σὺν⸃ χειρὶ ἀγγέλου τοῦ ὀφθέντος αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ βάτῳ.
verses.translit: Touton ton Moysen, on ernisanto eipontes* Tis se katestisen arhonta kai dikastin, touton o theos kai arhonta kai lytroten apestalken sun heiri aggeloy tou ofthentos auto en te vato.
verses.translation: This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge? the same did God send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel which appeared to him in the bush.

verses.original: οὗτος ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ποιήσας τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα ἐν ⸀γῇ Αἰγύπτῳ καὶ ἐν Ἐρυθρᾷ Θαλάσσῃ καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα.
verses.translit: outos exigagen autous poiisas terata kai simeia en ge Aigypto kai en Erythra Thalasse kai en te erimo eti tesserakonta.
verses.translation: He brought them out, after that he had shewed wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, and in the Red sea, and in the wilderness forty years.
