verses.original: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Μωϋσῆς ὁ ⸀εἴπας τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ· Προφήτην ὑμῖν ἀναστήσει ⸂ὁ θεὸς⸃ ἐκ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ὑμῶν ὡς ἐμέ.
verses.translit: outos estin o Moyses o eipas tois yiois Israil* Profitin umin anastisei o theos ek ton adelfon umon os eme.
verses.translation: This is that Moses, which said unto the children of Israel, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear.

verses.original: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ μετὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ λαλοῦντος αὐτῷ ἐν τῷ ὄρει Σινᾶ καὶ τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, ὃς ἐδέξατο ⸀λόγια ζῶντα δοῦναι ⸀ἡμῖν,
verses.translit: outos estin o genomenos en te ekklisia en te erimo meta tou aggeloy tou lalountos auto en to orei Sina kai ton pateron emon, os edexato logia zonta dounai emin,
verses.translation: This is he, that was in the church in the wilderness with the angel which spake to him in the mount Sina, and with our fathers: who received the lively oracles to give unto us:

verses.original: ᾧ οὐκ ἠθέλησαν ὑπήκοοι γενέσθαι οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν, ἀλλὰ ἀπώσαντο καὶ ἐστράφησαν ⸂ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις⸃ αὐτῶν εἰς Αἴγυπτον,
verses.translit: o ouk ethelisan upikooi genesthai oi pateres emon, alla aposanto kai estrafisan en tais kardiais auton eis Aigypton,
verses.translation: To whom our fathers would not obey, but thrust him from them, and in their hearts turned back again into Egypt,

verses.original: εἰπόντες τῷ Ἀαρών· Ποίησον ἡμῖν θεοὺς οἳ προπορεύσονται ἡμῶν· ὁ γὰρ Μωϋσῆς οὗτος, ὃς ἐξήγαγεν ἡμᾶς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου, οὐκ οἴδαμεν τί ⸀ἐγένετο αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: eipontes to Aaron* Poiison emin theous oi proporeysontai emon* o gar Moyses outos, os exigagen emas ek ges Aigyptoy, ouk oidamen ti egeneto auto.
verses.translation: Saying unto Aaron, Make us gods to go before us: for as for this Moses, which brought us out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.

verses.original: καὶ ἐμοσχοποίησαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις καὶ ἀνήγαγον θυσίαν τῷ εἰδώλῳ, καὶ εὐφραίνοντο ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai emoshopoiisan en tais emerais ekeinais kai anigagon thysian to eidolo, kai eufrainonto en tois ergois ton heiron auton.
verses.translation: And they made a calf in those days, and offered sacrifice unto the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands.

verses.original: ἔστρεψεν δὲ ὁ θεὸς καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς λατρεύειν τῇ στρατιᾷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν βίβλῳ τῶν προφητῶν· Μὴ σφάγια καὶ θυσίας προσηνέγκατέ μοι ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, οἶκος Ἰσραήλ;
verses.translit: estrepsen de o theos kai paredoken autous latreyein te stratia tou ouranou, kathos gegraptai en vivlo ton profiton* Me sfagia kai thysias prosinegkate moi eti tesserakonta en te erimo, oikos Israil;
verses.translation: Then God turned, and gave them up to worship the host of heaven; as it is written in the book of the prophets, O ye house of Israel, have ye offered to me slain beasts and sacrifices by the space of forty years in the wilderness?

verses.original: καὶ ἀνελάβετε τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ Μολὸχ καὶ τὸ ἄστρον τοῦ ⸀θεοῦ ⸀Ῥαιφάν, τοὺς τύπους οὓς ἐποιήσατε προσκυνεῖν αὐτοῖς. καὶ μετοικιῶ ὑμᾶς ἐπέκεινα Βαβυλῶνος.
verses.translit: kai anelavete ten skinen tou Moloh kai to astron tou theou Raifan, tous typoys ous epoiisate proskynein autois. kai metoikio umas epekeina Vavylonos.
verses.translation: Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.

verses.original: Ἡ σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἦν τοῖς πατράσιν ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, καθὼς διετάξατο ὁ λαλῶν τῷ Μωϋσῇ ποιῆσαι αὐτὴν κατὰ τὸν τύπον ὃν ἑωράκει,
verses.translit: E skine tou martyrioy en tois patrasin emon en te erimo, kathos dietaxato o lalon to Moyse poiesai auten kata ton typon on eorakei,
verses.translation: Our fathers had the tabernacle of witness in the wilderness, as he had appointed, speaking unto Moses, that he should make it according to the fashion that he had seen.

verses.original: ἣν καὶ εἰσήγαγον διαδεξάμενοι οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῇ κατασχέσει τῶν ἐθνῶν ὧν ἐξῶσεν ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ προσώπου τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν ἕως τῶν ἡμερῶν Δαυίδ·
verses.translit: en kai eisigagon diadexamenoi oi pateres emon meta Iisou en te katashesei ton ethnon on exosen o theos apo prosopoy ton pateron emon eos ton emeron Dayid*
verses.translation: Which also our fathers that came after brought in with Jesus into the possession of the Gentiles, whom God drave out before the face of our fathers, unto the days of David;

verses.original: ὃς εὗρεν χάριν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ᾐτήσατο εὑρεῖν σκήνωμα τῷ ⸀θεῷ Ἰακώβ.
verses.translit: os euren harin enopion tou theou kai etisato eurein skinoma to theo Iakov.
verses.translation: Who found favour before God, and desired to find a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.

verses.original: Σολομῶν δὲ οἰκοδόμησεν αὐτῷ οἶκον.
verses.translit: Solomon de oikodomisen auto oikon.
verses.translation: But Solomon built him an house.

verses.original: ἀλλʼ οὐχ ὁ ὕψιστος ἐν ⸀χειροποιήτοις κατοικεῖ· καθὼς ὁ προφήτης λέγει·
verses.translit: all' ouh o upsistos en heiropoiitois katoikei* kathos o profitis legei*
verses.translation: Howbeit the most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands; as saith the prophet,

verses.original: Ὁ οὐρανός μοι θρόνος, ⸂ἡ δὲ⸃ γῆ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν μου· ποῖον οἶκον οἰκοδομήσετέ μοι, λέγει κύριος, ἢ τίς τόπος τῆς καταπαύσεώς μου;
verses.translit: O ouranos moi thronos, e de ge upopodion ton podon moy* poion oikon oikodomisete moi, legei kyrios, e tis topos tes katapayseos moy;
verses.translation: Heaven is my throne, and earth is my footstool: what house will ye build me? saith the Lord: or what is the place of my rest?

verses.original: οὐχὶ ἡ χείρ μου ἐποίησεν ταῦτα πάντα;
verses.translit: ouhi e heir moy epoiisen tauta panta;
verses.translation: Hath not my hand made all these things?

verses.original: Σκληροτράχηλοι καὶ ἀπερίτμητοι ⸀καρδίαις καὶ τοῖς ὠσίν, ὑμεῖς ἀεὶ τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ ἀντιπίπτετε, ὡς οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν καὶ ὑμεῖς.
verses.translit: Sklirotrahiloi kai aperitmitoi kardiais kai tois osin, umeis aei to pneymati to agio antipiptete, os oi pateres umon kai umeis.
verses.translation: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did , so do ye.

verses.original: τίνα τῶν προφητῶν οὐκ ἐδίωξαν οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν; καὶ ἀπέκτειναν τοὺς προκαταγγείλαντας περὶ τῆς ἐλεύσεως τοῦ δικαίου οὗ νῦν ὑμεῖς προδόται καὶ φονεῖς ⸀ἐγένεσθε,
verses.translit: tina ton profiton ouk edioxan oi pateres umon; kai apekteinan tous prokataggeilantas peri tes eleyseos tou dikaioy ou nun umeis prodotai kai foneis egenesthe,
verses.translation: Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and they have slain them which shewed before of the coming of the Just One; of whom ye have been now the betrayers and murderers:

verses.original: οἵτινες ἐλάβετε τὸν νόμον εἰς διαταγὰς ἀγγέλων, καὶ οὐκ ἐφυλάξατε.
verses.translit: oitines elavete ton nomon eis diatagas aggelon, kai ouk efylaxate.
verses.translation: Who have received the law by the disposition of angels, and have not kept it.

verses.original: Ἀκούοντες δὲ ταῦτα διεπρίοντο ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν καὶ ἔβρυχον τοὺς ὀδόντας ἐπʼ αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Akoyontes de tauta dieprionto tais kardiais auton kai evryhon tous odontas ep' auton.
verses.translation: When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth.

verses.original: ὑπάρχων δὲ πλήρης πνεύματος ἁγίου ἀτενίσας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἶδεν δόξαν θεοῦ καὶ Ἰησοῦν ἑστῶτα ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ θεοῦ,
verses.translit: uparhon de pliris pneymatos agioy atenisas eis ton ouranon eiden doxan theou kai Iisoun estota ek dexion tou theou,
verses.translation: But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God,

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ θεωρῶ τοὺς οὐρανοὺς ⸀διηνοιγμένους καὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ δεξιῶν ἑστῶτα τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: kai eipen* Idou theoro tous ouranous diinoigmenoys kai ton yion tou anthropoy ek dexion estota tou theou.
verses.translation: And said, Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.

verses.original: κράξαντες δὲ φωνῇ μεγάλῃ συνέσχον τὰ ὦτα αὐτῶν, καὶ ὥρμησαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐπʼ αὐτόν,
verses.translit: kraxantes de fone megale syneshon ta ota auton, kai ormisan omothymadon ep' auton,
verses.translation: Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord,

verses.original: καὶ ἐκβαλόντες ἔξω τῆς πόλεως ἐλιθοβόλουν. καὶ οἱ μάρτυρες ἀπέθεντο τὰ ἱμάτια ⸀αὐτῶν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας νεανίου καλουμένου Σαύλου.
verses.translit: kai ekvalontes exo tes poleos elithovoloyn. kai oi martyres apethento ta imatia auton para tous podas neanioy kaloymenoy Sayloy.
verses.translation: And cast him out of the city, and stoned him : and the witnesses laid down their clothes at a young man’s feet, whose name was Saul.

verses.original: καὶ ἐλιθοβόλουν τὸν Στέφανον ἐπικαλούμενον καὶ λέγοντα· Κύριε Ἰησοῦ, δέξαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου·
verses.translit: kai elithovoloyn ton Stefanon epikaloymenon kai legonta* Kyrie Iisou, dexai to pneuma moy*
verses.translation: And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God , and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.

verses.original: θεὶς δὲ τὰ γόνατα ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Κύριε, μὴ στήσῃς αὐτοῖς ⸂ταύτην τὴν ἁμαρτίαν⸃· καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἐκοιμήθη.
verses.translit: theis de ta gonata ekraxen fone megale* Kyrie, me stises autois taytin ten amartian* kai touto eipon ekoimithi.
verses.translation: And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.

verses.original: Σαῦλος δὲ ἦν συνευδοκῶν τῇ ἀναιρέσει αὐτοῦ. Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ διωγμὸς μέγας ἐπὶ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τὴν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις· πάντες δὲ διεσπάρησαν κατὰ τὰς χώρας τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας πλὴν τῶν ἀποστόλων.
verses.translit: Saulos de en syneydokon te anairesei autou. Egeneto de en ekeine te emera diogmos megas epi ten ekklisian ten en Ierosolymois* pantes de diesparisan kata tas horas tes Ioydaias kai Samareias plen ton apostolon.
verses.translation: And Saul was consenting unto his death. And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judæa and Samaria, except the apostles.

verses.original: συνεκόμισαν δὲ τὸν Στέφανον ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς καὶ ⸀ἐποίησαν κοπετὸν μέγαν ἐπʼ αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: synekomisan de ton Stefanon andres eulaveis kai epoiisan kopeton megan ep' auto.
verses.translation: And devout men carried Stephen to his burial , and made great lamentation over him.

verses.original: Σαῦλος δὲ ἐλυμαίνετο τὴν ἐκκλησίαν κατὰ τοὺς οἴκους εἰσπορευόμενος, σύρων τε ἄνδρας καὶ γυναῖκας παρεδίδου εἰς φυλακήν.
verses.translit: Saulos de elymaineto ten ekklisian kata tous oikoys eisporeyomenos, syron te andras kai gynaikas paredidoy eis fylakin.
verses.translation: As for Saul, he made havock of the church, entering into every house, and haling men and women committed them to prison.

verses.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διασπαρέντες διῆλθον εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν λόγον.
verses.translit: Oi men oun diasparentes dielthon euaggelizomenoi ton logon.
verses.translation: Therefore they that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word.

verses.original: Φίλιππος δὲ κατελθὼν εἰς ⸀τὴν πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρείας ἐκήρυσσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν χριστόν.
verses.translit: Filippos de katelthon eis ten polin tes Samareias ekiryssen autois ton hriston.
verses.translation: Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria, and preached Christ unto them.

verses.original: προσεῖχον ⸀δὲ οἱ ὄχλοι τοῖς λεγομένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ Φιλίππου ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐν τῷ ἀκούειν αὐτοὺς καὶ βλέπειν τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει·
verses.translit: proseihon de oi ohloi tois legomenois upo tou Filippoy omothymadon en to akoyein autous kai vlepein ta simeia a epoiei*
verses.translation: And the people with one accord gave heed unto those things which Philip spake, hearing and seeing the miracles which he did.

verses.original: ⸀πολλοὶ γὰρ τῶν ἐχόντων πνεύματα ἀκάθαρτα βοῶντα φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ⸀ἐξήρχοντο, πολλοὶ δὲ παραλελυμένοι καὶ χωλοὶ ἐθεραπεύθησαν·
verses.translit: polloi gar ton ehonton pneymata akatharta voonta fone megale exirhonto, polloi de paralelymenoi kai holoi etherapeythisan*
verses.translation: For unclean spirits, crying with loud voice, came out of many that were possessed with them : and many taken with palsies, and that were lame, were healed.

verses.original: ⸂ἐγένετο δὲ⸃ ⸂πολλὴ χαρὰ⸃ ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ.
verses.translit: egeneto de polle hara en te polei ekeine.
verses.translation: And there was great joy in that city.

verses.original: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις ὀνόματι Σίμων προϋπῆρχεν ἐν τῇ πόλει μαγεύων καὶ ⸀ἐξιστάνων τὸ ἔθνος τῆς Σαμαρείας, λέγων εἶναί τινα ἑαυτὸν μέγαν,
verses.translit: Aner de tis onomati Simon proyperhen en te polei mageyon kai existanon to ethnos tes Samareias, legon einai tina eayton megan,
verses.translation: But there was a certain man, called Simon, which beforetime in the same city used sorcery, and bewitched the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one:

verses.original: ᾧ προσεῖχον ⸀πάντες ἀπὸ μικροῦ ἕως μεγάλου λέγοντες· Οὗτός ἐστιν ἡ Δύναμις τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ ⸀καλουμένη Μεγάλη.
verses.translit: o proseihon pantes apo mikrou eos megaloy legontes* Outos estin e Dynamis tou theou e kaloymeni Megali.
verses.translation: To whom they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the great power of God.

verses.original: προσεῖχον δὲ αὐτῷ διὰ τὸ ἱκανῷ χρόνῳ ταῖς μαγείαις ἐξεστακέναι αὐτούς.
verses.translit: proseihon de auto dia to ikano hrono tais mageiais exestakenai autoys.
verses.translation: And to him they had regard, because that of long time he had bewitched them with sorceries.

verses.original: ὅτε δὲ ἐπίστευσαν τῷ Φιλίππῳ εὐαγγελιζομένῳ ⸀περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ ὀνόματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἐβαπτίζοντο ἄνδρες τε καὶ γυναῖκες.
verses.translit: ote de episteysan to Filippo euaggelizomeno peri tes vasileias tou theou kai tou onomatos Iisou Hristou, evaptizonto andres te kai gynaikes.
verses.translation: But when they believed Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of God, and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Σίμων καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπίστευσεν, καὶ βαπτισθεὶς ἦν προσκαρτερῶν τῷ Φιλίππῳ, θεωρῶν τε ⸂σημεῖα καὶ δυνάμεις μεγάλας γινομένας⸃ ἐξίστατο.
verses.translit: o de Simon kai autos episteysen, kai vaptistheis en proskarteron to Filippo, theoron te simeia kai dynameis megalas ginomenas existato.
verses.translation: Then Simon himself believed also: and when he was baptized, he continued with Philip, and wondered, beholding the miracles and signs which were done.

verses.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἀπόστολοι ὅτι δέδεκται ἡ Σαμάρεια τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀπέστειλαν πρὸς ⸀αὐτοὺς Πέτρον καὶ Ἰωάννην,
verses.translit: Akoysantes de oi en Ierosolymois apostoloi oti dedektai e Samareia ton logon tou theou, apesteilan pros autous Petron kai Ioannin,
verses.translation: Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John:

verses.original: οἵτινες καταβάντες προσηύξαντο περὶ αὐτῶν ὅπως λάβωσιν πνεῦμα ἅγιον·
verses.translit: oitines katavantes prosiyxanto peri auton opos lavosin pneuma agion*
verses.translation: Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost:

verses.original: ⸀οὐδέπω γὰρ ἦν ἐπʼ οὐδενὶ αὐτῶν ἐπιπεπτωκός, μόνον δὲ βεβαπτισμένοι ὑπῆρχον εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ ⸀κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: oudepo gar en ep' oudeni auton epipeptokos, monon de vevaptismenoi uperhon eis to onoma tou kyrioy Iisou.
verses.translation: (For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.)

verses.original: τότε ⸀ἐπετίθεσαν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπʼ αὐτούς, καὶ ἐλάμβανον πνεῦμα ἅγιον.
verses.translit: tote epetithesan tas heiras ep' autoys, kai elamvanon pneuma agion.
verses.translation: Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.

verses.original: ⸀ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Σίμων ὅτι διὰ τῆς ἐπιθέσεως τῶν χειρῶν τῶν ἀποστόλων δίδοται τὸ ⸀πνεῦμα προσήνεγκεν αὐτοῖς χρήματα
verses.translit: idon de o Simon oti dia tes epitheseos ton heiron ton apostolon didotai to pneuma prosinegken autois hrimata
verses.translation: And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money,

verses.original: λέγων· Δότε κἀμοὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἵνα ᾧ ἐὰν ἐπιθῶ τὰς χεῖρας λαμβάνῃ πνεῦμα ἅγιον.
verses.translit: legon* Dote kamoi ten exoysian taytin ina o ean epitho tas heiras lamvane pneuma agion.
verses.translation: Saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost.

verses.original: Πέτρος δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Τὸ ἀργύριόν σου σὺν σοὶ εἴη εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὅτι τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐνόμισας διὰ χρημάτων κτᾶσθαι.
verses.translit: Petros de eipen pros auton* To argyrion soy sun soi eii eis apoleian oti ten dorean tou theou enomisas dia hrimaton ktasthai.
verses.translation: But Peter said unto him, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.

verses.original: οὐκ ἔστιν σοι μερὶς οὐδὲ κλῆρος ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ, ἡ γὰρ καρδία σου οὐκ ἔστιν εὐθεῖα ⸀ἔναντι τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: ouk estin soi meris oude kleros en to logo toyto, e gar kardia soy ouk estin eutheia enanti tou theou.
verses.translation: Thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter: for thy heart is not right in the sight of God.

verses.original: μετανόησον οὖν ἀπὸ τῆς κακίας σου ταύτης, καὶ δεήθητι τοῦ ⸀κυρίου εἰ ἄρα ἀφεθήσεταί σοι ἡ ἐπίνοια τῆς καρδίας σου·
verses.translit: metanoison oun apo tes kakias soy taytis, kai deithiti tou kyrioy ei ara afethisetai soi e epinoia tes kardias soy*
verses.translation: Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee.

verses.original: εἰς γὰρ χολὴν πικρίας καὶ σύνδεσμον ἀδικίας ὁρῶ σε ὄντα.
verses.translit: eis gar holen pikrias kai syndesmon adikias oro se onta.
verses.translation: For I perceive that thou art in the gall of bitterness, and in the bond of iniquity.

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Σίμων εἶπεν· Δεήθητε ὑμεῖς ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ πρὸς τὸν κύριον ὅπως μηδὲν ἐπέλθῃ ἐπʼ ἐμὲ ὧν εἰρήκατε.
verses.translit: apokritheis de o Simon eipen* Deithite umeis uper emou pros ton kyrion opos miden epelthe ep' eme on eirikate.
verses.translation: Then answered Simon, and said, Pray ye to the Lord for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me.

verses.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διαμαρτυράμενοι καὶ λαλήσαντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου ⸀ὑπέστρεφον εἰς ⸀Ἱεροσόλυμα, πολλάς τε κώμας τῶν Σαμαριτῶν ⸀εὐηγγελίζοντο.
verses.translit: Oi men oun diamartyramenoi kai lalisantes ton logon tou kyrioy upestrefon eis Ierosolyma, pollas te komas ton Samariton euiggelizonto.
verses.translation: And they, when they had testified and preached the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the gospel in many villages of the Samaritans.

verses.original: Ἄγγελος δὲ κυρίου ἐλάλησεν πρὸς Φίλιππον λέγων· Ἀνάστηθι καὶ πορεύου κατὰ μεσημβρίαν ἐπὶ τὴν ὁδὸν τὴν καταβαίνουσαν ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλὴμ εἰς Γάζαν· αὕτη ἐστὶν ἔρημος.
verses.translit: Aggelos de kyrioy elalisen pros Filippon legon* Anastithi kai poreyoy kata mesimvrian epi ten odon ten katavainoysan apo Ieroysalem eis Gazan* auti estin erimos.
verses.translation: And the angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert.

verses.original: καὶ ἀναστὰς ἐπορεύθη, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ Αἰθίοψ εὐνοῦχος δυνάστης ⸀Κανδάκης βασιλίσσης Αἰθιόπων, ὃς ἦν ἐπὶ πάσης τῆς γάζης αὐτῆς, ὃς ἐληλύθει προσκυνήσων εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ,
verses.translit: kai anastas eporeythi, kai idou aner Aithiops eunouhos dynastis Kandakis vasilissis Aithiopon, os en epi pasis tes gazis autes, os elilythei proskynison eis Ieroysalim,
verses.translation: And he arose and went: and, behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem for to worship,

verses.original: ἦν ⸀τε ὑποστρέφων καὶ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τοῦ ἅρματος αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀνεγίνωσκεν τὸν προφήτην Ἠσαΐαν.
verses.translit: en te upostrefon kai kathimenos epi tou armatos autou kai aneginosken ton profitin EsaIan.
verses.translation: Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τῷ Φιλίππῳ· Πρόσελθε καὶ κολλήθητι τῷ ἅρματι τούτῳ.
verses.translit: eipen de to pneuma to Filippo* Proselthe kai kollithiti to armati toyto.
verses.translation: Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot.

verses.original: προσδραμὼν δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ ἀναγινώσκοντος ⸂Ἠσαΐαν τὸν προφήτην⸃ καὶ εἶπεν· Ἆρά γε γινώσκεις ἃ ἀναγινώσκεις;
verses.translit: prosdramon de o Filippos ekoysen autou anaginoskontos EsaIan ton profitin kai eipen* Ara ge ginoskeis a anaginoskeis;
verses.translation: And Philip ran thither to him , and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest?

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Πῶς γὰρ ἂν δυναίμην ἐὰν μή τις ⸀ὁδηγήσει με; παρεκάλεσέν τε τὸν Φίλιππον ἀναβάντα καθίσαι σὺν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: o de eipen* Pos gar an dynaimin ean mi tis odigisei me; parekalesen te ton Filippon anavanta kathisai sun auto.
verses.translation: And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.

verses.original: ἡ δὲ περιοχὴ τῆς γραφῆς ἣν ἀνεγίνωσκεν ἦν αὕτη· Ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ ⸀κείραντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος, οὕτως οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: e de periohe tes grafes en aneginosken en auti* Os provaton epi sfagen ehthi, kai os amnos enantion tou keirantos auton afonos, outos ouk anoigei to stoma autou.
verses.translation: The place of the scripture which he read was this, He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth:

verses.original: ἐν τῇ ⸀ταπεινώσει ἡ κρίσις αὐτοῦ ἤρθη· ⸀τὴν γενεὰν αὐτοῦ τίς διηγήσεται; ὅτι αἴρεται ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: en te tapeinosei e krisis autou erthi* ten genean autou tis diigisetai; oti airetai apo tes ges e zoe autou.
verses.translation: In his humiliation his judgment was taken away: and who shall declare his generation? for his life is taken from the earth.

verses.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ εὐνοῦχος τῷ Φιλίππῳ εἶπεν· Δέομαί σου, περὶ τίνος ὁ προφήτης λέγει ⸀τοῦτο; περὶ ἑαυτοῦ ἢ περὶ ἑτέρου τινός;
verses.translit: apokritheis de o eunouhos to Filippo eipen* Deomai soy, peri tinos o profitis legei touto; peri eaytou e peri eteroy tinos;
verses.translation: And the eunuch answered Philip, and said, I pray thee, of whom speaketh the prophet this? of himself, or of some other man?

verses.original: ἀνοίξας δὲ ὁ Φίλιππος τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς γραφῆς ταύτης εὐηγγελίσατο αὐτῷ τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: anoixas de o Filippos to stoma autou kai arxamenos apo tes grafes taytis euiggelisato auto ton Iisoun.
verses.translation: Then Philip opened his mouth, and began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἐπορεύοντο κατὰ τὴν ὁδόν, ἦλθον ἐπί τι ὕδωρ, καί φησιν ὁ εὐνοῦχος· Ἰδοὺ ὕδωρ, τί κωλύει με ⸀βαπτισθῆναι;
verses.translit: os de eporeyonto kata ten odon, elthon epi ti udor, kai fisin o eunouhos* Idou udor, ti kolyei me vaptisthenai;
verses.translation: And as they went on their way, they came unto a certain water: and the eunuch said, See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized?
And Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.

verses.original: καὶ ἐκέλευσεν στῆναι τὸ ἅρμα, καὶ κατέβησαν ἀμφότεροι εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ ὅ τε Φίλιππος καὶ ὁ εὐνοῦχος, καὶ ἐβάπτισεν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai ekeleysen stenai to arma, kai katevisan amfoteroi eis to udor o te Filippos kai o eunouhos, kai evaptisen auton.
verses.translation: And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him.

verses.original: ὅτε δὲ ἀνέβησαν ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος, πνεῦμα κυρίου ἥρπασεν τὸν Φίλιππον, καὶ οὐκ εἶδεν αὐτὸν οὐκέτι ὁ εὐνοῦχος, ἐπορεύετο γὰρ τὴν ὁδὸν αὐτοῦ χαίρων.
verses.translit: ote de anevisan ek tou udatos, pneuma kyrioy erpasen ton Filippon, kai ouk eiden auton ouketi o eunouhos, eporeyeto gar ten odon autou hairon.
verses.translation: And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing.

verses.original: Φίλιππος δὲ εὑρέθη εἰς Ἄζωτον, καὶ διερχόμενος εὐηγγελίζετο τὰς πόλεις πάσας ἕως τοῦ ἐλθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς Καισάρειαν.
verses.translit: Filippos de eurethi eis Azoton, kai dierhomenos euiggelizeto tas poleis pasas eos tou elthein auton eis Kaisareian.
verses.translation: But Philip was found at Azotus: and passing through he preached in all the cities, till he came to Cæsarea.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Σαῦλος ἔτι ἐμπνέων ἀπειλῆς καὶ φόνου εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς τοῦ κυρίου, προσελθὼν τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ
verses.translit: O de Saulos eti empneon apeiles kai fonoy eis tous mathitas tou kyrioy, proselthon to arhierei
verses.translation: And Saul, yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went unto the high priest,

verses.original: ᾐτήσατο παρʼ αὐτοῦ ἐπιστολὰς εἰς Δαμασκὸν πρὸς τὰς συναγωγάς, ὅπως ἐάν τινας εὕρῃ τῆς ὁδοῦ ὄντας, ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας, δεδεμένους ἀγάγῃ εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ.
verses.translit: etisato par' autou epistolas eis Damaskon pros tas synagogas, opos ean tinas eure tes odou ontas, andras te kai gynaikas, dedemenoys agage eis Ieroysalim.
verses.translation: And desired of him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem.

verses.original: ἐν δὲ τῷ πορεύεσθαι ἐγένετο αὐτὸν ἐγγίζειν τῇ Δαμασκῷ, ⸂ἐξαίφνης τε αὐτὸν περιήστραψεν⸃ φῶς ⸀ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ,
verses.translit: en de to poreyesthai egeneto auton eggizein te Damasko, exaifnis te auton periistrapsen fos ek tou ouranou,
verses.translation: And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven:

verses.original: καὶ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἤκουσεν φωνὴν λέγουσαν αὐτῷ Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;
verses.translit: kai peson epi ten gen ekoysen fonen legoysan auto Saoul Saoyl, ti me diokeis;
verses.translation: And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

verses.original: εἶπεν δέ· Τίς εἶ, κύριε; ὁ ⸀δέ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις·
verses.translit: eipen de* Tis ei, kyrie; o de* Ego eimi Iisous on su diokeis*
verses.translation: And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ἀνάστηθι καὶ εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν πόλιν, καὶ λαληθήσεταί σοι ⸂ὅ τί⸃ σε δεῖ ποιεῖν.
verses.translit: alla anastithi kai eiselthe eis ten polin, kai lalithisetai soi o ti se dei poiein.
verses.translation: And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἄνδρες οἱ συνοδεύοντες αὐτῷ εἱστήκεισαν ἐνεοί, ἀκούοντες μὲν τῆς φωνῆς μηδένα δὲ θεωροῦντες.
verses.translit: oi de andres oi synodeyontes auto eistikeisan eneoi, akoyontes men tes fones midena de theorountes.
verses.translation: And the men which journeyed with him stood speechless, hearing a voice, but seeing no man.

verses.original: ἠγέρθη δὲ ⸀Σαῦλος ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς, ἀνεῳγμένων ⸀δὲ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτοῦ ⸀οὐδὲν ἔβλεπεν· χειραγωγοῦντες δὲ αὐτὸν εἰσήγαγον εἰς Δαμασκόν.
verses.translit: egerthi de Saulos apo tes ges, aneogmenon de ton ofthalmon autou ouden evlepen* heiragogountes de auton eisigagon eis Damaskon.
verses.translation: And Saul arose from the earth; and when his eyes were opened, he saw no man: but they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus.

verses.original: καὶ ἦν ἡμέρας τρεῖς μὴ βλέπων, καὶ οὐκ ἔφαγεν οὐδὲ ἔπιεν.
verses.translit: kai en emeras treis me vlepon, kai ouk efagen oude epien.
verses.translation: And he was three days without sight, and neither did eat nor drink.

verses.original: Ἦν δέ τις μαθητὴς ἐν Δαμασκῷ ὀνόματι Ἁνανίας, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ⸂ἐν ὁράματι ὁ κύριος⸃· Ἁνανία. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ, κύριε.
verses.translit: En de tis mathites en Damasko onomati Ananias, kai eipen pros auton en oramati o kyrios* Anania. o de eipen* Idou ego, kyrie.
verses.translation: And there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and to him said the Lord in a vision, Ananias. And he said, Behold, I am here , Lord.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν· ⸀Ἀναστὰς πορεύθητι ἐπὶ τὴν ῥύμην τὴν καλουμένην Εὐθεῖαν καὶ ζήτησον ἐν οἰκίᾳ Ἰούδα Σαῦλον ὀνόματι Ταρσέα, ἰδοὺ γὰρ προσεύχεται,
verses.translit: o de kyrios pros auton* Anastas poreythiti epi ten Rymin ten kaloymenin Eutheian kai zitison en oikia Ioyda Saulon onomati Tarsea, idou gar proseyhetai,
verses.translation: And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the street which is called Straight, and enquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul, of Tarsus: for, behold, he prayeth,

verses.original: καὶ εἶδεν ⸂ἄνδρα ἐν ὁράματι Ἁνανίαν ὀνόματι⸃ εἰσελθόντα καὶ ἐπιθέντα αὐτῷ ⸀χεῖρας ὅπως ἀναβλέψῃ.
verses.translit: kai eiden andra en oramati Ananian onomati eiselthonta kai epithenta auto heiras opos anavlepse.
verses.translation: And hath seen in a vision a man named Ananias coming in, and putting his hand on him, that he might receive his sight.

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ Ἁνανίας· Κύριε, ⸀ἤκουσα ἀπὸ πολλῶν περὶ τοῦ ἀνδρὸς τούτου, ὅσα κακὰ ⸂τοῖς ἁγίοις σου ἐποίησεν⸃ ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ·
verses.translit: apekrithi de Ananias* Kyrie, ekoysa apo pollon peri tou andros toytoy, osa kaka tois agiois soy epoiisen en Ieroysalim*
verses.translation: Then Ananias answered, Lord, I have heard by many of this man, how much evil he hath done to thy saints at Jerusalem:

verses.original: καὶ ὧδε ἔχει ἐξουσίαν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων δῆσαι πάντας τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους τὸ ὄνομά σου.
verses.translit: kai ode ehei exoysian para ton arhiereon desai pantas tous epikaloymenoys to onoma soy.
verses.translation: And here he hath authority from the chief priests to bind all that call on thy name.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος· Πορεύου, ὅτι σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς ⸂ἐστίν μοι⸃ οὗτος τοῦ βαστάσαι τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐνώπιον ⸀ἐθνῶν ⸀τε καὶ βασιλέων υἱῶν τε Ἰσραήλ,
verses.translit: eipen de pros auton o kyrios* Poreyoy, oti skeuos ekloges estin moi outos tou vastasai to onoma moy enopion ethnon te kai vasileon yion te Israil,
verses.translation: But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel:

verses.original: ἐγὼ γὰρ ὑποδείξω αὐτῷ ὅσα δεῖ αὐτὸν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματός μου παθεῖν.
verses.translit: ego gar upodeixo auto osa dei auton uper tou onomatos moy pathein.
verses.translation: For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name’s sake.

verses.original: ἀπῆλθεν δὲ Ἁνανίας καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν, καὶ ἐπιθεὶς ἐπʼ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας εἶπεν· Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ, ὁ κύριος ἀπέσταλκέν με, ⸀Ἰησοῦς ὁ ὀφθείς σοι ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ᾗ ἤρχου, ὅπως ἀναβλέψῃς καὶ πλησθῇς πνεύματος ἁγίου.
verses.translit: apelthen de Ananias kai eiselthen eis ten oikian, kai epitheis ep' auton tas heiras eipen* Saoul adelfe, o kyrios apestalken me, Iisous o oftheis soi en te odo e erhoy, opos anavlepses kai plisthes pneymatos agioy.
verses.translation: And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost.

verses.original: καὶ εὐθέως ἀπέπεσαν ⸂αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν⸃ ⸀ὡς λεπίδες, ἀνέβλεψέν τε καὶ ἀναστὰς ἐβαπτίσθη,
verses.translit: kai eutheos apepesan autou apo ton ofthalmon os lepides, anevlepsen te kai anastas evaptisthi,
verses.translation: And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.

verses.original: καὶ λαβὼν τροφὴν ⸀ἐνίσχυσεν. Ἐγένετο ⸀δὲ μετὰ τῶν ἐν Δαμασκῷ μαθητῶν ἡμέρας τινὰς,
verses.translit: kai lavon trofen enishysen. Egeneto de meta ton en Damasko mathiton emeras tinas,
verses.translation: And when he had received meat, he was strengthened. Then was Saul certain days with the disciples which were at Damascus.

verses.original: καὶ εὐθέως ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ἐκήρυσσεν τὸν ⸀Ἰησοῦν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: kai eutheos en tais synagogais ekiryssen ton Iisoun oti outos estin o yios tou theou.
verses.translation: And straightway he preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God.

verses.original: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες οἱ ἀκούοντες καὶ ἔλεγον· Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ πορθήσας ⸀ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους τὸ ὄνομα τοῦτο, καὶ ὧδε εἰς τοῦτο ἐληλύθει ἵνα δεδεμένους αὐτοὺς ἀγάγῃ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς;
verses.translit: existanto de pantes oi akoyontes kai elegon* Ouh outos estin o porthisas en Ieroysalem tous epikaloymenoys to onoma touto, kai ode eis touto elilythei ina dedemenoys autous agage epi tous arhiereis;
verses.translation: But all that heard him were amazed, and said; Is not this he that destroyed them which called on this name in Jerusalem, and came hither for that intent, that he might bring them bound unto the chief priests?

verses.original: Σαῦλος δὲ μᾶλλον ἐνεδυναμοῦτο καὶ ⸀συνέχυννεν ⸀τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐν Δαμασκῷ, συμβιβάζων ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός.
verses.translit: Saulos de mallon enedynamouto kai synehynnen tous Ioydaioys tous katoikountas en Damasko, symvivazon oti outos estin o hristos.
verses.translation: But Saul increased the more in strength, and confounded the Jews which dwelt at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦντο ἡμέραι ἱκαναί, συνεβουλεύσαντο οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν·
verses.translit: Os de eplirounto emerai ikanai, synevoyleysanto oi Ioydaioi anelein auton*
verses.translation: And after that many days were fulfilled, the Jews took counsel to kill him:

verses.original: ἐγνώσθη δὲ τῷ Σαύλῳ ἡ ἐπιβουλὴ αὐτῶν. ⸂παρετηροῦντο δὲ καὶ⸃ τὰς πύλας ἡμέρας τε καὶ νυκτὸς ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀνέλωσιν·
verses.translit: egnosthi de to Saylo e epivoyle auton. paretirounto de kai tas pylas emeras te kai nyktos opos auton anelosin*
verses.translation: But their laying await was known of Saul. And they watched the gates day and night to kill him.

verses.original: λαβόντες δὲ ⸂οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ⸃ νυκτὸς ⸂διὰ τοῦ τείχους καθῆκαν αὐτὸν⸃ χαλάσαντες ἐν σπυρίδι.
verses.translit: lavontes de oi mathitai autou nyktos dia tou teihoys kathekan auton halasantes en spyridi.
verses.translation: Then the disciples took him by night, and let him down by the wall in a basket.

verses.original: Παραγενόμενος δὲ ⸀εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ⸀ἐπείραζεν κολλᾶσθαι τοῖς μαθηταῖς· καὶ πάντες ἐφοβοῦντο αὐτόν, μὴ πιστεύοντες ὅτι ἐστὶν μαθητής.
verses.translit: Paragenomenos de eis Ieroysalem epeirazen kollasthai tois mathitais* kai pantes efovounto auton, me pisteyontes oti estin mathitis.
verses.translation: And when Saul was come to Jerusalem, he assayed to join himself to the disciples: but they were all afraid of him, and believed not that he was a disciple.

verses.original: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ ἐπιλαβόμενος αὐτὸν ἤγαγεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους, καὶ διηγήσατο αὐτοῖς πῶς ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶδεν τὸν κύριον καὶ ὅτι ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ καὶ πῶς ἐν Δαμασκῷ ἐπαρρησιάσατο ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι ⸀τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: Varnavas de epilavomenos auton egagen pros tous apostoloys, kai diigisato autois pos en te odo eiden ton kyrion kai oti elalisen auto kai pos en Damasko eparrisiasato en to onomati tou Iisou.
verses.translation: But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles, and declared unto them how he had seen the Lord in the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how he had preached boldly at Damascus in the name of Jesus.

verses.original: καὶ ἦν μετʼ αὐτῶν εἰσπορευόμενος ⸂καὶ ἐκπορευόμενος⸃ εἰς ⸀Ἰερουσαλήμ, παρρησιαζόμενος ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ ⸀κυρίου,
verses.translit: kai en met' auton eisporeyomenos kai ekporeyomenos eis Ieroysalim, parrisiazomenos en to onomati tou kyrioy,
verses.translation: And he was with them coming in and going out at Jerusalem.

verses.original: ἐλάλει τε καὶ συνεζήτει πρὸς τοὺς Ἑλληνιστάς· οἱ δὲ ἐπεχείρουν ⸂ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν⸃.
verses.translit: elalei te kai synezitei pros tous Ellinistas* oi de epeheiroyn anelein auton.
verses.translation: And he spake boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus, and disputed against the Grecians: but they went about to slay him.

verses.original: ἐπιγνόντες δὲ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ κατήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς Καισάρειαν καὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν αὐτὸν εἰς Ταρσόν.
verses.translit: epignontes de oi adelfoi katigagon auton eis Kaisareian kai exapesteilan auton eis Tarson.
verses.translation: Which when the brethren knew, they brought him down to Cæsarea, and sent him forth to Tarsus.

verses.original: ⸂Ἡ μὲν οὖν ἐκκλησία καθʼ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Γαλιλαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας εἶχεν εἰρήνην οἰκοδομουμένη, καὶ πορευομένη τῷ φόβῳ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ τῇ παρακλήσει τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐπληθύνετο⸃.
verses.translit: E men oun ekklisia kath' olis tes Ioydaias kai Galilaias kai Samareias eihen eirinin oikodomoymeni, kai poreyomeni to fovo tou kyrioy kai te paraklisei tou agioy pneymatos eplithyneto.
verses.translation: Then had the churches rest throughout all Judæa and Galilee and Samaria, and were edified; and walking in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Ghost, were multiplied.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ Πέτρον διερχόμενον διὰ πάντων κατελθεῖν καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ἁγίους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας Λύδδα.
verses.translit: Egeneto de Petron dierhomenon dia panton katelthein kai pros tous agioys tous katoikountas Lydda.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, as Peter passed throughout all quarters , he came down also to the saints which dwelt at Lydda.

verses.original: εὗρεν δὲ ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπόν τινα ⸂ὀνόματι Αἰνέαν⸃ ἐξ ἐτῶν ὀκτὼ κατακείμενον ἐπὶ ⸀κραβάττου, ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος.
verses.translit: euren de ekei anthropon tina onomati Ainean ex eton okto katakeimenon epi kravattoy, os en paralelymenos.
verses.translation: And there he found a certain man named Æneas, which had kept his bed eight years, and was sick of the palsy.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος· Αἰνέα, ἰᾶταί σε Ἰησοῦς ⸀Χριστός· ἀνάστηθι καὶ στρῶσον σεαυτῷ· καὶ εὐθέως ἀνέστη.
verses.translit: kai eipen auto o Petros* Ainea, iatai se Iisous Hristos* anastithi kai stroson seayto* kai eutheos anesti.
verses.translation: And Peter said unto him, Æneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole: arise, and make thy bed. And he arose immediately.

verses.original: καὶ εἶδαν αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ κατοικοῦντες Λύδδα καὶ τὸν ⸀Σαρῶνα, οἵτινες ἐπέστρεψαν ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον.
verses.translit: kai eidan auton pantes oi katoikountes Lydda kai ton Sarona, oitines epestrepsan epi ton kyrion.
verses.translation: And all that dwelt at Lydda and Saron saw him, and turned to the Lord.

verses.original: Ἐν Ἰόππῃ δέ τις ἦν μαθήτρια ὀνόματι Ταβιθά, ἣ διερμηνευομένη λέγεται Δορκάς· αὕτη ἦν πλήρης ⸂ἔργων ἀγαθῶν⸃ καὶ ἐλεημοσυνῶν ὧν ἐποίει.
verses.translit: En Ioppe de tis en mathitria onomati Tavitha, e diermineyomeni legetai Dorkas* auti en pliris ergon agathon kai eleimosynon on epoiei.
verses.translation: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.

verses.original: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἀσθενήσασαν αὐτὴν ἀποθανεῖν· λούσαντες δὲ ⸂ἔθηκαν αὐτὴν⸃ ἐν ὑπερῴῳ.
verses.translit: egeneto de en tais emerais ekeinais asthenisasan auten apothanein* loysantes de ethikan auten en uperoo.
verses.translation: And it came to pass in those days, that she was sick, and died: whom when they had washed, they laid her in an upper chamber.

verses.original: ἐγγὺς δὲ οὔσης Λύδδας τῇ Ἰόππῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Πέτρος ἐστὶν ἐν αὐτῇ ἀπέστειλαν ⸂δύο ἄνδρας⸃ πρὸς αὐτὸν παρακαλοῦντες· Μὴ ⸀ὀκνήσῃς διελθεῖν ἕως ⸀ἡμῶν·
verses.translit: eggus de ousis Lyddas te Ioppe oi mathitai akoysantes oti Petros estin en aute apesteilan dyo andras pros auton parakalountes* Me oknises dielthein eos emon*
verses.translation: And forasmuch as Lydda was nigh to Joppa, and the disciples had heard that Peter was there, they sent unto him two men, desiring him that he would not delay to come to them.

verses.original: ἀναστὰς δὲ Πέτρος συνῆλθεν αὐτοῖς· ὃν παραγενόμενον ἀνήγαγον εἰς τὸ ὑπερῷον, καὶ παρέστησαν αὐτῷ πᾶσαι αἱ χῆραι κλαίουσαι καὶ ἐπιδεικνύμεναι χιτῶνας καὶ ἱμάτια ὅσα ἐποίει μετʼ αὐτῶν οὖσα ἡ Δορκάς.
verses.translit: anastas de Petros synelthen autois* on paragenomenon anigagon eis to uperoon, kai parestisan auto pasai ai herai klaioysai kai epideiknymenai hitonas kai imatia osa epoiei met' auton ousa e Dorkas.
verses.translation: Then Peter arose and went with them. When he was come, they brought him into the upper chamber: and all the widows stood by him weeping, and shewing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them.

verses.original: ἐκβαλὼν δὲ ἔξω πάντας ὁ Πέτρος ⸀καὶ θεὶς τὰ γόνατα προσηύξατο, καὶ ἐπιστρέψας πρὸς τὸ σῶμα εἶπεν· Ταβιθά, ἀνάστηθι. ἡ δὲ ἤνοιξεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῆς, καὶ ἰδοῦσα τὸν Πέτρον ἀνεκάθισεν.
verses.translit: ekvalon de exo pantas o Petros kai theis ta gonata prosiyxato, kai epistrepsas pros to soma eipen* Tavitha, anastithi. e de enoixen tous ofthalmous autes, kai idousa ton Petron anekathisen.
verses.translation: But Peter put them all forth, and kneeled down, and prayed; and turning him to the body said, Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes: and when she saw Peter, she sat up.

verses.original: δοὺς δὲ αὐτῇ χεῖρα ἀνέστησεν αὐτήν, φωνήσας δὲ τοὺς ἁγίους καὶ τὰς χήρας παρέστησεν αὐτὴν ζῶσαν.
verses.translit: dous de aute heira anestisen autin, fonisas de tous agioys kai tas hiras parestisen auten zosan.
verses.translation: And he gave her his hand, and lifted her up, and when he had called the saints and widows, presented her alive.

verses.original: γνωστὸν δὲ ἐγένετο καθʼ ὅλης ⸀τῆς Ἰόππης, καὶ ⸂ἐπίστευσαν πολλοὶ⸃ ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον.
verses.translit: gnoston de egeneto kath' olis tes Ioppis, kai episteysan polloi epi ton kyrion.
verses.translation: And it was known throughout all Joppa; and many believed in the Lord.

verses.original: ἐγένετο ⸀δὲ ἡμέρας ἱκανὰς ⸀μεῖναι ἐν Ἰόππῃ παρά τινι Σίμωνι βυρσεῖ.
verses.translit: egeneto de emeras ikanas meinai en Ioppe para tini Simoni vyrsei.
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that he tarried many days in Joppa with one Simon a tanner.

verses.original: Ἀνὴρ δέ ⸀τις ἐν Καισαρείᾳ ὀνόματι Κορνήλιος, ἑκατοντάρχης ἐκ σπείρης τῆς καλουμένης Ἰταλικῆς,
verses.translit: Aner de tis en Kaisareia onomati Kornilios, ekatontarhis ek speiris tes kaloymenis Italikes,
verses.translation: There was a certain man in Cæsarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band ,

verses.original: εὐσεβὴς καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν θεὸν σὺν παντὶ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ, ⸀ποιῶν ἐλεημοσύνας πολλὰς τῷ λαῷ καὶ δεόμενος τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ παντός,
verses.translit: euseves kai fovoymenos ton theon sun panti to oiko autou, poion eleimosynas pollas to lao kai deomenos tou theou dia pantos,
verses.translation: A devout man , and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.

verses.original: εἶδεν ἐν ὁράματι φανερῶς ὡσεὶ ⸀περὶ ὥραν ἐνάτην τῆς ἡμέρας ἄγγελον τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθόντα πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ εἰπόντα αὐτῷ· Κορνήλιε.
verses.translit: eiden en oramati faneros osei peri oran enatin tes emeras aggelon tou theou eiselthonta pros auton kai eiponta auto* Kornilie.
verses.translation: He saw in a vision evidently about the ninth hour of the day an angel of God coming in to him, and saying unto him, Cornelius.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἔμφοβος γενόμενος εἶπεν· Τί ἐστιν, κύριε; εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ· Αἱ προσευχαί σου καὶ αἱ ἐλεημοσύναι σου ἀνέβησαν εἰς μνημόσυνον ⸀ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θεοῦ·
verses.translit: o de atenisas auto kai emfovos genomenos eipen* Ti estin, kyrie; eipen de auto* Ai proseyhai soy kai ai eleimosynai soy anevisan eis mnimosynon emprosthen tou theou*
verses.translation: And when he looked on him, he was afraid, and said, What is it, Lord? And he said unto him, Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.

verses.original: καὶ νῦν πέμψον ⸂ἄνδρας εἰς Ἰόππην⸃ καὶ μετάπεμψαι Σίμωνά ⸂τινα ὃς ἐπικαλεῖται Πέτρος⸃·
verses.translit: kai nun pempson andras eis Ioppin kai metapempsai Simona tina os epikaleitai Petros*
verses.translation: And now send men to Joppa, and call for one Simon, whose surname is Peter:

verses.original: οὗτος ξενίζεται παρά τινι Σίμωνι βυρσεῖ, ᾧ ἐστιν οἰκία παρὰ θάλασσαν.
verses.translit: outos xenizetai para tini Simoni vyrsei, o estin oikia para thalassan.
verses.translation: He lodgeth with one Simon a tanner, whose house is by the sea side: he shall tell thee what thou oughtest to do.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἀπῆλθεν ὁ ἄγγελος ὁ λαλῶν ⸀αὐτῷ, φωνήσας δύο τῶν ⸀οἰκετῶν καὶ στρατιώτην εὐσεβῆ τῶν προσκαρτερούντων αὐτῷ
verses.translit: os de apelthen o aggelos o lalon auto, fonisas dyo ton oiketon kai stratiotin euseve ton proskarteroynton auto
verses.translation: And when the angel which spake unto Cornelius was departed, he called two of his household servants, and a devout soldier of them that waited on him continually;

verses.original: καὶ ἐξηγησάμενος ⸂ἅπαντα αὐτοῖς⸃ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν Ἰόππην.
verses.translit: kai exigisamenos apanta autois apesteilen autous eis ten Ioppin.
verses.translation: And when he had declared all these things unto them, he sent them to Joppa.

verses.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ὁδοιπορούντων ἐκείνων καὶ τῇ πόλει ἐγγιζόντων ἀνέβη Πέτρος ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα προσεύξασθαι περὶ ὥραν ἕκτην.
verses.translit: Te de epayrion odoiporoynton ekeinon kai te polei eggizonton anevi Petros epi to doma proseyxasthai peri oran ektin.
verses.translation: On the morrow, as they went on their journey, and drew nigh unto the city, Peter went up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour:

verses.original: ἐγένετο δὲ πρόσπεινος καὶ ἤθελεν γεύσασθαι· παρασκευαζόντων δὲ ⸀αὐτῶν ⸀ἐγένετο ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ἔκστασις,
verses.translit: egeneto de prospeinos kai ethelen geysasthai* paraskeyazonton de auton egeneto ep' auton ekstasis,
verses.translation: And he became very hungry, and would have eaten: but while they made ready, he fell into a trance,

verses.original: καὶ θεωρεῖ τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεῳγμένον καὶ ⸀καταβαῖνον σκεῦός τι ὡς ὀθόνην μεγάλην τέσσαρσιν ⸀ἀρχαῖς καθιέμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς,
verses.translit: kai theorei ton ouranon aneogmenon kai katavainon skeuos ti os othonin megalin tessarsin arhais kathiemenon epi tes ges,
verses.translation: And saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners, and let down to the earth:

verses.original: ἐν ᾧ ὑπῆρχεν πάντα τὰ τετράποδα ⸂καὶ ἑρπετὰ τῆς γῆς καὶ⸃ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
verses.translit: en o uperhen panta ta tetrapoda kai erpeta tes ges kai peteina tou ouranou.
verses.translation: Wherein were all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.

verses.original: καὶ ἐγένετο φωνὴ πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἀναστάς, Πέτρε, θῦσον καὶ φάγε.
verses.translit: kai egeneto fone pros auton* Anastas, Petre, thuson kai fage.
verses.translation: And there came a voice to him, Rise, Peter; kill, and eat.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος εἶπεν· Μηδαμῶς, κύριε, ὅτι οὐδέποτε ἔφαγον πᾶν κοινὸν ⸀καὶ ἀκάθαρτον.
verses.translit: o de Petros eipen* Midamos, kyrie, oti oudepote efagon pan koinon kai akatharton.
verses.translation: But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean.

verses.original: καὶ φωνὴ πάλιν ἐκ δευτέρου πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἃ ὁ θεὸς ἐκαθάρισεν σὺ μὴ κοίνου.
verses.translit: kai fone palin ek deyteroy pros auton* A o theos ekatharisen su me koinoy.
verses.translation: And the voice spake unto him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.

verses.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τρίς, καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἀνελήμφθη τὸ σκεῦος εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.
verses.translit: touto de egeneto epi tris, kai euthus anelimfthi to skeuos eis ton ouranon.
verses.translation: This was done thrice: and the vessel was received up again into heaven.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ διηπόρει ὁ Πέτρος τί ἂν εἴη τὸ ὅραμα ὃ εἶδεν, ⸀ἰδοὺ οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ ἀπεσταλμένοι ⸀ὑπὸ τοῦ Κορνηλίου διερωτήσαντες τὴν οἰκίαν ⸀τοῦ Σίμωνος ἐπέστησαν ἐπὶ τὸν πυλῶνα,
verses.translit: Os de en eayto diiporei o Petros ti an eii to orama o eiden, idou oi andres oi apestalmenoi upo tou Kornilioy dierotisantes ten oikian tou Simonos epestisan epi ton pylona,
verses.translation: Now while Peter doubted in himself what this vision which he had seen should mean, behold, the men which were sent from Cornelius had made enquiry for Simon’s house, and stood before the gate,

verses.original: καὶ φωνήσαντες ⸀ἐπυνθάνοντο εἰ Σίμων ὁ ἐπικαλούμενος Πέτρος ἐνθάδε ξενίζεται.
verses.translit: kai fonisantes epynthanonto ei Simon o epikaloymenos Petros enthade xenizetai.
verses.translation: And called, and asked whether Simon, which was surnamed Peter, were lodged there.

verses.original: τοῦ δὲ Πέτρου διενθυμουμένου περὶ τοῦ ὁράματος εἶπεν ⸂αὐτῷ τὸ πνεῦμα⸃· Ἰδοὺ ⸀ἄνδρες ⸀ζητοῦντές σε·
verses.translit: tou de Petroy dienthymoymenoy peri tou oramatos eipen auto to pneuma* Idou andres zitountes se*
verses.translation: While Peter thought on the vision, the Spirit said unto him, Behold, three men seek thee.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ἀναστὰς κατάβηθι καὶ πορεύου σὺν αὐτοῖς μηδὲν διακρινόμενος, ⸀ὅτι ἐγὼ ἀπέσταλκα αὐτούς.
verses.translit: alla anastas katavithi kai poreyoy sun autois miden diakrinomenos, oti ego apestalka autoys.
verses.translation: Arise therefore, and get thee down, and go with them, doubting nothing: for I have sent them.

verses.original: καταβὰς δὲ Πέτρος πρὸς τοὺς ἄνδρας εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ εἰμι ὃν ζητεῖτε· τίς ἡ αἰτία διʼ ἣν πάρεστε;
verses.translit: katavas de Petros pros tous andras eipen* Idou ego eimi on ziteite* tis e aitia di' en pareste;
verses.translation: Then Peter went down to the men which were sent unto him from Cornelius; and said, Behold, I am he whom ye seek: what is the cause wherefore ye are come?

verses.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Κορνήλιος ἑκατοντάρχης, ἀνὴρ δίκαιος καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν θεὸν μαρτυρούμενός τε ὑπὸ ὅλου τοῦ ἔθνους τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἐχρηματίσθη ὑπὸ ἀγγέλου ἁγίου μεταπέμψασθαί σε εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ῥήματα παρὰ σοῦ.
verses.translit: oi de eipan* Kornilios ekatontarhis, aner dikaios kai fovoymenos ton theon martyroymenos te upo oloy tou ethnoys ton Ioydaion, ehrimatisthi upo aggeloy agioy metapempsasthai se eis ton oikon autou kai akousai Rimata para sou.
verses.translation: And they said, Cornelius the centurion, a just man, and one that feareth God, and of good report among all the nation of the Jews, was warned from God by an holy angel to send for thee into his house, and to hear words of thee.

verses.original: εἰσκαλεσάμενος οὖν αὐτοὺς ἐξένισεν. Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ⸀ἀναστὰς ἐξῆλθεν σὺν αὐτοῖς, καί τινες τῶν ἀδελφῶν τῶν ἀπὸ Ἰόππης συνῆλθον αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: eiskalesamenos oun autous exenisen. Te de epayrion anastas exelthen sun autois, kai tines ton adelfon ton apo Ioppis synelthon auto.
verses.translation: Then called he them in, and lodged them . And on the morrow Peter went away with them, and certain brethren from Joppa accompanied him.

verses.original: ⸂τῇ δὲ⸃ ἐπαύριον ⸀εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν Καισάρειαν. ὁ δὲ Κορνήλιος ἦν προσδοκῶν αὐτοὺς συγκαλεσάμενος τοὺς συγγενεῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἀναγκαίους φίλους.
verses.translit: te de epayrion eiselthen eis ten Kaisareian. o de Kornilios en prosdokon autous sygkalesamenos tous syggeneis autou kai tous anagkaioys filoys.
verses.translation: And the morrow after they entered into Cæsarea. And Cornelius waited for them, and had called together his kinsmen and near friends.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο τοῦ εἰσελθεῖν τὸν Πέτρον, συναντήσας αὐτῷ ὁ Κορνήλιος πεσὼν ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας προσεκύνησεν.
verses.translit: os de egeneto tou eiselthein ton Petron, synantisas auto o Kornilios peson epi tous podas prosekynisen.
verses.translation: And as Peter was coming in, Cornelius met him, and fell down at his feet, and worshipped him .

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ⸂ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν⸃ λέγων· Ἀνάστηθι· καὶ ἐγὼ αὐτὸς ἄνθρωπός εἰμι.
verses.translit: o de Petros egeiren auton legon* Anastithi* kai ego autos anthropos eimi.
verses.translation: But Peter took him up, saying, Stand up; I myself also am a man.

verses.original: καὶ συνομιλῶν αὐτῷ εἰσῆλθεν, καὶ εὑρίσκει συνεληλυθότας πολλούς,
verses.translit: kai synomilon auto eiselthen, kai euriskei synelilythotas polloys,
verses.translation: And as he talked with him, he went in, and found many that were come together.

verses.original: ἔφη τε πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ὡς ἀθέμιτόν ἐστιν ἀνδρὶ Ἰουδαίῳ κολλᾶσθαι ἢ προσέρχεσθαι ἀλλοφύλῳ· κἀμοὶ ὁ θεὸς ἔδειξεν μηδένα κοινὸν ἢ ἀκάθαρτον λέγειν ἄνθρωπον·
verses.translit: efi te pros autoys* Umeis epistasthe os athemiton estin andri Ioydaio kollasthai e proserhesthai allofylo* kamoi o theos edeixen midena koinon e akatharton legein anthropon*
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation; but God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.

verses.original: διὸ καὶ ἀναντιρρήτως ἦλθον μεταπεμφθείς. πυνθάνομαι οὖν τίνι λόγῳ μετεπέμψασθέ με.
verses.translit: dio kai anantirritos elthon metapemftheis. pynthanomai oun tini logo metepempsasthe me.
verses.translation: Therefore came I unto you without gainsaying, as soon as I was sent for: I ask therefore for what intent ye have sent for me?

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ Κορνήλιος ἔφη· Ἀπὸ τετάρτης ἡμέρας μέχρι ταύτης τῆς ὥρας ⸀ἤμην τὴν ⸀ἐνάτην προσευχόμενος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ μου, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ἔστη ἐνώπιόν μου ἐν ἐσθῆτι λαμπρᾷ
verses.translit: Kai o Kornilios efi* Apo tetartis emeras mehri taytis tes oras emin ten enatin proseyhomenos en to oiko moy, kai idou aner esti enopion moy en estheti lampra
verses.translation: And Cornelius said, Four days ago I was fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour I prayed in my house, and, behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing,

verses.original: καὶ φησί· Κορνήλιε, εἰσηκούσθη σου ἡ προσευχὴ καὶ αἱ ἐλεημοσύναι σου ἐμνήσθησαν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: kai fisi* Kornilie, eisikoysthi soy e proseyhe kai ai eleimosynai soy emnisthisan enopion tou theou.
verses.translation: And said, Cornelius, thy prayer is heard, and thine alms are had in remembrance in the sight of God.

verses.original: πέμψον οὖν εἰς Ἰόππην καὶ μετακάλεσαι Σίμωνα ὃς ἐπικαλεῖται Πέτρος· οὗτος ξενίζεται ἐν οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος βυρσέως παρὰ ⸀θάλασσαν.
verses.translit: pempson oun eis Ioppin kai metakalesai Simona os epikaleitai Petros* outos xenizetai en oikia Simonos vyrseos para thalassan.
verses.translation: Send therefore to Joppa, and call hither Simon, whose surname is Peter; he is lodged in the house of one Simon a tanner by the sea side: who, when he cometh, shall speak unto thee.

verses.original: ἐξαυτῆς οὖν ἔπεμψα πρὸς σέ, σύ τε καλῶς ἐποίησας παραγενόμενος. νῦν οὖν πάντες ἡμεῖς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ πάρεσμεν ἀκοῦσαι πάντα τὰ προστεταγμένα σοι ὑπὸ τοῦ ⸀κυρίου.
verses.translit: exaytes oun epempsa pros se, sy te kalos epoiisas paragenomenos. nun oun pantes emeis enopion tou theou paresmen akousai panta ta prostetagmena soi upo tou kyrioy.
verses.translation: Immediately therefore I sent to thee; and thou hast well done that thou art come. Now therefore are we all here present before God, to hear all things that are commanded thee of God.

verses.original: Ἀνοίξας δὲ Πέτρος τὸ στόμα εἶπεν· Ἐπʼ ἀληθείας καταλαμβάνομαι ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν προσωπολήμπτης ὁ θεός,
verses.translit: Anoixas de Petros to stoma eipen* Ep' alitheias katalamvanomai oti ouk estin prosopolimptis o theos,
verses.translation: Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:

verses.original: ἀλλʼ ἐν παντὶ ἔθνει ὁ φοβούμενος αὐτὸν καὶ ἐργαζόμενος δικαιοσύνην δεκτὸς αὐτῷ ἐστιν.
verses.translit: all' en panti ethnei o fovoymenos auton kai ergazomenos dikaiosynin dektos auto estin.
verses.translation: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.

verses.original: τὸν λόγον ⸀ὃν ἀπέστειλεν τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ εὐαγγελιζόμενος εἰρήνην διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· οὗτός ἐστιν πάντων κύριος.
verses.translit: ton logon on apesteilen tois yiois Israel euaggelizomenos eirinin dia Iisou Hristou* outos estin panton kyrios.
verses.translation: The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: (he is Lord of all:)

verses.original: ὑμεῖς οἴδατε τὸ γενόμενον ῥῆμα καθʼ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας, ⸀ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα ὃ ἐκήρυξεν Ἰωάννης,
verses.translit: umeis oidate to genomenon Rema kath' olis tes Ioydaias, arxamenos apo tes Galilaias meta to vaptisma o ekiryxen Ioannis,
verses.translation: That word, I say , ye know, which was published throughout all Judæa, and began from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached;

verses.original: Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρέθ, ὡς ἔχρισεν αὐτὸν ὁ θεὸς πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ δυνάμει, ὃς διῆλθεν εὐεργετῶν καὶ ἰώμενος πάντας τοὺς καταδυναστευομένους ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου, ὅτι ὁ θεὸς ἦν μετʼ αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: Iisoun ton apo Nazareth, os ehrisen auton o theos pneymati agio kai dynamei, os dielthen euergeton kai iomenos pantas tous katadynasteyomenoys upo tou diavoloy, oti o theos en met' autou*
verses.translation: How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him.

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἡμεῖς μάρτυρες πάντων ὧν ἐποίησεν ἔν τε τῇ χώρᾳ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ⸀καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ· ὃν καὶ ἀνεῖλαν κρεμάσαντες ἐπὶ ξύλου.
verses.translit: kai emeis martyres panton on epoiisen en te te hora ton Ioydaion kai Ieroysalim* on kai aneilan kremasantes epi xyloy.
verses.translation: And we are witnesses of all things which he did both in the land of the Jews, and in Jerusalem; whom they slew and hanged on a tree:

verses.original: τοῦτον ὁ θεὸς ἤγειρεν ⸀τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν ἐμφανῆ γενέσθαι,
verses.translit: touton o theos egeiren te trite emera kai edoken auton emfane genesthai,
verses.translation: Him God raised up the third day, and shewed him openly;

verses.original: οὐ παντὶ τῷ λαῷ ἀλλὰ μάρτυσι τοῖς προκεχειροτονημένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἡμῖν, οἵτινες συνεφάγομεν καὶ συνεπίομεν αὐτῷ μετὰ τὸ ἀναστῆναι αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν·
verses.translit: ou panti to lao alla martysi tois prokeheirotonimenois upo tou theou, emin, oitines synefagomen kai synepiomen auto meta to anastenai auton ek nekron*
verses.translation: Not to all the people, but unto witnesses chosen before of God, even to us, who did eat and drink with him after he rose from the dead.

verses.original: καὶ παρήγγειλεν ἡμῖν κηρύξαι τῷ λαῷ καὶ διαμαρτύρασθαι ὅτι ⸀οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ὡρισμένος ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ κριτὴς ζώντων καὶ νεκρῶν.
verses.translit: kai pariggeilen emin kiryxai to lao kai diamartyrasthai oti outos estin o orismenos upo tou theou krites zonton kai nekron.
verses.translation: And he commanded us to preach unto the people, and to testify that it is he which was ordained of God to be the Judge of quick and dead.

verses.original: τούτῳ πάντες οἱ προφῆται μαρτυροῦσιν, ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν λαβεῖν διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ πάντα τὸν πιστεύοντα εἰς αὐτόν.
verses.translit: toyto pantes oi profetai martyrousin, afesin amartion lavein dia tou onomatos autou panta ton pisteyonta eis auton.
verses.translation: To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.

verses.original: Ἔτι λαλοῦντος τοῦ Πέτρου τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα ἐπέπεσε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας τὸν λόγον.
verses.translit: Eti lalountos tou Petroy ta Rimata tauta epepese to pneuma to agion epi pantas tous akoyontas ton logon.
verses.translation: While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξέστησαν οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς πιστοὶ ⸀ὅσοι συνῆλθαν τῷ Πέτρῳ, ὅτι καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ ἔθνη ἡ δωρεὰ τοῦ ⸂ἁγίου πνεύματος⸃ ἐκκέχυται·
verses.translit: kai exestisan oi ek peritomes pistoi osoi synelthan to Petro, oti kai epi ta ethni e dorea tou agioy pneymatos ekkehytai*
verses.translation: And they of the circumcision which believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost.

verses.original: ἤκουον γὰρ αὐτῶν λαλούντων γλώσσαις καὶ μεγαλυνόντων τὸν θεόν. τότε ⸀ἀπεκρίθη Πέτρος·
verses.translit: ekoyon gar auton laloynton glossais kai megalynonton ton theon. tote apekrithi Petros*
verses.translation: For they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God. Then answered Peter,

verses.original: Μήτι τὸ ὕδωρ ⸂δύναται κωλῦσαί⸃ τις τοῦ μὴ βαπτισθῆναι τούτους οἵτινες τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἔλαβον ⸀ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς;
verses.translit: Miti to udor dynatai kolusai tis tou me vaptisthenai toytoys oitines to pneuma to agion elavon os kai emeis;
verses.translation: Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we?

verses.original: προσέταξεν ⸀δὲ αὐτοὺς ⸂ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ βαπτισθῆναι⸃. τότε ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν ἐπιμεῖναι ἡμέρας τινάς.
verses.translit: prosetaxen de autous en to onomati Iisou Hristou vaptisthenai. tote erotisan auton epimeinai emeras tinas.
verses.translation: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then prayed they him to tarry certain days.

verses.original: Ἤκουσαν δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ οἱ ὄντες κατὰ τὴν Ἰουδαίαν ὅτι καὶ τὰ ἔθνη ἐδέξαντο τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: Ekoysan de oi apostoloi kai oi adelfoi oi ontes kata ten Ioydaian oti kai ta ethni edexanto ton logon tou theou.
verses.translation: And the apostles and brethren that were in Judæa heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.

verses.original: ⸂ὅτε δὲ⸃ ἀνέβη Πέτρος εἰς ⸀Ἰερουσαλήμ, διεκρίνοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς
verses.translit: ote de anevi Petros eis Ieroysalim, diekrinonto pros auton oi ek peritomes
verses.translation: And when Peter was come up to Jerusalem, they that were of the circumcision contended with him,

verses.original: λέγοντες ὅτι ⸂Εἰσῆλθες πρὸς ἄνδρας ἀκροβυστίαν ἔχοντας καὶ συνέφαγες⸃ αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: legontes oti Eiselthes pros andras akrovystian ehontas kai synefages autois.
verses.translation: Saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.

verses.original: ἀρξάμενος ⸀δὲ Πέτρος ἐξετίθετο αὐτοῖς καθεξῆς λέγων·
verses.translit: arxamenos de Petros exetitheto autois kathexes legon*
verses.translation: But Peter rehearsed the matter from the beginning, and expounded it by order unto them, saying,

verses.original: Ἐγὼ ἤμην ἐν πόλει Ἰόππῃ προσευχόμενος καὶ εἶδον ἐν ἐκστάσει ὅραμα, καταβαῖνον σκεῦός τι ὡς ὀθόνην μεγάλην τέσσαρσιν ἀρχαῖς καθιεμένην ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἦλθεν ἄχρι ἐμοῦ·
verses.translit: Ego emin en polei Ioppe proseyhomenos kai eidon en ekstasei orama, katavainon skeuos ti os othonin megalin tessarsin arhais kathiemenin ek tou ouranou, kai elthen ahri emou*
verses.translation: I was in the city of Joppa praying: and in a trance I saw a vision, A certain vessel descend, as it had been a great sheet, let down from heaven by four corners; and it came even to me:

verses.original: εἰς ἣν ἀτενίσας κατενόουν καὶ εἶδον τὰ τετράποδα τῆς γῆς καὶ τὰ θηρία καὶ τὰ ἑρπετὰ καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ·
verses.translit: eis en atenisas katenooyn kai eidon ta tetrapoda tes ges kai ta thiria kai ta erpeta kai ta peteina tou ouranou*
verses.translation: Upon the which when I had fastened mine eyes, I considered, and saw fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.

verses.original: ἤκουσα δὲ ⸀καὶ φωνῆς λεγούσης μοι· Ἀναστάς, Πέτρε, θῦσον καὶ φάγε.
verses.translit: ekoysa de kai fones legoysis moi* Anastas, Petre, thuson kai fage.
verses.translation: And I heard a voice saying unto me, Arise, Peter; slay and eat.

verses.original: εἶπον δέ· Μηδαμῶς, κύριε, ⸀ὅτι κοινὸν ἢ ἀκάθαρτον οὐδέποτε εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ στόμα μου.
verses.translit: eipon de* Midamos, kyrie, oti koinon e akatharton oudepote eiselthen eis to stoma moy.
verses.translation: But I said, Not so, Lord: for nothing common or unclean hath at any time entered into my mouth.

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ ⸂φωνὴ ἐκ δευτέρου⸃ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ· Ἃ ὁ θεὸς ἐκαθάρισεν σὺ μὴ κοίνου.
verses.translit: apekrithi de fone ek deyteroy ek tou ouranou* A o theos ekatharisen su me koinoy.
verses.translation: But the voice answered me again from heaven, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.

verses.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τρίς, καὶ ⸂ἀνεσπάσθη πάλιν⸃ ἅπαντα εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.
verses.translit: touto de egeneto epi tris, kai anespasthi palin apanta eis ton ouranon.
verses.translation: And this was done three times: and all were drawn up again into heaven.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐξαυτῆς τρεῖς ἄνδρες ἐπέστησαν ἐπὶ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐν ᾗ ⸀ἦμεν, ἀπεσταλμένοι ἀπὸ Καισαρείας πρός με.
verses.translit: kai idou exaytes treis andres epestisan epi ten oikian en e emen, apestalmenoi apo Kaisareias pros me.
verses.translation: And, behold, immediately there were three men already come unto the house where I was, sent from Cæsarea unto me.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ⸂τὸ πνεῦμά μοι⸃ συνελθεῖν αὐτοῖς μηδὲν ⸀διακρίναντα. ἦλθον δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ καὶ οἱ ἓξ ἀδελφοὶ οὗτοι, καὶ εἰσήλθομεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ ἀνδρός.
verses.translit: eipen de to pneuma moi synelthein autois miden diakrinanta. elthon de sun emoi kai oi ex adelfoi outoi, kai eisilthomen eis ton oikon tou andros.
verses.translation: And the Spirit bade me go with them, nothing doubting. Moreover these six brethren accompanied me, and we entered into the man’s house:

verses.original: ἀπήγγειλεν ⸀δὲ ἡμῖν πῶς εἶδεν τὸν ἄγγελον ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ σταθέντα καὶ ⸀εἰπόντα· Ἀπόστειλον εἰς ⸀Ἰόππην καὶ μετάπεμψαι Σίμωνα τὸν ἐπικαλούμενον Πέτρον,
verses.translit: apiggeilen de emin pos eiden ton aggelon en to oiko autou stathenta kai eiponta* Aposteilon eis Ioppin kai metapempsai Simona ton epikaloymenon Petron,
verses.translation: And he shewed us how he had seen an angel in his house, which stood and said unto him, Send men to Joppa, and call for Simon, whose surname is Peter;

verses.original: ὃς λαλήσει ῥήματα πρὸς σὲ ἐν οἷς σωθήσῃ σὺ καὶ πᾶς ὁ οἶκός σου.
verses.translit: os lalisei Rimata pros se en ois sothise su kai pas o oikos soy.
verses.translation: Who shall tell thee words, whereby thou and all thy house shall be saved.

verses.original: ἐν δὲ τῷ ἄρξασθαί με λαλεῖν ἐπέπεσεν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς ὥσπερ καὶ ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς ἐν ἀρχῇ.
verses.translit: en de to arxasthai me lalein epepesen to pneuma to agion ep' autous osper kai ef' emas en arhe.
verses.translation: And as I began to speak, the Holy Ghost fell on them, as on us at the beginning.

verses.original: ἐμνήσθην δὲ τοῦ ῥήματος ⸀τοῦ κυρίου ὡς ἔλεγεν· Ἰωάννης μὲν ἐβάπτισεν ὕδατι, ὑμεῖς δὲ βαπτισθήσεσθε ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ.
verses.translit: emnisthin de tou Rimatos tou kyrioy os elegen* Ioannis men evaptisen udati, umeis de vaptisthisesthe en pneymati agio.
verses.translation: Then remembered I the word of the Lord, how that he said, John indeed baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost.

verses.original: εἰ οὖν τὴν ἴσην δωρεὰν ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς ὡς καὶ ἡμῖν πιστεύσασιν ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, ⸀ἐγὼ τίς ἤμην δυνατὸς κωλῦσαι τὸν θεόν;
verses.translit: ei oun ten isin dorean edoken autois o theos os kai emin pisteysasin epi ton kyrion Iisoun Hriston, ego tis emin dynatos kolusai ton theon;
verses.translation: Forasmuch then as God gave them the like gift as he did unto us, who believed on the Lord Jesus Christ; what was I, that I could withstand God?

verses.original: ἀκούσαντες δὲ ταῦτα ἡσύχασαν καὶ ⸀ἐδόξασαν τὸν θεὸν λέγοντες· ⸀Ἄρα καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ὁ θεὸς τὴν μετάνοιαν ⸂εἰς ζωὴν ἔδωκεν⸃.
verses.translit: akoysantes de tauta esyhasan kai edoxasan ton theon legontes* Ara kai tois ethnesin o theos ten metanoian eis zoen edoken.
verses.translation: When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life.

verses.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διασπαρέντες ἀπὸ τῆς θλίψεως τῆς γενομένης ἐπὶ Στεφάνῳ διῆλθον ἕως Φοινίκης καὶ Κύπρου καὶ Ἀντιοχείας μηδενὶ λαλοῦντες τὸν λόγον εἰ μὴ μόνον Ἰουδαίοις.
verses.translit: Oi men oun diasparentes apo tes thlipseos tes genomenis epi Stefano dielthon eos Foinikis kai Kyproy kai Antioheias mideni lalountes ton logon ei me monon Ioydaiois.
verses.translation: Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch, preaching the word to none but unto the Jews only.

verses.original: ἦσαν δέ τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν ἄνδρες Κύπριοι καὶ Κυρηναῖοι, οἵτινες ⸀ἐλθόντες εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν ἐλάλουν ⸀καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ⸀Ἑλληνιστάς, εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: esan de tines ex auton andres Kyprioi kai Kyrinaioi, oitines elthontes eis Antioheian elaloyn kai pros tous Ellinistas, euaggelizomenoi ton kyrion Iisoun.
verses.translation: And some of them were men of Cyprus and Cyrene, which, when they were come to Antioch, spake unto the Grecians, preaching the Lord Jesus.

verses.original: καὶ ἦν χεὶρ κυρίου μετʼ αὐτῶν, πολύς τε ἀριθμὸς ⸀ὁ πιστεύσας ἐπέστρεψεν ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον.
verses.translit: kai en heir kyrioy met' auton, polys te arithmos o pisteysas epestrepsen epi ton kyrion.
verses.translation: And the hand of the Lord was with them: and a great number believed, and turned unto the Lord.

verses.original: ἠκούσθη δὲ ὁ λόγος εἰς τὰ ὦτα τῆς ἐκκλησίας τῆς ⸀οὔσης ἐν ⸀Ἰερουσαλὴμ περὶ αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν ⸀Βαρναβᾶν ἕως Ἀντιοχείας·
verses.translit: ekoysthi de o logos eis ta ota tes ekklisias tes ousis en Ieroysalem peri auton, kai exapesteilan Varnavan eos Antioheias*
verses.translation: Then tidings of these things came unto the ears of the church which was in Jerusalem: and they sent forth Barnabas, that he should go as far as Antioch.

verses.original: ὃς παραγενόμενος καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν χάριν ⸀τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐχάρη καὶ παρεκάλει πάντας τῇ προθέσει τῆς καρδίας ⸀προσμένειν τῷ κυρίῳ,
verses.translit: os paragenomenos kai idon ten harin ten tou theou, ehari kai parekalei pantas te prothesei tes kardias prosmenein to kyrio,
verses.translation: Who, when he came, and had seen the grace of God, was glad, and exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would cleave unto the Lord.

verses.original: ὅτι ἦν ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς καὶ πλήρης πνεύματος ἁγίου καὶ πίστεως. καὶ προσετέθη ὄχλος ἱκανὸς τῷ κυρίῳ.
verses.translit: oti en aner agathos kai pliris pneymatos agioy kai pisteos. kai prosetethi ohlos ikanos to kyrio.
verses.translation: For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Ghost and of faith: and much people was added unto the Lord.

verses.original: ἐξῆλθεν δὲ εἰς ⸀Ταρσὸν ἀναζητῆσαι Σαῦλον,
verses.translit: exelthen de eis Tarson anazitesai Saulon,
verses.translation: Then departed Barnabas to Tarsus, for to seek Saul:

verses.original: καὶ εὑρὼν ⸀ἤγαγεν εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν. ἐγένετο δὲ ⸂αὐτοῖς καὶ⸃ ἐνιαυτὸν ὅλον συναχθῆναι ⸀ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ καὶ διδάξαι ὄχλον ἱκανόν, χρηματίσαι τε ⸀πρώτως ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ τοὺς μαθητὰς Χριστιανούς.
verses.translit: kai euron egagen eis Antioheian. egeneto de autois kai eniayton olon synahthenai en te ekklisia kai didaxai ohlon ikanon, hrimatisai te protos en Antioheia tous mathitas Hristianoys.
verses.translation: And when he had found him, he brought him unto Antioch. And it came to pass, that a whole year they assembled themselves with the church, and taught much people. And the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.

verses.original: Ἐν ταύταις δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις κατῆλθον ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων προφῆται εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν·
verses.translit: En taytais de tais emerais katelthon apo Ierosolymon profetai eis Antioheian*
verses.translation: And in these days came prophets from Jerusalem unto Antioch.

verses.original: ἀναστὰς δὲ εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν ὀνόματι Ἅγαβος ἐσήμανεν διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος λιμὸν ⸀μεγάλην μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι ἐφʼ ὅλην τὴν οἰκουμένην· ⸀ἥτις ἐγένετο ἐπὶ ⸀Κλαυδίου.
verses.translit: anastas de eis ex auton onomati Agavos esimanen dia tou pneymatos limon megalin mellein esesthai ef' olin ten oikoymenin* etis egeneto epi Klaydioy.
verses.translation: And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the Spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Cæsar.

verses.original: τῶν δὲ μαθητῶν καθὼς εὐπορεῖτό τις ὥρισαν ἕκαστος αὐτῶν εἰς διακονίαν πέμψαι τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ ἀδελφοῖς·
verses.translit: ton de mathiton kathos euporeito tis orisan ekastos auton eis diakonian pempsai tois katoikousin en te Ioydaia adelfois*
verses.translation: Then the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren which dwelt in Judæa:

verses.original: ὃ καὶ ἐποίησαν ἀποστείλαντες πρὸς τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους διὰ χειρὸς Βαρναβᾶ καὶ Σαύλου.
verses.translit: o kai epoiisan aposteilantes pros tous presvyteroys dia heiros Varnava kai Sayloy.
verses.translation: Which also they did, and sent it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.

verses.original: Κατʼ ἐκεῖνον δὲ τὸν καιρὸν ἐπέβαλεν Ἡρῴδης ὁ βασιλεὺς τὰς χεῖρας κακῶσαί τινας τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας.
verses.translit: Kat' ekeinon de ton kairon epevalen Erodis o vasileus tas heiras kakosai tinas ton apo tes ekklisias.
verses.translation: Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church.

verses.original: ἀνεῖλεν δὲ Ἰάκωβον τὸν ἀδελφὸν Ἰωάννου μαχαίρῃ.
verses.translit: aneilen de Iakovon ton adelfon Ioannoy mahaire.
verses.translation: And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.

verses.original: ⸂ἰδὼν δὲ⸃ ὅτι ἀρεστόν ἐστιν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις προσέθετο συλλαβεῖν καὶ Πέτρον (ἦσαν ⸀δὲ ἡμέραι τῶν ἀζύμων),
verses.translit: idon de oti areston estin tois Ioydaiois prosetheto syllavein kai Petron (esan de emerai ton azymon),
verses.translation: And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.)

verses.original: ὃν καὶ πιάσας ἔθετο εἰς φυλακήν, παραδοὺς τέσσαρσιν τετραδίοις στρατιωτῶν φυλάσσειν αὐτόν, βουλόμενος μετὰ τὸ πάσχα ἀναγαγεῖν αὐτὸν τῷ λαῷ.
verses.translit: on kai piasas etheto eis fylakin, paradous tessarsin tetradiois stratioton fylassein auton, voylomenos meta to pasha anagagein auton to lao.
verses.translation: And when he had apprehended him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four quaternions of soldiers to keep him; intending after Easter to bring him forth to the people.

verses.original: ὁ μὲν οὖν Πέτρος ἐτηρεῖτο ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ· προσευχὴ δὲ ἦν ⸀ἐκτενῶς γινομένη ὑπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ⸀περὶ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: o men oun Petros etireito en te fylake* proseyhe de en ektenos ginomeni upo tes ekklisias pros ton theon peri autou.
verses.translation: Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him.

verses.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἤμελλεν ⸂προαγαγεῖν αὐτὸν⸃ ὁ Ἡρῴδης, τῇ νυκτὶ ἐκείνῃ ἦν ὁ Πέτρος κοιμώμενος μεταξὺ δύο στρατιωτῶν δεδεμένος ἁλύσεσιν δυσίν, φύλακές τε πρὸ τῆς θύρας ἐτήρουν τὴν φυλακήν.
verses.translit: Ote de emellen proagagein auton o Erodis, te nykti ekeine en o Petros koimomenos metaxu dyo stratioton dedemenos alysesin dysin, fylakes te pro tes thyras etiroyn ten fylakin.
verses.translation: And when Herod would have brought him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains: and the keepers before the door kept the prison.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος κυρίου ἐπέστη, καὶ φῶς ἔλαμψεν ἐν τῷ οἰκήματι· πατάξας δὲ τὴν πλευρὰν τοῦ Πέτρου ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Ἀνάστα ἐν τάχει· καὶ ἐξέπεσαν αὐτοῦ αἱ ἁλύσεις ἐκ τῶν χειρῶν.
verses.translit: kai idou aggelos kyrioy epesti, kai fos elampsen en to oikimati* pataxas de ten pleyran tou Petroy egeiren auton legon* Anasta en tahei* kai exepesan autou ai alyseis ek ton heiron.
verses.translation: And, behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him , and a light shined in the prison: and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.

verses.original: εἶπεν ⸀δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος πρὸς αὐτόν· ⸀Ζῶσαι καὶ ὑπόδησαι τὰ σανδάλιά σου· ἐποίησεν δὲ οὕτως. καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Περιβαλοῦ τὸ ἱμάτιόν σου καὶ ἀκολούθει μοι.
verses.translit: eipen de o aggelos pros auton* Zosai kai upodisai ta sandalia soy* epoiisen de outos. kai legei auto* Perivalou to imation soy kai akoloythei moi.
verses.translation: And the angel said unto him, Gird thyself, and bind on thy sandals. And so he did. And he saith unto him, Cast thy garment about thee, and follow me.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξελθὼν ⸀ἠκολούθει, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει ὅτι ἀληθές ἐστιν τὸ γινόμενον διὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου, ἐδόκει δὲ ὅραμα βλέπειν.
verses.translit: kai exelthon ekoloythei, kai ouk edei oti alithes estin to ginomenon dia tou aggeloy, edokei de orama vlepein.
verses.translation: And he went out, and followed him; and wist not that it was true which was done by the angel; but thought he saw a vision.

verses.original: διελθόντες δὲ πρώτην φυλακὴν καὶ δευτέραν ἦλθαν ἐπὶ τὴν πύλην τὴν σιδηρᾶν τὴν φέρουσαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν, ἥτις αὐτομάτη ἠνοίγη αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐξελθόντες προῆλθον ῥύμην μίαν, καὶ εὐθέως ἀπέστη ὁ ἄγγελος ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: dielthontes de protin fylaken kai deyteran elthan epi ten pylin ten sidiran ten feroysan eis ten polin, etis automati enoigi autois, kai exelthontes proelthon Rymin mian, kai eutheos apesti o aggelos ap' autou.
verses.translation: When they were past the first and the second ward, they came unto the iron gate that leadeth unto the city; which opened to them of his own accord: and they went out, and passed on through one street; and forthwith the angel departed from him.

verses.original: καὶ ὁ Πέτρος ⸂ἐν ἑαυτῷ γενόμενος⸃ εἶπεν· Νῦν οἶδα ἀληθῶς ὅτι ἐξαπέστειλεν ⸀ὁ κύριος τὸν ἄγγελον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξείλατό με ἐκ χειρὸς Ἡρῴδου καὶ πάσης τῆς προσδοκίας τοῦ λαοῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
verses.translit: kai o Petros en eayto genomenos eipen* Nun oida alithos oti exapesteilen o kyrios ton aggelon autou kai exeilato me ek heiros Erodoy kai pasis tes prosdokias tou laou ton Ioydaion.
verses.translation: And when Peter was come to himself, he said, Now I know of a surety, that the Lord hath sent his angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.

verses.original: Συνιδών τε ἦλθεν ἐπὶ τὴν οἰκίαν ⸀τῆς Μαρίας τῆς μητρὸς Ἰωάννου τοῦ ἐπικαλουμένου Μάρκου, οὗ ἦσαν ἱκανοὶ συνηθροισμένοι καὶ προσευχόμενοι.
verses.translit: Synidon te elthen epi ten oikian tes Marias tes mitros Ioannoy tou epikaloymenoy Markoy, ou esan ikanoi synithroismenoi kai proseyhomenoi.
verses.translation: And when he had considered the thing , he came to the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying.

verses.original: κρούσαντος δὲ ⸀αὐτοῦ τὴν θύραν τοῦ πυλῶνος προσῆλθε παιδίσκη ὑπακοῦσαι ὀνόματι Ῥόδη,
