verses.translit: kroysantos de autou ten thyran tou pylonos proselthe paidiski upakousai onomati Rodi,
verses.translation: And as Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a damsel came to hearken, named Rhoda.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ Πέτρου ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς οὐκ ἤνοιξεν τὸν πυλῶνα, εἰσδραμοῦσα δὲ ἀπήγγειλεν ἑστάναι τὸν Πέτρον πρὸ τοῦ πυλῶνος.
verses.translit: kai epignousa ten fonen tou Petroy apo tes haras ouk enoixen ton pylona, eisdramousa de apiggeilen estanai ton Petron pro tou pylonos.
verses.translation: And when she knew Peter’s voice, she opened not the gate for gladness, but ran in, and told how Peter stood before the gate.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ πρὸς αὐτὴν εἶπαν· Μαίνῃ. ἡ δὲ διϊσχυρίζετο οὕτως ἔχειν. οἱ δὲ ἔλεγον· Ὁ ἄγγελός ⸂ἐστιν αὐτοῦ⸃.
verses.translit: oi de pros auten eipan* Maine. e de diishyrizeto outos ehein. oi de elegon* O aggelos estin autou.
verses.translation: And they said unto her, Thou art mad. But she constantly affirmed that it was even so. Then said they, It is his angel.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἐπέμενεν κρούων· ἀνοίξαντες δὲ εἶδαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐξέστησαν.
verses.translit: o de Petros epemenen kroyon* anoixantes de eidan auton kai exestisan.
verses.translation: But Peter continued knocking: and when they had opened the door , and saw him, they were astonished.

verses.original: κατασείσας δὲ αὐτοῖς τῇ χειρὶ σιγᾶν διηγήσατο αὐτοῖς πῶς ὁ κύριος αὐτὸν ἐξήγαγεν ἐκ τῆς φυλακῆς, εἶπέν ⸀τε· Ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰακώβῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ταῦτα. καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη εἰς ἕτερον τόπον.
verses.translit: kataseisas de autois te heiri sigan diigisato autois pos o kyrios auton exigagen ek tes fylakes, eipen te* Apaggeilate Iakovo kai tois adelfois tauta. kai exelthon eporeythi eis eteron topon.
verses.translation: But he, beckoning unto them with the hand to hold their peace, declared unto them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. And he said, Go shew these things unto James, and to the brethren. And he departed, and went into another place.

verses.original: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ἦν τάραχος οὐκ ὀλίγος ἐν τοῖς στρατιώταις, τί ἄρα ὁ Πέτρος ἐγένετο.
verses.translit: Genomenis de emeras en tarahos ouk oligos en tois stratiotais, ti ara o Petros egeneto.
verses.translation: Now as soon as it was day, there was no small stir among the soldiers, what was become of Peter.

verses.original: Ἡρῴδης δὲ ἐπιζητήσας αὐτὸν καὶ μὴ εὑρὼν ἀνακρίνας τοὺς φύλακας ἐκέλευσεν ἀπαχθῆναι, καὶ κατελθὼν ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας ⸀εἰς Καισάρειαν διέτριβεν.
verses.translit: Erodis de epizitisas auton kai me euron anakrinas tous fylakas ekeleysen apahthenai, kai katelthon apo tes Ioydaias eis Kaisareian dietriven.
verses.translation: And when Herod had sought for him, and found him not, he examined the keepers, and commanded that they should be put to death. And he went down from Judæa to Cæsarea, and there abode.

verses.original: Ἦν ⸀δὲ θυμομαχῶν Τυρίοις καὶ Σιδωνίοις· ὁμοθυμαδὸν δὲ παρῆσαν πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ πείσαντες Βλάστον τὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ κοιτῶνος τοῦ βασιλέως ᾐτοῦντο εἰρήνην διὰ τὸ τρέφεσθαι αὐτῶν τὴν χώραν ἀπὸ τῆς βασιλικῆς.
verses.translit: En de thymomahon Tyriois kai Sidoniois* omothymadon de paresan pros auton, kai peisantes Vlaston ton epi tou koitonos tou vasileos etounto eirinin dia to trefesthai auton ten horan apo tes vasilikes.
verses.translation: And Herod was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon: but they came with one accord to him, and, having made Blastus the king’s chamberlain their friend, desired peace; because their country was nourished by the king’s country .

verses.original: τακτῇ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἐνδυσάμενος ἐσθῆτα βασιλικὴν ⸀καὶ καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐδημηγόρει πρὸς αὐτούς·
verses.translit: takte de emera o Erodis endysamenos estheta vasiliken kai kathisas epi tou vimatos edimigorei pros autoys*
verses.translation: And upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ δῆμος ἐπεφώνει· ⸂Θεοῦ φωνὴ⸃ καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώπου.
verses.translit: o de demos epefonei* Theou fone kai ouk anthropoy.
verses.translation: And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.

verses.original: παραχρῆμα δὲ ἐπάταξεν αὐτὸν ἄγγελος κυρίου ἀνθʼ ὧν οὐκ ἔδωκεν ⸀τὴν δόξαν τῷ θεῷ, καὶ γενόμενος σκωληκόβρωτος ἐξέψυξεν.
verses.translit: parahrema de epataxen auton aggelos kyrioy anth' on ouk edoken ten doxan to theo, kai genomenos skolikovrotos exepsyxen.
verses.translation: And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ λόγος τοῦ ⸀θεοῦ ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐπληθύνετο.
verses.translit: O de logos tou theou iuxanen kai eplithyneto.
verses.translation: But the word of God grew and multiplied.

verses.original: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ καὶ Σαῦλος ὑπέστρεψαν, ⸀εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ πληρώσαντες τὴν διακονίαν, ⸀συμπαραλαβόντες Ἰωάννην τὸν ἐπικληθέντα Μᾶρκον.
verses.translit: Varnavas de kai Saulos upestrepsan, eis Ieroysalem plirosantes ten diakonian, symparalavontes Ioannin ton epiklithenta Markon.
verses.translation: And Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, when they had fulfilled their ministry, and took with them John, whose surname was Mark.

verses.original: Ἦσαν ⸀δὲ ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ κατὰ τὴν οὖσαν ἐκκλησίαν προφῆται καὶ διδάσκαλοι ὅ τε Βαρναβᾶς καὶ Συμεὼν ὁ καλούμενος Νίγερ, καὶ Λούκιος ὁ Κυρηναῖος, Μαναήν τε Ἡρῴδου τοῦ τετραάρχου σύντροφος καὶ Σαῦλος.
verses.translit: Esan de en Antioheia kata ten ousan ekklisian profetai kai didaskaloi o te Varnavas kai Symeon o kaloymenos Niger, kai Loykios o Kyrinaios, Manain te Erodoy tou tetraarhoy syntrofos kai Saulos.
verses.translation: Now there were in the church that was at Antioch certain prophets and teachers; as Barnabas, and Simeon that was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, which had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

verses.original: λειτουργούντων δὲ αὐτῶν τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ νηστευόντων εἶπεν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον· Ἀφορίσατε δή μοι τὸν Βαρναβᾶν ⸀καὶ Σαῦλον εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ προσκέκλημαι αὐτούς.
verses.translit: leitoyrgoynton de auton to kyrio kai nisteyonton eipen to pneuma to agion* Aforisate di moi ton Varnavan kai Saulon eis to ergon o proskeklimai autoys.
verses.translation: As they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.

verses.original: τότε νηστεύσαντες καὶ προσευξάμενοι καὶ ἐπιθέντες τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῖς ἀπέλυσαν.
verses.translit: tote nisteysantes kai proseyxamenoi kai epithentes tas heiras autois apelysan.
verses.translation: And when they had fasted and prayed, and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.

verses.original: ⸀Αὐτοὶ μὲν οὖν ἐκπεμφθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ ⸂ἁγίου πνεύματος⸃ κατῆλθον ⸀εἰς Σελεύκειαν, ἐκεῖθέν ⸀τε ἀπέπλευσαν ⸁εἰς Κύπρον,
verses.translit: Autoi men oun ekpemfthentes upo tou agioy pneymatos katelthon eis Seleykeian, ekeithen te apepleysan eis Kypron,
verses.translation: So they, being sent forth by the Holy Ghost, departed unto Seleucia; and from thence they sailed to Cyprus.

verses.original: καὶ γενόμενοι ἐν Σαλαμῖνι κατήγγελλον τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων· εἶχον δὲ καὶ Ἰωάννην ὑπηρέτην.
verses.translit: kai genomenoi en Salamini katiggellon ton logon tou theou en tais synagogais ton Ioydaion* eihon de kai Ioannin upiretin.
verses.translation: And when they were at Salamis, they preached the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews: and they had also John to their minister.

verses.original: διελθόντες δὲ ⸀ὅλην τὴν νῆσον ἄχρι Πάφου εὗρον ⸀ἄνδρα τινὰ μάγον ψευδοπροφήτην Ἰουδαῖον ᾧ ὄνομα ⸀Βαριησοῦ,
verses.translit: dielthontes de olin ten neson ahri Pafoy euron andra tina magon pseydoprofitin Ioydaion o onoma Variisou,
verses.translation: And when they had gone through the isle unto Paphos, they found a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-jesus:

verses.original: ὃς ἦν σὺν τῷ ἀνθυπάτῳ Σεργίῳ Παύλῳ, ἀνδρὶ συνετῷ. οὗτος προσκαλεσάμενος Βαρναβᾶν καὶ Σαῦλον ἐπεζήτησεν ἀκοῦσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ·
verses.translit: os en sun to anthypato Sergio Paylo, andri syneto. outos proskalesamenos Varnavan kai Saulon epezitisen akousai ton logon tou theou*
verses.translation: Which was with the deputy of the country, Sergius Paulus, a prudent man; who called for Barnabas and Saul, and desired to hear the word of God.

verses.original: ἀνθίστατο δὲ αὐτοῖς Ἐλύμας ὁ μάγος, οὕτως γὰρ μεθερμηνεύεται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, ζητῶν διαστρέψαι τὸν ἀνθύπατον ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως.
verses.translit: anthistato de autois Elymas o magos, outos gar methermineyetai to onoma autou, ziton diastrepsai ton anthypaton apo tes pisteos.
verses.translation: But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turn away the deputy from the faith.

verses.original: Σαῦλος δέ, ὁ καὶ Παῦλος, πλησθεὶς πνεύματος ⸀ἁγίου ἀτενίσας εἰς αὐτὸν
verses.translit: Saulos de, o kai Paulos, plistheis pneymatos agioy atenisas eis auton
verses.translation: Then Saul, (who also is called Paul,) filled with the Holy Ghost, set his eyes on him,

verses.original: εἶπεν· Ὦ πλήρης παντὸς δόλου καὶ πάσης ῥᾳδιουργίας, υἱὲ διαβόλου, ἐχθρὲ πάσης δικαιοσύνης, οὐ παύσῃ διαστρέφων τὰς ⸀ὁδοὺς κυρίου τὰς εὐθείας;
verses.translit: eipen* O pliris pantos doloy kai pasis Radioyrgias, yie diavoloy, ehthre pasis dikaiosynis, ou payse diastrefon tas odous kyrioy tas eutheias;
verses.translation: And said, O full of all subtilty and all mischief, thou child of the devil, thou enemy of all righteousness, wilt thou not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord?

verses.original: καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ χεὶρ κυρίου ἐπὶ σέ, καὶ ἔσῃ τυφλὸς μὴ βλέπων τὸν ἥλιον ἄχρι καιροῦ. παραχρῆμα ⸀δὲ ⸀ἔπεσεν ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ἀχλὺς καὶ σκότος, καὶ περιάγων ἐζήτει χειραγωγούς.
verses.translit: kai nun idou heir kyrioy epi se, kai ese tyflos me vlepon ton elion ahri kairou. parahrema de epesen ep' auton ahlus kai skotos, kai periagon ezitei heiragogoys.
verses.translation: And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is upon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun for a season. And immediately there fell on him a mist and a darkness; and he went about seeking some to lead him by the hand.

verses.original: τότε ἰδὼν ὁ ἀνθύπατος τὸ γεγονὸς ἐπίστευσεν ἐκπλησσόμενος ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ τοῦ κυρίου.
verses.translit: tote idon o anthypatos to gegonos episteysen ekplissomenos epi te didahe tou kyrioy.
verses.translation: Then the deputy, when he saw what was done, believed, being astonished at the doctrine of the Lord.

verses.original: Ἀναχθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς Πάφου οἱ ⸀περὶ Παῦλον ἦλθον εἰς Πέργην τῆς Παμφυλίας· Ἰωάννης δὲ ἀποχωρήσας ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ὑπέστρεψεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
verses.translit: Anahthentes de apo tes Pafoy oi peri Paulon elthon eis Pergin tes Pamfylias* Ioannis de apohorisas ap' auton upestrepsen eis Ierosolyma.
verses.translation: Now when Paul and his company loosed from Paphos, they came to Perga in Pamphylia: and John departing from them returned to Jerusalem.

verses.original: αὐτοὶ δὲ διελθόντες ἀπὸ τῆς Πέργης παρεγένοντο εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν ⸂τὴν Πισιδίαν⸃, καὶ ⸀εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων ἐκάθισαν.
verses.translit: autoi de dielthontes apo tes Pergis paregenonto eis Antioheian ten Pisidian, kai eiselthontes eis ten synagogen te emera ton savvaton ekathisan.
verses.translation: But when they departed from Perga, they came to Antioch in Pisidia, and went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and sat down.

verses.original: μετὰ δὲ τὴν ἀνάγνωσιν τοῦ νόμου καὶ τῶν προφητῶν ἀπέστειλαν οἱ ἀρχισυνάγωγοι πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγοντες· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, εἴ ⸀τίς ἐστιν ⸂ἐν ὑμῖν λόγος⸃ παρακλήσεως πρὸς τὸν λαόν, λέγετε.
verses.translit: meta de ten anagnosin tou nomoy kai ton profiton apesteilan oi arhisynagogoi pros autous legontes* Andres adelfoi, ei tis estin en umin logos parakliseos pros ton laon, legete.
verses.translation: And after the reading of the law and the prophets the rulers of the synagogue sent unto them, saying, Ye men and brethren, if ye have any word of exhortation for the people, say on.

verses.original: ἀναστὰς δὲ Παῦλος καὶ κατασείσας τῇ χειρὶ εἶπεν· Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται καὶ οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν θεόν, ἀκούσατε.
verses.translit: anastas de Paulos kai kataseisas te heiri eipen* Andres Israilitai kai oi fovoymenoi ton theon, akoysate.
verses.translation: Then Paul stood up, and beckoning with his hand said, Men of Israel, and ye that fear God, give audience.

verses.original: ὁ θεὸς τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου ⸀Ἰσραὴλ ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν, καὶ τὸν λαὸν ὕψωσεν ἐν τῇ παροικίᾳ ἐν γῇ ⸀Αἰγύπτου, καὶ μετὰ βραχίονος ὑψηλοῦ ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ἐξ αὐτῆς,
verses.translit: o theos tou laou toytoy Israel exelexato tous pateras emon, kai ton laon upsosen en te paroikia en ge Aigyptoy, kai meta vrahionos upsilou exigagen autous ex autes,
verses.translation: The God of this people of Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they dwelt as strangers in the land of Egypt, and with an high arm brought he them out of it.

verses.original: καί, ὡς τεσσερακονταετῆ χρόνον ἐτροποφόρησεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ,
verses.translit: kai, os tesserakontaete hronon etropoforisen autous en te erimo,
verses.translation: And about the time of forty years suffered he their manners in the wilderness.

verses.original: ⸀καὶ καθελὼν ἔθνη ἑπτὰ ἐν γῇ Χανάαν ⸀κατεκληρονόμησεν τὴν γῆν αὐτῶν
verses.translit: kai kathelon ethni epta en ge Hanaan kateklironomisen ten gen auton
verses.translation: And when he had destroyed seven nations in the land of Chanaan, he divided their land to them by lot.

verses.original: ⸂ὡς ἔτεσι τετρακοσίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα. καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα⸃ ἔδωκεν κριτὰς ἕως Σαμουὴλ ⸀τοῦ προφήτου.
verses.translit: os etesi tetrakosiois kai pentikonta. kai meta tauta edoken kritas eos Samoyel tou profitoy.
verses.translation: And after that he gave unto them judges about the space of four hundred and fifty years, until Samuel the prophet.

verses.original: κἀκεῖθεν ᾐτήσαντο βασιλέα, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς τὸν Σαοὺλ υἱὸν Κίς, ἄνδρα ἐκ φυλῆς Βενιαμίν, ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα·
verses.translit: kakeithen etisanto vasilea, kai edoken autois o theos ton Saoul yion Kis, andra ek fyles Veniamin, eti tesserakonta*
verses.translation: And afterward they desired a king: and God gave unto them Saul the son of Cis, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, by the space of forty years.

verses.original: καὶ μεταστήσας αὐτὸν ἤγειρεν ⸂τὸν Δαυὶδ αὐτοῖς⸃ εἰς βασιλέα, ᾧ καὶ εἶπεν μαρτυρήσας· Εὗρον Δαυὶδ τὸν τοῦ Ἰεσσαί, ἄνδρα κατὰ τὴν καρδίαν μου, ὃς ποιήσει πάντα τὰ θελήματά μου.
verses.translit: kai metastisas auton egeiren ton Dayid autois eis vasilea, o kai eipen martyrisas* Euron Dayid ton tou Iessai, andra kata ten kardian moy, os poiisei panta ta thelimata moy.
verses.translation: And when he had removed him, he raised up unto them David to be their king; to whom also he gave testimony, and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will.

verses.original: τούτου ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ σπέρματος κατʼ ἐπαγγελίαν ἤγαγεν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ ⸂σωτῆρα Ἰησοῦν⸃,
verses.translit: toytoy o theos apo tou spermatos kat' epaggelian egagen to Israel sotera Iisoun,
verses.translation: Of this man’s seed hath God according to his promise raised unto Israel a Saviour, Jesus:

verses.original: προκηρύξαντος Ἰωάννου πρὸ προσώπου τῆς εἰσόδου αὐτοῦ βάπτισμα μετανοίας ⸂παντὶ τῷ λαῷ⸃ Ἰσραήλ.
verses.translit: prokiryxantos Ioannoy pro prosopoy tes eisodoy autou vaptisma metanoias panti to lao Israil.
verses.translation: When John had first preached before his coming the baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἐπλήρου ⸀Ἰωάννης τὸν δρόμον, ἔλεγεν· ⸂Τί ἐμὲ⸃ ὑπονοεῖτε εἶναι; οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγώ· ἀλλʼ ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται μετʼ ἐμὲ οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἄξιος τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν λῦσαι.
verses.translit: os de epliroy Ioannis ton dromon, elegen* Ti eme uponoeite einai; ouk eimi ego* all' idou erhetai met' eme ou ouk eimi axios to upodima ton podon lusai.
verses.translation: And as John fulfilled his course, he said, Whom think ye that I am? I am not he . But, behold, there cometh one after me, whose shoes of his feet I am not worthy to loose.

verses.original: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, υἱοὶ γένους Ἀβραὰμ καὶ οἱ ἐν ὑμῖν φοβούμενοι τὸν θεόν, ⸀ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος τῆς σωτηρίας ταύτης ⸀ἐξαπεστάλη.
verses.translit: Andres adelfoi, yioi genoys Avraam kai oi en umin fovoymenoi ton theon, emin o logos tes sotirias taytis exapestali.
verses.translation: Men and brethren, children of the stock of Abraham, and whosoever among you feareth God, to you is the word of this salvation sent.

verses.original: οἱ γὰρ κατοικοῦντες ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες αὐτῶν τοῦτον ἀγνοήσαντες καὶ τὰς φωνὰς τῶν προφητῶν τὰς κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον ἀναγινωσκομένας κρίναντες ἐπλήρωσαν,
verses.translit: oi gar katoikountes en Ieroysalem kai oi arhontes auton touton agnoisantes kai tas fonas ton profiton tas kata pan savvaton anaginoskomenas krinantes eplirosan,
verses.translation: For they that dwell at Jerusalem, and their rulers, because they knew him not, nor yet the voices of the prophets which are read every sabbath day, they have fulfilled them in condemning him .

verses.original: καὶ μηδεμίαν αἰτίαν θανάτου εὑρόντες ᾐτήσαντο Πιλᾶτον ἀναιρεθῆναι αὐτόν·
verses.translit: kai midemian aitian thanatoy eurontes etisanto Pilaton anairethenai auton*
verses.translation: And though they found no cause of death in him , yet desired they Pilate that he should be slain.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἐτέλεσαν πάντα τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένα, καθελόντες ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου ἔθηκαν εἰς μνημεῖον.
verses.translit: os de etelesan panta ta peri autou gegrammena, kathelontes apo tou xyloy ethikan eis mnimeion.
verses.translation: And when they had fulfilled all that was written of him, they took him down from the tree, and laid him in a sepulchre.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ θεὸς ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν·
verses.translit: o de theos egeiren auton ek nekron*
verses.translation: But God raised him from the dead:

verses.original: ὃς ὤφθη ἐπὶ ἡμέρας πλείους τοῖς συναναβᾶσιν αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, οἵτινες ⸀νῦν εἰσὶ μάρτυρες αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὸν λαόν.
verses.translit: os ofthi epi emeras pleioys tois synanavasin auto apo tes Galilaias eis Ieroysalim, oitines nun eisi martyres autou pros ton laon.
verses.translation: And he was seen many days of them which came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are his witnesses unto the people.

verses.original: καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμᾶς εὐαγγελιζόμεθα τὴν πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ἐπαγγελίαν γενομένην
verses.translit: kai emeis umas euaggelizometha ten pros tous pateras epaggelian genomenin
verses.translation: And we declare unto you glad tidings, how that the promise which was made unto the fathers,

verses.original: ὅτι ταύτην ὁ θεὸς ἐκπεπλήρωκεν τοῖς τέκνοις ⸀ἡμῶν ἀναστήσας Ἰησοῦν, ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ ⸂ψαλμῷ γέγραπται τῷ δευτέρῳ⸃· Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε.
verses.translit: oti taytin o theos ekpepliroken tois teknois emon anastisas Iisoun, os kai en to psalmo gegraptai to deytero* Yios moy ei sy, ego simeron gegennika se.
verses.translation: God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.

verses.original: ὅτι δὲ ἀνέστησεν αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν μηκέτι μέλλοντα ὑποστρέφειν εἰς διαφθοράν, οὕτως εἴρηκεν ὅτι Δώσω ὑμῖν τὰ ὅσια Δαυὶδ τὰ πιστά.
verses.translit: oti de anestisen auton ek nekron miketi mellonta upostrefein eis diafthoran, outos eiriken oti Doso umin ta osia Dayid ta pista.
verses.translation: And as concerning that he raised him up from the dead, now no more to return to corruption, he said on this wise, I will give you the sure mercies of David.

verses.original: ⸀διότι καὶ ἐν ἑτέρῳ λέγει· Οὐ δώσεις τὸν ὅσιόν σου ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν·
verses.translit: dioti kai en etero legei* Ou doseis ton osion soy idein diafthoran*
verses.translation: Wherefore he saith also in another psalm , Thou shalt not suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.

verses.original: Δαυὶδ μὲν γὰρ ἰδίᾳ γενεᾷ ὑπηρετήσας τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ βουλῇ ἐκοιμήθη καὶ προσετέθη πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶδεν διαφθοράν,
verses.translit: Dayid men gar idia genea upiretisas te tou theou voyle ekoimithi kai prosetethi pros tous pateras autou kai eiden diafthoran,
verses.translation: For David, after he had served his own generation by the will of God, fell on sleep, and was laid unto his fathers, and saw corruption:

verses.original: ὃν δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἤγειρεν οὐκ εἶδεν διαφθοράν.
verses.translit: on de o theos egeiren ouk eiden diafthoran.
verses.translation: But he, whom God raised again, saw no corruption.

verses.original: γνωστὸν οὖν ἔστω ὑμῖν, ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ὅτι διὰ τούτου ὑμῖν ἄφεσις ἁμαρτιῶν καταγγέλλεται, καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων ὧν οὐκ ἠδυνήθητε ⸀ἐν νόμῳ Μωϋσέως δικαιωθῆναι
verses.translit: gnoston oun esto umin, andres adelfoi, oti dia toytoy umin afesis amartion kataggelletai, kai apo panton on ouk edynithite en nomo Moyseos dikaiothenai
verses.translation: Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins:

verses.original: ἐν τούτῳ πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων δικαιοῦται.
verses.translit: en toyto pas o pisteyon dikaioutai.
verses.translation: And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.

verses.original: βλέπετε οὖν μὴ ⸀ἐπέλθῃ τὸ εἰρημένον ἐν τοῖς προφήταις·
verses.translit: vlepete oun me epelthe to eirimenon en tois profitais*
verses.translation: Beware therefore, lest that come upon you, which is spoken of in the prophets;

verses.original: Ἴδετε, οἱ καταφρονηταί, καὶ θαυμάσατε καὶ ἀφανίσθητε, ὅτι ἔργον ⸂ἐργάζομαι ἐγὼ⸃ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ὑμῶν, ⸀ἔργον ὃ οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε ἐάν τις ἐκδιηγῆται ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: Idete, oi katafronitai, kai thaymasate kai afanisthite, oti ergon ergazomai ego en tais emerais umon, ergon o ou me pisteysite ean tis ekdiigetai umin.
verses.translation: Behold, ye despisers, and wonder, and perish: for I work a work in your days, a work which ye shall in no wise believe, though a man declare it unto you.

verses.original: Ἐξιόντων δὲ ⸀αὐτῶν ⸀παρεκάλουν εἰς τὸ μεταξὺ σάββατον λαληθῆναι αὐτοῖς τὰ ῥήματα ⸀ταῦτα.
verses.translit: Exionton de auton parekaloyn eis to metaxu savvaton lalithenai autois ta Rimata tauta.
verses.translation: And when the Jews were gone out of the synagogue, the Gentiles besought that these words might be preached to them the next sabbath.

verses.original: λυθείσης δὲ τῆς συναγωγῆς ἠκολούθησαν πολλοὶ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ τῶν σεβομένων προσηλύτων τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Βαρναβᾷ, οἵτινες προσλαλοῦντες ⸀αὐτοῖς ἔπειθον αὐτοὺς ⸀προσμένειν τῇ χάριτι τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: lytheisis de tes synagoges ekoloythisan polloi ton Ioydaion kai ton sevomenon prosilyton to Paylo kai to Varnava, oitines proslalountes autois epeithon autous prosmenein te hariti tou theou.
verses.translation: Now when the congregation was broken up, many of the Jews and religious proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas: who, speaking to them, persuaded them to continue in the grace of God.

verses.original: Τῷ ⸀δὲ ἐρχομένῳ σαββάτῳ σχεδὸν πᾶσα ἡ πόλις συνήχθη ἀκοῦσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ ⸀κυρίου.
verses.translit: To de erhomeno savvato shedon pasa e polis synihthi akousai ton logon tou kyrioy.
verses.translation: And the next sabbath day came almost the whole city together to hear the word of God.

verses.original: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τοὺς ὄχλους ἐπλήσθησαν ζήλου καὶ ἀντέλεγον τοῖς ⸀ὑπὸ Παύλου ⸀λαλουμένοις ⸀βλασφημοῦντες.
verses.translit: idontes de oi Ioydaioi tous ohloys eplisthisan ziloy kai antelegon tois upo Payloy laloymenois vlasfimountes.
verses.translation: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy, and spake against those things which were spoken by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming.

verses.original: παρρησιασάμενοί ⸀τε ὁ Παῦλος καὶ ὁ Βαρναβᾶς εἶπαν· Ὑμῖν ἦν ἀναγκαῖον πρῶτον λαληθῆναι τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ· ⸀ἐπειδὴ ἀπωθεῖσθε αὐτὸν καὶ οὐκ ἀξίους κρίνετε ἑαυτοὺς τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς, ἰδοὺ στρεφόμεθα εἰς τὰ ἔθνη·
verses.translit: parrisiasamenoi te o Paulos kai o Varnavas eipan* Umin en anagkaion proton lalithenai ton logon tou theou* epeide apotheisthe auton kai ouk axioys krinete eaytous tes aionioy zoes, idou strefometha eis ta ethni*
verses.translation: Then Paul and Barnabas waxed bold, and said, It was necessary that the word of God should first have been spoken to you: but seeing ye put it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles.

verses.original: οὕτως γὰρ ἐντέταλται ἡμῖν ὁ κύριος· Τέθεικά σε εἰς φῶς ἐθνῶν τοῦ εἶναί σε εἰς σωτηρίαν ἕως ἐσχάτου τῆς γῆς.
verses.translit: outos gar entetaltai emin o kyrios* Tetheika se eis fos ethnon tou einai se eis sotirian eos eshatoy tes ges.
verses.translation: For so hath the Lord commanded us, saying , I have set thee to be a light of the Gentiles, that thou shouldest be for salvation unto the ends of the earth.

verses.original: ἀκούοντα δὲ τὰ ἔθνη ⸀ἔχαιρον καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν λόγον τοῦ ⸀κυρίου, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν ὅσοι ἦσαν τεταγμένοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον·
verses.translit: akoyonta de ta ethni ehairon kai edoxazon ton logon tou kyrioy, kai episteysan osoi esan tetagmenoi eis zoen aionion*
verses.translation: And when the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of the Lord: and as many as were ordained to eternal life believed.

verses.original: διεφέρετο δὲ ὁ λόγος τοῦ κυρίου διʼ ὅλης τῆς χώρας.
verses.translit: diefereto de o logos tou kyrioy di' olis tes horas.
verses.translation: And the word of the Lord was published throughout all the region.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ Ἰουδαῖοι παρώτρυναν τὰς σεβομένας ⸀γυναῖκας τὰς εὐσχήμονας καὶ τοὺς πρώτους τῆς πόλεως καὶ ἐπήγειραν διωγμὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Παῦλον ⸀καὶ Βαρναβᾶν, καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: oi de Ioydaioi parotrynan tas sevomenas gynaikas tas eushimonas kai tous protoys tes poleos kai epigeiran diogmon epi ton Paulon kai Varnavan, kai exevalon autous apo ton orion auton.
verses.translation: But the Jews stirred up the devout and honourable women, and the chief men of the city, and raised persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and expelled them out of their coasts.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐκτιναξάμενοι τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ⸀ποδῶν ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς ἦλθον εἰς Ἰκόνιον,
verses.translit: oi de ektinaxamenoi ton koniorton ton podon ep' autous elthon eis Ikonion,
verses.translation: But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came unto Iconium.

verses.original: οἵ ⸀τε μαθηταὶ ἐπληροῦντο χαρᾶς καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου.
verses.translit: oi te mathitai eplirounto haras kai pneymatos agioy.
verses.translation: And the disciples were filled with joy, and with the Holy Ghost.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν Ἰκονίῳ κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ λαλῆσαι οὕτως ὥστε πιστεῦσαι Ἰουδαίων τε καὶ Ἑλλήνων πολὺ πλῆθος.
verses.translit: Egeneto de en Ikonio kata to auto eiselthein autous eis ten synagogen ton Ioydaion kai lalesai outos oste pisteusai Ioydaion te kai Ellinon polu plethos.
verses.translation: And it came to pass in Iconium, that they went both together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spake, that a great multitude both of the Jews and also of the Greeks believed.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ⸀ἀπειθήσαντες Ἰουδαῖοι ἐπήγειραν καὶ ἐκάκωσαν τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν.
verses.translit: oi de apeithisantes Ioydaioi epigeiran kai ekakosan tas psyhas ton ethnon kata ton adelfon.
verses.translation: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles, and made their minds evil affected against the brethren.

verses.original: ἱκανὸν μὲν οὖν χρόνον διέτριψαν παρρησιαζόμενοι ἐπὶ τῷ κυρίῳ τῷ μαρτυροῦντι ⸀τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ, διδόντι σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα γίνεσθαι διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: ikanon men oun hronon dietripsan parrisiazomenoi epi to kyrio to martyrounti to logo tes haritos autou, didonti simeia kai terata ginesthai dia ton heiron auton.
verses.translation: Long time therefore abode they speaking boldly in the Lord, which gave testimony unto the word of his grace, and granted signs and wonders to be done by their hands.

verses.original: ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ πλῆθος τῆς πόλεως, καὶ οἱ μὲν ἦσαν σὺν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις οἱ δὲ σὺν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις.
verses.translit: eshisthi de to plethos tes poleos, kai oi men esan sun tois Ioydaiois oi de sun tois apostolois.
verses.translation: But the multitude of the city was divided: and part held with the Jews, and part with the apostles.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο ὁρμὴ τῶν ἐθνῶν τε καὶ Ἰουδαίων σὺν τοῖς ἄρχουσιν αὐτῶν ὑβρίσαι καὶ λιθοβολῆσαι αὐτούς,
verses.translit: os de egeneto orme ton ethnon te kai Ioydaion sun tois arhoysin auton uvrisai kai lithovolesai autoys,
verses.translation: And when there was an assault made both of the Gentiles, and also of the Jews with their rulers, to use them despitefully, and to stone them,

verses.original: συνιδόντες κατέφυγον εἰς τὰς πόλεις τῆς Λυκαονίας Λύστραν καὶ Δέρβην καὶ τὴν περίχωρον,
verses.translit: synidontes katefygon eis tas poleis tes Lykaonias Lystran kai Dervin kai ten perihoron,
verses.translation: They were ware of it , and fled unto Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia, and unto the region that lieth round about:

verses.original: κἀκεῖ ⸂εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ἦσαν⸃.
verses.translit: kakei euaggelizomenoi esan.
verses.translation: And there they preached the gospel.

verses.original: Καί τις ἀνὴρ ⸂ἀδύνατος ἐν Λύστροις⸃ τοῖς ποσὶν ἐκάθητο, χωλὸς ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς ⸀αὐτοῦ, ὃς οὐδέποτε ⸀περιεπάτησεν.
verses.translit: Kai tis aner adynatos en Lystrois tois posin ekathito, holos ek koilias mitros autou, os oudepote periepatisen.
verses.translation: And there sat a certain man at Lystra, impotent in his feet, being a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked:

verses.original: οὗτος ⸀ἤκουσεν τοῦ Παύλου λαλοῦντος· ὃς ἀτενίσας αὐτῷ καὶ ἰδὼν ὅτι ⸂ἔχει πίστιν⸃ τοῦ σωθῆναι
verses.translit: outos ekoysen tou Payloy lalountos* os atenisas auto kai idon oti ehei pistin tou sothenai
verses.translation: The same heard Paul speak: who stedfastly beholding him, and perceiving that he had faith to be healed,

verses.original: εἶπεν ⸀μεγάλῃ φωνῇ· Ἀνάστηθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου ⸀ὀρθός· καὶ ⸀ἥλατο καὶ περιεπάτει.
verses.translit: eipen megale fone* Anastithi epi tous podas soy orthos* kai elato kai periepatei.
verses.translation: Said with a loud voice, Stand upright on thy feet. And he leaped and walked.

verses.original: οἵ ⸀τε ὄχλοι ἰδόντες ὃ ⸀ἐποίησεν Παῦλος ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν Λυκαονιστὶ λέγοντες· Οἱ θεοὶ ὁμοιωθέντες ἀνθρώποις κατέβησαν πρὸς ἡμᾶς
verses.translit: oi te ohloi idontes o epoiisen Paulos eperan ten fonen auton Lykaonisti legontes* Oi theoi omoiothentes anthropois katevisan pros emas
verses.translation: And when the people saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in the speech of Lycaonia, The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men.

verses.original: ἐκάλουν τε ⸀τὸν Βαρναβᾶν Δία, τὸν δὲ Παῦλον Ἑρμῆν, ἐπειδὴ αὐτὸς ἦν ὁ ἡγούμενος τοῦ λόγου.
verses.translit: ekaloyn te ton Varnavan Dia, ton de Paulon Ermen, epeide autos en o egoymenos tou logoy.
verses.translation: And they called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercurius, because he was the chief speaker.

verses.original: ὅ ⸀τε ἱερεὺς τοῦ Διὸς τοῦ ὄντος πρὸ τῆς ⸀πόλεως ταύρους καὶ στέμματα ἐπὶ τοὺς πυλῶνας ἐνέγκας σὺν τοῖς ὄχλοις ἤθελεν θύειν.
verses.translit: o te iereus tou Dios tou ontos pro tes poleos tayroys kai stemmata epi tous pylonas enegkas sun tois ohlois ethelen thyein.
verses.translation: Then the priest of Jupiter, which was before their city, brought oxen and garlands unto the gates, and would have done sacrifice with the people.

verses.original: ἀκούσαντες δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι Βαρναβᾶς καὶ Παῦλος, διαρρήξαντες τὰ ἱμάτια ⸀αὐτῶν ⸀ἐξεπήδησαν εἰς τὸν ὄχλον κράζοντες
verses.translit: akoysantes de oi apostoloi Varnavas kai Paulos, diarrixantes ta imatia auton exepidisan eis ton ohlon krazontes
verses.translation: Which when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of , they rent their clothes, and ran in among the people, crying out,

verses.original: καὶ λέγοντες· Ἄνδρες, τί ταῦτα ποιεῖτε; καὶ ἡμεῖς ὁμοιοπαθεῖς ἐσμεν ὑμῖν ἄνθρωποι, εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τούτων τῶν ματαίων ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ ⸀θεὸν ζῶντα ὃς ἐποίησεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς·
verses.translit: kai legontes* Andres, ti tauta poieite; kai emeis omoiopatheis esmen umin anthropoi, euaggelizomenoi umas apo toyton ton mataion epistrefein epi theon zonta os epoiisen ton ouranon kai ten gen kai ten thalassan kai panta ta en autois*
verses.translation: And saying, Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and preach unto you that ye should turn from these vanities unto the living God, which made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all things that are therein:

verses.original: ὃς ἐν ταῖς παρῳχημέναις γενεαῖς εἴασεν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη πορεύεσθαι ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτῶν·
verses.translit: os en tais parohimenais geneais eiasen panta ta ethni poreyesthai tais odois auton*
verses.translation: Who in times past suffered all nations to walk in their own ways.

verses.original: ⸀καίτοι οὐκ ἀμάρτυρον ⸀αὑτὸν ἀφῆκεν ⸀ἀγαθουργῶν, οὐρανόθεν ὑμῖν ὑετοὺς διδοὺς καὶ καιροὺς καρποφόρους, ἐμπιπλῶν τροφῆς καὶ εὐφροσύνης τὰς καρδίας ⸀ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: kaitoi ouk amartyron auton afeken agathoyrgon, ouranothen umin uetous didous kai kairous karpoforoys, empiplon trofes kai eufrosynis tas kardias umon.
verses.translation: Nevertheless he left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.

verses.original: καὶ ταῦτα λέγοντες μόλις κατέπαυσαν τοὺς ὄχλους τοῦ μὴ θύειν αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: kai tauta legontes molis katepaysan tous ohloys tou me thyein autois.
verses.translation: And with these sayings scarce restrained they the people, that they had not done sacrifice unto them.

verses.original: Ἐπῆλθαν δὲ ἀπὸ Ἀντιοχείας καὶ Ἰκονίου Ἰουδαῖοι, καὶ πείσαντες τοὺς ὄχλους καὶ λιθάσαντες τὸν Παῦλον ἔσυρον ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, ⸀νομίζοντες αὐτὸν τεθνηκέναι.
verses.translit: Epelthan de apo Antioheias kai Ikonioy Ioydaioi, kai peisantes tous ohloys kai lithasantes ton Paulon esyron exo tes poleos, nomizontes auton tethnikenai.
verses.translation: And there came thither certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium, who persuaded the people, and, having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead.

verses.original: κυκλωσάντων δὲ ⸂τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτὸν⸃ ἀναστὰς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν. καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τῷ Βαρναβᾷ εἰς Δέρβην.
verses.translit: kyklosanton de ton mathiton auton anastas eiselthen eis ten polin. kai te epayrion exelthen sun to Varnava eis Dervin.
verses.translation: Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe.

verses.original: Εὐαγγελισάμενοί τε τὴν πόλιν ἐκείνην καὶ μαθητεύσαντες ἱκανοὺς ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν Λύστραν καὶ ⸀εἰς Ἰκόνιον καὶ ⸁εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν,
verses.translit: Euaggelisamenoi te ten polin ekeinin kai mathiteysantes ikanous upestrepsan eis ten Lystran kai eis Ikonion kai eis Antioheian,
verses.translation: And when they had preached the gospel to that city, and had taught many, they returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and Antioch,

verses.original: ἐπιστηρίζοντες τὰς ψυχὰς τῶν μαθητῶν, παρακαλοῦντες ἐμμένειν τῇ πίστει καὶ ὅτι διὰ πολλῶν θλίψεων δεῖ ἡμᾶς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: epistirizontes tas psyhas ton mathiton, parakalountes emmenein te pistei kai oti dia pollon thlipseon dei emas eiselthein eis ten vasileian tou theou.
verses.translation: Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.

verses.original: χειροτονήσαντες δὲ αὐτοῖς ⸂κατʼ ἐκκλησίαν πρεσβυτέρους⸃ προσευξάμενοι μετὰ νηστειῶν παρέθεντο αὐτοὺς τῷ κυρίῳ εἰς ὃν πεπιστεύκεισαν.
verses.translit: heirotonisantes de autois kat' ekklisian presvyteroys proseyxamenoi meta nisteion parethento autous to kyrio eis on pepisteykeisan.
verses.translation: And when they had ordained them elders in every church, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord, on whom they believed.

verses.original: καὶ διελθόντες τὴν Πισιδίαν ἦλθον εἰς ⸀τὴν Παμφυλίαν,
verses.translit: kai dielthontes ten Pisidian elthon eis ten Pamfylian,
verses.translation: And after they had passed throughout Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.

verses.original: καὶ λαλήσαντες ἐν Πέργῃ τὸν λόγον κατέβησαν εἰς Ἀττάλειαν,
verses.translit: kai lalisantes en Perge ton logon katevisan eis Attaleian,
verses.translation: And when they had preached the word in Perga, they went down into Attalia:

verses.original: κἀκεῖθεν ἀπέπλευσαν εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, ὅθεν ἦσαν παραδεδομένοι τῇ χάριτι τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ ἐπλήρωσαν.
verses.translit: kakeithen apepleysan eis Antioheian, othen esan paradedomenoi te hariti tou theou eis to ergon o eplirosan.
verses.translation: And thence sailed to Antioch, from whence they had been recommended to the grace of God for the work which they fulfilled.

verses.original: παραγενόμενοι δὲ καὶ συναγαγόντες τὴν ἐκκλησίαν ⸀ἀνήγγελλον ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς μετʼ αὐτῶν καὶ ὅτι ἤνοιξεν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν θύραν πίστεως.
verses.translit: paragenomenoi de kai synagagontes ten ekklisian aniggellon osa epoiisen o theos met' auton kai oti enoixen tois ethnesin thyran pisteos.
verses.translation: And when they were come, and had gathered the church together, they rehearsed all that God had done with them, and how he had opened the door of faith unto the Gentiles.

verses.original: διέτριβον ⸀δὲ χρόνον οὐκ ὀλίγον σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς.
verses.translit: dietrivon de hronon ouk oligon sun tois mathitais.
verses.translation: And there they abode long time with the disciples.

verses.original: Καί τινες κατελθόντες ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἐδίδασκον τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὅτι Ἐὰν μὴ ⸀περιτμηθῆτε τῷ ἔθει ⸀τῷ Μωϋσέως, οὐ δύνασθε σωθῆναι.
verses.translit: Kai tines katelthontes apo tes Ioydaias edidaskon tous adelfous oti Ean me peritmithete to ethei to Moyseos, ou dynasthe sothenai.
verses.translation: And certain men which came down from Judæa taught the brethren, and said , Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.

verses.original: γενομένης ⸀δὲ στάσεως καὶ ζητήσεως οὐκ ὀλίγης τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Βαρναβᾷ πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἔταξαν ἀναβαίνειν Παῦλον καὶ Βαρναβᾶν καί τινας ἄλλους ἐξ αὐτῶν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους καὶ πρεσβυτέρους εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ περὶ τοῦ ζητήματος τούτου.
verses.translit: genomenis de staseos kai zitiseos ouk oligis to Paylo kai to Varnava pros autous etaxan anavainein Paulon kai Varnavan kai tinas alloys ex auton pros tous apostoloys kai presvyteroys eis Ieroysalem peri tou zitimatos toytoy.
verses.translation: When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.

verses.original: οἱ μὲν οὖν προπεμφθέντες ὑπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας διήρχοντο τήν ⸀τε Φοινίκην καὶ Σαμάρειαν ἐκδιηγούμενοι τὴν ἐπιστροφὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν, καὶ ἐποίουν χαρὰν μεγάλην πᾶσι τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς.
verses.translit: oi men oun propemfthentes upo tes ekklisias diirhonto tin te Foinikin kai Samareian ekdiigoymenoi ten epistrofen ton ethnon, kai epoioyn haran megalin pasi tois adelfois.
verses.translation: And being brought on their way by the church, they passed through Phenice and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles: and they caused great joy unto all the brethren.

verses.original: παραγενόμενοι δὲ εἰς ⸀Ἱεροσόλυμα ⸀παρεδέχθησαν ⸀ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας καὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, ἀνήγγειλάν τε ὅσα ὁ θεὸς ἐποίησεν μετʼ αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: paragenomenoi de eis Ierosolyma paredehthisan apo tes ekklisias kai ton apostolon kai ton presvyteron, aniggeilan te osa o theos epoiisen met' auton.
verses.translation: And when they were come to Jerusalem, they were received of the church, and of the apostles and elders, and they declared all things that God had done with them.

verses.original: ἐξανέστησαν δέ τινες τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς αἱρέσεως τῶν Φαρισαίων πεπιστευκότες, λέγοντες ὅτι δεῖ περιτέμνειν αὐτοὺς παραγγέλλειν τε τηρεῖν τὸν νόμον Μωϋσέως.
verses.translit: exanestisan de tines ton apo tes aireseos ton Farisaion pepisteykotes, legontes oti dei peritemnein autous paraggellein te tirein ton nomon Moyseos.
verses.translation: But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.

verses.original: Συνήχθησάν ⸀τε οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἰδεῖν περὶ τοῦ λόγου τούτου.
verses.translit: Synihthisan te oi apostoloi kai oi presvyteroi idein peri tou logoy toytoy.
verses.translation: And the apostles and elders came together for to consider of this matter.

verses.original: πολλῆς δὲ ⸀ζητήσεως γενομένης ἀναστὰς Πέτρος εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ὅτι ἀφʼ ἡμερῶν ἀρχαίων ⸂ἐν ὑμῖν ἐξελέξατο ὁ θεὸς⸃ διὰ τοῦ στόματός μου ἀκοῦσαι τὰ ἔθνη τὸν λόγον τοῦ εὐαγγελίου καὶ πιστεῦσαι,
verses.translit: polles de zitiseos genomenis anastas Petros eipen pros autoys* Andres adelfoi, umeis epistasthe oti af' emeron arhaion en umin exelexato o theos dia tou stomatos moy akousai ta ethni ton logon tou euaggelioy kai pisteusai,
verses.translation: And when there had been much disputing, Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe.

verses.original: καὶ ὁ καρδιογνώστης θεὸς ἐμαρτύρησεν αὐτοῖς ⸀δοὺς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καθὼς καὶ ἡμῖν,
verses.translit: kai o kardiognostis theos emartyrisen autois dous to pneuma to agion kathos kai emin,
verses.translation: And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us;

verses.original: καὶ ⸀οὐθὲν διέκρινεν μεταξὺ ἡμῶν τε καὶ αὐτῶν, τῇ πίστει καθαρίσας τὰς καρδίας αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai outhen diekrinen metaxu emon te kai auton, te pistei katharisas tas kardias auton.
verses.translation: And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.

verses.original: νῦν οὖν τί πειράζετε τὸν θεόν, ἐπιθεῖναι ζυγὸν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τῶν μαθητῶν ὃν οὔτε οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν οὔτε ἡμεῖς ἰσχύσαμεν βαστάσαι;
verses.translit: nun oun ti peirazete ton theon, epitheinai zygon epi ton trahilon ton mathiton on oute oi pateres emon oute emeis ishysamen vastasai;
verses.translation: Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?

verses.original: ἀλλὰ διὰ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ πιστεύομεν σωθῆναι καθʼ ὃν τρόπον κἀκεῖνοι.
verses.translit: alla dia tes haritos tou kyrioy Iisou pisteyomen sothenai kath' on tropon kakeinoi.
verses.translation: But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.

verses.original: Ἐσίγησεν δὲ πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος, καὶ ἤκουον Βαρναβᾶ καὶ Παύλου ἐξηγουμένων ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν διʼ αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Esigisen de pan to plethos, kai ekoyon Varnava kai Payloy exigoymenon osa epoiisen o theos simeia kai terata en tois ethnesin di' auton.
verses.translation: Then all the multitude kept silence, and gave audience to Barnabas and Paul, declaring what miracles and wonders God had wrought among the Gentiles by them.

verses.original: μετὰ δὲ τὸ σιγῆσαι αὐτοὺς ἀπεκρίθη Ἰάκωβος λέγων· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἀκούσατέ μου.
verses.translit: meta de to sigesai autous apekrithi Iakovos legon* Andres adelfoi, akoysate moy.
verses.translation: And after they had held their peace, James answered, saying, Men and brethren, hearken unto me:

verses.original: Συμεὼν ἐξηγήσατο καθὼς πρῶτον ὁ θεὸς ἐπεσκέψατο λαβεῖν ἐξ ἐθνῶν ⸀λαὸν τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Symeon exigisato kathos proton o theos epeskepsato lavein ex ethnon laon to onomati autou.
verses.translation: Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.

verses.original: καὶ τούτῳ συμφωνοῦσιν οἱ λόγοι τῶν προφητῶν, καθὼς γέγραπται·
verses.translit: kai toyto symfonousin oi logoi ton profiton, kathos gegraptai*
verses.translation: And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written,

verses.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἀναστρέψω καὶ ἀνοικοδομήσω τὴν σκηνὴν Δαυὶδ τὴν πεπτωκυῖαν καὶ τὰ ⸀κατεσκαμμένα αὐτῆς ἀνοικοδομήσω καὶ ἀνορθώσω αὐτήν,
verses.translit: Meta tauta anastrepso kai anoikodomiso ten skinen Dayid ten peptokyian kai ta kateskammena autes anoikodomiso kai anorthoso autin,
verses.translation: After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up:

verses.original: ὅπως ἂν ἐκζητήσωσιν οἱ κατάλοιποι τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὸν κύριον, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἐφʼ οὓς ἐπικέκληται τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐπʼ αὐτούς, λέγει ⸀κύριος ποιῶν ⸀ταῦτα
verses.translit: opos an ekzitisosin oi kataloipoi ton anthropon ton kyrion, kai panta ta ethni ef' ous epikeklitai to onoma moy ep' autoys, legei kyrios poion tauta
verses.translation: That the residue of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called, saith the Lord, who doeth all these things.

verses.original: γνωστὰ ἀπʼ ⸀αἰῶνος.
verses.translit: gnosta ap' aionos.
verses.translation: Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world.

verses.original: διὸ ἐγὼ κρίνω μὴ παρενοχλεῖν τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐπιστρέφουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν,
verses.translit: dio ego krino me parenohlein tois apo ton ethnon epistrefoysin epi ton theon,
verses.translation: Wherefore my sentence is, that we trouble not them, which from among the Gentiles are turned to God:

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ἐπιστεῖλαι αὐτοῖς τοῦ ⸀ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν ἀλισγημάτων τῶν εἰδώλων καὶ τῆς πορνείας καὶ ⸀τοῦ πνικτοῦ καὶ τοῦ αἵματος·
verses.translit: alla episteilai autois tou apehesthai ton alisgimaton ton eidolon kai tes porneias kai tou pniktou kai tou aimatos*
verses.translation: But that we write unto them, that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood.

verses.original: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ ἐκ γενεῶν ἀρχαίων κατὰ πόλιν τοὺς κηρύσσοντας αὐτὸν ἔχει ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον ἀναγινωσκόμενος.
verses.translit: Moyses gar ek geneon arhaion kata polin tous kiryssontas auton ehei en tais synagogais kata pan savvaton anaginoskomenos.
verses.translation: For Moses of old time hath in every city them that preach him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath day.

verses.original: Τότε ἔδοξε τοῖς ἀποστόλοις καὶ τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις σὺν ὅλῃ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐκλεξαμένους ἄνδρας ἐξ αὐτῶν πέμψαι εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν σὺν ⸀τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ Βαρναβᾷ, Ἰούδαν τὸν ⸀καλούμενον Βαρσαββᾶν καὶ Σιλᾶν, ἄνδρας ἡγουμένους ἐν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς,
verses.translit: Tote edoxe tois apostolois kai tois presvyterois sun ole te ekklisia eklexamenoys andras ex auton pempsai eis Antioheian sun to Paylo kai Varnava, Ioydan ton kaloymenon Varsavvan kai Silan, andras egoymenoys en tois adelfois,
verses.translation: Then pleased it the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; namely , Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren:

verses.original: γράψαντες διὰ χειρὸς ⸀αὐτῶν· Οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ ⸀πρεσβύτεροι ἀδελφοὶ τοῖς κατὰ τὴν Ἀντιόχειαν καὶ Συρίαν καὶ Κιλικίαν ἀδελφοῖς τοῖς ἐξ ἐθνῶν χαίρειν.
verses.translit: grapsantes dia heiros auton* Oi apostoloi kai oi presvyteroi adelfoi tois kata ten Antioheian kai Syrian kai Kilikian adelfois tois ex ethnon hairein.
verses.translation: And they wrote letters by them after this manner; The apostles and elders and brethren send greeting unto the brethren which are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia:

verses.original: ἐπειδὴ ἠκούσαμεν ὅτι τινὲς ἐξ ἡμῶν ⸀ἐξελθόντες ἐτάραξαν ὑμᾶς λόγοις ἀνασκευάζοντες τὰς ψυχὰς ⸀ὑμῶν οἷς οὐ διεστειλάμεθα,
verses.translit: epeide ekoysamen oti tines ex emon exelthontes etaraxan umas logois anaskeyazontes tas psyhas umon ois ou diesteilametha,
verses.translation: Forasmuch as we have heard, that certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, Ye must be circumcised, and keep the law: to whom we gave no such commandment:

verses.original: ἔδοξεν ἡμῖν γενομένοις ὁμοθυμαδὸν ⸀ἐκλεξαμένοις ἄνδρας πέμψαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς σὺν τοῖς ἀγαπητοῖς ἡμῶν Βαρναβᾷ καὶ Παύλῳ,
verses.translit: edoxen emin genomenois omothymadon eklexamenois andras pempsai pros umas sun tois agapitois emon Varnava kai Paylo,
verses.translation: It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,

verses.original: ἀνθρώποις παραδεδωκόσι τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: anthropois paradedokosi tas psyhas auton uper tou onomatos tou kyrioy emon Iisou Hristou.
verses.translation: Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.original: ἀπεστάλκαμεν οὖν Ἰούδαν καὶ Σιλᾶν, καὶ αὐτοὺς διὰ λόγου ἀπαγγέλλοντας τὰ αὐτά.
verses.translit: apestalkamen oun Ioydan kai Silan, kai autous dia logoy apaggellontas ta auta.
verses.translation: We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who shall also tell you the same things by mouth.

verses.original: ἔδοξεν γὰρ τῷ ⸂πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ⸃ καὶ ἡμῖν μηδὲν πλέον ἐπιτίθεσθαι ὑμῖν βάρος πλὴν ⸂τούτων τῶν ἐπάναγκες⸃,
verses.translit: edoxen gar to pneymati to agio kai emin miden pleon epitithesthai umin varos plen toyton ton epanagkes,
verses.translation: For it seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us, to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things;

verses.original: ἀπέχεσθαι εἰδωλοθύτων καὶ αἵματος καὶ ⸀πνικτῶν καὶ πορνείας· ἐξ ὧν διατηροῦντες ἑαυτοὺς εὖ πράξετε. ἔρρωσθε.
verses.translit: apehesthai eidolothyton kai aimatos kai pnikton kai porneias* ex on diatirountes eaytous eu praxete. errosthe.
verses.translation: That ye abstain from meats offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication: from which if ye keep yourselves, ye shall do well. Fare ye well.

verses.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν ἀπολυθέντες ⸀κατῆλθον εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, καὶ συναγαγόντες τὸ πλῆθος ἐπέδωκαν τὴν ἐπιστολήν·
verses.translit: Oi men oun apolythentes katelthon eis Antioheian, kai synagagontes to plethos epedokan ten epistolin*
verses.translation: So when they were dismissed, they came to Antioch: and when they had gathered the multitude together, they delivered the epistle:

verses.original: ἀναγνόντες δὲ ἐχάρησαν ἐπὶ τῇ παρακλήσει.
verses.translit: anagnontes de eharisan epi te paraklisei.
verses.translation: Which when they had read, they rejoiced for the consolation.

verses.original: Ἰούδας τε καὶ Σιλᾶς, καὶ αὐτοὶ προφῆται ὄντες, διὰ λόγου πολλοῦ παρεκάλεσαν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἐπεστήριξαν·
verses.translit: Ioydas te kai Silas, kai autoi profetai ontes, dia logoy pollou parekalesan tous adelfous kai epestirixan*
verses.translation: And Judas and Silas, being prophets also themselves, exhorted the brethren with many words, and confirmed them .

verses.original: ποιήσαντες δὲ χρόνον ἀπελύθησαν μετʼ εἰρήνης ἀπὸ τῶν ἀδελφῶν πρὸς τοὺς ⸂ἀποστείλαντας αὐτούς⸃.
verses.translit: poiisantes de hronon apelythisan met' eirinis apo ton adelfon pros tous aposteilantas autoys.
verses.translation: And after they had tarried there a space, they were let go in peace from the brethren unto the apostles.
Notwithstanding it pleased Silas to abide there still.

verses.original: Παῦλος δὲ καὶ Βαρναβᾶς διέτριβον ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ διδάσκοντες καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι μετὰ καὶ ἑτέρων πολλῶν τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου.
verses.translit: Paulos de kai Varnavas dietrivon en Antioheia didaskontes kai euaggelizomenoi meta kai eteron pollon ton logon tou kyrioy.
verses.translation: Paul also and Barnabas continued in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, with many others also.

verses.original: Μετὰ δέ τινας ἡμέρας εἶπεν ⸂πρὸς Βαρναβᾶν Παῦλος⸃· Ἐπιστρέψαντες δὴ ἐπισκεψώμεθα τοὺς ⸀ἀδελφοὺς κατὰ ⸂πόλιν πᾶσαν⸃ ἐν αἷς κατηγγείλαμεν τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου, πῶς ἔχουσιν.
verses.translit: Meta de tinas emeras eipen pros Varnavan Paulos* Epistrepsantes de episkepsometha tous adelfous kata polin pasan en ais katiggeilamen ton logon tou kyrioy, pos ehoysin.
verses.translation: And some days after Paul said unto Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brethren in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they do.

verses.original: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ ⸀ἐβούλετο συμπαραλαβεῖν ⸀καὶ τὸν Ἰωάννην τὸν καλούμενον Μᾶρκον·
verses.translit: Varnavas de evoyleto symparalavein kai ton Ioannin ton kaloymenon Markon*
verses.translation: And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark.

verses.original: Παῦλος δὲ ἠξίου, τὸν ἀποστάντα ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Παμφυλίας καὶ μὴ συνελθόντα αὐτοῖς εἰς τὸ ἔργον, μὴ ⸀συμπαραλαμβάνειν τοῦτον.
verses.translit: Paulos de exioy, ton apostanta ap' auton apo Pamfylias kai me synelthonta autois eis to ergon, me symparalamvanein touton.
verses.translation: But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.

verses.original: ἐγένετο ⸀δὲ παροξυσμὸς ὥστε ἀποχωρισθῆναι αὐτοὺς ἀπʼ ἀλλήλων, τόν τε Βαρναβᾶν παραλαβόντα τὸν Μᾶρκον ἐκπλεῦσαι εἰς Κύπρον,
verses.translit: egeneto de paroxysmos oste apohoristhenai autous ap' allilon, ton te Varnavan paralavonta ton Markon ekpleusai eis Kypron,
verses.translation: And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus;

verses.original: Παῦλος δὲ ἐπιλεξάμενος Σιλᾶν ἐξῆλθεν παραδοθεὶς τῇ χάριτι τοῦ ⸀κυρίου ὑπὸ τῶν ἀδελφῶν,
verses.translit: Paulos de epilexamenos Silan exelthen paradotheis te hariti tou kyrioy upo ton adelfon,
verses.translation: And Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God.

verses.original: διήρχετο δὲ τὴν Συρίαν καὶ ⸀τὴν Κιλικίαν ἐπιστηρίζων τὰς ἐκκλησίας.
verses.translit: diirheto de ten Syrian kai ten Kilikian epistirizon tas ekklisias.
verses.translation: And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches.

verses.original: Κατήντησεν δὲ ⸀καὶ εἰς Δέρβην καὶ ⸀εἰς Λύστραν. καὶ ἰδοὺ μαθητής τις ἦν ἐκεῖ ὀνόματι Τιμόθεος, υἱὸς ⸀γυναικὸς Ἰουδαίας πιστῆς, πατρὸς δὲ Ἕλληνος,
verses.translit: Katintisen de kai eis Dervin kai eis Lystran. kai idou mathitis tis en ekei onomati Timotheos, yios gynaikos Ioydaias pistes, patros de Ellinos,
verses.translation: Then came he to Derbe and Lystra: and, behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek:

verses.original: ὃς ἐμαρτυρεῖτο ὑπὸ τῶν ἐν Λύστροις καὶ Ἰκονίῳ ἀδελφῶν·
verses.translit: os emartyreito upo ton en Lystrois kai Ikonio adelfon*
verses.translation: Which was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium.

verses.original: τοῦτον ἠθέλησεν ὁ Παῦλος σὺν αὐτῷ ἐξελθεῖν, καὶ λαβὼν περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν διὰ τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τοὺς ὄντας ἐν τοῖς τόποις ἐκείνοις, ᾔδεισαν γὰρ ἅπαντες ⸂ὅτι Ἕλλην ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ⸃ ὑπῆρχεν.
verses.translit: touton ethelisen o Paulos sun auto exelthein, kai lavon perietemen auton dia tous Ioydaioys tous ontas en tois topois ekeinois, edeisan gar apantes oti Ellin o pater autou uperhen.
verses.translation: Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ διεπορεύοντο τὰς πόλεις, ⸀παρεδίδοσαν αὐτοῖς φυλάσσειν τὰ δόγματα τὰ κεκριμένα ὑπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων ⸀καὶ πρεσβυτέρων τῶν ἐν ⸀Ἱεροσολύμοις.
verses.translit: os de dieporeyonto tas poleis, paredidosan autois fylassein ta dogmata ta kekrimena upo ton apostolon kai presvyteron ton en Ierosolymois.
verses.translation: And as they went through the cities, they delivered them the decrees for to keep, that were ordained of the apostles and elders which were at Jerusalem.

verses.original: αἱ μὲν οὖν ἐκκλησίαι ἐστερεοῦντο τῇ πίστει καὶ ἐπερίσσευον τῷ ἀριθμῷ καθʼ ἡμέραν.
verses.translit: ai men oun ekklisiai estereounto te pistei kai eperisseyon to arithmo kath' emeran.
verses.translation: And so were the churches established in the faith, and increased in number daily.

verses.original: ⸀Διῆλθον δὲ τὴν Φρυγίαν ⸀καὶ Γαλατικὴν χώραν, κωλυθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος λαλῆσαι τὸν λόγον ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ,
verses.translit: Dielthon de ten Frygian kai Galatiken horan, kolythentes upo tou agioy pneymatos lalesai ton logon en te Asia,
verses.translation: Now when they had gone throughout Phrygia and the region of Galatia, and were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia,

verses.original: ἐλθόντες ⸀δὲ κατὰ τὴν Μυσίαν ἐπείραζον ⸀εἰς τὴν Βιθυνίαν ⸀πορευθῆναι καὶ οὐκ εἴασεν αὐτοὺς τὸ πνεῦμα ⸀Ἰησοῦ·
verses.translit: elthontes de kata ten Mysian epeirazon eis ten Vithynian poreythenai kai ouk eiasen autous to pneuma Iisou*
verses.translation: After they were come to Mysia, they assayed to go into Bithynia: but the Spirit suffered them not.

verses.original: παρελθόντες δὲ τὴν Μυσίαν κατέβησαν εἰς Τρῳάδα.
verses.translit: parelthontes de ten Mysian katevisan eis Troada.
verses.translation: And they passing by Mysia came down to Troas.

verses.original: καὶ ὅραμα ⸀διὰ νυκτὸς ⸂τῷ Παύλῳ ὤφθη⸃, ἀνὴρ ⸂Μακεδών τις ἦν⸃ ἑστὼς ⸀καὶ παρακαλῶν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγων· Διαβὰς εἰς Μακεδονίαν βοήθησον ἡμῖν.
verses.translit: kai orama dia nyktos to Paylo ofthi, aner Makedon tis en estos kai parakalon auton kai legon* Diavas eis Makedonian voithison emin.
verses.translation: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ τὸ ὅραμα εἶδεν, εὐθέως ἐζητήσαμεν ἐξελθεῖν ⸀εἰς Μακεδονίαν, συμβιβάζοντες ὅτι προσκέκληται ἡμᾶς ὁ ⸀θεὸς εὐαγγελίσασθαι αὐτούς.
verses.translit: os de to orama eiden, eutheos ezitisamen exelthein eis Makedonian, symvivazontes oti proskeklitai emas o theos euaggelisasthai autoys.
verses.translation: And after he had seen the vision, immediately we endeavoured to go into Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord had called us for to preach the gospel unto them.

verses.original: Ἀναχθέντες ⸀οὖν ⸀ἀπὸ Τρῳάδος εὐθυδρομήσαμεν εἰς Σαμοθρᾴκην, τῇ ⸀δὲ ἐπιούσῃ εἰς ⸂Νέαν Πόλιν⸃,
verses.translit: Anahthentes oun apo Troados euthydromisamen eis Samothrakin, te de epioyse eis Nean Polin,
verses.translation: Therefore loosing from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothracia, and the next day to Neapolis;

verses.original: ⸀κἀκεῖθεν εἰς Φιλίππους, ἥτις ἐστὶν ⸂πρώτη τῆς μερίδος⸃ Μακεδονίας πόλις, κολωνία. ἦμεν δὲ ἐν ⸀ταύτῃ τῇ πόλει διατρίβοντες ἡμέρας τινάς.
verses.translit: kakeithen eis Filippoys, etis estin proti tes meridos Makedonias polis, kolonia. emen de en tayte te polei diatrivontes emeras tinas.
verses.translation: And from thence to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, and a colony: and we were in that city abiding certain days.

verses.original: τῇ τε ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων ἐξήλθομεν ἔξω τῆς ⸀πύλης παρὰ ποταμὸν οὗ ⸂ἐνομίζομεν προσευχὴν⸃ εἶναι, καὶ καθίσαντες ἐλαλοῦμεν ταῖς συνελθούσαις γυναιξίν.
verses.translit: te te emera ton savvaton exilthomen exo tes pylis para potamon ou enomizomen proseyhen einai, kai kathisantes elaloumen tais synelthoysais gynaixin.
verses.translation: And on the sabbath we went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was wont to be made; and we sat down, and spake unto the women which resorted thither.

verses.original: καί τις γυνὴ ὀνόματι Λυδία, πορφυρόπωλις πόλεως Θυατείρων σεβομένη τὸν θεόν, ἤκουεν, ἧς ὁ κύριος διήνοιξεν τὴν καρδίαν προσέχειν τοῖς λαλουμένοις ὑπὸ ⸀τοῦ Παύλου.
verses.translit: kai tis gyne onomati Lydia, porfyropolis poleos Thyateiron sevomeni ton theon, ekoyen, es o kyrios diinoixen ten kardian prosehein tois laloymenois upo tou Payloy.
verses.translation: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us : whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἐβαπτίσθη καὶ ὁ οἶκος αὐτῆς, παρεκάλεσεν λέγουσα· Εἰ κεκρίκατέ με πιστὴν τῷ κυρίῳ εἶναι, εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου ⸀μένετε· καὶ παρεβιάσατο ἡμᾶς.
verses.translit: os de evaptisthi kai o oikos autes, parekalesen legoysa* Ei kekrikate me pisten to kyrio einai, eiselthontes eis ton oikon moy menete* kai pareviasato emas.
verses.translation: And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought us , saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there . And she constrained us.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ πορευομένων ἡμῶν εἰς ⸀τὴν προσευχὴν παιδίσκην τινὰ ἔχουσαν πνεῦμα ⸀πύθωνα ⸀ὑπαντῆσαι ἡμῖν, ἥτις ἐργασίαν πολλὴν παρεῖχεν τοῖς κυρίοις αὐτῆς μαντευομένη·
verses.translit: Egeneto de poreyomenon emon eis ten proseyhen paidiskin tina ehoysan pneuma pythona upantesai emin, etis ergasian pollen pareihen tois kyriois autes manteyomeni*
verses.translation: And it came to pass, as we went to prayer, a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination met us, which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying:

verses.original: αὕτη ⸀κατακολουθοῦσα τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ ἡμῖν ἔκραζεν λέγουσα· Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι δοῦλοι τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου εἰσίν, οἵτινες καταγγέλλουσιν ⸀ὑμῖν ὁδὸν σωτηρίας.
verses.translit: auti katakoloythousa to Paylo kai emin ekrazen legoysa* Outoi oi anthropoi douloi tou theou tou upsistoy eisin, oitines kataggelloysin umin odon sotirias.
verses.translation: The same followed Paul and us, and cried, saying, These men are the servants of the most high God, which shew unto us the way of salvation.

verses.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἐποίει ἐπὶ πολλὰς ἡμέρας. διαπονηθεὶς ⸀δὲ Παῦλος καὶ ἐπιστρέψας τῷ πνεύματι εἶπεν· Παραγγέλλω σοι ⸀ἐν ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐξελθεῖν ἀπʼ αὐτῆς· καὶ ἐξῆλθεν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ.
verses.translit: touto de epoiei epi pollas emeras. diaponitheis de Paulos kai epistrepsas to pneymati eipen* Paraggello soi en onomati Iisou Hristou exelthein ap' autes* kai exelthen aute te ora.
verses.translation: And this did she many days. But Paul, being grieved, turned and said to the spirit, I command thee in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her. And he came out the same hour.

verses.original: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ κύριοι αὐτῆς ὅτι ἐξῆλθεν ἡ ἐλπὶς τῆς ἐργασίας αὐτῶν ἐπιλαβόμενοι τὸν Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἵλκυσαν εἰς τὴν ἀγορὰν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας,
verses.translit: Idontes de oi kyrioi autes oti exelthen e elpis tes ergasias auton epilavomenoi ton Paulon kai ton Silan eilkysan eis ten agoran epi tous arhontas,
verses.translation: And when her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone, they caught Paul and Silas, and drew them into the marketplace unto the rulers,

verses.original: καὶ προσαγαγόντες αὐτοὺς τοῖς στρατηγοῖς εἶπαν· Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι ἐκταράσσουσιν ἡμῶν τὴν πόλιν Ἰουδαῖοι ὑπάρχοντες,
verses.translit: kai prosagagontes autous tois stratigois eipan* Outoi oi anthropoi ektarassoysin emon ten polin Ioydaioi uparhontes,
verses.translation: And brought them to the magistrates, saying, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city,

verses.original: καὶ καταγγέλλουσιν ἔθη ἃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ἡμῖν παραδέχεσθαι οὐδὲ ποιεῖν Ῥωμαίοις οὖσιν.
verses.translit: kai kataggelloysin ethi a ouk exestin emin paradehesthai oude poiein Romaiois ousin.
verses.translation: And teach customs, which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans.

verses.original: καὶ συνεπέστη ὁ ὄχλος κατʼ αὐτῶν, καὶ οἱ στρατηγοὶ περιρήξαντες αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐκέλευον ῥαβδίζειν,
verses.translit: kai synepesti o ohlos kat' auton, kai oi stratigoi peririxantes auton ta imatia ekeleyon Ravdizein,
verses.translation: And the multitude rose up together against them: and the magistrates rent off their clothes, and commanded to beat them .

verses.original: πολλάς ⸀τε ἐπιθέντες αὐτοῖς πληγὰς ἔβαλον εἰς φυλακήν, παραγγείλαντες τῷ δεσμοφύλακι ἀσφαλῶς τηρεῖν αὐτούς·
verses.translit: pollas te epithentes autois pligas evalon eis fylakin, paraggeilantes to desmofylaki asfalos tirein autoys*
verses.translation: And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely:

verses.original: ὃς παραγγελίαν τοιαύτην ⸀λαβὼν ἔβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν ἐσωτέραν φυλακὴν καὶ τοὺς πόδας ⸂ἠσφαλίσατο αὐτῶν⸃ εἰς τὸ ξύλον.
verses.translit: os paraggelian toiaytin lavon evalen autous eis ten esoteran fylaken kai tous podas esfalisato auton eis to xylon.
verses.translation: Who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks.

verses.original: Κατὰ δὲ τὸ μεσονύκτιον Παῦλος καὶ Σιλᾶς προσευχόμενοι ὕμνουν τὸν θεόν, ἐπηκροῶντο δὲ αὐτῶν οἱ δέσμιοι·
verses.translit: Kata de to mesonyktion Paulos kai Silas proseyhomenoi umnoyn ton theon, epikroonto de auton oi desmioi*
verses.translation: And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.

verses.original: ἄφνω δὲ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας ὥστε σαλευθῆναι τὰ θεμέλια τοῦ δεσμωτηρίου, ἠνεῴχθησαν ⸀δὲ παραχρῆμα αἱ θύραι πᾶσαι, καὶ πάντων τὰ δεσμὰ ἀνέθη.
verses.translit: afno de seismos egeneto megas oste saleythenai ta themelia tou desmotirioy, eneohthisan de parahrema ai thyrai pasai, kai panton ta desma anethi.
verses.translation: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one’s bands were loosed.

verses.original: ἔξυπνος δὲ γενόμενος ὁ δεσμοφύλαξ καὶ ἰδὼν ἀνεῳγμένας τὰς θύρας τῆς φυλακῆς σπασάμενος ⸀τὴν μάχαιραν ἤμελλεν ἑαυτὸν ἀναιρεῖν, νομίζων ἐκπεφευγέναι τοὺς δεσμίους.
verses.translit: exypnos de genomenos o desmofylax kai idon aneogmenas tas thyras tes fylakes spasamenos ten mahairan emellen eayton anairein, nomizon ekpefeygenai tous desmioys.
verses.translation: And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.

verses.original: ἐφώνησεν δὲ ⸂φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὁ Παῦλος⸃ λέγων· Μηδὲν πράξῃς σεαυτῷ κακόν, ἅπαντες γάρ ἐσμεν ἐνθάδε.
verses.translit: efonisen de fone megale o Paulos legon* Miden praxes seayto kakon, apantes gar esmen enthade.
verses.translation: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.

verses.original: αἰτήσας δὲ φῶτα εἰσεπήδησεν καὶ ἔντρομος γενόμενος προσέπεσεν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ ⸀τῷ Σιλᾷ,
verses.translit: aitisas de fota eisepidisen kai entromos genomenos prosepesen to Paylo kai to Sila,
verses.translation: Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas,

verses.original: καὶ προαγαγὼν αὐτοὺς ἔξω ἔφη· Κύριοι, τί με δεῖ ποιεῖν ἵνα σωθῶ;
verses.translit: kai proagagon autous exo efi* Kyrioi, ti me dei poiein ina sotho;
verses.translation: And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?

verses.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Πίστευσον ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον ⸀Ἰησοῦν, καὶ σωθήσῃ σὺ καὶ ὁ οἶκός σου.
verses.translit: oi de eipan* Pisteyson epi ton kyrion Iisoun, kai sothise su kai o oikos soy.
verses.translation: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.

verses.original: καὶ ἐλάλησαν αὐτῷ τὸν λόγον τοῦ ⸀κυρίου ⸀σὺν πᾶσι τοῖς ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai elalisan auto ton logon tou kyrioy sun pasi tois en te oikia autou.
verses.translation: And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house.

verses.original: καὶ παραλαβὼν αὐτοὺς ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τῆς νυκτὸς ἔλουσεν ἀπὸ τῶν πληγῶν, καὶ ἐβαπτίσθη αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ αὐτοῦ ⸀πάντες παραχρῆμα,
verses.translit: kai paralavon autous en ekeine te ora tes nyktos eloysen apo ton pligon, kai evaptisthi autos kai oi autou pantes parahrema,
verses.translation: And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway.

verses.original: ἀναγαγών τε αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν ⸀οἶκον παρέθηκεν τράπεζαν καὶ ⸀ἠγαλλιάσατο πανοικεὶ πεπιστευκὼς τῷ θεῷ.
verses.translit: anagagon te autous eis ton oikon parethiken trapezan kai egalliasato panoikei pepisteykos to theo.
verses.translation: And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.

verses.original: Ἡμέρας δὲ γενομένης ἀπέστειλαν οἱ στρατηγοὶ τοὺς ῥαβδούχους λέγοντες· Ἀπόλυσον τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἐκείνους.
verses.translit: Emeras de genomenis apesteilan oi stratigoi tous Ravdoyhoys legontes* Apolyson tous anthropoys ekeinoys.
verses.translation: And when it was day, the magistrates sent the serjeants, saying, Let those men go.

verses.original: ἀπήγγειλεν δὲ ὁ δεσμοφύλαξ τοὺς λόγους ⸀τούτους πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον, ὅτι Ἀπέσταλκαν οἱ στρατηγοὶ ἵνα ἀπολυθῆτε· νῦν οὖν ἐξελθόντες πορεύεσθε ἐν εἰρήνῃ.
verses.translit: apiggeilen de o desmofylax tous logoys toytoys pros ton Paulon, oti Apestalkan oi stratigoi ina apolythete* nun oun exelthontes poreyesthe en eirine.
verses.translation: And the keeper of the prison told this saying to Paul, The magistrates have sent to let you go: now therefore depart, and go in peace.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη πρὸς αὐτούς· Δείραντες ἡμᾶς δημοσίᾳ ἀκατακρίτους, ἀνθρώπους Ῥωμαίους ὑπάρχοντας, ἔβαλαν εἰς φυλακήν· καὶ νῦν λάθρᾳ ἡμᾶς ἐκβάλλουσιν; οὐ γάρ, ἀλλὰ ἐλθόντες αὐτοὶ ⸀ἡμᾶς ἐξαγαγέτωσαν.
verses.translit: o de Paulos efi pros autoys* Deirantes emas dimosia akatakritoys, anthropoys Romaioys uparhontas, evalan eis fylakin* kai nun lathra emas ekvalloysin; ou gar, alla elthontes autoi emas exagagetosan.
verses.translation: But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out.

verses.original: ⸀ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ τοῖς στρατηγοῖς οἱ ῥαβδοῦχοι τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα· ⸂ἐφοβήθησαν δὲ⸃ ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Ῥωμαῖοί εἰσιν,
verses.translit: apiggeilan de tois stratigois oi Ravdouhoi ta Rimata tauta* efovithisan de akoysantes oti Romaioi eisin,
verses.translation: And the serjeants told these words unto the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans.

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθόντες παρεκάλεσαν αὐτούς, καὶ ἐξαγαγόντες ἠρώτων ⸂ἀπελθεῖν ἀπὸ⸃ τῆς πόλεως.
verses.translit: kai elthontes parekalesan autoys, kai exagagontes eroton apelthein apo tes poleos.
verses.translation: And they came and besought them, and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city.

verses.original: ἐξελθόντες δὲ ⸀ἀπὸ τῆς φυλακῆς εἰσῆλθον πρὸς τὴν Λυδίαν, καὶ ἰδόντες ⸂παρεκάλεσαν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς⸃ καὶ ἐξῆλθαν.
verses.translit: exelthontes de apo tes fylakes eiselthon pros ten Lydian, kai idontes parekalesan tous adelfous kai exelthan.
verses.translation: And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.

verses.original: Διοδεύσαντες δὲ τὴν Ἀμφίπολιν καὶ ⸀τὴν Ἀπολλωνίαν ἦλθον εἰς Θεσσαλονίκην, ὅπου ⸀ἦν συναγωγὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
verses.translit: Diodeysantes de ten Amfipolin kai ten Apollonian elthon eis Thessalonikin, opoy en synagoge ton Ioydaion.
verses.translation: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews:

verses.original: κατὰ δὲ τὸ εἰωθὸς τῷ Παύλῳ εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς καὶ ἐπὶ σάββατα τρία διελέξατο αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν γραφῶν,
verses.translit: kata de to eiothos to Paylo eiselthen pros autous kai epi savvata tria dielexato autois apo ton grafon,
verses.translation: And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,

verses.original: διανοίγων καὶ παρατιθέμενος ὅτι τὸν χριστὸν ἔδει παθεῖν καὶ ἀναστῆναι ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ⸂ὁ χριστός, ὁ⸃ Ἰησοῦς ὃν ἐγὼ καταγγέλλω ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: dianoigon kai paratithemenos oti ton hriston edei pathein kai anastenai ek nekron, kai oti outos estin o hristos, o Iisous on ego kataggello umin.
verses.translation: Opening and alleging, that Christ must needs have suffered, and risen again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach unto you, is Christ.

verses.original: καί τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπείσθησαν καὶ προσεκληρώθησαν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Σιλᾷ, τῶν τε σεβομένων Ἑλλήνων ⸂πλῆθος πολὺ⸃ γυναικῶν τε τῶν πρώτων οὐκ ὀλίγαι.
verses.translit: kai tines ex auton epeisthisan kai proseklirothisan to Paylo kai to Sila, ton te sevomenon Ellinon plethos polu gynaikon te ton proton ouk oligai.
verses.translation: And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.

verses.original: ⸂ζηλώσαντες δὲ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ προσλαβόμενοι⸃ τῶν ἀγοραίων ⸂ἄνδρας τινὰς⸃ πονηροὺς καὶ ὀχλοποιήσαντες ἐθορύβουν τὴν πόλιν, ⸂καὶ ἐπιστάντες⸃ τῇ οἰκίᾳ Ἰάσονος ἐζήτουν αὐτοὺς ⸀προαγαγεῖν εἰς τὸν δῆμον·
verses.translit: zilosantes de oi Ioydaioi kai proslavomenoi ton agoraion andras tinas ponirous kai ohlopoiisantes ethoryvoyn ten polin, kai epistantes te oikia Iasonos ezitoyn autous proagagein eis ton demon*
verses.translation: But the Jews which believed not, moved with envy, took unto them certain lewd fellows of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city on an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people.

verses.original: μὴ εὑρόντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ⸀ἔσυρον Ἰάσονα καί τινας ἀδελφοὺς ἐπὶ τοὺς πολιτάρχας, βοῶντες ὅτι Οἱ τὴν οἰκουμένην ἀναστατώσαντες οὗτοι καὶ ἐνθάδε πάρεισιν,
verses.translit: me eurontes de autous esyron Iasona kai tinas adelfous epi tous politarhas, voontes oti Oi ten oikoymenin anastatosantes outoi kai enthade pareisin,
verses.translation: And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also;

verses.original: οὓς ὑποδέδεκται Ἰάσων· καὶ οὗτοι πάντες ἀπέναντι τῶν δογμάτων Καίσαρος πράσσουσι, βασιλέα ⸂ἕτερον λέγοντες⸃ εἶναι Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: ous upodedektai Iason* kai outoi pantes apenanti ton dogmaton Kaisaros prassoysi, vasilea eteron legontes einai Iisoun.
verses.translation: Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Cæsar, saying that there is another king, one Jesus.

verses.original: ἐτάραξαν δὲ τὸν ὄχλον καὶ τοὺς πολιτάρχας ἀκούοντας ταῦτα,
verses.translit: etaraxan de ton ohlon kai tous politarhas akoyontas tauta,
verses.translation: And they troubled the people and the rulers of the city, when they heard these things.

verses.original: καὶ λαβόντες τὸ ἱκανὸν παρὰ τοῦ Ἰάσονος καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν ἀπέλυσαν αὐτούς.
verses.translit: kai lavontes to ikanon para tou Iasonos kai ton loipon apelysan autoys.
verses.translation: And when they had taken security of Jason, and of the other, they let them go.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀδελφοὶ εὐθέως ⸀διὰ νυκτὸς ἐξέπεμψαν τόν τε Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἰς Βέροιαν, οἵτινες παραγενόμενοι εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν ⸂τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀπῄεσαν⸃·
verses.translit: Oi de adelfoi eutheos dia nyktos exepempsan ton te Paulon kai ton Silan eis Veroian, oitines paragenomenoi eis ten synagogen ton Ioydaion apeesan*
verses.translation: And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.

verses.original: οὗτοι δὲ ἦσαν εὐγενέστεροι τῶν ἐν Θεσσαλονίκῃ, οἵτινες ἐδέξαντο τὸν λόγον μετὰ πάσης προθυμίας, ⸀τὸ καθʼ ἡμέραν ἀνακρίνοντες τὰς γραφὰς εἰ ἔχοι ταῦτα οὕτως.
verses.translit: outoi de esan eugenesteroi ton en Thessalonike, oitines edexanto ton logon meta pasis prothymias, to kath' emeran anakrinontes tas grafas ei ehoi tauta outos.
verses.translation: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.

verses.original: πολλοὶ μὲν οὖν ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπίστευσαν, καὶ τῶν Ἑλληνίδων γυναικῶν τῶν εὐσχημόνων καὶ ἀνδρῶν οὐκ ὀλίγοι.
verses.translit: polloi men oun ex auton episteysan, kai ton Ellinidon gynaikon ton eushimonon kai andron ouk oligoi.
verses.translation: Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Θεσσαλονίκης Ἰουδαῖοι ὅτι καὶ ἐν τῇ Βεροίᾳ κατηγγέλη ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ, ἦλθον κἀκεῖ σαλεύοντες ⸂καὶ ταράσσοντες⸃ τοὺς ὄχλους.
verses.translit: os de egnosan oi apo tes Thessalonikis Ioydaioi oti kai en te Veroia katiggeli upo tou Payloy o logos tou theou, elthon kakei saleyontes kai tarassontes tous ohloys.
verses.translation: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred up the people.

verses.original: εὐθέως δὲ τότε τὸν Παῦλον ἐξαπέστειλαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πορεύεσθαι ⸀ἕως ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν· ⸂ὑπέμεινάν τε⸃ ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος ἐκεῖ.
verses.translit: eutheos de tote ton Paulon exapesteilan oi adelfoi poreyesthai eos epi ten thalassan* upemeinan te o te Silas kai o Timotheos ekei.
verses.translation: And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus abode there still.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ⸀καθιστάνοντες τὸν Παῦλον ⸀ἤγαγον ἕως Ἀθηνῶν, καὶ λαβόντες ἐντολὴν πρὸς τὸν Σιλᾶν καὶ ⸀τὸν Τιμόθεον ἵνα ὡς τάχιστα ἔλθωσιν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐξῄεσαν.
verses.translit: oi de kathistanontes ton Paulon egagon eos Athinon, kai lavontes entolen pros ton Silan kai ton Timotheon ina os tahista elthosin pros auton exeesan.
verses.translation: And they that conducted Paul brought him unto Athens: and receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timotheus for to come to him with all speed, they departed.

verses.original: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς Ἀθήναις ἐκδεχομένου αὐτοὺς τοῦ Παύλου, παρωξύνετο τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ⸀θεωροῦντος κατείδωλον οὖσαν τὴν πόλιν.
verses.translit: En de tais Athinais ekdehomenoy autous tou Payloy, paroxyneto to pneuma autou en auto theorountos kateidolon ousan ten polin.
verses.translation: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry.

verses.original: διελέγετο μὲν οὖν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις καὶ τοῖς σεβομένοις καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ κατὰ πᾶσαν ἡμέραν πρὸς τοὺς παρατυγχάνοντας.
verses.translit: dielegeto men oun en te synagoge tois Ioydaiois kai tois sevomenois kai en te agora kata pasan emeran pros tous paratyghanontas.
verses.translation: Therefore disputed he in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout persons, and in the market daily with them that met with him.

verses.original: τινὲς δὲ καὶ τῶν Ἐπικουρείων ⸀καὶ Στοϊκῶν φιλοσόφων συνέβαλλον αὐτῷ, καί τινες ἔλεγον· Τί ἂν θέλοι ὁ σπερμολόγος οὗτος λέγειν; οἱ δέ· Ξένων δαιμονίων δοκεῖ καταγγελεὺς εἶναι· ὅτι τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ τὴν ἀνάστασιν εὐηγγελίζετο.
verses.translit: tines de kai ton Epikoyreion kai Stoikon filosofon synevallon auto, kai tines elegon* Ti an theloi o spermologos outos legein; oi de* Xenon daimonion dokei kataggeleus einai* oti ton Iisoun kai ten anastasin euiggelizeto.
verses.translation: Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection.

verses.original: ἐπιλαβόμενοί ⸀τε αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν Ἄρειον Πάγον ἤγαγον, λέγοντες· Δυνάμεθα γνῶναι τίς ἡ καινὴ αὕτη ἡ ὑπὸ σοῦ λαλουμένη διδαχή;
