verses.translit: epilavomenoi te autou epi ton Areion Pagon egagon, legontes* Dynametha gnonai tis e kaine auti e upo sou laloymeni didahi;
verses.translation: And they took him, and brought him unto Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof thou speakest, is ?

verses.original: ξενίζοντα γάρ τινα εἰσφέρεις εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς ἡμῶν· βουλόμεθα οὖν γνῶναι ⸂τίνα θέλει⸃ ταῦτα εἶναι.
verses.translit: xenizonta gar tina eisfereis eis tas akoas emon* voylometha oun gnonai tina thelei tauta einai.
verses.translation: For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears: we would know therefore what these things mean.

verses.original: Ἀθηναῖοι δὲ πάντες καὶ οἱ ἐπιδημοῦντες ξένοι εἰς οὐδὲν ἕτερον ηὐκαίρουν ἢ λέγειν τι ⸀ἢ ἀκούειν ⸀τι καινότερον.
verses.translit: Athinaioi de pantes kai oi epidimountes xenoi eis ouden eteron iukairoyn e legein ti e akoyein ti kainoteron.
verses.translation: (For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.)

verses.original: Σταθεὶς ⸀δὲ Παῦλος ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ Ἀρείου Πάγου ἔφη· Ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, κατὰ πάντα ὡς δεισιδαιμονεστέρους ὑμᾶς θεωρῶ·
verses.translit: Statheis de Paulos en meso tou Areioy Pagoy efi* Andres Athinaioi, kata panta os deisidaimonesteroys umas theoro*
verses.translation: Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars’ hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious.

verses.original: διερχόμενος γὰρ καὶ ἀναθεωρῶν τὰ σεβάσματα ὑμῶν εὗρον καὶ βωμὸν ἐν ᾧ ἐπεγέγραπτο· Ἀγνώστῳ θεῷ. ⸀ὃ οὖν ἀγνοοῦντες εὐσεβεῖτε, ⸀τοῦτο ἐγὼ καταγγέλλω ὑμῖν.
verses.translit: dierhomenos gar kai anatheoron ta sevasmata umon euron kai vomon en o epegegrapto* Agnosto theo. o oun agnoountes euseveite, touto ego kataggello umin.
verses.translation: For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you.

verses.original: ὁ θεὸς ὁ ποιήσας τὸν κόσμον καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ, οὗτος οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς ⸂ὑπάρχων κύριος⸃ οὐκ ἐν χειροποιήτοις ναοῖς κατοικεῖ
verses.translit: o theos o poiisas ton kosmon kai panta ta en auto, outos ouranou kai ges uparhon kyrios ouk en heiropoiitois naois katoikei
verses.translation: God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands;

verses.original: οὐδὲ ὑπὸ χειρῶν ⸀ἀνθρωπίνων θεραπεύεται προσδεόμενός τινος, αὐτὸς διδοὺς πᾶσι ζωὴν καὶ πνοὴν ⸂καὶ τὰ⸃ πάντα·
verses.translit: oude upo heiron anthropinon therapeyetai prosdeomenos tinos, autos didous pasi zoen kai pnoen kai ta panta*
verses.translation: Neither is worshipped with men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things;

verses.original: ἐποίησέν τε ἐξ ⸀ἑνὸς πᾶν ἔθνος ἀνθρώπων κατοικεῖν ἐπὶ ⸂παντὸς προσώπου⸃ τῆς γῆς, ὁρίσας προστεταγμένους καιροὺς καὶ τὰς ὁροθεσίας τῆς κατοικίας αὐτῶν,
verses.translit: epoiisen te ex enos pan ethnos anthropon katoikein epi pantos prosopoy tes ges, orisas prostetagmenoys kairous kai tas orothesias tes katoikias auton,
verses.translation: And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;

verses.original: ζητεῖν τὸν ⸀θεὸν εἰ ἄρα γε ψηλαφήσειαν αὐτὸν καὶ εὕροιεν, καί γε οὐ μακρὰν ἀπὸ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου ἡμῶν ὑπάρχοντα.
verses.translit: zitein ton theon ei ara ge psilafiseian auton kai euroien, kai ge ou makran apo enos ekastoy emon uparhonta.
verses.translation: That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us:

verses.original: ἐν αὐτῷ γὰρ ζῶμεν καὶ κινούμεθα καὶ ἐσμέν, ὡς καί τινες τῶν καθʼ ὑμᾶς ποιητῶν εἰρήκασιν· Τοῦ γὰρ καὶ γένος ἐσμέν.
verses.translit: en auto gar zomen kai kinoymetha kai esmen, os kai tines ton kath' umas poiiton eirikasin* Tou gar kai genos esmen.
verses.translation: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.

verses.original: γένος οὖν ὑπάρχοντες τοῦ θεοῦ οὐκ ὀφείλομεν νομίζειν χρυσῷ ἢ ἀργύρῳ ἢ λίθῳ, χαράγματι τέχνης καὶ ἐνθυμήσεως ἀνθρώπου, τὸ θεῖον εἶναι ὅμοιον.
verses.translit: genos oun uparhontes tou theou ouk ofeilomen nomizein hryso e argyro e litho, haragmati tehnis kai enthymiseos anthropoy, to theion einai omoion.
verses.translation: Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man’s device.

verses.original: τοὺς μὲν οὖν χρόνους τῆς ἀγνοίας ὑπεριδὼν ὁ θεὸς τὰ νῦν ⸀παραγγέλλει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ⸀πάντας πανταχοῦ μετανοεῖν,
verses.translit: tous men oun hronoys tes agnoias uperidon o theos ta nun paraggellei tois anthropois pantas pantahou metanoein,
verses.translation: And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:

verses.original: ⸀καθότι ἔστησεν ἡμέραν ἐν ᾗ μέλλει κρίνειν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ ἐν ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ὥρισεν, πίστιν παρασχὼν πᾶσιν ἀναστήσας αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν.
verses.translit: kathoti estisen emeran en e mellei krinein ten oikoymenin en dikaiosyne en andri o orisen, pistin parashon pasin anastisas auton ek nekron.
verses.translation: Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men , in that he hath raised him from the dead.

verses.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ ἀνάστασιν νεκρῶν οἱ μὲν ἐχλεύαζον οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Ἀκουσόμεθά σου ⸂περὶ τούτου καὶ πάλιν⸃.
verses.translit: Akoysantes de anastasin nekron oi men ehleyazon oi de eipan Akoysometha soy peri toytoy kai palin.
verses.translation: And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, We will hear thee again of this matter .

verses.original: ⸀οὕτως ὁ Παῦλος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν·
verses.translit: outos o Paulos exelthen ek mesoy auton*
verses.translation: So Paul departed from among them.

verses.original: τινὲς δὲ ἄνδρες κολληθέντες αὐτῷ ἐπίστευσαν, ἐν οἷς καὶ Διονύσιος ὁ Ἀρεοπαγίτης καὶ γυνὴ ὀνόματι Δάμαρις καὶ ἕτεροι σὺν αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: tines de andres kollithentes auto episteysan, en ois kai Dionysios o Areopagitis kai gyne onomati Damaris kai eteroi sun autois.
verses.translation: Howbeit certain men clave unto him, and believed: among the which was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.

verses.original: ⸀Μετὰ ταῦτα ⸀χωρισθεὶς ἐκ τῶν Ἀθηνῶν ἦλθεν εἰς Κόρινθον.
verses.translit: Meta tauta horistheis ek ton Athinon elthen eis Korinthon.
verses.translation: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;

verses.original: καὶ εὑρών τινα Ἰουδαῖον ὀνόματι Ἀκύλαν, Ποντικὸν τῷ γένει, προσφάτως ἐληλυθότα ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰταλίας καὶ Πρίσκιλλαν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ διὰ τὸ ⸀διατεταχέναι Κλαύδιον χωρίζεσθαι πάντας τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ⸀ἀπὸ τῆς Ῥώμης, προσῆλθεν αὐτοῖς,
verses.translit: kai euron tina Ioydaion onomati Akylan, Pontikon to genei, prosfatos elilythota apo tes Italias kai Priskillan gynaika autou dia to diatetahenai Klaydion horizesthai pantas tous Ioydaioys apo tes Romis, proselthen autois,
verses.translation: And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:) and came unto them.

verses.original: καὶ διὰ τὸ ὁμότεχνον εἶναι ἔμενεν παρʼ αὐτοῖς καὶ ⸀ἠργάζετο, ἦσαν γὰρ σκηνοποιοὶ ⸂τῇ τέχνῃ⸃.
verses.translit: kai dia to omotehnon einai emenen par' autois kai ergazeto, esan gar skinopoioi te tehne.
verses.translation: And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.

verses.original: διελέγετο δὲ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον, ἔπειθέν τε Ἰουδαίους καὶ Ἕλληνας.
verses.translit: dielegeto de en te synagoge kata pan savvaton, epeithen te Ioydaioys kai Ellinas.
verses.translation: And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ κατῆλθον ἀπὸ τῆς Μακεδονίας ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος, συνείχετο τῷ ⸀λόγῳ ὁ Παῦλος, διαμαρτυρόμενος τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ⸀εἶναι τὸν χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: Os de katelthon apo tes Makedonias o te Silas kai o Timotheos, syneiheto to logo o Paulos, diamartyromenos tois Ioydaiois einai ton hriston Iisoun.
verses.translation: And when Silas and Timotheus were come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the spirit, and testified to the Jews that Jesus was Christ.

verses.original: ἀντιτασσομένων δὲ αὐτῶν καὶ βλασφημούντων ἐκτιναξάμενος τὰ ἱμάτια εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τὸ αἷμα ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν ὑμῶν· καθαρὸς ἐγώ· ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν εἰς τὰ ἔθνη πορεύσομαι.
verses.translit: antitassomenon de auton kai vlasfimoynton ektinaxamenos ta imatia eipen pros autoys* To aima umon epi ten kefalen umon* katharos ego* apo tou nun eis ta ethni poreysomai.
verses.translation: And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles.

verses.original: καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ⸀εἰσῆλθεν εἰς οἰκίαν τινὸς ὀνόματι ⸀Τιτίου Ἰούστου σεβομένου τὸν θεόν, οὗ ἡ οἰκία ἦν συνομοροῦσα τῇ συναγωγῇ.
verses.translit: kai metavas ekeithen eiselthen eis oikian tinos onomati Titioy Ioystoy sevomenoy ton theon, ou e oikia en synomorousa te synagoge.
verses.translation: And he departed thence, and entered into a certain man’s house, named Justus, one that worshipped God, whose house joined hard to the synagogue.

verses.original: Κρίσπος δὲ ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος ἐπίστευσεν τῷ κυρίῳ σὺν ὅλῳ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ, καὶ πολλοὶ τῶν Κορινθίων ἀκούοντες ἐπίστευον καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο.
verses.translit: Krispos de o arhisynagogos episteysen to kyrio sun olo to oiko autou, kai polloi ton Korinthion akoyontes episteyon kai evaptizonto.
verses.translation: And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος ⸂ἐν νυκτὶ διʼ ὁράματος⸃ τῷ Παύλῳ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, ἀλλὰ λάλει καὶ μὴ σιωπήσῃς,
verses.translit: eipen de o kyrios en nykti di' oramatos to Paylo* Me fovou, alla lalei kai me siopises,
verses.translation: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace:

verses.original: διότι ἐγώ εἰμι μετὰ σοῦ καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπιθήσεταί σοι τοῦ κακῶσαί σε, διότι λαός ἐστί μοι πολὺς ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ.
verses.translit: dioti ego eimi meta sou kai oudeis epithisetai soi tou kakosai se, dioti laos esti moi polus en te polei tayte.
verses.translation: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city.

verses.original: ἐκάθισεν ⸀δὲ ἐνιαυτὸν καὶ μῆνας ἓξ διδάσκων ἐν αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: ekathisen de eniayton kai menas ex didaskon en autois ton logon tou theou.
verses.translation: And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.

verses.original: Γαλλίωνος δὲ ⸂ἀνθυπάτου ὄντος⸃ τῆς Ἀχαΐας κατεπέστησαν ⸂ὁμοθυμαδὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι⸃ τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα,
verses.translit: Gallionos de anthypatoy ontos tes AhaIas katepestisan omothymadon oi Ioydaioi to Paylo kai egagon auton epi to vema,
verses.translation: And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment seat,

verses.original: λέγοντες ὅτι Παρὰ τὸν νόμον ⸂ἀναπείθει οὗτος⸃ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους σέβεσθαι τὸν θεόν.
verses.translit: legontes oti Para ton nomon anapeithei outos tous anthropoys sevesthai ton theon.
verses.translation: Saying, This fellow persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law.

verses.original: μέλλοντος δὲ τοῦ Παύλου ἀνοίγειν τὸ στόμα εἶπεν ὁ Γαλλίων πρὸς τοὺς Ἰουδαίους· Εἰ ⸀μὲν ἦν ἀδίκημά τι ἢ ῥᾳδιούργημα πονηρόν, ὦ Ἰουδαῖοι, κατὰ λόγον ἂν ἀνεσχόμην ὑμῶν·
verses.translit: mellontos de tou Payloy anoigein to stoma eipen o Gallion pros tous Ioydaioys* Ei men en adikima ti e Radioyrgima poniron, o Ioydaioi, kata logon an aneshomin umon*
verses.translation: And when Paul was now about to open his mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, O ye Jews, reason would that I should bear with you:

verses.original: εἰ δὲ ⸀ζητήματά ἐστιν περὶ λόγου καὶ ὀνομάτων καὶ νόμου τοῦ καθʼ ὑμᾶς, ὄψεσθε αὐτοί· ⸀κριτὴς ἐγὼ τούτων οὐ βούλομαι εἶναι.
verses.translit: ei de zitimata estin peri logoy kai onomaton kai nomoy tou kath' umas, opsesthe autoi* krites ego toyton ou voylomai einai.
verses.translation: But if it be a question of words and names, and of your law, look ye to it ; for I will be no judge of such matters .

verses.original: καὶ ἀπήλασεν αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ βήματος.
verses.translit: kai apilasen autous apo tou vimatos.
verses.translation: And he drave them from the judgment seat.

verses.original: ἐπιλαβόμενοι δὲ ⸀πάντες Σωσθένην τὸν ἀρχισυνάγωγον ἔτυπτον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ βήματος· καὶ οὐδὲν τούτων τῷ Γαλλίωνι ⸀ἔμελεν.
verses.translit: epilavomenoi de pantes Sosthenin ton arhisynagogon etypton emprosthen tou vimatos* kai ouden toyton to Gallioni emelen.
verses.translation: Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔτι προσμείνας ἡμέρας ἱκανὰς τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ἀποταξάμενος ἐξέπλει εἰς τὴν Συρίαν, καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ Πρίσκιλλα καὶ Ἀκύλας, κειράμενος ⸂ἐν Κεγχρεαῖς τὴν κεφαλήν⸃, εἶχεν γὰρ εὐχήν.
verses.translit: O de Paulos eti prosmeinas emeras ikanas tois adelfois apotaxamenos exeplei eis ten Syrian, kai sun auto Priskilla kai Akylas, keiramenos en Keghreais ten kefalin, eihen gar euhin.
verses.translation: And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.

verses.original: ⸀κατήντησαν δὲ εἰς Ἔφεσον, κἀκείνους κατέλιπεν αὐτοῦ, αὐτὸς δὲ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν ⸀διελέξατο τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις.
verses.translit: katintisan de eis Efeson, kakeinoys katelipen autou, autos de eiselthon eis ten synagogen dielexato tois Ioydaiois.
verses.translation: And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.

verses.original: ἐρωτώντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐπὶ πλείονα χρόνον ⸀μεῖναι οὐκ ἐπένευσεν,
verses.translit: erotonton de auton epi pleiona hronon meinai ouk epeneysen,
verses.translation: When they desired him to tarry longer time with them, he consented not;

verses.original: ⸂ἀλλὰ ἀποταξάμενος καὶ⸃ ⸀εἰπών· ⸀Πάλιν ἀνακάμψω πρὸς ὑμᾶς τοῦ θεοῦ θέλοντος ἀνήχθη ἀπὸ τῆς Ἐφέσου,
verses.translit: alla apotaxamenos kai eipon* Palin anakampso pros umas tou theou thelontos anihthi apo tes Efesoy,
verses.translation: But bade them farewell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem: but I will return again unto you, if God will. And he sailed from Ephesus.

verses.original: καὶ κατελθὼν εἰς Καισάρειαν, ἀναβὰς καὶ ἀσπασάμενος τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, κατέβη εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν,
verses.translit: kai katelthon eis Kaisareian, anavas kai aspasamenos ten ekklisian, katevi eis Antioheian,
verses.translation: And when he had landed at Cæsarea, and gone up, and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch.

verses.original: καὶ ποιήσας χρόνον τινὰ ἐξῆλθεν, διερχόμενος καθεξῆς τὴν Γαλατικὴν χώραν καὶ Φρυγίαν, ⸀στηρίζων πάντας τοὺς μαθητάς.
verses.translit: kai poiisas hronon tina exelthen, dierhomenos kathexes ten Galatiken horan kai Frygian, stirizon pantas tous mathitas.
verses.translation: And after he had spent some time there , he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.

verses.original: Ἰουδαῖος δέ τις Ἀπολλῶς ὀνόματι, Ἀλεξανδρεὺς τῷ γένει, ἀνὴρ λόγιος, κατήντησεν εἰς Ἔφεσον, δυνατὸς ὢν ἐν ταῖς γραφαῖς.
verses.translit: Ioydaios de tis Apollos onomati, Alexandreus to genei, aner logios, katintisen eis Efeson, dynatos on en tais grafais.
verses.translation: And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.

verses.original: οὗτος ἦν κατηχημένος τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ κυρίου, καὶ ζέων τῷ πνεύματι ἐλάλει καὶ ἐδίδασκεν ἀκριβῶς τὰ περὶ τοῦ ⸀Ἰησοῦ, ἐπιστάμενος μόνον τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου.
verses.translit: outos en katihimenos ten odon tou kyrioy, kai zeon to pneymati elalei kai edidasken akrivos ta peri tou Iisou, epistamenos monon to vaptisma Ioannoy.
verses.translation: This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.

verses.original: οὗτός τε ἤρξατο παρρησιάζεσθαι ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ· ἀκούσαντες δὲ αὐτοῦ ⸂Πρίσκιλλα καὶ Ἀκύλας⸃ προσελάβοντο αὐτὸν καὶ ἀκριβέστερον αὐτῷ ἐξέθεντο τὴν ⸂ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ⸃.
verses.translit: outos te erxato parrisiazesthai en te synagoge* akoysantes de autou Priskilla kai Akylas proselavonto auton kai akrivesteron auto exethento ten odon tou theou.
verses.translation: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them , and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.

verses.original: βουλομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ διελθεῖν εἰς τὴν Ἀχαΐαν προτρεψάμενοι οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ἔγραψαν τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἀποδέξασθαι αὐτόν· ὃς παραγενόμενος συνεβάλετο πολὺ τοῖς πεπιστευκόσιν διὰ τῆς χάριτος·
verses.translit: voylomenoy de autou dielthein eis ten AhaIan protrepsamenoi oi adelfoi egrapsan tois mathitais apodexasthai auton* os paragenomenos synevaleto polu tois pepisteykosin dia tes haritos*
verses.translation: And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace:

verses.original: εὐτόνως γὰρ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις διακατηλέγχετο δημοσίᾳ ἐπιδεικνὺς διὰ τῶν γραφῶν εἶναι τὸν χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: eutonos gar tois Ioydaiois diakatilegheto dimosia epideiknus dia ton grafon einai ton hriston Iisoun.
verses.translation: For he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publickly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν Ἀπολλῶ εἶναι ἐν Κορίνθῳ Παῦλον διελθόντα τὰ ἀνωτερικὰ μέρη ⸀ἐλθεῖν εἰς Ἔφεσον καὶ ⸀εὑρεῖν τινας μαθητάς,
verses.translit: Egeneto de en to ton Apollo einai en Korintho Paulon dielthonta ta anoterika meri elthein eis Efeson kai eurein tinas mathitas,
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples,

verses.original: εἶπέν ⸀τε πρὸς αὐτούς· Εἰ πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐλάβετε πιστεύσαντες; οἱ ⸀δὲ πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἀλλʼ οὐδʼ εἰ πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἔστιν ἠκούσαμεν.
verses.translit: eipen te pros autoys* Ei pneuma agion elavete pisteysantes; oi de pros auton* All' oud' ei pneuma agion estin ekoysamen.
verses.translation: He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.

verses.original: εἶπέν ⸀τε· Εἰς τί οὖν ἐβαπτίσθητε; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Εἰς τὸ Ἰωάννου βάπτισμα.
verses.translit: eipen te* Eis ti oun evaptisthite; oi de eipan* Eis to Ioannoy vaptisma.
verses.translation: And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John’s baptism.

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ Παῦλος· ⸀Ἰωάννης ἐβάπτισεν βάπτισμα μετανοίας, τῷ λαῷ λέγων εἰς τὸν ἐρχόμενον μετʼ αὐτὸν ἵνα πιστεύσωσιν, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν εἰς ⸀τὸν Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: eipen de Paulos* Ioannis evaptisen vaptisma metanoias, to lao legon eis ton erhomenon met' auton ina pisteysosin, tout' estin eis ton Iisoun.
verses.translation: Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.

verses.original: ἀκούσαντες δὲ ἐβαπτίσθησαν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ·
verses.translit: akoysantes de evaptisthisan eis to onoma tou kyrioy Iisou*
verses.translation: When they heard this , they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπιθέντος αὐτοῖς τοῦ ⸀Παύλου χεῖρας ἦλθε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἐπʼ αὐτούς, ἐλάλουν τε γλώσσαις καὶ ἐπροφήτευον.
verses.translit: kai epithentos autois tou Payloy heiras elthe to pneuma to agion ep' autoys, elaloyn te glossais kai eprofiteyon.
verses.translation: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.

verses.original: ἦσαν δὲ οἱ πάντες ἄνδρες ὡσεὶ ⸀δώδεκα.
verses.translit: esan de oi pantes andres osei dodeka.
verses.translation: And all the men were about twelve.

verses.original: Εἰσελθὼν δὲ εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν ἐπαρρησιάζετο ἐπὶ μῆνας τρεῖς διαλεγόμενος καὶ ⸀πείθων περὶ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: Eiselthon de eis ten synagogen eparrisiazeto epi menas treis dialegomenos kai peithon peri tes vasileias tou theou.
verses.translation: And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.

verses.original: ὡς δέ τινες ἐσκληρύνοντο καὶ ἠπείθουν κακολογοῦντες τὴν ὁδὸν ἐνώπιον τοῦ πλήθους, ἀποστὰς ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ἀφώρισεν τοὺς μαθητάς, καθʼ ἡμέραν διαλεγόμενος ἐν τῇ σχολῇ ⸀Τυράννου.
verses.translit: os de tines esklirynonto kai epeithoyn kakologountes ten odon enopion tou plithoys, apostas ap' auton aforisen tous mathitas, kath' emeran dialegomenos en te shole Tyrannoy.
verses.translation: But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.

verses.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ ἔτη δύο, ὥστε πάντας τοὺς κατοικοῦντας τὴν Ἀσίαν ἀκοῦσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ ⸀κυρίου, Ἰουδαίους τε καὶ Ἕλληνας.
verses.translit: touto de egeneto epi eti dyo, oste pantas tous katoikountas ten Asian akousai ton logon tou kyrioy, Ioydaioys te kai Ellinas.
verses.translation: And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.

verses.original: Δυνάμεις τε οὐ τὰς τυχούσας ⸂ὁ θεὸς ἐποίει⸃ διὰ τῶν χειρῶν Παύλου,
verses.translit: Dynameis te ou tas tyhoysas o theos epoiei dia ton heiron Payloy,
verses.translation: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:

verses.original: ὥστε καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας ⸀ἀποφέρεσθαι ἀπὸ τοῦ χρωτὸς αὐτοῦ σουδάρια ἢ σιμικίνθια καὶ ἀπαλλάσσεσθαι ἀπʼ αὐτῶν τὰς νόσους, τά τε πνεύματα τὰ πονηρὰ ⸀ἐκπορεύεσθαι.
verses.translit: oste kai epi tous asthenountas apoferesthai apo tou hrotos autou soydaria e simikinthia kai apallassesthai ap' auton tas nosoys, ta te pneymata ta ponira ekporeyesthai.
verses.translation: So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.

verses.original: ἐπεχείρησαν δέ τινες ⸀καὶ τῶν περιερχομένων Ἰουδαίων ἐξορκιστῶν ὀνομάζειν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἔχοντας τὰ πνεύματα τὰ πονηρὰ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ λέγοντες· ⸀Ὁρκίζω ὑμᾶς τὸν Ἰησοῦν ⸀ὃν Παῦλος κηρύσσει.
verses.translit: epeheirisan de tines kai ton perierhomenon Ioydaion exorkiston onomazein epi tous ehontas ta pneymata ta ponira to onoma tou kyrioy Iisou legontes* Orkizo umas ton Iisoun on Paulos kiryssei.
verses.translation: Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.

verses.original: ἦσαν δέ ⸀τινος Σκευᾶ Ἰουδαίου ἀρχιερέως ἑπτὰ ⸀υἱοὶ τοῦτο ποιοῦντες.
verses.translit: esan de tinos Skeya Ioydaioy arhiereos epta yioi touto poiountes.
verses.translation: And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, and chief of the priests, which did so.

verses.original: ἀποκριθὲν δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ πονηρὸν εἶπεν ⸀αὐτοῖς· ⸀Τὸν Ἰησοῦν γινώσκω καὶ τὸν Παῦλον ἐπίσταμαι, ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνες ἐστέ;
verses.translit: apokrithen de to pneuma to poniron eipen autois* Ton Iisoun ginosko kai ton Paulon epistamai, umeis de tines este;
verses.translation: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?

verses.original: καὶ ⸀ἐφαλόμενος ⸂ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς⸃ ἐν ᾧ ἦν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ πονηρὸν ⸂κατακυριεύσας ἀμφοτέρων⸃ ἴσχυσεν κατʼ αὐτῶν, ὥστε γυμνοὺς καὶ τετραυματισμένους ἐκφυγεῖν ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου ἐκείνου.
verses.translit: kai efalomenos o anthropos ep' autous en o en to pneuma to poniron katakyrieysas amfoteron ishysen kat' auton, oste gymnous kai tetraymatismenoys ekfygein ek tou oikoy ekeinoy.
verses.translation: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.

verses.original: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο γνωστὸν πᾶσιν Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Ἕλλησιν τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν τὴν Ἔφεσον, καὶ ⸀ἐπέπεσεν φόβος ἐπὶ πάντας αὐτούς, καὶ ἐμεγαλύνετο τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: touto de egeneto gnoston pasin Ioydaiois te kai Ellisin tois katoikousin ten Efeson, kai epepesen fovos epi pantas autoys, kai emegalyneto to onoma tou kyrioy Iisou.
verses.translation: And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus; and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.

verses.original: πολλοί τε τῶν πεπιστευκότων ἤρχοντο ἐξομολογούμενοι καὶ ἀναγγέλλοντες τὰς πράξεις αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: polloi te ton pepisteykoton erhonto exomologoymenoi kai anaggellontes tas praxeis auton.
verses.translation: And many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds.

verses.original: ἱκανοὶ δὲ τῶν τὰ περίεργα πραξάντων συνενέγκαντες τὰς βίβλους κατέκαιον ἐνώπιον πάντων· καὶ συνεψήφισαν τὰς τιμὰς αὐτῶν καὶ εὗρον ἀργυρίου μυριάδας πέντε.
verses.translit: ikanoi de ton ta perierga praxanton synenegkantes tas vivloys katekaion enopion panton* kai synepsifisan tas timas auton kai euron argyrioy myriadas pente.
verses.translation: Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men : and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.

verses.original: οὕτως κατὰ κράτος ⸂τοῦ κυρίου ὁ λόγος⸃ ηὔξανεν καὶ ἴσχυεν.
verses.translit: outos kata kratos tou kyrioy o logos iuxanen kai ishyen.
verses.translation: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληρώθη ταῦτα, ἔθετο ὁ Παῦλος ἐν τῷ πνεύματι διελθὼν τὴν Μακεδονίαν καὶ Ἀχαΐαν πορεύεσθαι εἰς ⸀Ἱεροσόλυμα, εἰπὼν ὅτι Μετὰ τὸ γενέσθαι με ἐκεῖ δεῖ με καὶ Ῥώμην ἰδεῖν.
verses.translit: Os de eplirothi tauta, etheto o Paulos en to pneymati dielthon ten Makedonian kai AhaIan poreyesthai eis Ierosolyma, eipon oti Meta to genesthai me ekei dei me kai Romin idein.
verses.translation: After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.

verses.original: ἀποστείλας δὲ εἰς τὴν Μακεδονίαν δύο τῶν διακονούντων αὐτῷ, Τιμόθεον καὶ Ἔραστον, αὐτὸς ἐπέσχεν χρόνον εἰς τὴν Ἀσίαν.
verses.translit: aposteilas de eis ten Makedonian dyo ton diakonoynton auto, Timotheon kai Eraston, autos epeshen hronon eis ten Asian.
verses.translation: So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν ἐκεῖνον τάραχος οὐκ ὀλίγος περὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ.
verses.translit: Egeneto de kata ton kairon ekeinon tarahos ouk oligos peri tes odou.
verses.translation: And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.

verses.original: Δημήτριος γάρ τις ὀνόματι, ἀργυροκόπος, ποιῶν ναοὺς ἀργυροῦς Ἀρτέμιδος παρείχετο τοῖς τεχνίταις ⸂οὐκ ὀλίγην ἐργασίαν⸃,
verses.translit: Dimitrios gar tis onomati, argyrokopos, poion naous argyrous Artemidos pareiheto tois tehnitais ouk oligin ergasian,
verses.translation: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;

verses.original: οὓς συναθροίσας καὶ τοὺς περὶ τὰ τοιαῦτα ἐργάτας εἶπεν· Ἄνδρες, ἐπίστασθε ὅτι ἐκ ταύτης τῆς ἐργασίας ἡ εὐπορία ⸀ἡμῖν ἐστιν,
verses.translit: ous synathroisas kai tous peri ta toiauta ergatas eipen* Andres, epistasthe oti ek taytis tes ergasias e euporia emin estin,
verses.translation: Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth.

verses.original: καὶ θεωρεῖτε καὶ ἀκούετε ὅτι οὐ μόνον Ἐφέσου ἀλλὰ σχεδὸν πάσης τῆς Ἀσίας ὁ Παῦλος οὗτος πείσας μετέστησεν ἱκανὸν ὄχλον, λέγων ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶν θεοὶ οἱ διὰ χειρῶν γινόμενοι.
verses.translit: kai theoreite kai akoyete oti ou monon Efesoy alla shedon pasis tes Asias o Paulos outos peisas metestisen ikanon ohlon, legon oti ouk eisin theoi oi dia heiron ginomenoi.
verses.translation: Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:

verses.original: οὐ μόνον δὲ τοῦτο κινδυνεύει ἡμῖν τὸ μέρος εἰς ἀπελεγμὸν ἐλθεῖν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ τῆς μεγάλης θεᾶς ⸂Ἀρτέμιδος ἱερὸν⸃ εἰς οὐθὲν λογισθῆναι, μέλλειν ⸀τε καὶ καθαιρεῖσθαι ⸂τῆς μεγαλειότητος⸃ αὐτῆς, ἣν ὅλη ἡ Ἀσία καὶ ἡ οἰκουμένη σέβεται.
verses.translit: ou monon de touto kindyneyei emin to meros eis apelegmon elthein, alla kai to tes megalis theas Artemidos ieron eis outhen logisthenai, mellein te kai kathaireisthai tes megaleiotitos autes, en oli e Asia kai e oikoymeni sevetai.
verses.translation: So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.

verses.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ καὶ γενόμενοι πλήρεις θυμοῦ ἔκραζον λέγοντες· Μεγάλη ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων.
verses.translit: Akoysantes de kai genomenoi plireis thymou ekrazon legontes* Megali e Artemis Efesion.
verses.translation: And when they heard these sayings , they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπλήσθη ἡ ⸀πόλις τῆς συγχύσεως, ὥρμησάν τε ὁμοθυμαδὸν εἰς τὸ θέατρον συναρπάσαντες Γάϊον καὶ Ἀρίσταρχον Μακεδόνας, συνεκδήμους Παύλου.
verses.translit: kai eplisthi e polis tes syghyseos, ormisan te omothymadon eis to theatron synarpasantes Gaion kai Aristarhon Makedonas, synekdimoys Payloy.
verses.translation: And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.

verses.original: ⸂Παύλου δὲ⸃ βουλομένου εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν δῆμον οὐκ εἴων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταί·
verses.translit: Payloy de voylomenoy eiselthein eis ton demon ouk eion auton oi mathitai*
verses.translation: And when Paul would have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.

verses.original: τινὲς δὲ καὶ τῶν Ἀσιαρχῶν, ὄντες αὐτῷ φίλοι, πέμψαντες πρὸς αὐτὸν παρεκάλουν μὴ δοῦναι ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὸ θέατρον.
verses.translit: tines de kai ton Asiarhon, ontes auto filoi, pempsantes pros auton parekaloyn me dounai eayton eis to theatron.
verses.translation: And certain of the chief of Asia, which were his friends, sent unto him, desiring him that he would not adventure himself into the theatre.

verses.original: ἄλλοι μὲν οὖν ἄλλο τι ἔκραζον, ἦν γὰρ ἡ ἐκκλησία συγκεχυμένη, καὶ οἱ πλείους οὐκ ᾔδεισαν τίνος ἕνεκα συνεληλύθεισαν.
verses.translit: alloi men oun allo ti ekrazon, en gar e ekklisia sygkehymeni, kai oi pleioys ouk edeisan tinos eneka synelilytheisan.
verses.translation: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.

verses.original: ἐκ δὲ τοῦ ὄχλου ⸀συνεβίβασαν Ἀλέξανδρον προβαλόντων αὐτὸν τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὁ δὲ Ἀλέξανδρος κατασείσας τὴν χεῖρα ἤθελεν ἀπολογεῖσθαι τῷ δήμῳ.
verses.translit: ek de tou ohloy synevivasan Alexandron provalonton auton ton Ioydaion, o de Alexandros kataseisas ten heira ethelen apologeisthai to dimo.
verses.translation: And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people.

verses.original: ἐπιγνόντες δὲ ὅτι Ἰουδαῖός ἐστιν φωνὴ ἐγένετο μία ἐκ πάντων ⸀ὡς ἐπὶ ὥρας δύο κραζόντων· Μεγάλη ἡ Ἄρτεμις Ἐφεσίων.
verses.translit: epignontes de oti Ioydaios estin fone egeneto mia ek panton os epi oras dyo krazonton* Megali e Artemis Efesion.
verses.translation: But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.

verses.original: καταστείλας δὲ ⸂ὁ γραμματεὺς τὸν ὄχλον⸃ φησίν· Ἄνδρες Ἐφέσιοι, τίς γάρ ἐστιν ⸀ἀνθρώπων ὃς οὐ γινώσκει τὴν Ἐφεσίων πόλιν νεωκόρον οὖσαν τῆς ⸀μεγάλης Ἀρτέμιδος καὶ τοῦ διοπετοῦς;
verses.translit: katasteilas de o grammateus ton ohlon fisin* Andres Efesioi, tis gar estin anthropon os ou ginoskei ten Efesion polin neokoron ousan tes megalis Artemidos kai tou diopetous;
verses.translation: And when the townclerk had appeased the people, he said, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there that knoweth not how that the city of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana, and of the image which fell down from Jupiter?

verses.original: ἀναντιρρήτων οὖν ὄντων τούτων δέον ἐστὶν ὑμᾶς κατεσταλμένους ὑπάρχειν καὶ μηδὲν προπετὲς πράσσειν.
verses.translit: anantirriton oun onton toyton deon estin umas katestalmenoys uparhein kai miden propetes prassein.
verses.translation: Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.

verses.original: ἠγάγετε γὰρ τοὺς ἄνδρας τούτους οὔτε ἱεροσύλους οὔτε βλασφημοῦντας τὴν θεὸν ⸀ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: egagete gar tous andras toytoys oute ierosyloys oute vlasfimountas ten theon emon.
verses.translation: For ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.

verses.original: εἰ μὲν οὖν Δημήτριος καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ τεχνῖται ἔχουσιν πρός τινα λόγον, ἀγοραῖοι ἄγονται καὶ ἀνθύπατοί εἰσιν, ἐγκαλείτωσαν ἀλλήλοις.
verses.translit: ei men oun Dimitrios kai oi sun auto tehnitai ehoysin pros tina logon, agoraioi agontai kai anthypatoi eisin, egkaleitosan allilois.
verses.translation: Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.

verses.original: εἰ δέ τι ⸀περαιτέρω ἐπιζητεῖτε, ἐν τῇ ἐννόμῳ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐπιλυθήσεται.
verses.translit: ei de ti peraitero epiziteite, en te ennomo ekklisia epilythisetai.
verses.translation: But if ye enquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly.

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ κινδυνεύομεν ἐγκαλεῖσθαι στάσεως περὶ τῆς σήμερον μηδενὸς αἰτίου ὑπάρχοντος περὶ οὗ οὐ δυνησόμεθα ⸀ἀποδοῦναι λόγον ⸀περὶ τῆς συστροφῆς ταύτης. καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν ἀπέλυσεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν.
verses.translit: kai gar kindyneyomen egkaleisthai staseos peri tes simeron midenos aitioy uparhontos peri ou ou dynisometha apodounai logon peri tes systrofes taytis. kai tauta eipon apelysen ten ekklisian.
verses.translation: For we are in danger to be called in question for this day’s uproar, there being no cause whereby we may give an account of this concourse.
And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.

verses.original: Μετὰ δὲ τὸ παύσασθαι τὸν θόρυβον ⸀μεταπεμψάμενος ὁ Παῦλος τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ ⸀παρακαλέσας, ἀσπασάμενος ἐξῆλθεν ⸀πορεύεσθαι ⸀εἰς Μακεδονίαν.
verses.translit: Meta de to paysasthai ton thoryvon metapempsamenos o Paulos tous mathitas kai parakalesas, aspasamenos exelthen poreyesthai eis Makedonian.
verses.translation: And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them , and departed for to go into Macedonia.

verses.original: διελθὼν δὲ τὰ μέρη ἐκεῖνα καὶ παρακαλέσας αὐτοὺς λόγῳ πολλῷ ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν Ἑλλάδα
verses.translit: dielthon de ta meri ekeina kai parakalesas autous logo pollo elthen eis ten Ellada
verses.translation: And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,

verses.original: ποιήσας τε μῆνας τρεῖς· γενομένης ⸂ἐπιβουλῆς αὐτῷ⸃ ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων μέλλοντι ἀνάγεσθαι εἰς τὴν Συρίαν ἐγένετο ⸀γνώμης τοῦ ὑποστρέφειν διὰ Μακεδονίας.
verses.translit: poiisas te menas treis* genomenis epivoyles auto upo ton Ioydaion mellonti anagesthai eis ten Syrian egeneto gnomis tou upostrefein dia Makedonias.
verses.translation: And there abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.

verses.original: συνείπετο δὲ ⸀αὐτῷ Σώπατρος ⸀Πύρρου Βεροιαῖος, Θεσσαλονικέων δὲ Ἀρίσταρχος καὶ Σεκοῦνδος, καὶ Γάϊος Δερβαῖος καὶ Τιμόθεος, Ἀσιανοὶ δὲ Τυχικὸς καὶ Τρόφιμος·
verses.translit: syneipeto de auto Sopatros Pyrroy Veroiaios, Thessalonikeon de Aristarhos kai Sekoundos, kai Gaios Dervaios kai Timotheos, Asianoi de Tyhikos kai Trofimos*
verses.translation: And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.

verses.original: οὗτοι ⸀δὲ ⸀προσελθόντες ἔμενον ἡμᾶς ἐν Τρῳάδι·
verses.translit: outoi de proselthontes emenon emas en Troadi*
verses.translation: These going before tarried for us at Troas.

verses.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐξεπλεύσαμεν μετὰ τὰς ἡμέρας τῶν ἀζύμων ἀπὸ Φιλίππων, καὶ ἤλθομεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν Τρῳάδα ἄχρι ἡμερῶν πέντε, ⸀οὗ διετρίψαμεν ἡμέρας ἑπτά.
verses.translit: emeis de exepleysamen meta tas emeras ton azymon apo Filippon, kai elthomen pros autous eis ten Troada ahri emeron pente, ou dietripsamen emeras epta.
verses.translation: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.

verses.original: Ἐν δὲ τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων συνηγμένων ⸀ἡμῶν κλάσαι ἄρτον ὁ Παῦλος διελέγετο αὐτοῖς, μέλλων ἐξιέναι τῇ ἐπαύριον, παρέτεινέν τε τὸν λόγον μέχρι μεσονυκτίου.
verses.translit: En de te mia ton savvaton synigmenon emon klasai arton o Paulos dielegeto autois, mellon exienai te epayrion, pareteinen te ton logon mehri mesonyktioy.
verses.translation: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight.

verses.original: ἦσαν δὲ λαμπάδες ἱκαναὶ ἐν τῷ ὑπερῴῳ οὗ ἦμεν συνηγμένοι·
verses.translit: esan de lampades ikanai en to uperoo ou emen synigmenoi*
verses.translation: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.

verses.original: ⸀καθεζόμενος δέ τις νεανίας ὀνόματι Εὔτυχος ἐπὶ τῆς θυρίδος, καταφερόμενος ὕπνῳ βαθεῖ διαλεγομένου τοῦ Παύλου ἐπὶ πλεῖον, κατενεχθεὶς ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου ἔπεσεν ἀπὸ τοῦ τριστέγου κάτω καὶ ἤρθη νεκρός.
verses.translit: kathezomenos de tis neanias onomati Eutyhos epi tes thyridos, kataferomenos upno vathei dialegomenoy tou Payloy epi pleion, katenehtheis apo tou upnoy epesen apo tou tristegoy kato kai erthi nekros.
verses.translation: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.

verses.original: καταβὰς δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἐπέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ συμπεριλαβὼν εἶπεν· Μὴ θορυβεῖσθε, ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἐστιν.
verses.translit: katavas de o Paulos epepesen auto kai symperilavon eipen* Me thoryveisthe, e gar psyhe autou en auto estin.
verses.translation: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.

verses.original: ἀναβὰς δὲ καὶ κλάσας ⸀τὸν ἄρτον καὶ γευσάμενος ἐφʼ ἱκανόν τε ὁμιλήσας ἄχρι αὐγῆς, οὕτως ἐξῆλθεν.
verses.translit: anavas de kai klasas ton arton kai geysamenos ef' ikanon te omilisas ahri auges, outos exelthen.
verses.translation: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.

verses.original: ἤγαγον δὲ τὸν παῖδα ζῶντα, καὶ παρεκλήθησαν οὐ μετρίως.
verses.translit: egagon de ton paida zonta, kai pareklithisan ou metrios.
verses.translation: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.

verses.original: Ἡμεῖς δὲ ⸀προελθόντες ⸀ἐπὶ τὸ πλοῖον ἀνήχθημεν ἐπὶ τὴν Ἆσσον, ἐκεῖθεν μέλλοντες ἀναλαμβάνειν τὸν Παῦλον, οὕτως γὰρ ⸂διατεταγμένος ἦν⸃ μέλλων αὐτὸς πεζεύειν.
verses.translit: Emeis de proelthontes epi to ploion anihthimen epi ten Asson, ekeithen mellontes analamvanein ton Paulon, outos gar diatetagmenos en mellon autos pezeyein.
verses.translation: And we went before to ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go afoot.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ⸀συνέβαλλεν ἡμῖν εἰς τὴν Ἆσσον, ἀναλαβόντες αὐτὸν ἤλθομεν εἰς Μιτυλήνην,
verses.translit: os de synevallen emin eis ten Asson, analavontes auton elthomen eis Mitylinin,
verses.translation: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.

verses.original: κἀκεῖθεν ἀποπλεύσαντες τῇ ἐπιούσῃ κατηντήσαμεν ⸀ἄντικρυς Χίου, τῇ δὲ ἑτέρᾳ παρεβάλομεν εἰς ⸀Σάμον, τῇ ⸀δὲ ἐχομένῃ ἤλθομεν εἰς Μίλητον·
verses.translit: kakeithen apopleysantes te epioyse katintisamen antikrys Hioy, te de etera parevalomen eis Samon, te de ehomene elthomen eis Militon*
verses.translation: And we sailed thence, and came the next day over against Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.

verses.original: ⸀κεκρίκει γὰρ ὁ Παῦλος παραπλεῦσαι τὴν Ἔφεσον, ὅπως μὴ γένηται αὐτῷ χρονοτριβῆσαι ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ, ἔσπευδεν γὰρ εἰ δυνατὸν ⸀εἴη αὐτῷ τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς πεντηκοστῆς γενέσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
verses.translit: kekrikei gar o Paulos parapleusai ten Efeson, opos me genitai auto hronotrivesai en te Asia, espeyden gar ei dynaton eii auto ten emeran tes pentikostes genesthai eis Ierosolyma.
verses.translation: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.

verses.original: Ἀπὸ δὲ τῆς Μιλήτου πέμψας εἰς Ἔφεσον μετεκαλέσατο τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους τῆς ἐκκλησίας.
verses.translit: Apo de tes Militoy pempsas eis Efeson metekalesato tous presvyteroys tes ekklisias.
verses.translation: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ παρεγένοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ἀπὸ πρώτης ἡμέρας ἀφʼ ἧς ἐπέβην εἰς τὴν Ἀσίαν πῶς μεθʼ ὑμῶν τὸν πάντα χρόνον ἐγενόμην,
verses.translit: os de paregenonto pros auton eipen autois* Umeis epistasthe apo protis emeras af' es epevin eis ten Asian pos meth' umon ton panta hronon egenomin,
verses.translation: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,

verses.original: δουλεύων τῷ κυρίῳ μετὰ πάσης ταπεινοφροσύνης ⸀καὶ δακρύων καὶ πειρασμῶν τῶν συμβάντων μοι ἐν ταῖς ἐπιβουλαῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων·
verses.translit: doyleyon to kyrio meta pasis tapeinofrosynis kai dakryon kai peirasmon ton symvanton moi en tais epivoylais ton Ioydaion*
verses.translation: Serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews:

verses.original: ὡς οὐδὲν ὑπεστειλάμην τῶν συμφερόντων τοῦ μὴ ἀναγγεῖλαι ὑμῖν καὶ διδάξαι ὑμᾶς δημοσίᾳ καὶ κατʼ οἴκους,
verses.translit: os ouden upesteilamin ton symferonton tou me anaggeilai umin kai didaxai umas dimosia kai kat' oikoys,
verses.translation: And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you , but have shewed you, and have taught you publickly, and from house to house,

verses.original: διαμαρτυρόμενος Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Ἕλλησιν τὴν ⸀εἰς θεὸν μετάνοιαν καὶ ⸀πίστιν εἰς τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν ⸀Ἰησοῦν.
verses.translit: diamartyromenos Ioydaiois te kai Ellisin ten eis theon metanoian kai pistin eis ton kyrion emon Iisoun.
verses.translation: Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.original: καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ ⸂δεδεμένος ἐγὼ⸃ τῷ πνεύματι πορεύομαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ συναντήσοντά ⸀μοι μὴ εἰδώς,
verses.translit: kai nun idou dedemenos ego to pneymati poreyomai eis Ieroysalim, ta en aute synantisonta moi me eidos,
verses.translation: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:

verses.original: πλὴν ὅτι τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον κατὰ πόλιν διαμαρτύρεταί ⸀μοι λέγον ὅτι δεσμὰ ⸂καὶ θλίψεις με⸃ μένουσιν·
verses.translit: plen oti to pneuma to agion kata polin diamartyretai moi legon oti desma kai thlipseis me menoysin*
verses.translation: Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.

verses.original: ἀλλʼ οὐδενὸς ⸀λόγου ⸀ποιοῦμαι τὴν ⸀ψυχὴν τιμίαν ἐμαυτῷ ὡς ⸀τελειῶσαι τὸν δρόμον ⸀μου καὶ τὴν διακονίαν ἣν ἔλαβον παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ, διαμαρτύρασθαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς χάριτος τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: all' oudenos logoy poioumai ten psyhen timian emayto os teleiosai ton dromon moy kai ten diakonian en elavon para tou kyrioy Iisou, diamartyrasthai to euaggelion tes haritos tou theou.
verses.translation: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.

verses.original: Καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ οἶδα ὅτι οὐκέτι ὄψεσθε τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ὑμεῖς πάντες ἐν οἷς διῆλθον κηρύσσων τὴν ⸀βασιλείαν.
verses.translit: Kai nun idou ego oida oti ouketi opsesthe to prosopon moy umeis pantes en ois dielthon kirysson ten vasileian.
verses.translation: And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.

verses.original: ⸀διότι μαρτύρομαι ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ σήμερον ἡμέρᾳ ὅτι καθαρός ⸀εἰμι ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος πάντων,
verses.translit: dioti martyromai umin en te simeron emera oti katharos eimi apo tou aimatos panton,
verses.translation: Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men .

verses.original: οὐ γὰρ ὑπεστειλάμην τοῦ μὴ ἀναγγεῖλαι ⸂πᾶσαν τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ὑμῖν⸃.
verses.translit: ou gar upesteilamin tou me anaggeilai pasan ten voylen tou theou umin.
verses.translation: For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God.

verses.original: ⸀προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς καὶ παντὶ τῷ ποιμνίῳ, ἐν ᾧ ὑμᾶς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἔθετο ἐπισκόπους, ποιμαίνειν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ ⸀θεοῦ, ἣν περιεποιήσατο διὰ τοῦ ⸂αἵματος τοῦ ἰδίου⸃.
verses.translit: prosehete eaytois kai panti to poimnio, en o umas to pneuma to agion etheto episkopoys, poimainein ten ekklisian tou theou, en periepoiisato dia tou aimatos tou idioy.
verses.translation: Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.

verses.original: ἐγὼ ⸀οἶδα ὅτι εἰσελεύσονται μετὰ τὴν ἄφιξίν μου λύκοι βαρεῖς εἰς ὑμᾶς μὴ φειδόμενοι τοῦ ποιμνίου,
verses.translit: ego oida oti eiseleysontai meta ten afixin moy lykoi vareis eis umas me feidomenoi tou poimnioy,
verses.translation: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.

verses.original: καὶ ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν ἀναστήσονται ἄνδρες λαλοῦντες διεστραμμένα τοῦ ἀποσπᾶν τοὺς μαθητὰς ὀπίσω ⸀ἑαυτῶν·
verses.translit: kai ex umon auton anastisontai andres lalountes diestrammena tou apospan tous mathitas opiso eayton*
verses.translation: Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.

verses.original: διὸ γρηγορεῖτε, μνημονεύοντες ὅτι τριετίαν νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν οὐκ ἐπαυσάμην μετὰ δακρύων νουθετῶν ἕνα ἕκαστον.
verses.translit: dio grigoreite, mnimoneyontes oti trietian nykta kai emeran ouk epaysamin meta dakryon noytheton ena ekaston.
verses.translation: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.

verses.original: καὶ τὰ νῦν παρατίθεμαι ⸀ὑμᾶς τῷ ⸀θεῷ καὶ τῷ λόγῳ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ, τῷ δυναμένῳ ⸀οἰκοδομῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι ⸀τὴν κληρονομίαν ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πᾶσιν.
verses.translit: kai ta nun paratithemai umas to theo kai to logo tes haritos autou, to dynameno oikodomesai kai dounai ten klironomian en tois egiasmenois pasin.
verses.translation: And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.

verses.original: ἀργυρίου ἢ χρυσίου ἢ ἱματισμοῦ οὐδενὸς ἐπεθύμησα·
verses.translit: argyrioy e hrysioy e imatismou oudenos epethymisa*
verses.translation: I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.

verses.original: αὐτοὶ γινώσκετε ὅτι ταῖς χρείαις μου καὶ τοῖς οὖσι μετʼ ἐμοῦ ὑπηρέτησαν αἱ χεῖρες αὗται.
verses.translit: autoi ginoskete oti tais hreiais moy kai tois ousi met' emou upiretisan ai heires autai.
verses.translation: Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.

verses.original: πάντα ὑπέδειξα ὑμῖν ὅτι οὕτως κοπιῶντας δεῖ ἀντιλαμβάνεσθαι τῶν ἀσθενούντων, μνημονεύειν τε τῶν λόγων τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ ὅτι αὐτὸς εἶπεν Μακάριόν ἐστιν μᾶλλον διδόναι ἢ λαμβάνειν.
verses.translit: panta upedeixa umin oti outos kopiontas dei antilamvanesthai ton asthenoynton, mnimoneyein te ton logon tou kyrioy Iisou oti autos eipen Makarion estin mallon didonai e lamvanein.
verses.translation: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.

verses.original: Καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν θεὶς τὰ γόνατα αὐτοῦ σὺν πᾶσιν αὐτοῖς προσηύξατο.
verses.translit: Kai tauta eipon theis ta gonata autou sun pasin autois prosiyxato.
verses.translation: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.

verses.original: ἱκανὸς δὲ ⸂κλαυθμὸς ἐγένετο⸃ πάντων, καὶ ἐπιπεσόντες ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τοῦ Παύλου κατεφίλουν αὐτόν,
verses.translit: ikanos de klaythmos egeneto panton, kai epipesontes epi ton trahilon tou Payloy katefiloyn auton,
verses.translation: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul’s neck, and kissed him,

verses.original: ὀδυνώμενοι μάλιστα ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ ᾧ εἰρήκει ὅτι οὐκέτι μέλλουσιν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ θεωρεῖν. προέπεμπον δὲ αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον.
verses.translit: odynomenoi malista epi to logo o eirikei oti ouketi melloysin to prosopon autou theorein. proepempon de auton eis to ploion.
verses.translation: Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο ἀναχθῆναι ἡμᾶς ἀποσπασθέντας ἀπʼ αὐτῶν, εὐθυδρομήσαντες ἤλθομεν εἰς τὴν ⸀Κῶ, τῇ δὲ ἑξῆς εἰς τὴν Ῥόδον, κἀκεῖθεν εἰς Πάταρα·
verses.translit: Os de egeneto anahthenai emas apospasthentas ap' auton, euthydromisantes elthomen eis ten Ko, te de exes eis ten Rodon, kakeithen eis Patara*
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:

verses.original: καὶ εὑρόντες πλοῖον διαπερῶν εἰς Φοινίκην ἐπιβάντες ἀνήχθημεν.
verses.translit: kai eurontes ploion diaperon eis Foinikin epivantes anihthimen.
verses.translation: And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.

verses.original: ⸀ἀναφάναντες δὲ τὴν Κύπρον καὶ καταλιπόντες αὐτὴν εὐώνυμον ἐπλέομεν εἰς Συρίαν, καὶ ⸀κατήλθομεν εἰς Τύρον, ἐκεῖσε γὰρ ⸂τὸ πλοῖον ἦν⸃ ἀποφορτιζόμενον τὸν γόμον.
verses.translit: anafanantes de ten Kypron kai katalipontes auten euonymon epleomen eis Syrian, kai katilthomen eis Tyron, ekeise gar to ploion en apofortizomenon ton gomon.
verses.translation: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unlade her burden.

verses.original: ⸂ἀνευρόντες δὲ τοὺς⸃ μαθητὰς ἐπεμείναμεν αὐτοῦ ἡμέρας ἑπτά, οἵτινες τῷ Παύλῳ ἔλεγον διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος μὴ ⸀ἐπιβαίνειν εἰς ⸀Ἱεροσόλυμα.
verses.translit: aneyrontes de tous mathitas epemeinamen autou emeras epta, oitines to Paylo elegon dia tou pneymatos me epivainein eis Ierosolyma.
verses.translation: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.

verses.original: ὅτε δὲ ἐγένετο ⸂ἐξαρτίσαι ἡμᾶς⸃ τὰς ἡμέρας, ἐξελθόντες ἐπορευόμεθα προπεμπόντων ἡμᾶς πάντων σὺν γυναιξὶ καὶ τέκνοις ἕως ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, καὶ θέντες τὰ γόνατα ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν ⸀προσευξάμενοι
verses.translit: ote de egeneto exartisai emas tas emeras, exelthontes eporeyometha propemponton emas panton sun gynaixi kai teknois eos exo tes poleos, kai thentes ta gonata epi ton aigialon proseyxamenoi
verses.translation: And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.

verses.original: ⸂ἀπησπασάμεθα ἀλλήλους, καὶ⸃ ⸀ἐνέβημεν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὰ ἴδια.
verses.translit: apispasametha alliloys, kai enevimen eis to ploion, ekeinoi de upestrepsan eis ta idia.
verses.translation: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.

verses.original: Ἡμεῖς δὲ τὸν πλοῦν διανύσαντες ἀπὸ Τύρου κατηντήσαμεν εἰς Πτολεμαΐδα, καὶ ἀσπασάμενοι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ἐμείναμεν ἡμέραν μίαν παρʼ αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: Emeis de ton ploun dianysantes apo Tyroy katintisamen eis PtolemaIda, kai aspasamenoi tous adelfous emeinamen emeran mian par' autois.
verses.translation: And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.

verses.original: τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ἐξελθόντες ⸀ἤλθομεν εἰς Καισάρειαν, καὶ εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὸν οἶκον Φιλίππου τοῦ εὐαγγελιστοῦ ὄντος ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἐμείναμεν παρʼ αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: te de epayrion exelthontes elthomen eis Kaisareian, kai eiselthontes eis ton oikon Filippoy tou euaggelistou ontos ek ton epta emeinamen par' auto.
verses.translation: And the next day we that were of Paul’s company departed, and came unto Cæsarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him.

verses.original: τούτῳ δὲ ἦσαν θυγατέρες ⸂τέσσαρες παρθένοι⸃ προφητεύουσαι.
verses.translit: toyto de esan thygateres tessares parthenoi profiteyoysai.
verses.translation: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.

verses.original: ἐπιμενόντων ⸀δὲ ἡμέρας πλείους κατῆλθέν τις ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας προφήτης ὀνόματι Ἅγαβος,
verses.translit: epimenonton de emeras pleioys katelthen tis apo tes Ioydaias profitis onomati Agavos,
verses.translation: And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judæa a certain prophet, named Agabus.

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν πρὸς ἡμᾶς καὶ ἄρας τὴν ζώνην τοῦ Παύλου δήσας ⸀ἑαυτοῦ τοὺς πόδας καὶ τὰς χεῖρας εἶπεν· Τάδε λέγει τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον Τὸν ἄνδρα οὗ ἐστιν ἡ ζώνη αὕτη, οὕτως δήσουσιν ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ παραδώσουσιν εἰς χεῖρας ἐθνῶν.
verses.translit: kai elthon pros emas kai aras ten zonin tou Payloy disas eaytou tous podas kai tas heiras eipen* Tade legei to pneuma to agion Ton andra ou estin e zoni auti, outos disoysin en Ieroysalem oi Ioydaioi kai paradosoysin eis heiras ethnon.
verses.translation: And when he was come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ἠκούσαμεν ταῦτα, παρεκαλοῦμεν ἡμεῖς τε καὶ οἱ ἐντόπιοι τοῦ μὴ ἀναβαίνειν αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ.
verses.translit: os de ekoysamen tauta, parekaloumen emeis te kai oi entopioi tou me anavainein auton eis Ieroysalim.
verses.translation: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.

verses.original: ⸂τότε ἀπεκρίθη⸃ ὁ Παῦλος· Τί ποιεῖτε κλαίοντες καὶ συνθρύπτοντές μου τὴν καρδίαν; ἐγὼ γὰρ οὐ μόνον δεθῆναι ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀποθανεῖν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἑτοίμως ἔχω ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.
verses.translit: tote apekrithi o Paulos* Ti poieite klaiontes kai synthryptontes moy ten kardian; ego gar ou monon dethenai alla kai apothanein eis Ieroysalem etoimos eho uper tou onomatos tou kyrioy Iisou.
verses.translation: Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.original: μὴ πειθομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἡσυχάσαμεν εἰπόντες· ⸂Τοῦ κυρίου τὸ θέλημα⸃ ⸀γινέσθω.
verses.translit: me peithomenoy de autou esyhasamen eipontes* Tou kyrioy to thelima ginestho.
verses.translation: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.

verses.original: Μετὰ δὲ τὰς ἡμέρας ταύτας ἐπισκευασάμενοι ἀνεβαίνομεν εἰς ⸀Ἱεροσόλυμα·
verses.translit: Meta de tas emeras taytas episkeyasamenoi anevainomen eis Ierosolyma*
verses.translation: And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.

verses.original: συνῆλθον δὲ καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν ἀπὸ Καισαρείας σὺν ἡμῖν, ἄγοντες παρʼ ᾧ ξενισθῶμεν Μνάσωνί τινι Κυπρίῳ, ἀρχαίῳ μαθητῇ.
verses.translit: synelthon de kai ton mathiton apo Kaisareias sun emin, agontes par' o xenisthomen Mnasoni tini Kyprio, arhaio mathite.
verses.translation: There went with us also certain of the disciples of Cæsarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.

verses.original: Γενομένων δὲ ἡμῶν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀσμένως ⸀ἀπεδέξαντο ἡμᾶς οἱ ἀδελφοί.
verses.translit: Genomenon de emon eis Ierosolyma asmenos apedexanto emas oi adelfoi.
verses.translation: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.

verses.original: τῇ δὲ ἐπιούσῃ εἰσῄει ὁ Παῦλος σὺν ἡμῖν πρὸς Ἰάκωβον, πάντες τε παρεγένοντο οἱ πρεσβύτεροι.
verses.translit: te de epioyse eiseei o Paulos sun emin pros Iakovon, pantes te paregenonto oi presvyteroi.
verses.translation: And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.

verses.original: καὶ ἀσπασάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐξηγεῖτο καθʼ ἓν ἕκαστον ὧν ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν διὰ τῆς διακονίας αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai aspasamenos autous exigeito kath' en ekaston on epoiisen o theos en tois ethnesin dia tes diakonias autou.
verses.translation: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ἐδόξαζον τὸν ⸀θεόν, ⸂εἶπόν τε⸃ αὐτῷ· Θεωρεῖς, ἀδελφέ, πόσαι μυριάδες εἰσὶν ⸂ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις⸃ τῶν πεπιστευκότων, καὶ πάντες ζηλωταὶ τοῦ νόμου ὑπάρχουσιν·
verses.translit: oi de akoysantes edoxazon ton theon, eipon te auto* Theoreis, adelfe, posai myriades eisin en tois Ioydaiois ton pepisteykoton, kai pantes zilotai tou nomoy uparhoysin*
verses.translation: And when they heard it , they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law:

verses.original: κατηχήθησαν δὲ περὶ σοῦ ὅτι ἀποστασίαν διδάσκεις ἀπὸ Μωϋσέως τοὺς κατὰ τὰ ἔθνη πάντας Ἰουδαίους, λέγων μὴ περιτέμνειν αὐτοὺς τὰ τέκνα μηδὲ τοῖς ἔθεσιν περιπατεῖν.
verses.translit: katihithisan de peri sou oti apostasian didaskeis apo Moyseos tous kata ta ethni pantas Ioydaioys, legon me peritemnein autous ta tekna mide tois ethesin peripatein.
verses.translation: And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.

verses.original: τί οὖν ἐστιν; πάντως ⸀ἀκούσονται ὅτι ἐλήλυθας.
verses.translit: ti oun estin; pantos akoysontai oti elilythas.
verses.translation: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.

verses.original: τοῦτο οὖν ποίησον ὅ σοι λέγομεν· εἰσὶν ἡμῖν ἄνδρες τέσσαρες εὐχὴν ἔχοντες ⸀ἀφʼ ἑαυτῶν.
verses.translit: touto oun poiison o soi legomen* eisin emin andres tessares euhen ehontes af' eayton.
verses.translation: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men which have a vow on them;

verses.original: τούτους παραλαβὼν ἁγνίσθητι σὺν αὐτοῖς καὶ δαπάνησον ἐπʼ αὐτοῖς ἵνα ⸀ξυρήσονται τὴν κεφαλήν, καὶ ⸀γνώσονται πάντες ὅτι ὧν κατήχηνται περὶ σοῦ οὐδέν ἐστιν, ἀλλὰ στοιχεῖς καὶ αὐτὸς ⸂φυλάσσων τὸν νόμον⸃.
verses.translit: toytoys paralavon agnisthiti sun autois kai dapanison ep' autois ina xyrisontai ten kefalin, kai gnosontai pantes oti on katihintai peri sou ouden estin, alla stoiheis kai autos fylasson ton nomon.
verses.translation: Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.

verses.original: περὶ δὲ τῶν πεπιστευκότων ἐθνῶν ἡμεῖς ⸀ἀπεστείλαμεν ⸀κρίναντες φυλάσσεσθαι αὐτοὺς τό τε εἰδωλόθυτον ⸀καὶ αἷμα καὶ πνικτὸν καὶ πορνείαν.
verses.translit: peri de ton pepisteykoton ethnon emeis apesteilamen krinantes fylassesthai autous to te eidolothyton kai aima kai pnikton kai porneian.
verses.translation: As touching the Gentiles which believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.

verses.original: τότε ὁ Παῦλος παραλαβὼν τοὺς ἄνδρας τῇ ἐχομένῃ ἡμέρᾳ σὺν αὐτοῖς ἁγνισθεὶς εἰσῄει εἰς τὸ ἱερόν, διαγγέλλων τὴν ἐκπλήρωσιν τῶν ἡμερῶν τοῦ ἁγνισμοῦ ἕως οὗ προσηνέχθη ὑπὲρ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου αὐτῶν ἡ προσφορά.
verses.translit: tote o Paulos paralavon tous andras te ehomene emera sun autois agnistheis eiseei eis to ieron, diaggellon ten ekplirosin ton emeron tou agnismou eos ou prosinehthi uper enos ekastoy auton e prosfora.
verses.translation: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ ἔμελλον αἱ ἑπτὰ ἡμέραι συντελεῖσθαι, οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι θεασάμενοι αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ συνέχεον πάντα τὸν ὄχλον καὶ ἐπέβαλον ⸂ἐπʼ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας⸃,
verses.translit: Os de emellon ai epta emerai synteleisthai, oi apo tes Asias Ioydaioi theasamenoi auton en to iero syneheon panta ton ohlon kai epevalon ep' auton tas heiras,
verses.translation: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,

verses.original: κράζοντες· Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται, βοηθεῖτε· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ κατὰ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ τοῦ νόμου καὶ τοῦ τόπου τούτου πάντας ⸀πανταχῇ διδάσκων, ἔτι τε καὶ Ἕλληνας εἰσήγαγεν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ κεκοίνωκεν τὸν ἅγιον τόπον τοῦτον.
verses.translit: krazontes* Andres Israilitai, voitheite* outos estin o anthropos o kata tou laou kai tou nomoy kai tou topoy toytoy pantas pantahe didaskon, eti te kai Ellinas eisigagen eis to ieron kai kekoinoken ton agion topon touton.
verses.translation: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.

verses.original: ἦσαν γὰρ ⸀προεωρακότες Τρόφιμον τὸν Ἐφέσιον ἐν τῇ πόλει σὺν αὐτῷ, ὃν ἐνόμιζον ὅτι εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν εἰσήγαγεν ὁ Παῦλος.
verses.translit: esan gar proeorakotes Trofimon ton Efesion en te polei sun auto, on enomizon oti eis to ieron eisigagen o Paulos.
verses.translation: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)

verses.original: ἐκινήθη τε ἡ πόλις ὅλη καὶ ἐγένετο συνδρομὴ τοῦ λαοῦ, καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενοι τοῦ Παύλου εἷλκον αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ εὐθέως ἐκλείσθησαν αἱ θύραι.
verses.translit: ekinithi te e polis oli kai egeneto syndrome tou laou, kai epilavomenoi tou Payloy eilkon auton exo tou ierou, kai eutheos ekleisthisan ai thyrai.
verses.translation: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.

verses.original: ζητούντων ⸀τε αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι ἀνέβη φάσις τῷ χιλιάρχῳ τῆς σπείρης ὅτι ὅλη ⸀συγχύννεται Ἰερουσαλήμ,
verses.translit: zitoynton te auton apokteinai anevi fasis to hiliarho tes speiris oti oli syghynnetai Ieroysalim,
verses.translation: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

verses.original: ὃς ἐξαυτῆς παραλαβὼν στρατιώτας καὶ ἑκατοντάρχας κατέδραμεν ἐπʼ αὐτούς, οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες τὸν χιλίαρχον καὶ τοὺς στρατιώτας ἐπαύσαντο τύπτοντες τὸν Παῦλον.
verses.translit: os exaytes paralavon stratiotas kai ekatontarhas katedramen ep' autoys, oi de idontes ton hiliarhon kai tous stratiotas epaysanto typtontes ton Paulon.
verses.translation: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.

verses.original: ⸂τότε ἐγγίσας⸃ ὁ χιλίαρχος ἐπελάβετο αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκέλευσε δεθῆναι ἁλύσεσι δυσί, καὶ ἐπυνθάνετο ⸀τίς εἴη καὶ τί ἐστιν πεποιηκώς.
verses.translit: tote eggisas o hiliarhos epelaveto autou kai ekeleyse dethenai alysesi dysi, kai epynthaneto tis eii kai ti estin pepoiikos.
verses.translation: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.

verses.original: ἄλλοι δὲ ἄλλο τι ⸀ἐπεφώνουν ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ· μὴ ⸂δυναμένου δὲ αὐτοῦ⸃ γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς διὰ τὸν θόρυβον ἐκέλευσεν ἄγεσθαι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν.
verses.translit: alloi de allo ti epefonoyn en to ohlo* me dynamenoy de autou gnonai to asfales dia ton thoryvon ekeleysen agesthai auton eis ten paremvolin.
verses.translation: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.

verses.original: ὅτε δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀναβαθμούς, συνέβη βαστάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν στρατιωτῶν διὰ τὴν βίαν τοῦ ὄχλου,
verses.translit: ote de egeneto epi tous anavathmoys, synevi vastazesthai auton upo ton stratioton dia ten vian tou ohloy,
verses.translation: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.

verses.original: ἠκολούθει γὰρ τὸ πλῆθος τοῦ λαοῦ ⸀κράζοντες· Αἶρε αὐτόν.
verses.translit: ekoloythei gar to plethos tou laou krazontes* Aire auton.
verses.translation: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.

verses.original: Μέλλων τε εἰσάγεσθαι εἰς τὴν παρεμβολὴν ὁ Παῦλος λέγει τῷ χιλιάρχῳ· Εἰ ἔξεστίν μοι εἰπεῖν ⸀τι πρὸς σέ; ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ἑλληνιστὶ γινώσκεις;
verses.translit: Mellon te eisagesthai eis ten paremvolen o Paulos legei to hiliarho* Ei exestin moi eipein ti pros se; o de efi* Ellinisti ginoskeis;
verses.translation: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?

verses.original: οὐκ ἄρα σὺ εἶ ὁ Αἰγύπτιος ὁ πρὸ τούτων τῶν ἡμερῶν ἀναστατώσας καὶ ἐξαγαγὼν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον τοὺς τετρακισχιλίους ἄνδρας τῶν σικαρίων;
verses.translit: ouk ara su ei o Aigyptios o pro toyton ton emeron anastatosas kai exagagon eis ten erimon tous tetrakishilioys andras ton sikarion;
verses.translation: Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Παῦλος· Ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος μέν εἰμι Ἰουδαῖος, Ταρσεὺς τῆς Κιλικίας, οὐκ ἀσήμου πόλεως πολίτης· δέομαι δέ σου, ἐπίτρεψόν μοι λαλῆσαι πρὸς τὸν λαόν.
verses.translit: eipen de o Paulos* Ego anthropos men eimi Ioydaios, Tarseus tes Kilikias, ouk asimoy poleos politis* deomai de soy, epitrepson moi lalesai pros ton laon.
verses.translation: But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.

verses.original: ἐπιτρέψαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος ἑστὼς ἐπὶ τῶν ἀναβαθμῶν κατέσεισε τῇ χειρὶ τῷ λαῷ, πολλῆς δὲ σιγῆς γενομένης ⸀προσεφώνησεν τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ λέγων
verses.translit: epitrepsantos de autou o Paulos estos epi ton anavathmon kateseise te heiri to lao, polles de siges genomenis prosefonisen te EvraIdi dialekto legon
verses.translation: And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,

verses.original: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες, ἀκούσατέ μου τῆς πρὸς ὑμᾶς νυνὶ ἀπολογίας.
verses.translit: Andres adelfoi kai pateres, akoysate moy tes pros umas nyni apologias.
verses.translation: Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence which I make now unto you.

verses.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ ὅτι τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ προσεφώνει αὐτοῖς μᾶλλον παρέσχον ἡσυχίαν. καὶ φησίν·
verses.translit: Akoysantes de oti te EvraIdi dialekto prosefonei autois mallon pareshon esyhian. kai fisin*
verses.translation: (And when they heard that he spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)

verses.original: ⸀Ἐγώ εἰμι ἀνὴρ Ἰουδαῖος, γεγεννημένος ἐν Ταρσῷ τῆς Κιλικίας, ἀνατεθραμμένος δὲ ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ παρὰ τοὺς πόδας Γαμαλιήλ, πεπαιδευμένος κατὰ ἀκρίβειαν τοῦ πατρῴου νόμου, ζηλωτὴς ὑπάρχων τοῦ θεοῦ καθὼς πάντες ὑμεῖς ἐστε σήμερον,
verses.translit: Ego eimi aner Ioydaios, gegennimenos en Tarso tes Kilikias, anatethrammenos de en te polei tayte para tous podas Gamaliil, pepaideymenos kata akriveian tou patrooy nomoy, zilotes uparhon tou theou kathos pantes umeis este simeron,
verses.translation: I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.

verses.original: ὃς ταύτην τὴν ὁδὸν ἐδίωξα ἄχρι θανάτου, δεσμεύων καὶ παραδιδοὺς εἰς φυλακὰς ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας,
verses.translit: os taytin ten odon edioxa ahri thanatoy, desmeyon kai paradidous eis fylakas andras te kai gynaikas,
verses.translation: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.

verses.original: ὡς καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς μαρτυρεῖ μοι καὶ πᾶν τὸ πρεσβυτέριον· παρʼ ὧν καὶ ἐπιστολὰς δεξάμενος πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς εἰς Δαμασκὸν ἐπορευόμην ἄξων καὶ τοὺς ἐκεῖσε ὄντας δεδεμένους εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἵνα τιμωρηθῶσιν.
verses.translit: os kai o arhiereus martyrei moi kai pan to presvyterion* par' on kai epistolas dexamenos pros tous adelfous eis Damaskon eporeyomin axon kai tous ekeise ontas dedemenoys eis Ieroysalem ina timorithosin.
verses.translation: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι πορευομένῳ καὶ ἐγγίζοντι τῇ Δαμασκῷ περὶ μεσημβρίαν ἐξαίφνης ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ περιαστράψαι φῶς ἱκανὸν περὶ ἐμέ,
verses.translit: Egeneto de moi poreyomeno kai eggizonti te Damasko peri mesimvrian exaifnis ek tou ouranou periastrapsai fos ikanon peri eme,
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.

verses.original: ἔπεσά τε εἰς τὸ ἔδαφος καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς λεγούσης μοι· Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;
verses.translit: epesa te eis to edafos kai ekoysa fones legoysis moi* Saoul Saoyl, ti me diokeis;
verses.translation: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

verses.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ἀπεκρίθην· Τίς εἶ, κύριε; εἶπέν τε πρὸς ⸀ἐμέ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος ὃν σὺ διώκεις.
verses.translit: ego de apekrithin* Tis ei, kyrie; eipen te pros eme* Ego eimi Iisous o Nazoraios on su diokeis.
verses.translation: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ ὄντες τὸ μὲν φῶς ⸀ἐθεάσαντο τὴν δὲ φωνὴν οὐκ ἤκουσαν τοῦ λαλοῦντός μοι.
verses.translit: oi de sun emoi ontes to men fos etheasanto ten de fonen ouk ekoysan tou lalountos moi.
verses.translation: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.

verses.original: εἶπον δέ· Τί ποιήσω, κύριε; ὁ δὲ κύριος εἶπεν πρός με· Ἀναστὰς πορεύου εἰς Δαμασκόν, κἀκεῖ σοι λαληθήσεται περὶ πάντων ὧν τέτακταί σοι ποιῆσαι.
verses.translit: eipon de* Ti poiiso, kyrie; o de kyrios eipen pros me* Anastas poreyoy eis Damaskon, kakei soi lalithisetai peri panton on tetaktai soi poiesai.
verses.translation: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ οὐκ ἐνέβλεπον ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τοῦ φωτὸς ἐκείνου, χειραγωγούμενος ὑπὸ τῶν συνόντων μοι ἦλθον εἰς Δαμασκόν.
verses.translit: os de ouk enevlepon apo tes doxis tou fotos ekeinoy, heiragogoymenos upo ton synonton moi elthon eis Damaskon.
verses.translation: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.

verses.original: Ἁνανίας δέ τις ἀνὴρ ⸀εὐλαβὴς κατὰ τὸν νόμον μαρτυρούμενος ὑπὸ πάντων τῶν κατοικούντων Ἰουδαίων,
verses.translit: Ananias de tis aner eulaves kata ton nomon martyroymenos upo panton ton katoikoynton Ioydaion,
verses.translation: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there ,

verses.original: ἐλθὼν πρὸς ⸀ἐμὲ καὶ ἐπιστὰς εἶπέν μοι· Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ, ἀνάβλεψον· κἀγὼ αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἀνέβλεψα εἰς αὐτόν.
verses.translit: elthon pros eme kai epistas eipen moi* Saoul adelfe, anavlepson* kago aute te ora anevlepsa eis auton.
verses.translation: Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν προεχειρίσατό σε γνῶναι τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰδεῖν τὸν δίκαιον καὶ ἀκοῦσαι φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: o de eipen* O theos ton pateron emon proeheirisato se gnonai to thelima autou kai idein ton dikaion kai akousai fonen ek tou stomatos autou,
verses.translation: And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will, and see that Just One, and shouldest hear the voice of his mouth.

verses.original: ὅτι ἔσῃ μάρτυς αὐτῷ πρὸς πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὧν ἑώρακας καὶ ἤκουσας.
verses.translit: oti ese martys auto pros pantas anthropoys on eorakas kai ekoysas.
verses.translation: For thou shalt be his witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.

verses.original: καὶ νῦν τί μέλλεις; ἀναστὰς βάπτισαι καὶ ἀπόλουσαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου ἐπικαλεσάμενος τὸ ὄνομα ⸀αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: kai nun ti melleis; anastas vaptisai kai apoloysai tas amartias soy epikalesamenos to onoma autou.
verses.translation: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δέ μοι ὑποστρέψαντι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ προσευχομένου μου ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ γενέσθαι με ἐν ἐκστάσει
verses.translit: Egeneto de moi upostrepsanti eis Ieroysalem kai proseyhomenoy moy en to iero genesthai me en ekstasei
verses.translation: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;

verses.original: καὶ ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν λέγοντά μοι· Σπεῦσον καὶ ἔξελθε ἐν τάχει ἐξ Ἰερουσαλήμ, διότι οὐ παραδέξονταί ⸀σου μαρτυρίαν περὶ ἐμοῦ.
verses.translit: kai idein auton legonta moi* Speuson kai exelthe en tahei ex Ieroysalim, dioti ou paradexontai soy martyrian peri emou.
verses.translation: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.

verses.original: κἀγὼ εἶπον· Κύριε, αὐτοὶ ἐπίστανται ὅτι ἐγὼ ἤμην φυλακίζων καὶ δέρων κατὰ τὰς συναγωγὰς τοὺς πιστεύοντας ἐπὶ σέ·
verses.translit: kago eipon* Kyrie, autoi epistantai oti ego emin fylakizon kai deron kata tas synagogas tous pisteyontas epi se*
verses.translation: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:

verses.original: καὶ ὅτε ⸀ἐξεχύννετο τὸ αἷμα Στεφάνου τοῦ μάρτυρός σου, καὶ αὐτὸς ἤμην ἐφεστὼς καὶ συνευδοκῶν ⸀καὶ φυλάσσων τὰ ἱμάτια τῶν ἀναιρούντων αὐτόν.
verses.translit: kai ote exehynneto to aima Stefanoy tou martyros soy, kai autos emin efestos kai syneydokon kai fylasson ta imatia ton anairoynton auton.
verses.translation: And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν πρός με· Πορεύου, ὅτι ἐγὼ εἰς ἔθνη μακρὰν ἐξαποστελῶ σε.
verses.translit: kai eipen pros me* Poreyoy, oti ego eis ethni makran exapostelo se.
verses.translation: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.

verses.original: Ἤκουον δὲ αὐτοῦ ἄχρι τούτου τοῦ λόγου καὶ ἐπῆραν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτῶν λέγοντες· Αἶρε ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς τὸν τοιοῦτον, οὐ γὰρ καθῆκεν αὐτὸν ζῆν.
verses.translit: Ekoyon de autou ahri toytoy tou logoy kai eperan ten fonen auton legontes* Aire apo tes ges ton toiouton, ou gar katheken auton zen.
verses.translation: And they gave him audience unto this word, and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.

verses.original: ⸀κραυγαζόντων ⸀τε αὐτῶν καὶ ῥιπτούντων τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ κονιορτὸν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸν ἀέρα,
verses.translit: kraygazonton te auton kai Riptoynton ta imatia kai koniorton vallonton eis ton aera,
verses.translation: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air,

verses.original: ἐκέλευσεν ⸂ὁ χιλίαρχος εἰσάγεσθαι αὐτὸν⸃ εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν, ⸀εἴπας μάστιξιν ἀνετάζεσθαι αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιγνῷ διʼ ἣν αἰτίαν οὕτως ἐπεφώνουν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: ekeleysen o hiliarhos eisagesthai auton eis ten paremvolin, eipas mastixin anetazesthai auton ina epigno di' en aitian outos epefonoyn auto.
verses.translation: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ ⸀προέτειναν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἱμᾶσιν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν ἑστῶτα ἑκατόνταρχον ὁ Παῦλος· Εἰ ἄνθρωπον Ῥωμαῖον καὶ ἀκατάκριτον ἔξεστιν ὑμῖν μαστίζειν;
verses.translit: os de proeteinan auton tois imasin eipen pros ton estota ekatontarhon o Paulos* Ei anthropon Romaion kai akatakriton exestin umin mastizein;
verses.translation: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
