verses.original: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης προσελθὼν ⸂τῷ χιλιάρχῳ ἀπήγγειλεν⸃ λέγων· ⸀Τί μέλλεις ποιεῖν; ὁ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν.
verses.translit: akoysas de o ekatontarhis proselthon to hiliarho apiggeilen legon* Ti melleis poiein; o gar anthropos outos Romaios estin.
verses.translation: When the centurion heard that , he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.

verses.original: προσελθὼν δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Λέγε μοι, ⸀σὺ Ῥωμαῖος εἶ; ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ναί.
verses.translit: proselthon de o hiliarhos eipen auto* Lege moi, su Romaios ei; o de efi* Nai.
verses.translation: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.

verses.original: ἀπεκρίθη ⸀δὲ ὁ χιλίαρχος· Ἐγὼ πολλοῦ κεφαλαίου τὴν πολιτείαν ταύτην ἐκτησάμην. ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη· Ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ γεγέννημαι.
verses.translit: apekrithi de o hiliarhos* Ego pollou kefalaioy ten politeian taytin ektisamin. o de Paulos efi* Ego de kai gegennimai.
verses.translation: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.

verses.original: εὐθέως οὖν ἀπέστησαν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ οἱ μέλλοντες αὐτὸν ἀνετάζειν· καὶ ὁ χιλίαρχος δὲ ἐφοβήθη ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν καὶ ὅτι ⸂αὐτὸν ἦν⸃ δεδεκώς.
verses.translit: eutheos oun apestisan ap' autou oi mellontes auton anetazein* kai o hiliarhos de efovithi epignous oti Romaios estin kai oti auton en dedekos.
verses.translation: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.

verses.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον βουλόμενος γνῶναι τὸ ἀσφαλὲς τὸ τί κατηγορεῖται ⸀ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἔλυσεν ⸀αὐτόν, καὶ ἐκέλευσεν ⸀συνελθεῖν τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ ⸀πᾶν τὸ ⸀συνέδριον, καὶ καταγαγὼν τὸν Παῦλον ἔστησεν εἰς αὐτούς.
verses.translit: Te de epayrion voylomenos gnonai to asfales to ti katigoreitai upo ton Ioydaion elysen auton, kai ekeleysen synelthein tous arhiereis kai pan to synedrion, kai katagagon ton Paulon estisen eis autoys.
verses.translation: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.

verses.original: ἀτενίσας δὲ ⸂ὁ Παῦλος τῷ συνεδρίῳ⸃ εἶπεν· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἐγὼ πάσῃ συνειδήσει ἀγαθῇ πεπολίτευμαι τῷ θεῷ ἄχρι ταύτης τῆς ἡμέρας.
verses.translit: atenisas de o Paulos to synedrio eipen* Andres adelfoi, ego pase syneidisei agathe pepoliteymai to theo ahri taytis tes emeras.
verses.translation: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀρχιερεὺς Ἁνανίας ἐπέταξεν τοῖς παρεστῶσιν αὐτῷ τύπτειν αὐτοῦ τὸ στόμα.
verses.translit: o de arhiereus Ananias epetaxen tois parestosin auto typtein autou to stoma.
verses.translation: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.

verses.original: τότε ὁ Παῦλος πρὸς αὐτὸν εἶπεν· Τύπτειν σε μέλλει ὁ θεός, τοῖχε κεκονιαμένε· καὶ σὺ κάθῃ κρίνων με κατὰ τὸν νόμον, καὶ παρανομῶν κελεύεις με τύπτεσθαι;
verses.translit: tote o Paulos pros auton eipen* Typtein se mellei o theos, toihe kekoniamene* kai su kathe krinon me kata ton nomon, kai paranomon keleyeis me typtesthai;
verses.translation: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?

verses.original: οἱ δὲ παρεστῶτες εἶπαν· Τὸν ἀρχιερέα τοῦ θεοῦ λοιδορεῖς;
verses.translit: oi de parestotes eipan* Ton arhierea tou theou loidoreis;
verses.translation: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest?

verses.original: ἔφη τε ὁ Παῦλος· Οὐκ ᾔδειν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι ἐστὶν ἀρχιερεύς· γέγραπται γὰρ ⸀ὅτι Ἄρχοντα τοῦ λαοῦ σου οὐκ ἐρεῖς κακῶς.
verses.translit: efi te o Paulos* Ouk edein, adelfoi, oti estin arhiereys* gegraptai gar oti Arhonta tou laou soy ouk ereis kakos.
verses.translation: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.

verses.original: Γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ὅτι τὸ ἓν μέρος ἐστὶν Σαδδουκαίων τὸ δὲ ἕτερον Φαρισαίων ⸀ἔκραζεν ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἐγὼ Φαρισαῖός εἰμι, υἱὸς ⸀Φαρισαίων· περὶ ἐλπίδος καὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν ⸀ἐγὼ κρίνομαι.
verses.translit: Gnous de o Paulos oti to en meros estin Saddoykaion to de eteron Farisaion ekrazen en to synedrio* Andres adelfoi, ego Farisaios eimi, yios Farisaion* peri elpidos kai anastaseos nekron ego krinomai.
verses.translation: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.

verses.original: τοῦτο δὲ αὐτοῦ ⸀λαλοῦντος ἐγένετο στάσις τῶν Φαρισαίων ⸂καὶ Σαδδουκαίων⸃, καὶ ἐσχίσθη τὸ πλῆθος.
verses.translit: touto de autou lalountos egeneto stasis ton Farisaion kai Saddoykaion, kai eshisthi to plethos.
verses.translation: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.

verses.original: Σαδδουκαῖοι ⸀μὲν γὰρ λέγουσιν μὴ εἶναι ἀνάστασιν ⸀μήτε ἄγγελον μήτε πνεῦμα, Φαρισαῖοι δὲ ὁμολογοῦσιν τὰ ἀμφότερα.
verses.translit: Saddoykaioi men gar legoysin me einai anastasin mite aggelon mite pneuma, Farisaioi de omologousin ta amfotera.
verses.translation: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.

verses.original: ἐγένετο δὲ κραυγὴ μεγάλη, καὶ ἀναστάντες ⸂τινὲς τῶν γραμματέων⸃ τοῦ μέρους τῶν Φαρισαίων διεμάχοντο λέγοντες· Οὐδὲν κακὸν εὑρίσκομεν ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ· εἰ δὲ πνεῦμα ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ ἢ ⸀ἄγγελος—
verses.translit: egeneto de krayge megali, kai anastantes tines ton grammateon tou meroys ton Farisaion diemahonto legontes* Ouden kakon euriskomen en to anthropo toyto* ei de pneuma elalisen auto e aggelos--
verses.translation: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees’ part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.

verses.original: πολλῆς δὲ ⸀γινομένης στάσεως ⸀φοβηθεὶς ὁ χιλίαρχος μὴ διασπασθῇ ὁ Παῦλος ὑπʼ αὐτῶν ἐκέλευσεν τὸ στράτευμα ⸀καταβὰν ἁρπάσαι αὐτὸν ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν, ἄγειν ⸀τε εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν.
verses.translit: polles de ginomenis staseos fovitheis o hiliarhos me diaspasthe o Paulos up' auton ekeleysen to strateyma katavan arpasai auton ek mesoy auton, agein te eis ten paremvolin.
verses.translation: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.

verses.original: Τῇ δὲ ἐπιούσῃ νυκτὶ ἐπιστὰς αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος εἶπεν· ⸀Θάρσει, ὡς γὰρ διεμαρτύρω τὰ περὶ ἐμοῦ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ οὕτω σε δεῖ καὶ εἰς Ῥώμην μαρτυρῆσαι.
verses.translit: Te de epioyse nykti epistas auto o kyrios eipen* Tharsei, os gar diemartyro ta peri emou eis Ieroysalem outo se dei kai eis Romin martyresai.
verses.translation: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.

verses.original: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ποιήσαντες ⸂συστροφὴν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι⸃ ἀνεθεμάτισαν ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες μήτε φαγεῖν μήτε πιεῖν ἕως οὗ ἀποκτείνωσιν τὸν Παῦλον.
verses.translit: Genomenis de emeras poiisantes systrofen oi Ioydaioi anethematisan eaytous legontes mite fagein mite piein eos ou apokteinosin ton Paulon.
verses.translation: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.

verses.original: ἦσαν δὲ πλείους τεσσεράκοντα οἱ ταύτην τὴν συνωμοσίαν ⸀ποιησάμενοι·
verses.translit: esan de pleioys tesserakonta oi taytin ten synomosian poiisamenoi*
verses.translation: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.

verses.original: οἵτινες προσελθόντες τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις εἶπαν· Ἀναθέματι ἀνεθεματίσαμεν ἑαυτοὺς μηδενὸς γεύσασθαι ἕως οὗ ἀποκτείνωμεν τὸν Παῦλον.
verses.translit: oitines proselthontes tois arhiereusin kai tois presvyterois eipan* Anathemati anethematisamen eaytous midenos geysasthai eos ou apokteinomen ton Paulon.
verses.translation: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.

verses.original: νῦν οὖν ὑμεῖς ἐμφανίσατε τῷ χιλιάρχῳ σὺν τῷ συνεδρίῳ ⸀ὅπως ⸂καταγάγῃ αὐτὸν εἰς⸃ ὑμᾶς ὡς μέλλοντας διαγινώσκειν ἀκριβέστερον τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ· ἡμεῖς δὲ πρὸ τοῦ ἐγγίσαι αὐτὸν ἕτοιμοί ἐσμεν τοῦ ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν.
verses.translit: nun oun umeis emfanisate to hiliarho sun to synedrio opos katagage auton eis umas os mellontas diaginoskein akrivesteron ta peri autou* emeis de pro tou eggisai auton etoimoi esmen tou anelein auton.
verses.translation: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.

verses.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀδελφῆς Παύλου ⸂τὴν ἐνέδραν⸃ παραγενόμενος καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολὴν ἀπήγγειλεν τῷ Παύλῳ.
verses.translit: Akoysas de o yios tes adelfes Payloy ten enedran paragenomenos kai eiselthon eis ten paremvolen apiggeilen to Paylo.
verses.translation: And when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.

verses.original: προσκαλεσάμενος δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἕνα τῶν ἑκατονταρχῶν ἔφη· Τὸν νεανίαν τοῦτον ⸀ἄπαγε πρὸς τὸν χιλίαρχον, ἔχει γὰρ ⸂ἀπαγγεῖλαί τι⸃ αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: proskalesamenos de o Paulos ena ton ekatontarhon efi* Ton neanian touton apage pros ton hiliarhon, ehei gar apaggeilai ti auto.
verses.translation: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him , and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.

verses.original: ὁ μὲν οὖν παραλαβὼν αὐτὸν ἤγαγεν πρὸς τὸν χιλίαρχον καὶ φησίν· Ὁ δέσμιος Παῦλος προσκαλεσάμενός με ἠρώτησεν τοῦτον τὸν ⸀νεανίαν ἀγαγεῖν πρὸς σέ, ἔχοντά τι λαλῆσαί σοι.
verses.translit: o men oun paralavon auton egagen pros ton hiliarhon kai fisin* O desmios Paulos proskalesamenos me erotisen touton ton neanian agagein pros se, ehonta ti lalesai soi.
verses.translation: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him , and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.

verses.original: ἐπιλαβόμενος δὲ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτοῦ ὁ χιλίαρχος καὶ ἀναχωρήσας κατʼ ἰδίαν ἐπυνθάνετο· Τί ἐστιν ὃ ἔχεις ἀπαγγεῖλαί μοι;
verses.translit: epilavomenos de tes heiros autou o hiliarhos kai anahorisas kat' idian epynthaneto* Ti estin o eheis apaggeilai moi;
verses.translation: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him , What is that thou hast to tell me?

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὅτι Οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι συνέθεντο τοῦ ἐρωτῆσαί σε ὅπως αὔριον ⸂τὸν Παῦλον καταγάγῃς εἰς τὸ συνέδριον⸃ ὡς ⸀μέλλον τι ἀκριβέστερον πυνθάνεσθαι περὶ αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: eipen de oti Oi Ioydaioi synethento tou erotesai se opos aurion ton Paulon katagages eis to synedrion os mellon ti akrivesteron pynthanesthai peri autou*
verses.translation: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.

verses.original: σὺ οὖν μὴ πεισθῇς αὐτοῖς, ἐνεδρεύουσιν γὰρ αὐτὸν ἐξ αὐτῶν ἄνδρες πλείους τεσσεράκοντα, οἵτινες ἀνεθεμάτισαν ἑαυτοὺς μήτε φαγεῖν μήτε πιεῖν ἕως οὗ ἀνέλωσιν αὐτόν, καὶ νῦν ⸂εἰσιν ἕτοιμοι⸃ προσδεχόμενοι τὴν ἀπὸ σοῦ ἐπαγγελίαν.
verses.translit: su oun me peisthes autois, enedreyoysin gar auton ex auton andres pleioys tesserakonta, oitines anethematisan eaytous mite fagein mite piein eos ou anelosin auton, kai nun eisin etoimoi prosdehomenoi ten apo sou epaggelian.
verses.translation: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.

verses.original: ὁ μὲν οὖν χιλίαρχος ἀπέλυσε τὸν ⸀νεανίσκον παραγγείλας μηδενὶ ἐκλαλῆσαι ὅτι ταῦτα ἐνεφάνισας πρὸς ⸀ἐμέ.
verses.translit: o men oun hiliarhos apelyse ton neaniskon paraggeilas mideni eklalesai oti tauta enefanisas pros eme.
verses.translation: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.

verses.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενός ⸂τινας δύο⸃ τῶν ἑκατονταρχῶν εἶπεν· Ἑτοιμάσατε στρατιώτας διακοσίους ὅπως πορευθῶσιν ἕως Καισαρείας, καὶ ἱππεῖς ἑβδομήκοντα καὶ δεξιολάβους διακοσίους, ἀπὸ τρίτης ὥρας τῆς νυκτός,
verses.translit: Kai proskalesamenos tinas dyo ton ekatontarhon eipen* Etoimasate stratiotas diakosioys opos poreythosin eos Kaisareias, kai ippeis evdomikonta kai dexiolavoys diakosioys, apo tritis oras tes nyktos,
verses.translation: And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Cæsarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;

verses.original: κτήνη τε παραστῆσαι ἵνα ἐπιβιβάσαντες τὸν Παῦλον διασώσωσι πρὸς Φήλικα τὸν ἡγεμόνα,
verses.translit: ktini te parastesai ina epivivasantes ton Paulon diasososi pros Filika ton egemona,
verses.translation: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.

verses.original: γράψας ἐπιστολὴν ⸀ἔχουσαν τὸν τύπον τοῦτον·
verses.translit: grapsas epistolen ehoysan ton typon touton*
verses.translation: And he wrote a letter after this manner:

verses.original: Κλαύδιος Λυσίας τῷ κρατίστῳ ἡγεμόνι Φήλικι χαίρειν.
verses.translit: Klaydios Lysias to kratisto egemoni Filiki hairein.
verses.translation: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sendeth greeting.

verses.original: τὸν ἄνδρα τοῦτον συλλημφθέντα ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ μέλλοντα ἀναιρεῖσθαι ὑπʼ αὐτῶν ἐπιστὰς σὺν τῷ στρατεύματι ⸀ἐξειλάμην, μαθὼν ὅτι Ῥωμαῖός ἐστιν,
verses.translit: ton andra touton syllimfthenta upo ton Ioydaion kai mellonta anaireisthai up' auton epistas sun to strateymati exeilamin, mathon oti Romaios estin,
verses.translation: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.

verses.original: βουλόμενός ⸀τε ⸀ἐπιγνῶναι τὴν αἰτίαν διʼ ἣν ἐνεκάλουν αὐτῷ, ⸀κατήγαγον εἰς τὸ συνέδριον αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: voylomenos te epignonai ten aitian di' en enekaloyn auto, katigagon eis to synedrion auton.
verses.translation: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:

verses.original: ὃν εὗρον ἐγκαλούμενον περὶ ζητημάτων τοῦ νόμου αὐτῶν, μηδὲν ⸀δὲ ἄξιον θανάτου ἢ δεσμῶν ⸂ἔχοντα ἔγκλημα⸃.
verses.translit: on euron egkaloymenon peri zitimaton tou nomoy auton, miden de axion thanatoy e desmon ehonta egklima.
verses.translation: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.

verses.original: μηνυθείσης δέ μοι ἐπιβουλῆς εἰς τὸν ⸀ἄνδρα ἔσεσθαι ⸀ἐξαυτῆς ἔπεμψα πρὸς σέ, παραγγείλας καὶ τοῖς κατηγόροις ⸀λέγειν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐπὶ ⸀σοῦ.
verses.translit: minytheisis de moi epivoyles eis ton andra esesthai exaytes epempsa pros se, paraggeilas kai tois katigorois legein pros auton epi sou.
verses.translation: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what they had against him. Farewell.

verses.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν στρατιῶται κατὰ τὸ διατεταγμένον αὐτοῖς ἀναλαβόντες τὸν Παῦλον ἤγαγον ⸀διὰ νυκτὸς εἰς τὴν Ἀντιπατρίδα·
verses.translit: Oi men oun stratiotai kata to diatetagmenon autois analavontes ton Paulon egagon dia nyktos eis ten Antipatrida*
verses.translation: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.

verses.original: τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον ἐάσαντες τοὺς ἱππεῖς ⸀ἀπέρχεσθαι σὺν αὐτῷ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς τὴν παρεμβολήν·
verses.translit: te de epayrion easantes tous ippeis aperhesthai sun auto upestrepsan eis ten paremvolin*
verses.translation: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:

verses.original: οἵτινες εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὴν Καισάρειαν καὶ ἀναδόντες τὴν ἐπιστολὴν τῷ ἡγεμόνι παρέστησαν καὶ τὸν Παῦλον αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: oitines eiselthontes eis ten Kaisareian kai anadontes ten epistolen to egemoni parestisan kai ton Paulon auto.
verses.translation: Who, when they came to Cæsarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.

verses.original: ἀναγνοὺς ⸀δὲ καὶ ἐπερωτήσας ἐκ ποίας ⸀ἐπαρχείας ἐστὶν καὶ πυθόμενος ὅτι ἀπὸ Κιλικίας,
verses.translit: anagnous de kai eperotisas ek poias eparheias estin kai pythomenos oti apo Kilikias,
verses.translation: And when the governor had read the letter , he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;

verses.original: Διακούσομαί σου, ἔφη, ὅταν καὶ οἱ κατήγοροί σου παραγένωνται· ⸀κελεύσας ἐν τῷ πραιτωρίῳ ⸀τοῦ Ἡρῴδου φυλάσσεσθαι ⸀αὐτόν.
verses.translit: Diakoysomai soy, efi, otan kai oi katigoroi soy paragenontai* keleysas en to praitorio tou Erodoy fylassesthai auton.
verses.translation: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s judgment hall.

verses.original: Μετὰ δὲ πέντε ἡμέρας κατέβη ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς Ἁνανίας μετὰ ⸂πρεσβυτέρων τινῶν⸃ καὶ ῥήτορος Τερτύλλου τινός, οἵτινες ἐνεφάνισαν τῷ ἡγεμόνι κατὰ τοῦ Παύλου.
verses.translit: Meta de pente emeras katevi o arhiereus Ananias meta presvyteron tinon kai Ritoros Tertylloy tinos, oitines enefanisan to egemoni kata tou Payloy.
verses.translation: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.

verses.original: κληθέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἤρξατο κατηγορεῖν ὁ Τέρτυλλος λέγων· Πολλῆς εἰρήνης τυγχάνοντες διὰ σοῦ καὶ ⸀διορθωμάτων γινομένων τῷ ἔθνει τούτῳ διὰ τῆς σῆς προνοίας
verses.translit: klithentos de autou erxato katigorein o Tertyllos legon* Polles eirinis tyghanontes dia sou kai diorthomaton ginomenon to ethnei toyto dia tes ses pronoias
verses.translation: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him , saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,

verses.original: πάντῃ τε καὶ πανταχοῦ ἀποδεχόμεθα, κράτιστε Φῆλιξ, μετὰ πάσης εὐχαριστίας.
verses.translit: pante te kai pantahou apodehometha, kratiste Felix, meta pasis euharistias.
verses.translation: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.

verses.original: ἵνα δὲ μὴ ἐπὶ πλεῖόν σε ἐγκόπτω, παρακαλῶ ἀκοῦσαί σε ἡμῶν συντόμως τῇ σῇ ἐπιεικείᾳ.
verses.translit: ina de me epi pleion se egkopto, parakalo akousai se emon syntomos te se epieikeia.
verses.translation: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.

verses.original: εὑρόντες γὰρ τὸν ἄνδρα τοῦτον λοιμὸν καὶ κινοῦντα ⸀στάσεις πᾶσι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις τοῖς κατὰ τὴν οἰκουμένην πρωτοστάτην τε τῆς τῶν Ναζωραίων αἱρέσεως,
verses.translit: eurontes gar ton andra touton loimon kai kinounta staseis pasi tois Ioydaiois tois kata ten oikoymenin protostatin te tes ton Nazoraion aireseos,
verses.translation: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow , and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:

verses.original: ὃς καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν ἐπείρασεν βεβηλῶσαι, ὃν καὶ ⸀ἐκρατήσαμεν,
verses.translit: os kai to ieron epeirasen vevilosai, on kai ekratisamen,
verses.translation: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.
But the chief captain Lysias came upon us , and with great violence took him away out of our hands,

verses.original: παρʼ οὗ δυνήσῃ αὐτὸς ἀνακρίνας περὶ πάντων τούτων ἐπιγνῶναι ὧν ἡμεῖς κατηγοροῦμεν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: par' ou dynise autos anakrinas peri panton toyton epignonai on emeis katigoroumen autou.
verses.translation: Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.

verses.original: συνεπέθεντο δὲ καὶ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι φάσκοντες ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχειν.
verses.translit: synepethento de kai oi Ioydaioi faskontes tauta outos ehein.
verses.translation: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.

verses.original: Ἀπεκρίθη ⸀τε ὁ Παῦλος νεύσαντος αὐτῷ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος λέγειν· Ἐκ πολλῶν ἐτῶν ὄντα σε κριτὴν τῷ ἔθνει τούτῳ ἐπιστάμενος ⸀εὐθύμως τὰ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ ἀπολογοῦμαι,
verses.translit: Apekrithi te o Paulos neysantos auto tou egemonos legein* Ek pollon eton onta se kriten to ethnei toyto epistamenos euthymos ta peri emaytou apologoumai,
verses.translation: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:

verses.original: δυναμένου σου ⸀ἐπιγνῶναι, ὅτι οὐ πλείους εἰσίν μοι ἡμέραι ⸀δώδεκα ἀφʼ ἧς ἀνέβην προσκυνήσων ⸀εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ,
verses.translit: dynamenoy soy epignonai, oti ou pleioys eisin moi emerai dodeka af' es anevin proskynison eis Ieroysalim,
verses.translation: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship.

verses.original: καὶ οὔτε ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ εὗρόν με πρός τινα διαλεγόμενον ἢ ⸀ἐπίστασιν ποιοῦντα ὄχλου οὔτε ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς οὔτε κατὰ τὴν πόλιν,
verses.translit: kai oute en to iero euron me pros tina dialegomenon e epistasin poiounta ohloy oute en tais synagogais oute kata ten polin,
verses.translation: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:

verses.original: ⸀οὐδὲ ⸀παραστῆσαι δύνανταί ⸀σοι περὶ ὧν ⸀νυνὶ κατηγοροῦσίν μου.
verses.translit: oude parastesai dynantai soi peri on nyni katigorousin moy.
verses.translation: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.

verses.original: ὁμολογῶ δὲ τοῦτό σοι ὅτι κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἣν λέγουσιν αἵρεσιν οὕτως λατρεύω τῷ πατρῴῳ θεῷ, πιστεύων πᾶσι τοῖς κατὰ τὸν νόμον καὶ ⸂τοῖς ἐν⸃ τοῖς προφήταις γεγραμμένοις,
verses.translit: omologo de touto soi oti kata ten odon en legoysin airesin outos latreyo to patroo theo, pisteyon pasi tois kata ton nomon kai tois en tois profitais gegrammenois,
verses.translation: But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:

verses.original: ἐλπίδα ἔχων εἰς τὸν θεόν, ἣν καὶ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι προσδέχονται, ἀνάστασιν μέλλειν ⸀ἔσεσθαι δικαίων τε καὶ ἀδίκων·
verses.translit: elpida ehon eis ton theon, en kai autoi outoi prosdehontai, anastasin mellein esesthai dikaion te kai adikon*
verses.translation: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.

verses.original: ἐν τούτῳ ⸀καὶ αὐτὸς ἀσκῶ ἀπρόσκοπον συνείδησιν ⸀ἔχειν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους διὰ παντός.
verses.translit: en toyto kai autos asko aproskopon syneidisin ehein pros ton theon kai tous anthropoys dia pantos.
verses.translation: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.

verses.original: διʼ ἐτῶν δὲ πλειόνων ⸂ἐλεημοσύνας ποιήσων εἰς τὸ ἔθνος μου παρεγενόμην⸃ καὶ προσφοράς,
verses.translit: di' eton de pleionon eleimosynas poiison eis to ethnos moy paregenomin kai prosforas,
verses.translation: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.

verses.original: ἐν ⸀αἷς εὗρόν με ἡγνισμένον ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, οὐ μετὰ ὄχλου οὐδὲ μετὰ θορύβου,
verses.translit: en ais euron me egnismenon en to iero, ou meta ohloy oude meta thoryvoy,
verses.translation: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.

verses.original: τινὲς δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι, οὓς ⸀ἔδει ἐπὶ σοῦ παρεῖναι καὶ κατηγορεῖν εἴ τι ἔχοιεν πρὸς ⸀ἐμέ,
verses.translit: tines de apo tes Asias Ioydaioi, ous edei epi sou pareinai kai katigorein ei ti ehoien pros eme,
verses.translation: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.

verses.original: ἢ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι εἰπάτωσαν τί ⸀εὗρον ἀδίκημα στάντος μου ἐπὶ τοῦ συνεδρίου
verses.translit: e autoi outoi eipatosan ti euron adikima stantos moy epi tou synedrioy
verses.translation: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,

verses.original: ἢ περὶ μιᾶς ταύτης φωνῆς ἧς ἐκέκραξα ⸂ἐν αὐτοῖς ἑστὼς⸃ ὅτι Περὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν ἐγὼ κρίνομαι σήμερον ⸀ἐφʼ ὑμῶν.
verses.translit: e peri mias taytis fones es ekekraxa en autois estos oti Peri anastaseos nekron ego krinomai simeron ef' umon.
verses.translation: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.

verses.original: ⸂Ἀνεβάλετο δὲ αὐτοὺς ὁ Φῆλιξ⸃, ἀκριβέστερον εἰδὼς τὰ περὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ, ⸀εἴπας· Ὅταν Λυσίας ὁ χιλίαρχος καταβῇ διαγνώσομαι τὰ καθʼ ὑμᾶς·
verses.translit: Anevaleto de autous o Felix, akrivesteron eidos ta peri tes odou, eipas* Otan Lysias o hiliarhos katave diagnosomai ta kath' umas*
verses.translation: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.

verses.original: ⸀διαταξάμενος τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ τηρεῖσθαι ⸀αὐτὸν ἔχειν τε ἄνεσιν καὶ μηδένα κωλύειν τῶν ἰδίων αὐτοῦ ⸀ὑπηρετεῖν αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: diataxamenos to ekatontarhe tireisthai auton ehein te anesin kai midena kolyein ton idion autou upiretein auto.
verses.translation: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.

verses.original: Μετὰ δὲ ἡμέρας τινὰς παραγενόμενος ὁ Φῆλιξ σὺν Δρουσίλλῃ τῇ ⸀ἰδίᾳ γυναικὶ οὔσῃ Ἰουδαίᾳ μετεπέμψατο τὸν Παῦλον καὶ ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ περὶ τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν ⸀Ἰησοῦν πίστεως.
verses.translit: Meta de emeras tinas paragenomenos o Felix sun Droysille te idia gynaiki ouse Ioydaia metepempsato ton Paulon kai ekoysen autou peri tes eis Hriston Iisoun pisteos.
verses.translation: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.

verses.original: διαλεγομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ περὶ δικαιοσύνης καὶ ἐγκρατείας καὶ τοῦ κρίματος τοῦ ⸀μέλλοντος ἔμφοβος γενόμενος ὁ Φῆλιξ ἀπεκρίθη· Τὸ νῦν ἔχον πορεύου, καιρὸν δὲ μεταλαβὼν μετακαλέσομαί σε·
verses.translit: dialegomenoy de autou peri dikaiosynis kai egkrateias kai tou krimatos tou mellontos emfovos genomenos o Felix apekrithi* To nun ehon poreyoy, kairon de metalavon metakalesomai se*
verses.translation: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.

verses.original: ἅμα καὶ ἐλπίζων ὅτι χρήματα δοθήσεται αὐτῷ ὑπὸ τοῦ ⸀Παύλου· διὸ καὶ πυκνότερον αὐτὸν μεταπεμπόμενος ὡμίλει αὐτῷ.
verses.translit: ama kai elpizon oti hrimata dothisetai auto upo tou Payloy* dio kai pyknoteron auton metapempomenos omilei auto.
verses.translation: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.

verses.original: Διετίας δὲ πληρωθείσης ἔλαβεν διάδοχον ὁ Φῆλιξ Πόρκιον Φῆστον· θέλων τε ⸀χάριτα καταθέσθαι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὁ Φῆλιξ κατέλιπε τὸν Παῦλον δεδεμένον.
verses.translit: Dietias de plirotheisis elaven diadohon o Felix Porkion Feston* thelon te harita katathesthai tois Ioydaiois o Felix katelipe ton Paulon dedemenon.
verses.translation: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix’ room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.

verses.original: Φῆστος οὖν ἐπιβὰς τῇ ἐπαρχείᾳ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀνέβη εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀπὸ Καισαρείας,
verses.translit: Festos oun epivas te eparheia meta treis emeras anevi eis Ierosolyma apo Kaisareias,
verses.translation: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Cæsarea to Jerusalem.

verses.original: ἐνεφάνισάν ⸀τε αὐτῷ ⸂οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς⸃ καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι τῶν Ἰουδαίων κατὰ τοῦ Παύλου, καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν
verses.translit: enefanisan te auto oi arhiereis kai oi protoi ton Ioydaion kata tou Payloy, kai parekaloyn auton
verses.translation: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,

verses.original: αἰτούμενοι χάριν κατʼ αὐτοῦ ὅπως μεταπέμψηται αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἐνέδραν ποιοῦντες ἀνελεῖν αὐτὸν κατὰ τὴν ὁδόν.
verses.translit: aitoymenoi harin kat' autou opos metapempsitai auton eis Ieroysalim, enedran poiountes anelein auton kata ten odon.
verses.translation: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.

verses.original: ὁ μὲν οὖν Φῆστος ἀπεκρίθη τηρεῖσθαι τὸν Παῦλον ⸂εἰς Καισάρειαν⸃, ἑαυτὸν δὲ μέλλειν ἐν τάχει ἐκπορεύεσθαι·
verses.translit: o men oun Festos apekrithi tireisthai ton Paulon eis Kaisareian, eayton de mellein en tahei ekporeyesthai*
verses.translation: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Cæsarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither .

verses.original: Οἱ οὖν ⸂ἐν ὑμῖν, φησίν, δυνατοὶ⸃ συγκαταβάντες εἴ τί ἐστιν ἐν τῷ ἀνδρὶ ⸀ἄτοπον κατηγορείτωσαν αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Oi oun en umin, fisin, dynatoi sygkatavantes ei ti estin en to andri atopon katigoreitosan autou.
verses.translation: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me , and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.

verses.original: Διατρίψας δὲ ἐν αὐτοῖς ἡμέρας ⸂οὐ πλείους ὀκτὼ⸃ ἢ δέκα, καταβὰς εἰς Καισάρειαν, τῇ ἐπαύριον καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐκέλευσεν τὸν Παῦλον ἀχθῆναι.
verses.translit: Diatripsas de en autois emeras ou pleioys okto e deka, katavas eis Kaisareian, te epayrion kathisas epi tou vimatos ekeleysen ton Paulon ahthenai.
verses.translation: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Cæsarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.

verses.original: παραγενομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ περιέστησαν ⸀αὐτὸν οἱ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καταβεβηκότες Ἰουδαῖοι, πολλὰ καὶ βαρέα αἰτιώματα ⸀καταφέροντες ἃ οὐκ ἴσχυον ἀποδεῖξαι,
verses.translit: paragenomenoy de autou periestisan auton oi apo Ierosolymon katavevikotes Ioydaioi, polla kai varea aitiomata kataferontes a ouk ishyon apodeixai,
verses.translation: And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.

verses.original: ⸂τοῦ Παύλου ἀπολογουμένου⸃ ὅτι Οὔτε εἰς τὸν νόμον τῶν Ἰουδαίων οὔτε εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν οὔτε εἰς Καίσαρά τι ἥμαρτον.
verses.translit: tou Payloy apologoymenoy oti Oute eis ton nomon ton Ioydaion oute eis to ieron oute eis Kaisara ti emarton.
verses.translation: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Cæsar, have I offended any thing at all.

verses.original: ὁ Φῆστος δὲ ⸂θέλων τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις⸃ χάριν καταθέσθαι ἀποκριθεὶς τῷ Παύλῳ εἶπεν· Θέλεις εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀναβὰς ἐκεῖ περὶ τούτων ⸀κριθῆναι ἐπʼ ἐμοῦ;
verses.translit: o Festos de thelon tois Ioydaiois harin katathesthai apokritheis to Paylo eipen* Theleis eis Ierosolyma anavas ekei peri toyton krithenai ep' emou;
verses.translation: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Παῦλος· ⸂Ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος Καίσαρος ἑστώς⸃ εἰμι, οὗ με δεῖ κρίνεσθαι. Ἰουδαίους οὐδὲν ⸀ἠδίκησα, ὡς καὶ σὺ κάλλιον ἐπιγινώσκεις.
verses.translit: eipen de o Paulos* Epi tou vimatos Kaisaros estos eimi, ou me dei krinesthai. Ioydaioys ouden edikisa, os kai su kallion epiginoskeis.
verses.translation: Then said Paul, I stand at Cæsar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.

verses.original: εἰ μὲν ⸀οὖν ἀδικῶ καὶ ἄξιον θανάτου πέπραχά τι, οὐ παραιτοῦμαι τὸ ἀποθανεῖν· εἰ δὲ οὐδέν ἐστιν ὧν οὗτοι κατηγοροῦσίν μου, οὐδείς με δύναται αὐτοῖς χαρίσασθαι· Καίσαρα ἐπικαλοῦμαι.
verses.translit: ei men oun adiko kai axion thanatoy pepraha ti, ou paraitoumai to apothanein* ei de ouden estin on outoi katigorousin moy, oudeis me dynatai autois harisasthai* Kaisara epikaloumai.
verses.translation: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Cæsar.

verses.original: τότε ὁ Φῆστος συλλαλήσας μετὰ τοῦ συμβουλίου ἀπεκρίθη· Καίσαρα ἐπικέκλησαι, ἐπὶ Καίσαρα πορεύσῃ.
verses.translit: tote o Festos syllalisas meta tou symvoylioy apekrithi* Kaisara epikeklisai, epi Kaisara poreyse.
verses.translation: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Cæsar? unto Cæsar shalt thou go.

verses.original: Ἡμερῶν δὲ διαγενομένων τινῶν Ἀγρίππας ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ Βερνίκη κατήντησαν εἰς Καισάρειαν ἀσπασάμενοι τὸν Φῆστον.
verses.translit: Emeron de diagenomenon tinon Agrippas o vasileus kai Verniki katintisan eis Kaisareian aspasamenoi ton Feston.
verses.translation: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Cæsarea to salute Festus.

verses.original: ὡς δὲ πλείους ἡμέρας ⸀διέτριβον ἐκεῖ, ὁ Φῆστος τῷ βασιλεῖ ἀνέθετο τὰ κατὰ τὸν Παῦλον λέγων· Ἀνήρ τίς ἐστιν καταλελειμμένος ὑπὸ Φήλικος δέσμιος,
verses.translit: os de pleioys emeras dietrivon ekei, o Festos to vasilei anetheto ta kata ton Paulon legon* Anir tis estin kataleleimmenos upo Filikos desmios,
verses.translation: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul’s cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:

verses.original: περὶ οὗ γενομένου μου εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐνεφάνισαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τῶν Ἰουδαίων, αἰτούμενοι κατʼ αὐτοῦ ⸀καταδίκην·
verses.translit: peri ou genomenoy moy eis Ierosolyma enefanisan oi arhiereis kai oi presvyteroi ton Ioydaion, aitoymenoi kat' autou katadikin*
verses.translation: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me , desiring to have judgment against him.

verses.original: πρὸς οὓς ἀπεκρίθην ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ἔθος Ῥωμαίοις χαρίζεσθαί τινα ⸀ἄνθρωπον πρὶν ἢ ὁ κατηγορούμενος κατὰ πρόσωπον ἔχοι τοὺς κατηγόρους τόπον τε ἀπολογίας λάβοι περὶ τοῦ ἐγκλήματος.
verses.translit: pros ous apekrithin oti ouk estin ethos Romaiois harizesthai tina anthropon prin e o katigoroymenos kata prosopon ehoi tous katigoroys topon te apologias lavoi peri tou egklimatos.
verses.translation: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.

verses.original: συνελθόντων ⸀οὖν ἐνθάδε ἀναβολὴν μηδεμίαν ποιησάμενος τῇ ἑξῆς καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐκέλευσα ἀχθῆναι τὸν ἄνδρα·
verses.translit: synelthonton oun enthade anavolen midemian poiisamenos te exes kathisas epi tou vimatos ekeleysa ahthenai ton andra*
verses.translation: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.

verses.original: περὶ οὗ σταθέντες οἱ κατήγοροι οὐδεμίαν αἰτίαν ⸀ἔφερον ὧν ⸂ἐγὼ ὑπενόουν⸃ ⸀πονηρῶν,
verses.translit: peri ou stathentes oi katigoroi oudemian aitian eferon on ego upenooyn poniron,
verses.translation: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:

verses.original: ζητήματα δέ τινα περὶ τῆς ἰδίας δεισιδαιμονίας εἶχον πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ περί τινος Ἰησοῦ τεθνηκότος, ὃν ἔφασκεν ὁ Παῦλος ζῆν.
verses.translit: zitimata de tina peri tes idias deisidaimonias eihon pros auton kai peri tinos Iisou tethnikotos, on efasken o Paulos zen.
verses.translation: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

verses.original: ἀπορούμενος δὲ ἐγὼ τὴν περὶ ⸀τούτων ζήτησιν ἔλεγον εἰ βούλοιτο πορεύεσθαι εἰς ⸀Ἱεροσόλυμα κἀκεῖ κρίνεσθαι περὶ τούτων.
verses.translit: aporoymenos de ego ten peri toyton zitisin elegon ei voyloito poreyesthai eis Ierosolyma kakei krinesthai peri toyton.
verses.translation: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.

verses.original: τοῦ δὲ Παύλου ἐπικαλεσαμένου τηρηθῆναι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ διάγνωσιν, ἐκέλευσα τηρεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἕως οὗ ⸀ἀναπέμψω αὐτὸν πρὸς Καίσαρα.
verses.translit: tou de Payloy epikalesamenoy tirithenai auton eis ten tou Sevastou diagnosin, ekeleysa tireisthai auton eos ou anapempso auton pros Kaisara.
verses.translation: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Cæsar.

verses.original: Ἀγρίππας δὲ πρὸς τὸν ⸀Φῆστον· Ἐβουλόμην καὶ αὐτὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀκοῦσαι. ⸀Αὔριον, φησίν, ἀκούσῃ αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Agrippas de pros ton Feston* Evoylomin kai autos tou anthropoy akousai. Aurion, fisin, akoyse autou.
verses.translation: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.

verses.original: Τῇ οὖν ἐπαύριον ἐλθόντος τοῦ Ἀγρίππα καὶ τῆς Βερνίκης μετὰ πολλῆς φαντασίας καὶ εἰσελθόντων εἰς τὸ ἀκροατήριον σύν ⸀τε χιλιάρχοις καὶ ἀνδράσιν τοῖς κατʼ ⸀ἐξοχὴν τῆς πόλεως καὶ κελεύσαντος τοῦ Φήστου ἤχθη ὁ Παῦλος.
verses.translit: Te oun epayrion elthontos tou Agrippa kai tes Vernikis meta polles fantasias kai eiselthonton eis to akroatirion syn te hiliarhois kai andrasin tois kat' exohen tes poleos kai keleysantos tou Fistoy ehthi o Paulos.
verses.translation: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus’ commandment Paul was brought forth.

verses.original: καί φησιν ὁ Φῆστος· Ἀγρίππα βασιλεῦ καὶ πάντες οἱ συμπαρόντες ἡμῖν ἄνδρες, θεωρεῖτε τοῦτον περὶ οὗ ⸀ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος τῶν Ἰουδαίων ⸀ἐνέτυχόν μοι ἔν τε Ἱεροσολύμοις καὶ ἐνθάδε, ⸀βοῶντες μὴ δεῖν ⸂αὐτὸν ζῆν⸃ μηκέτι.
verses.translit: kai fisin o Festos* Agrippa vasileu kai pantes oi symparontes emin andres, theoreite touton peri ou apan to plethos ton Ioydaion enetyhon moi en te Ierosolymois kai enthade, voontes me dein auton zen miketi.
verses.translation: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

verses.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ⸀κατελαβόμην μηδὲν ἄξιον ⸂αὐτὸν θανάτου⸃ πεπραχέναι, ⸀αὐτοῦ δὲ τούτου ἐπικαλεσαμένου τὸν Σεβαστὸν ἔκρινα ⸀πέμπειν.
verses.translit: ego de katelavomin miden axion auton thanatoy peprahenai, autou de toytoy epikalesamenoy ton Sevaston ekrina pempein.
verses.translation: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.

verses.original: περὶ οὗ ἀσφαλές τι γράψαι τῷ κυρίῳ οὐκ ἔχω· διὸ προήγαγον αὐτὸν ἐφʼ ὑμῶν καὶ μάλιστα ἐπὶ σοῦ, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, ὅπως τῆς ἀνακρίσεως γενομένης σχῶ τί ⸀γράψω·
verses.translit: peri ou asfales ti grapsai to kyrio ouk eho* dio proigagon auton ef' umon kai malista epi sou, vasileu Agrippa, opos tes anakriseos genomenis sho ti grapso*
verses.translation: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.

verses.original: ἄλογον γάρ μοι δοκεῖ πέμποντα δέσμιον μὴ καὶ τὰς κατʼ αὐτοῦ αἰτίας σημᾶναι.
verses.translit: alogon gar moi dokei pemponta desmion me kai tas kat' autou aitias simanai.
verses.translation: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him.

verses.original: Ἀγρίππας δὲ πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον ἔφη· Ἐπιτρέπεταί σοι ⸀ὑπὲρ σεαυτοῦ λέγειν. τότε ὁ Παῦλος ⸂ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἀπελογεῖτο⸃·
verses.translit: Agrippas de pros ton Paulon efi* Epitrepetai soi uper seaytou legein. tote o Paulos ekteinas ten heira apelogeito*
verses.translation: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:

verses.original: Περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐγκαλοῦμαι ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, ἥγημαι ἐμαυτὸν μακάριον ἐπὶ σοῦ μέλλων ⸂σήμερον ἀπολογεῖσθαι⸃,
verses.translit: Peri panton on egkaloumai upo Ioydaion, vasileu Agrippa, egimai emayton makarion epi sou mellon simeron apologeisthai,
verses.translation: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:

verses.original: μάλιστα γνώστην ὄντα σε πάντων τῶν κατὰ Ἰουδαίους ⸀ἐθῶν τε καὶ ζητημάτων· διὸ ⸀δέομαι μακροθύμως ἀκοῦσαί μου.
verses.translit: malista gnostin onta se panton ton kata Ioydaioys ethon te kai zitimaton* dio deomai makrothymos akousai moy.
verses.translation: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.

verses.original: Τὴν μὲν οὖν βίωσίν μου ⸀τὴν ἐκ νεότητος τὴν ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς γενομένην ἐν τῷ ἔθνει μου ἔν ⸀τε Ἱεροσολύμοις ἴσασι ⸀πάντες Ἰουδαῖοι,
verses.translit: Ten men oun viosin moy ten ek neotitos ten ap' arhes genomenin en to ethnei moy en te Ierosolymois isasi pantes Ioydaioi,
verses.translation: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;

verses.original: προγινώσκοντές με ἄνωθεν, ἐὰν θέλωσι μαρτυρεῖν, ὅτι κατὰ τὴν ἀκριβεστάτην αἵρεσιν τῆς ἡμετέρας θρησκείας ἔζησα Φαρισαῖος.
verses.translit: proginoskontes me anothen, ean thelosi martyrein, oti kata ten akrivestatin airesin tes emeteras thriskeias ezisa Farisaios.
verses.translation: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

verses.original: καὶ νῦν ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι τῆς ⸀εἰς τοὺς πατέρας ⸀ἡμῶν ἐπαγγελίας γενομένης ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἕστηκα κρινόμενος,
verses.translit: kai nun ep' elpidi tes eis tous pateras emon epaggelias genomenis upo tou theou estika krinomenos,
verses.translation: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers:

verses.original: εἰς ἣν τὸ δωδεκάφυλον ἡμῶν ἐν ἐκτενείᾳ νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν λατρεῦον ἐλπίζει καταντῆσαι· περὶ ἧς ἐλπίδος ἐγκαλοῦμαι ⸂ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων, βασιλεῦ⸃·
verses.translit: eis en to dodekafylon emon en ekteneia nykta kai emeran latreuon elpizei katantesai* peri es elpidos egkaloumai upo Ioydaion, vasileu*
verses.translation: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.

verses.original: τί ἄπιστον κρίνεται παρʼ ὑμῖν εἰ ὁ θεὸς νεκροὺς ἐγείρει;
verses.translit: ti apiston krinetai par' umin ei o theos nekrous egeirei;
verses.translation: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?

verses.original: Ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν ἔδοξα ἐμαυτῷ πρὸς τὸ ὄνομα Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου δεῖν πολλὰ ἐναντία πρᾶξαι·
verses.translit: Ego men oun edoxa emayto pros to onoma Iisou tou Nazoraioy dein polla enantia praxai*
verses.translation: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

verses.original: ὃ καὶ ἐποίησα ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις, καὶ πολλούς ⸀τε τῶν ἁγίων ἐγὼ ⸀ἐν φυλακαῖς κατέκλεισα τὴν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων ἐξουσίαν λαβών, ἀναιρουμένων τε αὐτῶν κατήνεγκα ψῆφον,
verses.translit: o kai epoiisa en Ierosolymois, kai polloys te ton agion ego en fylakais katekleisa ten para ton arhiereon exoysian lavon, anairoymenon te auton katinegka psefon,
verses.translation: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them .

verses.original: καὶ κατὰ πάσας τὰς συναγωγὰς πολλάκις τιμωρῶν αὐτοὺς ἠνάγκαζον βλασφημεῖν, περισσῶς τε ἐμμαινόμενος αὐτοῖς ἐδίωκον ἕως καὶ εἰς τὰς ἔξω πόλεις.
verses.translit: kai kata pasas tas synagogas pollakis timoron autous enagkazon vlasfimein, perissos te emmainomenos autois ediokon eos kai eis tas exo poleis.
verses.translation: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.

verses.original: Ἐν ⸀οἷς πορευόμενος εἰς τὴν Δαμασκὸν μετʼ ἐξουσίας καὶ ἐπιτροπῆς ⸀τῆς τῶν ἀρχιερέων
verses.translit: En ois poreyomenos eis ten Damaskon met' exoysias kai epitropes tes ton arhiereon
verses.translation: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,

verses.original: ἡμέρας μέσης κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν εἶδον, βασιλεῦ, οὐρανόθεν ὑπὲρ τὴν λαμπρότητα τοῦ ἡλίου περιλάμψαν με φῶς καὶ τοὺς σὺν ἐμοὶ πορευομένους·
verses.translit: emeras mesis kata ten odon eidon, vasileu, ouranothen uper ten lamprotita tou elioy perilampsan me fos kai tous sun emoi poreyomenoys*
verses.translation: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.

verses.original: πάντων ⸀τε καταπεσόντων ἡμῶν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἤκουσα φωνὴν ⸀λέγουσαν πρός ⸀με τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ· Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις; σκληρόν σοι πρὸς κέντρα λακτίζειν.
verses.translit: panton te katapesonton emon eis ten gen ekoysa fonen legoysan pros me te EvraIdi dialekto* Saoul Saoyl, ti me diokeis; skliron soi pros kentra laktizein.
verses.translation: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

verses.original: ἐγὼ δὲ εἶπα· Τίς εἶ, κύριε; ὁ δὲ ⸀κύριος εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις·
verses.translit: ego de eipa* Tis ei, kyrie; o de kyrios eipen* Ego eimi Iisous on su diokeis*
verses.translation: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.

verses.original: ἀλλὰ ἀνάστηθι καὶ στῆθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου· εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ὤφθην σοι, προχειρίσασθαί σε ὑπηρέτην καὶ μάρτυρα ὧν τε εἶδές ⸀με ὧν τε ὀφθήσομαί σοι,
verses.translit: alla anastithi kai stethi epi tous podas soy* eis touto gar ofthin soi, proheirisasthai se upiretin kai martyra on te eides me on te ofthisomai soi,
verses.translation: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;

verses.original: ἐξαιρούμενός σε ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ⸀ἐκ τῶν ἐθνῶν, εἰς οὓς ἐγὼ ⸂ἀποστέλλω σε⸃
verses.translit: exairoymenos se ek tou laou kai ek ton ethnon, eis ous ego apostello se
verses.translation: Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,

verses.original: ἀνοῖξαι ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν, τοῦ ⸀ἐπιστρέψαι ἀπὸ σκότους εἰς φῶς καὶ τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ Σατανᾶ ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, τοῦ λαβεῖν αὐτοὺς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ κλῆρον ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πίστει τῇ εἰς ἐμέ.
verses.translit: anoixai ofthalmous auton, tou epistrepsai apo skotoys eis fos kai tes exoysias tou Satana epi ton theon, tou lavein autous afesin amartion kai kleron en tois egiasmenois pistei te eis eme.
verses.translation: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.

verses.original: Ὅθεν, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, οὐκ ἐγενόμην ἀπειθὴς τῇ οὐρανίῳ ὀπτασίᾳ,
verses.translit: Othen, vasileu Agrippa, ouk egenomin apeithes te ouranio optasia,
verses.translation: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:

verses.original: ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἐν Δαμασκῷ πρῶτόν ⸀τε καὶ Ἱεροσολύμοις, ⸀πᾶσάν τε τὴν χώραν τῆς Ἰουδαίας, καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ⸀ἀπήγγελλον μετανοεῖν καὶ ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, ἄξια τῆς μετανοίας ἔργα πράσσοντας.
verses.translit: alla tois en Damasko proton te kai Ierosolymois, pasan te ten horan tes Ioydaias, kai tois ethnesin apiggellon metanoein kai epistrefein epi ton theon, axia tes metanoias erga prassontas.
verses.translation: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judæa, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.

verses.original: ἕνεκα τούτων ⸂με Ἰουδαῖοι⸃ ⸀συλλαβόμενοι ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐπειρῶντο διαχειρίσασθαι.
verses.translit: eneka toyton me Ioydaioi syllavomenoi en to iero epeironto diaheirisasthai.
verses.translation: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me .

verses.original: ἐπικουρίας οὖν τυχὼν τῆς ⸀ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἄχρι τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης ἕστηκα μαρτυρόμενος μικρῷ τε καὶ μεγάλῳ, οὐδὲν ἐκτὸς λέγων ὧν τε οἱ προφῆται ἐλάλησαν μελλόντων γίνεσθαι καὶ Μωϋσῆς,
verses.translit: epikoyrias oun tyhon tes apo tou theou ahri tes emeras taytis estika martyromenos mikro te kai megalo, ouden ektos legon on te oi profetai elalisan mellonton ginesthai kai Moyses,
verses.translation: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:

verses.original: εἰ παθητὸς ὁ χριστός, εἰ πρῶτος ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν φῶς μέλλει καταγγέλλειν τῷ ⸀τε λαῷ καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.
verses.translit: ei pathitos o hristos, ei protos ex anastaseos nekron fos mellei kataggellein to te lao kai tois ethnesin.
verses.translation: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.

verses.original: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀπολογουμένου ὁ Φῆστος μεγάλῃ τῇ φωνῇ ⸀φησιν· Μαίνῃ, Παῦλε· τὰ πολλά σε γράμματα εἰς μανίαν περιτρέπει.
verses.translit: Tauta de autou apologoymenoy o Festos megale te fone fisin* Maine, Paule* ta polla se grammata eis manian peritrepei.
verses.translation: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ⸀Παῦλος· Οὐ μαίνομαι, φησίν, κράτιστε Φῆστε, ἀλλὰ ἀληθείας καὶ σωφροσύνης ῥήματα ἀποφθέγγομαι.
verses.translit: o de Paulos* Ou mainomai, fisin, kratiste Feste, alla alitheias kai sofrosynis Rimata apoftheggomai.
verses.translation: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.

verses.original: ἐπίσταται γὰρ περὶ τούτων ὁ βασιλεύς, πρὸς ὃν ⸀καὶ παρρησιαζόμενος λαλῶ· λανθάνειν γὰρ ⸀αὐτὸν τούτων οὐ πείθομαι ⸀οὐθέν, οὐ γάρ ⸀ἐστιν ἐν γωνίᾳ πεπραγμένον τοῦτο.
verses.translit: epistatai gar peri toyton o vasileys, pros on kai parrisiazomenos lalo* lanthanein gar auton toyton ou peithomai outhen, ou gar estin en gonia pepragmenon touto.
verses.translation: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.

verses.original: πιστεύεις, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, τοῖς προφήταις; οἶδα ὅτι πιστεύεις.
verses.translit: pisteyeis, vasileu Agrippa, tois profitais; oida oti pisteyeis.
verses.translation: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἀγρίππας πρὸς τὸν ⸀Παῦλον· Ἐν ὀλίγῳ με πείθεις Χριστιανὸν ⸀ποιῆσαι.
verses.translit: o de Agrippas pros ton Paulon* En oligo me peitheis Hristianon poiesai.
verses.translation: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ⸀Παῦλος· Εὐξαίμην ἂν τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐν ὀλίγῳ καὶ ἐν ⸀μεγάλῳ οὐ μόνον σὲ ἀλλὰ καὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντάς μου σήμερον γενέσθαι τοιούτους ὁποῖος καὶ ἐγώ εἰμι παρεκτὸς τῶν δεσμῶν τούτων.
verses.translit: o de Paulos* Euxaimin an to theo kai en oligo kai en megalo ou monon se alla kai pantas tous akoyontas moy simeron genesthai toioytoys opoios kai ego eimi parektos ton desmon toyton.
verses.translation: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.

verses.original: ⸀Ἀνέστη ⸀τε ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἥ τε Βερνίκη καὶ οἱ συγκαθήμενοι αὐτοῖς,
verses.translit: Anesti te o vasileus kai o egemon e te Verniki kai oi sygkathimenoi autois,
verses.translation: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:

verses.original: καὶ ἀναχωρήσαντες ἐλάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες ὅτι Οὐδὲν θανάτου ⸂ἢ δεσμῶν ἄξιον⸃ ⸀τι πράσσει ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος.
verses.translit: kai anahorisantes elaloyn pros alliloys legontes oti Ouden thanatoy e desmon axion ti prassei o anthropos outos.
verses.translation: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.

verses.original: Ἀγρίππας δὲ τῷ Φήστῳ ἔφη· Ἀπολελύσθαι ἐδύνατο ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος εἰ μὴ ἐπεκέκλητο Καίσαρα.
verses.translit: Agrippas de to Fisto efi* Apolelysthai edynato o anthropos outos ei me epekeklito Kaisara.
verses.translation: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Cæsar.
